english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat or sudden changes between very dry soil and heavy watering.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nu ni fa babaoo teŋ.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that blocks water from moving up inside the plant stem. Rotating crops helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods dry up and turn dark before the beans inside grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This happens when pod-sucking bugs pierce the young cowpea pods and drain their liquid, which starves the developing seeds inside.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ pod lɛ tswa tsina ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ni amɛjie nu lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If your previous crops grew very slowly, looked pale yellow, or gave poor harvests, it is a sign that the soil is low on essential nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ dara blɛoo waa Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa No ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested fresh coconuts spoil so quickly compared to the fully dried ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii ni mikpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto ŋmei ni egbi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Fresh green coconuts contain high amounts of water and soft flesh that spoil and ferment rapidly once cut from the tree. As a coconut fully matures on the tree, its husk hardens and dries out, creating a natural sealed shell that protects the inner meat and allows it to stay good for months without spoiling.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ni afee ehee lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ afo kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, efiteɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ kwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Ehewolo lɛ wa ni egbi. Enɛ haa loo lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni buɔ loo lɛ he, ni ehaa ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee.

english: Why does my homemade coconut oil spoil and smell bad after keeping it for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔ ni akɛfee shia lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔɔ kɛ́ akɛto otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Spoil and unpleasant smells happen when tiny drops of water or wet fruit pulp remain in the oil after extraction. Bacteria react with this leftover moisture; drying the coconut meat completely in the sun or heat before pressing out the oil prevents it from going bad.
ga: Nu mli nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Aloo aduawai amli ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ hiɔ fɔ lɛ mli beni ajie lɛ sɛɛ. Bacteria kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei loo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo awo mli la dani ajie fɔ lɛ, no haaa ŋmei loo lɛ afite.

english: How can I tell when my coconut fruits are mature enough for heavy oil processing instead of fresh drinking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-koko lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afee lɛ fɔ ni tsii yɛ nu kpakpa ni anuɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Young coconuts are bright green and filled mostly with sweet liquid. As the fruit matures over 11 to 12 months, the outer skin turns brown, the husk dries out, and the inner water thickens into a dense white meat, which provides the maximum oil yield.
ga: Kokoo bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni nu ni mli ŋɔɔ babaoo eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ nɔ ni fe nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 12 lɛ, ehewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ feɔ blɔfo, ehewolo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, ni emli nu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛŋ. ni haa mu ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my coconut trees take several years to produce fruit while crops like maize produce in months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli.

english: Coconut palms are long-term tree crops that must build a massive root system and a sturdy trunk first. It takes 4 to 6 years for the palm to store enough structural energy before it can begin producing heavy clusters of fruit continuously every month.
ga: Kokoo tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esa akɛ amɛná shishifãi wuji kɛ tso ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Akɛ afii 4 kɛyashi 6 tsuɔ nii dani tsei ni ji palms lɛ toɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani amɛjeɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ shishi daa nyɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why do so many small flowers fall off my coconut tree before they ever turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mɛi babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔɔ aduawai?

english: Coconut trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. If the tree experiences hot weather or lack of water, it intentionally drops excess young flowers to save its strength and focus energy on maturing the remaining healthy fruits.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmei tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ na kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu bɛ lɛ Ebaatsɔ yiŋtoo nɔ ekɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lolo lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young coconut trees turning yellow and dropping their fruit early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai lɛ miiho oya lɛ?

english: Early yellowing and premature fruit drop are usually symptoms of root damage, nutrient shortages, or diseases like Lethal Yellowing. When the tree is sick or underfed, it cuts off nourishment to the fruit to keep the main palm alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii lɛ ni shwieɔ mra kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efite, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli, loo helai tamɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbeɔ mɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ loo enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa nɔ lɛ Efoɔ aduawai lɛ niyenii lɛ mli koni ekɛbu tso titri lɛ he.

english: What is causing large holes and chewed fiber near the top leaves of my coconut palms?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli ni bɛŋkɛ mi ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Rhinoceros beetle, which drills into the soft heart of the palm crown to feed on sap. If the beetle destroys the central growing tip at the top, the palm stops producing new leaves and will eventually die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tso lɛ yitso tsui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli koni eye nu lɛ Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ kpata ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ahiɛ Tso lɛ baakpa baai heei feemɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo.

english: Why do coconut palms grow well in sandy coastal soils where crops like cocoa struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut palms have tough, fibrous root systems that tolerate high salt levels and poor nutrients. Sandy soil allows their roots to spread wide and deep to drink underground freshwater without getting clogged in heavy waterlogged clay.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ fiber ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni enu shikpɔŋ shishi nu kpakpa ni ekɛ ehe wooo shikpɔŋ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava between my coconut trees, or will they steal nutrients from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ? Aloo amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: You can safely grow low-growing crops between mature coconut trees because the palms have deep roots while cassava feeds near the surface. As long as you space the coconut trees far enough apart to let sunlight through, both crops will thrive together.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu gbɛ ni baa shi yɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ ateŋ shweshweeshwe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmei yeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni obaaha ŋmeii tsei lɛ ahi he ko ni kɛ hulu lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ, Tsei enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekome.

english: Why do the shells of my coconuts split open on the tree during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shwieɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Coconut shells split when heavy rain comes right after a long dry season. The tree suddenly absorbs large amounts of water, causing the soft inner fruit to expand faster than the hard outer shell can stretch.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tsei lɛ gbalaa nu babaoo trukaa. Enɛ haa mligbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a natural umbrella that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have small holes in them with little worms hiding in the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They feed on young leaves and burrow into the growing point of the plant, which can stop growth completely if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dalɛ akpa kwraa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling upwards and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids. As they feed on the sap, they spread viruses that deform the leaves and reduce flower production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛnuɔ mliki Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Soil-borne bacteria or fungi attack the roots and block the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from traveling up into the stem even if the ground is moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Muawai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa nu akabote tso lɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the roots fight each other for soil nutrients and moisture, while the leaves block each other from getting sunlight. This leads to tall, thin, weak stalks with tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my main crops immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long hot, dry spell before the real rainy season begins. Planting right after the first rain can cause seeds to sprout, only for the young seedlings to dry up and die in the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Tsei bibii pɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when the soil is damp rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe ni egbi lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve into a form that plant roots can absorb. Placing chemical fertilizer on dry soil keeps it trapped at the surface, which can scorch the plant roots when heat rises.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nɔ ko ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã be mli ni latsaa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable stems with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic material (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from getting light to grow.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aná la koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly and look pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mitsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are more aggressive than farm crops. They consume the soil's fertilizers and water and crowd out sunlight, leaving your crops starved of essential nutrition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛhaa hulu la shɛɛɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ onibii amli.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open from the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Trunk lɛ mli bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, which reduces your yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while they are still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cold, and shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and prevent the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo be. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap, which can also pass harmful viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ashwã tsei amli

english: Why did my plantain trees fall over so easily during the recent small rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can easily be weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes or root borers, leaving the heavy tree without a strong grip in the wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei ni tsii nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have very large bushy leaves but tiny tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: If cassava receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my young yam mounds as soon as the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Pile sweet potatoes mra be mli ni wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɔɔ pɛ?

english: Young yam plants need all the sunlight, water, and fertilizer they can get to form tubers; early weeds steal these resources before the yam vine is strong enough to shade them out.
ga: Hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná lɛ he miihia sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛfee bulbs. Jwɛi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ baaju nibii nɛɛ dani sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my pineapples so they don't taste sour?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmei?

english: Pineapples do not get any sweeter after you cut them from the plant, so you must wait until the bottom shell changes color from dark green to golden-yellow before harvesting.
ga: Pineapples lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ beni ofo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shishigbɛ fã lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛya shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli dani okpa.

english: Why are my okra pods becoming very hard and difficult to cut with a knife?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa waa ni ewa akɛ akɛ tsɔne baafo lɛ?

english: Okra pods turn woody and hard when they stay on the plant past their peak maturity. They should be picked every two to three days while they are still small, soft, and snap easily.
ga: Roselle pods lɛ baatsɔ tso ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛdara kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ajie amɛ daa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii, amɛhe jɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the central shoot of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ayitsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on young crop leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended insecticides or neem-based spray directly into the leaf whorls protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai bibii. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ awo baai lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛbashi shi lɛ?

english: This yellowing in a 'V' pattern indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize requires nitrogen to stay green and build food, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore green growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ‘V’ mfoniri nɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni efee niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted and covered in patches of light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Your cassava plant likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The best cure is prevention by planting certified disease-resistant stem cuttings.
ga: Ekolɛ o-cassava tso lɛ yɛ cassava mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Tsamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni atsĩ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture energy to grow big tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases quickly spread.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb agboi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and soft while hanging on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ amɛyɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excessive shade. Pruning extra shade tree branches, removing infected pods early, and spraying approved fungicides helps stop the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kroko baa. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my plantain stems snapping and falling over right when they start bearing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi beni amɛbɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Underground pests like root nematodes or stem weevils often weaken the base and roots of the plant. Using clean planting suckers and supporting heavy fruiting plants with wooden props prevents them from toppling.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ root nematodes loo stem weevils Bei pii lɛ, ehaa tsei ashishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sucker ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the branches instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates sharply. Ensuring steady watering and giving crops light shade during peak heat helps flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu daa ni aha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes get dry, dark spots at the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egbi yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium uptake during fruit development. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps roots continuously carry soil calcium up into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni calcium ni bɛ yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward like cups during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoo yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce water evaporation in strong sunlight. If the leaves unroll when temperatures cool down in the evening, your plants are managing heat normally.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​hulutsoo he nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my crop growing huge, leafy stems, but failing to produce solid fruits or roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsei wuji shi ebɛ yibii loo shishifãi ni wa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages lush leaf growth at the expense of fruits and roots. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium gives plants the signal to start flowering and swelling roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa baai lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni efiteɔ aduawai kɛ shishifãi. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso lɛ naa okadi akɛ ebaaje fɔfɔii ashishi ni eshishifãi lɛ afuu.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn yellow when there are no big trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei ni eda ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sun. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them, the leaves burn and the soil dries out quickly, stopping the cocoa from growing properly.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni buɔ he lɛ bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baashã ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, kookoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and watery when I plant them in soil that holds a lot of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil to swell and store starch. Excess water in the soil chokes the roots, causes them to rot, and prevents the plant from growing large, firm tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛfuu ni amɛhiɛ starch mli. Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize crop turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is limited, the plant naturally drains nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to capture maximum energy for leaf growth, which in turn feeds the tuber growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground also protects them from leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni hulu la anyɛ aŋɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. ni baaha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná niyenii Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baabii ahe helai anaa.

english: Why does my main plantain tree give me small bunches if I allow all the young shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ haa mi ŋmei bibioo ko kɛji miha ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ? Nakai plantain tso lɛ

english: Young shoots, called suckers, compete with the mother plantain tree for nutrients, water, and space. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to feed on the soil, leading to bigger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu kɛ he ko he. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa plantain tsei ni dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent soil moisture and proper organic matter help the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nibii ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit. Irregular watering often prevents the plant roots from taking up calcium efficiently, causing the bottom of the tomato to decay.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ haaa amɛná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into their roots. When the plant leaves and roots decay after harvest, they release natural nitrogen into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why should I plant my oil palm seedlings far apart instead of crowding them together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu oil palm dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require maximum sunlight and root space to build thick trunks and yield heavy fresh fruit bunches. Crowding palms makes them grow tall and thin as they fight for light, which reduces total fruit yield.
ga: Mu tsei ahe miihia hulu la kɛ shishifãi babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee tsei ni mli tse ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii ni yɔɔ ehee. Tɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ shwiili ni amɛfeɔ shwiili be mli ni amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la lɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) traps moisture during hot weather, keeps root zones cool, reduces weed growth, and slowly decomposes to feed organic matter back into the ground.
ga: Mulching (mulching) mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: This happens when the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green leaves. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔlii Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛ baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plant curl up and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves fold or droop during hot weather as a self-defense mechanism to save water. Shrinking the surface area exposed to direct sunlight reduces evaporation so the plant can survive dry heat.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋmɛ hulutsoo ni haa egbiɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or extreme nutrient imbalances. The plant drops its flowers to save energy until growing conditions become stable.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa kwraa Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaves with dark spots and rot when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes too close stops air from flowing between the leaves, trapping humidity and moisture. Damp leaves in warm conditions easily trap fungal spores, causing diseases and leaf rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tomato yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Locks yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Baai ni mli efɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mɔɔ fungal spores oya. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela kɛ baai ni fiteɔ aba.

english: Why is it bad if I bury my maize seeds very deep in the soil when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui futuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deeply exhaust all their stored energy trying to push through the soil before reaching sunlight. This causes seeds to either die underground or produce very weak seedlings.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed nitrogen into the soil, making your maize grow stronger without as much artificial fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha o-abele lɛ ada waa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsuuu nii.

english: Why should I avoid growing cassava on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko he tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crops grow small and produce low yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and plant nutrients directly from the soil surrounding your crops. Without enough light, water, and nutrients, your crops cannot produce healthy grains or fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ awo ŋmaa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I trim or remove the small extra branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji bibii loo majie amɛ? Jiemɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ tomato tsei lɛ amli.

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches, known as suckers, directs the plant's water and nutrients toward growing big, healthy fruits instead of burning energy on excessive leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni he ehiaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ni aaafolɔ Enɛ baaha tso lɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ asusu aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã hewalɛ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Is it better for me to water my garden crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the plant roots drink water before the day gets hot. Watering late in the evening leaves the foliage wet overnight, which promotes fungal infections and stem rot.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tso lɛ mli fitemɔ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sun. Direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and evaporates soil moisture faster than their short root systems can absorb it, which is why shade trees or plantains are needed to protect them early on.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi kukuji lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni aha amɛ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui koni abu amɛhe mra lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of oil palm fruits is fully ripe and ready to cut?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni oil palm yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afolɔ?

english: An oil palm fruit bunch is mature and ready for harvest when at least two to five loose, bright orange-red fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground at the base of the palm.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kɛ hoo lɛ, tso yibii 2-5 ni kpɛɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs high amounts of nitrogen to stay green, so when nutrients run low, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni eye ebua shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on a plot where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and fixes it into the soil. Planting groundnuts after maize restores soil nutrients that the maize crop consumed.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei lɛ yeɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds end up with small holes and dust after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Those holes are caused by cowpea weevils, tiny insects whose eggs or larvae hide inside the seeds during harvest and eat their way out as they grow during storage.
ga: Cowpea ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtee dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli ni eyeɔ kpojeei lɛ beni amɛdaraa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even though the leaves above ground look bushy and tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmeii ni amɛkwɔ moŋ?

english: When cassava receives too much foliage-promoting nutrients or is planted too close to other stems, it directs all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches instead of expanding its underground storage roots.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ ná niyenii ni haa baai lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo tsɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe tsɔ lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a haa sisifãhi nɛ a toɔ ngɛ zugba sisi ɔ waa.

english: Why is it necessary to prune extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers attached to one plantain mother plant creates competition for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers allows the main plant to produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso nyɛ kome nɔ Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high daytime heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms. When pollen becomes infertile, pollination fails and the plant naturally sheds the flower instead of developing fruit.
ga: Gbi mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Beni pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ lɛ Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ yibiiwoo najiaŋ.

english: Why do large ragged holes appear in the leaves of my cabbage plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii wuji jeɔ kpo yɛ kaabii tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Humid and rainy conditions encourage pest insects, like caterpillars and moth larvae, to hatch on the undersides of cabbage leaves and feed heavily on the leafy tissue.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii baa. Wɔɔji fɔɔ yɛ kaabɛji baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji babaoo.

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from young foliage, or by viruses transmitted by these pests that distort normal plant tissue growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ bɔ ni tsei amli fãji lɛ daa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ

english: How do I know if a new seed variety has been officially tested and approved by the government before I buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ aka dumɔwui heei lɛ akwɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni nɔyeli lɛ eha amɛhe odaseyeli dani mihe?

english: Approved seeds come in sealed bags with official certification tags from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, showing they have passed purity, germination, and crop safety inspections.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni nɔ ni maŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eji nɔ ni jɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tse, bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe ha lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the government plant small demonstration plots of new crops in our villages before releasing the seeds to everyone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ miidu ŋmɔshi nibii heei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔji yɛ wɔ akrowai lɛ amli dani ejie dumɔwui lɛ eha mɔ fɛɛ mɔ lɛ?

english: Demonstration plots allow agricultural officers to see how the crop behaves in your local soil and climate, while giving local farmers a chance to evaluate its performance before full public release.
ga: Demo shikpɔji lɛ haa okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ naa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ hegbɛ koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ mli dani ajie lɛ kpo atsɔɔ maŋbii lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do these new government-approved seeds grow faster than the traditional seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui heei ni nɔyeli lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ nɛɛ daa oya fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Newly approved varieties are specifically bred to absorb soil nutrients more efficiently and mature faster, helping them outpace traditional seeds.
ga: Afɔ ŋmeii heei ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwere oya. Enɛ haa nɛkɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi nɛɛ yeɔ blema dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Can I save and plant seeds from my harvest of improved hybrid crop varieties for the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid nikpamɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ ato ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended because seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation, leading to lower yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Why does an improved crop variety produce a bigger yield than my traditional crop on the exact same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni atsake lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mishishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties direct more of their energy into developing large fruits or grains rather than growing excess leaves and stems.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji ni afeɔ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, duɔ baai kɛ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a he hiɛ ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: How do drought-tolerant crops manage to survive long dry spells in Ghana without dying?
ga: Te tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo?

english: Drought-tolerant crops grow deeper roots to reach underground moisture and have specialized leaves that slow down water loss during hot sun.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ, ni amɛyɛ baai krɛdɛɛi ni haa nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties suffer less damage from insect pests compared to my local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei komɛi fiteee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ akɛto mimaŋ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Bred crop varieties often have natural physical or chemical defenses that discourage insects from feeding on them or allow the plant to recover quickly after an attack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ loo tsofafeemɔ mli hebuu. Enɛ haaa kooloi aye amɛ. aloo ha tso lɛ aya hiɛ oya yɛ tutuamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds closer together than what the extension officer advises?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, making them grow tall, thin, and weak with smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does a seed variety that performs very well in another region of Ghana fail to yield well on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ Ghana kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops react differently to local rainfall patterns, temperatures, and soil types, which is why a variety must suit your specific agro-ecological zone to thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi ahe. Enɛ hewɔ ni esa akɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ afee nɔ ni sa kɛha o-agro-ecological zone lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up and turn yellow when it stops raining for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to save water during dry spells by reducing the surface area exposed to the sun. When the dry weather lasts too long, the plant cannot pull nutrients from the dry soil, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and dry out.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains come irregularly at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets a deep soaking rain rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting too early during unpredictable weather often causes seeds to germinate and then scorch when a sudden dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ kpakpa anɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba trukaa.

english: How does putting dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops help them during hot dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or straw, called mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight and stops the moisture in the ground from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying when weather conditions are too stressful.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he kɛ́ shihilɛi bafee nɔ ni haoɔ mɔ tsɔ.

english: Why did my cassava roots stay small this season even though the stems and leaves grew very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When cassava gets plenty of early rain, it puts all its energy into growing big leaves and tall stems. If the rains cut short before the plant starts storing food underground, the tubers stay small despite the tall top growth.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ná nugbɔ babaoo mra Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii kakadaji. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ dani tsei lɛ bɔi niyenii toomɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, Yitso lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open right on the vine just before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when there is a sudden heavy rain after a period of dry weather. The plant drinks up a lot of water quickly, causing the inside of the tomato to swell faster than its skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ be ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei nuɔ nu babaoo oya. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ mli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow well in one part of my field but stay small and weak in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil depth, water retention, and nutrient levels vary across the same farm field. Stunted areas often have hard subsoil that stops roots from growing deep, or sandy soil that loses water and fertilizer too fast.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli nu ni akɛhiɛɔ Ni niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya tsɔ

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas together with maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for the maize. They also spread across the ground to shade the soil, keeping it moist and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa Amɛ hu amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds bought from agro-dealers survive dry weather better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to grow strong root systems that reach deep into the soil for water. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time, making them weaker against harsh weather.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná nu. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ amɛyaje kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli.

english: Why do my groundnuts turn black and moldy under the soil if the rains continue during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When groundnuts stay in wet soil for too long after maturity, moisture gets trapped inside the pods. This warm, wet environment encourages soil fungi to grow, causing the nuts to rot before they can be harvested and dried.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii hi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshwere lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Moisture baatsi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa amɛ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade when they are young to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh heat. Leaving some shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo be mli ni amɛji bibii lɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baa lɛ ashã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows them to grow larger and produce bigger ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground so leaves get maximum sunlight and stay away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ, ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for the crop. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away into gutters or deep into the soil where crop roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui amli loo sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi otsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How does planting groundnuts make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny natural bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. When you harvest them, they leave behind natural food that helps your next crop grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the central growing leaves of maize. Spraying approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot in the soil when water sits on the land for too long or due to fungal infections. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil diseases that target tomatoes to build up. Rotating with maize or beans breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ. ni ekɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, efoɔ hela lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is enough land for everything to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ he ko yɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. If weeds grow close to your crops, your crops get weaker, grow slower, and produce fewer fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ebaada blɛoo ni ebaawo yibii fioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from too much water in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving land drainage helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo shishifãi lɛ amli nu efo yɛ nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the exact same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally and breaks crop disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ. ni ekpa tso helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and easily damaged by harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide broad leaf shade, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato tsei amli lɛ he hiaa koni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to catch sunlight. Staking holds the leaves off the wet ground, maximizing sunlight exposure for energy while preventing fungal leaves and diseases from soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la. Staking jieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni baa lɛ baa lɛ naa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why does a cassava stem cutting grow into a full plant without using real seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ dumɔwui tsuuu nii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems store water and plant food inside their nodes. When planted in moist soil, these nodes automatically sprout root systems and leaves to form a complete new plant.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ toɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ nodes lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwereɔ shishifãi kɛ baai gbɛjianɔtoi ni amɛfeɔ tso hee kwraa.

english: Why should I pinch off extra shoots and lower leaves from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi kɛ baai ni ajie kɛjɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing non-essential shoots prevents the plant from wasting energy on foliage. This directs water and nutrients straight into producing larger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ kudɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ koni ená ŋmɔtɔ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their pollen, preventing successful fertilization. Without fertilization, the blossoms wither and drop off before fruit can start growing.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Kɛji akɛ fɔmɔ nii bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi dani aduawai lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry straw keep the ground wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: A layer of dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket, blocking direct sunlight from baking the topsoil and stopping water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashã hewolo lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Even with good rain, crops suffer because weeds aggressively steal the food needed for growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu lɛ waa.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which seek out the tender, growing leaves inside the central whorl of maize plants. Early treatment stops them before they destroy the main growing tip of the corn.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni taoɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Mra be mli tsamɔ Ekpaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa titrii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the new growth at the top, leaving the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ nɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and feeling tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often a defense reaction to extreme heat or attack by tiny pests like whiteflies that transmit viruses. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss or as a symptom of a pest infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo tutuamɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ helai amli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ he. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi loo akɛ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without forming pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce during the dry season, a cocoa tree goes into survival mode. It drops its flowers to save water and energy for its main stem and roots until the rains return.
ga: Beni nu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cacao tso lɛ baaya shihilɛ mli. Abaashwie fɔfɔi lɛ koni akɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains flood the soil and water cannot drain away, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen, allowing fungus to enter and cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ, ni nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ aho kɛya. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ abote mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why is it bad if I pour fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that attract water. Placing it directly against the plant stem sucks moisture out of the plant tissue, causing leaf burn or killing the plant completely.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa loo egboɔ kwraa.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps the sun from drying out the soil too fast and protects beneficial organisms in the ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. ni ebuɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans on the land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the ground weak, but beans have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shi ŋmeii yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ babaoo aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ

english: Yams grow crooked or short when the soil underneath them is too hard or full of rocks. Making tall, loose soil mounds allows the root to expand easily downwards without pushing against hard dirt.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kukuji kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa shi ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to come up after I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A seed contains only a tiny amount of stored food to start growing. If you bury it too deep, it spends all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ niyenii fioo ko pɛ ni ato koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji ofu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ashɛ shi waa. ni egbo dani eshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions with very little water or nutrients. They aggressively steal sunlight, fertilizer, and water away from your farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni nu loo niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ hulu la, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and look weak during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during hot afternoons as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss from evaporation. If they recover by early morning, the plant is managing the heat, but if they remain curled, the soil around the root zone requires deeper watering.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛba nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ohe wa bo leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ latsaa lɛ miikpe. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ tee nɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni afɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifã lɛ he lɛ nɔ nu babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, commonly caused by extreme soil dryness, irregular watering, or excessive heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root area helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Why does my maize crop stay short and turn pale green even when rain falls regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooloi lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While rain supplies water, plants also need nutrients from the soil to stay healthy and green. Pale yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizer or rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe moŋ, shi Tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ nibii ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ adumɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves above ground but very thin roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil is too hard or heavy in leaf-growing nutrients, the cassava plant puts its energy into leaf production instead of tubers. Loosening the soil before planting allows the roots room to swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa baai lɛ dalɛ tsii tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifã tsu lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn dry and brown at the edges when the dry Harmattan season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dry winds strip moisture from leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Providing shade trees around cocoa trees creates a microclimate that shields the leaves from harsh dry winds.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ hulutsoo haa he fɛɛ he Cocoa tso lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa he.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are wilting from lack of water or from a plant disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni aduawai ko miigbo loo eji tso hela?

english: Water-stressed plants wilting from heat will usually recover overnight after receiving water, affecting broad areas evenly. Disease wilting often starts on individual plants, leaves patches or spots, and does not improve after soil watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo ni hulutsoo be lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shoo nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ amɛná nu sɛɛ. ni saa he ko ni da he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei aŋkroaŋkroi anɔ yɛ baai loo hei srɔtoi amli ni ehiɛɛɛ shi kɛji akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu sɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to apply water to my crops early in the morning rather than under the mid-day sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Morning watering lets soil absorb moisture down to the roots before the heat evaporates it. Mid-day watering loses much of the water to heat evaporation and can cause temperature shock to hot plant roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nu babaoo kɛyaa dɔlɛ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulutsoo be aba tso shishifãi ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my watermelon fruits crack open in the field before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons crack when they absorb a sudden large amount of water after a prolonged dry period. The inside swells faster than the skin can stretch, which can be prevented by providing steady, uniform watering.
ga: Watermelon tswaa kɛji eŋɔ nu babaoo trukaa beni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs turn bright yellow and taste bitter while still small on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Garden eggs over-ripen quickly and turn yellow/bitter under extreme heat and drought stress as they rush to produce seeds. Harvesting them early while green and glossy prevents bitterness.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ/ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ he be mli ni amɛyaa oya koni amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ. mra be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔlɔ naa.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to survive and grow fast on my land even when my crops struggle to survive drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi hiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛje hɔmɔ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Wild weeds have naturally deep root systems adapted over generations to find water in tough conditions, whereas cultivated crop plants need managed weed clearance and steady soil moisture to establish their softer roots.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni atsake amɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli koni amɛna nu yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni efee shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and provide shade and moisture, acting like natural umbrellas during the cocoa tree's early years.
