ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key plant food. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore leaf greenness and supports fast growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri lɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Cassava root rot is usually caused by excess water logging the soil or fungal infections in damp earth. Good soil drainage prevents water from sitting around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava shishifãi fiteɔ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or water stress can prevent tomato flowers from pollinating. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting during cooler weather helps fruit set.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu mli haomɔ baanyɛ atsĩ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ dumɔ yɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai aba.

english: Why should I plant my maize seeds in rows with proper spacing instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Proper row spacing stops plants from competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spaced plants grow stronger stems and produce larger, fuller ears of corn.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ atoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei nyɛŋ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni yɔɔ teŋ lɛ daa tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji, ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores soil nutrients without relying entirely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ he afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Seeds need moist soil to germinate, but planting after just one light shower can kill seeds if dry weather returns. Wait until rains are consistent and soil stays damp a few inches deep.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi dumɔwui ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly when I put them in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ?

english: Rotting happens when yams get bruised during harvest or are stored in warm, poorly ventilated areas. Storing undamaged tubers off the ground in cool, shaded, well-aired yam barns slows decay.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ atswa sweet potato yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmeii atoohe ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ afite fiofio.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help the plants grow faster?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops by drinking water and stealing fertilizer from the soil. Removing weeds leaves all soil nutrients and sunlight available to your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otso titri lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ajie ehe.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds every season instead of re-using seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase daa be mli yɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Seeds saved from harvested hybrid maize lose their high yield traits and disease resistance in the next generation, producing smaller ears and uneven growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ baafite yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa toi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize grow thin and yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief neighbors in your field—they steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your maize. When weeds crowd your crops, the maize roots cannot feed properly, causing the plant to turn yellow and stay weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni jɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle onibii ahe lɛ Abele shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: How do weeds in my farm bring insect pests and diseases to my vegetable crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa mi-vegetables ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds provide safe hiding places and food for harmful insects and plant diseases. Once pests build up on the weeds around your field, they easily jump onto your vegetables and destroy them.
ga: Jwɛi haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai náa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ba jwɛi ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ anɔ lɛ, amɛhoɔ amɛshwieɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still very young instead of waiting until harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Young crops are fragile and need maximum nutrients to establish strong roots. If weeds grow alongside young crops, they quickly overwhelm them, but clearing weeds early gives your crops the best chance to grow big and healthy.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni ehe miihia ni amɛná niyenii babaoo koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ fata he lɛ Jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Shi jwɛi ni ooojie mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds from an agrodealer instead of planting seeds I collect from the bush or my old harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i duɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ i buaa kɛ jeɔ tso tsɔwi aloo ngmlaa momohi a mi ɔ.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to fight off local diseases and grow uniformly. Seeds saved from old farms or wild bush plants often carry hidden diseases and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai awuu ni amɛdara daa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momoi loo koo mli tsei amli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny without fruiting when trees from the nearby bush shade them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ haa hulutsoo lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food. When tall bush trees block the sun, your crops stretch upward searching for light instead of using their energy to produce flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Beni tsei kakadaji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛna la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: If I clear a thick bush to start a new farm, why do my crops struggle to grow well in the first season?
ga: Kɛji mijie brɔshi ni mli tse lɛ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly cleared bush land often has hard soil, hidden root competition, and unbalanced nutrients. Preparing the soil properly and letting it rest helps release the natural goodness in the ground for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni ajie brɔshi ehee lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa. Shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni ejaaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosaa jogbaŋŋ ni oha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ kpo.

english: Why does breaking up hard farm soil with machines help my crop roots grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Hard soil suffocates plant roots and blocks them from moving. Breaking up the soil opens up spaces for air and rain to enter, allowing crop roots to spread easily and drink water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛfaa naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mligbalamɔ haa gbɛ ko baa koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ abote mli. Helps plant roots spread easily and drink water.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need physical space under the soil to expand. When you plant them too close, the roots crush against each other and fight for the same soil food, resulting in thin, small tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ mlɛo

english: Why do some of my pepper seedlings wilt and die right after I move them from the nursery into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes root shock because the sudden hot sun and dry field soil take away moisture faster than the young roots can absorb it. Protecting them with light shade helps them recover.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ trukaa kɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo bu amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhe waa.

english: How does using a water motor pump to irrigate my field keep crops growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu pɔmp ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Crops need a constant flow of water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. Using a motor pump supplies steady water so the plants continue making food and growing fruits even when it does not rain.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni hoɔ daa koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ. Motor pɔmp ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nu aba daa. Tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ afee niyenii ni amɛwo yibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do my harvested mangoes go soft and rot within just a few days of picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mangoes continue to breathe and ripen rapidly after harvest, especially in warm temperatures. Storing them in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated structure slows down their respiration so they stay fresh much longer before going to market.
ga: Mango yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. titri lɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ Akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ebaaha mumɔ aya hiɛ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: What causes mold to grow on my cocoa beans while I am drying them?
ga: Mɛni miiha ŋmeii miije kpo yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni migbiɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when beans stay damp for too long or get wet from rain during drying. Spreading beans thinly on raised platforms and turning them frequently allows air to circulate, drying them faster and preventing mold.
ga: Mold daa kɛji kɔfi yibii lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa fioo yɛ kpoku ko ni awo nɔ ni atsakeɔ shii abɔ lɛ nɔ Ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii baa.

english: How does keeping my harvested crops in a proper storage structure protect them better than keeping them at home?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ he ko ni sa lɛ baabu he jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ?

english: Proper storage structures regulate air flow and temperature while keeping out rain, rodents, and insects. This prevents the heat and moisture build-up that causes stored produce to rot or get eaten by pests.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ dɔlɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i akabua amɛhe naa ni haa nibii ni ato lɛ fiteɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce a huge harvest one year, but barely any fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa baajɛ mli aba?

english: This behavior is called biennial bearing. After a tree expends immense energy and nutrients to produce a massive crop, it needs the following year to rebuild its nutrient reserves before it can bear heavy fruit again.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ afii enyɔ fɔmɔ. Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Eheɔ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ dani ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ekoŋŋ.

english: This is a natural defense mechanism against drought. Cocoa trees shed leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss through transpiration, conserving precious moisture inside their stem and roots to survive.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa hiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: Why do all the flowers fall off my mango tree without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Mango flowers drop easily due to dry soil stress, strong winds, or fungal diseases like powdery mildew during the bloom period. Ensuring proper moisture and protecting flowers from fungal attack helps them set into fruit.
ga: Mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni abu fɔfɔi ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp shade. Pruning extra branches to let in sunlight and removing infected pods keeps the rest of your tree healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji hydrophilic fungus ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni shade yɔɔ ni edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa pods show ripeness through color change: green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting when fully ripe ensures the beans inside have built up enough sugar for proper fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛshwere ha lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do grafted mango trees bear fruit so much faster than mango trees grown straight from a seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mango tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: A seed grows a juvenile plant that must mature for 5 to 7 years before flowering. A graft uses a branch taken from an already mature, fruit-bearing tree, allowing it to skip the youth stage and produce fruit in just 2 to 3 years.
ga: Dumɔwui baabi ni tso bibioo lɛ ada afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani ewo fɔfɔi. Akɛ tsei ni eda ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ grafting. Ha efo oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ be lɛ mli ni ewo yibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ mli.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my field help my crops grow better than clearing by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baajieɔ amɛ?

english: Tractor plowing breaks up deep, hard soil layers, making it much easier for plant roots to grow deep, breathe air, and reach underground moisture and nutrients that shallow hand-clearing cannot reach.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, amɛmuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baaha amɛná lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tip along the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and energy to grow, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the season will turn the crop green and improve your yield.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni ebaaha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when I plant them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi dumɔwui lɛ abɔ he kɛjɛ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Spacing your maize about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plant holes ensures each stalk gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to produce large, full cobs without overcrowding.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 75, ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 40, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmãa wuji lɛ ayi obɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ tsɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or gets excessive shade, cassava plants put all their energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food in their roots. Planting cassava in open sunlight and avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers helps the plant grow big tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ kɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing the leaves on my tomato plants to curl up and stop producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil sprays or proper crop sanitation prevents the spread and keeps your tomatoes fruiting longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ mra loo phytosanitary nifeemɔi ni sa baanyɛ aye abua ni akagbɛ ashwã ni eha tomato awo yibii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from my current hybrid maize harvest to plant during the next rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds harvested from hybrid crops will not perform as well if replanted; they produce uneven plants with weak yields. Buying fresh certified hybrid seeds every planting season guarantees strong, disease-resistant plants with high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ tsei be fɛɛ be ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their flowers instead of turning them into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from harsh direct sunlight, high heat, or lack of water. Planting shade trees like plantains alongside young cocoa keeps the farm cool and moist so the flowers can turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii ni aduɔ kɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my yam plants during the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally sprout fast to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before your crops can build deep roots. Clearing weeds during the first four to six weeks of growth gives your yams the boost they need to climb their stakes and outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛju hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi lɛ je kpo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4-6 ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa o-sweet potato lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɔ ni amɛye jwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers during the hottest part of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers as a natural defence mechanism when extreme heat prevents proper pollination. Covering the soil with organic mulch like dried grass keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the plant hold its blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ jwɛi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my sweet potatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Sweet potatoes are ready when their leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, usually three to four months after planting. Digging up one or two test plants allows you to check if the tubers are fully developed before harvesting the entire field.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 3-4 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, kaa tso kome loo enyɔ ni ooofo lɛ haa okwɛɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ jogbaŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns natural nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to provide cover, keep the soil cool, and retain moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. koni aná abobaahe Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa

english: Why should I cut off excess branches from my cocoa tree when it is already growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso ko nɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Pruning off extra or dead branches lets sunlight and air pass through the tree, which prevents diseases and directs the plant's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa mɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the plants to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin stalks and small harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa bibioo ko.

english: Why do some of the seeds I store at home fail to grow when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ ekwɛ̃ɛɛ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Stored seeds can die if they get exposed to heat, damp air, or insects. Storing seeds in cool, dry, sealed containers keeps them alive and ready to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ agboi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, loo koolooi ahe. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsinsii ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ wala mli ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is too dry or waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen he miihia onibii lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ kɛyashɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or sudden heavy rains, which stops the flower from turning into actual pepper.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa Enɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do pests attack my crops more during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates a warm, moist environment that helps pests hatch faster, while soft young leaf shoots give them plenty of fresh food to eat.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ haa amɛ niyenii hee babaoo ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my yam plants help them grow better?
ga: Hay ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te sweet potato tsei yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil that traps moisture, keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ mulch blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if they are just growing in the soil next to them?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your crops weak and reducing your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ baa shi.

english: If I see diseased or yellowing stems on my crops, should I cut them off or wait for them to heal on their own?
ga: Kɛji mina ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ majie loo mamɛ ni lɛ diɛŋtsɛ efo?

english: Diseased plant parts rarely heal on their own and will continue to produce germs or attract pests. Cutting away infected branches or stems removes the source of sickness before it can multiply and destroy the entire crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ fãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe baatsa ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛfee helai loo amɛbaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ejieɔ hela lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ dani egbɛɔ eshwaa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut down healthy-looking trees surrounding a diseased crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛgbɛ nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ

english: Certain crop diseases, like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, spread through underground roots or tiny insects long before visible symptoms appear. Removing neighboring 'contact' trees stops the hidden sickness from spreading further into your farm.
ga: Tsei ahe helai komɛi, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ, jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi loo kooloi bibii amli. Be kakadaŋŋ dani okadii lɛ baaje kpo lɛ, ajieɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni ‘ajie amɛhe kpo’ lɛ. Ebaatsi helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo.

english: What is the best immediate action to take when I notice a plant disease starting in just one small corner of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina tso hela ko ni je shishi yɛ koŋ bibioo ko nɔ? Ekome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: The best step is fast containment by cutting out the infected plants along with a safety boundary of contact plants around them to isolate the disease before it covers your whole land.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akudɔ oya kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ amɛ kɛ husu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Koni ojie hela lɛ kɛjɛ ohe dani eha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: If I cut off a diseased plant stem, can I leave the cut branch lying on the ground in my farm?
ga: Kɛji mifo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ shishi Ani manyɛ mashi tsei niji ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, because pests and disease germs can live on fallen branches and spread back to healthy crops through wind or rain spray. Cut diseased parts should be carried away, dried, and burned or safely buried.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ ahi tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ anɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ajie hei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, agbi, ashã loo afu amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How far around an infected plant do I need to clear crops to keep the rest of my farm safe?
ga: Te esa akɛ majie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni koni miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe?

english: Clearing a distance of a few meters (or roughly 10 to 25 surrounding contact plants) creates an effective buffer zone that catches hidden infections that haven't shown signs on leaves yet.
ga: Mitai fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ (loo aaafee tsei 10 kɛyashi 25 ni ebɔle he lɛ) feɔ buffer zone ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni akɛmɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni ejieee okadii komɛi akpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How does leaving empty space between sections of my crops help protect them from sickness?
ga: Gbɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi ateŋ Te ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Empty spaces or physical barriers break the chain of infection because crawling insects and airborne disease spores cannot easily bridge the gap to reach your healthy crops.
ga: He ni yɔɔ yaka loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii fiteɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afo gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ mli mlɛo koni amɛshɛ onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do diseases move from one sick crop to a healthy crop on a farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai jɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Diseases usually travel through sap-sucking insects like mealybugs, contaminated water droplets splashing during rain, infected soil, or shared farming tools moving across the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai tsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, kɛ nu mli nu ni mli ewo muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ amli. shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli loo okwaayeli nibii ni ajaa ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Do I need to clean my cutlass after pruning a diseased plant before moving to healthy crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsumɔ mi-daggers lɛ ahe beni mifo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ dani mikɛ amɛ awo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Yes, disease-causing bacteria and viruses stick to tool blades through plant sap. If you do not clean your cutlass with disinfectant or fire after cutting a sick plant, you will inject the disease directly into healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dɛŋdadei ahe kɛtsɔɔ tso mli nu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ helai loo la etsuuu o-knife lɛ he beni ofo tso ni hela mɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Obaafee mɔ ni kɛ hela baawo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I cut down a sick crop, can I plant a new seed in that exact same spot right away?
ga: Kɛji mifo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to wait because disease pathogens and pests often remain active in the leftover roots and soil. Allowing the area to rest and treating the soil prevents the new seedling from catching the same illness.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshwɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui heei anaa koni amɛkaná hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can plant diseases spread into my farm from my neighbor's land?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, plant sickness does not respect boundaries. Pests carry diseases across farm borders, and water runoff during heavy rain can carry fungal spores from a neighbor's infected land directly into your field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai ebuuu husui. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ ahe ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ kɛya oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves and make food. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or adding well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ baai ni wa ni amɛnyɛ amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK tsu nii loo akɛ kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts adds natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ helai lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak with tiny harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for its roots to spread and leaves to capture sunlight, leading to stronger plants and larger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni baai lɛ hu anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and develop large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the young cocoa from harsh heat and keeping the surrounding soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛnáa baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa

english: What causes small ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf funnel. Inspecting your field early and spraying neem leaf extracts or recommended bio-pesticides into the plant funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips carrying a plant virus, or extreme heat stress. Spraying a light soapy neem water solution keeps insect numbers low and protects healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Neem nu kɛ samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Enɛ baaha kooloi ayibɔ aba shi ni ebu baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb moisture before the day's heat begins. Afternoon watering wastes water through fast evaporation, while hot soil combined with cold water can shock the plant's roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Nu ni akɛhaa shwane mli lɛ baafite nu lɛ yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ fata he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ akpokpo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops dry out and wilt much faster during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thirsty neighbors, stealing groundwater and soil nutrients directly from your crop's root zone. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all available soil water exclusively for your crops to survive dry periods.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ. Ejuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or if the soil lacks phosphorus. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the plant base lowers soil heat and preserves flowers.
ga: Tomato baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ muji awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: When too many seeds grow in the same spot, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Removing extra weak plants leaves enough room and nutrients for the remaining strong ones to grow bigger, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ ni miida yɛ he kome lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ titri lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why should I cut down the extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food directly from the main tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plantain tree to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off the green shoots growing straight up from my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mikoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These shoots, known as chupons or water shoots, drink up large amounts of water and energy from the tree without producing any cocoa pods, taking away the strength the tree needs to form healthy pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons, loo nu ŋmeii lɛ, nuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni amɛjieee kookoo ŋmeii ko kwraa, ni no haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting plantains nearby creates living shade umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and moist until they grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ la fɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes instead of growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to sunlight and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha hulu la lɛ akpɛ ni otsi helai anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Extremely hot weather and lack of water cause tomato plants to get stressed. To survive the heat, the plant drops its flowers to conserve moisture instead of using energy to grow new fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hulutsoo be lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai heei.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of the leaves. As they suck the plant juice, they cause the leaf to wrinkle and deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni ekɛ tso nu lɛ shwieɔ Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: How do weeds growing close to my crop roots affect the health of my plants?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ saa mitso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and suck up the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving your plants and slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛmuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: When cassava leaves turn yellow from the bottom up, the soil is usually low in essential nutrients like nitrogen or lacking water. The plant sheds its oldest leaves to send its remaining energy down into the roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu efo mli. Tsei ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ aya amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can drink it in. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots or leave the fertilizer useless until heavy rain washes it away.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akatsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes start rotting so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested tomatoes continue to breathe and produce heat after picking. If they are left under the hot sun or packed tightly in closed containers, moisture and heat build up quickly, causing bacteria and fungi to multiply and rot the fruit.
ga: Tomato ni akpa lɛ baaya nɔ amu ni ekɛ dɔlɛ aba beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ Fɛ̃i kɛ dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, muawai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why does my stored maize get hot and full of small insects even in a shaded storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli edɔɔ ni kooloi bibii eyi mli obɔ yɛ nitoohe ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo po mli lɛ?

english: Maize grains contain hidden moisture if they are not dried properly before storage. Damp grain breathes and generates heat inside bags, creating a warm, damp environment that causes grain weevils to multiply rapidly.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa mli kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ muɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots get dark lines inside them just a few days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ mli yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is dug up from the ground, it loses its water supply and undergoes a natural chemical breakdown called spoilage. The root tries to heal itself from being cut, which causes the inner flesh to turn dark and spoil within 48 to 72 hours.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsa ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Elaajeɔ kɛyaa nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni fiteɔ nii ni ale lɛ akɛ putrefaction lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsa amɛhe koni akafo amɛ. Enɛ haa emli lɛ feɔ duŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen all at once when I put a few yellow ones in the same basket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome beni mikɛ ŋmɔŋ fioo komɛi woɔ tsɛnsi kome mli lɛ?

english: Ripening plantains release a natural gas called ethylene. When green plantains are exposed to this gas from nearby ripe fruit, it signals them to start softening and ripening quickly at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. Kɛji akɛ plantains eŋɔlii lɛ kɛ gas nɛɛ ni jɛ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ kpe lɛ, Etsɔɔ plantains lɛ akɛ amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ be kome too mli.

english: Why do my harvested cowpea seeds develop tiny holes after keeping them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni akɛto otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Small insects called cowpea weevils lay tiny, invisible eggs on the pods while the crop is still in the field. After harvest, the eggs hatch into grubs inside the stored seeds and eventually eat their way out, leaving small holes.
ga: Kooloo bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cowpea moth lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa yɛ pods lɛ anɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Eggs fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli. ni naagbee lɛ eye gbɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ aahu kɛyashi bu bibioo ko eshwɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants curling up like pipes during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism maize uses to protect itself from drying out. By rolling its leaves tightly, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct heat, which slows down water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ baa ni egbi lɛ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulutsoo baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive fertilizer. The plant sacrifices its flowers to save energy and water so that the main plant can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves turn yellow and stop growing when there is heavy rain on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets flooded with too much water, air is pushed out of the soil pores. Without oxygen, the roots cannot breathe or absorb plant food from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stop.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ, anyɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ tso mli niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my okra plants develop white powdery spots during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white powder is a fungal infection called powdery mildew. It thrives during dry weather with warm days and humid nights, feeding on the leaves and reducing the plant's ability to make food.
ga: Nakai powda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli. Eyɛ gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu tsoɔ waa. Ye baai lɛ ni oha nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested so they don't rot easily?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa koni amɛkafite oya?

english: Yam plants indicate maturity when their leaves turn yellow and the above-ground vines completely dry up. Harvesting at this stage ensures the tuber has stored all its energy into thick starch, making it durable for long storage.
ga: Sweet potato tsei jieɔ dalɛ he okadi kpo kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi kwraa. Nɛkɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fã nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ. Ehaa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛha nitoo.

english: This usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong leaves. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has left to the top young leaves, causing the bottom older leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai momo lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get too stressed, usually from extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. When the plant senses conditions are harsh, it drops the flowers to conserve energy so the rest of the plant can survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiifee basaa tsɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ. Kɛ tsei kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa kpe lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are suffering from drought?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiye hɔmɔ?

english: Cassava plants show drought stress by drooping their leaves during the hottest part of the day or curling their leaves inward to hold onto moisture. If the dry spell continues for too long, the plant will shed its lower leaves completely to save water.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ jieɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpo kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Aloo tsɔ baai lɛ amli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ tee nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on my crops when the soil is dry or after rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a rain. Crop roots cannot absorb dry fertilizer granules; they need water to dissolve the nutrients so the roots can drink them up into the stem and leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ. Amɛmiitao nu koni amɛjie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ kɛya tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my vegetable plants stay small and stunted even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering keeps crops hydrated, but it does not feed them if the soil lacks plant food. Stunted growth usually means the soil is low on essential nutrients, or the soil is packed too tightly for the roots to breathe and grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa nu. Shi amɛyeŋ niyenii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii bɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my bean plants spread across the ground while my neighbor's bean plants climb up sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-nut tso lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nut tso lɛ kwɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: There are two different growth habits for beans: bush beans and climbing beans. Bush beans grow into short, freestanding bushes, while climbing beans naturally grow long vines that seek out poles or trees to climb toward the sunlight.
ga: Beans yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi enyɔ: tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɔɔ. Cowpeas kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni damɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ amli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa wain tsei kakadaji ni taoɔ tsei loo tsei ni amɛkwɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he lɛ.

english: Early fruit drop in peppers usually happens when tiny insects like fruit flies damage the young pepper, or when the plant lacks enough water and calcium to support the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei yibii ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii fite ŋmei bibii. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce a poorer harvest than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni baa shi fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred to give a high yield for only one generation. If you plant seeds harvested from those crops, the offspring lose that special strength and result in mixed, weaker plants with smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ yinɔ kome pɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Seshi lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ ni nɔ ni baaba ji tso ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni ji tso ni akɛfee ekome ni ŋmei bibioo ko yɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and have broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kooloi bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important to leave enough space between my plantain suckers when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for nutrients and water, and their heavy leaves block sunlight from each other. Proper spacing allows every plant to get enough light and food to grow big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Ni amɛbaai ni tsii lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ kui wuji.

english: What does cocoa rehabilitation mean, and why should I cut down my old or sick cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo sɛɛkuu shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa rehabilitation means replacing old, unproductive, or diseased trees with healthy new seedlings. Cutting down sick trees stops diseases like Swollen Shoot from spreading to healthy parts of your farm and gives new plants space and nutrients to produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kokoo ni aku sɛɛ akɛba ekoŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsei ni egbɔ, ni wooo yibii loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baatsake tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ haa helai tamɔ akɔɔble ni efuuɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. ni ehaa tsei heei hegbɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: What is the benefit of planting plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui heei lɛ ahe lɛ he?

english: Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that shield tender young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and heat. They also provide your family with food and quick income while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Amɛhaa oweku lɛ niyenii hu ni amɛnáa shika oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ adara lɛ.

english: Why is it important to consult community traditional leaders or chiefs before starting a major farm renovation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akutso lɛ mli kusum mli hiɛnyiɛlɔi loo maŋtsɛmɛi lɛ asusu he dani aje ŋmɔ mli tsakemɔi wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Traditional leaders and chiefs oversee local land ownership and boundary agreements. Getting their guidance ensures your land claims are secured, prevents future land disputes with neighbors, and builds community support for your farm.
ga: Kusum mli hiɛnyiɛlɔi kɛ maŋtsɛmɛi kwɛɔ akutsoŋ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛ husu he kpaŋmɔi anɔ. Amɛ ŋaawoo lɛ ni oootsu he nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni okɛbiɔ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe. Tsi shikpɔŋ he béi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ kɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ anaa. ni oma akutsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ

english: How do I know if my farm soil is rich enough to plant new crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Rich, healthy soil is usually dark in color, soft to the touch, holds water well, and contains living organisms like earthworms. Soil that is hard, pale, or causes crop leaves to turn yellow without pest damage usually needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su tsuɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he, ni ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, shikpɔŋ ni wa, su ni mli tse, loo nɔ ni haa tsei ahe baai feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii efiteee nɔ ko lɛ yɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: When is the best time of year to clear my land and start planting in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni mikɛbaajie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mibɔi dumɔwui yɛ Ghana?

english: Land clearing is best done toward the end of the dry season, while planting should start right at the beginning of the major rainy season (around April or May) so seedlings receive enough rain to build strong roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. (Aaafee April loo May) koni dumɔwui lɛ aná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by a lack of nutrients in the soil, too much direct sunlight, or damage from pests and viral diseases like Swollen Shoot. Shade trees and proper soil feeding help keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli, tamɔ tsei ni efuu lɛ amli baa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to regularly clear weeds from around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops. They also create damp hiding places for insects and pests that can attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Amɛfeɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni baanyɛ atutua otsei lɛ hu.

english: Why do my young crops suffer so much during the dry Harmattan season, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ naa amanehulu waa yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu amɛhe?

english: The Harmattan brings dry winds and intense heat that suck water out of the soil and plant leaves rapidly. You can protect young crops by planting shade trees and placing dry grass or leaves around the plant bases to trap moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shwieɔ nu oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ooodu ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ koni akɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do diseases move from one tree to another across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Crop diseases are often spread by insects carrying viruses, wind blowing fungal spores, contaminated water runoff, or farmers using uncleaned tools like cutlasses on healthy trees after cutting infected ones.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni hiɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai. Fungal spores ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛbaa lɛ efite nu ni hoɔ lɛ Aloo okwaafoi kɛ nibii ni he tseee, tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ beni amɛfo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to prune dry or overcrowded branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni egbi loo ni egbɔ fe nine kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or sick wood, lets sunlight and fresh air flow through the farm, reduces pest hideouts, and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to leave a section of my farmland unplanted for a season before sowing seeds on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi midumɔi lɛ amli be kome dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving land uncultivated or fallow gives the soil time to rest and naturally restore nutrients and organic matter lost from previous harvests. Soil that has had a break produces healthier crops and better yields when you eventually plant seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ loo nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni elaaje kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shikpɔŋ ni akumɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai beni naagbee lɛ oduɔ odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying essential shade and keeping the soil moist so the tender cocoa trees can survive their early development.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni cacao tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to one another, the growing stalks must compete aggressively for water, sunlight, and essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. This shortage starves the plants, causing lower leaves to turn yellow and reducing yield.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei ni miida lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Nɛkɛ nibii ni bɛ nɛɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tso lɛ. Ehaa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require steady, reliable moisture to break open and grow. If dry spells follow the first light rains, or if seeds are buried too deep in dry soil, the seeds dry out, stall, or rot underground before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. Kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ nyiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ Aloo, kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaagbi, amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and develop light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-cassava baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curled, mottled leaves on cassava plants are typically caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus stops the leaves from producing food properly, leading to small, stunted tuber roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off before developing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme midday heat, erratic watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady soil moisture and balanced soil nutrients helps the plant hold onto flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than the crop seeds I planted on my cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to quickly seize sunlight, water, and nutrients from freshly cleared earth. Because they absorb soil nutrients faster than cultivated seeds, early clearing and weeding are required to prevent crops from being choked out.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli mra. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and wilt during hot afternoons even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, tomato plants release water vapor through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the ground. This temporary wilting is a protective reaction to save water; the leaves normally spring back up by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tomato tsei jieɔ nu mli la kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu he. Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is low in nutrients without testing it in a lab?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa ni mifeee laboratorio mli kaa?

english: Your crops act as signposts: slow or stunted growth usually points to general low fertility, pale or yellow lower leaves show a lack of nitrogen, and purplish stems or leaves point to low phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Oŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ okadi: bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔmɔ baa shi. Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ŋmeii loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How do I know that my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam plants signal maturity when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up toward the end of the rainy season. This indicates the plant has finished storing energy underground and the tuber is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa. ni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Officer, why do all my tomato plants produce ripe fruit at the exact same time instead of giving me small harvests every week?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ shikome yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii pɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ daa otsi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Certain tomato varieties, known as determinate varieties, are naturally programmed to bush out, flower, and set all their fruit in one short period. If you want fruit bit by bit throughout the season, you need to plant indeterminate varieties or stagger your planting dates every few weeks.
ga: Ale tomato henɔi komɛi akɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ nɔ ni baaba. Eyɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛ ŋmɔ, fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fɛɛ awo mli yɛ be kukuoo mli, kɛji oosumɔ aduawai fiofio yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Esa akɛ odu tsei srɔtoi ni aleee loo otsake gbii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ be fɛɛ be. otsii enyɔ komɛi

english: Why does my watermelon crop produce so many beautiful flowers, but very few actual watermelons form on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi fɛfɛji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi watermelon diɛŋtsɛ yɛ. Fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Watermelons produce separate male and female flowers on the same vine. The male flowers open first to supply pollen, and if bees are missing to transfer that pollen to the female flowers, the female flowers drop off without making fruit.
ga: Watermelon woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ wain tso kome nɔ. Fɔfɔi hii fɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkɛ pollen aha. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ laaje koni amɛkɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ aya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi yei lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Officer, why do my cocoa trees keep dropping their tiny green pods before they grow into big pods?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaada ni etsɔ pod agbo?

english: This natural dropping is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees often sprout more young pods than they can feed, so when water is scarce or nutrients run low, the tree naturally sheds extra small pods to save energy for the remaining ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu faaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie ŋmeii bibii. Yaa kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni okɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha hejɔɔmɔ.

english: Can I plant pepper on the same piece of land where I am growing cassava, or will they fight each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu pepper yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ loo béi baaba?

english: You can plant pepper alongside cassava in the early months of the season. Cassava grows slowly at first and leaves open space, allowing fast-growing pepper to get sunlight and yield before the cassava canopy grows wide and shades the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Yucca lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni eshiɔ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ naa hulu la ni amɛwoɔ yibii dani ŋmei ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me that planting groundnuts together with my maize will make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Okɛɔ mi akɛ kɛ́ okɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have natural tiny nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs lots of nitrogen to grow strong, so planting groundnuts gives your maize a free, natural boost of plant food.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii aná adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants fall off completely during the dry season, but the root underground stays alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of surviving heat and drought. By shedding its leaves, the plant stops losing water through evaporation and keeps its energy safely stored in the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nu shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ hewalɛ lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight cups and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking juice from the underside of the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. The attack damages the leaves, causing them to twist and lose green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Tutuamɔ lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Ekɛ sɛɛkuu kɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni laajeɔ baa.

english: Officer, why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow after heavy rains cover the field for several days?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?
