english: Heavy rains wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the soil where roots cannot reach, while sitting water starves the roots of air. Without air and nitrogen, the leaves lose their deep green color and turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Beni nu lɛ damɔ shi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baaje amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast in the barn after I dig them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams decay quickly if their outer skin gets cut or bruised during digging, which lets fungal spores inside. Storing yams in warm, crowded spaces with poor airflow also speeds up rotting, so they need shade and fresh air circulating around them.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite oya kɛji akɛ afo kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ loo atswa lɛ yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ boteɔ mli. Atomo ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hu haa fitemɔ yaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɔleɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize ears develop white mold while they are still standing on the farm before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ amli ŋmãa yɛŋ be mli ni amɛdamɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Mold grows when rainwater gets trapped inside the husks of upright maize ears during late rains. Bending the maize stalks downward (doubling) when the ears mature allows rainwater to run right off, keeping the cobs dry until you harvest them.
ga: Fuji lɛ daa kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ bote ŋmãa toi ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwie shi (shii enyɔ) beni toi lɛ edara kwraa lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ ajɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni oha ŋmeii lɛ agbi kɛyashi obaakpa amɛ

english: Can I use river water filled with leaves and floating trash directly to irrigate my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ faa mli nu ni eyi kɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni hoɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛshwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Using dirty water without a filter or sieve can clog your irrigation pipes and carry weed seeds and disease germs directly onto your farmland. Straining debris out ensures clean water flow and protects your young crops from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji ni filta loo skrin bɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ paipii amli. ni okɛ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aya he ni okwɛɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni efite lɛ ni oootsi lɛ haa nu ni mli tse hoɔ, ni ebuɔ onibii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: How does dirt or small stones inside my irrigation pipe affect the growth of my garden eggs?
ga: Muji loo tɛi bibii Te nu shwiemɔ paipii amli lɛ saa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When debris gets trapped in irrigation pipes, it blocks water from reaching certain sections of your farm. This causes uneven watering, leaving some plants stunted and thirsty while others get too much water.
ga: Kɛji sũ ni efite lɛ efo nu shwiemɔ paipi lɛ mli Nu lɛ baatsi gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi ahe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ. yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi náa nu babaoo tsɔ.

english: How do shallow ditches or concrete channels help my crops grow better during heavy rains?
ga: Te nubu ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɔnkrit gbɛ ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Channels direct excess rainwater safely off your field instead of allowing it to flood the crops. This prevents fast water from washing away topsoil and exposing the fragile roots of your plants.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ hoɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Enɛ ji koni nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ akafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ejie tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni waaa lɛ kpo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers start to fall over when heavy rain collects in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa bua amɛhe naa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Uncontrolled water flowing across crop beds washes away the soil holding the roots down. Without proper water channels to direct the flow, soft ground gives way and crops lose their anchor.
ga: Nu ni akudɔɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔji ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ sũ ni haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ. Kɛ nu gbɛi ni sa ni baakudɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and soft when water sits around the plants for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? tso lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo?

english: Tomato roots need air to breathe just like they need water. When water stays trapped around the roots without flowing away, the roots drown, rot, and can no longer send nutrients up to the leaves.
ga: Tomato shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ŋmɛ ehe ni ejooo foi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya baa lɛ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun. This is a natural reaction that helps the plant conserve moisture inside its stems during dry heat.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop lose most of its leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava intentionally drops its leaves to survive severe dry periods, saving water inside its roots. Once water becomes available again through irrigation or rain, it rapidly sprouts new leaves.
ga: Akɛ yiŋtoo shwieɔ ŋmei baai koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. koni eye ebua ni abu nu he yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli Beni nu baa ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do so many strange weeds sprout in my bed right after I flood it with water from a pond?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ naakpɛɛ nɛkɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, nibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ mi saatso lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ nubu lɛ mli lɛ ewo nɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Pond and river water carries wild weed seeds and floating organic debris. Straining the water before it enters your planting beds prevents weed seeds from taking root next to your crops.
ga: Ko mli jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni hoɔ nu lɛ yɛ nubu kɛ faa mli nu mli. Nu ni oootsɔ mli dani eho kɛbote onibii ni odu lɛ amli lɛ baatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo onibii amli shishifãi.

english: Why do my pepper plants get dark leaf spots after dirty mud splashes onto them during rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baa lɛ he ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni muji ni mli ewo muji shwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dirty splash water carries fungal germs from the soil directly onto the crop leaves. Setting up clean water channels and mulching reduces mud splash and keeps leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ahe baai amli. Nu gbɛi ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ haa sũ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa roots die when they are left in soggy soil that doesn't drain properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa roots are delicate and require well-aerated soil. Soil that stays waterlogged encourages root-rot fungi, which destroy tender feeding roots and prevent the cocoa seedling from growing.
ga: Kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ahe hewalɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ blɛoo, ni ehaaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does cocoa take several years to start bearing fruits compared to food crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani kookoo jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi kɛ akɛto niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that needs to build a strong root system and trunk to support heavy pods for decades, whereas annual crops like maize grow quickly just to produce seeds once before dying.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni esa akɛ ehiɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii ni tsii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ dani amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow pods directly on their main trunk instead of on the thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: This natural trait is called cauliflory. Cocoa pods are heavy, so growing directly on the thick trunk and strong limbs allows the tree to hold heavy fruit safely without breaking its branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli su nɛɛ akɛ kɔlifloa. Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ niji ni wa lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ aduawai ni tsii shweshweeshwe ni efoŋ tsei lɛ aniji.

english: If I cut off branches from my cocoa tree, won't that weaken the plant and reduce my harvest?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso nine ko Ani ebaaha kookoo tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually strengthens the tree by removing weak or diseased branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach the main trunk so the tree directs its energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa kɛtsɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: My father left me old cocoa trees that barely bear fruit—do old trees naturally stop producing or can they be brought back to life?
ga: Ataa shi kookoo tso momo ko yɛ esɛɛ. Yɛ mi ni shwɛ fioo ni ebaawo yibii lɛ gbɛfaŋ lɛ, ani tsei momo lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba wala mli ekoŋŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their production drops, but you can revive them through heavy pruning, replacing old soil nutrients with fertilizer, or grafting fresh shoots onto old roots.
ga: Beni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, shi obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni afolɔ waa lɛ aha amɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ato niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ momo mli lɛ najiaŋ. aloo niji heei ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi momoi ahe

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and small pods during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli

english: During extreme dry weather, cocoa trees drop flowers and small pods as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water and keep the main tree alive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Cacao tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu nu he ni akɛbu tsei wuji lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do young cocoa plants burn and die when planted directly in open sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight; they require shade trees like plantains or forest trees to shield them and trap soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛhiɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Will using modern chemical fertilizers spoil the cocoa soil or reduce the quality of the cocoa beans?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite kookoo shikpɔŋ lɛ loo ebaaha kookoo yibii lɛ afee fɛo?

english: Properly applied fertilizers replenish essential nutrients like potassium and phosphorus that cocoa trees pull from the ground over time, improving bean size and yield without lowering bean quality.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus ni cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ kpakpafeemɔ baaa shi.

english: Does spraying pesticides on cocoa trees harm the pods or make them unsafe to process?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ awui loo ehaa amɛhe feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha nitsumɔ?

english: Approved cocoa pesticides target harmful pests like capsids and pod borers without affecting the beans inside, as long as you follow spraying schedules and safety guidelines.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kookoo ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids kɛ pod borers. ni enaaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ Shii abɔ ni onyiɛɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact time a cocoa pod is ready for harvesting so I don't pick it too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? koni akabua naa oya tsɔ

english: Cocoa pods are ready when their skin changes color completely—usually turning bright yellow or orange—which signals that the sweet pulp and seeds inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛhiɛ tsake su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ loo kɛ dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etsɔ hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some green cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and dark conditions; removing infected pods immediately stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant moves what little it has from the older bottom leaves up to the young, developing ears, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but then the flowers drop off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face extreme heat or dry soil during flowering. When the plant feels stressed by the hot weather or lack of water, it sheds its flowers to save energy so the whole plant doesn't die.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Koni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbo.

english: Cassava leaves curl and droop to reduce their leaf surface area facing the direct sun. This is the plant's natural shield to slow down water evaporation from its leaves during the heat of the day, and they usually bounce back once the evening cools down.
ga: Afolɔ cassava baai lɛ amli koni ekɛba hiɛ shi, ni ekɛ hulu la lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛhaa nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Ni esumɔɔ ni eku esɛɛ kɛji edɔ pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under full, harsh sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or mature trees to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil around their shallow roots damp.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji amli. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ ahe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: If I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant next season, will they yield the same good crop?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani nakai dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai tamɔ nɛkɛ?

english: No, seeds saved from hybrid crops will not perform like the parent plant. Hybrid varieties are created through a special cross-breeding process, and their secondary seeds break down, resulting in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and much lower yields.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ efeŋ amɛnii tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ. Akɛ fɔmɔ gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko tsuɔ Hybrid henɔi ahe nii. ni dumɔwui ni ji enyɔ lɛ baajara. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa

english: Why do my yam tubers grow thin and bent instead of smooth and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow thin and deformed when the soil is too hard, compact, or filled with rocks that block the tuber from pushing downward smoothly. Loose, well-drained soil in high mounds gives the yam tuber room to expand fully.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyi obɔ kɛ tɛi, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ aahu akɛ anyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwie shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa.

english: Why are my tomato seedlings growing very tall, thin, and falling over in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato dumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛshwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and weak—known as being leggy—when they don't get enough direct sunlight. They are stretching out rapidly to search for light, which drains their energy and leaves them with weak, thin stems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Ale amɛ hu akɛ naji kakadaji Beni amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ Amɛmiikpã amɛhe oya koni amɛmiitao la. Enɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ ni ehaa amɛnáa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are armyworms completely destroying my maize crop while leaving the nearby cassava untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kpata mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ kwraa, ni amɛshi ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer cereal crops like maize, sorghum, and rice because these plants have soft, sweet leaves that are easy for the worms to digest. Cassava leaves contain bitter compounds that pests dislike, so armyworms avoid them.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa ejaakɛ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ oya. Nɔ ko ni mli wa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui sumɔɔɔ yɛ cassava baai amli.

english: How can I know that my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready for harvesting without pulling up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa ni mifiteee ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can test crop maturity by pulling up two or three sample plants across the farm. Open the pods: if the inner pod shell has dark brown markings and the seed skins have taken on their full color, the crop is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka tsei lɛ ahewalɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooogbala yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Gbelemɔ ŋmeii lɛ: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees get black spots and turn brown from the bottom leaves upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Sigatoka, a leaf spot disease caused by a fungus that thrives in warm, wet weather. It starts on the lowest leaves because they are older, stay damp longer, and sit closest to fungal spores living in the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji baa mli hela ko ni ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Je shishi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛdara. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ ni etaa shi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ fungal spores ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fe fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sun because their delicate leaves burn easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby provides natural shade and moisture needed to protect young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf tissue above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ potassium he lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in high humidity and dark conditions. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning tall branches lets sunshine and airflow dry out the pods, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep dropping off without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny beneficial insects called midges for pollination. If the soil is dried out or there is no organic leaf mulch on the ground for midges to live in, flowers remain unpollinated and drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nɔ ni akɛfeɔ pollination. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo ebɛ nɔ ko lɛ, okɛ organic mulch afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni dwarfs lɛ ahi mli, fɔfɔi lɛ baafee pollination ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: How many shoots should I leave on my plantain plant so that I can harvest large bunches?
ga: Plantain tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa tsei babaoo?

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for water and soil nutrients. Keeping only one main fruiting stem, one medium sucker, and one small shoot per stand allows the main plant to receive enough nourishment to produce large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Akpaa yibiiwoo tso titri kome pɛ, tso ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ tso bibioo kome yɛ shidaamɔ fɛɛ shidaamɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akpa.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so the rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. Burying or lightly covering the fertilizer with soil near the plant root zone prevents running surface water from washing it off your fields.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Fuumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ fioo Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seed corn instead of replanting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Saved seeds from harvested crops lose their strength in the next generation, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields. Certified seeds are specially produced to guarantee strong growth, uniform ears, and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛha amɛdara waa, toi po kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil moisture, and essential fertilizer nutrients, while also acting as breeding grounds for insect pests that attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa otsei lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: How can I tell when my maize is fully mature and ready to be harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer leaves surrounding the cob dry out and turn brown, and a small dark layer forms at the tip of each kernel where it connects to the cob.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ dara. Cob lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsɔɔ blɔfo. Ni ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naagbee, ni kɛ ŋmei lɛ tsaa lɛ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check if my crops are developing diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Walking through your field at least once or twice a week allows you to spot early signs of pests or disease before they spread across the entire farm, making treatment easier and cheaper.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔji amli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe okadi mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa helatsamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ejara waaa

english: Why does one sick tomato plant make all the nearby plants get spots and die so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Crop diseases like fungal blights produce tiny spores that travel through wind, rain splashes, and insects to neighboring plants. Removing and destroying the first infected plant immediately stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Tse helai tamɔ fungal leaf blight lɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. No tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ kooloi amli kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie tso klɛŋklɛŋ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ ni akpata hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up after the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity which encourages pests like mirids and diseases like black pod to attack young cocoa leaves and shoots. Regular farm clearing and pruning help reduce moisture traps.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua kookoo lɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ otsu oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ahe nii ni ofolɔ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi.

english: Is there a cheaper way to protect my crops from insects when spray chemical prices are too high?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni jara waaa ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe be mli ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ jara wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: You can reduce chemical costs by using Integrated Pest Management, such as spraying neem leaf extracts, removing infected leaves by hand, and practicing crop rotation to naturally lower pest numbers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa he nyɔmɔwoo aba shi kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ ni akɛfee ekome, tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nine ni ajieɔ baa ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ koni akɛba tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I bought is actually working or hurting my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ loo eyeɔ mitsei lɛ awui?

english: If the medicine works, pest damage stops and fresh green shoots appear. If leaves turn scorched, yellow, or drop within days of spraying, the chemical mixture was likely too strong or incorrect for that crop.
ga: Kɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpaɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shã, amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛgbee shi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo ejaaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together to kill weeds and insects at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ afutu mli koni magbe jwɛi kɛ kooloi bibii yɛ be kome mli?

english: Mixing different chemicals without expert guidance can cause severe leaf burn, weaken your crops, or neutralize the medicines completely so they no longer protect your plants.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛji ŋaawoo ni he esa bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ shãa ni naa wa baanyɛ aba. ha ŋmɔshi nibii afee gbɔjɔmɔ loo tsofa lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ Bɔni afee ni akabu otsei lɛ ahe dɔŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava dropping all its leaves during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry weather to save water and protect their tubers underground. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the soil lacks water, when temperatures are extremely hot, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that waterlogged roots cannot absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he loo akɛ shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: What information should I write down about my damaged crops before calling an extension officer for help?
ga: Mɛɛ saji esa akɛ maŋma yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni efite lɛ ahe dani matsɛ extension agent koni eye ebua mi?

english: Take note of when the problem started, which plant parts are affected (leaves, stems, or roots), how many plants are affected, and what chemicals or fertilizers you recently applied so the officer can give you the right solution.
ga: ŋmaa be ni naagba lɛ je shishi lɛ oshwie shi. Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã enaa (baai, shishifãi, loo shishifãi?) Tsei enyiɛ enaa? Ni mɛɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii okɛtsu nii nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ? Bɔni afee ni nitsulɔi lɛ aha bo tsabaa ni ja.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them during their first few years to provide shade and cool moisture while their roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni amɛha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees when the tree already looks full and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ eyi obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ momo lɛ?

english: Pruning overcrowded or dead branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. This helps reduce humidity that causes pod rot and directs the tree's strength into growing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni eyi obɔ loo ni egboi lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekabote tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa nu ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ewajeɔ tso lɛ koni ekɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving plantains proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ kui ni tsii amli.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet conditions. Keeping weeds low, pruning branches to let air flow, and picking off infected pods immediately prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Jwɛi lɛ Ashishijee Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target young maize crops. Catching them early by checking the center leaves and applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the leaf whorls stops them from destroying the farm.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ni akwɛɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants look twisted with yellow patches instead of remaining smooth and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected stems. Planting disease-free stem varieties provided by extension services stops the virus from damaging your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Hela bɛ stem henɔi ni aduɔ kɛtsɔɔ extension service nɔ lɛ tsiɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafite onibii.

english: Why do I see tiny white insects covered in cotton-like fluff sticking to my crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii yɛŋ lɛ? Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ehà nɔ, ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: These are mealybugs, pests that suck the sap out of stems and can transmit viruses like swollen shoot disease in cocoa. Removing heavily infested branches and applying recommended sprays helps control their population.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni gbeɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai tamɔ cocoa bud swollen disease lɛ amɛshwã. Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ gbɔmɛi ayibɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its power to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ dɔŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves, or produce smaller harvests than before, the soil is low on nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or the right fertilizer restores essential minerals to the land.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe tsutsu lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and attracts crop-specific pests. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning black and soft before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and adding organic matter helps prevent the fruit from spoiling.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa kwraa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. kɛ koni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rain floods the soil without proper drainage, it suffocates the roots and creates an environment for fungal diseases that rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ nu ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa ŋmeii shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow tall. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds growing around my okra make the crop stay stunted and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi okra ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crop for light, water, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow very fast, they steal essential food from the soil before the okra roots can reach it, causing the crop to stay small.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. No hewɔ lɛ ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okra shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Why do I need to clear away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they fight with the main stem for nutrients and water. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛkɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshiɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that relies on tall support to spread its leaves upward toward the sun. Proper sunlight exposure on the leaves allows the plant to manufacture more food, which leads to larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni nɔ kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ hulu la lɛ shɛ tsei lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any small peppers can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper bibii baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that forces the plant to grow leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Aloo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do groundnut pods end up growing under the dirt after the plant flowers above ground?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni tsei lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the flower stems turn downward into long pegs that push themselves into the loose soil. Once buried underneath, the tip of the peg swells to form the groundnut pod.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu yɛ shishi lɛ Pin lɛ naagbee lɛ baafu aahu kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why does paddy rice manage to grow well in waterlogged fields while my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli shi ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ gbo?

english: Rice plants have specialized internal air tubes running from their leaves to their roots, allowing oxygen to reach underwater roots so they can breathe even in submerged soils where other crop roots would rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ shɛɔ nu shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ emuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebote nu shishi yɛ he ni tsei krokomɛi ashishifãi baanyɛ agbo lɛ po mli.

english: What causes the leaves on my tomato plants to curl inward and stop expanding?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli ni amɛgbɛɛɛ amɛhe?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit plant viruses, or by stress from intense heat and drought. Managing pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ mli baa lɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees suddenly looking sick and not producing as many pods as before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɔ ko ni hela mɔ lɛ trukaa ni ewooo ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees can become sickly when infected by diseases like Swollen Shoot virus or Black Pod, or when pests attack them. Soil losing its natural nutrients over time also makes trees weaker and less productive.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ aná hela kɛji helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo ŋmeii ni ewo diŋ lɛ ahe hela lɛ ye amɛnɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hu haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Can older cocoa trees catch diseases more easily than young ones?
ga: Ani helai nyɛɔ emɔ cacao tsei ni edara lɛ oya fe cacao tsei?

english: Yes, older trees often have weaker natural defense systems, making it much easier for fungal infections, viruses, and insects to take hold and spread throughout the farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ fungal, virus, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe helai lɛ baahi shi ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes cocoa pods to turn dark and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, wet, or heavily shaded farm conditions with poor air circulation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ, ni efɔ, loo ni kɔɔyɔɔ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by nutrient shortages in the soil, extreme drought, or deadly infections like the Swollen Shoot virus.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo helai ni naa wa tamɔ bud virus ni efuu

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are too old to produce good fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa trees usually produce their best yields between 10 and 25 years of age. If a tree is over 30 years old and yields very few pods even with proper care, it has passed its prime and should be replaced.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25. Kɛji tso lɛ eye fe afii 30 ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po lɛ, Amrɔ nɛɛ tso lɛ eho he ni esa akɛ edara lɛ he, ni esa akɛ atsake lɛ.

english: Why did my elders' cocoa farm last for over 50 years, but my current farm seems to struggle much earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛmi nuu lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ehi shi nɔ ni fe afii 50 nɛ, shi etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɛɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔ oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Older farms were planted on rich, untouched forest land with balanced natural shade and fewer disease outbreaks. Modern farms often face worn-out soil, changing rainfall patterns, and stronger pest populations.
ga: Okwaafoi momo ni adu yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse nɔ. Adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ja yɛ jɛmɛ, ni helai ni baa lɛ hu faaa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔji kɛ shikpɔji ni efite kpeɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ ni tsakeɔ lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: What is the best thing to do when an old section of my cocoa farm stops bearing fruit completely?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei momo lɛ kpa yibiiwoo kwraa?

english: The best step is to cut down the unproductive old trees and replant the land with modern, high-yielding cocoa varieties that resist common diseases better.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni afolɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ, ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ eyeɔ amɛhe lɛ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: How can I keep my cocoa farm healthy and productive for many decades?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ?

english: Regularly prune dead branches, remove sick pods promptly, apply recommended fertilizers to feed the soil, and manage shade trees properly to keep the cocoa trees strong.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ daa. Jiemɔ helatsɛmɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. ni akwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni eha kookoo tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does planting cocoa trees too close together make them get sick more easily?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, hela mɔɔ amɛ oya?

english: Yes, overcrowded trees block airflow and sunshine. This creates a dark, moist environment where fungal diseases spread rapidly from tree to tree.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli woɔ duŋ ni edɔɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the health of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While cocoa trees need water, excessive rainfall creates damp conditions that encourage Black Pod disease and can wash valuable nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia kookoo tsei moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize plants need to build strong leaves and healthy stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off when the weather gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry periods as a natural way to save water, and the plant will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Ni tsei lɛ baajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat or irregular watering, as stress causes the plant to abort flower production to protect itself.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Yɛ haomɔ hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ akpa fɔfɔii afeemɔ koni ebu ehe.

english: Why do my growing tomatoes get dark rotten spots on the bottom end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miida lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: This issue, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium or experience irregular watering while the fruits are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛná nu ni ejaaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo lɛ.

english: Why does my yam plant need to climb up a tall stick to give me big yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ koni enyɛ ená ŋmɔshi nibii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to reach up high to capture maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to make more food and store it in the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ he babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves fold up during peak heat to reduce their exposure to direct sunlight, which prevents the plant from losing too much water.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo.

english: Growing the same crop every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear them from my land with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dade jie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many weeds have deep root systems or underground stems that store food, allowing them to shoot up new leaves quickly even after being cut above ground.
ga: Jwɛi babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akɛ niyenii toɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ baai heei oya kɛji afo amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why do some seeds sprout in just a few days while others take weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi heɔ otsii babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds have different outer shell thicknesses and resting periods; seeds with tough shells take more time and water to soften before the seedling can push through.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi kɛ be ni amɛwɔɔ. Dumɔwui ni amɛhe wa lɛ baahe be babaoo kɛ nu dani amɛfee blɛoo dani dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and leafy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans before your maize helps put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli loo ni aduɔ ŋmãa dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce small, weak cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet soil, catching more sunlight and protecting the leaves from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Egbalaa hulu la babaoo ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them past the harvest time during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the soil stays soaked with rain for too long, air cannot reach the roots and the cassava begins to suffocate and decay. Harvesting mature cassava at the right time prevents waterlogging damage.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kasava lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni ebaagbo. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni eda yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ akafite nɔ ko.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajieɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ.

english: Having too many shoots causes them to steal food and water from the main plant. Keeping only two or three strong shoots allows the main plant to produce a much bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛye ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when water is scarce to conserve energy and keep the main tree alive. Planting shade trees and mulching around the roots helps retain moisture so flowers stay on.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hewalɛ ahi shi ni eha tso titri lɛ ahi shi lɛ bɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade helps the flowers set into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato nɔ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects sucking sap from the young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying with neem water or safe insect control helps protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo tsofa kroko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but not forming a hard, round head in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather is too hot or if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces wide leaf growth instead of tight folding.
ga: Kaabaji lɛ ewaŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas gather nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land as my new young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo tsei heei lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily dry up and die. Plantains grow quickly with large, broad leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist while your cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni okkoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main plant food maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can help keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri kɛha tsei ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Should I apply my dry fertilizer to the farm right before a heavy rain starts?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: It is best to wait until after a heavy rain has passed. Applying fertilizer right before heavy downpours causes the water to wash the expensive fertilizer away into rivers before your crops' roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eho. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ faa lɛ mli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stems slanting into the soil instead of standing straight up?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni ja?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems at a slight angle encourages the roots to spread out wider and produce more large tubers underground than planting them completely upright.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ odu o-yucca tso lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji fe be mli ni odu lɛ shiŋŋ kwraa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch and kill fresh sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains are regular so your seeds have steady water to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: What is making small holes in my young maize leaves, leaving fine powdery mess inside the plant heart?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baai lɛ miifee bu bibii? Powda fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ. Ani ekã tso ko tsui mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into maize plants. Spraying approved bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract directly into the center of the plant early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my mature cocoa tree if it seems like I am hurting the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni miiye tso lɛ awui?

english: Trimming extra branches allows fresh air and sunlight to pass through the tree canopy. This dries up extra moisture that breeds black pod disease and encourages the tree to grow fresh cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ agbi, ni ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ cocoa ŋmɔtɔi heei.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the soil gets too dry, when temperatures get extremely hot, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly watered and mulched can fix this.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium bɛ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass or cocoa shells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds from invading, and decomposes into rich plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekabote mli ni efite ni etsɔ tsei niyenii babaoo

english: Why do some seed packets have official labels with lots of numbers printed on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui akui komɛi yɛ nɔ ni amralo lɛ ŋmaa nɔ ni yibɔi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those numbers are official registration codes from authorities like the National Seed Council. They show that the seed has been tested, certified, and proven to grow healthy crops with good yields.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ ji gbɛi ni aŋmalaa mɛi agbɛi awoɔ mli ni jɛ nitsumɔhei tamɔ National Seed Council lɛ adɛŋ. Amɛtsɔɔ akɛ aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ, aha amɛ odaseyeli ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I buy in the market will actually sprout well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Look for certified seeds that carry official approval labels with registration numbers. Certified seeds are tested in laboratories to guarantee high germination rates before they are sold.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni yɔɔ wolo ni maŋ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ ni aŋmala nɔmba awo mli lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ laboratori mli koni ana akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do certified seeds sprout much faster and evenly than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya kwraa ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ daa fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected, cleaned, and stored under ideal conditions so every seed has full energy to sprout, whereas home-saved seeds often lose vigor or carry hidden diseases.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuuɔ he ni akɛtoɔ shihilɛi ni sa shishi. Bɔni afee ni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu aná hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ baa amɛnɔ.

english: If I save seeds from a high-yielding hybrid maize crop, why won't they give me the same bumper harvest next season?
ga: Kɛji mibua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ amɛhaaa mi ŋmãa ni fa babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid crops are created by crossing specific parent plants to produce extra vigor for one generation only. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special combined traits, leading to weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Afeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni akɛfoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kroko aba kɛha yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni haa amɛfeɔ ekome lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my certified maize crops grow to the exact same height while local varieties look uneven?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni awo he odase lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he kome yɛ be mli ni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ tamɔɔɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds have uniform genetic traits, meaning every single seed grows at the same speed, flowers at the same time, and reaches the same height.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe su kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu baakwɛ̃ oya nɔŋŋ. fɔfɔii yɛ be kome mli kɛ ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdo kome mli

english: Why do my cassava plants yield very small tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ woɔ bulbs bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops need enough space under the soil to expand their roots. When planted too close, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tiny harvests.
ga: Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli. Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji nikpamɔ fioo ko.

english: Why do some improved crop varieties stay green during dry spells while my traditional crops wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni atsake lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mishishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Certain registered crop varieties are specifically bred to tolerate drought by growing deeper roots or conserving water better than traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hɔmɔ naa kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ loo nu ni amɛbuɔ he jogbaŋŋ fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in crops. When it gets too hot, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy so that the rest of the plant can stay alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. koni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and fall off when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nutrients, causing the plant's leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my stored crop seeds get full of tiny insects after a few months in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui atoohe lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Stored seeds often contain invisible insect eggs from the field or high moisture levels. If seeds are not properly dried or treated before storage, warm temperatures cause pest eggs to hatch and multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli kooloi bibii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo atsuuu he nii dani akɛtoɔ. Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awɔlɔi fɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: How do I calculate how many acres are in one hectare of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu acre enyiɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ hectare kome mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: One hectare is equal to about 2.5 acres. Knowing this conversion helps you accurately calculate how much seed, fertilizer, and chemical you need for your land size.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre 2.5 yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ ole tsakemɔ nɛɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni obu dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni he baahia bo kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of produce I will harvest from my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu nibii ni makpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa?

english: You estimate yield by measuring your farm area in acres or hectares and multiplying it by the standard average yield per acre for your specific crop under good management practices.
ga: Obuɔ yibiiwoo he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooosusu yɛ acre loo hectares mli lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ enɛ afata yibiiwoo ni anáa kɛjɛɔ acre kome mli kɛha onibii pɔtɛɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are suffocating from too much water sitting in the soil.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu efo shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu babaoo ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops droop and wilt during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. The plant wilts to conserve moisture and usually recovers when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak plants with small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is good because beans pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to help the maize grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni hi ejaakɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually shortly after rain, so the nutrients can dissolve and be absorbed easily by the plant roots without burning them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ amɛ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my final harvest so much if I leave them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ awui waa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and space from your crops, leaving your plants undernourished and unable to produce full, healthy yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if pests like fall armyworms are attacking my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Look for rough holes chewed in the leaves and small sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel where new leaves grow.
ga: Taomɔ buji ni mli ewo muji ni atswa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii. Eyɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the grains become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my crop trees instead of just letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso ko niji komɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã ekwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or extra branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps the tree direct its energy into growing strong trunks and producing higher yields instead of wasting food on unproductive leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tsei ni mli wa lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do I know the right way to cut or prune my tree branches without damaging the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ loo afoɔ tsei ni afiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Always use sharp, clean tools to make smooth cuts close to the main branch collar without tearing the bark. Focus on removing dead wood, branches growing inward, or diseased parts, and avoid cutting off too much of the canopy at one time.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ dɛŋdade ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ atsu nii ni okɛfo tso lɛ nine wulu lɛ kuɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni ogbalaaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ. Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama tsei ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ nɔ. niji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mli loo fã ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ fã ni ooofo tsɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ he.

english: What simple maintenance steps should I follow to keep my trees healthy as they grow older?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ akwɛ nɔ? Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mitsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Regularly clean the farm floor of fallen weeds, clear unwanted shoots (suckers) growing from the trunk, inspect the bark for pests or diseases, and apply proper compost or fertilizer around the root zone.
