ga: Tsumɔ jwɛi ni egbee shi lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni ataooo ni miida kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii loo helai yɛ mli. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii yɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds around the base of my crops stop them from growing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ miitsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and vital soil nutrients away from your crops. If weeds cover the foundation of your plant, your crop becomes starved, weak, and more easily affected by diseases.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji jwɛi ha tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ nɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ oya, amɛbaagbɔjɔ ni helai baaye amɛnɔ.

english: How can I protect the soil foundation around my trees so they don't get weak?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ shishitoo ni bɔle mitso lɛ he lɛ he koni ekagbɔjɔ?

english: Keep the area around the trunk clean from heavy weeds, apply organic mulch like dry grass or cocoa husks to retain soil moisture, and avoid digging too close to the trunk to protect the upper roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ jogbaŋŋ Ha tso lɛ mli tse kɛjɛ jwɛi ni mli ewo muji ahe. Kɛ organic mulch tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋtayaa ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ he tsɔ koni obu ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he.

english: Can clearing weeds with a cutlass hurt the root foundation of my crop trees?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni akɛ ŋmei shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite mitsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ?

english: Yes, if you scrape or dig too deeply near the base of the tree, you can cut the shallow feeder roots that collect food and water. Carefully clear weeds on the surface around the trunk rather than tilling deep into the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji okɛ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Obaanyɛ ofo shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni buaa niyenii kɛ nu naa lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ hei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ

english: What causes my mature crop trees to fall down to the ground suddenly?
ga: Mɛni ha mitso ni eda lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ trukaa lɛ?

english: Trees usually fall over because of root rot caused by standing water, underground pest damage like termites destroying the root structure, or poor soil anchorage combined with strong winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. loo shikpɔŋ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he

english: How can I prevent my crop trees from collapsing or falling over during bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mitsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi loo amɛkagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli?

english: Ensure good drainage so water does not sit at the base and rot the roots, clear pests early, avoid damaging the root system while weeding, and leave windbreak trees around the edge of your farm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nu akatara shishigbɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ akagbo. Jiemɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ nifitemɔ he beni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni oshi tsei ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my tree crop is becoming sick before it collapses or dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ mitso lɛ dani egbo loo egbo?

english: Look out for early signs such as yellowing leaves, unusual sap oozing from the bark, premature leaf drop, or soft, rotting areas on the lower trunk and roots.
ga: Taomɔ mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nu ni ejaaa ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. baa ni fiteɔ oya loo hei ni egbo yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do young tree seedlings wither and die in the open sun, and how do I protect them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Young seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle intense direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava nearby provides temporary shade and moisture until the young trees mature.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i aba be kukuoo mli kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turn yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to grow strong green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost near the roots helps fix this.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli ni mli wa akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with brownish dirt inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni muji ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf funnel to feed on young leaves, leaving behind brownish droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded, and humid conditions. High rainfall splashes fungal spores from the soil or infected pods onto healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, shade, kɛ edɔ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread viruses that cripple normal leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela ko ni haaa baa lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ eshwa

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick leafy stems but give me small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi ehiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in heavy shade, the plant focuses all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of transferring energy underground to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo edaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ hewalɛ nɔ etsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes on hot sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures make tomato pollen dry out and become sterile. If flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tomato pollen lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their small tiny pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? lots dani etsɔ agbo

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees shed excess young pods that they cannot support with available nutrients, water, or sunlight.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, nu, loo hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra sucker shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to smaller plantain bunches and weaker stems.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad practice to throw dry fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ashwie miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated chemical salts. When placed directly against a plant stem, it burns the green stem tissue and shallow roots, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baashã. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their tender leaf buds and dries out the topsoil before their root system is strong enough to reach water deep underground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani amɛshishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni eshɛ nu lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to build healthy stems and green leaves.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa tsei ahe tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow huge green leaves above ground but produce very thin cassava tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi cassava ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much animal manure or nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its strength into growing leaves and branches instead of storing energy underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ eniji.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops compete for the same sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to stay weak and produce smaller yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni falɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do agricultural extension agents advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally feeding and improving the growth of nearby grains like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa niyenii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni haa ŋmaa ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ ji oshara kɛha mi.

english: The first short rain only moistens the top surface of the ground. If no more rain falls immediately after, the hot dry soil will bake the sprouting seeds and kill them before they push through the ground.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku lɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni egbe amɛ dani amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or lack water during the flowering stage, dropping flowers to save water and keep the main stem alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Amɛshɛrɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, which transmit plant viruses while feeding on the sap of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ tso lɛ mli hela lɛ eshwaa beni eyeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why does Striga weed grow aggressively in poor fields but disappear when the soil is well-fertilized?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni ehiii amli shi amɛlaaajeɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli tse jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that targets crop roots in worn-out soils. Healthy crops growing in rich soil produce strong roots that can fight off the parasite.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni tswaa tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ anɔ lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ awuu ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off the main stem, and the ground surrounding the stem begins to crack open from the expanding tubers below.
ga: Yucca lɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb ni mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing on the bottom leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Nitrogen helps the plant stay green, so when the soil doesn't have enough, the crop takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ, ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to apply fertilizer when my farm's soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji oshara be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so that crop roots can soak it up. Putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots and stays wasted on the surface until rain or water is added.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ loo nu baaha eyi mli obɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land yield smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws heavy amounts of specific nutrients from the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those nutrients completely, which is why rotating crops with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni atsake ŋmãa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛtswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops are crowded too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each seed proper spacing allows the roots to spread out and produces larger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade crops like plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa plant's first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni kookoo tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so short and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi tsei titrii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow rapidly and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the nutrition available in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the land for long periods, water fills all the empty spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni efee efolo lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off mainly due to heat stress or lack of water. When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm target the tender center leaves because they are soft and nutrient-rich. Checking the center roll of the leaves early helps you spot these pests before they destroy the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Centre leaf roll lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by a viral infection spread by insects. These pests suck the sap from tender leaves, causing them to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year even though I plant on the exact same farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth as they grow. When you farm the same soil continuously without giving it a break or adding compost, the land becomes tired and drained of its natural strength, leading to lower yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Beni oyaa nɔ otsuɔ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii ni ojaraaa mli loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its strength and needs a break?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni atsake lɛ?

english: If your plant leaves look pale or yellow, growth stays stunted, or the soil turns hard and dry quickly after rain, these are clear signs that the nutrients in your soil have been exhausted.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dalɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji okadii ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ etã.

english: How can I bring strength back to my exhausted land without buying expensive modern chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ nɔ ni miheee ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: You can restore soil strength naturally by planting nitrogen-fixing cover crops like cowpeas or groundnuts, spreading animal manure, and leaving fallen leaves on the ground to rot into rich, natural fertilizer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi, tamɔ tsina ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Okɛ kooloo ŋmei kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ koni egbo akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni jara wa.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I burn the weeds and old leaves before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishã jwɛi kɛ baai momoi dani midu?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys the organic material that feeds the soil. Over time, burning drains the soil's strength and leaves it weak, dry, and easily washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi ebaakpãtã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aba shi. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ, egbiɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why is it harmful to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that sucks specific nutrients out of deep soil. Planting it repeatedly on the same spot completely exhausts those nutrients and allows pests that attack cassava to multiply in the ground.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What does leaving my land to fallow actually do for my future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mishiɔ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha miwɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fallowing means letting your land rest for a few seasons. Wild plants and trees grow back, dropping leaves that rot and naturally rebuild the earth's strength so your crops yield heavily when you return.
ga: Foliation tsɔɔ akɛ obaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe be fioo komɛi. Tsei kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Eshiɔ baai ni egboi yɛ esɛɛ ni ewoɔ adebɔɔ mli je lɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo kɛ́ oku osɛɛ oba.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the ears fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, a key building block for plants. The plant is moving whatever limited food it finds from its lower leaves up to the developing ear.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii fioo ko kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya toi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli.

english: Yams need loose, deep, nutrient-filled soil to expand easily. If the ground is exhausted, packed hard, or full of stones, the tuber struggles to push outward and turns out small or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya kponɔgbɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee bibii loo amɛbaafite.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if there seems to be enough sunlight for all of them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ fɛɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink up underground moisture and steal vital plant nutrients from exhausted soil before your crops' roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni amɛmuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛjuɔ tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ mli dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my young crops wilt in the hot afternoon heat even when the soil feels slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po.

english: Extreme sun makes young plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from tired soil. Plantains or shade trees can protect delicate crops from burning under harsh sunlight.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks enough nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls natural nitrogen fertilizer out of the air and puts it back into the soil, keeping your land rich and helping your maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni oye obua o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spread fertilizer on my crop field right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain quickly washes away loose fertilizer off the top of the soil before your crop roots have a chance to drink it up, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ shika kɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally to save water when the weather gets hot and dry. Once the rains return, the plant uses stored energy in its stem to grow fresh new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu nu he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the hot afternoon even if the ground was damp in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can suck water out of the soil. Once the heat cools down in the evening, the crop usually recovers.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ latsaa be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he baajɔ amɛ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I put too many seeds into one single planting hole?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot makes the young plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my yam vines need high wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground lets sunlight reach every leaf easily. Leaves use sunlight to make food, which is then sent underground to swell the yam tuber.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tsei anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ hulu la baashɛ baa fɛɛ baa he. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly into tiny balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Tight leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by intense heat stress. Keeping pests away early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli Atsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa mra Ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why am I finding small round holes in the centers of my young maize plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: Holes in young leaf whorls are a clear sign that pests like fall armyworms are feeding inside the leaves. Finding them early helps you treat the crop before the pest destroys the growing point.
ga: Buu ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miiye baai lɛ. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohere ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani tsɛŋemɔ helai akpãtã he ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why does pinching off extra side shoots on my tomato plants make my fruits grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa mi-fruit lɛ feɔ agbo lɛ?

english: Removing unnecessary extra shoots forces the tomato plant to send its water and energy directly into expanding the fruit rather than feeding useless stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ, enyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ niyenii

english: Is it bad if I pour water directly on my crop leaves when the afternoon sun is very hot?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ nu wo mitsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering leaves under strong sunshine can burn them because water droplets act like small magnifying glasses in the heat. It is best to pour water directly around the roots early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ afɔ baai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli nui ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. yɛ hulutsoo be mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ nu awo shishitoo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my crops too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots cannot breathe and begin to rot. You will notice the leaves turning soft and pale yellow, and the soil around the plant will stay muddy and sticky for a long time.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Obaayɔse akɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baakã he afee muji ni ekpɛtɛ ehe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it good to save rainwater in buckets on my farm to water my crops later?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ nugbɔ nu baato baagi mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni akɛha tsei lɛ nu sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, storing rainwater in containers is a great way to ensure you have water for your crops during dry days, but you should keep the buckets covered so mosquitoes do not breed inside.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu ni okɛtoɔ tsɛnsii amli lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ona nu kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli. Shi esa akɛ oha tanki lɛ ahi shi koni ŋmeii akafɔ yɛ mli.

english: Why do the roots of my crops show above the ground after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away the top layer of soil, exposing the roots to the open air. When this happens, you need to gently cover the roots back up with soil so the hot sun does not dry them out and kill the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ ho shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛtee. Ejieɔ shishifãi lɛ akpo kɛtsɔɔ kponɔgbɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛji enɛ ba lɛ Esa akɛ okɛtsu nii blɛoo. Okɛ sũ aha shishifãi lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Can I plant small crops like pepper or tomatoes under big coconut trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato. Yɛ ŋmei tso agbo lɛ shishi?

english: Big coconut trees cast a lot of shade and their thick roots take up most of the water and food from the soil. Crops like pepper need plenty of direct sunlight and fresh soil space, so they will not yield well under tall coconut trees.
ga: Kokoo tsei wuji haa hulutsoo babaoo. Ni shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ ewo yibii kpakpai yɛ akokoo tsei kakadaji ashishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops drop down and curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during hot afternoons to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant hold onto its water. If the leaves bounce back in the cool evening, the plant is fine, but if they stay weak, the soil needs water.
ga: Ha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji ogbɔjɔ lolo lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nu.

english: Why do young crop seedlings need temporary shade when I first move them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli ni mikɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, delicate roots that cannot pull water from the ground fast enough to survive strong sunlight. Temporary shade protects them while they build stronger root systems in their new home.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ amɛshia hee lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry grass acts like a blanket over the dirt, keeping the soil cool, trapping moisture so you do not have to water as often, and stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is my plant growing very tall with plenty of green leaves but no fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni ekɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: When a plant gets too much nitrogen from animal manure or certain fertilizers, it puts all its energy into growing thick leaves instead of flowers and fruits. It may also mean the plant is not getting enough sunlight.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi amli Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ tso lɛ naaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Should I pour liquid fertilizer directly against the stem of my plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, pouring liquid fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin. You should pour it in a small circle a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can reach it safely.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo. Esa akɛ okɛwo kooloi bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Pruning lets sunlight and air pass freely through the farm. This dries out extra moisture inside the tree canopy so fungal diseases like black pod cannot easily grow and destroy your cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji nyɛŋ adara ni amɛfite kookoo ŋmeii lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody when I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant to live on. If left in the soil past maturity, the plant starts consuming its own stored food to stay alive, making the roots fibrous, dry, and hard to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch koni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shi. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi eda kwraa Tso lɛ baabɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eniyenii ni ekɛto lɛ yeli koni ehi wala mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fiber, amɛgbiɔ ni ewaa akɛ amɛhoomɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall sticks to give me large yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni enyɛ ená sweet potato agboi aha mi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. When vines climb wooden poles, the leaves catch more sunlight, which fuels the growth of larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo. ni ji tsofa ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of bottom maize leaves means the plant lacks nitrogen food in the soil. The maize plant is taking nutrients from its old lower leaves to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tso lɛ miigbala niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛmiijɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize rolls its leaves to shrink the area exposed to the hot sun. This natural reaction helps the plant trap moisture inside and stop water from evaporating too quickly during dry hours.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛfo hei ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and refusing to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap. The stress prevents the plant from flowering and forming health pepper fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies, ni miinu tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Haomɔ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ pepper yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries up tomato pollen so the flowers cannot fertilize properly. When pollination fails, the plant drops the useless flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas make my soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have natural partnerships with tiny organisms in the ground that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. After harvest, that trapped nitrogen feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakpaa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I remove broad-leaved plantain suckers and leave the ones with narrow leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ ni mashi baai bibii lɛ?

english: Narrow-leaved suckers have strong root systems connected to the main stem and produce heavy plantain bunches, while broad-leaved suckers have weak roots and yield smaller fruit.
ga: Baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kpãa gbee ni ehaa plantain tsei babaoo baa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: How can I know how much crop yield I will get at harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nibii ni maná yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ ayibɔ?

english: Your harvest size depends heavily on how well you care for the crops during the season, including timely fertilizing, weeding, watering, and pest control.
ga: Bɔ ni obaakpa nii lɛ dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni fata he ji ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ be ni sa mli. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ

english: Why do some farmers get a huge harvest while others get very little from the same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi náa nɔ ko fioo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: A bigger harvest comes from following proper farm practices, such as feeding the crops with the right fertilizer, clearing weeds, and monitoring the farm regularly for pests.
ga: Nikpamɔi wuji jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi kpakpai ni akɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa haa lɛ mli. jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ daa.

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food and nutrients to the plant roots, which helps crops grow strong stems, healthy green leaves, and bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa. baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji

english: How do I tell if my crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Crops usually show hunger by turning pale or yellow, growing slowly, having thin stems, or failing to produce flowers and healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ hɔmɔ he okadi kpo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ tsei bibii, loo amɛwooo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is clearing weeds so important for my crops to perform well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa waa koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops, which starves the plants and reduces your final harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni ehaa onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my plants look healthy in the beginning but produce very small fruits at the end?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli shi ewoɔ yibii bibii kwraa yɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Crops need extra nutrients and moisture during their flowering and fruiting stages; if care drops mid-season, fruit development will suffer.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajie kwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebaana Yibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: What are the essential daily or weekly tasks I must do to look after my crops properly?
ga: Mɛni ji daa gbi loo otsi nitsumɔi ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ mafee koni manyɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper crop care includes regularly inspecting plants for bugs, removing weeds around the roots, ensuring the soil has moisture, and applying recommended nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni sa he ji tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ daa kɛji kooloi yɛ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii

english: How often should I go to my field to check on my growing crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ mli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ?

english: Visiting your farm at least once or twice a week allows you to catch problems like pests, diseases, or dry soil early before they harm the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona naagbai tamɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mra. Dani ebaaye ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ awui

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my plants start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are a warning sign that the crop is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting too much or too little water, or being attacked by pests.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadi akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni enaa nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa amɛ

english: How does keeping my farm clean and well-cared for protect crops against bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni mibu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli?

english: Good soil care and weeding help the ground retain moisture longer and build deep, strong roots that help plants survive short dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni efee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up the soil moisture before their root systems are deep enough to draw water from underground.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ mli egbiɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the surface of the soil, which makes it easy for heavy fruit bunches and strong wind to pull the entire plant out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aduawai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔlii amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves before the plant matures.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii dani tsei lɛ adara.

english: What makes my cassava tubers rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava tubers usually rot when excess water collects around roots in poorly drained soil, creating wet conditions that encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks for my yam plants to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb sticks so their leaves can spread out in the air to catch sunlight, which allows the plant to make food and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei aniji anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering, causing stress that forces the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking leaf sap and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: Cowpeas gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil and sharing nutrients with neighboring maize plants.
ga: Cowpeas buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ekɛ ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cover my farm soil with dry leaves instead of burning the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã he lɛ dani madu nii?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves protects the ground from sun heat, traps soil moisture, and slowly breaks down into natural plant manure.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings wilt and look weak for a few days after I move them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa gbii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ ewo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When young seedlings are transplanted, their fine feeder roots suffer minor shock and cannot absorb water immediately. Giving them shade and adequate moisture helps the roots recover so the plant can settle into the new soil and resume normal growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui bibii Amɛshishifãi ni eye niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakpokpo fioo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni ebɔi dalɛ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: When I dig up plantain suckers to plant in a fresh field, what helps them survive the move?
ga: Beni mifoɔ plantains koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ Mɛni ye ebua amɛ ni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ shihilɛ ni amɛfã kɛtee jɛmɛ lɛ mli?

english: Trimming the top leaves and damaged roots before replanting reduces water loss. Planting them immediately in moist, rich soil allows the sucker to quickly establish new roots and settle into its new spot.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi baai kɛ shishifãi ni efite lɛ dani adu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi heei oya ni amɛhiɔ he ko hee.

english: If four maize seeds germinate in one hole, why is it better to pull out two and leave only two?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ abaajie dumɔwui enyɔ ni ashi enyɔ pɛ?

english: When too many plants share a single hole, their roots compete heavily for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. Thinning them out leaves enough space and food for the remaining plants to grow thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Beni tsei babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afee amɛ bibii lɛ, ehaa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay very small when I place my mounds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa beni mikɛ amɛ toɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Yam roots require adequate soil volume and nutrients to swell into large tubers. When mounds are spaced too tightly, the crop roots overlap and fight for limited food, stopping the tubers from expanding fully.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato shishifãi lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ gɔji lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra suckers pull water and nutrients away from the main mother stem. Leaving just one or two strong follow-up shoots ensures the main plant gets enough energy to bear a large bunch of fruit.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise pruning the lower leaves of tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afolɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Removing low leaves prevents diseases from splashing up from the soil and directs the plant's food supply toward growing healthy flowers and fruit rather than extra foliage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai ni fa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize turning yellow early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage after heavy rain. The plant moves nutrients from its older leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face heat stress, erratic rainfall, or a lack of soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to save its strength until growing conditions improve.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni bɛ faŋŋ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but yield tiny stems underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the plant to spend all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of storing food into thick root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli tse mli.

english: Why do crops in one corner of my farm mature faster than those in another area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ koŋ kome mli lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil depth, moisture retention, and shade levels naturally vary across a field. Crops growing in richer, wetter soil take longer to mature, while plants in drier spots may mature faster due to mild stress.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ mli Kɛ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa nɔ lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ adara oya yɛ nɔnyɛɛ fioo hewɔ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on my land after I finish harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize pulls a lot of food out of the soil, but plants like beans and groundnuts actually take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally refreshing your soil for the next farming season.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, shi tsei tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to cover the bare dirt around my vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi yaa nɔ amɛkɛɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ awo mli lɛ? Aduawai ni jwɛi loo baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the dirt, keeps water in the soil much longer, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my small farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli hu?

english: If seeds are planted too close together, the crops will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves you with weak, skinny stalks and very small harvests instead of big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe ejɔ, kɛ yibiiwoo fioo ko pɛ. Mohu ɔ, o náa yiblii nguahi nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do I have to make big soil mounds to plant yam seeds instead of planting them on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee muji agbo ko ni akɛdu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large and long under the ground, so they need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to expand easily. High mounds keep the roots from getting flooded with water and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ebiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaho ni amɛkafite.

english: Why are there tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to feed on the tender inner leaves of young maize. Finding them early and treating them with approved sprays or local methods keeps them from destroying the center of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa bibii bibii. Amɛtaomɔ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsa amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite tso lɛ mli fã lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by too much heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into tomato fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ babaoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi ni baatsɔ tomato aduawai lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava underground roots are mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is it better to sow my seeds right after the first heavy rain instead of planting in dry soil before rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to wake up and germinate. Planting in dry dirt risks the seeds sitting in hot soil too long, where insects or birds can eat them or they can spoil before the rain comes.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ woɔ oshara mli. ni kooloi bibii loo okpoi baanyɛ aye loo ebaanyɛ egbo dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants grow strong and green. Adding fertilizers like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the food the maize needs to recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it true that planting beans improves the soil for my next crop?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, beans and other legumes capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest the beans and let the root residues decompose, it leaves natural plant food in the soil for crops like maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi. Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji okpa ŋmeii ni oha shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ fite lɛ, Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa tsei tamɔ ŋmei.

english: How do I know the right direction to stick cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale gbɛ ni ja ni esa akɛ atsɔ nɔ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look at the small buds or leaf scars on the stem cutting—they should point upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down makes it very difficult for the cassava to sprout roots and produce good tubers.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo baai ahe ŋmeii yɛ tsei niji ni afo lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmei lɛ akɛ shishifãi baakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmei kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in the same small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds together causes overcrowding, so the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Spacing out your seeds allows each stalk to grow thick and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii agboi ni eyi obɔ lɛ aba.

english: Early morning is best because the water soaks deep into the soil before the hot sun can dry it up. Avoid watering late in the evening because leaving leaves wet overnight can encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha egbi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni oooha bo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ he ejaakɛ kɛ́ oshi baai lɛ ni efɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Yam vines need sunlight on their leaves to make food for the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and air, keeping them healthy and helping you harvest larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii aha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, soil food, and water meant for your crops. Removing weeds early removes this competition so your crops get all the food and space they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Koni oha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular soil moisture when the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost or lime helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo lime awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack water, suffer from insect attacks like mirids, or lack pollination from tiny midges. Maintaining moderate shade trees and controlling pests helps flowers stay on the tree and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids tutuaa amɛ, loo amɛbɛ pollination ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii adɛŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes or peppers on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases to build up in that exact spot. Rotating your tomatoes with crops like corn or beans starves those pests and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni eye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which acts as food for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the plants regain their deep green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ waa mli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why should I mix dried leaves and cow manure into my soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ tsina ŋmei afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani madu?

english: Mixing plant waste and manure into the soil creates organic matter, which holds moisture in the ground during dry spells and slowly releases natural nutrients to feed your crops throughout the season.
ga: Tso mli jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ baa, ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii fiofio koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special microscopic organisms on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize after cowpeas, the maize eats that leftover nitrogen and grows stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ nibii bibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa yɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ masɛi ŋmãa lɛ baaye nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: What is making ragged holes in my maize leaves with little brown dirt inside the plant's funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abele baai lɛ amli ewo muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center of the maize plant during the hottest part of the day to eat the young leaves, so spraying pest remedies early in the morning or late in the evening works best.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my vegetables grow smaller even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the nutrients, space, and water away from your vegetables. Even if you water daily, the weeds drink it up first and leave your vegetables starving.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, he ko, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ o-vegetables lɛ amli. Kɛji okɛ nu haa daa gbi po Jwɛi lɛ baanu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ni ebaaha hɔmɔ aye o-vegetables lɛ.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to spray weedkiller when there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Wind carries the fine liquid spray away from the weeds and blows it onto your good crops or your neighbor's farm, which can damage or kill plants you didn't mean to spray.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai loo okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite loo egbe tsei ni okɛ ohe wooo mli akɛ obaashwie nɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the air cool and the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants get uneven amounts of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves high up to catch light and prevents damp soil diseases from damaging the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Akɛ baai lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni la abote mli ni helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature enough to dig up from underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the dry ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni egbi ni ebɔle lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: If my farmland has very fertile soil, why do I still need to worry about how close I plant my seeds?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahao lolo yɛ bɔ ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ mabɛŋkɛ he lɛ he?

english: Even the most fertile soil has a limited amount of nutrients, water, and sunlight to give. If crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for these resources, which leads to weak plants and small yields despite the rich soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa lɛ po nine shɛɛɛ niyenii kpakpai, nu, kɛ hulu la fioo ko nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaawuu amɛha nibii nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I calculate the right number of plants to put on my one acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tsei ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ adu yɛ acre 1 nɔ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You calculate plant population by measuring the space between your planting rows and the distance between plants within each row. Following recommended spacing for your crop ensures you reach the target plant count needed for maximum yield without overcrowding.
ga: Obuɔ tsei ayibɔ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ kɛ jɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ateŋ lɛ susumɔ nɔ. Kɛji onyiɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ okɛto odumɔi lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha oshɛ tsei ayibɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni he hiaa koni aná yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ he ni mɛi babaoo akafee nɔ ko fe nine.

english: What will actually happen to my crops if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems, higher risk of fungal diseases due to poor airflow, and small or poorly filled fruits and ears.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Oshara ni yɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. ni aduawai kɛ toi lɛ ji bibii loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to plan my plant population before I buy seeds for the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mato tsei ayibɔ he gbɛjianɔ dani mahe dumɔwui kɛha be lɛ?

english: Planning your plant population beforehand helps you buy the exact amount of seed and fertilizer you need, avoiding wasted money while ensuring your land is fully utilized for the best possible harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oto tsei ayibɔ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shika ni baafite lɛ he Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: If I put three or four seeds in one planting hole, will I get more harvest from that spot?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ wo dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ, Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ jɛmɛ?

english: No, putting too many seeds in one hole creates severe root competition in that exact spot. The plants will starve each other of food and water, producing small, poor-quality crops compared to planting the recommended number of seeds per hole.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa nakai he lɛ. Tsei yeɔ amɛhe hɔmɔ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu yɛ bu kome mli lɛ he.

english: Why do the crops growing at the edges of my farm look bigger and healthier than the ones in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Plants at the edge of your field get extra sunlight from the open sides and have less competition for root space and nutrients than plants crowded in the center of the field.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaná hulu la kroko kɛjɛ he ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ. Ni akaŋshii fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛha shishifãi ahe he kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fe tsei ni ebua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and slender, but producing small ears?
