ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛyɛ toi bibii lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they stretch upward to reach sunlight instead of growing thick, strong stems. This energy waste leaves less strength for the plant to develop big, heavy ears or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e he wa. Hewalɛ ni laajeɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee toi wuji ni tsii loo aduawai.

english: How does proper crop spacing help my farm survive when the rains are poor?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehi shi beni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced correctly, each plant's roots have a larger area of soil to draw moisture from. If plants are crowded, they drink up the limited soil moisture very quickly and dry out faster during dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei lɛ, ha amɛteŋ gbɛ ni sa. Tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni da ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ mli. Kɛji tsei lɛ fa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu fioo lɛ oya ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What simple tool can I use to make sure my planting rows are straight and properly spaced?
ga: Mikɛ dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tsuɔ nii. Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni midumɔ ŋmɔji lɛ afee ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: You can use a long rope marked with knots or colored rags at the recommended planting distances, stretched tightly between two wooden pegs, to guide you in planting straight, evenly spaced rows.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kpã kakadaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmei loo tsɔji ni yɔɔ kɔla yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ lɛ yɛ tsei enyɔ ateŋ koni etsɔɔ bo gbɛ yɛ dumɔ ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Will planting fewer crops on my land automatically mean I will get a smaller harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ?

english: Not necessarily. If you plant below the recommended number, you underuse your land, but if you hit the correct target count, fewer healthy plants with big yields can produce more total grain than a crowded field of weak plants.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji odu nɔ ni shɛɛɛ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ okɛtsuɔ nii. Shi kɛji onine shɛ otii ni ja lɛ anɔ Tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baawo dumɔwui muu babaoo fe tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and small corn cobs instead of a bountiful yield.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaawo ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Yam plants need their leaves exposed to sunlight to make food. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum light and prevents diseases from spreading off the damp soil, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la koni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. ni kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even if I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your plants. Clearing weeds ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli kɛ hiɛdɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need for healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer early helps restore their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni eha shweremɔ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making small holes in the center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ ring lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding on the tender inner leaves. Checking your fields early and applying recommended pest control can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋaa ni akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses. Controlling these small insects early stops the leaves from twisting and drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them in heavy clay soil. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can easily pull out of the ground under the weight of a heavy fruit bunch. Propping up the main stem with strong wooden forks supports the tree until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni tsii lɛ ashishi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa to tso lɛ shishitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye ebua tso lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops like maize and cassava grow better when I plant them together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ fee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting different crops together, like maize and cassava, allows them to feed at different soil depths and maximize space. Taller plants can provide light shelter for lower crops, while their roots do not directly compete for the exact same nutrients.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Enɛ haa tsei yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ srɔtoi anɔ. ni afee he ko babaoo Tsei ni kwɔlɔ baanyɛ aha tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atswa akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation during extreme heat. It is a sign that the crop is stressed for moisture and would benefit from watering or soil mulching.
ga: Abɛi baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ hewɔ, ni kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaná he sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and balanced with plant food helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũɔ be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ tsei aniyenii kpãa gbee lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need for healthy leaf growth. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up air and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and woody instead of swelling up big and starchy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛji starch lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin and woody if the soil is packed too hard, lacks organic matter, or suffers from severe drought during early root formation. Loosening the soil before planting gives the tubers space to expand.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee mlɛo ni amɛbaafee tsei kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shishijee bei ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha tuber lɛ he lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak stems and small yields, such as undersized maize cobs or tiny vegetables.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa bibii loo aduawai bibii baa.

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crops. Even with abundant rain, the weeds consume the soil nutrients before your main crop gets a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi hu yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ náa hegbɛ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do pests attack the young green shoots of my crops more than the older leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tsei bibii lɛ fe baai momo lɛ?

english: Insects target young shoots because tender leaves are easier to bite, chew, and digest. Fresh growth is also rich in water, plant sugars, and nutrients that help pests reproduce rapidly.
ga: Kplukai kwɛɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ ŋmɔmɔ, ŋmɔmɔ kɛ shwiemɔ waaa. Nu, tsei amli sugar, kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya lɛ hu yɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ ehee lɛ amli babaoo.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts signal maturity above ground when their leaves begin turning yellow and drying up. You can test a single sample plant by pulling it up; if the inside of the pod shells has turned dark brown and the seeds are firm, the crop is ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni ooogbala lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: What is soluble fertilizer, and how is it different from the regular fertilizer I spread by hand?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ daa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ minine shwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Soluble fertilizer is designed to dissolve completely in water. Unlike standard dry fertilizers that sit on top of the dirt waiting for rain, soluble fertilizer feeds your crops immediately because the nutrients are already dissolved in liquid that root systems can easily drink up.
ga: Afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ nu mli lɛ koni amɛshwie nu mli kwraa. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa ni ta shikpɔŋ ni mɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ he. Nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii baaha onibii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ etsɔ nu lɛ mli momo, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to mix certain fertilizers with water before feeding my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu afutu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Water acts as a vehicle that breaks down the fertilizer into tiny particles. Mixing it with water ensures that the plant food is evenly spread out and can penetrate deep into the root zone without burning the plant.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli bibii bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ nu futu mli lɛ, tso lɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni eshãaa tso lɛ.

english: How do my crops behave differently when I give them liquid fertilizer instead of dry grains?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ha amɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Crops respond much faster to liquid fertilizer because their roots absorb liquid instantly. You will often see leaves greening up and stems growing stronger in a shorter period compared to using solid granules.
ga: Tsei lɛ tsuɔ nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ obaana akɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu mli waa yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Do I need to wait for heavy rains before applying water-soluble fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, because water-soluble fertilizer is already mixed with water, you do not have to rely on heavy rainfall to wash the nutrients into the soil for your crops to use them.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ efutu nu mli momo. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Can I use spraying equipment or machinery to apply fertilizer to my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ loo tsɔnei awo miŋmɔji lɛ amli?

english: Yes, using specialized sprayers or farm machinery allows you to apply liquid fertilizer evenly across large fields, saving you labor and ensuring every crop gets the exact same amount of nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔ mli tsɔne tsu nii lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔji wuji amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haaa aná nitsumɔ babaoo, ni ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni falɛ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ nɔ.

english: Is using farm machinery to apply liquid fertilizer better than traditional broadcasting by hand?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ hi fe blema nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii ni akɛtswaa adafi lɛ?

english: Using machinery with liquid fertilizer is more efficient because it target-delivers the nutrients directly to the soil or leaves, reducing waste and covering a much bigger area in far less time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ oti ni ma ehiɛ ji ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya shikpɔŋ loo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anɔ ni oha he ko ni da kwraa yɛ be fioo ko mli.

english: Is it safe to spray liquid fertilizer directly onto the leaves of my plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofɔ nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tso baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, as long as the fertilizer is fully dissolved in the correct amount of water, crops can safely absorb nutrients directly through their foliage as well as their roots without damaging the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ nu ni sa lɛ mli kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: How quickly should I distribute soluble fertilizer once it arrives on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ maja ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ oya ha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ ebashɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to distribute and apply soluble fertilizer promptly so that the dissolved chemical balance stays right and your crops get the feeding boost right when they need it most.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaaja ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ nu mli lɛ awo mli oya koni tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to wash and service my machinery after applying liquid fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mitsɔnei lɛ ahe ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dissolved fertilizers contain minerals and salts that can dry up, corrode metal parts, or clog sprayer nozzles. Cleaning and servicing your machine after every application keeps the equipment working smoothly for the next use.
ga: Minerals kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ amli. Efiteɔ dade fãi Aloo spray nozzle lɛ efo. Kɛ́ otsumɔ otsɔne lɛ he ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ be ni okɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does using machinery for liquid fertilizer help me manage a larger farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ?

english: Machinery allows you to distribute fluid fertilizer rapidly across broad acres with uniform coverage, preventing some parts of your field from being under-fed or over-fed.
ga: Shishitoo lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni da waa nɔ oya. kɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa daa Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi anaa koni akaye niyenii ni fa loo fe nine.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient plant need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color and improve growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny pods on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. When planted with maize, they naturally feed the soil and help your maize grow bigger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni edara ni ehe ehiaaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and hot winds. They need gentle shade from larger trees or temporary shade crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist during their first few years in the field.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo blɛoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce tiny yields when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to absorb what it needs to produce big, healthy ears or fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ atsu nii koni ekɛfee toi wuji ni mli wa loo aduawai.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves up on stakes exposes them to more light and keeps them off the hot, wet soil where diseases can easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ naa la babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ ni helai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo

english: If leaves turn soft yellow and wilt while the soil is still wet, the plant is drowning from too much water. If the leaves curl up, feel dry, and turn brown at the tips while the soil is dusty, the plant is thirsty and needs watering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Tso lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ nu babaoo mli kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi, enu he akɛ egbi, ni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ nu.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water stays trapped around their roots for too long, encouraging fungal growth in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa fungal lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does burning all the cleared bush on my farmland hurt my soil over time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Burning destroys the top layer of rich organic matter, dead leaves, and good soil organisms that naturally feed your crops and trap moisture. Over time, burning leaves the soil dry, hard, and poor in nutrients.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. baai ni egboi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ewaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is not enough wind or insects to shake and pollinate the blossoms. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpokpo ni amɛha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni aaakwɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the funnel of young maize leaves to eat the fresh growth. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pest control directly into the leaf funnels will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ helai ni akɛwo mli lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the center of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that water is sitting around the roots and suffocating them after heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants shedding all their flowers without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo beni enine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water in heavy soil cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots, creating ideal conditions for fungal rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away quickly.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting in the barn before I am ready to sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and sprout when exposed to warmth, high humidity, and sunlight. Keeping the storage barn cool, shaded, and well-ventilated slows down early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafo shihilɛ mli ni ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo, hulutsoo be ni mli wa, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli jɔ, eyɛ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu bote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, serving as natural umbrellas that provide vital shade and moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees drying up and turning black while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, wet conditions where air cannot move freely through dense branches.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli oya.

english: What is this pink-flowered weed attached to my maize roots that makes the maize stay short and thin?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ mi-abele shishifãi ahe ni haa abele lɛ feɔ kuku ni eyɛ mlɛo nɛɛ?

english: That weed is Striga, or witchweed. Its roots attach directly to the maize roots to steal water and food, which stunts the crop before it can produce ears.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, loo abɛi hazel. Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ toi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling tightly upward and turning stiff?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that transmit a plant virus, or it can be a self-defense reaction to extreme drought and hot winds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii gbɛɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ eshwaa tomato nɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly ni ji helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ Aloo ebaanyɛ efee hebuu hetoo kɛha hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting cassava at the exact same time as maize reduce my maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmã kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Cassava grows broad leaves and wide roots that quickly outcompete maize for sunlight and soil nutrients; planting maize a few weeks before cassava gives the maize time to establish.
ga: Cassava yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni daa oya fe ŋmãa yɛ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ namɔ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa lɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ náa be ni ekɛma shi.

english: Why will my crops produce less yield if I plant seeds very close together to fit more plants in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛdu nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants are planted too close, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield bigger crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, while groundnuts and beans fix nitrogen from the air back into the ground. Rotating them restores natural fertility to your soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsɔmɔmɔ koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I mix dried animal manure into my soil instead of using only chemical fertilizer bought from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ pɛ baatsu nii?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant quickly, but animal manure feeds and improves the soil itself by helping it hold moisture longer so crops survive dry spells better.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa sũ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when rainwater settles on my field for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu shwie ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo tsɔ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like water. When excess water sits on the field and floods the soil, it chokes the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Taakɛ nu ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lɛ. baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, damp, and shady farm conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees allows sunlight to dry out the farm and prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Tsei ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ koni hulu la lɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ekɛtsi enaa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating the inside leaf shoots of my young maize plants, and why are they dangerous?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ eyɛ oshara lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They burrow into the central growing tip of the plant, which destroys the developing leaves and stops the maize plant from forming cobs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli. Enɛ fiteɔ baai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upwards and turn yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by a plant virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Whiteflies multiply rapidly in dry, warm weather and infect the plant as they feed on the leaf sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Whiteflies lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ amli. ni ebaatswa tso lɛ hela be mli ni eyeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting since they grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is mature when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ tso lɛ eda kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi gbee.

english: Why does allowing tall weeds to grow in my farm reduce my total crop harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni mihaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal essential sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving your main crops weak, stunted, and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni he hiaa Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tsei nu leebi loo oooha amɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the plants absorb moisture before the sun gets hot. Afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can burn delicate foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils when the sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce evaporation and save moisture so it can survive until it gets water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa la ni hoɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi ebaaná nu.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes during the dry season if I give them water regularly?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli daa?

english: Yes, tomatoes can thrive during the dry season if given enough water because they get plenty of uninterrupted sunlight without rain-induced fungal diseases, leading to strong growth and good harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tomato baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ jɛɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nugbɔ kɛbaa lɛ bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Ekɛ dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmaa kpakpa baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves during dry spells to lower its water demand. By shedding extra leaves, the plant conserves moisture inside its stems and roots to stay alive until water becomes available again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishigbɛ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can soak up moisture before the day's heat begins. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air before reaching the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tso lɛ nu leebi koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aje shishi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up if I clear all the tall shade trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ? shi miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants need shade trees because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out topsoil quickly before their roots are strong and deep enough to gather deep groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ mli waa ni amɛmli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbua shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing peppers when the heat gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper baaa be mli ni latsaa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to shed their blossoms to conserve energy and water rather than trying to feed developing fruits that they cannot support.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ ashwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha tso yibii ni miida ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: How does spreading dry grass on the soil around my crop plants help them grow better?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mikɛshwãa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the hot sun, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing food and water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and weak with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When planted too close, maize plants compete for sunlight, air, and soil nutrients, forcing them to stretch upward for light instead of building sturdy stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi kɛ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ anyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛmɔ kane lɛ moŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji baa.

english: Why do my groundnuts make the soil richer for my maize when I plant them in the same farm later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa mi-ŋmeii lɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots, that trapped nitrogen stays in the ground as natural plant food for crops like maize.
ga: Peanut tsei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my seeds germinate so much faster when planted right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm soil combined with fresh rain water sends a signal to the sleeping seed to break its hard outer shell and use stored energy to sprout leaves and roots quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nu fata he lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ koni amɛgbala kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛbaa kɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are still short. They require partial shade from crops like plantains to keep their leaves cool and soil moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku lolo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to support new leaves at the top.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛfi baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ asɛɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt, naturally feeding the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshɛrɛɔ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause standing water, the air gets trapped out, allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply in the wet earth.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Ha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during hot afternoons but look healthy again the next morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛ hewalɛ enɔ jetsɛremɔ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf exposure to the sun to conserve moisture.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Defoliation ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the stem before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛwoɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture shifts rapidly between dry and wet. The plant discards flowers to preserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato baashwie baai lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Removing most of them ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why is it helpful to trim overcrowded branches from my mango tree after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaafolɔ mango tsei aniji ni egbɔjɔ fe nine lɛ amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting thick or dead branches allows air and sunlight to flow through the tree canopy, which prevents humidity build-up and reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni mli tse loo ni egboi ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I grow maize on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do I see small ragged holes and sawdust-like waste inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the leaf funnel are a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the cool center leaf area to feed away from direct sunlight.
ga: Buji ni egbɛ eshwa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli koni amɛye nii yɛ he ko ni hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around their roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ awo niyenii ni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist with organic mulch and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni etsɔ chili ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant four or five corn seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and small cobs; planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing gives every plant enough resources to yield bigger cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmei agbo.

english: How can I tell if the soil is ready for me to plant my maize seeds when the rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays wet for a few inches deep after two or three heavy rains. Planting after the very first light rain is risky because the ground might dry up quickly, killing the seeds before they fully sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my corn leaves and leaving green dirt inside the plant top?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji eŋɔli yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Those ragged holes and dirt are caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the corn. Checking your farm early and spraying neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides controls them before they destroy the entire crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ buji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ muji nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishi lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ afɔ shi koni akɛkudɔ ŋmɔji dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted while the stems stop growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Curled cassava leaves are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or by planting infected stem cuttings. Using disease-free stem cuttings from healthy plants for your next planting prevents this disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Kɛ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ wɔsɛɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my maize grow better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the land first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize uses this leftover natural food to grow faster and produce better yields.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my maize plants easily fall down on the ground when there is heavy rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are too shallow or when the soil around their bases is loose. Mounding soil around the base of the stems when the plants are knee-high gives them stronger support to stand firm against rain and wind.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ etse. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛdamɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know that my corn is completely ripe and dry enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Corn is ready for harvest when the leaves around the cob turn dry and brown, the cobs point downwards, and the individual kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot easily dent them.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ Ashishifã lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, abɛi lɛ tsɔɔ shi, ni ŋmeii lɛ aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ oniji ahe ŋmeii lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: Why does my harvested cassava rot so quickly just two or three days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a thick protective skin like yams, so air enters small cuts made during harvest and starts decaying the flesh rapidly. It is best to leave cassava in the ground until you are ready to process or sell it.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ hewolo ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. ni baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli ni ebɔi loo lɛ fitemɔ oya Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaatsu he nii loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to plant my crop cuttings or seeds?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cuttings loo dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: If you bury your seeds or cuttings too deep, they will struggle to get air and light, causing them to rot underground before they can push through the soil surface.
ga: Kɛji ofu dumɔwui lɛ loo ofo mli tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baaná naagba yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ni amɛaaná lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops start rotting after heavy rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls and water sits stagnant around your plants without draining away, it starves the roots of air and causes fungi to grow, which makes the crops rot.
ga: Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni nu lɛ ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lolo ni ekɛ amɛ efɔɔɔ. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii akwɛ̃. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: What can I do on my field so that rainwater does not settle around my crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ nu akabɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: You can plant your crops on raised mounds or ridges and dig simple water drainage paths across your farm so that heavy rain easily flows away instead of soaking the roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ. ni otsa nu ni hoɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ anyɛ atsɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu.

english: What will happen if I plant crops in an area of my farm where water naturally gathers?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he ko ni nu yɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Placing crops in naturally swampy or low areas without proper ridges causes water to drown the roots, leading to weak growth and crop rot.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hei ni ŋmeii loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmeii kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni tsei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Can I plant cassava on the same piece of land where I am growing young coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava alongside young tree crops like coconut is a great way to make money and harvest food from the land while waiting several years for the coconut trees to grow big.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ahe lɛ ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa shika ni akpaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni mɛɔ afii babaoo dani ŋmei tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Will planting a short-term crop like cassava hurt my main tree crops growing beside it?
ga: Ani be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei dumɔ baaná mitso titri ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ nɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: As long as you give enough space between the cassava and the young trees, the cassava will not harm them, and harvesting it will even help loosen the soil for the trees.
ga: Shii abɔ ni obaashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ yeŋ lɛ awui. Ni ŋmaakpamɔ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How long does cassava usually stay in the ground before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa amɛ?

english: Cassava is typically a one-year crop, meaning it matures and is ready for full harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ji afi kome ŋmɔshi nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ etsɔ hiɛ kwraa ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Is it fine to harvest all my cassava from the land at the same time after one year?
ga: Yɛ afi kome sɛɛ lɛ, abaakpa ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli. Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔkɛ wɔhe abɔ?

english: Yes, harvesting all your cassava after one year allows you to fully clear the land, prevent the cassava roots from becoming woody, and make room for other crops or trees to expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okpa o-cassava lɛ fɛɛ yɛ afi kome sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onyɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa. Etsiɔ cassava shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso. Ni ehaa gbɛ hu haa ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei krokomɛi ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do tree crops like coconut take so many years before I see any harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ akutui heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛkpaa amɛnibii lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their first few years developing deep roots and thick trunks to store energy before they are strong enough to flower and produce fruits like coconuts.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli lɛ heɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ baa koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Can I plant new crops immediately on the same land after harvesting all my cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso hee yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, but since cassava absorbs a lot of nutrients from the ground over a year, it is good to add manure or compost to restore the soil before planting new crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ afi kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani adu tsei heei.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping tall shade trees or planting plantains around them creates a cool environment that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop to the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shikpɔŋ ni etsɔko ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients. Keeping damp, shady leaf litter on the farm floor helps these tiny insects live and pollinate your flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ akaboteɔ jɛmɛ. Enɛɛmɛi yɛ wala mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha ofɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, which stops the fungus from destroying your pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the unwanted shoots growing from the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni ataooo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These shoots, often called chupons or suckers, waste the tree's food and energy. Removing them allows the main tree to send strength directly to producing healthy flowers and large pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ chupon loo ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting trees too close makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin trees with very few pods. It also keeps the farm dark and damp, which makes diseases spread faster.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ duŋ ni edɔɔ hu. ni haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa plants on the same field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kookoo tsei bibii afee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cassava roots grow very wide and heavy, taking away water and nutrients that young cocoa roots need to survive. It is better to plant plantain or cocoyam instead, which share the soil better and provide good shade.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daraa waa ni amɛhe wa. Eheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kookoo shishifãi bibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ. Esa akɛ adu plantain loo ŋmei tsei moŋ. Amɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo kpakpa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves and stop flowering during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the leaves and soil. The tree naturally drops leaves to save water and protect itself from drying out until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is exhausted and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ, ni kɛji akɛ ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crop leaves look pale green or yellowish, stems grow very slowly, and pods remain small, the soil has likely run out of essential food like nitrogen and potassium and needs organic compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ daa blɛoo waa. ni ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lolo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli

english: Pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely from green to yellow, or from dark red to bright orange. Picking them at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully grown and easy to ferment.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do small insects create dark, cracked spots on my young cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiha ŋmeii diji ni egbɛ eshwa mi-kookoo niji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those spots are caused by mirids (capsids), small pests that suck the juice from young stems and pods. Clearing weeds around your trees and letting sunlight into the farm reduces where these pests hide.
ga: Mirids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Otsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni ebote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha hei ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baanyɛ ahi amɛhe yɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates living shade that keeps the seedlings cool and moist until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa shade ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava roots need enough space underground to spread out and grow fat. When planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in very thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛshwere. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller harvests every year even though I am using the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the ground each time they grow. If you plant the same crop year after year without adding manure, compost, fertilizer, or resting the land, the soil loses its strength and cannot feed the crops well.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaadara. Kɛji odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni enyɛŋ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize help or harm my main crop?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua loo ebaaye mi ŋmãa titri lɛ awui?

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas or beans helps your maize because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua o-ŋmãa Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmãa-ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the real rainy season begins. Seeds that sprout after the first rain will dry up and die if no more rain falls in the following weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ dɔŋŋ yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are holes in my pepper leaves bad if the pepper fruits themselves look fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ ehiii kɛji akɛ pepper yibii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves are the plant's food factory that convert sunlight into energy. When insects destroy the leaves, the plant becomes weak and stops producing new fruits or drops the fruits it already has.
ga: Baai ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhei ni tsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi bibii fite baai lɛ Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ekpa aduawai heei ni ewoɔ lɛ loo ebaaha aduawai ni yɔɔ momo lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds when my crops are still small and the weeds aren't very tall yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ni jwɛi lɛ hu eshɛɛɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Small weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your crop needs to establish strong roots early on.
ga: Jwɛi bibii lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa mra.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during the peak hot season without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and high heat cause severe stress to tomato plants, drying up the flower pollen so fruit cannot form. Placing mulch on the soil keeps the roots cool and helps save the flowers.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ni aduawai nyɛŋ afee. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow and brown while the top stays light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen. The maize is pulling remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth on top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Abɛi lɛ miigbala nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know that my yams are fully mature under the soil without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛtsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yam plants tell you they are ready when the leaves and vines on top start turning yellow and drying up naturally, showing that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its food in the tuber below.
ga: O sweet potato tso lɛ kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni baai kɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ miito shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out root moisture; planting temporary shade crops like plantains beside them protects them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cowpeas survive dry weather so much better than my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi-cabbage tsei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have deep root systems adapted for dry conditions, whereas cabbage has shallow roots and compact leaves that trap water, making it vulnerable to heat stress and moisture rot.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Yɛ be mli ni cabbage yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa ni kɛ nu toɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ mlɛo kɛha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli fitemɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow during dry spells in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize turns yellow when water is scarce because the roots cannot absorb nitrogen from dry soil, which is the key nutrient responsible for keeping leaves green and healthy.
ga: Abele tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nu faaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa lɛ

english: Is it helpful for my farm if I plant beans together with my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very beneficial because beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil, acting as a natural food source for the maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do my yams turn out very small when I plant them on flat soil instead of making mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee gɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require soft, loose soil to expand; building soil mounds gives the roots space, aeration, and drainage needed to produce large, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi ni mli wa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is typically caused by tiny pests like whiteflies transmitting plant viruses, or by stress from sudden temperature changes and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo tsakemɔi trukaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa lɛ mli.

english: What makes the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, extreme drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow cassava without synthetic chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmei tsuuu nii?

english: If your field easily grows thick, dark green weeds and natural vegetation, it usually indicates rich soil with sufficient natural nutrients to support cassava growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ daa mlɛo kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmei dalɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can replant saved seeds, commercial hybrid seeds lose their strength after one season, leading to uneven growth and lower yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ moŋ, Shi jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ he waaa yɛ be kome sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell when my plantains are ready to harvest so they do not rot on the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-plantains lɛ eshɛ he koni amɛkafite?

english: Plantain bunches are ready to harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp cornered ridges, become plump and rounded, and the dried flower tips easily break off.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fite etsitsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbala oya

english: How many cocoa seedlings can my family realistically plant and care for in a year?
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui enyiɛ miweku lɛ baanyɛ adu ni amɛkwɛ nɔ yɛ afi kome mli?

english: A single household can typically only manage around 1,000 trees per year effectively. Taking on too many seedlings at once leads to neglected plants because routine care like weeding, watering, and pruning requires significant daily labor.
ga: Shia kome pɛ baanyɛ akwɛ tsei aaafee 1,000 pɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa afi. Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ haa akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ jɛɔ kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, nu ni akɛhaa kɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ebiɔ nitsumɔ babaoo daa gbi.

english: Why do some trees on my farm yield far more pods than neighboring trees of the same age?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni amɛye afii kome lɛ?

english: Crop yield naturally varies from plant to plant based on minor differences in soil nutrients, shade, and root strength. Even under similar conditions, some trees might produce 15 to 17 pods per harvest, while others average closer to 8 or 10.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli. Edamɔ srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, hulutsoo kɛ shishifãi ahewalɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ mli po lɛ Tsei komɛi baanyɛ awo ŋmeii 15 kɛyashi 17 yɛ kpamɔ kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ ŋmeii 8 loo 10 kɛ aja mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How does planting plantains help reduce the work I spend on weeding?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantain ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie jwɛi lɛ aba shi?

english: Plantain leaves cast heavy shade on the ground, which blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds. This naturally slows down weed growth, reducing the physical labor needed to keep the farm clean.
