ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand. When planted too close, the crops compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small tubers across the entire crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my maize leaves to turn yellow during the growing period?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or poor drainage around the roots. Healthy green foliage requires balanced soil nutrients and proper field drainage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ehiii. Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔ mli nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers during water stress as a survival reaction to save internal moisture. Without sufficient water, the plant halts fruit production until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nu mli haomɔ be mli akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo koni amɛkwɛ emli fɛ̃i nɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa yibiiwoo kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees drop many of their flowers before any nuts form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally drop surplus flowers that they do not have enough water or nutrients to turn into nuts, though pest attacks or dry winds can also cause excessive flower fall.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cashew tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛtsɔ ŋmeii. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite fe nine moŋ.

english: Why does my oil palm take several years before it starts producing good fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi aduawai kpakpai akui ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees focus their early energy on building strong roots and thick trunks. Attempting to force early fruiting weakens the tree, whereas waiting allows it to support heavy fruit bunches later on.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ amamɔ nɔ. Mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni anyɛ enɔ koni ewo yibii mra lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How much manual pollination or pruning work can one farm hand finish in a day?
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo nine ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ falɛ enyiɛ ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ afee yɛ gbi kome mli?

english: Delicate crop tasks depend on worker speed, with individuals typically managing between 8 to 17 plants per hour, averaging around 10. Planning field work around these realistic limits prevents crop damage from rushed work.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni he hiaa waa lɛ damɔ nitsulɔ lɛ oyaiyeli nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, mɔ fɛɛ mɔ tsuɔ tsei 8 kɛyashi 17 he nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome mli. kɛ aja mli lɛ, tsei aaafee 10 yɔɔ mli. Gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ he yɛ husui ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ nɛɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ oyaiyeli nitsumɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: How can I get improved seed yam varieties from government agriculture officers to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sweet potato henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ mimaŋ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Government extension officers (MOFA) regularly supply certified, high-yielding yam varieties to local farmer groups and agricultural offices to help farmers grow healthier crops and get better harvests.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ (MOFA) kɛ sweet potato henɔi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi akui kɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ daa. Koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some new yam varieties grow much bigger tubers than the traditional ones I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato henɔi heei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa fe blema henɔi ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: New yam varieties are specially bred to use soil nutrients and rainfall more efficiently, allowing the plant to store more energy and build larger, heavier tubers.
ga: Afee sweet potato henɔi heei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ. ni ebɔ yitso ni da ni tsii

english: Can I eat part of my harvested yams and still use the rest as seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ maye ŋmeii ni akpa fã ko ni mikɛtsu nii lolo akɛ dumɔwui kɛha ŋmeii ni yaa hiɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can eat the middle and bottom parts of a healthy yam tuber and plant the head section (seed sett) to grow a new yam plant for the next season.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oye sweet potato tuber lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ shishi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ bulbs (dumɔwui akui) lɛ koni okɛdu sweet potato tsei heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to know the exact name of the yam variety I am growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni male sweet potato henɔi ni miduɔ lɛ agbɛi pɔtɛɛ lɛ?

english: Knowing the variety name helps you understand how long it takes to mature, what weather conditions suit it best, and whether market traders prefer buying that specific type.
ga: Kɛ́ ole tso lɛ gbɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onuɔ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ shishi. Mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ? Ni ani jarayelɔi miisumɔ ni amɛhe nakai nɔ̃ lɛ loo amɛsumɔɔɔ?

english: Will a yam variety that grows well in forest areas perform just as well in drier grassland areas?
ga: Ani sweet potato henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni jwɛi egbi yɛ lɛ?

english: Not always; varieties like 'sare' types are specifically selected to withstand drier, hotter grassland conditions, whereas forest varieties need higher moisture and shade.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be; Ahala tsei srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Sari’ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ kooloi alɛɛhei ni mli egbi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni koo mli kooloi lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo.

english: What makes 'Pona' yam so popular in Ghanaian markets compared to other yam types?
ga: Mɛni haa ‘Pona’ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he gbɛi waa yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔtɔ henɔi krokomɛi ahe?

english: Pona yam is highly soft and sweet when boiled, cooks very quickly, and commands higher prices in town markets because consumers prefer its taste and texture.
ga: Pona yam lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa kɛ́ ahoo lɛ, ehooɔ oya waa ni efãa jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ maŋtiase jarayeli hei ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ sumɔɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ.

english: How do I know when a harvested yam tuber is ready to sprout and grow after resting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛdara beni mikɛ mihe ejɔ amɛhe yɛ nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam tubers undergo a natural sleeping period called dormancy; once small white buds or green shoots appear on the head of the tuber in the barn, it is ready to be planted.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Kɛji ŋmeii yɛŋ loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je kpo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ abaadu.

english: Is it better to plant a new yam variety in a separate field or mix it with my old local varieties?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu sweet potato henɔ hee yɛ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ loo mikɛ mimaŋ tso momo lɛ afutu mli?

english: It is best to plant new varieties in a separate plot so you can track how well they perform, manage their unique care needs, and easily collect pure seed yams at harvest.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu srɔtoi heei yɛ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ srɔtoi anɔ. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ amɛhaa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ekwɛmɔ he hiamɔ nii krɛdɛɛi lɛ anɔ Ni abaanyɛ akɛ sweet potatoes ni ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ lɛ ato mlɛo kɛji akpa.

english: Why do yam leaves need tall stakes or sticks to climb on during the growing period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji loo niji koni amɛkwɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently, while keeping the leaves off the wet ground prevents disease and leaf rot.
ga: Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai kɛ baai lɛ akafite.

english: How long does a newly planted yam usually stay in the ground before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmeii ni adu ehee lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Most yam varieties mature between six to nine months after planting, signaling harvest time when the leafy vines turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Sweet potatoes babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi nɛɛhu mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ kpamɔ be beni wain tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and thin roots that cannot hold much water. Direct, harsh sunlight causes them to lose water quickly and burn, which is why they need shade crops like plantains to protect them while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nu afo amɛmli oya ni amɛshã. Nɔ ni haa ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is proper spacing between my cocoa trees important when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ateŋ lɛ he hiaa beni miduɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for food and water in the soil. Their branches will also block air and sunlight, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Eniji lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are suffering from Black Pod disease when I inspect my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ black pod hela? Beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Black Pod disease starts as small brown spots on the pod that quickly spread until the entire pod turns dark black and rots. It spreads fast in wet, damp conditions, especially if there is too much shade or poor airflow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛyashiɔ ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they do not get pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or if the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil, or insect attacks. Keeping the farm healthy helps the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli, loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal water and nutrients from the main trunk. Removing them helps the tree direct all its energy into producing strong branches, flowers, and large cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers loo chupons lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa tsei niji, fɔfɔii, kɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: How does clearing weeds around my crops help them produce more yield?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, fertilizer, and water. Clearing weeds regularly ensures your crop gets all the nourishment it needs while removing hiding places for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: It is best to avoid planting cassava close to young cocoa because cassava roots grow aggressively and take away essential water and nutrients from the soil, which starves the young cocoa plants.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hia kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo tsei bibii.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need fertilizer or extra soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ mli nibii krokomɛi afata he?

english: When cocoa trees lack nutrients, their leaves often turn yellowish instead of dark green, and the trees stop producing new flowers or healthy pods. Applying the right crop fertilizer restores leaf color and pod growth.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ baakpa fɔfɔi heei loo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do insects like mirids attack my cocoa shoots mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mirid lɛ tutuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mirids (akate) love the soft, tender new shoots and young pods that sprout heavily during the rainy season. They suck the sap from these fresh parts, causing dark wounds and killing young growth.
ga: Mirid (Agate) sumɔɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ fãi heei nɛɛ amli lɛ. Ekɛ pilamɔi diji baa ni efiteɔ gbekɛbii bibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Green pods are unripe, which means the beans inside have not fully developed their natural sweet pulp or flavor. Unripe beans will not ferment correctly, leading to poor-quality cocoa that buyers will reject.
ga: Pods eŋɔli lɛ eshɛko lolo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ lolo. Beans ni ahoko lɛ shwieŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kpooɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ebaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so when it runs out, the plant pulls nutrients from its lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: When cowpeas receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the plant focuses all its energy on growing leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas need less nitrogen because they naturally capture it from the air, so excess nutrients stop them from fruiting properly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo ŋmei babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Cowpeas biɔ nitrogen fioo ejaakɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their flowers before producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their blossoms when they suffer from water stress or extreme heat. They also drop flowers if there are not enough tiny insects called midges in the soil leaf litter to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nu he haomɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa kpe amɛ. Amɛjieɔ fɔfɔii hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ bɛ baa lɛ mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Hot afternoon weather causes pepper plants to lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water from the soil. The plant wilts to protect itself from drying out, but usually bounces back once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my plantain crop take much longer to produce fruit when grown under big tree shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need plenty of direct sunshine to generate energy for fast growth. Heavy canopy shade slows down the plant's food-making process, causing it to take many extra months to flower and mature fruit.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha amɛdalɛ oya. Kpojiemɔ ni tsii haa tso lɛ niyenii ni efeɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa eheɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi kwraa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome mli Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and small when planted in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are soft storage roots that need loose, soft soil to push downward easily. Hard or compact soil blocks their natural growth path, forcing the tubers to become stunted or bend sideways into awkward shapes.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shishifãi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ bɔdɔɔ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛkuɔ amɛhe kɛyaa afã kɛyaa he ko ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: Why do fall armyworms always attack the young leaves right in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms target the central whorl of young maize plants because those internal leaves are soft, tender, and easy to chew. Hiding deep inside the center also protects the caterpillars from sunlight and natural predators.
ga: Fallworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ ŋmei lɛ tee teŋgbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ hu buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop spots during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl during dry spells to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, which keeps moisture inside the plant. Dry weather also encourages spider mites to feed on the underside of leaves, causing tiny spots.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hu woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛye baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa

english: How do weeds growing close to my tomato plants stop them from growing big?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crop plants and steal water, root space, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. They can also block air movement around tomato leaves, creating damp conditions that attract diseases.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakwɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tomato baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu naa, ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa helai baa.

english: What should I do if heavy rains cause water to pool and flood around the stems of my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shi ni ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Excess standing water smothers plant roots by removing air from the soil, causing root rot. Digging simple drainage channels or gutters between your crop beds allows surplus water to safely flow away from your plants.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Nu homɔ gbɛ loo gutter ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaafo. O tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: How can I stop heavy rainwater from washing away my seeds and soil on sloping land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekajie dumɔwui kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Planting across the slope in ridges (contour farming) slows down running water, giving it time to sink into the soil to feed crop roots rather than washing your topsoil and seeds away.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ (Curved farming) lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei shishifãi lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e shwieɔ zugba nɛ ngɛ yi mi ɔ kɛ duwu ɔmɛ a nɔ.

english: Planting in straight lines ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, space, and nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also leaves clear paths for you to walk, weed, and harvest without damaging crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Gbɛ ko hu yɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ, okɛ jwɛi atsu nii ni okpa nibii ni okɛfiteee onibii lɛ.

english: How does proper spacing between my crop rows help protect plants from diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe?

english: Leaving clean, measured spaces between rows allows breeze and sunlight to dry wet leaves quickly after rain. Dry plants make it much harder for destructive fungal diseases and mildews to spread.
ga: He ko ni he tse, ni asusu he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la haa baai ni efɔ lɛ agbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Tsei ni egbi lɛ haa ewaa kwraa akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baagbɛ ashwã.

english: Will walking and stepping on the soil close to my young seedlings hurt how they grow?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni minyiɛɔ yɛ midumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaná amɛdalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Yes, heavy footsteps press the soil tight and pack it down (soil compaction). Hard soil makes it difficult for delicate roots to spread out and stops rainwater from soaking down to the root zone.
ga: Hɛɛ, naji ni tsii nyɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa ekpɛɔ shi. (shikpɔŋ ni mli wa) Shikpɔŋ ni wa haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni ehaaa nugbɔ nu abote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and look weak when the soil around them becomes hard and packed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Compacted soil suffocates plant roots by cutting off oxygen and preventing roots from absorbing fertilizer and nutrients. Gently loosening the topsoil with a hoe allows the roots to breathe and absorb food again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Okɛ ŋmei atse shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it dangerous to let people walk freely through my plant nursery area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã gbɔmɛi anyiɛ he ni mifɔɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Young nursery plants have very fragile roots and stems that snap easily underfoot. Restricting entry prevents plants from being trampled and stops people from bringing soil diseases on their shoes into the nursery.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni waaa kwraa ni fãa oya yɛ naji ashishi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni atsiɔ naa lɛ haaa akanyiɛ tsei anɔ, ni ehaaa gbɔmɛi kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa amɛ tokotai anɔ lɛ aba tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ.

english: What should I do if I find tiny insect eggs hidden under the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina kooloi bibii bibii? Akɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ashishi?

english: Clusters of tiny eggs under leaves are usually laid by pests like caterpillars or armyworms. Destroying those leaves or spraying early breaks the pest life cycle before the eggs hatch and eat your whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ji mɛi ni woɔ fɔmɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Kpata nakai baai lɛ ahiɛ loo okɛ tsofa afɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I cut open or break growing crop pods while they are still attached to the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ loo mifoɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: Opening growing pods breaches the plant's natural protective shell, exposing the soft fruit inside to insects, moisture, and fungal rot that destroys the crop before harvest.
ga: Pod ni miida lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ kuɔ tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu mli. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa ŋmeii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Can I just wash insect eggs off my crop leaves with plain water when I see them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu afɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ ahe kɛ mina amɛ?

english: Insects produce a strong natural glue to attach their eggs firmly to leaves, so plain water rarely washes them away. You need to pick off affected leaves or use targeted neem oil sprays to safely remove them.
ga: Kplukai feɔ adebɔɔ mli glu ni mli wa ni amɛkɛkpɛtɛɔ wɔji ahe yɛ baai ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, nu shwieee ŋmeii lɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ loo okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛjie amɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly even though I am using the traditional farming methods my ancestors used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ blema okwaayeli gbɛi ni miblematsɛmɛi lɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Over many years, continuous farming without resting the land removes natural nutrients from the soil. While the land was naturally rich in ancestral times, repeated farming has depleted those nutrients, meaning crops now need extra soil enrichment like fertilizer to yield well.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii yɛ wɔblematsɛmɛi lɛ abeaŋ moŋ, shi okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ eha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ elaaje Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves turning yellow means the plant needs fertilizer or just water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmãa loo nu kɛkɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of the bottom leaves and moves up usually means the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer, whereas leaves that wilt, curl, and turn dry across the whole plant indicate a lack of water.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen fertilizer bɛ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava sticks very close to each other if I want a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he kroko kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and space to develop large roots and healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa baa.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly away from your crops, leaving your main crops starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yitsoŋ wa, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my vegetable crops more heavily during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-vegetables lɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects seek out fresh, green plants for moisture when surrounding wild vegetation dries up, and the warm dry weather helps insect populations hatch and multiply much faster.
ga: Kplukai kwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ amli koni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ kɛji koo mli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi, ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi ayibɔ ni amɛfɔɔ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: Why should I trim off some of the leaves and extra shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming extra branches helps the tomato plant focus its food and energy into growing larger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on growing unnecessary foliage.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tomato tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii kɛ ehewalɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between using animal manure and using chemical bag fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ kooloi aŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ teŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the overall soil texture and feeds the plant slowly over time, while chemical bag fertilizer gives plants a fast, direct boost of specific concentrated nutrients.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii fiofio. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ oya ni tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I put in the ground fail to sprout while others grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are old or damaged, buried too deep in the soil, or if the soil is either too dry or completely soaked in standing water.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji amɛgbɔ loo amɛfite. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi ewo mli.

english: How can I test if my saved maize seeds are still good for planting before I take them to the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii dani mikɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can do a simple wet cloth test: roll 10 seeds inside a damp piece of cloth for about four to five days. If at least 8 of them sprout strong shoots, your seed lot is healthy and ready to plant in your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee mama ni mli efɔ kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, tsei 8 kwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eheɔ aaafee gbii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crop seeds taking so many days to sprout after I planted them in the dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ gbii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds go into a resting state when there isn't enough moisture in the soil. Without sufficient water and warmth to wake the seed up, germination slows down or stops completely.
ga: Dumɔwui boteɔ wɔɔhe mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Kɛji nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ atswa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Ekwɛ̃mɔ baa shi loo ebaakpa kwraa.

english: How do I keep my stored bean seeds from sprouting or spoiling early before the next farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ loo efite dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Seeds need to be dried completely until hard and stored in sealed, airtight containers in a cool, dark room. Keeping moisture away prevents the seeds from waking up or rotting before planting time.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛhe wa ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Kɛ́ aha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkate shi loo amɛkafite dani dumɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How can I check if my cassava tubers are big enough without destroying the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni efiteee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can practice sample harvesting by gently digging away the topsoil around the base of one plant with a small stick to feel or inspect the tuber size, then carefully covering the roots back up if they need more time.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ anaabuamɔ akase nii fiofio. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ. Akɛ tso bibioo ko jie tso kome shishi. Bɔni afee ni onu he loo okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha lɛ, no lɛ, ha shishifãi lɛ ahe blɛoo kɛku sɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛji akɛ be babaoo he miihia.

english: How do I know if my cocoa pods are fully mature and ready to pick without cutting them open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie amɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color distinctly—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or dark pods turn orange-yellow—and they produce a hollow sound when you tap them gently with your knuckles.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su jogbaŋŋ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔtɔ tsuru loo ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Ni amɛfeɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa amɛ fioo.

english: What happens if I leave my yam tubers inside the soil for too long after the vines have dried up?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature tubers in hot, dry soil for too long makes them lose moisture and shrink. It also exposes them to soil pests like termites and beetles that can damage the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu ahi mli ni ebaagbɔjɔ. Ehaa amɛyaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ dani akpa amɛ lɛ hu anɔ.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients stress the plant, causing it to shed its flowers prematurely before pollination can happen.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni esaaa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani pollination baa.

english: Why is my cocoa tree producing only one or two pods this season instead of full clusters?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli moŋ fe ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Low pod production usually happens when the tree lacks nutrients, receives too much heavy shade from big trees, or suffered pest damage to its flowers during the blooming stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pod ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enaa hulutsoo babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei wuji amli loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli

english: Why do my pepper plants stop producing new leaves and fruits after a few months of harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai kɛ aduawai heei feemɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop plants naturally slow down their growth after heavy fruiting periods or when dry weather sets in to conserve energy, unless they receive extra nutrients and proper pruning.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ yibiiwoo be ni mli wa sɛɛ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ba koni akɛto hewalɛ he. ja aha lɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa

english: Why are crops on one side of my farm growing tall while the ones on the other side stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ shwereɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ mli lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ kuku lɛ?

english: Uneven crop growth across the same field is often caused by differences in soil fertility, uneven water flow, or shade from nearby trees blocking sunlight on one section of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsei ni edaaa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baa. nu ni hoɔ ni ejaaa loo hulutsoo ni jɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli lɛ.

english: When my maize grows taller than my sprinkler pipes, do I need to raise the pipes higher?
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ da fe paipi ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ Ani esa akɛ mawo paipi lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yes, you should raise your sprinkler pipes as crops grow taller. If the plants are higher than the nozzles, the leaves will block the water from spreading, leaving parts of your field dry.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ owó nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ nɔ kwɔ fe nozzle lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa hei ni oyɔɔ lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is a 360-degree rotating sprinkler good for my newly planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ ni tsɔɔ 360 degree lɛ hi kɛha tsei ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: A 360-degree sprinkler distributes water evenly in a wide circle, mimicking light rain. This soft, equal spray waters tender young crops without washing away the seedbed or damaging fragile shoots.
ga: 360 degree sprinkler lɛ jaa nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni mli kwɔ mli. Mimics light rain Nɛkɛ nu ni yɔɔ blɛoo, ni po shwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ efɔɔɔ dumɔwui ashishi loo efiteee tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Why are some of the crops on one side of my farm growing taller while the rest remain short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ kã shi lɛ?

english: Uneven growth often happens when water or fertilizer is not reaching all parts of the farm equally. Checking if your watering system or rainfall reaches every corner evenly can fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ fãi fɛɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shɛɔ he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, etsuuu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Is it better to water my crops high from above or directly near the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu yɛ shishitoo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ?

english: Watering from above with a gentle spray works great for young crops and widespread coverage, but as crops get tall, make sure the water is still reaching the soil and roots rather than just sitting on leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ shi fioo. Etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ ni eha he ko ni da waa. Shi kɛ tso lɛ shwere Kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ ayashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lolo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohi baai lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ

english: My maize is growing very tall, does that automatically mean I will get a large harvest?
ga: Mi ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ waa. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ maná nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mihe?

english: Not always. Extremely tall maize can sometimes have thin stalks that fall over easily in strong winds. Healthy crops need a good balance of stalk strength, leafy growth, and heavy grain formation.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ waa lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he miihia ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ adalɛ kɛ ŋmaa ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize suddenly start growing very fast in height after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ bɔi dalɛ oya trukaa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once a maize plant builds a strong root system in its early weeks, it enters a rapid growth stage where it absorbs nutrients quickly to shoot upward before producing cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Ebaabote ŋmãa ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ mli. Amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya koni amɛya ŋwɛi dani amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: How do strong winds affect tall maize plants when the soil is wet?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ?

english: When the soil is very wet and soft, tall heavy maize plants can easily be blown over by strong winds because their roots lose firm grip in the mud. Planting at the right depth helps prevent this.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa ŋmã tsei ni kɛlɛ ni tsii lɛ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ muji lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How can I make sure liquid chemicals reach the tops of my tall crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai ni ji nu lɛ baashɛ mitsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ayiteŋ?

english: You can raise your sprayer system on stands or use long extension wands on backpack sprayers so the spray droplets can reach over the top leaves evenly.
ga: Obaanyɛ owó o-spray system lɛ nɔ yɛ shidaamɔhe ko nɔ loo okɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agbo ni akɛ backpack sprayer tsuɔ nii koni spray lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can spraying farm chemicals through my irrigation pipes damage the equipment over time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ mi nu paipii lɛ anɔ lɛ baafite nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Certain chemicals can cause corrosion or clog sprinkler nozzles if left inside. Flushing the pipes with clean water right after spraying will protect your system from damage.
ga: Tsofai komɛi baanyɛ afite loo amɛtsi sprinkler yitsei lɛ anaa kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ paipii lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ogbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Will spraying chemicals near young, newly sprouting crops harm them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe lɛ baaye amɛ awui?

english: Young crops are very delicate. Strong chemicals or herbicides can burn their tender leaves unless you use crop-safe products or direct the spray away from the young plants.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Tsofai loo tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ. No ji ja okɛ nɔ ko ni nyɛɔ efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii loo okɛshwie dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up from the tip while the upper leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong. When the soil runs low on nitrogen, the plant takes whatever food it has left and sends it to the growing leaves at the top, leaving the older leaves at the bottom to turn yellow and die early.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ heɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ baai ni miida yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Shi baai ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi oya.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend that I plant groundnuts or beans on my land before I plant corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of crops called legumes. Their roots work with friendly soil organisms to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, acting like a natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like corn.
ga: Ajara ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mli akɛ ŋmei. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but when I harvest, the tubers underground are tiny and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ, ani amɛji bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: When cassava gets too much water or excess nitrogen early on, it spends all its energy growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing reserve food underground to form fat cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei nine shɛ nu babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo nɔ mra Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee ŋmei shishifãi ni eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on to give me a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni eha mi ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves into the air so they can catch maximum sunlight, stay clean, and avoid diseases living on the damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ha ohe atse ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ helai ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over and die after producing just one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gboɔ beni ewo aduawai akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A single plantain trunk is built to flower and fruit only once in its life. Once the bunch ripens, that main trunk naturally dies so that the young shoots, or suckers, growing around its base can take over and produce the next crop.
ga: Abɔ plantain kome pɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ shwere lɛ Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ The cones lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni amɛya nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Rolling up leaves is the maize plant's way of protecting itself from heat. By curling into tight tubes, the leaves hide from the strong sun and reduce water loss, helping the plant stay alive during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he. Kɛtsɔ lɛ ni oootsɔ mli ewo tsɔne ni mli wa mli lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baate shi kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ebaaha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air put excessive stress on pepper plants. To protect themselves from drying out completely, the plants drop their delicate flowers until cooler temperatures return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni fe nine baa pepper tsei anɔ. Koni okɛbu ohe he koni okagbi kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shiɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn dark brown, rot, and smell bad during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous rainfall cause a fungal disease called Black Pod to thrive. Raindrops splash the fungus onto the pods, and without good air movement through pruned branches, the pods rot quickly.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod lɛ daa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plant crumpled, twisted, and covered in yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents leaves from capturing sunlight properly, leading to small roots and low yields.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly droop and die during the day even when the soil around them has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. Bad bacteria in the soil enter the roots and block the plant's water pipes, preventing water from reaching the leaves even when the soil itself is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni gbeɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛbaa. Muawai gbohii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa. Enɛ haaa nu ashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows its stem to grow thick and strong so it can feed full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee shiŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food from the soil, especially nitrogen. Rain supplies water, but if the soil lacks key nutrients, the plant cannot stay green and healthy without added fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji foomɔ kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, titri lɛ nitrogen. Nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my last harvest instead of getting new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihereɔ ni miduɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, a náa dumɔwuhi ehehi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved over multiple harvests lose their strength and are more likely to carry diseases. Certified seeds are specially bred to fight off local pests, handle dry weather better, and give you a bigger yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ kpamɔ shii abɔ mli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai aba. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from intense heat, lack of water, or too much leaves. Keeping the soil consistently damp and removing extra leaves helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo baai babaoo kpe amɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ajie baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the size of my cassava roots if they are growing on the same land?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ he kome?

english: Weeds steal the underground room, water, and food that cassava roots need to expand. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil resources free for your cassava to grow big and heavy.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ tsũi amli tsũi, nu, kɛ niyenii be mli ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii lɛ ajie amɛhe koni eha o-cassava lɛ adara ni efee mlɛo.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sun. Leaving or planting shade plants keeps the air cool and soil moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni oooshi loo odu lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural trick to protect itself and reduce water loss through its leaves when the sun is harsh. If the leaves stay curled in the evening, it means the plant needs deep watering.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni ekɛbuɔ ehe he ni ekɛbaa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ efo gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni mli kwɔ he miihia tso lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking lower branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower branches prevents food from being wasted on extra leaves and allows the plant to send all its energy to the growing fruit while letting air flow through to stop fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haaa niyenii afite yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛkpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Maize heavy-feeds on soil nutrients. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, making the land fertile again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms appear on my young maize crops right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Moths lay their eggs on tender green shoots that sprout after the first rains. Monitoring your field as soon as shoots emerge lets you catch and control the tiny caterpillars before they destroy the growing points.
ga: Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Ohe ni oyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ pɛ kɛji ŋmeii je kpo Ehaa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How can I estimate the total number of bags I will harvest from my farm before I finish the harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu baagi fɛɛ ni makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ lɛ agbe naa lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You can estimate your total yield by harvesting a small test section of your field, counting how many bags you get from that area, and multiplying it by the total size of your farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã bibioo ko ni oookpa lɛ nɔ, ni okane baagi enyiɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nakai he lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ afata he.

english: Why is it important for me to count and record how many bags of crops I harvest each day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makane ni maŋma nibii ni mikpaa kotokui enyiɛ daa gbi lɛ?

english: Recording your daily harvest helps you know your exact total yield, track whether your farm output is improving, and calculate your market profits accurately.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmala gbi fɛɛ gbi ŋmaa lɛ he saji oshwie shi lɛ, ebaaha ona ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ etee hiɛ loo etee hiɛ. ni abu sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa yɛ jarayelihe lɛ he akɔntaa pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: How do I calculate how much crop is still left in my field while I am halfway through harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa beni mishɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fã lɛ?

english: Subtract the number of bags you have harvested so far from your initial estimated yield; this shows you what is remaining so you can plan for labor and transport.
ga: Jiemɔ kotokui ayibɔ ni okpaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishijee yibiiwoo ni osusu akɛ obaakpa lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsɔɔ bo nɔ ni eshwɛ koni onyɛ oto gbɛjianɔ kɛha nitsumɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do some of my crops allow me to harvest every few days while others can only be harvested once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi haa mikpaa daa gbii fioo komɛi, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa shikome pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like pepper and okra produce flowers continuously over a season, allowing multiple harvests, while crops like maize mature all at once and are harvested in a single go.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ okra woɔ fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Ehaa anyɛɔ akpaa nii shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ be kome mli ni akpaa yɛ be kome mli.

english: How many weeks can I expect to keep harvesting from the same field before the plants stop producing?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ maya nɔ makpa nii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli dani tsei lɛ akpa yibiiwoo?

english: The harvest period depends on crop care and type; continuous crops can yield for 2 to 3 months if you give them enough water and fertilizer, after which production naturally stops.
ga: Nikpamɔ be lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahenɔi anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 kɛji oha amɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No sɛɛ lɛ, nibii afeemɔ kpaɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my farm still look full of fruit even after I have already harvested many bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ aduawai lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa baagii babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Healthy plants produce new fruit buds while older fruits are ripening, so as you pick mature crops, younger ones grow to take their place.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni egbɔ lɛ miikwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ohala tsei ni eda lɛ, fɔfɔi bibii baakwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe.

english: What causes the quantity of crops I harvest to drop every time I go back to the farm?
ga: Mɛni haa mikpamɔ lɛ falɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni maku misɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yield decreases as the crop reaches the end of its life cycle or when soil nutrients and water get depleted, which slows down new fruit formation.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ gbe amɛwala be lɛ naa loo kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ baaha aduawai heei ni afee lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: How can I tell if the crops left on my farm are fully mature and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Look for maturity signals such as changes in fruit color, pods drying up, leaves turning yellow, or the fruit reaching its full firm size.
ga: Taomɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ edara, tamɔ aduawai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ, ŋmeii ni egbiɔ, baai ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ. aloo aduawai lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ dalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do some left-over crops spoil quickly on the farm while others can stay on the stem for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu baanyɛ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water-rich crops like tomatoes rot quickly once fully ripe, while low-moisture crops like dry beans or cassava can safely remain in the field for longer periods.
ga: Tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ tomato lɛ, kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, amɛgboiɔ oya. be mli ni tsei ni hulutsoo be faaa tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbi loo ŋmeii Amɛbaanyɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe yɛ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my harvest bags feeling lighter this season even though the crop plants looked healthy in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ kotokui lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe efee mlɛo yɛ be nɛɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Irregular rain or nutrient shortage can cause crop seeds or fruits to develop smaller and hollow inside, reducing total weight despite a good visual appearance.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ afee bibii ni amɛmli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shwiili lɛ fɛɛ baa shi yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ fɛo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plant is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the season gives the maize the nutrients it needs to stay dark green and grow large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baa dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmei wuji.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the earth, enriching the soil for your next crop like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Niyenii ni ekã jɛmɛ lɛ baakã he ahi je lɛŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Curled cassava leaves are usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers helps prevent this damage and keeps your harvest large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwaafoi nitsulɔi du ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ yeɔ?

english: Small holes in young maize shoots are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf fold. Applying recommended organic liquid sprays like neem seed extract early in the morning destroys them before they ruin the entire stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaakpata amɛhiɛ dani tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ baafite.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct sunlight. Leaving some tall trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates shade and traps air moisture, protecting young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops yield small fruits when I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight underground for water and soil food while their leaves fight for sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light, water, and nutrients to produce big fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing at the base of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato nine lɛ shishi.

english: Extra side shoots, known as suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main plant. Removing them allows the plant to focus its energy on growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Tomato lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to spread across my farm cause my crop yields to drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi gbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and consume the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks of planting gives your crops full access to nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛyeɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them stay healthy in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the dirt from direct sun heat. It holds moisture in the ground much longer so the plant roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are completely ready to be dug up from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ?

english: Yams indicate maturity when the upper leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and transferred all its energy into the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ kɛji ŋwɛi baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad for me to clear trees and plant my crops right up to the edge of the river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mafo tsei ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyashi faa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Planting too close to the riverbank destroys the natural roots that hold the soil together. When river levels rise during heavy rains, the fast-moving water will easily wash away your soil and crops, and breaking river buffer zone regulations can leave you without government support when disaster strikes.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ naa tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ. Kɛ faa lɛ mli nu lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya. Ni faa mli buffer zone mlai ni oooku mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔyeli lɛ akaye abua bo kɛji oshara ko ba.

english: Why do my crops rot and die when rainwater sits on my field for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni gbii fioo pɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it smothers the roots, preventing them from taking in oxygen and nutrients, which causes the roots to rot and the plant to collapse.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haaa amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Which crops can I safely plant on land that regularly gets flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ daa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops like rice and taro (cocoyam) can handle wet, flooded soils much better than crops like maize or cassava. Maize and cassava roots rot quickly in standing water, whereas rice is adapted to thrive in flooded fields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ taro (kookoo) baanyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ nu afua he nii jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Abɛi kɛ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni atsakeɔ ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop heavy rainwater from washing away my topsoil and young crops down the hill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Planting your crops in rows across the slope rather than straight down the hill helps trap water. You can also plant vetiver grass along the contours of the slope to slow down moving rainwater so it soaks into the ground instead of carrying your soil away.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Obaanyɛ odu vetiver hu yɛ gɔji lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ekɛbaaya.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever a big rainstorm sweeps through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ wulu ko baatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have heavy tops and very shallow roots. When heavy rain thoroughly softens the soil, strong winds can easily pull those shallow roots out of the ground and knock the heavy tree down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala nakai shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha tsei ni tsii lɛ agbee shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly during a long hot dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a defense mechanism to save water. By rolling the leaves inward, less leaf area is exposed to the harsh sun, which reduces the amount of moisture escaping from the plant.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie mli lɛ, ebaaha he ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ baa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Can my vegetables survive if floodwater covers them for just one day and then recedes?
ga: Ani aduawai lɛ baahi shi kɛji nu afua lɛ ba shi gbi kome pɛ?

english: Vegetables can often survive a brief flood if the water drains away quickly and the hot sun doesn't immediately scorch the wet plants. However, you must wash off mud from the leaves and watch out for fungal diseases that thrive in damp conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai hiɔ shi yɛ nu afua be kukuoo mli. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛji nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãaa tso ni efɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ofɔ muji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ he, ni okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops get more diseases when I plant them in low-lying, wet areas of my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa helai babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Low-lying, wet areas hold trapped moisture and stay humid for long periods. High humidity creates the ideal environment for harmful fungi and bacteria to grow and spread quickly across plant leaves and stems.
ga: He ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ mli ni ebaahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, intense sunlight. Large trees act as living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from sun damage and conserve soil moisture until the cocoa trees are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni buɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: What steps should I take if a sudden river overflow completely destroys my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji faa lɛ ho trukaa, ni efite miŋmɔ lɛ kwraa?

english: Take photos of the destruction if possible and report the loss immediately to your local agriculture extension officer or district assembly. They can document the disaster for relief assistance and guide you on how to safely rehabilitate your land.
ga: Kɛji ebaahi lɛ, feemɔ hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ he mfoniri. ni abɔ nɔ ni elaaje lɛ he amaniɛ aha maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo kpokpaa nɔkwɛlɔi akuu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmala osharai ahe saji amɛshwie shi koni amɛye amɛbua yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ nitsumɔi amli, ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ bɔ ni ooofee okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shweshweeshwe lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when there are no bigger trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Shading them with fast-growing plants like plantains protects their delicate leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has up to its newest leaves, leaving the older lower leaves starving for nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen fioo ko yaa baai heei lɛ anɔ. Shi baai ni edara ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni hɔmɔ aye amɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow alongside maize, they feed the soil naturally with nitrogen, reducing your need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he hiamɔ baa shi

english: Why shouldn't I apply my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the topsoil before plant roots can drink it in, wasting your money and washing nutrients away into nearby streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eji shika fitemɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rainy season goes on for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out oxygen, effectively suffocating the roots. This lack of air combined with high moisture causes the cassava tubers to rot and attract soil fungi.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo fataa he lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without producing fruit during hot, dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsi kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to enter survival mode. They drop their blossoms to preserve moisture and energy in their main stems until conditions improve.
