ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ kɛ tomato tsei lɛ woɔ wala mli. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to cover the soil around my plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi No hewɔ ni okɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the hot sun off the dirt, prevents soil water from evaporating fast, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafite. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms once the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit. Mounding extra soil high around the base and supporting the heavy bunches with bamboo props prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ ni akɛbɔleɔ Base he lɛ ni akɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo akajie lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines on sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nine nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight needed to swell the underground tubers, while keeping foliage off wet soil prevents fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo tsei lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii akaye baai lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center whorl of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: This is characteristic damage caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls deep inside the central growing tip of the plant and feeds on young leaf tissue.
ga: Nɔ ni kadiɔ enɛ ji nibii ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my coconut trees produce very little juice inside the nuts while others are completely full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ekomɛi jieɔ nu fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsei komɛi eyi kɛ nu lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need consistent water and soil nutrients while the nuts are expanding. If the tree experiences dry spells or lacks potassium during growth, the nuts fail to build up high liquid reserves inside.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmei tsei be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ miigbɛ eshwa lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ loo potassium ni faaa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ Beans lɛ nyɛŋ ama nu ni fa babaoo yɛ emli.

english: What makes the juice inside green coconuts taste sweeter on some trees than on others?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei nu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ tsei komɛi anɔ fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Sweetness comes from sugars produced by the leaves through sunlight and stored in the fruit. Proper tree spacing for full sunlight, along with soils rich in potassium, naturally increases the sweetness of coconut water.
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmɔlɔ lɛ jɛɔ sugar ni hulu la lɛ feɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli ni akɛtoɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛha hulu la ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei nu lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I tell when a green coconut has reached its peak stage for maximum water content?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ko eshɛ he ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Coconuts usually reach peak juice volume around 7 to 8 months after flowering. At this stage, the outer skin is smooth and bright green, and shaking the nut produces a dull sloshing sound.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shɛɔ aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 8 sɛɛ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ ni akpokpoɔ lɛ haa gbɛɛmɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: How can I manage my coconut palms so they yield a very large amount of heavy nuts every harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo ŋmeii babaoo ni tsii be fɛɛ be ni makpa lɛ?

english: High yields require clearing weeds around the base, applying compost or potassium-rich fertilizers, and ensuring palms are planted far enough apart so their large fronds do not shade each other.
ga: Nibii ni anáa babaoo lɛ biɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo potassium ni fa babaoo afata he. Ni esa akɛ adu tɛŋ tsei yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛbaai wuji lɛ akatsĩ amɛhe naa.

english: Why do my coconut trees bear much fewer fruits when they are planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When palms are crowded, their roots fight for groundwater and their tall fronds block sunlight from one another. This stress reduces the tree's energy to produce and maintain large bunches of fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. ni baai kakadaji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa hewalɛ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does a tall coconut tree manage to pull so much water all the way up to the heavy fruits at the top?
ga: Kokoo tsei ni kɛlɛ Gbalaa nu babaoo ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ oyashɛ ŋwɛi?

english: Coconut trees have thousands of fibrous roots that absorb groundwater. As sunlight shines on the upper leaves, water is naturally pulled up through narrow sap channels in the trunk directly into the growing nuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi akpei abɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Kɛ hulu la lɛ kpɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Nu lɛ tsɔɔ mliki gbɛi bibii amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do young baby coconuts drop off my tree long before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Early nut drop usually happens due to sudden dry weather, poor soil fertility, or insect attacks on the flower stems. Keeping the tree well-watered and mulched helps hold the young fruit on the bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nut ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni awoɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhiɛ aduawai bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does spreading wood ash or salt around the base of my coconut trees really help them perform better?
ga: Tso mli sũ loo ŋoo ni akɛshwieɔ he Ani ŋmei tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, wood ash provides potassium which improves fruit size and sweetness. Coconut palms also naturally tolerate moderate salt, which helps the roots absorb and retain soil moisture during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ haa potassium, ni haa aduawai lɛ daraa ni ehaa amɛmli ŋɔɔ. Kokoo tsei hu nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ ŋmei ni fa fioo gbɛ yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are the bottom fronds on my coconut tree turning yellow and drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Lower leaves turn yellow when the tree lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, or during severe dry seasons when the palm drops older leaves to save water for the growing top nuts.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium. aloo yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli beni ŋmei tsei lɛ shiɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu kɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do dwarf coconut trees start bearing fruit so much faster than traditional tall coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa fe blema ŋmeii tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties are naturally bred to direct energy into early flower production within 3 to 4 years, whereas tall varieties spend their early years building a thick, tall trunk before producing heavy fruit.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkudɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛwoɔ. koni ekɛfee tsei ni kɛlɛ ni mli tse dani ewo yibii ni tsii

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade trees like plantains above them because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the moisture they need to grow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ kooyigbɛ tsei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I need to trim off branches from my mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ niji?

english: Trimming or pruning removes weak and overlapping branches, allowing sunlight and air to reach the main trunk while guiding the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ajieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekanyaa tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my farm turning black and soft during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet conditions when water stays on pods for too long.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni daa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli beni nu hiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What makes tiny dark patches appear on the stems of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji bibii baa? Eje kpo yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishi

english: These patches are usually caused by mirid insects (capsids) that bite into the bark to suck the sap, which weakens the tree and damages new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirid kooloi (capsids) ni ŋmɔɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ koni amɛnu nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ nibii heei ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo babaoo ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects called midges; if midges are not present or if the tree is stressed by drought, the unpollinated flowers dry up and fall off.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛji akɛ teŋdamɔlɔ ko bɛ loo hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa lɛ, fɔfɔi ni Unpollinated lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the dry season lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees reduce flower and pod production during long dry spells to conserve water and protect themselves from dying.
ga: Cacao tsei haa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do weeds growing under my cocoa trees reduce my final harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ haa minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cocoa trees' root systems, leaving less food for the cocoa trees to produce fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my older cocoa trees turning yellow even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil has run out of important plant nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, which the tree needs to maintain green leaves and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ nɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why should I leave fresh cocoa beans covered in plantain leaves for several days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi kookoo yibii heei ni akɛ plantain baai ehà nɔ lɛ gbii babaoo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Covering fresh cocoa beans allows them to ferment properly, which develops the chocolate flavor, kills the seed inside so it doesn't sprout, and turns the beans brown.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ cocoa ŋmeii heei ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha efee tsokolate ŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni kookoo yibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it good to plant food crops like cassava together with my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsei ni adu ehee?

english: Planting food crops like plantain or cocoyam helps young cocoa by providing shade, but cassava can compete heavily underground and take too much water and nutrients away from the young cocoa roots.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains loo cocoa ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cocoa lɛ feɔ gbekɛ kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmei baanyɛ afee akaŋshii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni eŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there is too much sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni hulu la babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. They require shade plants like plantains to shelter them until they are strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce heavy pods directly on the trunk instead of on the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ niji bibii najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower and fruit on their main trunk and thick branches because cocoa pods are heavy. If pods grew on thin branches, the weight would snap the twigs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ tsii. Kɛji akɛ pods lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ niji bibii anɔ lɛ Muji lɛ baakumɔ niji lɛ.

english: Why do new leaves on my cocoa trees look soft and reddish-pink before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: New cocoa leaves emerge reddish-pink while they are young and expanding. Once the leaf matures and develops chlorophyll to make food from sunlight, it turns dark green.
ga: Kookoo baai heei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ-tsuru be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo ni amɛmiigbɛ amɛshwã. Beni baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ klorofil ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ. Baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce fewer pods each year even though they look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Over many years, cocoa trees pull essential nutrients out of the earth with every harvest. If you do not feed the soil with compost or suitable fertilizer, the soil runs out of food for new pods.
ga: Afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Niyenii ni akɛbaahã ŋmeii heei lɛ baaho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut back the old branches of my coffee bushes, will it kill the plant?
ga: Kɛ mifo kɔfe tso lɛ niji momo lɛ Ani ebaagbe kɔfe tso lɛ?

english: No, cutting back old branches encourages the coffee bush to sprout fresh, energetic shoots. These new branches yield far more coffee berries than old, tired stems.
ga: Dabi, niji ni egbɔ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha kɔfi tso lɛ mli ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃. Nɛkɛ tsei niji heei nɛɛ woɔ kɔfe babaoo fe tsei niji momo ni efite lɛ.

english: Why do my coffee trees suddenly bloom with white flowers right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii yɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Coffee buds sleep during the dry season to save energy. The sudden water from the first rain wakes the buds up, causing all the flowers to bloom together at once.
ga: Kɔfi fɔfɔi wɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛ lɛ te fɔfɔi lɛ ashishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ afɔlɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why are green coffee cherries dropping off my bushes onto the dirt before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔfi ŋmɔji ni ji eŋɔli lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ mi jwɛi lɛ amli kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Coffee cherries drop early when the tree lacks water during dry spells or when insect pests bore into the fruit. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and managing pests prevents early fruit drop.
ga: Coffee cherry aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nu bɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bote aduawai lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni atsi yibii ni fiteɔ mra lɛ naa.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite beni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a mold that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess leaves allows airflow and sunlight to dry the pods, stopping the mold from growing.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: How can I tell if my coffee trees are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kɔfi tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If coffee leaves curl up, feel dry, and drop off, the plant is thirsty. If leaves turn yellow and drop off while the ground is muddy, the roots are choking from excess water.
ga: Kɛji kɔfe baai lɛ shwie shi, enu he akɛ egbi, ni egbee shi lɛ, kumai miiye kɔfe tso lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava right next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ masɛi?

english: Cassava roots spread heavily and steal nutrients and moisture from young cocoa. It is better to plant plantains or legumes, which give beneficial shade without fighting the cocoa for soil food.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa waa ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo bibii lɛ amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu plantains loo ŋmeii ni haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni okɛ kookoo akaŋ akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to sort and grade my harvested crops by size before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahala mikpamɔ lɛ mli ni mato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ naa dani mikɛya jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Sorting produce into standard sizes allows buyers to clearly see the quality of what they are paying for, which helps you command better prices and makes selling faster and easier.
ga: Nibii ni ajara mli awoɔ dalɛi ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni amɛnaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ he nyɔmɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ toɔ. ni eha jarayeli aya oya ni efee mlɛo

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves turning dry or yellow, stems drying out, or fruits changing color. Harvesting at this stage prevents field rot and pest attacks.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ, loo aduawai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fitemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: How can I check if the crop seeds I bought from the market will actually sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani madu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds on a damp cloth for a few days; if 8 or 9 sprout, your seeds are healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Anáa enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni akɛwoɔ mama ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi lɛ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo 9 kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing them to stretch upward instead of producing big harvest yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha yibii babaoo.

english: Improved seed varieties are specially selected to grow faster, resist common field diseases, and yield significantly more crops during favorable rainy seasons compared to traditional saved seeds.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kpakpa lɛ mli Kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth; applying the right fertilizer early will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii mra Ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil lacks phosphorus, when temperatures get excessively hot, or when there are no pollinating insects like bees to help fertilize the blooms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ fɔsfɔs. Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmeii, bɛ ni baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee fɔmɔ nii.

english: Can I safely plant cassava and maize together on the same farm plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slower and deeper into the soil, allowing you to maximize land space without them competing heavily.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he nii babaoo ni akaŋshii ni mli wa bɛ mli.

english: What will happen to my grains if I put them in storage bags before they are completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baa midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛwo kotoku mli dani amɛgbi kwraa?

english: Storing wet or damp grains traps moisture in the bag, creating mold and encouraging insect pests that will rapidly ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efɔ loo ni efɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ awo kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛfite onibii fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do insect pests damage my crops more during dry spells than during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses crops due to water shortage, making them weaker and easier for insects to attack as the pests search for moisture inside the plants.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaatutua lɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ taoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Shading them with fast-growing plants like plantains protects them from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains wo amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete for the same nutrients and sunlight, resulting in tall thin plants with very small tubers instead of big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bulb bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ ngmɔ agbo nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to trap moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation when the sun is at its hottest.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Continuous rain creates high dampness that helps the Black Pod fungus spread rapidly. Pruning excess tree leaves improves airflow to keep pods dry and reduces fungal growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no yeɔ ebuaa blackpod fungus lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ akagbi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: Removing extra shoots ensures all food and water from the soil go directly to the main plantain tree, allowing it to grow faster and yield a much larger bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa dumɔwu titri lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients like nitrogen quickly. Planting it every season drains the soil completely, so rotating with crops like cowpea or groundnut helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen tsuɔ nii oya. Dumɔ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves look burned after applying chemical fertilizer during a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo mli yɛ otsi ni nu bɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve safely. Without water, concentrated fertilizer draws water directly out of plant roots, causing the leaves to burn and dry out.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or tiny insect pests that feed on the delicate blossoms before fruit formation begins.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii amli. No yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I store seeds from my last maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds harvested from improved or hybrid varieties lose their vigor in the next generation, producing weaker plants and much lower yields compared to original packaged seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto shishijee dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even if there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal nutrients and light, leaving your main crops starved even when there is enough water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do insect pests keep hiding underneath my plant leaves even after I spray my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa efɔ amɛnɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Insects seek shade and shelter under thick leaf canopies. Standard top-down spraying often misses the underside of leaves, allowing pests to feed safely unless the spray liquid thoroughly penetrates the dense crop foliage.
ga: Kplukai taoɔ hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi. Nɔ ni afɔɔ shwiemɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa shi lɛ haa ebaa lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ. Ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ Ja tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ bote tso lɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if pest damage on my crops has reached a point where I must spray chemicals as a last resort?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he ko ni ehe baahia ni mikɛ tsofai afɔse nɔ akɛ naagbee gbɛ?

english: When crop leaves show severe holes, start yellowing rapidly, or insect numbers multiply faster than basic physical methods can handle, chemical spraying becomes necessary as a final effort to prevent total crop loss.
ga: Beni tso lɛ baai lɛ ná bu ni mli wa waa lɛ Jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya Aloo kooloi bibii lɛ ayibɔ miiya hiɛ oya fe bɔ ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ baanyɛ atsu he nii. No hewɔ lɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he miihia yɛ naagbee mɔdɛŋbɔɔ mli koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why did the flowers on my tomato plants fall off after I sprayed them for insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Strong chemical sprays applied directly to open blossoms can burn tender flower parts or scare away pollinating insects like bees, causing the plant to drop its flowers instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã efãi komɛi. ni ji fɔfɔi bibii loo kooloi bibii ni haa mɔ naa kpɛɔ ehe tamɔ ŋmeii, ni haa tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do diseases destroy the inner leaves of my bushy plants more than the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela fiteɔ mitso lɛ mli baai lɛ fe kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: A dense canopy of leaves traps moisture and warm air inside the plant, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases can easily multiply out of sight.
ga: Kpoji ni mli tse lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni anaaa.

english: Why aren't my crops growing well in the exact paths where heavy farm tractors drove?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni traktɔi wuji kudɔɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy farm machinery presses the soil down very hard, compacting the earth so tightly that crop roots struggle to spread, breathe, and draw up water or nutrients.
ga: Okwaayeli tsɔnei ni tsii nyɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmu, ni amɛgbala nu loo niyenii.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and burn when I spray chemicals in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes liquid chemicals to evaporate rapidly and burn the leaf surface, while the plant's breathing pores stay closed to prevent water loss.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni eshãa baa lɛ hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ mumɔ bu lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi koni nu akaje mli.

english: Why are my crops still wilting even though I sprayed them with liquid chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo beni mikɛ tsofai ni ji nu shwieɔ nɔ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Spraying liquid chemicals onto leaves only treats leaf surfaces; wilting happens when the roots deep in the soil lack water or are being damaged by underground pests.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baatsa baai lɛ ahiɛ pɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ amli nu lɛ faaa loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite lɛ ji nɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops look stressed and weak when weeds grow closely around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhao ni amɛgbɔjɔ be mli ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for fertilizer nutrients, soil water, and sunlight, effectively starving the crop and making it too weak to grow properly.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ hulu la, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do insects stop dying even when I keep spraying my crops with the same chemical every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii lɛ kpaɔ gbele eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ daa otsi moŋ?

english: Using the exact same chemical repeatedly allows surviving insects to build resistance, passing that strength to their young until the chemical no longer affects them.
ga: Tsofai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ Ebaaha kooloi ni hiɛ ka lɛ aná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ hela lɛ. Amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ haa amɛbii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsofai lɛ enaaa amɛnɔ hewalɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crop plants turn yellow and drop off before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Bottom leaves turn yellow when upper leaves shade them from sunshine, or when the plant is redirecting its food energy and nitrogen upward to support new fruit growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji ŋwɛi baa lɛ tsi hulu la naa. aloo beni tsei tsɔɔ niyenii hewalɛ kɛ nitrogen lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua aduawai heei adalɛ.

english: Can I plant my yams on land that has a lot of small stones?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potatoes yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi bibii babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Stony soil makes it hard for yam tubers to grow long, straight, and smooth. The rocks block the growing tubers, leading to small, deformed yams that are hard to harvest and sell.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ kakadaŋŋ, amɛfee tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tɛi tsiɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni efite ni ewa akɛ abaakpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Is it good to plant my yams in swampy land near the river?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋshɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko mli?

english: Swampy land holds too much water, which suffocates the plant roots and causes yam tubers to rot in the soil before they can mature.
ga: Swamp hei lɛ toɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli dani amɛdaraa.

english: What kind of soil should I look for if I want to get a high yield of yams?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba lɛ, mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ otao?

english: Yams grow best in loose, deep, well-drained soil where water does not settle. This allows the tubers to expand easily deep into the ground without obstruction or rot.
ga: Atomɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nu lɛ shwieee shi Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ loo amɛgbooo.

english: How do I know if a piece of land will cause me waterlogging problems before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he naagbai baaba minɔ dani madu nii?

english: If rainwater stays pooled on top of the ground for days after a heavy rain without soaking in quickly, that land is too wet and swampy for crops like yams.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa ni etsɔɔɔ oya lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Do I need expensive new chemical inputs or special technology to get a successful yam farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa loo ŋaalee krɛdɛɛ ko atsu nii koni mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ aye omanye?

english: Successful yam farming does not require miraculous or expensive new inputs. Choosing the right soil, avoiding stony or swampy areas, and practicing proper land preparation are the key foundations for a great harvest.
ga: Sweet potato okwaayeli ni yeɔ omanye lɛ biɔ naakpɛɛ nibii loo nibii heei ni jara wa. Shikpɔŋ ni sa ni ahalaɔ He ni tɛi loo ŋmeii yɔɔ lɛ he ni aaatsi he Ni shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji shishitoo tɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kpele.

english: What is the biggest land selection mistake that wastes a farmer's hard work?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ halamɔ mli tɔmɔi wuji ni okwaafoi feɔ?

english: Planting in unsuitable land, like stony or swampy ground, is the biggest mistake. Even with great effort, bad soil prevents tubers from growing, resulting in wasted labor.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ hei ni esaaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi anɔ Enɛ ji tɔmɔ ni fe fɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo moŋ shi Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii hu tsiɔ bulbs naa koni ekakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni afiteɔ.

english: Should I clear rocks and hard gravel from my farm before making crop mounds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tɛi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani matswa gɔŋ?

english: Yes, clearing stones from the soil makes land preparation easier and ensures root crops can grow freely without hitting hard obstacles underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, tɛi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa sũ lɛ he saamɔ feɔ mlɛo. ni ehaa shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ shishi gbɛtsii nii ni wa.

english: Why are my harvested yams misshapen and small after spending so much time on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ efite ni efee bibii beni mikɛ be babaoo ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams become misshapen when planted in hard, stony ground that blocks their natural growth path under the dirt, preventing them from swelling smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tsi enaa koni ekafuu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam seeds keep rotting underground before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot underground when planted in soil that traps excessive water, preventing the seed from breathing and causing fungal and bacterial decay.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo hiɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How does choosing the right soil help reduce my physical stress and hardship as a farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni ooohala lɛ baanyɛ aba gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ kɛ naagbai ni baa mɔ nɔ akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ shi?

english: Selecting soft, well-drained soil makes digging mounds easier, prevents crop losses from rot or stunted growth, and ensures your hard labor pays off with large, healthy yams you can eat or sell.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oooha lɛ baaha gɔŋ ko ni oootsa lɛ afee mlɛo. Etsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa koni ekafite loo ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ekwɛɔ koni onitsumɔ ni wa lɛ awo yibii kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni obaanyɛ oye loo ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What benefit do my crops get when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ náa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu?

english: Animal manure acts like a slow-release food and water sponge for your crops. It enriches the soil with natural nutrients and helps sandy or hard soils hold moisture much longer during dry spells.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ blɛoo. kɛ sponge kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni wa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and put it directly into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize next to it, saving you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing overnight on my young corn leaves, and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse ehe lɛ je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These holes are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center leaves during the day and eats at night. If left unchecked, they destroy the leaves that the plant uses to capture sunlight and make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ shwane mli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Efiteɔ baai ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii lɛ.

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungal diseases or root rot from overwatering. The damaged roots can no longer suck up water or food, causing the leaves to dry out even when water is present.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ mli moŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before forming actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are under stress from prolonged heat, lack of soil moisture, or insect damage. Proper shade cover and keeping the soil moist help the tree feel safe enough to hold onto its flowers and turn them into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ latsaa he haomɔ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii lɛ fiteɔ Shade ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and food away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to focus its energy on producing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps leaves away from damp soil diseases and helps the underground tuber grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baabu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Look closely at the small raised nodes or 'eyes' along the stem where leaves used to grow. Make sure these nodes are pointing upward toward the sky when you put the cutting in the soil so the new leaves can grow straight up without wasting energy.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni awó nɔ loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni ofoɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ owoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the adult plants will fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to develop strong stems and maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They require partial shade, often provided by planting temporary shade crops like plantains, to shield them and retain moisture until they are mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo. Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ koni akɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the soft growing center of maize plants. Treating the plants early with recommended organic or chemical insecticides, or applying neem leaf extract into the funnel, stops them before they ruin the entire stalk.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ tsei ahe nii mra. Aloo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu awo cone mli. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers mainly due to heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Ensuring the soil stays evenly moist during the flowering period helps the flowers stay attached and develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots rot primarily when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots and causing fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Kassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light green and yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves are usually a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi he hiaa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaku ŋmãa ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already moist, but not during a heavy downpour. Burying or lightly covering the fertilizer with soil right after application prevents rainwater from washing it off the surface.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofu loo okɛwo nɔ fioo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛwo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ nu lɛ akaho kɛjɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more produce from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close actually reduces your overall yield because plants end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow large and produce a heavier harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe awo hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: It is safest to wait until the ground has received two or three heavy, steady rains so the soil is thoroughly wet deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if a hot spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulutsoo be ko ba.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around them for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves on your farm, aggressively stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow quickly.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ejuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small pods, but some of them turn black and dry up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo nɛkɛ, shi ekomɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops extra pods it cannot support, or by fungal diseases like black pod. Ensuring good ventilation through pruning and keeping the soil well-fed helps the tree hold onto healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa. he ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni baa kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ahi ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Can I save some of the seeds from this year's harvest to plant in my farm next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi ni baa lɛ?

english: For traditional open-pollinated crops like local maize or beans, you can save seeds from your healthiest plants for the next season. However, if you planted hybrid seeds, saving them will result in weaker plants and poor yield, so it is better to buy fresh hybrid seeds every year.
ga: Kɛha blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni agbele naa tamɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ ato kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Shi, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ, Frugality baaha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa afi.

english: Why are some of my dried cocoa beans very light and flat when weighed, while others are heavy and full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ekomɛi ahe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ asusu he lɛ? Beni kookoo yibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ, ekomɛi feɔ tsiimɔ ni eyiɔ obɔ.

english: Flat or light beans happen when cocoa pods are harvested before they fully mature, or when the trees suffer from diseases or poor nutrition. Letting pods ripen fully and fermenting the beans properly ensures plump, heavy beans that weigh more on the scale.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ni edako lɛ baa kɛji akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdara kwraa. aloo be mli ni hela loo niyenii ni esaaa lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwere kwraa ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii kɛji akɛ asusu he.

english: Why is it important to dry my cocoa beans properly on mats before bringing them to be weighed and sold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni magbi mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ dani asusu amɛhe ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Properly drying cocoa beans reduces their moisture content so they do not grow mould during storage and transport. Buyers test for moisture because wet beans ruin the quality of the chocolate and rot quickly.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa hulutsoo be lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsokolate lɛ mli ni efiteɔ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft roots and thin leaves that lose water quickly in intense heat. Dropping leaves is the tree's defense to survive drought, which is why planting temporary shade crops like plantains is necessary to protect them from direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has high nitrogen but lacks potassium and phosphorus, the cassava plant puts all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its underground roots into thick tubers.
ga: Be mli ni nitrogen fa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi potassium kɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is ready for harvesting so it doesn't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn completely brown, the silk at the top of the cob is dark and dry, and a black layer forms at the tip of the maize kernels when you scrape one off.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. Siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni egbi. Ni ŋmei diŋŋ ko baa ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ anaagbee kɛji okɛ amɛ shwie shi.

english: Why do my food crops grow thin and weak when I plant them close to large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Large trees block the sunlight that small crops need to produce food for growth. The big tree's extensive root system also steals most of the water and soil nutrients from the smaller surrounding crops.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii koni amɛná niyenii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ naa. Tsei wuji lɛ ashishifãi ni fa babaoo lɛ hu juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli lɛ ateŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a lot of flowers right after the first major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rainfall after a dry spell signals to the cocoa tree that water is now available to nourish pods. The water triggers a surge of growth hormones inside the tree, causing it to burst into flower.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ akɛ nu yɛ agbɛnɛ ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ. Nu haa tso lɛ mli tsofai ni haa mɔ daa lɛ yaa hiɛ. ha etsɔ fɔfɔi

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting and restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should I face my greenhouse or crop shelter to help my plants grow best?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi-greenhouse loo shĩa lɛ mli koni eye ebua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Positioning your greenhouse East to West ensures your crops receive uniform sunlight throughout the day while preventing overheating from direct midday sun exposure.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-greenhouse lɛ to bokagbɛ kɛtee anaigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulu la be fɛɛ be yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are my vegetable crops leaning towards one side of my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ efo miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ?

english: Crops naturally bend and stretch towards the direction where sunlight is strongest. If tall trees or structures block light on one side, the plants will lean to reach the sun.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe yɛ he ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa lɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsũi ni kwɔlɔ tsi kane lɛ naa yɛ fa kome lɛ Tso lɛ baatsɔ ehe kɛya hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with pale leaves when planted under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive insufficient sunlight, they spend energy stretching upwards to look for light rather than growing strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Akɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la. Mohu ɔ, mo tsɔ tso nɛ he wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a ngɛ he wami, nɛ e ngɛ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my greenhouse pepper plants drop their flowers before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi greenhouse chili tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: When heat builds up inside a poorly designed shelter, extreme temperatures can sterilize pollen, causing flowers to fall off instead of setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ dɔlɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shĩa ko ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ mli lɛ Dɔlɛ ni fe nine baanyɛ agbe ŋmeii. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl and wilt inside my farm shelter during the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ mli shĩa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When temperatures inside a greenhouse get too hot, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can suck it up from the soil, causing temporary wilting to protect themselves.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe.

english: Why is proper airflow so important for crops growing inside a farming shelter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ okwaayeli hei amli lɛ?

english: Good air circulation cools plant leaves and removes trapped moisture, which stops destructive mold and fungal diseases from spreading across your farm.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does the distance between support posts in my crop shelter affect plant growth?
ga: Te sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni yɔɔ yelikɛbuamɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing of support posts ensures crop leaves have enough space to spread out for air and light while preventing plants from shading each other.
ga: Nibii ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaajara kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa tsei lɛ afee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to crop yield if I plant too many crops inside a small greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mini greenhouse lɛ mli?

english: Overcrowded crops compete for soil nutrients, root space, and sunlight, resulting in smaller harvests and making it easier for pests to move from plant to plant.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, shishifãi, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi. ni eha efee mlɛo aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akɛ amɛbaajɛ tso kome mli kɛya tso kroko mli.

english: How does wind direction affect where I should set up my crop shelter?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ saa he ni esa akɛ ma miŋmɔshi nibii atoohe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Building your crop structure so its closed side faces strong prevailing winds protects young stems from snapping and keeps structural covers from tearing.
ga: Bɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni fã ni aŋã lɛ akwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkakumɔ. ni otsi tsɔne lɛ he tsɔne lɛ naa koni ekagbala.

english: Why does soil inside a crop shelter dry out differently than soil in an open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shĩai amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Shelter covers block natural rainfall while trapped heat speeds up soil water evaporation, making manual watering schedule and mulching critical for root survival.
ga: He ni wɔyɔɔ lɛ tsiɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ naa. yɛ be mli ni la ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong and green. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tso lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ adara ni efee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and starves the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away naturally, keeping the tubers safe underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Why do flowers fall off my cowpea plants without making any beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when tiny insects like thrips attack the blooms to feed on their nectar. Spraying your crop with neem oil or an approved insect spray just as flowering starts stops these pests so the pods can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii, tamɔ thrips, tutua fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛye fɔfɔi lɛ amli nu lɛ. Okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ koni akɛkpa kooloi nɛɛ. koni pods lɛ anyɛ afee

english: Why do I have to erect wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ koni mi sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch as much direct sunlight as possible, which feeds the growing tuber beneath the soil. Leaving vines on the wet ground causes leaf diseases and results in much smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ baaha bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná niyenii. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ kɛ foliar hela baa ni ehaa sweet potato bibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn dark brown and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This darkening is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, shaded environments. Pruning overhead shade trees and weeding around your cocoa trees increases airflow and sunlight, which dries out the farm and slows the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ su ni tsuɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo aba yiteŋ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Cacao baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa hela lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and sunken before they can turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, usually because the soil moisture keeps changing from dry to wet. Watering your plants on a regular schedule helps them draw calcium from the soil into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. ni calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa Be fɛɛ be lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to get more crops from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants with low yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce large, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and draining their sap. Treating the plants with soapy water or a recommended pesticide gets rid of the insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu tso lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ kɛjɛ mli bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches, especially during strong winds. Propping up the main stem with strong wooden Y-sticks provides external support until the bunch is fully ripe for harvesting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y damɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha eye ebua kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ kɛyashi be mli ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: My cocoa trees are over ten years old and producing fewer pods. Do older trees need different care than young ones?
ga: Mi-cocoa tso lɛ eye fe afii nyɔŋma ni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ woɔ. Ani tsei ni edara lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe tsei ni darako lɛ?

english: Yes, as cocoa trees pass ten years of age, their root systems and the soil nutrients around them change. Older trees often require targeted fertilizer applications and strategic pruning to restore their vigor and maintain good pod yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ kookoo tso ko ye afii 10 lɛ, eshishifãi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ baatsake. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ lɛ biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛha amɛná pod kpakpa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn pale green instead of dark vibrant green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale leaves usually indicate that the tree is starving for essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Giving the tree proper plant food or fertilizer restores the deep green color required for strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ha otso lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm actually needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If your trees show slow growth, pale or yellowing leaves, or produce fewer and smaller cocoa pods despite good rainfall, your soil is likely exhausted and needs fertilizer to replenish its nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ miida blɛoo Pale loo yellow leaves loo eewo cocoa ŋmɔtɔi fioo ni efee bibioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can fertilizer bring back high pod yields on my older cocoa trees, or is it only for young plants?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei momo lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba podi ni fa babaoo mli? loo tsei bibii pɛ

english: Fertilizer works very well on older cocoa trees. While young plants use nutrients to grow leaves and roots, mature trees use nutrients to produce strong flowers and heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei bibii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ shishifãi amli moŋ, shi tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What is the best season to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the onset of the rainy season when the soil is moist. Moisture allows the cocoa roots to dissolve and drink in the nutrients easily without burning the tree.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ mli ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why can't I cut down all the large shade trees and let my cocoa get full sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mafo tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni maha Cocoa hulu ni eyi obɔ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Direct, harsh sunlight creates intense heat that stresses cocoa trees and dries out the soil. Balanced shade protects the leaves from burning, retains moisture, and creates the ideal cooling environment for cocoa to thrive.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Shade ni ja lɛ buɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ofee shihilɛ ni sa ni mli ejɔ koni kookoo akwɛ̃.

english: Do old cocoa trees require as much shade as newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo tamɔ bɔ ni amɛhe hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: No, newly planted cocoa trees need heavy shade because their leaves burn easily under the sun. Mature cocoa trees develop their own dense branches and foliage, so they need less shade from companion trees.
ga: Dabi, kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ he miihia hulutsoo be ni mli wa ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niji kɛ baai ni mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a lot of flowers that dry up and drop before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Flower dropping happens when a tree is under stress from nutrient shortages, drought, or too much direct sunlight. Proper soil nutrition and balanced shade help the tree keep its flowers long enough to turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa, hɔmɔ, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni sa yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees yield more pods?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ni afolɔ afata he lɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overgrown branches so the tree stops wasting energy on them. It opens up the tree canopy to let air flow through, preventing fungal diseases and directing energy into growing pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egbɔjɔ, ni egboi, loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni otsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa pods ni miida lɛ anɔ

english: When cocoa trees are overcrowded, they compete for water, sunlight, and soil food. This causes them to grow thin and weak with reduced yields, and creates a damp environment where diseases like black pod spread easily.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo baa shi. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why does my new cocoa crop take several years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend their early years building strong root systems and sturdy branches. They need to mature fully before they have enough energy to support and grow healthy cocoa pods, which usually takes 3 to 5 years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa. Esa akɛ amɛdara dani amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye amɛbua ni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop some of their flowers before they turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed. If the tree lacks water, soil nutrients, or proper pollination, it sheds excess flowers to save its strength for the pods it can successfully nourish.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo pollination ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛ hewalɛ ahi ŋmeii ni baanyɛ aye omanye lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the larger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. They rely on shade from taller trees or food crops to protect their tender leaves and keep the soil moist while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji loo niyenii tsei ahe hulutsoo nɔ koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to focus on growing just one crop like cocoa first instead of planting many different crops all at once?
