ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii kome tamɔ kookoo nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tsei babaoo shikome lɛ?

english: Starting with one main crop helps you learn its specific care, pest challenges, and growth stages without getting overwhelmed. Once that main crop is established after a few years, you can safely introduce other crops step by step.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tso titri kome je shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okase bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ahaa. Pest Challenge kɛ dalɛ mli nibii ni anuuu he akɛ egbɔjɔ Be mli ni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi amli Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi atsɔɔ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Can I plant plantains and food crops together on the same plot with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting crops like plantain alongside young cocoa works well because the plantain leaves provide temporary shade for the young cocoa while giving you early food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ plantain baai lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa trees are well-established enough for me to start introducing new crops to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii heei dumɔ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Your cocoa trees are established when they have developed deep root systems, thick main stems, and a full leaf canopy—usually after two to three years—meaning they are strong enough to share soil space without dying.
ga: O-cacao tso lɛ maa shi beni ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, tso lɛ shishifã titri ni mli tse, kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaja ni egbooo.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I plant them too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight for limited sunlight and soil nutrients. This results in thin trunks, low pod yields, and trapped moisture that encourages fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, pod yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ fungal helai tamɔ pod diji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to trim off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo ŋwɛi bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots growing at the bottom steal valuable water and food away from the main trunk. Removing them forces the tree to direct all its energy into growing strong upper branches and producing pods.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ juɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋwɛi niji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does my farm soil seem to lose its richness after growing crops on it for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ afii fioo komɛi ni mikɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops continuously pull nutrients out of the earth to grow and make fruits. If you do not replenish the soil with organic manure, compost, or fertilizers, the soil gradually runs out of food for future crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii wɔsɛɛ lɛ baaho fiofio.

english: Why do insect pests spread so quickly when I plant only one single crop across my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting only one crop across large acreage creates an endless food supply for specific pests, allowing them to multiply fast. Mixing different plants breaks up their path and naturally slows down pest invasions.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da lɛ haa niyenii ni bɛ naagbee baa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ he lɛ baafo egbɛ lɛ mli ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and tall. Adding animal manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer gives the soil back its strength so your crops can grow healthy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ afee ehee bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ adara waa.

english: Is it good for me to burn the bushy grass on my field before planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi kui yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning seems fast, but it destroys the natural food in the soil and kills good living organisms that keep the dirt healthy. Clearing the bush by hand or leaving the cut grass to rot naturally keeps the soil rich and moist.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni shãa lɛ yaa oya. Shi efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni muji lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ niji jieɔ tsei bibii loo jwɛi ni afo lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I use fresh droppings from my farm animals directly as manure on my young crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii heei ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi amli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ akɛ ŋmeii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure produces too much heat and can burn young plant roots. You need to stack the manure in a heap and let it decompose for a few weeks until it cools down into dark, rich compost before putting it around your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dɔɔ fe nine, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni oha egbo otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani okɛwo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent this disease from ruining your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop all their flowers before fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani eyibii lɛ baa?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun heat or dry soil. Giving your plants consistent water and providing light shade during very hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Watering your tomato plants regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil stops the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Okɛ nu awo o-tomato tsei lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni aduawai lɛ ashishi akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose many of their young pods before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii babaoo miifite dani amɛshɛɔ amɛdalɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop or turn black mainly due to fungal diseases like black pod disease during rainy periods, or because the canopy is too crowded. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight in helps protect the pods.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbee shi loo amɛbaatsɔ ediŋŋ, titri lɛ yɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji hela yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize next to them. Planting them together saves money on chemical fertilizers and improves overall soil fertility.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii. Dumɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shika baa shi yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my yam mounds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni ka sweet potatoes ni abua naa lɛ ateŋ beni aduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents crop roots from competing for water and nutrients underground. Leaving about one meter of space between yam mounds allows the tubers enough room to grow large without squeezing each other.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛmiimii amɛhe.

english: Weeds have strong, deep root systems that react quickly to rain and steal food from the soil faster than young crop seeds. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the space, sunlight, and food they need to get ahead.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe dumɔwui bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: How does strong wind affect my crops when they are growing?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa midumɔ nii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Strong winds can physically break tall plant stems, strip off leaves, and dry out soil moisture rapidly. Wind also blows away flowers and young fruits before they can fully mature.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akpata tsei ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahiɛ, ebaagbee shi, ni eha sũ mli nu lɛ agbi oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa fɔfɔi bibii kɛ aduawai hu dani amɛdaraa.

english: What can I plant around my farm boundary to protect my crops from strong winds?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ehe? Okwaa husu ni akɛbuɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he?

english: Planting rows of tall trees or dense grass hedges like vetiver around your farm edges creates a natural windbreak. This slows down harsh winds and prevents crop damage.
ga: Tsei kakadaji loo jwɛi ni mli edɔ tamɔ vetiver jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba shi ni ebaatsi ŋmɔshinii afitemɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to spray agricultural chemicals on my crops when it is windy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makɛ okwaayeli tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Wind blows the chemical spray away from your target crops, wasting expensive product and potentially drifting onto non-target crops, nearby animals, or water sources.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni okɛmamɔ ohiɛ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni jara wa lɛ elaaje ni ebaanyɛ eya ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ lɛ anɔ. Koolooi loo nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ

english: How do chemical fertilizers actually help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed essential nutrients directly to the soil that plants need to build strong roots, green leaves, and healthy fruits faster than unfertilized soil can provide.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa, baai eŋɔli, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya fe shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if agricultural chemicals are damaging my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: If you apply too much chemical or spray at the wrong time, leaves may turn yellow, develop brown burnt edges, or curl up, causing plant growth to stall.
ga: Kɛ okɛ tsofa loo spray babaoo tsu nii yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Eshishigbɛi lɛ shãa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ebɔleɔ ehe, ni no haa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do crops grow well in some parts of Ghana but perform poorly in other areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei komɛi lɛ? Shi etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Ghana has different agricultural zones with distinct rainfall levels, soil types, and temperatures. Crops tailored for moist forest areas struggle in drier northern savannah regions.
ga: Ghana yɛ okwaayeli hei srɔtoi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ srɔtoi, shikpɔŋ henɔi, kɛ dɔlɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo kooi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ kooyigbɛ savannas ni mli egbi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and dry up when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from dry soil, causing stress that turns leaves yellow and limp.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ baa.

english: What causes my maize plants to bend over and lie flat on the ground after a storm?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-abele tsei lɛ shwie shi ni amɛkã shi shiŋŋ yɛ ahum ko sɛɛ?

english: A combination of heavy rain softening the soil around the roots and strong gusts of wind pushing the plant stems causes tall crops to lodge or fall over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ feɔ ekome ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa ni hosoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ ais loo amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: If I move to a new town in Ghana, how do I know which crops will yield best on my land?
ga: Kɛji mifã kɛtee maŋ hee ko mli yɛ Ghana Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Observing what successful local farmers grow and testing a small patch of your land with local crop varieties reveals how well your soil responds before full-scale planting.
ga: Nɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi edu yɛ omanyeyeli mli ni amɛka amɛkwɛ yɛ hei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ. Onifeemɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa dani oduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rain right after planting affect my new seeds in the soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa midumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain provides necessary moisture for seeds to sprout, but extremely heavy downpours can wash seeds away or clog the soil with water, suffocating the young sprouts.
ga: Nugbɔ haa fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo ekɛ nu atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why should I spend extra money on improved hybrid maize seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite shika babaoo koni mahe ŋmãa ni afee lɛ hybrid ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛ heɔ wuhi nɛ a je nyagbe ní kpami be ɔ mi ɔ yi wami.

english: Improved seeds are specially bred to resist local pests and dry spells while yielding much higher harvests. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their strength over time, leading to smaller cobs and uneven crop growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do improved cassava varieties mature faster and give bigger tubers than our traditional local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji fe wɔmaŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties have been developed by agricultural scientists to naturally resist diseases like Cassava Mosaic Virus and efficiently turn soil nutrients into tuber growth, allowing them to mature in 9 to 12 months instead of up to two years.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efee ŋmei henɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ helai tamɔ ŋmei mosaic virus lɛ atsu nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni etsakeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ewoɔ tuber ŋmɔshi nibii amli Enɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ afii enyɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen or the soil is waterlogged. Heavy rains can wash away nitrogen from the soil, preventing the maize leaves from producing the green chlorophyll needed for food and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee klorofil eŋɔli ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii kɛ dalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yams are fully mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. Harvesting early yields small, soft tubers, while leaving mature yams in wet soil too long invites rot and beetle attacks.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda kwraa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. kpamɔɔ mra Enɛ baaha yitso bibioo ni yɔɔ blɛoo aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Tomato plants shed blossoms when they suffer heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo mli baa lɛ kpe. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why is it harmful for me to burn my land before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashãa dani aduɔ nii lɛ yeɔ mi awui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial living organisms in the soil that naturally feed your crops. It leaves the soil exposed to hot sun and heavy rains, which wash away fertile topsoil.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade, cooling the soil, and retaining moisture for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni sũ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná fɛ̃i

english: Why should I rotate my land with beans or peanuts instead of planting maize every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the soil of nitrogen and allows maize pests to build up in the ground. Legumes like beans trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, keeping your land fertile for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to fruit when I move them straight from an old farm to my new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Old plantain suckers often carry hidden soil worms and weevils inside their roots. If you do not trim and treat the root base before planting, these pests destroy the new roots and delay the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers momo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ofolɔɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani odu lɛ, Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fiteɔ shishifãi heei ni amɛhaa tsei lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits getting dark, rotten spots at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi bell pepper aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit during dry periods. It usually happens when watering is uneven, preventing the roots from steadily absorbing essential nutrients from the soil.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my mango fruits split open and start rotting while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango kwɛ̃ɔ ni ebɔi fitemɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting and rotting usually happen when the mango's skin gets weak and cannot handle internal pressure or fungal attacks. When the fruit cracks open, germs enter and cause rapid decay.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli fãmɔ kɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji mango lɛ hewolo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni enyɛɛɛ edamɔ mligbɛ nɔnyɛɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa lɛ naa. Kɛji aduawai lɛ fã lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baabote mli ni ekɛ fitemɔ baaba oya.

english: What causes my green mangoes to rot before they are even ripe for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-mango ni eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ dani eshɛɔ kɛha nikpamɔ?

english: Premature rotting is often caused by fungal infections that attack the fruit when the tree's natural defense system is weak, causing the fruit to spoil early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa aduawai lɛ beni tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Does a mango splitting open mean that the tree itself is sick?
ga: Ani mango ni etse lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ?

english: Yes, splitting is often a sign of stress or imbalance in the tree's internal system. It shows the tree needs support to strengthen the fruit's structure.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, mligbalamɔ ji nɔnyɛɛ loo tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi ni ejaaa lɛ he okadi. Etsɔɔ akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia tso lɛ koni ewaje yibii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Can plant medicine actually help a mango tree fight off diseases on its own?
ga: Ani tsofai ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mango tsei ni amɛwu amɛshi helai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, certain systemic treatments act like medicine for the tree by strengthening its internal immune system, helping it naturally fight off diseases like rot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofafeemɔi komɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa kɛhaa tso lɛ kɛtsɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ wuɔ.

english: How does crop protection medicine work inside a mango tree to stop fruit decay?
ga: Te tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mango tsei amli koni amɛkpa aduawai ni fiteɔ lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The medicine is absorbed into the tree's system to fix internal vulnerabilities, giving the plant the strength to resist infections that cause fruit breaking and rotting.
ga: Akɛ tsofa lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli koni ekɛsaa mligbɛ gbɔjɔmɔi lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni haa aduawai lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛgboɔ lɛ.

english: Is there a specific treatment I can give my mango trees to prevent the fruit from breaking apart?
ga: Ani tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko yɛ ni manyɛ maha mi mango tso lɛ koni ekɛtsi yibii lɛ anaa koni ekagbala?

english: Yes, using specialized protective treatments helps reinforce the fruit's cell walls and boosts the tree's defense system so the mangoes grow strong without cracking.
ga: Hɛɛ, hebuu krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso yibii lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi lɛ mli waa, ni ehaa tso lɛ hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli waa. Bɔni afee ni mango lɛ adara waa ni etseee.

english: How can I prevent my mango harvest from spoiling before I take them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mango ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite dani mikɛwo jara nɔ?

english: Applying protective crop treatments early in the season builds up the tree's internal defenses, ensuring the fruit stays healthy and intact until market time.
ga: Tsei ni buɔ mɔ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa tso lɛ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ emaa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: What should I do if I notice many of my mangoes rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ ofee kɛ́ ona mango ni egbo babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Moisture encourages fungal growth. You should treat your trees with protective remedies that help the plant's internal system combat rot caused by excess humidity.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmɔtɔ daa. Esa akɛ okwɛ otso lɛ nɔ kɛ gbɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ fitemɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ.

english: How do I know if my mango trees need internal treatment rather than just surface spraying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi mango tso lɛ he miihia mligbɛ kwɛmɔ babaoo fe nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: If fruits are cracking open or rotting from the inside, it means the issue is within the tree's system, requiring a treatment that works inside the plant to fix the problem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ egbɛ eshwa loo egbo kɛjɛ emli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ naagba lɛ yɛ tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Enɛ biɔ ni atsa lɛ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ mli koni akɛtsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: What is the best way to make my mangoes strong enough to resist diseases naturally?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi-mango lɛ mli awa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ helai akpee yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Supporting your trees with balanced nutrients and defensive plant medicines helps tune their internal systems so they can automatically resist pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni ja kɛ tsei ahe tsofai fi otso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa otso lɛ mli nibii lɛ tsakeɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ eshi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning brown and looking like they were burnt by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves dry out and look burnt, it usually means the plant is losing water faster than its roots can take it up during intense heat, or the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Adding mulch around the crop helps retain moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ egbi ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight lines instead of broadcasting the seeds across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every plant gets equal access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and walking through your farm much easier.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Ehaa jwɛi shwiemɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nyiɛmɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but give me small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehaa mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients ensure the plant directs energy down into swelling the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Niyenii ni ja ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi ni ehaa bulb lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my garden pepper plants are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mibɔɔ mli pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: If pepper plants receive too much water, their roots suffocate from lack of air, causing the leaves to turn yellow and droop even when the ground is wet. Overwatering also rots the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tso lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hu haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the lower branches of my young oil palm trees turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: While older leaves naturally dry up as oil palms grow, widespread yellowing on lower branches usually means the tree lacks potassium in the soil or isn't getting enough water during dry spells.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai momo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni mu tso lɛ daa lɛ moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Enɛ haa anyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are dark spots appearing on my yam leaves and spreading across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ sweet potato baai anɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by fungal diseases like anthracnose, which thrive in hot and humid weather when water drops stay on the leaves for long periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai tamɔ anthracnose, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu mli ŋmeii hiɔ baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Does cutting off extra side branches from my tomato plants actually help them grow better?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing extra side branches allows the plant to send its water and nutrients directly to the main fruits, resulting in larger, healthier tomatoes instead of many small, weak ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomatoi lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa fe tomatoi bibii babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds produce thousands of hardy seeds that lie dormant in the soil, waiting for rain and sunlight. Because weeds are naturally adapted to tough conditions, they sprout and consume nutrients faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is too weak to feed my maize crop before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmãa dani madu?

english: If wild grasses on your land look pale green instead of dark green, or if your previous crops had thin stems and low yields, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs animal manure or fertilizer before planting.
ga: Kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse shi jeee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi awo mli dani odu.

english: How can I estimate how many bags of corn I will get from my field before harvest time comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa ni maná kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa ŋmãa lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: By counting the average number of healthy corn cobs on a few sample rows shortly before harvest, you can estimate your total yield. Knowing your expected bag count early helps you buy the right number of storage sacks, arrange transport, and plan sales ahead of time.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ fioo komɛi amli lɛ ayibɔ ni akaneɔ dani akpaa lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ osusu nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ fɛɛ he. Ni ooole kotokui ayibɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ohé kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ ayibɔ ni sa. Too gbɛfaa he gbɛjianɔ ni obaanyɛ oto jarayeli he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ

english: How do I know when my corn is mature enough and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Corn is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard and shiny. If you press a kernel with your fingernail and no milky liquid comes out, the crop has reached full maturity.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni amɛkpɛɔ Kɛji okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ nyɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ ni nu ko ni tamɔ mliki ejeee kpo. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants curl up tightly like tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a natural defense mechanism where the maize plant protects itself from losing too much water during heat stress. Once the temperature drops or the soil gets moisture, the leaves uncurl and flatten out again.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Abɛi tsei buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ he. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai lɛ baagbala ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing corn turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. The plant starves from the bottom up as it shifts its remaining nutrients to feed the top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi beni eshiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and produce small cobs when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up competing for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong and yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: What causes small holes in my corn leaves and dark dirt inside the center funnels of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that feeds on tender young leaves inside the plant funnel. Treating the crop early protects the growing point before the worm damages the developing cobs.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ baa ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ he dani ŋmeii akpata ŋmei ni miida lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my stored bags of corn turn to dust and get full of holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu eyi mli obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils and insects lay tiny eggs inside stored corn kernels, and their larvae eat the grains from the inside out. Drying your corn thoroughly and storing it in airtight bags or treated sacks prevents these pests from destroying your harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni woɔ ŋmeii Yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni ato mli Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi o-corn lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotokui ni atsa mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to leave my mature corn to dry on the stalks in the field during the rainy season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi ŋmãa momo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Leaving ripe corn in the field during rain allows water to soak into the husks, causing molds, rot, and harmful toxins to grow on the kernels. It is safer to harvest early and dry the corn off the stalk in a well-ventilated area.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha nu atsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookpa mra ni ogbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ.

english: Why does my field produce fewer bags of corn every year if I keep planting maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting maize on the same plot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your maize with crops like beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks easily fall over during light wind or rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ?

english: Corn stalks fall over easily when their root systems are shallow, weak from nutrient lack, or damaged by underground pests. Piling soil around the base of the stems during weeding strengthens root support against wind.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbɔjɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efite Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all big trees exposes them to intense heat, causing the leaves to scorch and the seedling to dry up.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat during the afternoon causes heat stress, which prevents tomato flowers from pollinating successfully. When the plant gets too hot, it sheds its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni yeɔ omanye. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ babaoo Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: Why are my crop yields getting smaller every year even though I plant on the same family land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ weku kome shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same small piece of land every season drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your crops or planting legumes like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he bibioo ko Nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa Be lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni baa shi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip of the leaf and moves down the middle in a V-shape shows that the maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ená baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and thin, but fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ lɛ, efoɔ oya lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak when planted too close together because they are competing for sunshine. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough light and room to build a thick, sturdy stem.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa la kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce small bunches when many small shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain titri lɛ daa kɛfeɔ kui bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko yɛ lɛ Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he. Nɛkɛ gbɛjianɔtoo tso nɛɛ

english: The small shoots, or suckers, attached to the base share the root system and steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce large fruit.
ga: ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ, amɛjaraa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo kome ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii wuji.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to stop losing water through its foliage. As long as the main stem stays green and healthy, the plant will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛkpa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ ji eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Heavy rains and high humidity allow the fungus that causes Black Pod disease to spread through splashing water drops. Pruning extra branches lets airflow into the farm to dry off the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa ŋmei ni kɛ blackpod hela baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha tsei lɛ agbi.

english: Why do I get small yams if I don't clear the weeds before the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani wain tsei lɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Yam vines need full sunlight and undisturbed soil nutrients to send food down into the ground to build big tubers. Weeds shade the vines and steal fertilizer, leaving you with thin, small yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu ni eyi obɔ kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni gbaaa amɛnaa lɛ koni amɛye nii amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Jwɛi haa wain tsei lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Akpɔlɔi bibii fioo komɛi pɛ eshwɛ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on soft new growth, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these small insects early prevents the plant leaves from twisting and stunting.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ anɔ. small insect control Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaatsi tso lɛ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I cut one big yam tuber into multiple small pieces to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo sweet potato tuber agbo kome mli bibii babaoo koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can cut a single healthy yam tuber into many small pieces called minisetts to plant. As long as each piece has skin and is properly treated to prevent rotting, it will sprout and grow into a full yam plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ sweet potato tuber ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli bibii babaoo, ni atsɛɔ lɛ minisettes, ni okɛdu. Shii abɔ ni fã fɛɛ fã yɛ hewolo ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekafite lɛ. Ebaakwɛ̃ ni eda ni etsɔ sweet potato tso ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I quickly produce enough seed yams to expand my farm next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo sweet potato dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa oya koni mikɛgbala miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can use the minisett technique by cutting clean yams into dozens of smaller pieces. This allows you to multiply your planting material much faster than planting whole tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mini-set ŋaa lɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ sweet potato ni he tse ni ooofo mli bibii srɔtoi babaoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ nibii ni okɛduɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya fe bulb muu ni ooodu.

english: Is it better to plant small seed yams or large yams cut into pieces?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli loo ooofolɔ ŋmeii wuji amli?

english: Small whole seed yams are often better because they do not have open cuts where rot and pests can enter. However, cut pieces from clean yams also grow very well if treated properly before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni eye emuu lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbɛ pilamɔi ni agbele ni baanyɛ agbo ni amɛha ŋmeii abote mli.Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni he tse mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why do my yams produce smaller harvests every year even when I reuse my best tubers as seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ bulb ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ akɛ dumɔwui moŋ.

english: Yams often collect hidden diseases like viruses inside the tuber over time. Reusing the same farm stock passes these hidden infections to the next generation, gradually reducing your yields every year.
ga: Sweet potatoes fɔɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii momoi tsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ aya yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha onibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi fiofio afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do viruses get inside my seed yams and how do they affect my crop?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni hela lɛ bote mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Viruses are often spread by tiny insects or infected soil and live inside the yam tissue itself. Once inside, they steal the plant's energy, causing yellowish or twisted leaves and smaller tuber growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii gbɛɔ helai amli. loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli ni ehiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli Kɛ́ amɛbote mli pɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo etsake kɛ bulb bibii.

english: If my seed yam looks healthy on the outside, can it still carry a disease into the new season?
ga: Kɛji mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ Ani ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aya be hee lɛ mli lolo?

english: Yes, many yam viruses live deep inside the tuber without showing visible rot or skin damage. Planting these infected tubers passes the virus straight into your new soil and crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato mli helai babaoo hiɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛjieee ŋmeii loo hewolo ni efite lɛ he okadi kpo. Bulbs ni hela emɔ amɛ nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ onibii heei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says seed yams were cleaned in a laboratory?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ akɛ atsuuɔ sweet potatoes he yɛ laboratorio mli?

english: Laboratory cleaning, or tissue culture, means scientists grow tiny plant cells in sterile conditions to remove hidden viruses and diseases, producing completely clean, healthy planting material.
ga: Laboratory mli saamɔ Loo fãji akusum tsɔɔ akɛ jeŋ nilelɔi kwɛɔ tsei amli wala yibii bibii. yɛ shihilɛi ni mli tseee mli koni akɛjie helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ Enɛ haa dumɔ nibii ni he tse kwraa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are some disease-free seed yams sold by extension officers so small compared to my traditional seed yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni hela bɛ mli ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ ji bibioo kwraa kɛ akɛto mishishijee dumɔwui ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: These small seed tubers are high-quality starters grown from laboratory tissue culture. Although small, they are free of internal viruses and will grow into healthy, high-yielding plants.
ga: Nɛkɛ dumɔwui bibii ayitsei nɛɛ ji nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ fãji amli yɛ laboratori lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ eji bibioo moŋ Shi ebɛ emli helai, ni ebaada ni etsɔ tso ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Will buying certified disease-free seed yams actually increase my farm's crop yield?
ga: Ani sweet potatoes ni hela bɛ mli ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ miheɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because clean seed yams do not waste energy fighting off internal diseases. They grow stronger, stay green longer, and produce significantly larger tubers at harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ efiteee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ mligbɛ helai. Amɛdaraa waa. Ehiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ ni ewoɔ bulbs wuji babaoo kɛji akpa.

english: What should I do to stop cut yam seed pieces from rotting after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: After cutting seed yams, you should treat the wet cut surfaces with wood ash or a recommended fungicide and let them dry in a shady spot so a protective skin forms before planting.
ga: Beni ofo sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu he ni ofo lɛ he nii ni efɔ lɛ. Ni ha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ená hewolo ni buɔ ehe dani adu.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun. This keeps the soil moist longer, prevents weed growth, and protects plant roots from overheating.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni amɛkadɔ tsɔ

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the tender inner whorl of maize leaves. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars feed will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa ŋmei baai amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my hot pepper plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Spraying to control these insects early keeps the foliage healthy and helps fruit grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ koni akɛye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Ewajeɔ baai lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Cassava roots need air to live and will rot if left standing in soggy, waterlogged soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to drive tall wooden sticks into the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa tso ni nɔ kwɔ nɛkɛ? Shikpɔŋ kɛha mi sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight to produce big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ehaaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This leaves you with tall, weak plants that produce smaller fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli, ni baanyɛ aha oná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii.

english: Cocoa flowers drop easily when the tree experiences stress from hot, direct sunlight or lack of soil moisture. Providing shade trees or planting plantains nearby keeps the environment cool enough for pods to form.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shading loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ bɔ ni sa ni pods baanyɛ afee.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my young tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee blɛoo lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom end rot, happen when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the fruit grow healthy.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive and burn under full, direct sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a shaded environment that keeps the air humid and the soil moist so the seedlings can establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa ni amɛshãa amɛ. Shi tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔ tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa shihilɛ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot underground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them in heavy soil without good drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season, draining the land over time. Rotating your crop by planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts every other season puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ daa be lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed manure restores the dark green color and leads to bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni dara lɛ aba.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko Yɛ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the leaf whorl during the day and feed on soft leaf tissue. Applying early-morning biological treatments or neem extracts directly into the leaf center controls them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo neem mli nu lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaakudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining consistent soil moisture with mulch and balancing fertilizer helps the flowers stay on the stem and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over easily during heavy rains right when the bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni jwɛi lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a mature fruit bunch during high winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden Y-fork prop absorbs the weight and keeps the plant standing.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni eda lɛ akui ni tsii lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tamɔ Y lɛ fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ muji shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to produce the food that swells the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil into the air, preventing leaf rot diseases and encouraging larger tuber growth.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: How do fast-growing weeds harm my crop yields during the first few weeks of planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ amli?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight before young crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds early within the first three to four weeks leaves resources available for your crop to develop strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la dani tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ enɛ baaha nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do my saved maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to germinate if they absorb moisture and grow mold during storage, or if tiny insects eat the inside embryo. Drying seeds fully and storing them in airtight containers with ash or insect control keeps them viable for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji amɛmu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi kwraa ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni sũ loo kooloi yɔɔ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ duɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop curling up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up tightly in midday heat to protect themselves from losing water. If the leaves unroll in the cool evening, the plant is surviving, but if they stay rolled up in the morning, your soil is dangerously dry and needs water.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli koni nu akaje mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ miihi wala mli, shi kɛji akɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛshwie shi leebi lɛ, no lɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ oshara nɔ, ni nu he miihia lɛ.

english: How can I keep the soil in my farm moist when there is bright sun and no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the ground around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or fallen leaves. This layer, called mulch, acts like a shade that keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ atsu nii. Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ashishifãi. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ mulch, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade ni haa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: What will happen to my maize if a hot dry spell hits while the flowers are forming?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ miifee lɛ?

english: Flowering is the most delicate stage for maize. High heat and lack of water at this time prevent effective pollination, which leads to weak cobs with missing or poorly formed grains.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni elaaje loo amɛhe bɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How long does it usually take for a plantain plant to produce mature fruits after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii ni ekwɛ̃ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: In general, a plantain sucker takes about 12 to 15 months from the day you plant it until the fruit bunch is mature and ready for harvesting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ gbi ni odu amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso yibii lɛ akui lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants bend over and break before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems often break due to heavy bunch weight, strong winds, or weak roots caused by pests. You can protect them by propping up the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden pole.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tso titri lɛ ni okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa maa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What can I do to make my plantain trees produce larger and heavier bunches?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mi-plantain lɛ afee jwɛi agbo ni tsii?

english: To get bigger bunches, prune away extra young suckers so that only 2 or 3 healthy stems remain per plant stand, and ensure the soil has plenty of organic compost or manure.
ga: Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ ŋmeii wuji anɔ lɛ Kpãa ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ahi tso kome nɔ, ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Space your plantain plants about 3 meters (10 feet) apart in all directions. Giving them enough space prevents them from shading each other out and competing for soil water and plant food.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ odumɔwui lɛ ateŋ aaafee mitai 3 (naji 10) yɛ he fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa ni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii he akaŋ.

english: Older outer leaves naturally yellow and die as the plant grows, but if many leaves yellow at once, it usually means the plant is suffering from intense sun heat, dry soil, or a lack of plant nutrients.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome lɛ Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa.

english: How do I tell if my maize field is getting too much or too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo pɛ?

english: Too little water makes maize leaves turn dull blue-green and curl tight, while too much water turns the lower leaves yellow and causes roots to rot in soggy soil.
ga: Nu fioo tsɔ baaha ŋmãa baa lɛ atsɔ bluu-ŋɔli ni egbɔjɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nu babaoo baaha shishigbɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my crops from getting ruined during intense sunshine before harvest time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu minibii ahe koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can protect young crops by providing ground cover using dry plant materials, planting temporary shade crops, and regularly clearing weeds that steal limited moisture from the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni egbi ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi ni juɔ nu fioo ko kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa lɛ adumɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and dry up when rain stops for just two weeks in the northern region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛ yɛ Kooyigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize needs a continuous supply of water to transport nutrients from the soil up to its leaves and stalks. When rain stops, the plant starves and dries out; having stored water in local dams allows you to keep watering them so they remain green and productive.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmã be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu to maŋ lɛ mli nu ŋshɔnaa lɛ, ebaaha oya nɔ okɛ nu awo mli bɔni afee ni ehi shi akɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes and peppers during the dry season instead of waiting for the main rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa?

english: Yes, you can farm year-round if you have access to water stored in dams or catchments. Crops actually thrive in the dry season because there is plentiful sunshine and fewer plant diseases, provided they get regular water.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsu okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji oyɛ nu ni ato yɛ faa loo nutoohe mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ, ni tsei ahe helai hu faaa kɛji akɛ amɛná nu daa.

english: Plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense heat. Supplying them with extra water from a nearby dam or reservoir keeps them hydrated so their leaves stay open and capture sunlight.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛfataa he kɛjɛɔ faa loo nutoohe ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai lɛ ahiɔ shi ni amɛnaa hulu la.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my fertilizer and crop seedlings down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa miifɔ mi-fertilizer kɛ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Uncontrolled rainwater rushes across the land, carrying topsoil and nutrients with it. Directing rain runoff into catchments and dams slows down the water flow, protecting your crop fields from erosion while saving that water for later use.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ nubui amli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ haa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo. Buu oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋshɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, too nakai nu lɛ koni okɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: How does giving my crops water from a dam speed up how quickly they produce flowers and fruit?
ga: Te nu ni akɛwoɔ dam mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops lack water, they stop growing to conserve energy for survival. Consistent watering from stored water reserves keeps the plant growing without interruption, helping it flower and fruit much earlier.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ nu Tsei lɛ kpaɔ amɛdalɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni akɛtoɔ he ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii oya kwraa.

english: Why does my millet survive dry weather better than my rice crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet lɛ kpɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe mi-rice tsei lɛ?

english: Millet naturally has deep roots and low water requirements, whereas rice requires constantly wet soil to grow properly. Water-loving crops like rice rely heavily on irrigation water captured in dams to survive in dry regions.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni nu ni he hiaa lɛ faaa. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa he hiaa shikpɔŋ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsei ni sumɔɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu ni aŋɔɔ yɛ nu ŋshɔi amli lɛ nɔ waa koni amɛhi shi yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops fail even when I plant right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite eyɛ mli akɛ midu kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ?

english: Rainfall in recent years has become unpredictable, often stopping suddenly right when crops are forming fruits or seeds. Storing rain in community dams creates a backup water supply to safeguard your crops when the rain unexpectedly stops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli lɛ ebafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Bei pii lɛ, ekpaa trukaa kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii miikwɛ̃ loo adu dumɔwui. Nugbɔ ni akɛtoɔ akutso lɛ mli nu ŋshɔnaa lɛ haa nu ni akɛtoɔ he ko baa koni akɛbu onibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: Why do my crops wither even when the top of the soil looks slightly damp after light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ moŋ?

english: A crop's feeding roots are situated deep under the soil, not on the surface. Light rain only wets the top layer, leaving the roots dry; deep watering using reserved dam water ensures moisture reaches the deep roots.
ga: Shishifãi ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Jeee yɛ hiɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ faa ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ shɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Will having a water supply near my farm help my yam and cassava tubers grow bigger?
ga: Ani nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaye abua ni mi-sweet potatoes kɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ adara?

english: Yes, root and tuber crops need consistent soil moisture over many months to expand underground. If the soil gets too dry, the tubers stop swelling, so access to reserved water ensures maximum tuber size.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baakpa fũu, no hewɔ lɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni anáa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ amɛdalɛ he fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are my bean plants dropping their young flowers instead of turning them into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience water stress as a defense mechanism to save their own lives. Providing reliable water from a catchment or dam keeps the soil moist so the plant retains its flowers and sets plenty of pods.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛkɛ nu mli haomɔ kpe akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala. Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nutoohei loo nu ŋshɔi amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo woɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant nutrient, or that excessive rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with thick green leaves but give me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani oooha bulb lɛ afee bibioo kɛ́ ookpa nii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of sending nutrients down to swell the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ebaai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ zugba a sisi sisi ɔ nɛ tsɔ.

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making flowers fall off prematurely before pollination can take place.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani pollination baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings scorch easily under direct sunshine; fast-growing plantain leaves create immediate shade to keep the young cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain baai ni miida oya lɛ haa hulutsoo baa amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eha kookoo bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short and bent when I plant them in flat ground instead of high mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe gɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to expand downwards easily; hard or flat ground blocks the growing tip, causing the yam to remain small or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsiɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why does planting maize seeds too close together result in thin stems and small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Crowded maize plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving insufficient energy to develop thick stems or full cobs.
ga: Abele tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ wuɔ koni hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha afee tso ni mli edɔ loo tso ni eyi obɔ.
