english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the undersides of young leaves, damaging them as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ amɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop in the hot afternoon but stand upright again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot hours, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilting to conserve moisture until temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my stored yams start producing green shoots inside the barn even before I take them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ dani mikɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams naturally enter a resting stage after harvest; once this natural dormancy period ends, warm temperatures signal the tuber to wake up and sprout roots and leaves.
ga: Sweet potatoes boteɔ wɔɔhe be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bulbs lɛ teɔ shi ni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths to feed; removing excess suckers directs all water and food from the soil straight into the main plant to build a heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛyeɔ nii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, etsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help restore the plant's healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ su eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will know it is ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack open due to the expanding roots beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaale akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves toward the sun to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposed to sunlight, which feeds the underground tuber and helps it grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni efee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akafo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ dara babaoo.

english: Why do I need to remove extra shoot sprouts growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil food. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the parent tree to direct its energy into producing bigger, heavier bunches.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei krokomɛi kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up and become small?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by very small insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli Ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the branch during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Trimming excess tree branches lets sunlight and fresh air into your farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsei lɛ aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why am I finding small holes and caterpillars in the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common caterpillar pest. You can control them early by applying organic neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments directly into the central funnel of the maize leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ mra. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ organic neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting my crops very close together give me a bigger total harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo?

english: No, planting crops too closely forces them to fight each other for water, light, and soil food, leading to thin plants and tiny harvests. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures every individual plant yields at its best.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ yɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmaa fioo pɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly watered and providing light shade during very hot afternoons helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I clear small weeds if my crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even small weeds steal nutrients and moisture from the soil through their roots beneath the surface. Clearing weeds ensures that all available plant food goes directly to your crop's development.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei aniyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashweremɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep turning yellow and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct sunlight and severe heat. Without shade plants like plantain trees nearby to block the harsh sun and keep moisture in the soil, the delicate leaves burn and the plant dries out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baashã ni tso lɛ baagbi.

english: Why does my cassava produce big green leaves above ground but tiny roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter without enough potassium, the plant spends all its food growing leaves instead of growing thick, starchy root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ starch lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are tiny green worms chewing holes in my maize leaves at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center heart of the maize plant during the bright day to avoid heat and come out in the evening to feed on tender leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he, ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and the plants stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is caused by a tiny virus spread by small white insects called whiteflies. When whiteflies feed on your tomatoes, they pass the disease into the leaves, causing them to twist and stop growing.
ga: Virus bibioo ko ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji ŋmeii ye tomato Amɛgbɛɔ hela amɛshwãa baai lɛ anɔ. ni haa etsɔ ehe ni ekpaa dalɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and turn dark at the stem root after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants dislike sitting in flooded water. Heavy rain that does not drain away starves the roots of air and allows harmful soil fungi to rot the stems and roots, causing sudden plant death.
ga: Pepper tsei sumɔɔɔ ni amɛtaraa nu afua mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni ajieee lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ tsei kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso lɛ gbele trukaa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition makes all the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu hu he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of soil water, or when there are no bees and beneficial insects around to transfer pollen so the fruit can begin to grow.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ, nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛ́ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ amɛhe. Mɛɛmɔ ni akɛ pollen lɛ aya koni aduawai lɛ aje shishi eda.

english: Why is my maize crop producing smaller cobs than it did on the same land three years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii fe nɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ nɔŋŋ afii etɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains specific nutrients out of the ground and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛfa babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local conditions, so they absorb available water, sunlight, and soil food much faster than domesticated crop plants, choking out your young crops if left unchecked.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Enɛ baagbe oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛji akɛ okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get full of tiny holes inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni eyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Small insects called grain weevils burrow inside stored corn to feed and lay eggs. If the maize is not dried completely before storage, moisture helps insect eggs hatch faster and destroys the grain.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i baanyɛ aye abua ni kooloi akui lɛ afɔ oya ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in the nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwoɔ grow bag mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa seeds lose their power to germinate very quickly once taken out of the pod. If they dry out in the sun or are buried too deep in clay soil, they cannot breathe and will rot before sprouting.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli tsɔ lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu ni amɛbaafite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ajie ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting delicate young cocoa trees from getting scorched by harsh sunlight during their first two years.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are there small worms eating holes inside the leaves and stems of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are armyworms, a common pest that attacks young maize plants. They hide deep inside the plant's funnel during the day to feed on soft leaves, which weakens the plant if not caught early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers beneath the soil are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded, the cassava puts all its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of sending food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala yitso lɛ mli

english: Why should I avoid planting my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ dumɔ he?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight, leading to thin stalks and small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ebaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess branches allows air and sunlight into the farm to dry out the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil lacks the right nutrients for my crops to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii kpakpai?

english: Signs of weak soil include crops growing very slowly, leaves turning pale yellow instead of dark green, and plants remaining small and weak even when there is enough rainfall.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ji: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: Pruning removes useless branches that steal plant food and block sunlight, allowing the cocoa tree to direct its energy into developing bigger and healthier pods on the main trunk.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ niji ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli ni tsiɔ hulu la naa lɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no bees around to move pollen within the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baajie pollen awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can survive in the dry soil for months, allowing them to absorb the first rain instantly and grow before planted crops have time to establish roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ emɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni edaa dani tso lɛ naa be ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why are my fruit trees producing very few fruits even though they look big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When a fruit tree is not pruned, it spends most of its energy feeding useless extra leaves and wild branches instead of growing fruits. Trimming those extra branches allows the tree to focus its strength on producing more fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔɛɛ aduawai tsei lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛye koo mli baai kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ niyenii yɛ aduawai ni ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ. Nakai niji krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo.

english: Will cutting branches off my fruit tree hurt the plant or kill it?
ga: Ani niji ni mifoɔ yɛ mi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: No, cutting off selected branches—known as pruning—does not hurt the tree. It actually helps the plant by removing weak or dead parts so that the tree stays healthy and grows much stronger.
ga: Dabi, niji ni ahala lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Efiteee tso lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ fãi ni bɛ hewalɛ loo egboi lɛ ni ejieɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eda waa babaoo.

english: What does tree pruning mean, and why should I do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni tso ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pruning means carefully cutting away extra, weak, or overgrown branches from a fruit tree. It is important because an unpruned tree will not yield well, while a pruned tree produces an abundant harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine, ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eda fe nine kɛjɛɔ tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ he miihia ejaakɛ tsei ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some branches on my fruit tree grow leaves but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ niji komɛi yɛ baai shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Some branches only consume water and soil nutrients without making fruit because they don't get enough sunlight or are structurally weak. Removing these unproductive branches gives the fruiting branches more food to grow good crops.
ga: Niji komɛi yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ ni amɛwooo yibii ejaakɛ amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛhe waaa. Niji ni wooo yibii nɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niji ni woɔ yibii lɛ naa niyenii babaoo koni amɛkɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to let my fruit trees grow naturally without cutting them, or should I trim them regularly?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maha mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni mifolɔɔɔ amɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mafolɔ mli daa?

english: It is much better to trim them. A tree left to grow completely naturally becomes overcrowded with branches and gives low yields, whereas regular trimming ensures high yields every harvest season.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ mli. Tsei ni ashi amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ baatsɔ tsei niji ni shwereɔ babaoo ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni afoɔ daa lɛ baaha yibii babaoo aba yɛ kpamɔ be fɛɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: How can pruning my trees help me harvest six bags of crops instead of just two?
ga: Bɔ ni Tsei ni Afoɔ lɛ Yeɔ Ebuaa Mi ni Mikpaa Nibii ni Akɛwoɔ Mli lɛ Baagi Enumɔ yɛ Enyɔ Pɛɛ Najiaŋ

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree while directing all nutrients into fruit production. This simple management practice can triple your output from two bags to about six bags.
ga: Tso lɛ he ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ewo yibii. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ afee shii etɛ kɛjɛ kotokui enyɔ mli kɛyashi aaafee kotokui enumɔ.

english: How does removing extra leaves and branches help my tree grow bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai kɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: A tree has a limited amount of food it draws from the soil. When you remove extra branches, that food is shared among fewer, healthier fruits, making them grow larger and higher in quality.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii fioo ko ni amɛgbala kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ojie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ jaa yɛ aduawai ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the main reason an unpruned fruit tree fails to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoi titri ni haa tsei ni woɔ yibii ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: An unpruned tree becomes too crowded, blocking sunlight from reaching the inner branches and spreading plant energy too thin across too many useless stems.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔko amɛhe lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ni egbɛɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ eshwaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ babaoo nɔ fioo tsɔ.

english: Why do my fruit trees need sunlight and air to pass through their middle branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ he hiaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ koni ebote eniji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Sunlight and fresh air help the tree make food and stay free from diseases. Open space inside the branch canopy allows hidden stems to get light and produce healthy fruits.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni helai akamɔ amɛ. He ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ naa la ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the very first thing I should do to improve my fruit tree farm before applying extra inputs?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ ni esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛha mi tso yibii ŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ dani mikɛ nibii krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii?

english: The very first practice to start with is proper tree pruning. Clearing out unnecessary branches prepares the tree to make the best use of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients for maximum yield.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ ofee kɛje shishi ji ni ofolɔ otso lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ saa tso lɛ he koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to show new growth after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛjieɔ dalɛ hee kpo beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If you leave a sucker untouched, it takes a very long time to emerge. However, if you cut it properly, new shoots can emerge within a month at the latest.
ga: Kɛji oshi obi lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, Ebaahe be kakadaŋŋ waa dani ebaaje kpo, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji ofolɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ŋmeii heei baanyɛ aba yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli.

english: Does cutting my planting stem in a specific place really make a difference in how fast it grows?
ga: Ani tsei ni adu yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, tracing the stem back to where it originates and cutting it at the right spot allows new growth to emerge directly and much faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akwɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ kɛtee he ni ejɛ lɛ, ni afo lɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔɔ dalɛ hee ni yaa hiɛ oya.

english: What happens if I plant my crop cuttings directly without trimming or cutting them first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei ni afo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni mifolɔko loo mifolɔko amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If you leave the cuttings without making a proper cut, they will take a very long time to break through the ground, whereas cutting them speeds up emergence significantly.
ga: Kɛji oshi tso nine ko ni ofolɔko lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Amɛbaahe be kakadaŋŋ waa dani amɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni afoɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛje kpo oya waa.

english: How long should I expect to wait for a shoot to sprout after making a clean cut on the stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ beni mifo tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When cut correctly at the right spot, a new shoot can emerge directly, taking a month at the very latest to show growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, tsei heei hu baanyɛ ada tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, eheɔ nyɔŋ kome dani etsɔɔ dalɛ.

english: How can I encourage my crops to produce new shoots much faster?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii heei oya kwraa?

english: You can speed up shoot emergence by tracing where the growth originates on the plant and making a careful cut right at that spot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha bud lɛ akwɛ̃ oya kɛtsɔ he ni dalɛ baa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. ni ofo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor cut his seed tubers before planting while I plant mine whole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ dani eduɔ yɛ be mli ni mi hu miduɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting whole tubers takes a long time to sprout, but making proper cuts at the origin points allows new growth to emerge within a month.
ga: Bulb muu ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni ejɛɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii heei aba yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli.

english: If I want to trim my crop to make it sprout, how do I know where to cut?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni mafo tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: You should trace the growth back to the exact place where it originates; cutting it at that correct location ensures the shoot emerges directly.
ga: Esa akɛ otao dalɛ lɛ mli kɛya he ni eba lɛ. Kɛ́ afo lɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ atswaa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my cassava stems sprout immediately while others take months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Stems that are traced and cut at the correct origin points will emerge directly and quickly, while uncut or poorly cut stems take a very long time.
ga: Tsoi ni agbala ni afo yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaje kpo tɛ̃ɛ oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni afolɔko loo afolɔko jogbaŋŋ lɛ baahe be kakadaŋŋ waa.

english: Will making a cut on my plant stump hurt it or help it shoot up faster?
ga: Ani mitso lɛ shishifã ni mifo lɛ baafite lɛ loo ebaaye ebua ni eda oya?

english: Making a proper cut where the growth originates does not hurt it; it actually encourages the new shoot to emerge within a month at the latest.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni edaa lɛ, ekɛ nɔ ko fiteee. Ewoɔ hewalɛ koni ajie sini lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli kɛ hoo lɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to trace where a sucker starts before I cut it for propagation?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni akwɛ he ni suckers lɛ je shishi yɛ dani afo amɛ koni amɛfɔ bii?

english: Yes, tracing the sucker to its point of origin ensures you cut it in the right place, which makes a huge difference in how quickly it emerges.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ sucker lɛ sɛɛ kɛtee he ni ejɛɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ofoɔ lɛ yɛ he ni sa. Enɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa bɔ ni ejeɔ kpo oya lɛ mli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the food crops use to stay green and grow leaves. When the soil runs low on food, the plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni akɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ahe. Kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my maize whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: These worms are called Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and moist to eat the tender green leaves before they unfold.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ, he ni amɛfeɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I wait for steady rain before planting my seeds instead of planting right after the first shower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often dries up quickly. If seeds sprout after one rain and dry weather follows, the young roots will dry out and die. Waiting for continuous rain makes sure the soil stays wet enough to keep seedlings alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rain stays on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe just like people do. When water logs the farm and cannot drain away, it fills all the air spaces in the soil, causing the roots to drown and rot.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Yam leaves make food for the underground tuber using direct sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows leaves to catch more light and keeps them away from wet soil where fungal rot spreads.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã nɔ lɛ akabɔ he.

english: Why should I place fertilizer in a small ring around the crop base instead of broadcasting it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko mli yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop gets to drink the plant food directly. Scattering it all over the farm wastes money because rain washes it away and feeds surrounding weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ nuɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, eheɔ shika ejaakɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ lɛ ni eyeɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives pests a permanent home. Switching to crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nutrients and starves maize pests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha kooloi bibii lɛ ahi shi daa Ni atsakeɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or lack of soil moisture. When pepper plants feel weak from heat, they drop their flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji pepper tso lɛ nu he akɛ egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that greedily steal soil food and drinking water away from your crops. Clearing weeds early leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni kɛ hiɛjoomɔ juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu ni anuɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to grow strong leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the same nutrients out of the soil and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts goodness back into the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai baa shi Ebaanyɛ ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ kpakpafeemɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that grows easily in damp, dark, and warm weather during heavy rains. Pruning dense leaves to let sunlight and wind reach the trunk, and removing affected pods early, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni ojie pods ni ena naagba lɛ mra. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a sickness carried by these insects. Spraying your plants with neem water or insecticidal soap helps get rid of these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels stressed from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of calcium in the ground. Keeping the soil evenly moist and placing mulch around the base of the plant helps protect the flowers so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce large broad leaves that provide gentle shade and keep the soil moist around young cocoa trees while they are getting established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo be blɛoo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to make soft, high soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow under the ground and need loose, deep soil to expand freely. Making high mounds gives the roots space to grow long, thick, and smooth without fighting hard or compacted soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛshwere amɛhe. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ akpee.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable plants help them survive the heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-vegetable tsei lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass around your crops creates a cover called mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the dirt, protects the soil from hot sunshine, and stops weeds from growing and stealing food from your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni ooogbɛ ashwã Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the type. You will notice the lower leaves on the stalk turning yellow and falling off, and small cracks appearing in the dirt near the stem as the tubers grow bigger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How often should I water my crop seeds after planting them in my nursery bed?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo aduawai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need moist soil to sprout, but too much water rots them. Watering lightly twice a day—once early in the morning and once late in the afternoon—keeps the soil damp enough for sprouting without drowning the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi nu babaoo baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ fioo shii enyɔ daa gbi—leebi kɛ shwane ekoŋŋ lɛ—haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieee nu mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees suffer when I cut down all the shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Removing all shade trees exposes young cocoa to harsh sunlight and excessive heat, which dries out the canopy and stresses the plant, reducing its ability to bear healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ pods ni mli wa lɛ baa shi

english: Why is it bad to cut away too many upper branches from my fruit trees during pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ ooofolɔ mi tso lɛ nine ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni afoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing too many top branches uncovers the tree's inner stem to intense sunlight, which can burn the bark and weaken the tree's overall fruit production.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi niji babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mligbɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hulu la ni naa wa waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ yibii ashã ni eha tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my cassava plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Trimming excess branches reduces the leafy canopy, forcing the plant to send its food energy down into the ground to grow bigger tuber roots.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ashishifã lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tsei tsuɔ niyenii hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛwo shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my cocoa trees get more black pod disease when the leaves and branches become too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ aná black pod hela waa yɛ be mli ni baai kɛ amɛniji lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: A dense leaf cover traps moisture and blocks air flow, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How does trimming dead or weak branches help my tomato plants produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-tomato tso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji?

english: Removing weak parts stops the plant from wasting nutrients on useless leaves and directs those nutrients directly into forming larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ akafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I scrape away all the weeds and leave the ground uncovered?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ shwie shi ni mikɛ nɔ ko wooo mli?

english: Leaving soil bare exposes topsoil directly to heavy rains and hot sun, which washes away good nutrients and destroys the soil structure.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashɛ nɔ. Enɛ baajie niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: Why do the top roots of my yam tubers turn hard and stop growing when exposed to the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekpaa dalɛ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need dark, moist underground conditions to expand; direct sunlight hardens the growing head of the tuber and stunts its growth.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli efɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha bulb ni miida lɛ mli awa ni ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather suddenly becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a self-defense mechanism to save water and survival energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily after they grow heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni ekwɛ aduawai akuu ko ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and a top-heavy structure, so when the heavy canopy and fruit bunch grow without support, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli edɔ ni aduawai akui lɛ dara ni nɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when heavy rain floods the farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Flooded soil starves the roots of air and washes away nitrogen nutrients, making it impossible for the plant to keep its leaves green and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaafɔ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehe wa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and strength. It often happens when heavy rain washes away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that work with good bacteria in the ground to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Heavy rains will wash the fertilizer off the field or push it too deep into the ground before the crop roots can drink it in, which wastes your money and leaves the plant without food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii atsɔ ŋmɔji amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why do my garden vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In the hot afternoon heat, plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. They wilt on purpose to protect themselves from losing more moisture, and they usually recover when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjɛɔ yiŋtoo mli amɛgboiɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the rainy season stays too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When the ground stays flooded with water for a long time, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus carried by those insects that stunts the crop's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ woɔ ni haa tsei kpaɔ amɛdalɛ nɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the growing fruit does not get enough calcium, which usually occurs when watering is irregular or the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa lɛ kɛ́ aduawai ni miida lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree gets stressed by dry winds or hot weather, or if there are not enough tiny insects called midges around to carry pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ pollen baajɛ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛya ekroko mli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines and keep them off the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ tso nɔ ni mikɛ amɛ kpaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make the food that grows big tubers under the earth. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and protects the vine from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bulb agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he, ni ebuɔ wain tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots to anchor them securely in the soil. When a heavy fruit bunch grows at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs wooden props to support its weight against the wind.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ amɛ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji aduawai akuu ko ni tsii kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋwɛi Tsei lɛ ji ŋwɛi-tsii ni biɔ tso nibii ni akɛfiɔ muji lɛ sɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to grow strong stalks and produce larger corn ears.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa toi wuji baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can get maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Lifting leaves off the damp ground also prevents foliage diseases and pest damage, resulting in much larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛjie amɛhe tsei lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai kɛ nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ anaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why should I remove extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi tsɔne titri lɛ

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around one plantain tree, they will steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring a heavy, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, dumɔwu kome Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tso ni tsii ni he wa.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for growing green leaves and healthy stems. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ tsei ni wa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the top of the soil into streams or push it too deep into the ground below root level. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots can absorb it before heavy water carries it away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aho kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ kɛya faai amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ dani tsɔne ni tsii lɛ aŋɔ lɛ kɛya.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under hot sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your vegetable bed.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha o-vegetables shikpɔji lɛ anɔ

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a destructive pest that lays eggs on tender leaves. The caterpillars feed on the growing tip of the plant, which can destroy the crop if not spotted early and controlled with recommended sprays or botanical treatments.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ lɛ. Kplukai yeɔ tsei ashishifãi. ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akadiko mra. ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei amli lɛ kudɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when the rainy season gets too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air spaces in heavy soils, starving roots of oxygen and creating wet conditions where fungal diseases thrive. This causes the starch in cassava tubers to break down and rot before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Tomatoes often drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. When the plant feels threatened by harsh weather, it drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa miiwo amɛhe gbeyei lɛ Ebaashɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to hire trained helpers or instructors just to plant rubber seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ yelikɛbualɔ loo tsɔɔlɔ ko ni atsɔse lɛ koni ekɛdu rɔbɔt dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rubber seedlings have delicate roots that can easily bend or break if planted incorrectly. Trained planters ensure the taproot goes straight down and the tree is set at the right depth so it grows strong and healthy.
ga: Rɔba dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni baanyɛ abɔle loo akumɔ oya kɛji aduuu amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Abɔɔ mli nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ lɛ baaha taproot lɛ agbee shi tɛ̃ɛ. ni tso lɛ yɛ he ni mli kwɔ ni sa. Koni tso lɛ adara ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ

english: Can I plant food crops like maize or cassava between my rubber trees when they are still young?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi rɔba tsei lɛ ateŋ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping short-season crops like maize or legumes during the first two years gives you food and income while the young rubber trees grow, and it also helps suppress weeds on your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei lɛ miida lolo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why must I leave so much distance between rubber trees when planting them on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ gum tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishia lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rubber trees grow tall with large bushy tops. Leaving adequate space (usually about 6 meters by 3 meters) allows each tree to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to produce thick bark for high latex yields.
ga: Rɔba tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi agbo ko yɛ eyiteŋ. Kɛji akɛ ashi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa (bei pii lɛ, aaafee mitai 6 x mitai 3) lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse aba kɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo.

english: What kind of soil is best if I want to start growing rubber trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi rɔbɔt tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Rubber trees thrive in deep, well-drained soils that hold moisture but do not collect standing water. Waterlogged soils cause root rot, while shallow or rocky soils prevent the trees from rooting deeply.
ga: Rɔba tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ shi ehiɛɛɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo tɛi tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: How many years does it take from the day I plant a rubber tree until I can start harvesting from it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ rɔba lɛ dani ajeɔ ŋmaakpamɔ shishi?

english: Rubber trees generally take between 6 to 7 years to reach maturity. They are ready to be tapped for latex once the trunk grows to about 50 centimeters in circumference.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa. Efee klalo akɛ ebaatswa rɔba lɛ beni tso lɛ da kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 50 lɛ he.

english: Why does a rubber tree bleed white liquid when its bark is cut?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ afo rɔbɔt tso ko mli lɛ, lá hoɔ yɛŋ?

english: The white liquid is called latex, and it is the tree's natural defense system to heal wounds. Specialized tubes inside the trunk bark store this latex, which flows out safely when shallow cuts are made.
ga: Atsɛɔ nu yɛŋ lɛ akɛ latɛs. ni eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo kɛha pilamɔi tsamɔ. Pai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ latɛs lɛ toɔ. ni baajɛ mli aba shweshweeshwe kɛ́ pilamɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ

english: How can I tell if my young rubber trees are growing healthy or if they are sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi rɔba tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ loo hela mɔ lɛ?

english: Healthy young rubber trees produce deep green leaves, grow new leaf shoots regularly, and have a smooth, upright stem without dark spots, fungal growths, or leaf yellowing.
ga: Gum tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. Baai heei jeɔ kpo daa. ni eyɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ja, ni ŋmeii diji, ŋmeii, loo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young rubber trees need fertilizer even if the land was previously fertile forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni rɔbɔt tsei he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lolo lɛ? No mli lɛ, no ji koo ni yɔɔ nii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer gives young trees an extra boost of essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus, helping them build a thick trunk much faster so you can start tapping earlier.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa tsei ni mli tse oya kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oje shishi oya.

english: Why shouldn't I cut or tap my rubber trees during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ afoɔ rɔba tsei loo atswaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Rainwater washes away the fresh latex liquid before you can collect it, and moisture entering open bark cuts increases the risk of fungal infections that can permanently damage the tree.
ga: Nugbɔ nu baaho latɛs lɛ he dani obaanyɛ obua naa. Ni ŋmɔtɔ ni boteɔ tso lɛ yibii ni afo mli lɛ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baanyɛ afite tso lɛ kɛya naanɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: For how many years can a single rubber tree keep producing latex once it starts yielding?
ga: Afii enyiɛ rɔbɔt tso kome baanyɛ aya nɔ afee latɛs kɛji ebɔi feemɔ pɛ?

english: If the bark is tapped carefully without damaging the wood inside, a single rubber tree can continue producing latex steadily for 25 to 30 years.
ga: Kɛji otswa tso lɛ yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee tso lɛ, Rɔba tso kome baanyɛ ajie latɛs be fɛɛ be afii 25 kɛyashi 30.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa protects tender leaves from burning and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baabu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their young crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and rots into natural fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green growth. Adding NPK fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking the plant sap. Spraying early with neem oil water or approved crop protection stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baakpa shwiemɔ.

english: When the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, tomato plants get stressed and drop their blossoms to save water. Consistent watering early in the morning helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tomato tsei lɛ feɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in heavy soil around them. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas or beans alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better while giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to produce the food required for growing large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support the weight of a heavy fruit bunch during storms. Supporting the stems with bamboo forks or strong wooden poles keeps them upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ ahum be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi jaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why is it important to cut away the dead, dry fronds from my oil palm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni egbi kɛ gbohii kɛjɛ mi-oil palm tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning dry fronds allows sunlight and air to reach the center of the palm, prevents pests from nesting, and makes harvesting the ripe oil palm bunches much easier and safer.
ga: Fern tsei ni egbi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ ŋmeii. ni ehaa mu tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to grow. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the leaves back their green color so the maize can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ Nitrogen babaoo loo kooloi aŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does adding animal manure or decomposed dry leaves help my crops survive when the rains stop for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi aŋmei loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Organic materials like manure and compost act like sponges underground. They hold moisture in the soil for much longer, allowing your crops to keep drinking water even during short dry spells.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu ni anuɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft center of young maize plants. Treating the center of the plant early with ash, neem oil solution, or recommended sprays stops them from destroying the farm.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ni akɛ sũ, neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he nii mra Ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ akafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting and smelling bad under the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the soil runs out of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I plant too many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight over the same water, light, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to drink, feed, and grow thick stalks with good harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enu nu, eye niyenii ni ekwɛ tsei ni mli wa, ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched under direct harsh sunlight. Leaving mature shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains beside young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from intense heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and watered regularly helps the flowers stay on the plant and form healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce much smaller yields at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast runners that steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly from your crops' roots. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks of growth leaves all the food and water for your crops to produce heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji kooloi ni joɔ foi oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up in the land. Rotating maize with beans or cowpeas refills the soil with natural nitrogen and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Tse kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná nitrogen ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous hybrid maize harvest produce weaker crops than new seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mitsutsu ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields for only one harvest cycle. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special strength traits, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be kome mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when there is no plantain planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides temporary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tip and moving down the middle channel of maize leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa lɛ naagbee kɛyashiɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji ni atsɔ hiɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small leaf nodes with buds that must point upward. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow backward before reaching light, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber yield.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya sɛɛ dani amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to use stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso he hiaa mi koni manyɛ makwɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high into the sunlight and improves airflow, which helps the leaves make more food to feed large underground tubers and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp ground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. ni etsi tso helai ni hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers without developing them into mature pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛdarako ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eda lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed as pods. Lack of rainfall, poor soil nutrients, or low populations of tiny pollinating midges can also cause excess flower dropping.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ aye akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ faaa Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo tsɔ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: Extra suckers compete with the main plantain plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant grows strong and produces large fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. Planting too early can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the soil dries out completely before the main rainy period begins.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival strategy for cassava to stop losing water during hot dry weather. Once the rains return, the plant uses energy stored in its roots to grow new leaves.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛkpa nu ni elaajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai heei.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look droopy in the hot afternoon even though I watered the soil in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso be mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbi lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself and usually recovers in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ehe he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to dry up faster during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that suck up moisture and fertilizer from the soil much faster than your crops, leaving your main plants without the water they need to survive dry periods.
