ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ bɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow on land that was previously dug up or cleared by heavy machinery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii tsuɔ nii loo ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery strips away the rich topsoil where crops get their primary nutrients. It also compacts the ground so tightly that plant roots cannot easily spread or absorb water.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii jieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ, he ni tsei lɛ naa amɛ niyenii titrii lɛ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo amɛŋɔ nu mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops dry up and turn yellow when I water them with muddy stream water near disturbed mining areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ faa ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ he ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle he lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Water from streams disturbed by earth-moving carries heavy sediment and toxic chemical runoff that smothers root systems and prevents crops from absorbing clean water and food from the soil.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ faai amli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nyiɛmɔ gbalaa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni hoɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop roots remain short and stubby instead of growing deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ kuku lolo ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil becomes overly acidic or contaminated by chemical runoff, the delicate tips of the roots are burned, stopping them from penetrating deep into the ground to anchor the plant.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo acid tsɔ loo tsofai ni hoɔ lɛ efite lɛ. Abaashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyaye tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow bushy leaf tops but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has an excess of nitrogen or rich manure, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves above ground rather than storing energy in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmei babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough resources to produce thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and naturally deposit it back into the ground, restoring soil fertility for the next crop cycle without costly artificial fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa afee.

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the central vein of older leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency, meaning the crop has used up the available nitrogen food in the soil.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi yɛ amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with small powders left in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni eshwɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hide inside the central leaf funnel during the day and chew on tender young leaves as they form.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. ni okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii beni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into fruit during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When weather becomes extremely hot and dry, pepper plants shed their blossoms to conserve water and protect themselves from dying, sacrificing fruit production to survive the heat.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛnibii ashã afɔle bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen. As the plant grows, it moves available nitrogen to the new top leaves to keep growing, causing the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa ŋwɛi baai heei anɔ koni eha baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that work with good bacteria in the soil to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, this natural nitrogen stays in the soil and feeds the maize planted afterwards.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ bacteria kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa ni adu sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I avoid spreading fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the surface of the soil or pushes it too deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not during heavy downpours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain nearby provides a natural umbrella that protects the young cocoa and keeps the soil moist until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space allows them to grow strong stalks and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam plants produce vines that need sunlight to create energy for root growth. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more sunlight and preventing foliage diseases, which helps grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei woɔ wain tsei ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enaa hulu la babaoo ni etsiɔ foliar hela naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha yitso lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my cassava plants during the first three months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe hiaa mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly during their first three months and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water and nutrients. Keeping the farm clean early on allows the cassava to establish strong roots.
ga: Kasava tsei bibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Ni oooha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Pepper plants often shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during peak heat can help the plant retain its blossoms and grow fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit while it forms. Irregular watering prevents the roots from taking up calcium properly, so maintaining steady soil moisture prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ mli baa yɛ be mli ni efeɔ lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná calcium ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ calcium he.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the soil upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the crop is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the food crops use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when too much rain washes nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji tso niyenii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of crops that take natural food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil and feeds the next crop you plant there.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving small dark dropped dirt inside the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni miiha buji lɛ miigba mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni amɛmiishi muji fioo ko ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ? yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by a pest called Fall Armyworm. The young caterpillars hide inside the center of the corn plant where they chew the soft leaves before the leaves unfurl.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the leaves and spreading viruses, or by severe hot weather causing the plant to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni haa tsei kwɛɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the heat is too strong, when the air is too dry, or when they do not get enough water. Without proper conditions, the flowers cannot form seeds and turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Kɛji shihilɛi ni sa bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui ni amɛtsɔmɔ aduawai.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. When you stake them, the leaves spread out into the sunlight easily, which helps the plant send more energy down to swell the yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Beni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shi koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ashwere yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat and keep the soil damp while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small when I plant the stems too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for soil food and water, leaving none of the plants with enough energy to grow thick tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs ni mli tse lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and short even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ kuku kɛji nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your crops need to grow strong. Even with rain, the crops are starved because the weeds take the food first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nii klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after light rain. Do not apply it right before heavy rains, as water will wash the fertilizer away before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Kaaha okɛtsu nii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize pulls a lot of food out of the soil. Beans and leguminous plants work with natural microbes to grab nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, refreshing your field for the next planting season.
ga: Abele gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beans kɛ legumes kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔji lɛ afee ehee kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall green leaves but producing tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much water early on, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing branches and leaves instead of storing energy down in the roots to make big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli mra lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa eniji kɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and causing the center of the plant to die?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Ni eha tso lɛ mli fã lɛ agbo?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize and chew through them. Applying natural remedies like neem solution or recommended biopesticides early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch sunlight to feed the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot, damp ground, preventing leaves from rotting and allowing the plant to build larger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Rolling leaves is a self-defense trick maize uses to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf area exposed to the sun and slows down water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hebuu ŋaa ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛbu nu he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ baa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow with dark spots and dying from the bottom up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: This is a fungal disease called early blight, which spreads in hot, damp weather when rain splashes soil onto lower leaves. Removing infected lower leaves and mulching around the plant stems helps prevent it.
ga: Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ early blight. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni akɛ muji awo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: Why does striga weed keep appearing on my cereal farm and killing my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ miŋmaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Striga attaches its roots directly to crop roots to suck out their water and nutrients. Its seeds can stay alive in dry soil for years, so rotating your field with cowpeas or groundnuts helps clear the soil.
ga: Striga lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Edumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ afii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads fast in wet, humid conditions. You can reduce it by pruning crowded branches to let sunlight and air in, and removing infected pods promptly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ oba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli lɛ nɔ. ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the salts around the root zone, which can burn and damage the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ekome yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei

english: Why shouldn't I burn my farm bush after clearing the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ beni mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material, kills helpful organisms like earthworms, and dries out the ground. Leaving the cleared plants to decay naturally adds free nutrients back into the soil and helps retain moisture for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very slow and stay weak when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like hungry neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and excessive heat. Without shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to provide cover, the hot sun scorches the leaves and dries out the roots, causing the seedlings to die.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he waa. Kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni kwɛɔ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji dumɔwui lɛ agbele.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close to each other, their leaves block out sunlight and their roots compete for soil nutrients and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough light and food to grow faster and yield larger bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ kui wuji aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen. Even with plenty of rain, plants cannot thrive in exhausted soil, so adding manure, compost, or fertilizer is needed to restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the plant grows very tall with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? He ni sweet potato tsei lɛ daa waa ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted in very hard soil, it spends all its energy growing tall leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Loosening the soil and avoiding excess nitrogen encourages the plant to form bigger tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajie nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and covered in small white flies?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and spreading viral diseases. Controlling whiteflies early using soapy water sprays or recommended treatments protects the leaves and saves the tomato yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ baa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Kɛ akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ shwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe ni ehere tomato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, irregular watering, or excessive root heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛna haomɔ, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa ni mli edɔ waa lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo la ni mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwo mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch that bakes the soil heat back up. Planting too early causes seeds to get trapped in dry, hot soil and rot before steady rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. ni egboɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ yaa nɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting quickly when stored in the barn during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot easily if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, unventilated areas. Storing undamaged yams on raised racks in a cool, shady barn with good airflow keeps them dry and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ atomɔ ni mli ewo muji ato adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ tsũ ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa egbiɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the tree. This helps the tree direct its energy into growing healthy flowers and bigger cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabi ni akɛ baai krokomɛi afata he.

english: How do I know the right time of the year to prune my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Pruning is usually done before the major rainy season begins. Doing it at this time prepares the trees to absorb nutrients and produce fresh leaves and pods when the rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afoɔ tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ jeɔ shishi. Enɛ feemɔ saa tso lɛ he koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii heei aba kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to spray chemicals on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals helps protect your cocoa trees from pests like mirids (capsids) and fungal diseases like black pod disease, which can destroy your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Tsofai ni okɛshwieɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela, ni baanyɛ afite o-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemicals to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai awo cacao mli?

english: Chemicals are best applied early in the morning or late in the afternoon when insects are active and the sun isn't too hot, usually at the start of the wet season when pests and fungal diseases spread fastest.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai atsu nii leebi loo shwane mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii ni hulu lɛ edɔɔɔ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee ji be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Can using too many chemicals damage my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite mi cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, using more chemical than recommended can burn the leaves and flowers, waste your money, and kill friendly insects that help pollinate your cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha baai kɛ fɔfɔi ashã. Shika ni afiteɔ ni ogbeɔ naanyobɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni okɛ pollination woɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What preparations should I make on my cocoa farm before the flowering season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ hesaamɔi esa akɛ mafee yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before flowering, you should prune extra branches, clear weeds from around the tree bases, and inspect for diseases so the trees are healthy enough to hold and support the new flowers.
ga: Dani obaawo fɔfɔi lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni okwɛ kɛji hela ko yɛ mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ emɔ fɔfɔi heei ni ekɛfi sɛɛ.

english: What basic methods can I use to make my cocoa trees produce more yield this year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii manyɛ matsɔ nɔ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ?

english: Combining proper pruning, timely weed clearing, correct chemical spraying for pests, and keeping the soil nourished will give your trees the strength to produce more pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ he Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be ni sa mli Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni oooha lɛ baaha otso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, dark, and overly shaded conditions on the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo fe nine yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How does clearing tall weeds under my cocoa trees help prevent disease?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa?

english: Tall weeds trap moisture and create a damp environment where diseases thrive. Clearing them allows air to flow freely near the ground, keeping the farm dry and healthier.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai shwereɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie he lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Fully grown cocoa trees need light shade. Too much shade prevents the tree from getting sunlight to make pods, while too little shade can cause the soil to dry out and stress the tree.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo. Shade babaoo baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná hulu la ni ekɛfee ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to when my father first planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni Ataa du lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees heavy-feed on soil nutrients over decades. Without replacing these nutrients using fertilizers or organic matter, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to lower yields as trees age.
ga: Cocoa tsei eye sũ mli niyenii babaoo afii nyɔŋmai abɔ nɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsakeee niyenii nɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite, ni no baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does cleared forest land grow crops so well at first, but then struggles after just a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ? Shi yɛ afii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ani eji nɔmɔ?

english: Forest soil has a rich top layer made of decayed leaves and natural compost. Once cleared and exposed to heavy sun and rain, those rich nutrients quickly wash away or burn off.
ga: Koo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi fã ni baai ni fiteɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa nɛɛ shwieɔ shi loo shãa oya.

english: How do I know if my farmland has become too tired to support fresh cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ makwɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: If young seedlings turn yellow, dry up easily despite rainfall, or fail to grow deep roots, your soil has lost the essential nutrients and organic matter cocoa needs to establish.
ga: Kɛji tso bibioo lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po loo enyɛɛɛ etswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miifite niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa ni kookoo ema lɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees stop giving big fruit bunches as they grow very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ kpaɔ yibii wuji beni eda waa lɛ?

english: As oil palms age and grow tall, it takes more energy for nutrients and water to reach the canopy, causing fruit production to naturally drop off compared to younger trees.
ga: Beni mu tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ, eheɔ hewalɛ babaoo dani niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ baashɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he. Enɛ haa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛto tsei bibii ahe.

english: Can I grow oil palm and cocoa together on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ mu kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is not recommended because mature oil palms cast very dense shade and have strong shallow roots that steal water and nutrients away from cocoa trees.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ mu tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli.

english: If I plant only cocoa across my entire farm, will it ruin the land for other crops in the future?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi wɔsɛɛ?

english: Growing a single crop continuously drains specific nutrients and allows specialized soil pests to build up, making it harder for other crops to grow later without soil treatment.
ga: Tso kome pɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa sũ mli nibii krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei krokomɛi akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do diseases spread so fast when everyone in my community grows only cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela lɛ miigbɛ eshwa oya nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ duɔ kookoo pɛ lɛ?

english: When the same crop covers continuous stretches of land, diseases and pests can move freely from tree to tree without natural plant barriers to stop them.
ga: Beni tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ha shikpɔŋ ko ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ ni adebɔɔ mli tsei ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: If I cut down my unproductive cocoa trees, can I immediately plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact same holes?
ga: Kɛ mifo kookoo tso ni wooo yibii lɛ, Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwu hee yɛ nakai bu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, because the soil in those exact spots is depleted of nutrients and may harbor fungal pests from the old roots. It is best to treat the soil or plant cover crops first.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai hei pɔtɛɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ shishifãi momoi amli lɛ ahi shi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii loo oooha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why is it getting harder to find wild oil palm growing naturally in our area like it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa fe tsutsu lɛ akɛ aaana koo mli mu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As more land was cleared permanently for crops like cocoa, the natural forest conditions and moist soil that allowed wild oil palms to sprout naturally were lost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii kɛya naanɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo lɛ, adebɔɔ mli koo mli shihilɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni haa koo mli mu tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ laajeɔ.

english: How can I prepare land that was used for cocoa for thirty years so that oil palm can grow well on it?
ga: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔsaa shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ kookoo afii nyɔŋmai etɛ nɛ lɛ koni mu tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: You need to clear old stump roots, add organic manure or plant nitrogen-fixing cover crops for a season, and allow the soil time to rebuild its structure and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi momo ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nitrogen-fixing mulch afata he kɛha be kome. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa egbɛjianɔtoo kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants start turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. It can happen when the soil is poor, or when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Ebaanyɛ eba be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the plant's juices and spread viruses. Protecting plants early with proper sprays or natural pest barriers keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do caterpillars end up inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ bote mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli?

english: Night-flying moths lay tiny eggs directly on young leaves. When the eggs hatch into Fall Armyworms, the caterpillars crawl into the central funnel of the plant to feed where they are safe from birds.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni foɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ fɔɔ wɔji bibii. tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai bibii anɔ Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ he ko ni okpoi nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when rain falls heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long without draining, microorganisms multiply and rot the roots underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛgboɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: If I save seeds from my best maize harvest this year, why won't they grow as strong next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ to afi nɛɛ Mɛni hewɔ ehiɛɛɛ hewalɛ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Many modern high-yield seeds are hybrid breeds. While the first crop produces big yields, seeds saved from that harvest lose their original strength and produce smaller, weaker plants in the next generation.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Yɛ be mli ni klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛshishijee hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a sudden lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to preserve energy and survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam tubers grow sideways or bend when they hit hard, compact soil or stones beneath the mound. Loosening the earth deeply before planting creates a soft path for the tuber to grow straight down.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa afã loo amɛkotoɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ lɛ haa gbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo baa koni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than deep down. As the heavy bunch of plantains grows, the plant becomes top-heavy and wind easily pulls the shallow roots out of wet ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ fe bɔ ni mli kwɔ. Beni plantains babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe awo hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ amli oya

english: Why does my land produce less food each time I plant the same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Every crop pulls specific nutrients out of the earth. Planting the exact same crop repeatedly drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ atsɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ama ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why does my heap of fresh cocoa beans get hot and start steaming after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii heei lɛ mli edɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: The heat and steam are signs that your cocoa beans are fermenting correctly. Beneficial microbes eat the sweet pulp around the fresh seeds, generating natural heat that kills the germ inside the bean and creates the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ lasu ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa yibii lɛ miiho jogbaŋŋ. Nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ yeɔ loo ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ŋmeii heei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave my harvested cocoa pods directly on the wet ground before breaking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛkuɔ?

english: Leaving harvested pods on damp soil allows moisture and soil fungi to enter the pod. This causes the pods to rot faster and can spoil the beans inside before you even get the chance to ferment them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli ŋmeii abote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbo oya, ni ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani oná hegbɛ po ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli.

english: How does groundwater or damp soil damage cocoa beans when I dry them?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ shishi nu loo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ fiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ migbi amɛ?

english: If cocoa beans absorb moisture from the ground while drying, they will grow dark mold on the inside, smell bad, and lose their market value. That is why cocoa should always be dried on raised mats above the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ, no lɛ Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ emli, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ni amɛhe jara waaa yɛ jara nɔ. No hewɔ ni esa akɛ agbi kookoo yɛ tsɔji ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why do the cocoa pods on my trees turn black and soft when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rainwater and cool damp conditions encourage black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet weather and rots the pods directly on the tree.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does the ground under my cocoa trees stay cool and damp even on sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mikookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ po mli lɛ?

english: A thick layer of fallen leaves acts as a natural mulch blanket on the soil. It blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, and traps moisture in the soil so the roots have water during dry periods.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi ni mli tse lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni eha shishifãi lɛ aná nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from hot temperatures. Dropping leaves reduces the amount of moisture the tree loses through its foliage.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni tso lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it safe to leave rotten, diseased cocoa pods lying on the farm soil?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni efite ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, rotten pods left on the ground carry fungal spores that can splash onto healthy trees during rainfall, spreading disease throughout your entire farm.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashwie tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the big shade trees around them grow too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ daraa lɛ? edaa tsɔ

english: Too much shade prevents sunlight from reaching the cocoa leaves, reducing the tree's ability to make food. Heavy shade also traps moisture, making it easier for pod diseases to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be babaoo lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ kookoo baai lɛ ahe. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tsei yɔɔ ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Shade ni mli tse lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow when water collects around the stem after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa lɛ? Trunk yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates cocoa roots by cutting off their oxygen supply. When roots drown, they cannot send nutrients to the rest of the tree, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ bote nu mli lɛ Enyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa beans feel cold to the touch in the early morning before I dry them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ kɛji mɔ ko ta he leebi dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Overnight temperatures drop and dew moisture settles on the beans, cooling them down before the morning sun begins to heat them up again for drying.
ga: Dɔlɛ lɛ ba shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpɛtɛ kɔfe yibii lɛ ahe. Ha kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ afee fɛ̃i dani leebi hulu lɛ aje shishi edɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ koni amɛgbi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains provides fast-growing temporary shade that protects the young cocoa trees and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why can't I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other so I can harvest more pods on my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ manyɛ makpa pods babaoo yɛ mihe bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, while their branches block sunlight from reaching each other. This competition leaves all the trees weak and produces fewer pods overall.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei aniji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are drowning in waterlogged soil. When roots cannot breathe or feed properly, the plant loses its green color and growth slows down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ baafite eŋɔli su ni edalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal attack known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in high humidity and excess wetness. The rain splashes the fungus onto the pods, turning them black and destroying the beans inside.
ga: Fuŋɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine yɔɔ lɛ. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ diŋ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of some of my cocoa trees swell up and stop bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi akutsei lɛ fuɔ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a major symptom of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus blocks water and nutrients from moving through the tree, causing it to produce fewer pods and eventually die.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi titri. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Virus lɛ tsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ faaa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the young shoots on my cocoa trees to dry up and look burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã lɛ?

english: These insects are called capsids or 'Akate.' They pierce the stems and leaves to suck out plant juices and inject toxic saliva, which kills the young tissues and makes the shoots look scorched by fire.
ga: Atsɛɔ kooloi nɛɛ akɛ capsids loo acates. Amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai amli koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei awo mli. Enɛ gbeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la etswa lɛ.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa trees without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support, and many naturally drop off. However, if too many drop, it means there are not enough tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them, or the tree is under stress from dry weather and lack of nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Ni tsei babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔi babaoo ba lɛ, kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ. Aloo tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods now compared to five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, the soil loses essential nutrients, and the trees become more vulnerable to pests and shade imbalance. Without regular pruning, soil feeding, and pest control, a tree's pod production naturally declines over time.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hulutsoo ni ejaaa lɛ waa. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni akɛkpaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui daa lɛ, tso lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ be hoɔ.

english: Why must I cut off branches from my cocoa tree when it is already growing large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo niji kɛji kookoo tso lɛ ebɔi dalɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. Opening up the tree allows sunlight and air to pass through, which reduces disease risks and directs energy into growing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa. Tsei lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops whenever the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants adapted to steal food, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops. They react quickly to rain and will starve your crops of nutrients if they are not cleared regularly.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛtsuɔ he nii oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ, ni amɛbaahã hɔmɔ aye otsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ kɛji ajieee amɛ daa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them out in the open sun without any tall crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni tsei kakadaŋŋ abɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Shading crops like plantains protect young cocoa seedlings from sunburn and heat, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa roots can establish properly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Lifting yam leaves into the air gives them maximum sunlight to produce plant food, prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, and protects the vine from ground pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha tsei aniyenii. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni ebuɔ wain tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen runs low in the soil, the plant pulls it from older lower leaves to feed the upper growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil encourages cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in roots below. Balanced nutrients and proper potassium levels are needed for tubers to swell.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ ŋmei baato eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shishigbɛ. Niyenii ni sa kɛ potassium ni sa he miihia koni ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have friendly bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ naanyobɔɔ helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so much slower when I delay weeding during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo kwraa beni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital nutrients, water, and sunlight from your young crops. Clearing weeds in the first 3 to 4 weeks allows crop seedlings to establish strong roots without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many maize seeds as possible close together to get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo bɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowded crops compete with each other for limited water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak stalks and small yields instead of healthy, full cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he wa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience dry spells without steady water. Extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni tsei kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni nu bɛ mli daa lɛ kpeɔ lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants roll up tight like pencils during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a survival mechanism where corn plants reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly during extreme heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala. Abɛi tsei haa he ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni mli edɔ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the hidden central leaves of maize to feed on tender growth, leaving behind chewed holes and dark waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛshiɔ bu ni ashɛreɔ kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Is three months of rain enough for my plantain crop to grow fully and give a good yield?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ nyɔji etɛ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa koni midumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: No, plantains need consistent soil moisture throughout their entire 12 to 15-month growth cycle. While three months of rain helps them start growing, extended dry periods later on can shrink the bunch size or damage the crop if the soil dries out completely.
ga: Dabi, plantains biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli fɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ nyɔji etɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjeɔ amɛdalɛ shishi moŋ. Shi hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ baanyɛ aha panicle lɛ dalɛ aba shi loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain plants seem to endure long dry spells better than my other food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi plantains lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi be kakadaŋŋ fe mi niyenii tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains have thick, fleshy stems and underground corms that store large amounts of water and energy. This built-in storage allows them to survive dry periods much better than crops with thin stems or delicate roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ loo kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo loo shishifãi ni waaa lɛ.

english: What is the best time of year for me to plant plantain suckers so they do not dry up?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui koni amɛkagbi?

english: It is best to plant plantain suckers at the very beginning of the main rainy season. This allows the root system to grow deep and strong enough to keep the plant alive when the rains reduce.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa koni tso lɛ ahi wala mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: If I apply chemical treatments to my farm, will that automatically guarantee a big harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaaha ŋmaa babaoo aba lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Treatments help control pests and diseases, but they are not enough on their own. Good field practices—such as controlling weeds, cutting unnecessary shoots, mulching the soil, and proper spacing—are just as important for getting a high yield.
ga: Tsamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai anɔ. Shi enɛ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ nifeemɔi kpakpai tamɔ jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Tsobii ni he ehiaaa lɛ afolɔmɔ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Amɛhe hiaa hu kɛha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni anáa.

english: Why do my plantain stands grow so many extra shoots around the main stem, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi babaoo ni ebɔle tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ni ani esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Those extra shoots are called suckers, and they grow naturally from the main root. You should cut most of them away because too many shoots fight with the main plant for nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni fa lɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ mli babaoo ejaakɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ni kɛ tso titri lɛ miiwu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei niji lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow during the rainy season even though there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves during wet weather often mean the soil is waterlogged and drowning the roots, or the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen. Excess water prevents roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miiho. Aloo niyenii kpakpai tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: How do I know for sure that my plantain is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the fingers look full and rounded, the sharp edges on the fruit skin become smooth, and the top leaves naturally begin to yellow and dry up.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji niji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How many years can I keep harvesting from the same plantain farm before I have to replant?
ga: Afii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa plantains kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli dani ehe baahia ni madu amɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: With good maintenance, soil fertility management, and proper sucker selection, a plantain farm can stay productive for three to five years or more before yields start to drop significantly.
ga: kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ kɛ suction head ni sa lɛ halamɔ Plantain ŋmɔji baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai. dani nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ajeɔ shishi ebaa shi waa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and a heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy. When the soil is wet and soft, strong winds can easily pull the roots out. You can prevent this by supporting the heavy stems with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni aduawai akui ni tsii haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsɔne ni tsii lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes dark spots on my plantain leaves, and will it ruin my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaakpãtã midumɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Dark spots are usually caused by leaf spot fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka, which spread quickly in warm, moist air. Trimming away affected leaves and keeping clean spacing between plants keeps air moving and prevents serious damage to your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal leaf spot, tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Baai ni ena hela lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni akwɛ koni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli tse ahi mli Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa nɔ ni fiteɔ okpamɔ lɛ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees on my farm alongside my young cocoa crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool, preserving moisture, and protecting young leaves from harsh sunshine.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and thin when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly, their roots compete for the same food and water in the soil, while their leaves block sun from each other. Yellow leaves are a sign that the crop is starving for nutrients.
ga: Beni tsei eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry leaves help my cassava crops grow better during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves acts like a blanket. It prevents sunshine from drying out the earth quickly, keeps root temperatures low, and gradually decays into natural soil food.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ hulu la he ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa shi, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my orange trees drop most of their leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmath be lɛ mli kɛji egbi pɛ?

english: Trees lose water through their leaves. Shedding leaves during dry spells is a survival trick to help the tree retain moisture inside its trunk and branches until rain comes back.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Baai ni ashwieɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ ayeɔ wala koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛtso kɛ amɛniji amli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with maize on the same piece of land, and will it help my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpea kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ? Ni ani ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and feeds nearby maize plants naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii.

english: Why do tree seedlings I bring from the nursery often wilt immediately after I plant them in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛbaa lɛ gboɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes shock because root tips get disturbed. Planting late in the afternoon or on cloudy days helps seedlings recover without stress from hot sun.
ga: Dumɔwui ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ haoɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa amɛhao.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, choosing to save their energy to keep the main plant alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ ye amɛ awui. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ehala akɛ ekɛbaato koni ekɛbu tso titri lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Weed seeds lie hidden under the soil for years. Clearing the ground exposes these seeds to sunlight and moisture, causing them to sprout quickly before cultivated crops can take root.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui nɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, older bottom leaves naturally die off so the plant can send water and energy up to the fresh, new leaves at the top.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ gboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry gap that can dry out sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until rains become steady so the young roots always have moist soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kuku ko sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How long does a newly planted oil palm take before it starts giving fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: A well-cared-for oil palm tree usually begins producing its first fruit bunches about 3 to 4 years after you plant it in the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm tree turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Old lower leaves naturally age and turn yellow as the palm grows, but if many leaves turn yellow at once, it usually means the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium or the tree is stressed from a dry season.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai babaoo batsɔ ŋmɔŋ shikome hu? Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ hɔmɔ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy and humid weather. Removing infected pods and pruning excess shade branches helps keep the air dry around the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ latsaa be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why are many of the flowers on my cocoa tree falling off without making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but only a few get pollinated by tiny insects. High heat, heavy rain, or lack of water can also cause the tree to drop excess flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛnɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and getting yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected stems. Using healthy, disease-resistant stem varieties for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ loo egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso yibii sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei?

english: Most cassava is ready to harvest between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the plant base starts to crack.
ga: Kasava babaoo feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes into the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the center of young maize plants. Catching them early and applying recommended pesticides or organic remedies saves the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why is my young maize crop looking light green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Light green or yellow leaves mean the maize is hungry for nitrogen nutrients, often because heavy rains washed nutrients away or the soil is worn out. Applying fertilizer early helps them turn green and strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ elaaje loo shikpɔŋ lɛ efite. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree easily fall over when the fruit bunch becomes heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be weakened by root pests or soft soil. Supporting the trunk with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole holds the weight of the fruit until harvest.
