ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baanyɛ aha egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fĩɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ tso lɛ yibii lɛ atsitsinɔnii lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the ground for my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha mi sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can catch full sunlight, which helps the plant create energy to grow large yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: When soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, the plant behaves smartly by pulling food from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen Tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ nilee mli kɛtsɔ niyenii ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look sad and droopy right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye awerɛho ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Moving plants causes 'transplant shock.' The tiny root hairs that drink water get damaged during the move, so the plant wilts temporarily until its roots settle in and start drinking again.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ ‘Transplant shock’ baa - shishifãi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔi nu numɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing very tall and thin without producing many leaves or branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai loo niji babaoo lɛ?

english: When crop plants do not get enough direct sunlight, they spend all their energy stretching upwards toward the light instead of spreading wide and growing leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ baai lɛ eshwa babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei ni afolɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into big tubers. If planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil food and water, leaving you with small, thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Yes, because all those extra shoots (suckers) drink water and eat soil food meant for the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree produces a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nakai ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the big trees and leave them under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ ni mikɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, tender leaves that burn easily under hot direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains around them to trap moisture and block the harsh sun until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni nuɔ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei tamɔ plantains ni bɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛha amɛhe afee hulutsoo kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛbaaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant yam on the exact same piece of land three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop loves most out of the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei sumɔɔ waa lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after I clear and plant my bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie miŋmɔji lɛ amli ni midu mihe lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of hidden seeds in the soil that are natural survivors. The moment you clear the ground and expose it to sunlight and rain, those weed seeds wake up and grow faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ woɔ dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okɛwo hulu kɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli pɛ kɛkɛ Nakai jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baate shi ni amɛdara oya fe tsei ni amɛdu lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry spells as a survival trick to save water and energy.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hulutsoo trukaa hao amɛ. Taakɛ teemɔŋ sane kɛha wala yiwalaheremɔ yɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop roots start rotting when water stays on my field for days during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the farm without draining, it smothers the roots and rots them.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn and dry out easily under full sunshine. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted next to them to block the harsh sun and keep the moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food for crop growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has to the upper leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ. Kɛji nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than young crops, so they quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early allows your crop to get all the food it needs to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of surviving heat and drought. By shedding leaves, the plant saves water and protects its underground tubers until the rain comes back to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ buɔ nu he ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba koni ebaaha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too severe or when the plant doesn't get steady water. When the plant feels stressed by heat or drought, it drops flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba loo kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa loo hɔmɔ mli lɛ Ebaashi fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to lift its leaves off the wet ground to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the foliage healthy, prevents rotting, and encourages the plant to form bigger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ekanyaa tsei koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why shouldn't I allow too many suckers to grow around one plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ he lɛ? dumɔwu kome pɛ

english: When too many suckers grow on one plantain stool, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three, ensuring those few get enough energy to produce large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo yɛ plantain sɛi kome nɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashwɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi komɛi náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, the roots cannot breathe and fungi spread quickly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni ŋmei lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients out of the soil every season and lets maize pests build up. Changing crops or resting the land allows the soil to rebuild its natural fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛjɔɔ he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant pulls nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nitrogen faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the small cocoa pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience sudden water stress, such as a hot dry spell, or when attacked by insects like mirids. The tree sacrifices its flowers to save water and energy so the main tree can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba amɛnɔ trukaa, tamɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutua tsei lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from catching sunlight properly, which reduces the size and weight of the cassava roots beneath the ground.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa baa lɛ aná hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ aba shi.

english: Why are my tomato fruits developing black, rotten spots right at their bottoms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium while fruit is forming. It is usually caused by irregular watering, such as letting the soil dry out completely and then flooding it.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiwo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why do I need to cut away the extra suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same food, water, and sunlight in the soil. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, ensuring you harvest larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, Plantain kome Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa onine shɛɔ kuu ni da, ni tsii nɔ.

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which means their roots capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea roots rot after harvest, they leave behind free nitrogen fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I see small chewed holes in my maize leaves with stuff that looks like saw-dust inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ayɛ ŋmãa baai ni ashɛre kɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant. The sawdust-like material is actually the waste left behind by the caterpillar as it eats the young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagbai lɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ. Nibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii shĩɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ beni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying even when there is plenty of moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root rot or bacterial wilt. The disease attacks the roots and clogs the internal water tubes of the stem, preventing water from reaching the leaves even if the ground is soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Hela nɛɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni etsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why should I soak my rice seeds in clean water before sowing them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo nu ni mli tse mli dani madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Soaking rice seeds triggers the seed to wake up from its sleeping state and softens its hard outer coat. This ensures the seeds sprout faster and grow evenly across your field once planted.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ wo nu mli lɛ, eteɔ lɛ shi kɛjɛɔ ewɔ mli ni ehaa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji adu amɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my stored yam tubers start growing green shoots in the barn, and why does it make them soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yams sprout naturally when their resting phase ends and they detect heat or light. As the shoot grows, it drinks the water and nutrients stored inside the tuber, which causes the yam to lose weight, dry out, and become soft.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni ana dɔlɛ loo la. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ Ebaanu nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛto eyitso mli lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi, egbiɔ, ni efeɔ bɔdɔɔ.

english: Why do some of my crop flowers fall off without turning into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers need to be pollinated by insects, wind, or human hand to turn into fruit. If a flower is not pollinated, the plant drops it because it cannot produce seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo gbɔmɔ niji awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen dani amɛwo yibii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ pollination lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui.

english: Can I manually transfer pollen from one flower to another to help my crops form fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi nine ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, this is called hand pollination. By gently taking pollen from a male flower and touching it to a female flower, you ensure fertilization when natural pollinators like bees are scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ajieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi hii amli blɛoo. Ba ni obata fɔfɔi yei lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔmɔ baa beni adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ nii, tamɔ ŋmeii, faaa lɛ.

english: Are all the insects I see visiting my crop flowers harmful to my harvest?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni minaa ni amɛsaraa mi aduawai fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ mikpamɔ lɛ awui?

english: Not all insects are pests. Many insects like bees and butterflies are helpful pollinators that carry pollen between flowers, which is necessary for fruit and seed formation.
ga: Jeee kooloi bibii fɛɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kplukai babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi ateŋ lɛ. Amɛhe hia kɛha aduawai kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ.

english: Why do different varieties of the same crop perform so differently on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred with distinct characteristics; some resist diseases better, some survive drought, and others yield larger fruits depending on soil and weather conditions.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi. Helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Ni tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe.

english: If I save seeds from my best harvest this year, will they give me the exact same high yield next season?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to Ani dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Not always. Hybrid seeds lose their strength in the second generation, so crops grown from saved hybrid seeds will often yield less and grow unevenly.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ amli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant two different varieties of the same crop right next to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ midu tso kome lɛ henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ yɛ amɛhe?

english: They can cross-pollinate through wind or insects, mixing their traits. While this year's harvest may look normal, seeds saved from them will grow into mixed varieties next season.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ loo koolooi baanyɛ afee amɛ cross-pollination. Ekɛ sui srɔtoi feɔ ekome. Eyɛ mli akɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa moŋ, Shi dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Does plucking off the very first flowers on a young crop help it grow better later?
ga: Ani klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso bibioo ko mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, removing early flowers allows young plants to focus their energy on building strong roots and stems before spending energy on fruit production.
ga: Hɛɛ, fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa amamɔ nɔ. Dani ebaafite hewalɛ yɛ aduawai afeemɔ mli

english: Why do my crop flowers droop or close up during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants close or droop their flowers during intense heat to conserve internal water and protect sensitive floral parts from drying out.
ga: Tsei haa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni nu ahi mli ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my plants producing plenty of large green leaves but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leaf growth instead of flowering. Plants require phosphorus to encourage flower development.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Tsei he miihia phosphorus koni eha fɔfɔi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are crops planted on the same day in my field flowering at different times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Uneven soil nutrients, differences in shade, localized water levels, or variations in planting depth cause plants in the same field to mature and flower at different speeds.
ga: Niyenii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli srɔtofeemɔ Nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta loo srɔtofeemɔi yɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ mli Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major nutrient plants need to grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why has chemical fertilizer become so expensive and hard to buy in Ghana recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara wa ni ewa akɛ aaaná yɛ Ghana yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Much of the world's fertilizer ingredients come from countries involved in international conflicts, such as Russia, so trade disruptions overseas push prices up for local Ghanaian markets.
ga: Jeŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ maji ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ majimaji ateŋ tawuu mli, tamɔ Russia, no hewɔ lɛ jarayeli mligbalamɔi ni yaa nɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ haa Ghana jarayelihe ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jara yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield less food if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time or varied organic matter to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehe ehiaaa ni aha sũ lɛ loo nibii srɔtoi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ be koni ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: The very first rainfall is often followed by several dry weeks, which will dry out the soil and kill tender young sprouts before the real rainy season establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii babaoo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe tsei bibii lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Can I plant groundnuts together with my cassava, or will they fight for nutrients?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmei adu ŋmei? Aloo amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: Groundnuts actually help cassava because they trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, serving as a natural fertilizer while covering the ground to stop weeds.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei waa ejaakɛ emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa jwɛi.

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworms are destroying my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look inside the top leaf whorls of the young corn plant; if you see ragged holes and soft, sawdust-like waste, armyworm caterpillars are actively feeding there.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo ko yiteŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ona buji ni etse kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miitao niyenii yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much standing water fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots and allowing fungal diseases to attack and decay the cassava.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmei lɛ egbo.

english: How can I keep weevils from destroying my harvested maize in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni mikpa mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ nitoohe lɛ naa koni amɛkafite?

english: Dry the maize grains thoroughly in the sun until they are hard, then store them in airtight bags or sealed plastic drums so pests cannot breathe or enter.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo plastic baagi ni atsĩ naa mli. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamu loo akabote mli.

english: Why should I buy certified maize seeds instead of replanting seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Saved seeds lose their genetic strength over generations, leading to smaller yields, whereas certified seeds are bred to give uniform, strong plants with heavy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii ni tsii yɔɔ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct sunshine. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and humidity they need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to absorb more sunlight while keeping the leaves away from wet soil that causes rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ he.

english: Spreading dry grass around crops acts as mulch, which shades the soil, keeps the ground cool, and traps moisture in the earth so your crops do not dry out quickly under hot sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Crops lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ mulch. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when too much water drowns the roots and prevents them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo ha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why should I plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Beans gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow on my farm make my main crops small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water that your main crops need, leaving your crops hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ. Shimɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ gbɔjɔmɔ.

english: Why are holes appearing inside the fresh leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji miije kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai heei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the center of the stalk to eat the soft, developing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni buɔ amɛhe kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye baai bibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny insects such as thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves, or by viral diseases spread to the plant by these insects.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli lɛ amli

english: Cassava roots rot in the ground when the soil retains too much water after heavy rain, which suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients needed to develop fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth, or that excess water in the soil is preventing roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo, nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii.

english: How do I know the right time to start applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awomɔ?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied during active growth stages, typically a few weeks after seeds sprout or right after early weeding, when roots are ready to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ miida waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ loo beni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the root zone instead of scattering it all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer close to the plant roots ensures your crop gets direct access to the nutrients before rains wash them away or nearby weeds consume them.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the plants grow tall with lots of leafy stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is too hard and compact, the cassava plant spends its energy building stems and leaves above ground instead of expanding its tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ bulb lɛ mli kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops start flowering early before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi mra dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When crops experience stress like hot, dry weather or poor soil conditions, they quickly switch to producing flowers and seeds early to reproduce before dying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ oya kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ koni amɛfɔ dani amɛgboi.

english: How does planting my crops in straight, spaced rows help them yield better than planting randomly?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ aha yibii kpakpai aba fe ni aduɔ amɛ trukaa?

english: Proper row spacing ensures every plant receives equal sunlight, airflow, and soil nutrients without crowding each other, making field work and harvesting easier.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ egbɔ ni amɛhe ebɔko amɛhe Ehaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves get scorched and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct heat; they require shade plants like plantains to shield them from intense sunlight until mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to dry up and drop off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiiwo yibii?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, as the plant conserves water rather than spending energy to support new fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ buɔ nu he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baawo aduawai heei.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or by a viral infection spread by these insects that damages leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants naturally adapted to compete aggressively for water, sunlight, and nutrients, which is why regular clearing is necessary to protect your crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, no hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ daa koni akɛbu onibii ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stay small if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛji bibii lolo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry spell that leaves the soil too hot and dry for young roots. Planting too early starves the roots of consistent moisture, preventing the plant from absorbing nutrients and causing yellow, stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ tsɔ kɛha shishifãi bibii. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest produce weaker crops than new store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crop varieties lose their strength and disease resistance in subsequent generations. Certified store-bought seeds are specially bred to give strong, uniform plants with high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli. Akwɛ dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ shwapoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yaa nɔ daa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the dry season, and does this mean my crop is dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii miigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry spells to conserve water and protect its roots underground. The plant is not dying; it is simply resting and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso lɛ gbooo, ejɔɔ ehe kɛkɛ ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Shedding flowers is the plant's way of saving energy during times of stress.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo ni akɛfataa he Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he yɛ haomɔ bei amli.

english: How can I tell that my yam crop is fully mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the tuber?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ bulb lɛ efoŋ?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This signals that the vine has stopped growing and has transferred all its nutrients into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce smaller fruit and lower total yields than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii kɛ yibii fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the same spot where I harvested garden eggs last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mifolɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same soil diseases and pests. Planting them on the same spot allows hidden pests in the soil to immediately attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fata tsei akuu kome he, ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are holes appearing in my young maize leaves just a few weeks after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ nɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds on the tender leaves inside the heart of young maize plants. Treating the crop early protects the growing tip so the plant can mature fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmei ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebuɔ tso lɛ naagbee he koni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm for a few weeks cause my crops to turn pale and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal water and fertilizer from the soil. Depriving your main crop of these essential nutrients turns the leaves pale and slows down growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛ otso titri lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha eda blɛoo.

english: Yellowing leaves from the tip inward usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so applying urea fertilizer or compost early in the growing season fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ eshishigbɛ kɛyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the central shoot of young maize plants. Farmers control it by spraying recommended pesticides or neem oil early in the morning before the worms burrow deep.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Okwaafoi kudɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ leebi dani kooloi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: This is often caused by black pod disease or natural pod shedding called cherelle wilt. Black pod happens when humidity is high and trees are too dense, so pruning branches lets in sunlight and air to prevent fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela loo adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Black pods baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ fa ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water sits around the roots in heavy soil or during heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I do not give them tall sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs bibii kɛji mihaaa amɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛkwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce food for underground tuber growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, maximizing leaf sun exposure and increasing tuber size.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo kɛha baai lɛ. ni eha yitso lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots on the bottom side before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently moist prevents this skin breakdown at the bottom of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewolo ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Applying insecticidal soap or neem spray kills the pests and allows new leaves to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ ni eye ebua baa heei ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow with dark spots and dry up early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Sigatoka, a common leaf fungal disease that spreads quickly in moist weather. Cutting off and burning affected lower leaves reduces the spread and keeps the plant strong enough to yield heavy bunches.
ga: Enɛ ji Black Sigatoka, ni ji hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ baa mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo ni ashã shishigbɛ baai ni ena naagbai lɛ, ebaaha gbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ niji babaoo aba.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for the next season's crop without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture for me to start sowing seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should check that the rain has soaked into the soil at least hand-deep (about 10 to 15 centimeters). Sowing into dry soil after just a light rain can cause seeds to sprout and die if no more rain falls for a few days.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛshɛ nine he (aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15). Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi.

english: How can I tell if the seeds or chemicals I buy at the market are safe and effective for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui loo tsofai ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Always purchase inputs from certified agro-dealers, check for sealed containers with official labels, and verify expiration dates so you do not accidentally damage your crops with fake or expired products.
ga: Hemɔ nibii kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ akɛ wolo ko ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ efo tsɛnsi lɛ mli. ni okwɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ Enɛ ji koni okɛ amalei loo nibii ni efite lɛ akafite onibii yɛ oshara mli.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop chemicals together in one tank before spraying?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafutu yɛ tanki kome mli dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Mixing chemicals without expert advice can cause a harsh reaction that burns crop leaves or makes the chemicals ineffective. Always ask an extension officer before combining sprays.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni naa wa aba ni shãa tsei ahe baai loo ehaa tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ. Bi extension nitsulɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ spray lɛ afutu.

english: How should I store leftover farm chemicals to prevent contamination and accidents?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni muji kɛ osharai akafee nɔ ko?

english: Keep all farm chemicals in their original labelled containers inside a locked shed away from children, food, animal feed, and water sources to avoid accidental poisoning and crop damage.
ga: Kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ato amɛ shishijee tsɛnsii ni aŋmala nɔ nii lɛ amli yɛ tsũ ko ni aŋã mli yɛ he ko ni gbekɛbii, niyenii, niyenii kɛ nu bɛ he koni akafite ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni baa trukaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put too much chemical fertilizer on them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo fata he?

english: Applying too much fertilizer creates high salt levels in the soil that can scorch crop roots and turn leaves brown or yellow, ultimately slowing growth or killing the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmei babaoo aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa blɛoo loo yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: Why is it better to apply farm treatments to my land in smaller portions rather than doing the whole farm at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ tsofa fioo ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii shikome lɛ?

english: Treating your farm section by section allows you to test how your crops react to the application and prevents you from risking your entire yield if an error occurs.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ fã kɛ fã nɔkwɛmɔ haa okaa bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii. Ni etsĩɔ bo gbɛ ni okɛ onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ awo oshara mli kɛji nɔ ko fite.

english: How do I determine the right amount of fertilizer to give each of my crop plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha tso fɛɛ tso?

english: Dosage depends on crop age and soil type; following the specific measurement guides provided by extension officers ensures plants receive enough food without burning their roots.
ga: Bɔ ni abaaha lɛ fa ha lɛ damɔ afii ni tso lɛ eye kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ susumɔ he ni onukpai lɛ woɔ he hewalɛ lɛ anɔyeli baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛshãaa amɛshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings turn yellow and stop growing when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Intense heat causes young crops to lose water through leaves faster than tiny roots can suck it from the dry soil, putting the plant under extreme heat stress that halts growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni abaanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ.

english: What happens to my land if I grow the exact same crop on my whole farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply rapidly, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are hardier and adapted to quickly steal available rainwater and soil nutrients, which starves your young crops unless the weeds are removed early.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛtsake amɛhe oya koni amɛju nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ. Ja ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Why should I inspect my crop leaves early in the morning for pest damage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli leebi koni mana kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ?

english: Many leaf-eating insects are active during the cool morning hours, so checking early helps you spot pests and holes on leaves before an infestation spreads across your entire field.
ga: Kplukai babaoo ni yeɔ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii waa yɛ leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ dani tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa crop need shade from bigger forest trees to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ aná hulutsoo koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa naturally grows in the lower layer (canopy) of the forest, where taller trees protect it from direct, harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ shishigbɛ fã (canopy) lɛ mli, he ni tsei kakadaji buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: What does 'canopy level' mean when agriculture officers talk about forest farming?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘canopy level’ shishi kɛji okwaayeli he onukpai wie kooi ahe nitsumɔ he?

english: A canopy level refers to the different height layers of leaves and branches in a forest, where tall trees form an upper layer of cover and smaller plants like cocoa grow underneath in the protected lower layer.
ga: Canopy level tsɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai srɔtoi lɛ. ni kɔɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli he ni tsei kakadaji feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Ni tsei bibii tamɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi yɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he.

english: How does creating shade on my farm help protect my delicate crops from burning?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni shade ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la he?

english: Shade creates a cooler microclimate that reduces water loss from the soil and leaves, protecting sensitive crops from getting scorched by direct sunlight.
ga: Shade haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ baa shi. Ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do different plants on my farm need different amounts of sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ hulu la srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Plants are naturally adapted to different forest levels; while large trees thrive in full sun, lower crops like cocoa are suited for filtered shade beneath tree covers.
ga: Tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kooi srɔtoi amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei wuji daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi tamɔ kookoo hu sa kɛha tsei ashishifã.

english: Why do snails stay healthy in the bush but die when I put them in open cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli shi amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Snails need the cool, shady, and moist conditions provided by forest tree canopies to stay comfortable; open land gets too hot and dry, which quickly dehydrates them.
ga: Snails taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ, shade, kɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ koo lɛ mli koni amɛnu he akɛ amɛhe jɔ amɛ. Hei ni agbele naa lɛ mli edɔɔ tsɔ ni egbi. Enɛ baaha nu agbɔjɔ oya.

english: How can I make my farm comfortable enough for snails to stay and reproduce without escaping?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ mli afee fɛo bɔ ni sa koni ŋmeii ahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii ni amɛjooo foi?

english: You can recreate natural forest conditions by using shade plants and tree canopy layers that trap moisture and shield the snails from hot sunlight.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ afee bɔ ni koo lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do snails prefer living under plants with thick, dense leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛhi tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Thick plant leaves block sunshine and trap moisture near the ground, creating the cool, damp environment snails need to stay comfortable and grow.
ga: Tso baai ni tsii tsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni hulutsoo baa. Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛshwere.

english: Can I rear snails on my cocoa farm under the shade of the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmeii yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi?

english: Yes, because cocoa plants form a lower canopy layer that creates the cool, shady, and damp environment that snails need to stay comfortable and thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kookoo tsei feɔ ŋwɛitsu ko yɛ amɛshishi ni haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmeii lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ ni amɛshwere.

english: How does copying the structure of a natural bush or forest help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni adebɔɔ mli jwɛi loo koo ko yɔɔ lɛ he mfonirifeemɔ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Mimicking the bush creates natural canopy levels where taller trees shelter lower crops and animals, protecting them from heat and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Jwɛi akasemɔ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. He ni tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahiɔ. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why does keeping tall trees on my land prevent my crops from drying out during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ni mikɛtoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tall tree leaves form an overhead canopy cover that reduces ground temperature and prevents soil water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Tsei kakadaji lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ baa shi, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like urea gives the crop the food it needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving each seed proper space allows the plants to grow strong stems and produce larger maize cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my farm help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that naturally catch nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize on that same land next season, the maize uses that stored food to grow faster without needing as much extra fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ amli lɛ, ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa babaoo afata he tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why are there holes in my young corn leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi lɛ ji ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Minɔ lɛ yɛ bu ni akɛtee tso lɛ yiteŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the soft center leaves of corn plants. Checking your farm regularly and using recommended sprays or traditional remedies early will kill the caterpillars before they destroy the crop heart.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ awo mli mra. Egbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsui.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil mixture or recommended insecticide gets rid of the insects and protects leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni ebaatsi baai lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when the plant lacks certain nutrients. Regular watering during dry spells and keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay on the plant and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii komɛi Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the dirt. It holds rainwater in the soil longer, keeps roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi muji lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the cool morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso?

english: Watering in the early morning is best because the soil absorbs the water fully before the sun gets too hot. Watering in the hot afternoon wastes water through heat evaporation and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ kwraa dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nu lɛ kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli afu

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ Harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind pulls water out of leaves faster than young roots can collect it from dry soil. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby shields young cocoa trees from direct wind and sun.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ abua naa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: If I leave my mature cassava roots in the ground past the harvest time, will they rot or spoil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ Ani ebaagbo loo ebaafite?

english: Cassava can stay stored underground for a short while, but if left too long—especially through heavy rains—the roots become tough, woody, lost in starch, or rot, making them bad for eating or selling.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ cassava ato shikpɔŋ shishi be kukuoo ko. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, amɛfeɔ tsei, amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii loo amɛfiteɔ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ

english: How can I tell if my maize is fully mature and ready to harvest without waiting for the whole stalk to die?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni omɛɛɛɛ ni ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ agbo?

english: When maize reaches full maturity, a tiny dark layer forms at the tip of each grain where it attaches to the cob. This black layer signals that the plant has stopped sending food to the grain and it is safe to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa bibioo ko ni yɔɔ duŋ baaba. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ naagbee. Nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa niyenii kɛyaa ŋmaa lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomatoes burst open on the stem right when they start turning red during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ tswaa trukaa yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ beni ejeɔ shishi efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains cause the tomato plant to soak up large amounts of water very quickly. The inside of the fruit swells faster than the skin can stretch, causing the ripe tomato to split open.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo oya. Yibii lɛ amli fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Ehaa tomato ni egbɔ lɛ tswaa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots start turning black and rotting just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ bɔi ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots contain a lot of water and continue to breathe after harvest. Once detached from the soil, oxygen enters the root wounds and triggers rapid chemical changes that cause decay within two to three days unless processed or preserved.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛmuɔ kɛji akpa amɛ. Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Oxygen lɛ boteɔ shishifã lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsofa tsakemɔi ni baa oya ni haa fitemɔ baa yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli lɛ baa. ja atsu he nii loo ato he gbɛjianɔ

english: Why does my harvested corn go moldy so fast when I put it into cocoa sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kookoo kotokui amli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly picked corn still holds high natural moisture. Trapping damp grain inside sacks stops airflow and creates warm, moist conditions where mold fungi thrive and spoil the crop.
ga: Abele ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo lolo. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni aaawo kotokui amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ kpaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ, efɔ shihilɛi baa. he ni ŋmeii shwereɔ yɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why do small dark beetles start destroying my stored dried maize even when I keep the bags tied tightly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ebɔi mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ fitemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ efi shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is still in the field. When the grain sits in warm storage, these hidden eggs hatch into adult beetles that eat the corn from the inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ yɔɔ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Nakai tso lɛ je kpo?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that cannot draw water fast enough under full sun. Shade trees act as living covers, protecting young cocoa from direct sun heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa wala. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: When plantains are planted too close to each other, their broad leaves block sunlight from reaching neighboring plants, and their roots fight for the same soil nutrients, leaving the crop with too little energy to grow large fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ahe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of turning them into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, lack of soil water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save energy so it can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nitrogen ni fa fe nine Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of leafy stems but produce very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishitso lɛ yɔɔ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the yam plant direct all its food into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending starches down to develop big tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ adu niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsu ashikishaŋ shi koni ekɛ yitsei wuji aba

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow along the middle vein while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center vein of older, lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving its limited nitrogen supply from the bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cabbage sometimes taste or smell like chemical medicine after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ŋɔɔ loo eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ tsofa beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage absorbs liquid agrochemicals if they are sprayed too close to harvest day. Every chemical requires a waiting period—called a pre-harvest interval—so the plant can naturally break down the medicine before it is harvested for food.
ga: Cabbage shwieɔ okwaayeli tsofai ni ji nu kɛji akɛ afɔse ashwie he ni bɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ lɛ tsɔ. Tsofai fɛɛ biɔ be ni akɛmɛɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ be ni tsɔ ŋmaa lɛ hiɛ, koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akumɔ tsofa lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe dani akpa amɛ akɛ niyenii.

english: How long should I wait to harvest my vegetables after spraying them with pest medicine?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa aduawai beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Every chemical bottle has a mandatory waiting period, usually between 3 to 14 days depending on the type. Waiting allows sunlight, rain, and the plant's internal systems to break down the chemical so the produce becomes safe to eat.
ga: Tsofa tɔ fɛɛ tɔ yɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛmɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yeɔ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni eji lɛ nɔ. Mɛmɔ haa hulu la, nugbɔ, kɛ tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ tsofai lɛ koni nibii ni anáa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Will spraying double the amount of chemical medicine kill pests faster and protect my crops better?
ga: Ani tsofa ni fa fe shii enyɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui oya ni ebaabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, using too much chemical burns your crop leaves, leaves dangerous chemical poison on the produce, costs you extra money, and causes insects to build resistance so the medicine stops working in the future.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baashã otso lɛ baai lɛ. Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ashiɔ yɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ amli Ehaa ofiteɔ shika kroko ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛhe hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ kɛyashi tsofa lɛ baakpa nitsumɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Can I protect my cabbage crops from worms without using strong chemical sprays?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabu mi-cabbage tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, you can use natural bio-pesticides like neem tree seed extract, practice crop rotation, or plant strong-smelling crops like onions nearby to confuse and repel insect pests naturally without leaving chemical residues.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem dumɔwu mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Aloo dumɔ tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa, tamɔ sabolai, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Koni akɛfutu ni ashwie kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eshiuuu tsofa ko ni eshwɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my vegetable crops turning brown and dry after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as chemical burn, which happens when chemicals are mixed too strong, applied under direct hot sunlight, or when the wrong chemical is sprayed on sensitive young crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ tsofai futu mli waa tsɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. aloo beni akɛ tsofai ni ejaaa shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do worms and insects seem to attack my cabbage more than other leafy crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cabbage lɛ fe tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Cabbage leaves are soft, juicy, and rich in nutrients, making them a favorite food source for pests like the diamondback moth caterpillar, which requires early monitoring before the heads form.
ga: Cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli nu ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni ehe gbɛi waa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ diamondback ŋmeii. Esa akɛ akwɛ enɛ mli mra. Dani yitso lɛ baafee

english: Does washing my harvested cabbage with plain water remove all the chemical sprays from it?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nu shwie kaabɛji ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mli?

english: Washing removes outer dirt and surface chemical powder, but many farm chemicals are systemic, meaning they soak inside the plant tissue and cannot be washed off with water, which is why proper harvest waiting times are essential.
ga: He ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ muji ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Shi ŋmɔ mli tsofai babaoo yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai lɛ boteɔ tsei amli fãji amli ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu aho he. No hewɔ ni ŋmaakpamɔ ni sa lɛ mɛmɔ he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Can I spray my harvested maize or beans with regular farm insecticides to keep bugs away in storage?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa koni mikɛshwie kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, field spray insecticides are toxic for human consumption. You should only use approved food-grade storage powders or sealed hermetic storage bags (like PICS bags) to protect harvested grains safely.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji tsofai fɔji kɛha adesa niyenii. Esa akɛ okɛ powda ni akɛtoɔ niyenii he ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo vacuum ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe (tamɔ PICS kotokui) pɛ atsu nii koni okɛbu odumɔwui ni okpa lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I feel dizzy or weak after applying chemical medicine on my vegetable farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihe feɔ mi shoo loo migbɔjɔɔ beni mikɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farm chemicals enter your body easily through breathing or skin absorption if you do not wear protective clothing like boots, gloves, and nose masks, leading to mild or severe chemical poisoning.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ boteɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya kɛtsɔ mumɔ ni okɛmuɔ loo kɛtsɔ ohewolo nɔ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji owooo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ bɔɔtu, glɔvs kɛ hiɛ he mask. Enɛ kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ fioo loo nɔ ni naa wa baa.
