english: Does applying too much chemical medicine to my crops spoil the soil for future planting?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, continuous heavy chemical use kills good soil organisms like earthworms and beneficial microbes that keep the soil fertile, making your soil harder and less productive over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kpakpai tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ekɛ yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I use water from a nearby river that looks muddy and brownish from mining to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ ni tamɔ muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛya nu mli aduawai?

english: Water polluted by illegal mining often contains dangerous chemicals and heavy metals that poison the soil, damage root tips, and make the crops unsafe for people to eat. Clean, clear water is necessary so crops can absorb healthy nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ dade ni tsii ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni mli tse ni mli tse he miihia bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing when water sits on my field for days after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to survive. When water sits on the field and cannot drain, it drowns the roots, preventing them from absorbing plant food and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ ko mli ni enyɛɛɛ efo lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaaaa amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant only one type of crop across my entire land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu tso henɔ kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Relying on a single crop leaves you vulnerable to total failure if a specific pest outbreak, disease, or bad weather hits that crop. Growing different crops together or in sections protects your food supply and income.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ tsu nii lɛ, no kɛ bo baawo oshara mli akɛ obaaye omanye kwraa kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii ni baa lɛ saa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu yɛ he kome loo oja mli awo mli lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu niyenii ni oyɔɔ kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ he.

english: Why should I change the type of crop I grow on my plot from one season to the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ be kome mli kɛya be kroko mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that target that plant to build up. Switching crops keeps the soil balanced and breaks pest lifecycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe shi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry palm leaves or grass help them during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ ŋmei loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering bare ground acts like a protective blanket that blocks direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, allowing plant roots to stay moist longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out and wither so fast during the dry harmattan season even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Harmattan air is extremely dry and windy, which pulls water out of plant leaves much faster than usual. Without soil cover or windbreaks, the sun and wind dry out the soil before roots can suck up the water.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa waa. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my young crops grow better when I plant them on raised ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Raised ridges loosen hard soil, making it easier for soft young roots to spread out. They also allow excess rain to flow away easily so the base of the plant does not rot.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni awó nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hu hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiteee.

english: Leaf curling is a defense response. The plant rolls its leaves inward to hide from the harsh sun and reduce the amount of water escaping from its surface during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji hetoo ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ ebaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and thin with few leaves when planted under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy. When shaded, the plant stretches upward as fast as it can to find light, using its energy to grow long stems instead of strong roots and thick foliage.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Beni eyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ena la lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji amli yɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops cause my crops to grow smaller fruits?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, space, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots, leaving your plants with less energy to develop healthy fruits.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛwo yibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: I noticed a powdery, whitish layer on my crop leaves and fruits; is my crop sick or is this normal?
ga: Miyɔse akɛ powda yɛŋ ko yɛ mibaai kɛ miyibii lɛ anɔ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa?

english: That white layer is a natural waxy coating often called 'bloom.' It acts like a protective shield against diseases, viruses, and water loss, helping the crop stay healthy without chemical treatment.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛwo nɔ ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'bloom'. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Can my crops naturally defend their fruit and seeds against diseases on their own?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛyibii kɛ amɛdumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: Yes, healthy crops produce natural physical barriers like tough outer skins, waxy layers, and chemical defenses that protect developing seeds and fruit from viruses and fungal infections.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii tamɔ hewolo nɔ fã ni mli wa, wax layer, kɛ tsofai ni buɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: How do small insects actually carry and give diseases to my maize plants?
ga: Te kooloi bibii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛwoɔ helai ni amɛkɛyaa ŋmãa tsei anɔ?

english: Insects act like transporters; when they feed on an infected plant, they pick up viruses or bacteria and deposit them directly into healthy plant tissues when they bite into your crop.
ga: Kplukai tsuɔ nii tamɔ mɛi ni kɛ nibii yaa. kɛ amɛye tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ Amɛheɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛkɛwoɔ tsei ahe fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does sticky red or clear liquid come out of my tree bark when it gets cut or damaged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu lɛ tsuɔ loo eyɛ faŋŋ ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ejɛɔ mitso lɛ shishi kɛji afo loo efite?

english: That liquid is plant sap, which acts like plant blood. The plant releases sap to seal up cuts and prevent insects and disease-causing germs from entering deeper into the stem.
ga: Nakai nu lɛ ji tso mli mliki. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lá Tso lɛ jieɔ nu ko koni ekɛtsi he ni efo lɛ naa ni ekɛtsi kooloi kɛ helai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take after flowers open for a crop to actually start forming fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ yɛ fɔfɔii asɛɛ dani tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Once pollen enters the flower, it usually takes under 24 hours for fertilization to complete, after which the flower petals drop off and the young fruit begins to develop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pollen lɛ bote fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, eheee nɔ ni fe ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 dani fɔfɔi lɛ baagbe naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai bibii jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without forming any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress or lack of water, preventing pollen from successfully reaching the inside of the flower to trigger fruit development.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Etsiɔ pollen naa koni ekashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni eha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do seeds need to be protected inside hard shells or pods while developing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abu dumɔwui ahe yɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni wa mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: The hard shell or pod forms a protective chamber around the egg and seed, shielding it from soil diseases, harsh weather, and pests until it is ready to germinate.
ga: Kpoji loo pod ni wa lɛ feɔ tsu ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ebɔleɔ he. ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui Buu ehe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃

english: Why are some seeds coated with a sticky layer inside the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Akɛwo aduawai lɛ amli?

english: That sticky layer protects the young seed embryo from drying out and guards it against viruses and bacteria while it matures inside the fruit.
ga: Nakai ŋmei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ buɔ dumɔwu bibioo lɛ he koni ekagbi, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do nutrients from the fertilizer I put in the soil get inside my crop?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ shɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: Fertilizer dissolves in soil water, and the plant roots suck up this nutrient water, moving it up through internal plant channels to feed the leaves, flowers, and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔ nu mli. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baamu nu ni niyenii nɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, eyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ koni ekwɛ baai, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava plant turn yellow and drop off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, the plant sacrifices its older leaves to save water and nutrients for the younger leaves and internal structures necessary for survival.
ga: Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii kɛha baai bibii kɛ mligbɛ nibii ni he hiaa kɛha wala.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning completely pitch black on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa pods turn pitch black, it usually means they are infected with Black Pod disease. It starts as a small dark spot and spreads quickly across the outer shell, especially during wet weather.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ hela emɔ amɛ. Eje shishi akɛ he bibioo ko ni yɔɔ duŋ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod is just ripening or if it is dying from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛkɛ loo hela miigbe amɛ?

english: Healthy ripening cocoa pods turn from green to yellow or orange, whereas pods infected with disease develop spreading dark brown or pitch-black patches that eventually dry out or rot.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, pods ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ loo ediŋŋ kwraa ni egbɛ eshwã. ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbi loo ebaagbo.

english: Does the black spot on the outside of a cocoa pod damage the beans inside?
ga: Ani ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yes. As the black patch spreads on the outside, the fungus sends tiny root-like threads inside the pod shell, which rots the beans and destroys their quality.
ga: Hɛɛ. Beni wolo diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ. Fuŋ lɛ tsuɔ hyphae bibii ni tamɔ shishifãi. Yaa pod lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo ni efite amɛsu.

english: What causes a small dark spot on my cocoa pod to spread so fast?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: The spot is caused by a living fungus. High humidity and rain give this fungus the food and moisture it needs to grow rapidly across the surface of the pod.
ga: Fung ni hiɛ kã ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmei nɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ oya yɛ ŋmei lɛ hiɛ.

english: How does a dark pod disease move from one cocoa tree to another on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The fungus produces tiny invisible spores that travel through rain splash, wind, insects, or on harvesting tools from an infected pod to healthy pods nearby.
ga: Fungi jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii. Pods ni anaaa ni tsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii amli kɛjɛɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can rain splash bring diseases from the soil up to my lower cocoa pods?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ kɛya kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, the fungus that turns pods black often lives in the soil. Heavy rain splashes infected soil particles onto the lowest pods on the tree, starting new infections.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ sũ mli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. ni kɛ helai heei baa

english: Should I remove black, rotted cocoa pods from my trees or leave them to fall off naturally?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie kookoo diŋ ni miifite lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo maha amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe?

english: You should pluck and remove black pods immediately. Leaving them on the tree allows the disease to keep growing and spreading spores to your remaining healthy pods.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii diji lɛ ni ajie amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya hiɛ ni egbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ eshwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa pod diseases spread much faster during the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cocoa pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa yɛ nugbɔ be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases thrive in damp, shaded conditions. Constant rain keeps the pods wet and creates rain splashes, which help the fungus multiply and spread easily.
ga: Fungal helai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: What practical steps can I take to stop dark pod diseases from starting on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni black pod hela akaje shishi yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Prune your cocoa trees to let in sunshine and air, weed around the bases, remove infected pods regularly, and apply approved fungicides before the heavy rains start.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ kookoo tsei koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aje shishi.

english: If I harvest a cocoa pod that has a small black spot, can I still use the beans inside?
ga: Kɛji obua kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ anaa Ani manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii lolo?

english: If the spot is brand new and hasn't penetrated the inner shell, the beans inside might still be good. However, if the pod has turned pitch black, the disease has already reached the inside and ruined the beans.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ji ehee ni eboteee mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ, Ekolɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela lɛ ebote mli ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to just go to the market and buy seeds on the exact day I want to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ maya jara nɔ ni mayahe dumɔwui yɛ gbi ni misumɔɔ ni madu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Buying seeds at the last minute often leaves you with poor-quality or damaged seeds that sprout poorly. Planning early allows you to source certified, high-yielding seeds and test their germination before the planting season begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ooohe yɛ naagbee minitii lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha oná dumɔwui ni ehiii loo ni efite, ni ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛjianɔtoo mra Ehaa ona dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli, ni woɔ yibii babaoo. ni okwɛ kɛji ekwɛ̃ dani shweremɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: How far in advance should I start preparing and buying my crop seeds before the rains begin in Ghana?
ga: Te esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui asaamɔ kɛ amɛhemɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: You should start securing and preparing your seeds 1 to 2 months before the main rainy season. This ensures you have the right variety on hand and can plant immediately after the first good rains.
ga: Esa akɛ oje dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛhe saamɔ shishi nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 2 dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. Enɛ baaha oná tso ni sa ni obaanyɛ odu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I test if the seeds I saved from last year are still good enough to sprout?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds in a moist cloth or small patch of soil; if 8 or more sprout strongly within a few days, your seed lot is healthy and ready for the field.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ loo shikpɔŋ fioo ko mli lɛ nɔ. Ekpaa loo nɔ ni fe nakai baakwɛ̃ waa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ agbɛnɛ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do some seeds sprout fast in my field while others die under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Uneven sprouting usually happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when soil moisture is inconsistent, or when low-quality seeds lack the stored energy needed to push through the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ loo be mli ni dumɔwui ni ehiii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What will happen to my groundnuts if I just scatter a lot of seeds closely together in my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji migbɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When groundnuts are planted too closely, the plants fight for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This competition leads to weak stems, small underground pods, and a lower total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. shikpɔŋ shishi pod bibioo kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni baa shi

english: How deep in the ground should I put my groundnut seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Groundnut seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. Planting too deep prevents sprouts from reaching sunlight, while planting too shallow exposes seeds to drying heat and hungry birds.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ okpoi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do some of my groundnut plants look healthy on top, but the pods underground end up empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi pod lɛ mli efolo?

english: Empty groundnut pods—often called 'pops'—occur when the soil lacks sufficient calcium or when the ground dries out completely while the pods are developing underground.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘pops’ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium ni fa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I check how well my groundnuts are forming underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ bɔ ni mi-ŋmeii lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Walk through your field regularly and carefully dig up a few sample plants from different spots to check pod count, size, and maturity, giving you a clear picture of crop progress.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni otsa tsei fioo komɛi ni ji nɔkwɛmɔnii kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi. jogbaŋŋ Koni akwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ ji, amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ. Bɔni afee ni ona bɔ ni tsei lɛ yaa hiɛ amɛhaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to estimate my crop yield before harvest day actually arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani akpa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Estimating your yield early helps you arrange storage bags, labor, and transport in advance, while helping you spot issues like pest damage or crop loss early enough to take action.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ahe akɔntaabuu mra Ehaa onyɛɔ osaa nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli, nitsumɔ, kɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni oyɔseɔ saji tamɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ mra bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ otsu he nii.

english: What causes field losses or missing crops right around the time groundnuts mature?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔshi be mli lɛ baa?

english: As groundnuts mature underground, their rich odor attracts pests like rodents, while unmonitored fields are vulnerable to stray livestock or theft. Regular field visits help protect mature crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmeii ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kooloi ni elaaje loo juu baanyɛ aba. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop plants fall off before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers are the starting point for fruit growth. If flowers drop off, it usually means they were not pollinated or were damaged by harsh environmental factors like excessive heat before fruit could form.
ga: Fɔfɔi ji he ni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa yɛ. Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo shihilɛ mli nibii ni mli wa tamɔ la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ efite amɛ dani aduawai ba.

english: My crops are producing plenty of flowers, so why am I still not harvesting any fruit?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mikpako aduawai ko lolo lɛ?

english: Having flowers is only the first step to getting fruit. The flowers must be pollinated to develop into fruit; if heat destroys the pollen or prevents pollination, the flowers will dry up and produce nothing.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni aaaná lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ yibii. Esa akɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen koni amɛtsɔ aduawai. Kɛji latsaa lɛ kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ loo etsĩ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa.

english: What is pollination, and why does my farm need it to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ biɔ ni aŋɔ pollin awo mli koni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pollination is the transfer of pollen within or between flowers that allows a plant to create seeds and fruit. Without pollination, the flower cannot turn into a fruit.
ga: Pollination ji pollen ni akɛyaa fɔfɔi amli loo amɛteŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Kɛji pollination bɛ lɛ fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee aduawai.

english: Why don't I see bees visiting my crop flowers when the afternoon heat is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana ŋmeii ni miibasara mifɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pollinating insects like bees avoid active foraging in intense heat because high temperatures dehydrate them and dry up the flower nectar, driving them to seek shade during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Nibii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ niyenii taomɔ he yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ amɛmli, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli nu lɛ mli nu lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ tsirɛɔ amɛ koni amɛtao hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops look scorched and withered when the midday sun gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures can physically burn and dry out delicate flower parts. When the heat inside the flower gets too high, it damages the flower tissue and destroys the pollen.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛgbi. Kɛji hulutsoo ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ fa tsɔ Ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ amli fãji lɛ ni ebaafite fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Can severe heat prevent my crops from producing fruit even if I water the soil well?
ga: Ani latsaa ni fe nine baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Yes. Even if the plant has water at its roots, extreme air temperature can burn the delicate flowers and ruin pollen, preventing fruit from setting regardless of soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei yɛ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi amli moŋ, Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbe fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkagbee shi ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How can I tell if high temperatures are harming the flowers on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ miigba fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Signs of heat stress include flowers turning brown or dried out, dropping off the stem early, or failing to form small initial fruits after blooming.
ga: Nɔ ni fata hulutsoo he haomɔ he okadii ahe ji fɔfɔi ni tsɔɔ blɔfo loo ni amɛgbiɔ. Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ kpo oya. aloo ewooo yibii bibii beni efɔ fɔfɔi sɛɛ

english: Why should I try to finish flower-related farm tasks before 10 o'clock in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni magbe mi fɔfɔii anitsumɔ lɛ naa dani leebi ŋmɛji 10 ashɛ?

english: Early morning offers cooler temperatures that keep pollen viable and flowers moist. By 10 o'clock, rising heat can burn delicate flower parts and cause pollination activities to fail.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ daa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Yɛ 10 a.m. lɛ, dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why is hand-pollination more successful early in the morning than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yeɔ omanye leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Pollen is fresh and receptive in the cool, moist conditions of early morning. Afternoon heat dries out the pollen and flower tissues, making hand-pollination mostly ineffective after temperatures rise.
ga: Pollen lɛ ji ehee ni ejieɔ ehe jogbaŋŋ yɛ leebi shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Gbi gbɛkɛ latsaa lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fãji lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haa nine mli pollination lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ etee hiɛ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What basic steps can I take to shade or protect delicate flowering crops from burning in intense sun?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii manyɛ matsɔ nɔ mawo fɔfɔi tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo mabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he?

english: You can provide shade using temporary shade cloths or by planting taller companion crops like plantains to shelter delicate flowers from the direct, scorching heat of the sun.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mama ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ aha hulutsoo loo kɛtsɔ nanemɛi tsei kakadaji, tamɔ plantains ni ooodu lɛ nɔ, koni ekɛbu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do some crops produce food in just two months while trees like cocoa take years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo heɔ afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize or vegetables grow quick, simple stems and roots, so they put all their energy into making food right away. Tree crops like cocoa build deep root systems and wooden trunks first, which takes years before they can bear fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai daa oya. Eyɛ tso kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ niyenii feemɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli tamɔ kookoo lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: What kind of fast-growing crops can I harvest in only one month?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni daa oya manyɛ makpa yɛ nyɔŋ kome pɛ mli?

english: Leafy green vegetables such as amaranth, spinach, and lettuce grow very quickly and can be harvested in about 30 days because you only need their leaves, not fruits or seeds.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli tamɔ spinach, broccoli, kɛ lettuce lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee gbii 30 mli ejaakɛ baai lɛ pɛ he hiaa bo. Jeee aduawai loo dumɔwu ni.

english: Why do crops like maize die after one harvest while cocoa trees stay alive for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa gboiɔ yɛ kpamɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei hiɔ shi afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops are divided into annuals and perennials. Annual crops like maize finish their natural life cycle in one season after producing seed, while perennial crops like cocoa are designed by nature to live and produce fruit for many years.
ga: Ajara ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afi kɛ afii babaoo mli. Tsei ni yeɔ daa afi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛgbeɔ amɛwala be lɛ naa yɛ be kome mli beni amɛwo dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo, tamɔ kookoo lɛ ji nɔ ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo lɛ.

english: What can I grow to make money when my main cocoa trees are not bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika be mli ni mi-kookoo tso titri lɛ wooo yibii?

english: You can plant short-duration crops like tomatoes, peppers, cabbages, or cowpeas. These mature in one to three months, giving you quick food and money to sell at the market while waiting for the next cocoa season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kaabe loo tsina ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui nɛɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji kome kɛyashi etɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii oya kɛ shika ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ kookoo be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I grow vegetables on my farm during the dry season when main farming slows down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Yes, if you have access to a small stream, well, or water source, fast-growing vegetables thrive in the dry season and usually sell for higher prices because fewer farmers are producing them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ oyɛ gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ oyaa faa bibioo ko, nubu loo nu jɛɛhe ko mli lɛ, aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni bei pii lɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ ejaakɛ okwaafoi fioo pɛ feɔ amɛ.

english: How does growing fast crops help protect my family if cocoa prices fall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ abu miweku lɛ he kɛji akɛ kookoo jara ba shi?

english: Growing quick-maturing crops acts like a financial safety net. If cocoa yields are low or prices drop, the extra income from selling vegetables or grains keeps money coming into your home throughout the year.
ga: Nibii ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shika he shweshweeshwefeemɔ tsɔne. Kɛji akɛ kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ faaa loo ejara ba shi lɛ Shika kroko ni anáa kɛjɛɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni okɛ shika awo oshia lɛ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant crops that mature at different times instead of planting everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ

english: Staggering your planting or choosing crops with different maturity times (1 month, 2 months, 3 months) ensures you have a continuous supply of food and income every month rather than a single payout.
ga: Tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli (nyɔŋ kome, nyɔji enyɔ, nyɔji etɛ) ni ooodu loo ohala lɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo nyɔmɔ shikome pɛ

english: Will planting quick vegetables on my land take away nutrients from my main cocoa crop?
ga: Ani aduawai ni miduɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Not if managed correctly. Short-season crops have shallow roots that feed on upper soil layers, and legumes like beans can actually add nitrogen back into the soil, benefiting the surrounding land.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ atsu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ amɛkɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha kpokpaa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ

english: How do I know if a crop will take two months or three months to mature before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baahe nyɔji enyɔ loo nyɔji etɛ dani adu?

english: Every crop seed variety has a fixed growth length specified on seed packets or provided by extension officers, allowing you to choose seeds based on how quickly you need a harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni ato ni amɛdaraa tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ a-paketi lɛ nɔ loo mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kɛhaa lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni osumɔɔ ni okpa oya lɛ naa.

english: How do I decide which fast-growing crop is best for my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look at what buyers in your local market want, how much water you have available, and how quickly you need money—for very fast cash, pick leafy greens; for longer storage, pick maize or legumes.
ga: Kwɛmɔ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ taoɔ. Nu enyiɛ oyɔɔ? Ni te shika lɛ he hiaa bo oya ha tɛŋŋ? Halamɔ aduawai ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli koni oná shika oya waa. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛto be kakadaŋŋ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ obaahala ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight. They turn yellow and burn because they lack shade. Planting quick-growing shade crops like plantains around them protects them from harsh sunlight while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: This yellowing usually means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen hɔmɔ yeɔ o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I plant my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani miduɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he?

english: Yes, stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant will struggle to sprout properly, resulting in weak stems and very few cassava tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ kwɛ̃mɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmeii shishifãi fioo pɛ baa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my crops help them during dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates a protective layer called mulch. This layer shades the soil, keeps it cool, and stops moisture from evaporating quickly into the hot air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, overly shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to let air and sunlight in helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Curled and twisted leaves are usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents damage to new shoots and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmeii kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds are left in the field, they steal food from your crops, slowing down their growth and reducing yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli. Ehaa shweremɔ baa shi ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to share limited food and water with the main plant. Pruning extra suckers leaves only the strongest shoots, resulting in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ agba niyenii kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ, tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves into the sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch maximum light, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Staking haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their tender leaves burn and dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides necessary shade and preserves soil moisture, protecting the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo he kɛyashi ebaatsɔ shweremɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on the same plot of land where I harvested my maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the ground weak after harvest. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil through their root nodules, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the food it needs to produce green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and produce small cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkuɔ amɛfeɔ toi bibii lɛ? Beni akɛ dumɔwui babaoo fataa Dumɔwui awoɔ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for tuber development. Staking keeps the vines off the ground, maximizing sunlight absorption while reducing the risk of leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hulu la ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off mainly due to stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms until they turn into fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not spoil under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava tubers are generally mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop. Leaving tubers in the ground for too long, especially during heavy rains, causes them to absorb too much water and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛmɔmɔ nu babaoo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Spraying neem oil or an appropriate insecticide controls these insects and allows new leaves to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ ni eye ebua baai heei ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and easily washed away by rain or eaten by insects in an open field. A controlled nursery bed protects young seedlings until they are strong enough to survive transplanting into the field.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni nugbɔ shwieɔ amɛ oya loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Nibii ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ awo saatso lɛ mli.

english: Why should I build ridges across my sloping land instead of planting down the slope?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Building ridges across a slope creates physical barriers that slow down running water during heavy rains. This keeps the topsoil and applied fertilizers from washing away, preserving moisture for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋshɔkei ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ hoɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni nu akaho. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi onibii amli

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh sunlight and to keep the soil moist. Clearing all shade trees leaves them vulnerable to heat stress; keeping trees like plantains or shade trees shields them until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Tsei tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ haa hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build green leaves, so when soil nutrients run low, applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long, which suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plants face extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring consistent soil moisture and avoiding excessive nitrogen during flowering encourages fruit to form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baawo aduawai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛfee.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted like tiny bowls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite tamɔ tsɛnsi bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Treating the plants early with organic neem oil spray or soapy water helps suppress these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Organic neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla ewo mli lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off damp soil, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni haa hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni akɛtsi baai helai anaa.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants have holes and look like they are filled with sawdust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant to eat tender leaf tissue. Placing neem powder or approved treatments directly into the funnel early stops the pests.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem powder loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ fata ŋmei lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai mra.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap at the stem and fall over before the fruits are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ miikumɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain stems break easily when stem borers or root nematodes weaken the base of the plant. Using clean, pest-free planting suckers and removing infested stems prevents these pests from multiplying.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ ha tso lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ sucker ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli tsu nii, ni ajie tsei ni mli ewo muji lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akafa babaoo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass stop them from drying out during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Feed my crops with hay bɔni afee ni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunshine, keeping the soil cool and preventing moisture from evaporating into the air, allowing crop roots to stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. Rotated crops like maize can then use this natural soil fertilizer to grow bigger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni amɛdara.

english: Why are many farmers in Ghana switching from growing food crops to planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ niyenii adumɔ mli kɛmiiya kookoo dumɔ mli lɛ?

english: While food crops provide quick food for the family, cocoa acts as a long-term cash crop that brings in a steady, reliable income year after year.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ji niyenii ni wekui náa oya moŋ, shi abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shika ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ baa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Do I need a lot of money to start a small cocoa farm?
ga: Ani shika babaoo he miihia mi koni manyɛ maje kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi?

english: You can start small by intercropping cocoa with food crops like plantain and cassava, which provide food and income to cover farm costs while the cocoa matures.
ga: Obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo kɛtsɔ kookoo ni ooodu yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava masɛi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika kɛha ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Will I always find a guaranteed buyer for my cocoa harvest every year?
ga: Ani manyɛ mana hɔlɔ ko ni yɔɔ nɔmimaa kɛha kookoo ni abaakpa daa afi lɛ?

english: Yes, cocoa is in high global demand, and in Ghana, licensed buying companies operate in almost every farming community to purchase your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ataoɔ kookoo yɛ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he. kɛ yɛ Ghana Nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni amɛheɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaayeli akutso fɛɛ akutso mli koni amɛhe onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Who determines the price I get paid when I sell my cocoa beans in Ghana?
ga: Namɔ tsɔɔ jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii miihɔɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: In Ghana, the government through COCOBOD sets a guaranteed minimum price for cocoa farmers each season to protect you from sudden drops in world market prices.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, nɔyeli lɛ tsɔɔ COCOBOD nɔ ekɛ jara ni baa shi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ haa kookoo okwaafoi yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Koni ebu ohe kɛjɛ jeŋ jarayeli nibii ahe jara ni baa shi trukaa lɛ he.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years, unlike older varieties that used to take up to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni esoro no kwraa yɛ kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni tsutsu lɛ amɛheɔ afii enumɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How often throughout the year does a cocoa tree bear fruit?
ga: Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei woɔ yibii yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa trees yield pods every year, typically producing a major harvest during the main rainy season and a smaller mid-crop harvest later in the year.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ ŋmeii daa afi. Bei pii lɛ, kpamɔ lɛ fa fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa yɛ afi lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ nakai afi lɛ naagbee lɛ faaa.

english: How long will my cocoa farm keep producing pods once the trees mature?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baajie ŋmeii kɛji tsei lɛ eda kwraa?

english: With good farm maintenance and care, cocoa trees can continue producing healthy pods for 30 to 40 years or more.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose some of their flowers during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop excess flowers during dry weather to conserve water and energy so the tree can survive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is cocoa farming more stressful to manage than growing vegetables?
ga: Ani kookoo dumɔ haa mɔ haoɔ waa fe aduawai dumɔ?

english: Once cocoa trees are fully grown and shading the ground, they require less constant daily care than delicate vegetable crops, making management more predictable.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Cocoa tsei biɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ fioo fe aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cocoa on the same land where I currently grow my yam and cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ sweet potato kɛ cassava nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa thrives on fertile forest soils that retain moisture, making land previously used for food crops very suitable for cocoa planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hei ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ feɔ hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main food the plant needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do elderly farmers say planting cowpeas in my field makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are part of the legume family, which means they have tiny bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, working like natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to save water and keep from drying out. The plant goes into a resting state while keeping its roots alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi hulutsoo be lɛ naa. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: The first rain usually cools the top layer of ground, but the deeper soil underneath is still dry. If a long dry spell follows that first rain, your germinated seeds will dry up and die before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ nakai klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui ni jeɔ kpo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants, like plantains or shade trees, to protect them until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Keeping only two or three strong shoots lets the main plant produce larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji plantain tsei lɛ dara kɛbɔle Tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa niji bibii baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain jwɛi agbo.

english: Why are small worms hiding inside the central leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide in the moist, tender center of the maize plant where they feed on new leaves. Detecting them early lets you clear them out before they destroy the growing point of the stalk.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa teŋgbɛ ni mli efɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli he ni amɛyeɔ baai heei yɛ lɛ. mra ni anaa Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ojie amɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the juice from leaves and spread plant sicknesses, causing the leaves to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahelai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot or the soil stays too dry, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to protect itself, preventing fruit from forming until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Tsi aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam plants use leaves on their vines to catch sunlight and make food for the tubers underground. Climbing up stakes keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight and off the ground, where pests and rot can harm them.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ewoɔ amɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kooloi kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye baai lɛ awui.

english: Why do I need to clear and loosen my soil several weeks before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafolɔ mli otsii babaoo dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Preparing land early gives buried weeds time to die and decay into rich food for your crops. It also loosens hard ground so young plant roots can easily spread and reach moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha jwɛi ni afu lɛ aná be ni amɛgboi ni amɛgboi, ni ebaaha niyenii babaoo aha oŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ hu shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it so difficult to get my seeds to sprout at the very start of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: At the turn of the year, the soil is dry and compact after the long Harmattan season. Until initial rains properly soak the ground, seeds struggle to get the moisture needed to break open and grow.
ga: yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse shelter need so much more daily attention than field crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: A greenhouse creates a protected environment that traps heat and moisture. Because the crops are completely reliant on you for water, air circulation, and temperature control, missing even one day of care can stress the plants.
ga: Greenhouses haa shihilɛ ni abuɔ he ni haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii damɔ onɔ kɛha nu. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulutsoo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Gbi kome po ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Why is it so important to properly prepare the nursery bed before bringing my young vegetable seedlings into a greenhouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asaa ŋmɔ mli tsei jogbaŋŋ dani akɛ aduawai amli dumɔwui aba ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very delicate and sensitive to disease. Preparing clean, nutrient-rich soil beforehand ensures the plants establish strong root systems before exposure to the higher heat inside a structure.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ he kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa ni yɔɔ tsũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat. The plant reduces its leaf surface area to slow down water loss when sunlight is intense, even if the roots still have water.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa baai lɛ anɔ he ni nu lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu lolo moŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants start flowering early when the weather stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔmɔ shishi mra beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences water stress, it thinks it might die soon. It rushes to produce flowers and seeds quickly as a survival instinct to make sure it leaves behind new offspring.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe lɛ misusu akɛ ekolɛ tso lɛ baagbo etsɛŋ. Ekɛ oyaiyeli woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui amli oya akɛ wala yibiiwoo su koni ekwɛ akɛ eshi bii heei yɛ esɛɛ.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight and soil food. The plants spend all their energy stretching upward to catch light instead of storing energy in big roots underground.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato amɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do insects attack my young green shoots much more than my mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ fa babaoo fe mi tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young plants have soft, tender stems full of moisture and sugars, making them an easy and nutritious meal for pests compared to tough, woody older plants.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sugar eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni egbɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my second harvest of vegetables on the same plot yield much less than the first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa shii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe mi-klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: The first crop consumes the major nutrients stored in the soil. Without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer between plantings, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot nourish the second crop as well.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii titri ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ hu.

english: Why do heavy early rains sometimes make my newly planted corn seeds rot in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mra lɛ haa mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If soil does not drain well, heavy rains fill up all the tiny air pockets in the ground. Without oxygen, seeds drown and rot before they get a chance to sprout.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieee nu jogbaŋŋ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛgboi dani amɛna hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe for me to collect seeds from my neighbor's farm to plant on my own land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa yɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli koni madu yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: While using saved seeds from a neighbor is low-cost, those seeds may carry pests or produce lower yields over time. Certified seeds from agro-dealers are usually tested to yield more and resist common diseases better.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ akutsoŋbii adɛŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jara waaa moŋ, Shi nakai dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Bei pii lɛ, akaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: I heard about improved crop varieties brought in from foreign places like Korea—will they grow well in my soil here in Ghana?
ga: Minu akɛ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miijɛ maji tamɔ Korea amli aba. Ani amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ?

english: Foreign or improved varieties can yield very well, but they often require specific care, timely watering, and specific fertilizers. It is best to test them on a small patch of your land first to see if they tolerate your local heat and soil conditions.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ loo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha yibii kpakpai waa aba. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Nu yɛ be naa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ afata he Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka amɛ okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko. onɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona kɛji amɛkpɛlɛɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds that grow very well in coastal towns like Winneba fail when I plant them further inland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa maji tamɔ Winneba lɛ shwereɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hei ni mli kwɔ lɛ?

english: Crops adapt to specific local weather, humidity, and soil types. Coastal regions often have different rainfall patterns and soil moisture compared to inland areas, so a seed variety bred for the coast may stress and underperform under different climate conditions.
ga: Atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔnaa kpokpai lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ srɔtoi kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ni ji Mɛi ni atsɔse amɛ kɛha ŋshɔnaa lɛ baanyɛ afee mɛi ni haoɔ ni amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems and very small cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛshishifãi bibii waa.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and turn brown during the bright afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small, shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very fast under hot sun. Providing temporary shade crops or spreading dry grass (mulch) around the base keeps the soil moist and cool.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha tsei lɛ afee hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli loo okɛ jwɛi ni egbi afɔ nɔ. (Mulch) ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots without draining properly. Applying compost or the right fertilizer restores nutrients and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yield if I leave them growing in the farm for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi? Ni kɛji akɛ miha ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi pɛ hu?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need during their main growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ be mli.

english: In the dry season, natural wild plants dry up, forcing insects to move into green farm fields for food. The warm temperatures also make many farm pests reproduce much faster.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, koo mli tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehe bahiaa ni kooloi bibii aya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛyatao niyenii. He ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo fɔɔ oya.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water my farm early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the hot sun can evaporate it, giving your plants plenty of moisture to handle heat throughout the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu latsaa lɛ he nii yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested grains mold and get eaten by insects inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ lɛ?

english: Grains rot if they are stored before they are fully dry because hidden moisture encourages mold growth and attracts storage beetles. Drying your grains thoroughly on clean tarps before bagging keeps them safe.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛto ŋmaa lɛ he lɛ, ebaagbo dani egbi kwraa ejaakɛ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ he hewalɛ ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kanvas ni he tse nɔ dani okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by the strong sun. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist during their first couple of years.
ga: Hulu shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts in between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the dirt. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps the neighboring maize plants grow stronger without exhausting the soil.
ga: Akpɔlɔi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow, or that heavy rainfall has flooded the soil and starved the roots of air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa akwɛ̃. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or dry soil, as the plant tries to save its energy and water just to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi.

english: What makes the leaves on my hot pepper plants curl up and wrinkle?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck the juice from the leaves and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large underground and need soft, loose soil to expand easily. High mounds give the roots space to grow thick and long without pushing against hard dirt.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Pile ni kɛlɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ lɛ waa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot strips the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow plenty of leaves but very few beans during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ baa babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive too much water, the plant puts all its energy into growing green foliage and branches instead of focusing on making flowers and seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ cowpea nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi a peemi nɔ.
