english: Why does swamp rice require standing water in the field to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns out competing weeds, keeps the ground temperature stable, and supplies the constant moisture that swamp rice roots need to produce full grains.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efuɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ ahi shi daa. ni ekɛ nu ni haa ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa ni ji ŋmaa muu lɛ aba lɛ haa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off the stalk, typically between 9 and 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure near the roots will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, feels crumbly when squeezed in your hand, holds moisture well without staying soggy, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter that feed the crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ hɛ mi nyami ke o ngɔ o nine ɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaa. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on soft inner leaves during early plant growth. You can control them by spraying approved biopesticides or applying neem leaf extracts into the plant openings early in the morning.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii amli yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits have dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as Blossom End Rot, which happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium or when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding lime or organic compost helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ lime loo organic compost afata he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni kpamɔ fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high into the sunlight so their leaves can produce food, which is sent underground to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. yɛ hulu la mli koni ebaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii Atsuɔ enɛɛmɛi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil faster than domestic crops, which is why early weeding is necessary to protect your yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe shia tsei. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Ehe miihia ni abu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over easily when a windstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches in soft soil. Supporting the main stem with wooden props or planting in deeper soil prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ shishi loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why are the small flowers falling off my cocoa trees before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from harsh sunlight, dry weather, or pest attacks. Providing shade trees, pruning dead branches, and keeping soil moist helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ni haa hulutsoo, tsei niji ni egboi lɛ afolɔ Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and yellow when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crop seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each maize plant enough space allows its roots to spread wide and absorb what it needs to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛheɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji ni wa.

english: Why does cutting away extra side stems on my tomato plants give me bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo sɛɛ tsei ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tsei amli lɛ, ehaa amɛwoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Tomato plants spend food and water on every stem and leaf they produce. Removing extra side shoots forces the plant to send its food directly into growing larger, healthier tomatoes instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Tomato tsei kɛ niyenii kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ tso kɛ tso baa fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kpojiemɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛyaa tomato ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become small and woody when I farm cassava on the same soil every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei waa lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Planting it repeatedly on the exact same spot drains the soil, causing future crops to struggle. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas puts vital nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii baabɔ mɔdɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tamɔ tsina ŋmei tsake ŋmei lɛ, ehaa nitrogen ni he hiaa waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient in soil. When nitrogen is low, the pepper plant pulls food from its older bottom leaves to nourish new green growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen faaa Pepper tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under strong, full sunlight. Leaving tall shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects young cocoa seedlings until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni eyi obɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ daa.

english: How can I stop my young plantain suckers from drying out during the Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ Harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture rapidly from plant leaves and soil. Covering the ground around the base of your suckers with dry leaves or straw, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and traps moisture near the roots.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ oya. Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworm caterpillars attack my maize crop mostly when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworm ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ fe fɛɛ beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants produce tender, soft leaves that are easy for young caterpillars to chew and digest. Checking under leaves early lets you spot egg clusters before the worms hatch and destroy the crop.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni bibii ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ ni amɛye mli oya. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaha ona ŋmeii akui lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ afɔ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does plowing my farm deeply with a tractor help my yam tubers grow bigger than using a hand hoe?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛ trakta tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa fe bɔ ni mikɛ nine ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii?

english: Tractors loosen soil much deeper than hand hoes can. Deep, soft soil allows root crops like yam and cassava to expand easily underground without hitting hard soil layers that stunt their growth.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kwraa fe nine ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni haaa eda lɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature so it doesn't rot after I harvest it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ akɛ egboŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn dry and brown and a tiny black mark appears at the base of each grain kernel. Harvesting when grains are hard prevents mold and insects from destroying stored maize.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Nikpamɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite ŋmãa ni ato lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my vegetable crops right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in topsoil and sprout instantly with the first heavy rain. Clearing weeds while crops are small prevents weeds from stealing sunlight, water, and fertilizer meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaju hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside young cocoa protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and grow big ears. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or applying rich organic compost will bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Spraying the plants with neem oil water or recommended insecticidal soap gets rid of the pests and stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu, neem fɔ, loo samla ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaatsi baai heei lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I get a chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them for too long, especially in heavy soils during rain heavy seasons. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy after a few months of rest because warm, moist air signals to the tuber that it is time to start a new plant. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated and cool, and gently breaking off the early shoots, keeps the yams fresh for longer.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potatoes fiteɔ wɔɔhe yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ aje tso lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ. Ha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ, ni ofolɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii fioo lɛ blɛoo koni o-sweet potato lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of phosphorus in the ground. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and applying balanced plant food helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ tsei niyenii ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over right when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ dara pɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, so top-heavy stems struggle to hold up a heavy fruit bunch, especially when wind blows. Supporting your bearing plantain trees with a strong wooden prop stick stops the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ amli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ miitswa. Kɛ tsei ni wa fi dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo akajie lɛ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry period that dries out the ground and kills newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures there is enough soil moisture for seeds to grow without dying.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ mɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight directly from your crops. Clearing weeds around your crops early gives the plants full access to the nourishment they need to grow fast and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and tiny droppings inside maize leaves are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Applying biopesticides or a mixture of clean ash and sand into the leaf funnel early in the morning destroys the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Buu ni elaaje kɛ ŋmeii bibii Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni he tse kɛ ŋã ni akɛfutu mli lɛ wo baa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Removing excess suckers prevents them from stealing food and water from the main stem, ensuring the main plant grows a larger, healthier bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ ada ni efee kuu agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally fertilize the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When cassava is planted too close, leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and roots fight for soil nutrients, leading to small, thin tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the ground to catch more sunlight and prevents mud-borne diseases, which helps the plant build bigger yam tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni ekɛtsi helai ni jɛɔ klon mli baa lɛ anaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like someone shot ragged holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ tamɔ mɔ ko ni etswa bu ni etse ehe kɛtsɔ mli lɛ?

english: This pattern of damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center shoot, eating the young leaves as they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai bibii lɛ be mli ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã lɛ

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which spread viruses that distort plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei adalɛ fiteɔ lɛ eshwaa

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients stresses the tomato plant, forcing it to drop blossoms to conserve its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ agbee shi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to water my crops early in the morning instead of during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Morning watering gives roots time to absorb water before heat evaporates it, and allows leaf surfaces to dry quickly to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ hiɛ ni egbiɔ oya koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: What is the main difference between the traditional yam varieties I buy at the local market and the new ones developed by researchers?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ shishijee ŋmɔtɔ ni mihe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee ni niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ teŋ?

english: Traditional varieties like 'Dadako Nyame' are famous for their taste, but newer varieties developed by agricultural scientists are specifically bred to resist local diseases, grow faster, and yield bigger tubers even during dry spells.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Dadako Nyame’ lɛ ehe gbɛi waa yɛ amɛmli ŋmɔlɔ hewɔ. Shi henɔi heei Okwaayeli he nilelɔi fee, ni akwɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. edaa oya ni ehaa yitsei wuji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po

english: If I try planting a newly developed crop variety on my farm, will the tubers taste different from my usual traditional crops?
ga: Kɛ mika akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni afee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani bulbs lɛ naa ŋɔɔmɔ yɛ srɔto fe mi daa tsei lɛ?

english: Researchers specifically test new crop varieties with local farmers and consumers to make sure they keep the traditional taste, texture, and pounding quality that people love, while giving you better harvest yields.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi kɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi kɛ jarayelɔi kaa tsei srɔtoi heei amɛkwɛɔ titri lɛ Enɛ haa amɛhiɛɔ kusum mli ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni gbɔmɛi sumɔɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested yams stay dormant for months in the barn before they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams naturally go through a resting period called dormancy after harvest to protect themselves from dry weather. The tuber will only sprout when internal biological signals tell the plant that the ideal planting weather has returned.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ naa be ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ he Tubers baakwɛ̃ pɛ kɛji akɛ wala yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛɛ tso lɛ akɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ eku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do yam vines need wooden stakes or ropes to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei he hiaa tsei loo kpãi ni amɛkɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high above the moist ground, catching sunlight while protecting the plant from fungal diseases that thrive on wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Enaa hulu la ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow new yam plants from the tiny flowers on the vines, or must I always plant pieces of the tuber?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ sweet potato tsei heei kɛjɛ fɔfɔi bibii amli? Ani ebaanyɛ ehi wain tso lɛ nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ makwɛ bulb lɛ mli bibii bibii be fɛɛ be?

english: While yams do produce flowers and real seeds, farmers usually plant tuber pieces because true seeds are difficult to germinate and take much longer to produce edible, full-sized tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ sweet potatoes woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ moŋ, Shi bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ duɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli bibii bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewa akɛ anɔkwa dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ bulbs ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu ni ayeɔ.

english: Does planting yams in high earth mounds really help the tubers grow bigger than planting them in flat ground?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa diɛŋtsɛ fe ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, building loose, soft mounds makes it easy for yam tubers to expand deep underground without struggling against hard soil, while also preventing excess rainwater from pooling and rotting the tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on some of my yam vines turn black and drop off early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called leaf spot or anthracnose, which spreads quickly in hot, humid weather. Using disease-resistant varieties or spraying appropriate organic fungicides helps keep the leaves healthy so the tubers can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaf spot loo anthracnose kɛbaa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams rot quickly in the barn while others stay good for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi hi lolo nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Rot happens when tiny fungi or bacteria enter bruises on the yam skin created during harvest. Varieties with thicker skin and lower water content naturally resist rot better and store longer in warm barns.
ga: Rot baa kɛji ŋmeii bibii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ba. Nibii ni shwieɔ sweet potato nɔ ni baa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Hei srɔtoi ni amɛhewolo lɛ mli wa ni nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I get more seed yams to plant if I don't have enough full-sized tubers left over?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná sweet potato dumɔwui babaoo ni mikɛdu kɛji mibɛ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛ?

english: You can cut healthy, clean tubers into small 50-gram pieces called 'minisetts', treat the cut edges with wood ash to prevent rot, and plant them close together to produce many small seed yams for the following season.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli bibii ni tsiimɔ ji 50g ni atsɛɔ amɛ 'minisettes'. Okɛ tso sũ atsu ŋwɛigbɛi ni afo lɛ ahe nii koni amɛkafite. ni odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo dumɔwui bibii ni ji yams. Lots kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young yam plants turning light yellow long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the soil is running low on nutrients like nitrogen, or that microscopic worms called nematodes are damaging the roots underground and stopping the plant from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: If I spray my crops directly with very strong water pressure from a pipe, will it harm them?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli wa waa ni jɛ hose lɛ mli lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ani ebaaye tsei awui loo ebaayeee amɛ awui?

english: Yes, intense water pressure can wash away topsoil, expose roots, knock off flowers, and tear delicate leaves. It is better to break strong water streams into a gentle spray or soft flow so the plant can absorb moisture safely.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni mli wa baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ egbala baai ni waaa lɛ mli Esa akɛ agbala nu ni mli wa lɛ mli ni etsɔ nu ni hoɔ blɛoo loo nɔ ni hoɔ blɛoo koni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I safely use stagnant or standing water on my farm to water my crops during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo nu ni ekã shi shiŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe koni mikɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, stagnant water can be used for irrigation, but it should be applied directly to the soil near the base of the plant rather than sprayed over leaves, as standing water can sometimes carry pathogens that cause leaf diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ nu ni damɔ shi atsu nii kɛshwie nu nɔ. Shi esa akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, bei komɛi lɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni kɛ baai helai baa lɛ.

english: What happens to my pepper plants if heavy rainfall leaves water sitting around their roots for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu tara shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo?

english: Water standing around roots for too long suffocates them by cutting off oxygen. This leads to root rot, causing the plant's leaves to turn yellow, wilt, and eventually die even though there is plenty of water.
ga: Nu ni hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛgbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ kɛ nu babaoo po.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural self-defense trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai ni atsɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he koni akɛba he ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa egbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as intense heat, inconsistent watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant hold onto its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my yam vines droop during midday heat even when the soil still feels somewhat moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ gboɔ aaafee shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo lolo po.

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. As long as there is moisture in the soil, the vines usually recover and stand firm again in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, wain tsei lɛ he waaa ni amɛdamɔ shi ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and die if I do not plant plantains or shade trees next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a natural umbrella that protects cocoa seedlings from harsh sun and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli shade ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and fall off while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally shift nutrients from older lower leaves to support new growth at the top. However, if many leaves turn yellow early, it usually indicates a lack of nutrients like nitrogen or temporary drought stress.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baa ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi dalɛ hee aba. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai babaoo miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ he haomɔ bɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete fiercely for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants waste energy stretching tall to reach light instead of growing thick stems and large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yeɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛgbalaa amɛhe koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, du tso tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa.

english: Why is it better for me to transplant my vegetable seedlings in the evening instead of the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ aduawai adumɔwui awo he kroko gbɛkɛ moŋ fe leebi lɛ?

english: Transplanting in the evening gives seedlings a cool night to rest and establish their roots in new soil without facing immediate heat and direct sunlight, which reduces transplant shock and plant loss.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛɛɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tso ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ kɛ tso ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is soft, loose soil better for planting groundnuts than hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers produce pegs that must push down into the soil to grow nuts underground. Loose, sandy-loam soil allows these pegs to easily penetrate the ground and gives the pods enough room to expand properly.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow long leafy stems but small tubers when I put too much manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa shishifãi kakadaji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii babaoo fataa he lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure causes cassava to put all its energy into growing lush leaves and stems above ground, leaving very little energy to develop thick tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni baaha yitso ni mli wa aba shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do groundnut plants flower above the ground if the nuts grow under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated on the branches, the flower stems lengthen into stems called 'pegs.' These pegs automatically curve downward and bury themselves into the soil where the nuts safely develop away from sun heat and pests.
ga: Beni afee ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ 'pegs'. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfuɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a protective behavior maize uses to survive heat. By curling up, the leaves reduce their exposure to direct sunlight and trap moisture inside, keeping the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ, amɛhaa hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Tsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi

english: Plantain trees have broad leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly in severe heat. The plant sheds lower leaves to conserve water and protect its main trunk until the rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa he. Tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli ni ebu tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What makes plantain trees fall over easily when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots; instead, they have shallow root mats near the soil surface. When heavy bunches form, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily tip over in wet, loose soil unless supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, sisi fã ko nɛ e mi kuɔ we ngɛ zugba a hɛ mi. Beni jwɛi lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni etse lɛ nɔ oya. ja akɛ tso ko efi sɛɛ

english: Why do yam vines need tall bamboo sticks or poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ŋmei loo tso kakadaŋŋ koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce energy through their leaves. Staking spreads the leaves out toward the sunlight, preventing leaves from rotting on damp ground and helping the plant produce big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji

english: Is it safe to grow groundnuts and plantains on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts around young plantain plants works well. Groundnuts cover the soil to keep moisture in and fix natural nitrogen into the earth, which helps feed the growing plantain trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Plantain bibii hu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli ni ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when the bush around them is too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ beni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Thick weeds and dense shade trap wet air around cocoa trees. This humid environment creates ideal conditions for black pod fungal disease to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ bɔleɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha black pod fungus hela lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ pod mli kɛya pod mli.

english: How do I know groundnuts are mature and ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts show signs of maturity when the outer leaves turn yellowish and drop off. You can test-dig a few pods—if the inside of the pod shell has darkened veins and the seeds fill the shell completely, the crop is ready.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ dalɛ he okadi kpo kɛji kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Obaanyɛ oka dig pods 2-3 okwɛ kɛji pod lɛ mli yɛ fãji ni tsuɔ diŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ eyi kɛ dumɔwui. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Flowering is a very sensitive period for mango trees. Stress from sudden dry weather, pests, or disease can cause the tree to shed its blossoms early, so trees need careful attention as soon as flowers appear.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be ni mango tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo helai amli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afɔlɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji fɔfɔii je kpo pɛ.

english: What is the most critical time to care for my fruit trees if I want a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji miitao nikpamɔ babaoo?

english: The most critical period is from the moment the tree flowers until you harvest the fruit. Protecting the flowers, watering properly, and controlling pests during this window determines how much fruit you will actually harvest.
ga: Be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji kɛjɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi kɛyashi be mli ni obaakpa enɔ yibii lɛ. protecting flowers Nu ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ aduawai enyiɛ ni obaakpa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do young fruits keep falling off my tree weeks after the flowers have died off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii shwieɔ mitso lɛ nɔ otsii komɛi sɛɛ beni fɔfɔi lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Young fruits drop when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or water, or when fruit-boring insects attack. Sustaining tree care straight through from blossoming until harvest prevents this loss.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni sa. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ aduawai lɛ tutua bo Otsei lɛ akwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Can I still get a good crop yield if I am only farming part-time while keeping another job?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo kɛji mikɛ be fã tsu okwaayeli ni miná nitsumɔ kroko?

english: Yes, part-time farming can be productive if you focus your labor on key times—such as planting, flowering, and harvesting—and choose crops like fruit trees that do not require full-time daily attention.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fã mli okwaayeli baanyɛ awo yibii kɛji akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ma bei titrii tamɔ dumɔwui, fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nɔ. Ni halamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ aduawai tsei ni biɔ be fɛɛ, daa gbi kwɛmɔ.

english: Is it really possible to get a high yield of crops if I only have a small space around my home compound?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ maná yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ kɛji miyɛ he bibioo ko ni bɔle mishia lɛ he?

english: Yes, small spaces can produce high yields if you manage them intensively using techniques like container farming, vertical planting, or planting high-value crops that give plenty of harvest in limited areas.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei bibii baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɔɔ he kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋaa gbɛ̀i tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ tsu nii kɛkwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ he ko fioo pɛ lɛ adumɔ

english: How should I water my crops once they start showing flowers?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ?

english: Crops need consistent moisture when flowering to help flowers develop into fruits, but overwatering can cause blossoms to rot and fall off. Steady, moderate water is best during the flowering period.
ga: Tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ amɛmiifɔlɔ koni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai. Shi nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo ni amɛgbee shi. Nu ni anáa daa ni fa fioo lɛ hi fe fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: What can I do to protect delicate crop blossoms from being eaten by insects?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mabu mitsei lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Regularly inspect your crops when flowers emerge and use safe, recommended pest treatments so you kill harmful insects without harming beneficial bees that help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ. ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii. No hewɔ lɛ ogbeɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni oyeee ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni etsɔ aduawai lɛ awui.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so the flowers turn into heavy fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛfee nɔ ni tsii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied just before or at the start of the flowering stage so the plant has enough nutrients to support the blossoms and feed the growing fruits up until harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani fɔfɔii lɛ abɔi loo yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee mli. Koni aha tsei lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua amɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to clear weeds and trim branches before trees blossom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie jwɛi ni wɔfolɔ tsei lɛ anɔ dani tsei lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds and trimming dead branches allows maximum sunlight and airflow to reach the tree, helping it direct all its energy into producing healthy flowers and strong fruit set.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: How do I know if my fruit trees are producing as much harvest as they are supposed to?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ miiwo yibii babaoo bɔ ni sa?

english: If your tree puts out many flowers but ends up with very few fruits at harvest time, it means the tree lost potential along the way due to lack of care during the critical stage between flowering and harvesting.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ kwɛmɔ ni bɛ yɛ be ni he hiaa waa ni ka fɔfɔi kɛ kpamɔɔ teŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How can I use manure from my farm animals like pigs and chickens to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tsinai kɛ kooloi amli lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure is rich in essential nutrients that feed the soil. However, fresh manure can burn crop roots because it generates too much heat and has high nitrogen levels, so you must let it dry or compost it before spreading it around your crops.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii hee baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo babaoo baa, ni eyɛ nitrogen babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni oha egbi loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani okɛshwã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow because the soil is weak or because of insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kooloi bibii ahewɔ?

english: If lower, older leaves turn pale yellow evenly across the whole field, the soil usually lacks nitrogen. If the yellowing appears in random spots, with holes, curling leaves, or sticky film, pests are likely attacking the plants.
ga: Kɛji eba shi fe nakai lɛ, baai ni egbɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi je kpo trukaa ni bu, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo sini ko ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ atutua tsei.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up in the strong sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They naturally require shade from temporary plants like plantains or shade trees to block harsh heat and keep moisture in the air while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni amɛkafee hulutsoo fe nine, ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves fall off the trees during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a survival behavior for cocoa trees to save water during dry weather. By shedding leaves, the tree loses less water through evaporation and protects itself until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tsei lɛ ashihilɛ mli nifeemɔ ko koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu fioo pɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa lasu mli ni ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Cocoa trees shed extra flowers when they experience stress from drought, poor soil nutrients, or hot winds. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and maintaining good soil health helps more flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi titri lɛ kɛ́ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod on the tree is fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Mature cocoa pods change color completely, turning from green or dark red to bright yellow or yellow-orange. The seeds inside also loosen from the inner pod wall, making a hollow sound when gently tapped.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pod gbogbo lɛ mligbɛ. Ehaa gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ blɛoo.

english: Why should I cut off the soft green branches growing straight out from the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These straight shoots, called chupons, drain energy, water, and plant nutrients away from the main tree. Removing them directs all the plant's strength into growing flowers and healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ tsei ni ja nɛɛ akɛ chupon. Ejieɔ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajieɔ lɛ lɛ, eheɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree when it rains a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess water and high humidity create a perfect environment for Black Pod disease, which is caused by a fungus. Pruning thick overhead branches lets sunlight and air flow through to dry off the pods quickly.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko kɛbaa lɛ baa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni mli tse yɛ yiteŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya.

english: Will planting food crops like cassava close to my cocoa trees affect how the cocoa grows?
ga: Ani niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ masɛi lɛ baaná kookoo lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, cassava roots spread wide and draw heavily on soil moisture and nutrients. If planted too close to young cocoa, cassava will compete with the cocoa trees and slow down their development.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he ni egbalaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ cocoa bibioo lɛ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ cocoo baabɔ akaŋ ni ebaaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Is it safe for me to let my cattle or goats wander around inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã tsinai loo tooi ayashara shi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Allowing livestock to roam freely can harm your crops because they chew young leaves, break flower-bearing stems, and pack the soil down hard with their hooves, which makes it difficult for crop roots to breathe.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ kooloi gbɛ ni amɛnyiɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. ejaakɛ eyeɔ baai bibii Gbalamɔ tso ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. ni amɛkɛ amɛtsitsii tsu nii ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu.

english: How do I know if my land is fully prepared and ready before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Proper preparation means clearing weeds, loosening the soil so young roots can spread easily, and ensuring water can drain properly. Planting in unprepared ground makes it hard for seeds to sprout and access soil nutrients.
ga: Hesaamɔ ni sa tsɔɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni akwɛ koni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni asaaa he lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃ ni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain of the season before putting my seeds into the soil?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ koni madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should wait until the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days after rain. The very first rain often dries out quickly, and planting too early can cause seeds to dry up and die in the hot ground.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya. Ni kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient. When food is short, the plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko. Kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the heat, helping the plant save water and stay alive during peak sunshine.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to move pollen around. Without successful pollination, the plant drops the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bɛ ni baajie fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ yeee omanye Tso lɛ hu baashwie fɔfɔi.

english: What will happen to my yield if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin stalks with very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe tseee. Ayɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ŋmeii bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden stakes to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves upward toward direct sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the plant make food to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai kɛya ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii koni bulbs lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do farmers plant plantain trees before putting young cocoa seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains dani amɛkɛ kookoo dumɔwui woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide broad leaf shade and keep the soil moist, acting as protective umbrellas while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei bibii ni daa oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibioo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I put animal manure on my field weeks before planting instead of on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo ŋmɔji amli otsii babaoo dani adu nii yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Fresh manure produces heat and strong chemicals as it breaks down, which can burn young seed roots. Adding it weeks earlier allows it to break down safely into gentle nutrients that enrich the soil.
ga: Manɔ hee jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa kpo beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ashã. Kɛ́ akɛfata he otsi kome dani eba lɛ, ehaa egbɛɔ eshwaa shweshweeshwe ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni mli jɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What will happen to my cassava crop if the rains stop earlier than expected this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava is tough and will survive dry spells, but without enough rain, the plant stops growing big tubers underground and saves its energy just to stay alive, resulting in a smaller harvest.
ga: Cassava ji tso ni wa ni hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ baakpa bulbs ni amɛkwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛbaakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: What is eating the leaves inside the top funnel of my young maize plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji shishi akɛ ayeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-funnel lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar that hides inside the maize leaves. You can protect your crop by checking your farm early, spraying recommended pesticides when the plants are young, or applying clean ash mixed with sand directly into the plant funnels.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ. Aloo okɛ sũ ni he tse ni akɛ ŋã efutu mli lɛ awo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using infected stems for planting. You can prevent it by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agriculture offices and pulling out infected plants early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ adumɔ nɔ Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ mra.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them after maize naturally restores nutrients to the land, making the soil richer for your next crop without buying as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build strong roots, catch daylight, and produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa, nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: If previous crops had pale or yellow leaves, grew very slowly, or produced small yields, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Testing your soil through an extension officer or observing if weeds grow weakly can tell you if you need to add compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ekwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko lɛ Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ extension worker nɔ loo oyɔse jwɛi ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ loo edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo kɛji ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, because the plant cannot form seeds properly under extreme heat. Providing shade, watering regularly at the base, and mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Akɛni tomato tsei nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli hewɔ lɛ, ha amɛshishigbɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu daa. ni mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to young cocoa shields them from the hot sun and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ cocoa bibii ahe lɛ, ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first planting generation. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will yield much less grain and grow unevenly, so it is better to buy fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji obua nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni odu lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baawo dumɔwui fioo kwraa ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting quickly in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ekafite oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers rot when stored in hot, damp places or when bruised during harvesting. You can prevent rot by storing undamaged yams in a well-ventilated, shaded barn off the ground and checking them regularly to remove any decaying tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ loo kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Obaanyɛ otsi fitemɔ naa kɛtsɔ sweet potatoes ni efiteee ni oookɛto ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni okwɛ daa koni ojie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly even after I have cleared my farm with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dade shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Cutting weeds with a cutlass only removes the top parts, leaving seeds buried in the soil and strong roots underground that quickly sprout again. Clearing weeds early before they set seeds and using mulching or cover crops helps suppress them for longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ jwɛi lɛ, ejieɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra dani dumɔwui lɛ awoɔ Ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster when I mix chicken manure into my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and essential nutrients that feed the soil, giving your crops the quick energy boost they need to grow strong stems and healthy green leaves.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hewalɛ oya ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe to mix chicken manure together with local plant-based fertilizers before feeding my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei baafutu maŋ lɛ mli tsei ahe ŋmei dani akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, mixing chicken manure with plant-based organic fertilizer balances fast-acting nutrients with long-lasting organic matter, providing your crops with both immediate food and healthy soil throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei futu tso mli ŋmei mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni tsuɔ nii oya lɛ kɛ tsofa ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni afee klalo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How quickly will my crops show signs of improvement after I apply chicken manure?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔɔ hiɛyaa oya ha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: In warm, moist Ghanaian soil, chicken manure breaks down rapidly, usually showing visible results like greener leaves and stronger growth within two to three weeks.
ga: yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Kooloi ashishifã fiteɔ oya. Bei pii lɛ, amɛjieɔ yibii ni anaa tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa kpo yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: How should I sprinkle fertilizer around my crops so it doesn't burn them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie ehe? Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmɔshi nibii akashã?

english: Sprinkle the fertilizer around the base of the plant near the root line rather than dumping it directly on young stems or leaves, which prevents leaf burn and allows roots to absorb it safely.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie tsei bibii loo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Enɛ tsiɔ baa lɛ shãa naa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my crops yield better when I use locally produced organic fertilizer instead of leaving the soil natural?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii moŋ fe ni mahã shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses its natural food from repeated farming. Locally produced organic fertilizers restore essential plant nutrients and organic material to worn-out earth, helping crops produce larger harvests.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ miiho kɛjɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ mli. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ organic nibii baa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkpaa yibii babaoo.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer at once cause my crops to lose their flowers?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ afite?

english: Yes, giving crops too much fertilizer or uncomposted manure at one time can burn the roots or cause the plant to produce extra leaves while dropping its flowers and young fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ baai babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient that plants need to build food, grow leaves, and maintain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii, amɛkwɛ̃ baai, ni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy crops have sturdy upright stems, thick dark-green leaves, and steady growth without sudden leaf yellowing or stunted development before flowering.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wa, ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. Baai ni mli tse, ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baai lɛ efeee ŋmɔŋ loo edalɛ blɛoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do crop roots grow deeper when I add organic fertilizer made from trees and plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ tsei kɛ tsei fee lɛ fata he lɛ?

english: Plant-based organic fertilizers loosen hard soil and improve moisture retention, making it easier for roots to stretch wide and deep to find food and water.
ga: Organic tsei ahe ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu mlɛo.

english: How does using organic plant fertilizer help my crops survive when dry spells come?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic fertilizers add spongy natural matter to the soil that holds rainwater longer, allowing your crops to stay hydrated even when rains stop for a short period.
ga: Organic fertilizers kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be kukuoo ko po.

english: Why do my stored beans get full of tiny holes and white powder after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmɔji ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Those holes are caused by tiny pests called bean weevils that lay eggs inside the beans. Storing your dry beans in airtight bags or clean sealed containers starves the insects of air so they cannot multiply and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni yeɔ bu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Atsɛɔ lɛ bean weevil, ni woɔ wɔji yɛ bean dumɔwui amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsi ni mli tse ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛya hiɛ ni amɛfite nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to dry my harvested maize so it does not rot in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ koni ekafite yɛ mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: Spread your harvested maize on clean tarpaulins in full sunlight for several days until the kernels are hard enough that your fingernail cannot dent them. Removing all moisture prevents dampness, mold, and rot from destroying your grain.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbɛ ashwã tarp ni he tse nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii babaoo kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ oniji ahe tsɔi lɛ shwieŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested millet go bad so quickly if I gather it during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting during wet weather traps rain and humidity inside the grain heads, causing damp rot and dangerous molds to grow within days. It is best to wait for dry weather or dry the heads immediately off the ground in a well-ventilated area.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmaa yitso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui baa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi loo oooha oyitso agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my stored corn has gone bad and is unsafe to feed to my family?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ efite ni ehiii akɛ mahã miweku lɛ niyenii?

english: If your corn shows dark mold, smells damp or musty, or feels sticky, it has spoiled. This mold creates harmful toxins called aflatoxins that cause severe sickness and cannot be washed or cooked away.
ga: Kɛji o-corn lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ayɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ Tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ efite. Nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ feɔ tsofa ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin. ni kɛ hela ni naa wa baa ni anyɛɛɛ afɔ he loo ahoo lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant will help it turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ woɔ he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ shishi baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop armyworm caterpillars from chewing up my maize leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ anaa?

english: Check your farm regularly early in the morning when the worms come out to feed. You can spray safe approved insecticides early in the crop's growth or drop neem leaf extract mixed with soapy water into the funnel of each maize plant.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi beni ŋmeii jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie nɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tso lɛ dalɛ shishijee mli. Aloo okɛ neem baa mli nu ni akɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ efutu mli lɛ awo ŋmãa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli.

english: Your rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a bright golden yellow while the lower stem remains slightly green. Harvesting too late makes the grains shatter onto the ground or break into tiny pieces during milling.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsɔɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse lɛ. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ fioo. Kɛ́ akpa dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ loo amɛgbala bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni akpãa nii lɛ.

english: Why does my rice grow very tall in some parts of my field but stay short and weak in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice lɛ kɛlɛ waa yɛ hei komɛi shi eyɛ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Rice grows unevenly when water and soil nutrients are not spread equally across the field. leveling your plot before planting ensures that water sits at the same depth everywhere, allowing all the plants to feed equally.
ga: Omɔ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlijaa ejaaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fee pɛpɛɛpɛ dani odu nii lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ mli akwɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tsei fɛɛ aná niyenii pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are natural soil restorers that pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the earth. Planting them after maize refreshes the soil naturally, making it richer for the next crop.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save maize seeds from my current harvest to plant during the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu okwaayeli be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Most improved seed varieties bought from agro-dealers yield well only for their first planting. If you save seeds from your harvest to replant, the resulting plants will grow weak, uneven, and produce much smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaha yibii kpakpai aba kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ to koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ. Tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ, amɛfeee ekome ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Is it advisable to replace my old cocoa trees with new seedlings, and how will that affect my harvest?
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui heei awo kookoo tsei momoi lɛ anajiaŋ. Ni te ebaasa mikpamɔ lɛ he eha tɛŋŋ?
