english: Old cocoa trees become less productive and more prone to diseases over time. Replacing them with modern high-yielding, disease-resistant cocoa varieties restores long-term profit, even though you must wait a few years for the new trees to start bearing fruit.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni edara lɛ wooo yibii babaoo, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baato amɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ebaawo nyɔmɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ omɛ afii fioo komɛi dani tsei heei aje yibiiwoo shishi moŋ.

english: Why should I buy hybrid maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred to yield much higher harvests and withstand local pests and droughts better. Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations, resulting in smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my stored grains like maize turn into dust after keeping them in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa ni mikɛto, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, bafeɔ sũ beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Weevils and grain borers eat stored maize from the inside out if the grain is not dried completely before storage or if left unprotected. Drying grains properly and using airtight hermetic bags suffocates these pests without needing heavy chemicals.
ga: Weevils kɛ seed borers yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni abuuu amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛ vacuum bags ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɔjɔ ni tsofai ni tsii he ehiaaa.

english: How can I safely store my harvested grain for months so I can wait to sell when prices go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo koni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ amɛjara tee hiɛ?

english: To hold grain safely without spoilage, dry it until it is hard and crackling, store it in clean hermetic (airtight) bags, and keep the bags on raised wooden platforms away from concrete floors and moisture.
ga: Koni akɛ dumɔwui ato shweshweeshwe ni efiteee Ha egbi kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbɛ eshwa. Okɛwo kotoku ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli ni okɛ kotoku lɛ awo tso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛjɛ kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips that spread viral diseases. Checking under the leaves early and spraying with neem oil solution can prevent the disease from ruining your field investment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ hela naa koni ekafite oŋmɔ mli nibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: What makes my cassava roots rot underground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water collects in the soil due to poor drainage during heavy rains. The standing water suffocates the roots and allows fungal diseases in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa bulb lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Pale yellow leaves mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure early will restore the plant's health.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I protect my tomato crop investment from drying out and dying during a dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi tomato ni mikɛwo mli lɛ he koni ekagbi ni egbo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil around your tomato plants with dry grass or straw (mulching) traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents the sun from quickly drying out the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi (mulching) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa hulu la ni haa shishifãi lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to bear fruit when planted in worn-out soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of nutrients and organic matter to grow fast. In poor soil, the plant grows slowly because it lacks the food needed to develop strong stems and heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Niyenii babaoo kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli he miihia plantains koni ekwɛ̃ oya. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ Tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer that feeds the nearby maize and keeps the soil fertile for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when too much water stays around the roots after heavy rains. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist helps the leaves grow green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid applying fertilizer on my farm when the soil is completely dry during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve into the soil so roots can absorb them. Applying chemical fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch crop roots and waste money, as the nutrients sit on the surface without helping the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baahi ŋwɛi ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain seedlings next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantain dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put many seeds together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ bu kome lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving each crop proper space allows it to build strong roots and thick stems.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli wa.

english: Why is it important for me to lift and stake my yam vines on sticks instead of letting them creep on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni madu yɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking gets yam leaves off the ground and up into the sunlight so the plant can feed itself better, leading to bigger yam tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛwoɔ hulu la mli koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye amɛhe niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning dense branches, clearing weeds around cocoa trees, and removing infected pods keeps airflow high and lowers moisture levels.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. dense pruning Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the shoot funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ, Mine lɛ etee bud cone lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking crops early and applying recommended pest treatments directly into the central shoot helps stop the caterpillars before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. Ni kɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from young leaves and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents leaves from puckering and keeps fruit growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big foliage, but the tubers under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Cassava puts its energy into leaves instead of tubers when planted in soil with excessive nitrogen or when planted too close together. Proper plant spacing ensures energy is sent downward into root growth.
ga: Cassava jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ebaai lɛ amli yɛ eshishifãi lɛ najiaŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa hewalɛ yaa shi kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too high, when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, or when there are too few insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering at root level helps hold the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nu daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are people telling me to stop using chemical weedkillers on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ makpa tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers stay in the ground and can damage the soil's natural nutrients over time. Overusing them harms the land and weak roots of your cocoa trees, whereas clearing weeds physically keeps the soil rich and healthy.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ebaanyɛ efite sũ lɛ mli niyenii kpakpai yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaaye shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ awui. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does chemical weed killer actually affect my land over time?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ saa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli?

english: Chemical weed killers kill beneficial living organisms in the soil that help break down plant material into plant food. Over time, this leaves your land hard, dry, and less fertile for crop growth.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ tsei amli nibii amli kɛfeɔ tsei niyenii. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, nɔ ni egbi, ni nɔ ni baa shi kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: What is the safest way to clear weeds on my farm without damaging the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Using mechanical weed cutters or cutlasses cuts the weeds at the surface without putting harsh chemicals into the dirt. The cut weeds then rot on top of the soil and turn into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, efoɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni mli wa fataaa muji lɛ he. Jwɛi ni afo lɛ baagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Is it better to clear weeds with a machine or spray chemical weedicide on my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ tsɔne baakpa jwɛi loo mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baashwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clearing with a machine is better because it clears the thick bush fast without poisoning the earth. Your soil remains alive and fertile, allowing crops to feed well without chemical damage.
ga: Mashiŋ ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ejieɔ brɔshi ni mli tse oya ni ekɛ tsofa fɔŋ wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ebaa nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai efiteee amɛ.

english: How can a petrol weeding machine help me manage my land better than chemical sprays?
ga: Te tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛ petroleum tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A petrol weeding machine uses a small amount of fuel to slash down heavy grass quickly. It saves you heavy manual labor while protecting your soil from chemical damage.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ pɛtrol tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛ tsofa fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ jwɛi ni tsii oya. Ehaa onáaa nitsumɔ ni heɔ be babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Can I use motorized clearing machines when preparing my land before planting cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu kookoo?

english: Yes, motorized brush cutters are great for land preparation. They trim down unwanted vegetation cleanly so you can plant without disturbing or destroying the topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ saamɔ. Amɛfoɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu ni ogbalaaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ loo okpataaa ehiɛ.

english: What does pruning mean, and why should I cut branches off my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni ji tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji?

english: Pruning means cutting away unwanted, diseased, or overcrowded branches. It helps the tree save energy, lets air flow through, and allows sunlight to reach the main trunk where cocoa pods grow.
ga: Niji ni ataooo, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsɔɔ mli ni ehaa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree weaken it or make it die?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ baaha egbɔjɔ loo ebaagbe lɛ?

english: No, cutting the right branches makes the tree stronger. It forces the tree to direct its food and water toward flowering and pod growth rather than wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ afo tso lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aha fɔfɔi kɛ pod lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why is my cocoa tree growing so many green leaves but not bearing enough pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshishifãi lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many thick leaves and branches, it spends all its food maintaining them instead of making pods. Trimming off extra branches encourages the tree to produce more cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ baai kɛ eniji ni mli edɔ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmeii lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ehe nɔ. Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does cutting cocoa tree branches help stop crop diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cacao tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ tsei ahe helai anaa?

english: Thick, uncut branches trap damp air and shade, which creates a wet environment where diseases like black pod thrive. Pruning lets sunlight and dry air in to keep the tree dry and healthy.
ga: Niji ni mli tse ni afolɔko lɛ mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi boteɔ mli koni tso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when the ground is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture for the young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. You can prevent it by pruning tree branches to let in light and air, and by removing all infected pods immediately so the disease doesn't spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ooofolɔ sɛɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the field and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ tsei awo shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to manufacture the energy required to grow large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf rot and maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my young maize right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths on soft green leaves after early rains. Checking your field frequently and applying neem oil or recommended organic sprays early stops them before they destroy the crop's growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli shii abɔ Ni okɛ neem fɔ loo organic spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii mra. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop mainly due to stress caused by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and adding organic compost helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin tubers when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tseee waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, their roots compete heavily for nutrients, space, and water underground. Proper spacing allows each plant's roots to spread out freely and grow thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii, he ko, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Is burning the dried bush on my farm before planting good or bad for my soil?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egbi ni mishãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning gives a quick burst of ash nutrients, but it destroys important organic matter and kills beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops long-term. Clearing without fire preserves soil moisture and natural fertility.
ga: Shãa lɛ jieɔ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ. La bɛ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my cassava field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This enriches the soil with free fertilizer that helps nearby crops like cassava grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my plantain bunch is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp angular ridges and become full and plump, and when the dark flower remnants at the tips easily dry up and break off.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔji lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛkuu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi diji ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛkumɔ oya lɛ.

english: How do I use parts of my old cassava plant to grow new ones?
ga: Mikɛ fãi lɛ baatsu nii. Te abaafee tɛŋŋ adu ŋmei tsei momo yɛ tsei heei anɔ?

english: Cassava is grown using stem cuttings rather than seeds. You cut healthy, mature stems into short pieces and plant them in the soil; these cuttings sprout roots and fresh leaves, creating a new plant with the same qualities as the original.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Ofoɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli kukuji ni okɛduɔ shikpɔŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ baai heei aba. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso hee ni hiɛ nibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose thick, mature stems from cassava plants that showed no signs of disease or leaf damage. Healthy stems should be firm, moist on the inside, and have clear, raised buds that are ready to sprout when planted.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse ni eda kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni bɛ hela loo baa ni efite lɛ he okadi ko lɛ mli. Esa akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa. Ha emli afee fɛ̃i ni oha fɔfɔii ni mli tse afee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji adu.

english: Can I grow new plantain plants from seeds, or do I have to use shoots from the main plant?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli? Aloo esa akɛ okɛ tso titri lɛ mli ŋmeii atsu nii?

english: Plantains do not produce viable seeds for farming. Instead, you multiply them by carefully separating small shoots, called suckers, from the base of a healthy adult plant and planting those suckers in new soil.
ga: Plantain lɛ wooo dumɔwui ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi okɛ amɛ feɔ babaoo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ogbalaa mli lɛ nɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoots Ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ ashishi. ni okɛ nakai tsei lɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ

english: Why do my tomato seedlings die when I move them from the nursery bed to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate like newborn babies and suffer shock when transplanted. To protect them, water the nursery bed before lifting them, handle the roots carefully without stripping the soil, and transplant in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe waaa tamɔ abifao ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ, ni kɛ́ ajie amɛ awo he kroko lɛ, amɛbaafee naakpɛɛ. koni ebu amɛhe Numɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatsoi lɛ anɔ dani owó amɛ nɔ. Okɛ shishifãi lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbala. ni aduɔ yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains or shade trees growing right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ aná plantains loo shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Tender cocoa seedlings burn easily in direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a protective umbrella that keeps the young cocoa cool and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ he feɔ fɛo.

english: Why should I keep my harvested seeds in a cool, dry place before the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi dani shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Seeds are living plant embryos that react to heat and moisture. Keeping them in a cool, dry place keeps them asleep and healthy; moisture or heat causes them to rot or sprout too early before they reach the farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ji fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni feɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Fɛ̃i loo dɔlɛ haa amɛgboiɔ loo amɛshwereɔ oya tsɔ dani amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to plant maize seeds directly in the soil or raise them in a nursery first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo madu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Maize should be planted directly into the farm soil because its roots grow rapidly and do not tolerate being disturbed. Sowing seeds straight into the ground produces stronger stems and higher yields than transplanting.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni nɔ ko gbala amɛnaa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of planting my crops on raised mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Both flat and mound planting work well, but raised mounds loosen tight soil and help excess water drain away. This makes it much easier for root crops like yams and cassava to expand and yield larger tubers.
ga: Flat kɛ mound dumɔwui fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes kɛ cassava akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo tuber wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing when the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in young pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus carried by these insects. Keeping the young crop protected from pests prevents this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei bibii anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Nibii bibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings rot in the ground instead of sprouting fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ baai heei lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, placed in waterlogged soil, or taken from diseased parent plants. Always plant healthy stems with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky in well-drained soil.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. aloo ajie kɛjɛ nyɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli Dumɔ tsei ni wa ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting them next to fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that protect the delicate leaves from sun scorch while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop curling up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward as a natural defense mechanism to trap moisture and reduce water loss through evaporation during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures are too high or water supply is inconsistent, as the plant becomes too stressed to support fruit development.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have thick green leaves above ground but very tiny stems underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani tso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil encourages the cassava plant to put all its energy into growing leafy branches above ground rather than storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants shrinking, twisting, and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a plant virus spread by these insects, which stunts healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsilɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni haa baa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ afata he koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need support to lift their leaves off the ground and spread them out to capture full sunlight, which allows the plant to produce enough food to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my green maize turning pale yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei eŋɔli lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant is pulling nutrients from old leaves to feed newer growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihe niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha tso hee ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I remove the extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Main plantain tso lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to compete with the main plantain stem for water, light, and soil nutrients, leading to smaller fruit bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ plantain tso titri lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates sharply between dry and wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi kɛ nɔ ni edɔ teŋ.

english: Why are my cabbages growing tall with open leaves instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni agbele mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when exposed to high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of proper soil nutrients like phosphorus during their early growth stage.
ga: Kaabage lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ ekɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ shishijee bei amli.

english: Why does my crop field dry out completely just a few weeks after the heavy rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to sun and wind through evaporation. Without mulch, organic compost, or tree cover to shield the ground, the water from heavy downpours evaporates fast rather than staying stored in the ground for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛyaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ mulch material organic compost loo tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ bɛ Nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛto shikpɔŋ koni okɛdu onibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if there is still enough hidden moisture in my soil for my crops after a short dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be kukuoo ko ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can dig about 10 to 15 centimeters deep into your farm soil and squeeze a handful in your palm. If the soil forms a ball without crumbling immediately, there is still enough moisture left for your crop roots to drink.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15 yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ nine kome awo onine mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ŋmeii ni efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshwɛ lolo ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: Why do my crops still dry up and fail even when there is a small pond or dam nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nubu bibioo ko loo nubu ko bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Having water nearby is only half the work; crops need direct root irrigation and shaded soil to prevent high heat from evaporating the water off the field before the plant roots can actually drink it.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Eji nitsumɔ lɛ fã pɛ. Tsei biɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni hulutsoo ni naa wa akafee nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a self-defense trick to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside itself and survive until the next watering or rainfall.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nu loo nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is scarce, tomato plants experience heat stress. They drop their blossoms to preserve their own energy and survive, rather than spending limited water on developing fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu faaa lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Amɛshiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ nyu tsuɔ ní bɔɔ ko pɛ konɛ a yiblii ɔ nɛ wa.

english: Why does cassava survive the long dry season much better than maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmei loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its upper leaves during severe dry spells to stop water loss and stores its energy deep underground in its roots, going almost dormant until water becomes available again.
ga: Cassava shiɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni ekɛkpa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ebaahi shi aaafee dioo kɛyashi be mli ni nu baaba ekoŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I plant late in the rainy season that will mature quickly before my soil completely dries out?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei abaanyɛ adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee ni baakwɛ̃ oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi kwraa?

english: Fast-maturing vegetable crops like okro, leafy greens, cowpeas, or short-duration peppers reach harvest stage within 60 to 90 days, allowing you to harvest before underground soil water disappears.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai, tsina ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ baashɛ kpamɔ he yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli, ni no baaha okpa kpamɔ dani shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baaje mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help keep moisture in my soil for longer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cowpea spreads wide across the ground like a carpet, forming a living cover that shades the soil from direct sunlight, reduces water evaporation, and keeps soil cool.
ga: Cowpeas gbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti. Efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: How can I keep my small vegetable patch green when my main water source begins to dry up?
ga: Mafee aduawai ŋmɔ bibioo ko. Te minɔ lɛ ji tɛŋŋ? Beni mi nu jɛɛhe titri lɛ mli egbi lɛ

english: Covering the soil around your crops with a thick layer of dry grass or palm leaves (mulching) retains soil moisture, allowing you to use far less water while keeping plants healthy.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai (mulching) ni mli edɔ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ haa okɛ nu fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ohaa otsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when I travel to sell them in distant markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mifã gbɛ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting during the hot midday heat leaves vegetables with high internal heat, causing them to sweat, wilt, and rot fast in bags. Harvesting early in the morning when crops are cool keeps them fresh longer during transport.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa aduawai lɛ náa mli la ni mli edɔ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ ni fiteɔ oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ leebi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field with no plantains or big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains loo tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a living umbrella that shields the cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi. Kakao tso lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kakao baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young plantain suckers dry up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantains have shallow root systems that cannot reach deep soil water during dry spells. Covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or straw helps trap ground moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Plantain bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmei lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots rot in the soil after harvest, they release natural fertilizer that feeds the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops do to help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops, known as mulching, stops water in the dirt from evaporating quickly under the sun, prevents weed growth, and eventually turns into rich soil food as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa oya yɛ hulu la shishi. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebafeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like dust inside the plant tops?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni sũ tamɔ muji bibii yɛ tsei lɛ ayitsei amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day, chewing on leaves and leaving behind powdery droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ baai ni oshi jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward into tight tubes during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl tight during hot afternoons as a natural survival defense to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excess moisture loss.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni abu adebɔɔ mli wala he Koni ajie baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming out of the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Extra ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food and water from the main bearing plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one strong sucker, ensuring the main plant yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food through their leaves. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, allowing maximum light capture which feeds and expands the tuber underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ emɔɔ la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni eboteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I select the best part of a cassava stem to plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best cassava stems for planting come from the middle section of a fully grown, healthy plant. These mid-stem cuttings sprout faster and produce stronger roots than soft green tips or old woody bases.
ga: Cassava tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ jɛɔ tso ko ni wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ashishifãi ni etsɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to place wooden stakes in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight for making energy, which builds large tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tuber agbo ko baa shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu buɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green leaves and strong growth. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decay, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does a plantain trunk produce fruit only once and then stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu ko woɔ yibii shikome pɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit just one time. Once it completes fruiting, that main stem dies so new shoots (suckers) growing at the base can take over.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ agbe naa lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo. No hewɔ lɛ ŋmeii heei (suckers) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell underground cassava tubers are mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛ̃ɔ, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and soft while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center folded leaves of young maize plants and chews through the tender tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ekɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a sudden dry spell. If seeds sprout and then face heat without continuous rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni hulutsoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even if they are not touching them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mitaaa amɛhe po?

english: Weeds have deep and aggressive root systems that steal water and fertilizer nutrients from the soil before your crops can reach them, starving your plants underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I test my soil before I start putting fertilizer on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka shikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii womɔ?

english: Testing your soil tells you exactly what nutrients your land is missing. Applying fertilizer without checking the soil first is like taking medicine without knowing your sickness—it can waste your money or even harm your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dã lɛ, etamɔ tsofa ni oooye ni oleee akɛ hela mɔ bo. Ebaanyɛ efite bo shika loo eye onibii awui.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to make my cocoa trees produce well for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo kookoo tsei kpakpai afii babaoo?

english: Good farm soil feels dark, crumbly, and holds moisture well without staying flooded. An extension officer can test its nutrient levels and acidity to make sure it can support healthy cocoa production long-term.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ baanyɛ aka niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ acidity lɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua kookoo ni afeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer work very well on my neighbor's farm but might not work the same way on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi ekolɛ etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil condition changes from farm to farm, even if they are side by side. Your neighbor's land might have different moisture levels, depth, or existing nutrients than yours, which changes how crops react to fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli. Kɛji amɛyɔɔ amɛhe po Okutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, emlibotemɔ, loo niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔto fe onɔ̃ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Will applying fertilizer once keep my cocoa trees healthy forever, or do I need to keep adding it?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaaha kookoo tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛya naanɔ, aloo ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shikome?

english: Fertilizer gives trees an immediate food boost, but it does not stay in the soil forever. As trees grow and produce cocoa pods, they pull those nutrients out of the earth, so you must manage and feed the soil continuously.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya naanɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni ewo kookoo ŋmeii Ebaajie nakai niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oha lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be.

english: What bad things can happen if I put too much fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Using too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops, turn the leaves brown, and make the soil too acidic, which reduces your crop yield instead of increasing it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ asarasu. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ acid tsɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi moŋ fe ni eeeha eya hiɛ.

english: What is the best time of the year to apply fertilizer to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the rainy season when the ground is moist. Moisture helps the roots absorb the nutrients, but you should avoid applying it during heavy flooding so it doesn't wash away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shi esa akɛ okpa ekɛ nitsumɔ yɛ nu afua ni naa wa be mli koni ekɛkaho.

english: How do I prepare the ground around my cocoa trees before putting fertilizer down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa he ni mi-kookoo tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: You should clear the weeds and heavy bush around the tree's base while leaving the soil moist and loose, allowing the fertilizer to dissolve into the ground where the roots can reach it.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ. Ebɔle tso lɛ shishi, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are hungry for nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-cacao tsei lɛ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: Nutrient-starved cocoa trees often show signs like yellowing leaves, weak branches, slow growth, or dropping young pods before they can mature into full cocoa pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, loo ŋmeii bibii ni fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ kpo.

english: How do cocoa roots actually take in fertilizer from the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees have tiny feeder roots near the surface of the soil that drink up nutrients dissolved in soil water. You must spread fertilizer around the tree's canopy line where these roots feed, rather than against the main trunk.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni abaanyɛ aye yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni ekɛjie niyenii ni mli ewo nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ ehe. Tso lɛ shishifãi nɛɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Is chemical fertilizer better for my farm than natural organic manure?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi fe adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of missing nutrients, while organic manure improves the soil's ability to hold water and nutrients over time. Using both together gives your soil the best long-term health.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: If I give my vegetable crops a lot of water at once, why do their leaves still wilt in the afternoon heat?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu wo aduawai babaoo nɔ shikome lɛ, mɛni hewɔ amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Plants absorb water gradually through their roots over time. Flooding them with too much water at once can suffocate the root system, preventing the roots from taking up moisture effectively when the hot sun evaporates water from the leaves.
ga: Tsei gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ afɔ nu babaoo shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: How does irregular rainfall at the start of the planting season harm my newly sown maize seeds?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ saa ŋmãa dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Seeds require steady, consistent moisture to sprout. A single rainfall triggers the seed to begin germinating, but if rain stops for days afterward, the young sprout dries out and dies underground before reaching the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves turn yellow after several days of continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When soil remains flooded for days, air is forced out, preventing root respiration. Drowned roots lose their ability to absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, anyɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛjeɔ kpo. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akamumɔ Shifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: If I save and plant seeds from my best hybrid maize harvest, why is the next yield so small and uneven?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to ni midu lɛ Mɛni hewɔ nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ lɛ faaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are carefully bred from specific parent plants to produce a high-yielding crop. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those ideal combined traits, producing weak and unpredictable plants in the next generation.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli koni ekɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo aba. Dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai aggregate sui kpakpai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant sweet corn right next to local yellow maize, why do my sweet corn cobs develop hard yellow kernels?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni ji yellow ŋmãa lɛ masɛi Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni mli wa?

english: Wind carries pollen from the local yellow maize to the sweet corn flowers. This cross-pollination mixes the traits of both varieties, directly altering the texture and sweetness of your corn.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa pollen kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli kɛyaa ŋmãa fɔfɔi ni ŋɔɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ cross pollination nɛɛ kɛ sui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome. Etsakeɔ bɔ ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why does a high-yielding cassava variety from another region produce poorly when I plant it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni jɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop varieties react specifically to local soil conditions, rainfall patterns, and pests. A variety bred for one environment may struggle to adapt to different soil nutrients or moisture levels on your land.
ga: Tsei henɔi feɔ amɛnii yɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Ekolɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni afee aha shihilɛ kome lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii srɔtoi loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he tsakemɔ mli.

english: Is it better for me to apply all my fertilizer at planting time or spread it out in small doses as the crop grows?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fɛɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli loo magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko ashwã be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Spreading fertilizer in small doses throughout the season is far better because young roots cannot absorb large amounts at once, and heavy rains will wash away unabsorbed fertilizer before the plant can consume it.
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baafata he Be muu lɛ fɛɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɛɛ aŋɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa dani tsei baanyɛ aye.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying after I cleared all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas that shield young leaves from heat damage and maintain soil moisture around the roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni bɔleɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing very thick green leaves but failing to produce many flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into leafy growth. Tomatoes need balanced nutrients, particularly phosphorus and potassium, to produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia tomato. titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and bitter if I leave them in the ground past the main harvest period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: As cassava plants age beyond maturity, they convert stored starch into tough woody fibers and natural protective chemicals to survive dry conditions, making the tubers hard and bitter.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ eye fe afii pɔtɛɛ ko. Amɛtsakeɔ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amɛfeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Ha oyitso afee nɔ ni wa ni edɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, an important nutrient plants need to grow leaves and stay healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer can restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi amli ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting crops like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize helps your field because these legumes pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, which feeds the maize naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua oŋmɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and thin leaves that lose water rapidly under direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using plantain plants protects them from heat until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ plantains tsu nii ni okɛha amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he kɛyashi plantains lɛ baadara waa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the bare soil with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly during sunny days and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Tomato flowers usually drop when the plant feels stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa.

english: What is causing my cassava tubers to rot underground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani atsaa amɛ?

english: Underground root rot usually happens when water sits around the roots for too long in heavy, poorly drained soils during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Small holes and chewed edges on young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant leaves and eat the tender tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually harm their growth?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifite edalɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and fertilizer in the soil, while also providing a hiding place for insects and plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ tsei ahe helai hu baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main tree. Removing most of them leaves only the strongest shoots, allowing the plant to produce a much larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ajie babaoo lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and lifts them high into the sunlight so the plant can make enough energy to grow big tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli. ni owo sweet potato lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha bulbs agboi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if planting materials I get from another farmer's harvest are healthy enough to grow on my own land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔ nii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaafonyo kroko ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ nɔ?

english: Healthy planting materials or seeds should be free from visible dark spots, holes, or mold, and come from strong, high-yielding parent plants. Using weak or infected stems and seeds will pass diseases directly to your new field and reduce your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔ nibii loo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ duŋ. bu ni anaa loo ŋmɔtɔ Ni ejɛɔ nyɛ tso ko ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe tsei kɛ dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã he hee ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni okɛ nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it good practice to plant my crops in batches at different times instead of planting everything on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ

english: Staggering your planting dates ensures your crops mature at different times rather than all at once. This spreads out your workload during harvest, protects you if weather conditions suddenly change, and allows you to sell produce continuously over a longer period.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ be ni okɛbaadu nii lɛ to sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni oookwɛ fɛɛ shikome. Enɛ baajara onitsumɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ebuɔ ohe kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake trukaa. ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ be fɛɛ be be kakadaŋŋ

english: How can I safely save and store part of my current crop harvest to use as seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ fã ko ato ni mikɛto shweshweeshwe koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Seeds meant for future planting should be collected from the healthiest, fully mature plants, thoroughly dried in a shaded area, and stored in clean, airtight containers in a cool place. Keeping moisture and pests away prevents seeds from rotting or losing their power to germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ abua dumɔwui ni akɛbaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ anaa kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ amli. Gbimɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii bɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite loo amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my plants sometimes drop their flowers and tiny young fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mitso lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers or young fruits when they are stressed by irregular watering, extreme heat, or lack of nutrients in the soil. The plant sheds extra weight it cannot support so that it can save its energy to keep the main root and leaves alive.
ga: Tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi loo amɛbaafite aduawai kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Tso lɛ baaje muji ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ hewalɛ ato koni akɛkwɛ shishifãi kɛ baai titrii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the crops growing under big trees get very tall but give me very little yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward to reach sunlight when shaded by large trees, spending all their energy growing tall stems instead of developing flowers and fruits. Sunlight is the plant's main food source needed to produce heavy yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛná hulu la kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ tsei wuji ashishi. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Hulu la ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why did my farm give a huge harvest this season, but the same crop grows weak if I plant it on the same land next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ? Shi tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ baagbɔjɔ kɛji midu yɛ nakai he lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: A heavy harvest pulls a large amount of specific nutrients out of the soil. Planting the same crop repeatedly drains those exact nutrients completely, causing soil fatigue unless you rotate crops or add compost and fertilizer to replenish the land.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni tsii jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔlɛ No ji ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops of essential food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa onibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell the right time to harvest my crops so they don't spoil while still on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ akafite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ.

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as leaves turning yellow, fruits changing color, or stems drying out. Harvesting too early leaves fruits undersized, while waiting too long attracts pests and causes produce to rot on the plant.
ga: Tsei baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Yibii ni tsakeɔ su loo tso ni egbi Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, yibii lɛ feɔ bibii tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil and lose freshness so quickly when I transport them long distances to major markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ehee oya kɛji mikɛ amɛ tee jarayeli hei wuji lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe and release heat and moisture. When packed tightly in hot bags or exposed to direct sun during transport, heat builds up rapidly, causing vegetables and fruits to soften, bruise, and rot.
ga: Tsei ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛjieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛji akɛ awo kotokui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ loo akɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbɛfaa mli. Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai feɔ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe shwieɔ shi, ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: What causes my fruits to soften and rot on the farm even before I pick them for market?
ga: Mɛni haa mi yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ?

english: Pre-harvest rot is usually caused by excessive moisture remaining on the fruits or small insect punctures that allow fungal spores to enter. Keeping the area around crops clear of dense weeds improves airflow and reduces humidity around the fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa dani akpaa lɛ baa. aloo kooloi bibii yɛ Drill kɛyashi fungal spores baanyɛ abote mli.
