He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ jwɛi babaoo bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. The nearby maize uses this natural fertilizer to grow stronger and produce larger yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or heavy rains have washed the nitrogen deeper into the ground where small roots cannot reach it. Nitrogen is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch more sunlight, which the plant uses to make food for growing big tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off wet soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ oowo staking lɛ, wó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la babaoo aba onine ashɛ nɔ. Akɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehaa baai hu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top of the soil. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, wet soil and strong winds can easily pull the roots up unless the stem is supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. ja akɛ tso ni fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Seeds carry a limited amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts its energy trying to push through the heavy layer of dirt before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaho ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support. If the tree experiences stress from dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or insect attacks, it sheds extra flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ hu baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers during very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside pepper flowers, preventing fertilization. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant naturally drops them to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination Tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them harvested too late into the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Mature cassava tubers stop growing and begin to absorb excess water from waterlogged soil. This extra moisture breaks down the starch inside the root and attracts soil fungi that cause soft rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ nɛɛ gbálaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amli ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses, or by severe water stress when the days are too dry and hot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the dirt and are adapted to germinate instantly with very little water. They quickly absorb available surface nutrients before cultivated crops can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya dani tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the crop is knee-high will help restore its green color and fuel healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni afee baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛfataa he beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ baaye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli ni ewo amɛdalɛ kpakpa he hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and moisture for cocoa seedlings to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is ready to be harvested from under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. A good signal is when the lower leaves naturally dry up and fall off, or you can gently dig around one plant to check if the root tubers have reached a thick, usable size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Okadi kpakpa ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Tso ni mli tse Koni akɛkwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli tse ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii loo ehiii.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil with compost helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can develop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to light and off the damp ground, preventing diseases and helping the tubers grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is commonly caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Checking your field early in the morning and applying recommended treatments into the funnel can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye amɛnɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark black and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, wet weather. Trimming heavy tree branches to let in light and air, along with harvesting ripe pods promptly, stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Kɛfata he lɛ, obaakpa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop field.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially created to produce a very high yield only in their first planting. If you save and replant those harvested seeds, the second generation will yield far less corn and grow unevenly. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong yields.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baawo ŋmãa fioo kwraa ni ebaakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni mli wa baa.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant groundnuts on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, abuɔ lɛ akɛ nifeemɔ gbonyo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating groundnuts with maize or cassava breaks disease cycles and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, efoɔ hela lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some of my garden egg plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just fall off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers need pollen from the male parts to reach the female parts at the exact right time. If it rains heavily, or if there are no bees around to move the pollen, fertilization fails and the plant sheds the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia pollen ni jɛɔ hii lɛ ahe nibii amli koni amɛyashɛ yei lɛ ahe yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo ŋmeii ni baajie pollen lɛ bɛ lɛ Fɔmɔmɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ ni tso lɛ baafite fɔfɔi ni awoko lɛ.

english: Why do some small watermelons on my farm dry up and drop off when they are only the size of an egg?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ watermelon lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ ni egbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ Edalɛ tamɔ ŋmei pɛ moŋ.

english: Those tiny fruits are female flowers that were never fertilized. If bees do not transfer pollen from a male flower to that female flower on the day it opens, the plant gives up on it and lets it drop.
ga: Nakai aduawai bibii lɛ ji fɔfɔi yei ni awoko amɛ fɔmɔ kotoku pɛŋ. Kɛji ŋmeii ejieee pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛtee fɔfɔi yei anɔ yɛ gbi ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ baaha ehe ni eha egbee shi.

english: I heard that oil palm trees have male and female flowers—how does that affect my fruit harvest?
ga: Minu akɛ mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ enáa aduawai akpamɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: For an oil palm tree to produce fruit bunches, pollen from a male flower must reach a female flower while she is ready. If a tree produces only male flowers during a season, or if insects do not carry the pollen over, no fruit bunches will form.
ga: koni mu tsei lɛ awo aduawai akui Esa akɛ Pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli lɛ ayashɛ fɔfɔi yoo lɛ he be mli ni efee klalo lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ fɔfɔi amli pollen eyaaa Yibii akuu ko bɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged, which prevents roots from breathing. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or timber trees to act as natural sunshades while their roots grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei bibii koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why are my cassava stems growing very tall with bushy leaves, but when I dig them up, the cassava tubers are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi kɛ́ atsa lɛ Ani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the plant spends all its food energy growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei kɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ ngmlɛfia ɔ kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisi fã ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the middle of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt disease in the soil, which blocks the water tubes inside the stem. The plant cannot transport water up to its leaves, causing it to collapse quickly in hot weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya baai lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ gbee shi oya baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, providing natural food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto tall bamboo sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines raises the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch more sunlight and stay safe from soil fungal diseases, giving the plant more energy to build large tubers.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds before the bunch is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa nii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be weakened by tiny worms called root nematodes. Supporting the main stem with a wooden fork prop and piling rich soil around the base keeps the tree upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ shishifãi ni ji nematodes. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋtayaa kɛ sũ ni jara wa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛfi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly if I store them inside my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need proper air circulation and cool conditions after harvest. Keeping them inside a warm, closed room traps heat and moisture, which causes them to rot and soften rapidly before you can sell them.
ga: Tomato he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ahi mli. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo dani obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ.

english: How can I keep my tomatoes fresh for longer while waiting for market buyers to arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-tomato lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aba?

english: To extend their shelf life, store tomatoes in well-ventilated, shaded areas using open crates rather than closed rooms, and keep them cool to slow down natural decay.
ga: Bɔni afee ni okɛ be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ To tomatoi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli kɛtsɔ adeka ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ moŋ fe nɔ ni agbele mli. Ni okɛ tomato awo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ koni ekɛha adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ akafee mlɛo.

english: Can fresh tomatoes really stay good for up to a month after harvesting?
ga: Ani tomato hee baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome yɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fresh tomatoes usually only last one to two weeks under normal conditions. They can only last up to a month if kept under consistent cold storage or processed through drying or canning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato hee hiɔ shi otsii 1-2 pɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni sa mli. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli ejɔ mli daa loo atsu he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsinsii mii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I stack my harvested produce tightly in a closed room before taking them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ toɔ tsu ko ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tight stacking in a closed room traps the natural heat released by vegetables. This heat buildup creates moisture that spreads mold and speeds up rotting throughout the entire batch.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ to tsu ko ni aŋã mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni aduawai lɛ jieɔ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ eshwaa lɛ baa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ yaa oya yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What happens to fresh vegetables when the power goes off in a cold storage room?
ga: Mɛni baa aduawai heei anɔ kɛ́ tsɔne ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni akɛ la toɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite?

english: When electricity cuts off, temperature and humidity quickly rise inside the storage room. This causes vegetables like tomatoes to sweat and spoil rapidly due to heat trapped inside.
ga: Kɛji srawa hewalɛ gbo lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ baaya hiɛ oya. Enɛ haa aduawai, tamɔ tomato, shwieɔ latsaa ni efiteɔ oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does heat inside a house affect vegetables after they are picked?
ga: Te dɔlɛ ni yɔɔ shia lɛ mli lɛ saa aduawai ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛto he lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heat speeds up the natural breakdown of picked crops. Higher room temperatures make vegetables lose water faster, leading to shrinkage, softness, and decay.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya. Tsu mli latsaa ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa aduawai amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ, efeɔ blɛoo, ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do some crops last longer after harvest than soft fruits like tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ fe aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo tamɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Crops with thick skins or low water content lose moisture slowly, while soft-skinned crops like tomatoes breathe heavily and release moisture fast, making them spoil quickly without cooling.
ga: Tsei ni amɛhewolo lɛ mli edɔ loo nu faaa lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ fiofio. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni hewolo lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, tamɔ tomato lɛ, ewaa amɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya ni amɛhaaa amɛhe ajɔɔ.

english: What is the best place to keep my vegetables if transport to the market is delayed?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mikɛ mi-vegetables lɛ ato kɛji akɛ tsɔne ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: If transport is delayed, keep your crops in a cool, well-shaded, and elevated shelter with continuous breeze to slow down spoilage until transport arrives.
ga: Kɛji akɛ gbɛfaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ Ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ be fɛɛ be koni efite kɛyashi be mli ni nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn soft and start leaking liquid after sitting for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli efee blɛoo ni ebɔi nu shwiemɔ beni mita shi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: As tomatoes sit in warm places, their outer cells break down and lose internal water. This cell breakdown causes them to lose firmness and leak fluid as rot sets in.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tomatoi lɛ ta he ko ni mli edɔ. Amɛ kponɔgbɛ wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ ni nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɛkɛ wala yibii lɛ amligbalamɔ nɛɛ haa amɛhe waaa ni nu hoɔ yɛ be mli ni fitemɔ baa lɛ.

english: Is it safe to store harvested crops in the same room where my family sleeps?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmaa lɛ baato tsu ni miweku lɛ wɔɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Storing crops in living rooms is not ideal because body heat and warm room air accelerate rotting, and decaying produce can attract insects and create unhealthy odors.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ asa mli lɛ esaaa ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya. Ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi kɛba ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni esaaa aba.

english: What makes virgin land or fresh soil better for growing crops than land I have farmed for years?
ga: Mɛni haa shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ hee ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ hi fe shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Virgin land has not been cultivated before, meaning it still contains all its natural organic matter and plant nutrients. This makes the soil naturally fertile and capable of supporting strong crop growth without heavy reliance on added fertilizers initially.
ga: Atsuko shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ he nii dã. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ lolo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni enyɛɔ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ehe afɔ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ nɔ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is rich and good for growing crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse ni ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Rich soil typically has a dark brown or black color, feels soft and crumbly when you squeeze it, holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, and naturally supports thick, healthy wild plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ke a ngɔ lɛ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: What special care should I take when clearing a piece of land that has never been farmed before?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ mikwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miitsu shikpɔŋ ni atsuko nii yɛ nɔ dã lɛ he nii?

english: When clearing virgin land, remove large stumps and weeds that block sunlight, but try to avoid burning all the cleared plant material so you can leave organic matter in the soil to preserve its richness.
ga: Kɛji ootsu nii yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Jiemɔ tsei wuji kɛ jwɛi ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa lɛ. Shi bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ahe nibii fɛɛ ni ajie lɛ he lɛ ni oshãa lɛ he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni oshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Do I still need to apply chemical fertilizer if my farmland is already very fertile?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli lolo kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo momo?

english: Very rich soil may not need much fertilizer for the first planting season, but adding a small amount at key growth stages can support high crop yields and prevent the soil from losing its nutrients too quickly.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ waa lɛ he ehiaaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa oya tsɔ.

english: What is the main difference between planting local maize seeds and foreign hybrid maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛ maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ teŋ?

english: Local maize seeds are easily available and adapted to local conditions, allowing you to save seeds for the next season. Foreign or hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce higher yields and resist diseases, but you must purchase new seeds for every planting season.
ga: Anaa maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa dumɔwui oya ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ maŋ lɛ mli shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ dumɔwui toɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Akwɛɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. Shi esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Is it better for me to plant local maize or foreign maize on a brand-new farm field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa loo maŋsɛɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ hee ko nɔ?

english: Both local and foreign maize varieties will grow well on fresh, rich soil. However, foreign or hybrid maize varieties are designed to take full advantage of high soil fertility to produce a much larger harvest if you can afford the seed cost.
ga: Shia kɛ maŋsɛɛ abele henɔi lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa nii anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, afee ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ srɔtoi loo ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni baa lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni fa nɔ kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ awo mli.

english: Will my local maize seeds give me a good harvest if I plant them in very rich soil?
ga: Ani mimaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa nɔ?

english: Yes, local maize will produce a much healthier crop and better yield in rich soil compared to poor soil, though it may not yield as heavily as an improved hybrid variety.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa baawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii babaoo nɔ. kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ he Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ebaawo yibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ moŋ.

english: How do I know if my piece of land is suitable for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize thrives in well-drained, deep, and fertile soil that retains good moisture after rain without collecting standing water for long periods.
ga: Abele shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa hulutsoo be kpakpa hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni ehaaa nu ni ekã shi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: If I clear a bush to start a new farm, will the soil stay rich forever?
ga: Kɛji mijie jwɛi lɛ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa nii kɛya naanɔ?

english: No, every crop harvest takes nutrients out of the earth. Over time, even virgin land loses its richness unless you practice crop rotation, leave the land to rest, or add compost and fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ, no mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni He Tse lɛ Po ehiɛɛɛ emuuyeli mli. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Aloo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: How can I protect the rich topsoil on my new farm from washing away during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ hee lɛ nɔ lɛ he koni ekaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your topsoil by planting along the natural contour lines of the slope, leaving plant residues on the surface as mulch, and growing cover crops to hold the soil in place.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishigbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ. Shi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ nɔ akɛ mulch. ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested corn kernels spoil quickly if I store them right after picking without drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mifolɔ mli ni migbiko lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifolɔ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly picked corn contains a lot of natural moisture. Storing wet grains creates a dark, moist environment where mold, fungi, and insects thrive, causing the entire batch to rot within a short time.
ga: Abɛi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli efɔ ni ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ kooloi shwereɔ yɛ mli baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Is it better to dry groundnuts in their shells or peel them before leaving them in the sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooogbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo oootsi amɛhe dani ogbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: It is best to dry groundnuts inside their shells. The outer pod protects the delicate seeds from pest damage, dirt, and scorching heat while allowing moisture to escape gradually.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai, muji, kɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ajɛ mli fiofio.

english: Can I store fresh green maize for a long time in my barn like I do with dry corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni afee ehee lɛ ato ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa ni egbi?

english: No, fresh green maize has a high water content and will rot within a few days. Only fully matured corn that has been sun-dried until hard can be stored safely for long periods.
ga: Dabi, nu babaoo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ ni afee ehee lɛ mli, ni ebaagbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Abɛi ni ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni eha ewa yɛ hulutsoo be mli pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to grind dry corn into powder instead of feeding whole dried grains to my farm animals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafolɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli powda moŋ fe ni mahã miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ŋmãa ni egbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Whole dried corn kernels are extremely hard and difficult for animals to chew and digest fully. Grinding the corn into a powder breaks down the tough outer skin, making it easier for the animals to absorb all the nutrients.
ga: Abɛi muu ni egbi lɛ mli wa waa ni ewa kɛha kooloi akɛ amɛaaye ni amɛye mli jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ powda lɛ gbáa abele lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloo lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do people recommend mixing groundnut powder with crushed corn when preparing farm food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ kɛ́ oohoo ŋmɔ mli niyenii lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ afutu ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Corn mainly provides starch for quick energy, while groundnuts contain rich oils and proteins for body building. Combining them creates a rich, balanced diet that provides complete nutrition.
ga: Abɛi babaoo haa starch koni ekɛ hewalɛ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii amli fɔ kɛ protein babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ. Kɛ akɛ amɛ fɛɛ to he lɛ, amɛfeɔ niyenii ni jara wa ni ja ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stalks down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants flower above ground, but after pollination, the stalks naturally bend downwards and peg into the soil because the actual groundnut pods need darkness and dirt to grow and mature underground.
ga: Peanut tsei fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ baakoto shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ ehe baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ he miihia duŋ kɛ muji koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Curling leaves is a self-defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves tightly, the corn plant reduces the amount of surface area exposed to the harsh sun, helping it conserve water during hot periods.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni ŋmã tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ

english: What happens to my harvested groundnuts if I leave them lying on wet ground after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ beni mifo amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving harvested groundnuts on damp soil promotes the growth of dangerous molds that produce hidden poisons called aflatoxins, making the nuts unsafe for humans and animals to eat.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni feɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai kɛ kooloi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant is ready for fresh green harvest versus harvesting for dry storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-abele tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmaa hee ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtoɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: For fresh eating, harvest when the silk turns dark brown and squeezing a grain releases a milky juice. For dry storage, leave the crop in the field until the leaves turn brown and the kernels are hard.
ga: Kɛha Nikpamɔ hee ni ayeɔ beni siliki lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni kɛ́ amɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ, mliki baajɛ mli aba. Kɛha nibii ni akɛtoɔ he ni egbi lɛ Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it good for my soil if I plant groundnuts and corn together in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and adds it to the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps the heavy-feeding corn grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa sũ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni ayeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight and hot, dry winds. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted alongside them to block the intense sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce the energy required to grow large underground tubers. If vines are left crawling on the ground, they are more likely to get diseases and produce very small yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji oha wain tsei shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ Helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: How do I choose the best part of a cassava stem to cut and plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei fãi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should select the middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem that is about as thick as a thumb. Avoid the soft green tips at the top and the overly hard base at the bottom, as the middle section sprouts the fastest and produces the strongest roots.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei tso ni mli wa ni eda ni tamɔ otsitsi wulu lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni wa tsɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ, ni ewoɔ shishifãi ni wa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the middle tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and build big cobs. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base of the plant will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ afata tso lɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize while also providing an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi hu haa koni akpa.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds to decompose on my farm instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ koni amɛgbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural nutrients and leaves the soil dry and exposed to heat. Leaving cut weeds on top of the soil forms a natural blanket that holds in moisture, keeps the soil cool, and slowly breaks down into free organic manure.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa Jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and a powdery powder inside the leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ni powda yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the leaf funnel of young maize plants and eats the tender leaves. Spotting them early and using recommended botanical or mild chemical sprays protects the crop from major damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni waaa lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the juices from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these tiny pests early using neem oil or insect spray keeps the leaves broad and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Neem fɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔɔ tomato.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rainwater sits in the soil without draining, the roots drown and begin to rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the bottom of maize plants usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build strong, green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli, ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do people advise me not to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, causing lower yields over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from intense heat and harsh winds. Without large shade trees or food crops like plantain above them, the sun dries out the young seedlings faster than their roots can take up water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ bɛ. Hulu lɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why is it important for me to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight and keeps them off hot, moist soil. This helps the leaves make more food for bigger tubers and protects the plant from soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akashɛ hulu lɛ nɔ, ni ebaaha amɛkafee hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii wuji lɛ, ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ baai helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread so much faster than my planted crops after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local conditions, so their roots absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off because of extreme heat, lack of water during the flowering stage, or tiny pests like thrips feeding on the delicate blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is most commonly caused by a virus transmitted by tiny sucking insects called whiteflies, or by severe water stress during long dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant my seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the plants end up fighting each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them weak and less productive.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but avoid applying right before heavy downpours so the rain doesn't wash the nutrients away before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nugbɔ akajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the entire plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with fewer leaves at the top, and cracks appear in the soil near the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ. kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides essential shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking exposes yam leaves to maximum sunlight, which helps the plant make food and grow larger tubers. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ niyenii ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aba shi

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and turn hard?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Applying neem oil spray or an appropriate insecticide helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ ni sa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off due to stress from high temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollination. Keeping soil moisture steady and encouraging pollinators can fix this issue.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni aaatsirɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers so only two or three remain allows the main tree to produce larger bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi (shishifãi) ​​babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eshwɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 9 to 12 months, lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni tso lɛ eye nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 lɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in a plot where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil. Rotating them with maize restores soil fertility naturally and improves the next crop's yield.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Is it better for my vegetable crops if I water them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb water before the sun warms up, and excess water on leaves dries quickly, preventing fungal diseases that thrive in damp afternoon conditions.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ dɔɔ lɛ. Ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baagbi oya. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa yɛ shwane kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do the seeds saved from my harvested maize yield far less crop when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa kɛ́ midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize varieties lose their vigor and trait uniformity in the second generation. Buying fresh, certified seeds each season guarantees strong plants and maximum yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ kɛ sui ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why must I ferment and dry my cocoa beans properly before selling them to buyers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni migbiɔ dani mikɛhɔ̃ɔ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation and thorough drying develop the rich chocolate flavor and brown color that international chocolate makers require. Unfermented beans stay bitter, purple, and tend to mold quickly during shipping, causing buyers to reject them.
ga: Kɛ́ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ, ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni majimaji ateŋ tsokolatefeelɔi sumɔɔ lɛ. Beans ni awoko mli lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ purple, ni efɔɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛmaje. ni haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a soil fungus that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes like cowpeas in rotation restores food back to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ baaha niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with huge leaves but give me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or are planted too close together, they waste energy growing tall leaves to reach sunlight instead of storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa kakadaŋŋ lɛ kwɛɔ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young crops with dry straw or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that keeps sunlight from drying out the soil. It saves water, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni haaa egbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu baa shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. When the soil is too dry, the plant drops flowers to save water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛshihilɛ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my pepper farm more during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In dry weather, insects look for sap inside juicy crop leaves as their main source of water. The warm heat also causes insect eggs to hatch faster, leading to bigger swarms.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ Kplukai taoɔ nu yɛ tsei ahe baai ni mli edɔ mli akɛ amɛ nu jɛɛhe titri. Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ hu haa kooloi awɔlɔi fɔɔ oya. ni kɛ tooi akuu ni da fe tsutsu lɛ baa

english: Why do my yam seed tubers rot underground before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil that traps dampness around the seed. Planting on raised earthen mounds allows water to drain freely so the seed stays healthy while sprouting.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ waa ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when carrying large fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ mihiɛ aduawai wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are made of soft, water-filled leaves rather than solid wood, making them heavy at the top. Supporting the stem with strong wooden prop poles prevents high winds from snapping the trunk.
ga: Akɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ. Yɛ tso ni wa najiaŋ Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Tso ni mli wa ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baa koni ekakumɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why is it best for me to plant my crops immediately after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: The season's first rains release a natural surge of stored nutrients from the warm soil. Early planting ensures your young crop roots capture this rich nutrient flush to grow strong before dry spells return.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná niyenii babaoo koni amɛdara waa dani hulutsoo be lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans together with maize in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛfataa ŋmei he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize next to it, saving you money on artificial fertilizers and keeping the soil healthy.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant seeds saved from my previous harvest instead of buying new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, heɔ dumɔwui ehei ni awo he odase.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and are more prone to diseases. Certified seeds are specially bred to produce strong plants, resist local pests, and give higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ oya. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade like umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden poles next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko ma sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in the sunlight to make food for big tubers to grow underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing rot and getting maximum sunlight.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. This results in weak, thin plants that produce very small fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ baa.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Spraying the leaves with neem oil mixture helps drive these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: What is causing holes in my young maize leaves with dirt that looks like sawdust inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai ni yɔɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing plant stem and eats the leaves, which can ruin the crop if not treated early with proper sprays.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni eyeɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii mra.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if small insects attack the flowers. Regular watering and shielding crops from extreme heat help fruit form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo, kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in soggy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Sir, why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the cobs are ripe?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow starting from the tip in a V-shape, it means the crop is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is the plant food responsible for green leafy growth, so adding NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant stay green and fill out heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ V su ni yɔɔ naagbee lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tsei. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any tall trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that keep the young cocoa cool and humid during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ Kɛfataa kookoo he Enɛ baaye abua ni kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: What makes my cassava leaves curl up with yellow patches and produce very small stems underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies and spread when you plant cuttings from infected plants. Using disease-resistant cassava stem varieties recommended by agricultural extension officers stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji ofo tso ko ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Sir, why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when soil temperatures get too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks sufficient plant food. Covering the ground around the stems with dry grass mulch keeps the roots cool and moist so the flowers can set into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa tsɔ. Kɛ nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo kɛji tso lɛ bɛ tso niyenii ni fa lɛ, okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni anyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni afee lɛ tomato.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wooden stakes and train my yam vines to climb them instead of letting them spread across the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni majie tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tso ko koni ekwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp soil into the air and sunlight, which protects the leaves from ground fungi and helps the roots grow large.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn dry and drop so quickly during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ harmattan gbɛ́mɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants use a lot of water through their broad leaves to stay green and produce fruit bunches. During the dry Harmattan season, the plant drops older leaves to save moisture and stay alive unless watered and heavily mulched around the base.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ nu babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo aduawai akui. Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, tsei shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he. Ja nu ni mli wa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Sir, why do the bottoms of my sweet pepper fruits turn soft, dark, and rotten before they are ready to pick?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This dark rot at the bottom of peppers is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the growing fruit, often due to dry periods between waterings. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps pepper roots absorb calcium from the soil consistently.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni afɔɔ nu lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pepper shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of tall green leaves but failing to bring out any flowers or pod pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Giving cowpeas too much high-nitrogen fertilizer encourages the plant to grow leaves instead of flowers. It can also happen when tiny insects like thrips eat flower buds before they open, requiring early scouting and control.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ha tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ye fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ biɔ ni akwɛ mli mra ni akudɔ.

english: Sir, what causes my cabbage leaves to spread out wide and stay open instead of folding tight into a hard head?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni haa mi-cabbage baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfee yitso ni wa?

english: Cabbage heads require steady moisture, cool soil conditions, and sufficient spacing to fold into a tight ball. Planting them too close together or exposing them to high heat without mulching prevents the center leaves from wrapping tightly.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni eyɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaabɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ashi amɛ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli ni akɛ muji wooo mli lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop seedlings grow thin and pale even when the rain is falling well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crop's tender roots. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting ensures your crop gets all the nutrients it needs to build a strong foundation.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishitoo ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves have a white powder on them, and is it caused by bad spirits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani mumɔ fɔŋ ko ji mɔ ni kɛba?

english: The white powder is not caused by spirits; it is usually brought by tiny pests like mealybugs or a fungal disease called powdery mildew. These pests suck nutrients from the leaves, but you can manage them by spraying soapy water or using safe, recommended pesticides.
ga: Jeee mumɔi ji mɛi ni bɔ powda yɛŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Shi obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛ samla baashwie nɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn completely black and shrivel up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black because of a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight in and clearing weeds around the trees helps stop the fungus.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods lɛ hewɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tsei baaye abua ni akpa ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my citrus trees covered in a thick black, soot-like layer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ehà mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The black coating is a fungus called sooty mold that grows on the sweet liquid left behind by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids. Controlling the insects with proper sprays will clear up the black mold on your leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji ŋmei ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ sooty mold ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids lɛ shĩɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ obaai lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves have thin white webs and yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ yɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Thin white webs and yellow spots are signs of spider mites, which are very small pests that feed on leaves during dry weather. Keeping the soil moist and spraying the underside of leaves with water or insecticidal soap helps remove them.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ji ŋmeii ahe okadii. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii waa ni yeɔ baai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very thin and yellow instead of dark green and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Thin, yellow maize stalks usually mean the soil is low in nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding well-composted manure or the right fertilizer early in the planting season will help the stalks grow thick and healthy.
ga: ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What causes my crop stems to look weak and thin with tiny holes bored into them?
ga: Mɛni haa mitsɔne lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni afo bu bibii awo mli?

english: Tiny holes and weak stems are caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from moth eggs and eat the plant from the inside. Planting early in the season and clearing field debris helps keep stem borers away.
ga: Buji bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ jɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ amli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ stem borers naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look healthy in the morning but wilt and look thin by the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ leebi lɛ? Shi egbo ni etamɔ mɔ ko ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Wilting in the afternoon heat often happens when soil fungi attack the roots, preventing water from moving up the plant. Improving soil drainage so water does not sit around the roots will prevent root rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shwane mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu aya tso lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni abaafee jogbaŋŋ koni nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Can someone's bad spirit or evil eye cause my crops to dry up and die suddenly?
ga: Ani mɔ ko mumɔ fɔŋ loo hiŋmɛi fɔŋ baanyɛ aha midumɔ nii lɛ agbi trukaa ni amɛgboi?

english: Crops do not die from bad spirits or evil eyes; sudden drying is caused by physical issues like root damage, underground pests, or fungal diseases. Extension officers can inspect the roots and soil to find the exact biological cause and cure.
ga: Mumɔi fɔji loo hiŋmɛi fɔŋ lɛ gbooo ŋmɔshi nibii. Gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagba ko, tamɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa trukaa. shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛna nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa kɛ tsamɔi pɔtɛɛ.

english: I noticed a sticky white substance on my crop stems; what kind of creature is living in there?
ga: Miyɔse nɔ ko yɛŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he. yɛ mi tso lɛ shishi Mɛɛ kooloi hiɔ jɛmɛ?

english: That white substance is produced by small insects called mealybugs or scale insects that group together for protection while sucking plant sap. You can scrape them off or spray them with a mixture of mild soap and water to destroy their hiding place.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs loo scale insects ni buaa amɛhe naa koni amɛbu amɛhe beni amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛkpa nɔ loo okɛ samla ni mli ejɔ afɔ nɔ. kɛ nu koni ekɛfite he ni ekɛ ehe tee lɛ.

english: What is the white mold growing inside my maize ears before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmei yɛŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ anɔ dani kpamɔ?

english: White growth on maize ears is ear rot, a disease caused by fungi entering through rain or insect damage. Harvesting your maize as soon as it matures and choosing disease-resistant seeds prevents this mold from ruining your grain.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa toi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa ni nugbɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛbaa lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa be mli ni ekwɛ̃ pɛ ni ohala dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmãa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight and hot winds. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and humid so the young cocoa roots can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow. This happens when soil nutrients are exhausted or washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why does my land produce less food every season if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
