ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ ehiɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo, ni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni nu akabote mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin trees with few pods. It also blocks airflow, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases like black pod spread easily.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ amli tseee, ni amɛmli tsɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa is very good because plantain leaves provide shade for the delicate young trees. However, cassava should be planted a bit further away because its aggressive roots can steal water and nutrients from young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain ni akɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ hi waa. Shi, akɛni plantain baai haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ kookoo bibii amli lɛ.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take about 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, but modern hybrid cocoa varieties can start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years if given proper weed control, shade, and care.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ, aha amɛ hulutsoo kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves dry up and turn yellow when there is heavy sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They naturally require overhead shade from tall trees or temporary shade crops to protect them and keep the soil moist until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbiɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree lacks water or nutrients, or if tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate them. Keeping mulch on the soil creates a damp environment where pollinators thrive and helps flowers develop into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii bɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baa koni ebafee pollinate. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Biɛ ji he ni pollinators lɛ daa yɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Why do some of my very small cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ gboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often a natural behaviour called cherelle wilt, where the tree sheds extra young pods it cannot afford to feed due to a lack of water or soil nutrients, though pests and fungal diseases can also cause it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherelle wilt, he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛbaa moŋ.

english: How do cocoa trees behave during the dry Harmattan season, and how do I help them survive?
ga: Te cacao tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be mli, ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua amɛ ni amɛhi shi?

english: During the Harmattan dry season, cocoa trees drop many leaves to conserve water and stop producing new pods. Leaving a thick layer of dry leaves around the tree base helps retain soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai babaoo koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛkpa ŋmeii heei ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Baai ni mli tse ni egbi ni ajieɔ lɛ ni Akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Is it safe to cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree, or will it harm the crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-cacao tso lɛ he lɛ? Aloo ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaayeee awui?

english: Pruning unnecessary branches actually helps the cocoa tree yield more fruit. It redirects the tree's energy into pod production and allows light and air into the canopy, reducing disease outbreaks.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa pod feemɔ mli. ni eha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai ni baa lɛ baa shi

english: How do I know when cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when fully ripe, usually shifting from green to a bright golden yellow, or from deep red to orange-yellow. A ripe pod will also make a hollow sound when you tap it gently.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ otswa amɛ fioo.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before putting them out to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the cocoa beans starts the fermentation process, which naturally heats the beans up and breaks down the bitter pulp. This step is essential because it develops the chocolate flavor and brown color inside the bean before sun-drying.
ga: Kookoo yibii lɛ ahe ni akɛhaa lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔlɔ nitsumɔ lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ adɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ he miihia ejaakɛ ejieɔ tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ kpo dani amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very soft, sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving large trees nearby creates a humid canopy that protects the young cocoa until its root system is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tamɔ dumɔwui adumɔ loo tsei wuji ni ashiɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high moisture and cool shade. Pruning excess branches to allow airflow and sunlight into the canopy helps keep the pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left up to its upper growing leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Abele tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni amɛshi lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crop roots turn soft and rot when rainwater stays pooled on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe just like humans need air. When heavy rainwater builds up and cannot drain away, it drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, causing them to rot and kill the crop.
ga: Tsei shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu, taakɛ adesai hu taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa babaoo ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my crops cause my harvest to be much smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi kwraa?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your main crops. When weeds compete for these resources, your crops cannot produce full-sized fruits, tubers, or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe Beni jwɛi kɛ nibii nɛɛ miitswa akaŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmaa ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants so the vines can climb them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce tubers underground based on how much sunlight their leaves capture above ground. Staking lifts the vines into the air so all the leaves get full sunlight, which feeds the growing tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni enɛ damɔ hulu la ni amɛbaai lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any tomatoes during the very hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants and makes their pollen dry out and become sterile. Without successful pollination, the plant automatically sheds the flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni ehaa tomato mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I use the wide-leafed shoot from my plantain tree to start a new plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ plantain tsei amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjeɔ plantain ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Wide-leafed shoots, called water suckers, are weakly attached to the parent plant and produce poor, small bunches. You should use narrow, spear-shaped suckers (sword suckers) because they have strong reserves and yield healthier, larger plantain bunches.
ga: Tso ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ nu mli tsei lɛ, kpɛtɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he fioo ni ewoɔ niji bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ (klante ŋmeii) atsu nii ejaakɛ amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni dara.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the plant's lower leaves turn yellow and naturally drop off. You can also test harvest one side of a single plant to check if the roots have swollen to a good size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome fã kome hu okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ efu kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The strong dry winds and intense heat of the harmattan pull water out of leaves faster than young roots can pull it from the dry ground. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa protects them from direct sun and wind damage.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves with light-colored powdery dirt in the stem center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Mi ŋmãa bibioo ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on your crop. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant where it is soft to eat, which weakens the stalk and stops proper leaf growth.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli, he ni amɛyɔɔ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ayeɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling tightly upward and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of leaves. They inject saliva while feeding, which distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from flowering properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut down the small extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main mother tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large bunch.
ga: Tsoi krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dropping their blossoms without setting any fruit when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and sterile, so flowers cannot fertilize. The plant naturally sheds these unfertilized blossoms to save water and energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into direct sunlight so their leaves can make food. Elevating the vines exposes more leaves to light, which sends nutrients down to make bigger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ naa la babaoo. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii baa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest underground without digging up the whole stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛbaato shikpɔŋ shishi ni akuuu tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: When cassava is mature, the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, the lower stem turns dark and woody, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack upward as tubers expand.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ tso. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underneath are very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and branches instead of storing food in the roots. Proper sunlight and balanced nutrients encourage tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei aniji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, hulu la ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja haa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make my soil richer for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsina ŋmãa mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots have tiny nodules that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil that maize can easily feed on.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmãa baanyɛ aha kooloi lɛ mlɛo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when there is controlled standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ nu ni damɔ shi ni akudɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water suffocates weeds that try to steal light and food from rice plants. It also keeps the soil soft so rice roots can expand easily and absorb dissolved nutrients.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa jwɛi ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ.

english: If I stop using harsh chemical weedicides on my land, how does it help my crops grow better in the long run?
ga: Kɛji mikpa tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Te ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Harsh weedicides can kill the beneficial insects and tiny organisms living in the dirt that break down plant matter into food for your crops. Letting the soil heal allows natural nutrients to build up, helping your crops develop stronger, healthier roots.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. No hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ tsei koni ekɛ niyenii aha onibii. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ ni etsa lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi ni wa ni amɛhe wa.

english: How does using animal manure help my crops differently compared to buying chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahemɔ he?

english: Animal manure improves the soil's structure so it can hold water and nutrients for many seasons, whereas chemical fertilizers only feed the plant for a short time and can harden or ruin the soil if overused.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii amli yɛ be babaoo mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii yɛ be kukuoo mli pɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa loo efite kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii babaoo.

english: Why should I avoid burning the dry bush on my field before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛshãa yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ he dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Burning destroys the rich topsoil, kills friendly soil organisms, and burns away natural organic matter. Clearing the bush without fire preserves the soil's moisture and natural food for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ. ni oshã adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Tsei bibii ni afolɔ ni la bɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nutrients like nitrogen or getting choked by too much standing water around their roots. Proper drainage and organic compost help them regain their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tsei lɛ kɛha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo amɛmiiye nu babaoo ni ekã shi ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli tse ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves drop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the dirt is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. They temporarily wilt to protect themselves from burning, and usually perk back up when the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Amɛbaagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ la he. Ni bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry a limited amount of stored energy to push their shoots up toward the sunlight. If planted too deep, the shoot runs out of food before reaching the surface and suffocates under the heavy dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni amɛkɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Niyenii lɛ hoɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big green leaves but fail to produce many beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni ji eŋɔli shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: If cowpeas get too much nitrogen in the soil, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowers and pods. Giving them less rich fertilizer encourages them to stop growing leaves and start producing food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji fioo ha amɛ lɛ, ebaawo amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛbɔi niyenii feemɔ.

english: Why do my crops stay greener and healthier when I cover the soil around them with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ waa kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dried grass—called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents water from evaporating under the hot sun. As the grass rots, it also turns into natural plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii hu.

english: Why is it bad practice to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ ji nifeemɔ gbonyo lɛ?

english: Planting cassava in the same spot over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows cassava pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans lets the soil recover.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: How can I protect my tomato leaves from insects without using costly chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can make a natural spray using water mixed with a little mild soap or crushed neem leaves. Spraying this on your plants repels harmful pests without damaging the soil or leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛ samla ni mli ejɔ efutu mli lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. neem baai fioo loo ni atswa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ enɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings get burned easily under the full heat of the sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the soil moist and protecting the cocoa plants until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaahiɛ hewalɛ.

english: How do shade trees benefit my farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees reduce soil temperature, prevent water from evaporating too quickly from the ground, and drop leaves that rot and turn into natural organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ. ni ehaa baai ni egboi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps restore the green color and improves plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ ahiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Burning destroys valuable nutrients and beneficial soil organisms, leaves the soil exposed to erosion from heavy rains, and prevents organic matter from decaying into natural fertilizer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsĩɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni amɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it good for me to rotate different crops on the same land each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi yɛ he kome yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rotating crops prevents specific pests and diseases from building up in the soil and helps maintain soil fertility, as different plants take up and add back different nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei srɔtoi ŋmɛɔ niyenii srɔtoi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfataa he ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Removing infected pods regularly and clearing weeds improves airflow and reduces humidity around the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baa shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf curling from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why are my maize stalks falling over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when roots are weak or when stem borers tunnel into the stalk. Ensuring proper plant spacing and applying potassium fertilizer strengthens the stems so they resist wind.
ga: Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bote tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ to amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu nyɛŋ atswa amɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, rotten patches at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark patches at the bottom of tomatoes are known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or inconsistent watering during the fruiting stage.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ aduawai lɛ awomɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the growing stage helps the plants turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ shishijee be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans on the same piece of land where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans have a natural ability to catch nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural food restorer for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa trees burning and drying up in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates canopy shelter to keep the cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ. Amɛ fɛɛ amɛfeɔ hulutsoo koni eha kookoo lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: How do I pick the best part of a cassava stem to plant so I get big tubers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akwɛ koni onine ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji anɔ?

english: The best planting material comes from the middle part of a mature, healthy cassava stem. Avoid the woody base which is too hard and the green top which dries out quickly; the middle section sprouts fast and forms strong roots.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishitoo tsei ni wa tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ he. Teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ehiɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell which plantain shoot is best to dig up and plant in a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are small shoots with narrow, blade-like leaves and a thick base. Avoid 'water suckers' which have broad leaves while still small, because sword suckers produce stronger plants and bigger bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’ ni ji ŋmeii bibii. ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmei kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘nu mli tsei’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ shi amɛji bibii lolo lɛ ahe. Ejaakɛ klante tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaha tso lɛ awa ni eda ni etsɔ kui wuji.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to catch enough sunlight for their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, prevents disease, and helps the plant produce large, heavy tubers below ground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛbaai lɛ. Staking haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ehaa helai baaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the strong sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: What is causing holes in the leaves of my young maize crop that look like sawdust inside the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Early monitoring and spraying with recommended biological or chemical controls can protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akwɛ mli mra ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni naa wa aba.

english: The very first rain after a dry season often warms up the hot soil without soaking it deep enough, causing seeds to bake or rot. It is safer to wait until the rain becomes steady so the soil stays consistently moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa ekwɔ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ aba daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Will planting cassava and maize together on the same plot make them fight each other for food?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ani amɛbaawu yɛ niyenii he?

english: Maize and cassava can grow well together if spaced properly. Maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving the cassava behind to use the field for the rest of the year.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni eshiɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Maize plants need nitrogen to grow strong. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top, causing the lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots underneath are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stem branches instead of storing food energy down in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa kɛ eniji anɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and lose leaves during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted nearby to create shelter and keep the air and soil cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛfee wɔɔhe ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before turning into fruits during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ otsi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is scarce. Extreme heat damages the flower pollen, so the plant drops the flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why are the bunches on my main plantain tree so small when I let many shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ nɔ lɛ ji bibii waa beni mihaa ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Mi plantain titri lɛ

english: Every shoot or sucker growing out of the base shares the same water and soil nutrients with the main tree. Leaving too many shoots starves the main stem, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishi loo tso lɛ shishi fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa tso titri lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ hɔmɔ aye lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantains lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the root underground. Elevating the vines on stakes spreads the leaves out to capture sunlight efficiently and keeps leaves clear of ground rot.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ enɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight shapes and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on leaf juices and spreading plant viruses. This damages the leaf structure and stunts the overall growth of the pepper bush.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baa nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ehaa pepper bush lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits start rotting from the bottom while still hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛkã shi lolo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fruit rot often happens when soil-borne fungus splashes onto lower fruits during heavy rain, or when damp air stays trapped inside a dense crop canopy without proper airflow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli fitemɔ baa kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ shwie aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ hei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ emɔ tso ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested corn cobs have large gaps with missing grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty spaces on a corn cob mean pollination failed. This occurs if dry wind blows the pollen away, or if plants are spaced too far apart for pollen from the top tassels to reach the silks on neighboring ears.
ga: He ni bɛ nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ pollination lɛ eshɛɛɛ he. Enɛ baa mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ tswa pollen lɛ kɛtee. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ akashɛ siliki ŋmeii ni yɔɔ toi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my mature rice stalks bend over and fall flat onto the mud right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over, or lodge, when stems are too thin and weak to carry heavy grain heads. This happens when plants are seeded too close together or when too much nitrogen fertilizer softens the stems.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛjeɔ kpo kɛji tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei du dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ shishi gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting shade crops like plantains next to them shields the young plants from harsh sun and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb upward so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and helping the plant store energy to produce bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ akwɔ koni baai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ koni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base will help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where we harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ wɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔkpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts feed special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores natural fertility, making the land richer for the next crop without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yeɔ helatsɛmɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aba. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the top layer of dirt while the subsoil stays dry and hot. If rain does not fall again immediately, the seeds absorb a little water to start sprouting but quickly die and rot from heat and lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu fioo koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Shi amɛgboiɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ latsaa ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help my crops during hot days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves on top of the soil creates a protective layer called mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the ground so it doesn't evaporate quickly in the sun, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Mulch baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ lɛ, efoŋ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: How do I know which way to insert cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ oodu?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds along the stem. These buds must point upward toward the sky so the fresh shoots can easily grow up into the light while the roots develop downward into the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni ebɔle ehe loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya la lɛ mli mlɛo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra shoots steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from the main stem. Removing all but one or two healthy shoots ensures the main plant has enough energy to grow large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden center of the plant to feed on tender leaves. Spraying an approved treatment or neem extract directly into the central funnel early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ koni amɛye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Black, sunken spots at the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding wood ash to the soil helps prevent this issue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Does using chemical fertilizer spoil the natural taste and quality of my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ŋɔɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ?

english: No, chemical fertilizers simply supply essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that plants need to grow; when applied in the correct amounts, they increase crop yields without reducing food safety or taste.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus pɛ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ loo ŋɔɔmɔ baaa shi.

english: Can I grow healthy crops without spending money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, you can use natural organic matter like chicken manure, compost, and decomposed plant leaves to feed your soil, though it may take more labor and time to get high yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egboi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ebaabi nitsumɔ kɛ be babaoo dani anyɛ aná yibii babaoo moŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean you applied too much fertilizer, applied it during heavy rain which washed it away, or the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ewo mli. Wo lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ lɛ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is it true that planting the same crop on my farm every year makes the soil weak?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ?

english: Yes, planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season; rotating different crops helps the soil recover naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are insects eating my crops even when I bought good quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Good seeds give you strong, fast-growing plants, but pests are naturally attracted to healthy crops for food regardless of seed quality, so pest protection is still necessary.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai haa tsei lɛ waa ni amɛdaraa oya. Shi be fɛɛ be lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akɛ niyenii, ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lolo.

english: Will spraying pest control chemicals on my vegetables make them unsafe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Chemical sprays are safe if you follow the waiting period written on the container before harvesting, which gives the chemical enough time to break down completely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji onyiɛ be ni akɛmɛɔ ni aŋma yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ nɔ dani akpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfite kwraa.

english: Are chemical sprays the only way I can protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ pɛ ji gbɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: No, you can protect your crops naturally by using neem leaf extracts, practicing crop rotation, or planting pest-repelling plants alongside your main crops.
ga: Dabi, obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Loo dumɔ tsei ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ otsei titrii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my vegetables spoil so quickly after harvest compared to those grown naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ akɛto aduawai ni akwɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Applying too much chemical fertilizer causes crops to absorb excessive water and grow rapidly, making their tissues softer and prone to spoiling quickly if stored poorly.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aŋɔ nu babaoo ni amɛdara oya. Ehaa fãji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough natural power to grow crops without adding anything?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei akwɛ̃ ni mikɛ nɔ ko fataaa he?

english: You can tell your soil is fertile if previous plants grew tall with dark green leaves and produced good harvests without showing signs of stunted growth or leaf yellowing.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ tsutsu lɛ tsei lɛ dara kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni amɛjieee baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ he okadi kpo.

english: Why do my crops grow well at first but dry up right when they are about to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli shi trukaa lɛ egbiɔ beni eshwɛ fioo ni ebaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops require the most water and food when fruiting; if the soil lacks deep nutrients or has hidden root pests, the plant collapses under the stress of producing fruits.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii he hiaa tsei fe fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛyɛ aduawai amli. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni mli kwɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mli. Tsei baagbee shi yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ aduawai afeemɔ mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die during the intense sunshine of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting nurse crops like plantains around them provides critical shade and holds soil moisture, acting as a shield while the young cocoa trees develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Etsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves drop off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry weather as a natural defense mechanism to save water. Once the rains return, the plant naturally shoots out fresh green leaves and continues growing its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ ewo bulbs yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there small holes and chewed edges on the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ashɛreɔ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like fall armyworms feeding on the tender growth. Detecting them early and applying approved organic or chemical sprays into the leaf whorls protects the growing point of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fall armyworms ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Ni oooyɔse amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo baai lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies with suitable sprays and immediately removing infected plants prevents the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ akudɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and improves plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this trapped nitrogen, resulting in taller plants and better yield without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni ekpɛtɛ ehe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from around my crop stems regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei ashishifãi amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Keeping the base of your crops free of weeds ensures that all available food and water in the ground goes directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ehaa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I let too many shoot suckers grow around one plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a single plantain tree, they fight with the main plant for nutrients and water, leading to thin stems and small bunches. Pruning down extra suckers leaves only two or three strong ones for a bigger harvest.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛkɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, eshiɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make food for the roots. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent diseases and helps the plant produce larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛshishifãi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akabote mli ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes plants to lose leaf moisture faster than their roots can suck up from the ground. Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives roots enough time to absorb water before the peak heat arrives.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ nu dani hulutsoo be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which pulls natural nitrogen from the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that stored food stays behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni akɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect its tubers underground. The plant is not dying; as soon as the rains return, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Tso lɛ gbooo kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than roots can drink water from the soil, causing temporary wilting. As the temperature cools down in the evening, the plant naturally recovers.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry period that can dry out and kill delicate germinating seeds. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil stays wet enough for seedlings to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ blɛoo. Ebaanyɛ egbi ni egbo. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the ground and exposes them to sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make more food for the plant, which makes the yam tubers underground grow much bigger.
ga: Staking baajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving plants proper distance allows each one to get enough nutrients to grow full-sized crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ to he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso ni dalɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do black spots appear on my vegetable leaves when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ feɔ diji kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Heavy rain creates wet, humid conditions where fungal diseases thrive on plant leaves. Spacing your plants properly and trimming lower leaves allows air to dry the plant surface and prevent fungal growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ shwereɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akadara.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off the tree without developing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛmiitsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if there are not enough tiny insects to pollinate them, or if the tree is stressed by excessive heat and poor soil. Maintaining shade trees helps keep the area humid so pollinators can do their job.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ anyɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upward and turning pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that carry a plant virus. Controlling whiteflies early with proper field management stops the virus from spreading through your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni hiɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛji okwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua ni helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does mixing crushed charcoal and rich black dirt into my farm soil help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni atswa kɛ shikpɔŋ diŋ ni mli edɔ futu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ?

english: Dark organic materials like crushed charcoal (biochar) act like sponges in the soil. They hold water and natural fertilizers near the plant roots for a long time, preventing heavy Ghanaian rains from washing away all the good soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei (biochar) tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛhaa nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ naa koni ekajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Akɛ jwɛi loo baai ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the bare soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your maize is starving for nitrogen plant food. The plant is moving its remaining nutrients from its old bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves so it can stay alive.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha tsei niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop and curl up in the middle of a hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo moŋ?

english: Plants fold or droop their leaves during peak sunlight hours to reduce their surface area exposed to the heat. This helps them save body water from evaporating too quickly until the cool evening comes.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo lɛ baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akatsɔ oya tsɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, poor watering, or too much strong chemical fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo be mli. nu ni ehiii loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close to each other so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and tiny fruits instead of a healthy, big yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I wait until my crops sprout before applying strong fertilizer instead of putting it all in the dirt before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa awo mli moŋ fe ni mashɛrɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ashwie shi dani madu?

english: Seeds carry their own initial energy to sprout. Placing strong fertilizer in the soil too early can burn tender young sprouts or get washed away by rain before the plant roots are developed enough to drink it.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishijee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ ahoɔ amɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni amɛnuɔ nu.

english: Why do my crops yield so little when I allow weeds to grow around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ? Beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves on your farm; they aggressively drink up the water and suck away the fertilizer meant for your main crops, leaving your crops weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni amɛmuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop roots rot and turn soft when heavy rain leaves standing water on my land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When standing water fills up all the air pockets in the ground, it suffocates the roots, causing them to rot and die.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu lɛ efee dioo lɛ, eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up permanently in that area.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ jɛmɛ daa.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves starting from the tip usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer or compost gives the soil the extra food the plant needs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise that planting groundnuts or beans helps my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, this nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from under the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Protecting the plants with pest control or neem oil stops these insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ bu tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it chokes the roots and creates a wet environment where rot-causing fungi thrive, which is why planting on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmãa ni kɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller fruit bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every sucker that grows around the main plantain tree competes with it for water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two allows the main tree to put all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Sucker fɛɛ sucker ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni ena nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛto 1-2 pɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using tall poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ atsu nii kɛdu mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for expanding the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes exposes more leaves to the sun and prevents soil diseases from rotting the leaves.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ, ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when planted in open sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni hulutsoo bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sun and hot dry winds. Planting shade trees or plantains next to them provides a cool microclimate and protects their soil from drying out while they establish roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miitswa lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up the pollen inside the blossoms, preventing pollination. Without pollination, the plant drops the flower to save its energy rather than attempting to form a fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ofee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger on my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil faster than domestic crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your crops before they get a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I place chemical fertilizer right next to the stem of my young plants when applying it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifã lɛ he kɛ́ midu?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of plant tissues, which can chemically burn the tender roots and stem. Placing the fertilizer in a circle a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely absorb it without damage.
ga: Nuŋtɛi ni mli eyi obɔ ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. ni baanyɛ atsɔ tsofa nɔ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight so their leaves can make food, which grows the big tuber under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves spread out in the sun and off the damp soil where they could rot.
