ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ afee niyenii. ni kwɛ̃ɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking baaha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply. Changing crops gives the soil a break and starves out crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛi yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Is it good for me to plant beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize while giving you two different harvests from one field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, anáa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Young crops are weak and cannot fight for food. Weeds grow much faster and will steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your small crops, causing them to stay stunted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛha niyenii. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa ni ebaaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛ onibii bibii lɛ amli, ni no baaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and get covered in white powder?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni powda yɛŋ haa amɛhe?

english: This is caused by tiny sucking insects called mealybugs. They drink the juice out of the cassava leaves, making them curl. Clearing bad stalks and using healthy stems for planting helps prevent this issue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Amɛnuɔ ŋmei baa lɛ mli nu lɛ, ni no haa amɛkpãa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni ehiii ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the flower buds falling off my tomato plants before fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani aduawai baa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry, when it is excessively hot, or if they have too much leaf-growing fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch around the plant helps hold the flowers.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni edɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni akɛbaadu baai Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know it is the right time to start planting my seeds when the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: You should wait until the rainy season settles with two or three heavy rains that thoroughly soak deep into the soil. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up and die.
ga: You should wait until the rainy season. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of tiny holes and dust after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni sũ ni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Small insects called weevils eat into the grain when it is stored with too much moisture inside. Drying your maize in the sun until the grains are hard before putting them into airtight sacks or drums keeps insects out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo to mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani okɛwo kotokui loo tsɛnsii ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Is it safe for me to pick the small palm seedlings growing under my big oil palm trees and plant them on my new farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei tso bibioo ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-oil palm tso agbo lɛ shishi lɛ ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: No, planting wild seedlings that sprout under old trees is risky. Those seeds come from random cross-pollination and often grow into low-yielding trees with thick shells and very little oil.
ga: Dabi, koo mli dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei momoi ashishi lɛ adumɔ ji oshara. Those seeds come from random cross-pollination. and often grows into low-yielding trees. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɔ fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I buy certified palm seeds from agricultural offices instead of keeping seeds from my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmei dumɔwui ni Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ema nɔ mi lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumi ɔ yi wami kɛ je ní kpami be ɔ mi.

english: Seeds saved from your harvest will not produce trees like the parent plant. Certified seeds are specially bred hybrids (Tenera) designed to give you high oil yields, thin shells, and uniform tree growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo tsei tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni afee amɛ ekome (tenera) ni afee koni eha bo mu ni fa babaoo, ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tseee kɛ tso ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: How can I tell if a young oil palm seedling will produce plenty of oil before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mu tso ko baajie mu babaoo dani adu?

english: You cannot tell the oil yield of a palm tree just by looking at the seedling. The only way to guarantee a high-yielding tree is to buy certified seedlings from recognized nurseries or extension centers.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole mu ni jɛɔ ŋmei tso mli baa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ. Gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tsei woɔ yibii babaoo ji ni ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe loo tsei akwɛmɔhe ko ni akpɛlɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers discourage us from transplanting volunteer seedlings that sprout on their own after rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsiɔ mɛi anaa koni amɛkadu dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe eha ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Volunteer seedlings have unknown genetic quality. Many will turn out to be low-yielding varieties or trees that fail to produce proper fruit, wasting your land, labor, and fertilizer for years.
ga: Dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe eha lɛ ji nɔ ni aleee bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha, ni amɛteŋ babaoo baatsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii fioo loo tsei ni nyɛŋ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ, nitsumɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afii babaoo.

english: Do oil palm trees have separate male and female trees, or can one tree produce fruits on its own?
ga: Ani mu tsei yɛ tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi? Aloo tso kome pɛ baawo yibii?

english: Oil palm trees are not strictly male or female. A single palm tree produces both male and female flowers at different times, though both are needed for pollination so fruit bunches can form.
ga: Mu tsei jeee hii loo yei pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tɛŋ tso kome baawo fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe miihia ni pollination afee aduawai akui moŋ.

english: Why do some of my young oil palm trees only produce flowers that dry up without producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔi ni egbi pɛ ni amɛfeee aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Those dry flowers are male flowers, which produce pollen to fertilize female flowers. Young or stressed trees often produce mostly male flowers first, but they will produce fruit bunches once female flowers appear.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ ji fɔfɔi hii ni feɔ pollen koni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi yei amli. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii loo tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi ebaafee aduawai akuu beni fɔfɔi yei lɛ je kpo lɛ.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers talk about 'male' seeds or 'female' seeds when planting oil palms?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ wie ‘hii’ loo ‘yoo’ dumɔwui ahe beni amɛduɔ mu tso lɛ?

english: Farmers often misuse the terms 'male' and 'female' to describe different tree varieties or non-bearing trees. In reality, oil palm seeds are not male or female; you should focus on planting certified hybrid varieties instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ wiemɔi ni ji ‘nuu’ kɛ ‘yoo’ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛtsɔɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi loo tsei ni wooo yibii. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Oil palm dumɔwui jeee nuu loo yoo. Mohu ɔ, e sa nɛ o ngɔ o juɛmi kɛ ma hybrid tso slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ a nɔ.

english: What is the difference between hard-shell palm nuts and the high-yielding nuts extension officers recommend?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni mli wa kɛ ŋmei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mɛi ni woɔ yibiiwoo he hewalɛ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ateŋ?

english: Hard-shell nuts come from the 'Dura' variety, which has a thick shell and less oil flesh. Officers recommend the 'Tenera' hybrid, which has a thin shell, a thick layer of oil-rich pulp, and produces much more palm oil.
ga: Nuts jɛɔ ‘Dura’ henɔ lɛ mli, ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ehiɛ fɔ fioo. Amralofoi lɛ jieɔ tsofa ni ji ‘Tenera’ ni ji tsofa ni akɛfee tsofa lɛ he ŋaa, ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo. Eji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ mu. ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei fɔ babaoo

english: What happens if I plant oil palm seeds from a nut that has no shell inside it at all?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mu tso dumɔwui jɛ ŋmei ni bɛ ŋmei ko mli lɛ mli?

english: Shell-less nuts come from the 'Pisifera' variety. Trees grown from these seeds usually shed their female flowers early and produce almost no fruit bunches, making them unsuitable for commercial farming.
ga: Nuts ni bɛ ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ ‘Pisifera’ henɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ amɛ pistil fɔfɔi lɛ mra ni amɛfɔɔɔ yibii wooo. ni no haa esaaa kɛha jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are some wild palm trees on my land growing very tall quickly but giving small, poor-quality fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa oya, shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa lɛ?

english: Unselected wild palms focus their energy on vegetative growth rather than fruit production. Because their genetics are unrefined, they yield small bunches with thick shells and very little extractable oil.
ga: Koo mli tsei ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni shwereɔ lɛ anɔ fe aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, asaaa amɛfɔmɔ nii lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii bibii. Eyɛ tsitsi ni mli tse ni mu fioo ko pɛ abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why do some of these new seed varieties produce more harvest than the traditional seeds I have used for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mikɛtsu nii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: New seed varieties are specially bred by researchers to resist common diseases, withstand dry weather, and use nutrients more efficiently, allowing the plant to direct more energy into producing heavier crops.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi efɔ dumɔwui heei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛkɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why is my harvest still small even though I put plenty of fertilizer in my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Soil fertility is only part of the equation. If your seed variety is old or weak, the plant lacks the strength to turn those soil nutrients into a large harvest, regardless of how much fertilizer you apply.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ji equation lɛ fã kome pɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo amɛhe waaa lɛ Tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaatsake niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛwo yibii babaoo mli. Ekɔɔɔ he eko bɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafata he.

english: Why do extension officers keep bringing new seed varieties every few years instead of sticking to one good seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui heei baa daa afii fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni amɛaakpɛtɛ dumɔwu kpakpa kome he lɛ?

english: Pests and crop diseases change over time, and weather patterns shift. Researchers continuously develop new varieties to keep crops protected against new diseases and to cope better with changing weather.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi miitsake. Nibii amlitaolɔi feɔ tsei srɔtoi heei be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ helai heei ahe, ni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some maize varieties stay green during a dry spell while others wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different traits built into them. Drought-tolerant varieties grow deeper root systems or hold moisture better, allowing them to survive when rainfall is low.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ sui srɔtoi. Tsoi srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ daa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli loo amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ.

english: If a seed variety gives a huge yield in another country, will it automatically yield the same on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui wo yibii babaoo yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ Ani ebaawo yibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Seeds react strongly to local soil conditions, temperature, and rainfall patterns. A foreign variety must be tested locally to see if it can adapt to Ghana's specific environment.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui tsuɔ nii waa yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ, latsaa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he. Esa akɛ aka maŋsɛɛ tsofai srɔtoi lɛ akwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli koni ana kɛji amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana shihilɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ mli.

english: How can I try a new crop variety without risking my family's whole food supply for the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka ŋmɔshi nibii heei akwɛ ni mikɛ miweku lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ wooo oshara mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can plant the new variety on a small test plot alongside your regular crops. This allows you to observe how it grows and yields on your specific land before committing your entire farm to it.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei srɔtoi heei yɛ kaa shikpɔji bibii anɔ yɛ tsei ni okwɛɔ daa lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo yɔɔ ha dani okɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aha.

english: Why does a seed variety yield very well in the Volta region but perform poorly when planted in the Northern region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Volta Kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: Each region has different soil types, temperatures, and rainfall levels. A crop variety bred for wet or humid conditions will struggle in drier, hotter climates unless it is specifically adapted for them.
ga: Kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi, latsaa, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Tsei henɔi ni akwɛɔ kɛha hulutsoo loo hulutsoo shihilɛi baa bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. ja tsakemɔ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ kɛha amɛ.

english: Why should I buy fresh certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest to plant again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from improved hybrid varieties lose their special strengths over generations, leading to smaller yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures you get maximum yield and disease resistance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ baaye abua bo ni oná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ nyɛyeɔ nyɛnɔ.

english: Why do pests destroy one field of cassava while the neighbor's different cassava variety is untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmei ŋmɔ kome yɛ be mli ni ŋmei henɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee lɛ?

english: Certain crop varieties possess natural chemical defenses or tougher leaf textures that pests dislike, keeping them healthy while weaker varieties nearby get damaged.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he loo amɛyɛ baai ni wa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔɔ. Enɛ haa amɛhe wa yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do some new cassava varieties mature in six months while my old ones take over a year to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔi heei komɛi shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mitso momo lɛ he nɔ ni fe afi ni ekɛkpaa lɛ?

english: Researchers breed early-maturing varieties to grow fast and store starch quickly. This helps farmers harvest early to avoid dry seasons or pest invasions, and allows for multiple harvests in a year.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi fɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra koni amɛdara oya ni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nii mra koni hɔmɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai akatutua amɛ. ni ehaa akpaa nibii babaoo yɛ afi mli.

english: Why does the amount of medicine recommended for my cocoa trees look so small in the measuring cap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mi cacao lɛ he ŋaa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eji bibioo yɛ susumɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop chemicals are highly concentrated. Even a small amount like 30 milliliters contains enough active strength to protect the tree without scorching the leaves or stems.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ babaoo. Nɔ bibioo ko tamɔ mililitai 30 po he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ abu tso lɛ he ni eshãaa baai loo shishifã lɛ.

english: If I double the amount of medicine in my spray tank, will it clear the pests off my cocoa faster?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ spray tanki lɛ mli lɛ toi enyɔ Ani ebaajie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ oya?

english: No, doubling the dose will not clear pests faster; instead, the extra strength will burn the delicate cocoa leaves, destroy fresh flowers, and lower your yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ wo mli shii enyɔ lɛ, egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ oya. Shi hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baaha kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ashã. kpata fɔfɔi heei ahiɛ ni oha nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi

english: How can I accurately measure liquid medicine for my cocoa farm if I am worried about using too little?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu tsofa ni ji nu kɛha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mihaoɔ yɛ nɔ fioo pɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ he hu?

english: Always use the specific measuring cup provided with the container rather than guessing, as exact measurement ensures the medicine is strong enough to work without harming the plant.
ga: Okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo ni akɛha kɛfata tsɛnsi lɛ he lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. instead of guessing Enɛ ji akɛ, susumɔ pɔtɛɛ haa tsofa lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etsu nii ni eyeee tso lɛ awui.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning dark and drying up shortly after I sprayed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when too much medicine was poured into the mix, causing a chemical burn that damages the tree's foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ afɔse tsofa babaoo awo tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsofai shãa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa flowers are falling off because of disease or because of the spray I used?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela loo tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ ni mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi lɛ?

english: If flowers drop off suddenly and in large numbers right after spraying, it usually means the chemical mixture was too strong or applied too close to delicate blooms.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛyi fa babaoo beni afɔ amɛshwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo akɛwo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe tsɔ.

english: Will applying extra crop medicine prevent diseases from coming to my farm in the future?
ga: Ani tsei ahe tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi helai ni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ mli wɔsɛɛ lɛ anaa?

english: Over-applying medicine does not provide future protection; it damages the crop's leaves and bark, making the tree weaker and more vulnerable to future attacks.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haaa abu mɔ he wɔsɛɛ. Efiteɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛhewolo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni wɔsɛɛ be mli lɛ, enyɛɔ etutuaa lɛ.

english: Can I mix extra water into my sprayer if I feel the chemical mix is too strong for my young cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu krokomɛi afutu tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ? Kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa tsɔ kɛha mi-kookoo bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: You must follow the exact water-to-medicine ratio specified on the label, because too much water makes it ineffective against pests, while too little water burns the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ nu kɛ tsofa ni aŋmala yɛ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ mli. Yɛ be mli ni nu fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashã.

english: Is it safe to spray my cocoa trees when the afternoon sun is very hot?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooofɔ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying in hot sun combined with strong chemical dosages causes the medicine to heat up on the leaves, leading to severe leaf burn and wilting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli wa lɛ shwie hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ adɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baa lɛ shãa waa ni egboɔ.

english: Why do some farmers say that using too much pest medicine actually harms the cocoa pod harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ yeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni akpaa lɛ awui diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Excess chemical destroys the young pods and beneficial insects that help the cocoa tree produce, leading to fewer healthy pods at harvest time.
ga: Tsofai babaoo fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kpakpa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together in the same tank to save time when spraying?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ afutu mli yɛ tanki kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Mixing unapproved medicines can create a harsh mixture that damages cocoa leaves and neutralizes the power of the chemicals so they no longer kill pests.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nibii ni mli wa ni fiteɔ kookoo baai lɛ ni ehaa tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko dɔŋŋ

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava usually shows it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking open due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when I pick them in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting during peak heat causes crops to lose water rapidly and traps high heat inside the fruit, which makes them rot quickly. Harvesting early in the morning keeps crops fresh much longer.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni emɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ aduawai lɛ amli. ni haa tso lɛ fiteɔ oya Nikpamɔ leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall but not producing big ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida shi amɛbɛ toi wuji lɛ?

english: When maize gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it spends all its energy growing tall leaves and stalks instead of putting energy into developing thick, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kakadaji kɛ ŋmeii. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ a mi mi wa nɛ e hyi.

english: What causes my crop yields to drop when I plant the same crop on the same land every season?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be mli?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating different crops restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Hard or compacted soil prevents yam tubers from expanding smoothly underground. Planting in soft, well-heaped mounds or ridges allows the roots to spread and form large, clean tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ebɔle he jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he tse.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Peppers drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering prevents flower drop.
ga: Peppers baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ lɛ mli ba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight in and reduces moisture so pods stay healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni oha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rotten while still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium, usually due to irregular watering. Regular, even watering stops the rotting from occurring.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does weed growth affect the development and yield of my young crops?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashweremɔ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds during the early growing stages ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a high yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ shishijee be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my plantain farm is suffering from lack of water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu bɛ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When plantain plants are thirsty, their leaves turn yellow early, curl up, or collapse around the trunk. Covering the soil around the base with dry mulch helps trap moisture during hot periods.
ga: Kɛ́ kumai ye plantains lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ he loo efoɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: My farm land has a lot of rocks and hard soil. Can I still grow good crops on it?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ tɛi ni wa waa. Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ jɛmɛ lolo?

english: Yes, but you need to prepare it carefully. Removing surface stones, breaking up hard ground, and adding organic compost or manure helps loosen the soil so crop roots can easily reach water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ osaa he jogbaŋŋ. Tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ajiemɔ Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mligbalamɔ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: How can I make my farm soil fertile again without buying expensive chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can enrich your soil naturally by leaving cleared crop leaves to rot on the land, adding animal manure, and planting cover crops like cowpeas, which put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ahe baai ni he tse ni oooha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. kɛ kooloi amli ŋmeii afata he ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ni baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ afata he.

english: The rainfall patterns have changed and I do not know when to sow my maize seeds. How do I decide?
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi tsakeɔ Ni mileee be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui. Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ?

english: Instead of planting strictly by calendar months, wait until the ground receives two or three heavy rains that thoroughly wet the soil before sowing, ensuring young roots get enough moisture.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ kalanda nyɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ dani odu dumɔwui. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: I want to start farming in the Ashanti region, but I do not know which crop is best for a beginner.
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi okwaayeli yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ, shi mileee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Cassava and maize are great starting crops because they adapt well to the regional soil, grow reliably, and always have strong local market demand.
ga: Cassava kɛ ŋmãa ji shishijee tsei ni hi ejaakɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. grow reliably Ni be fɛɛ be lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ waa yɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other, will I harvest more food?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin plants and small yields. Giving each seed proper spacing yields stronger plants and bigger harvests.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ waa, ni ebaaha ŋmaa babaoo aba.

english: Is it better to plant only one type of crop on my land or mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Mixing complementary crops, such as planting legumes alongside cereal crops like maize, helps protect your farm from pest outbreaks and improves soil fertility.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ, baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ

english: Curling yellow leaves usually mean small sap-sucking insects like aphids are attacking the plant. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or boiled neem tree leaf water can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, miitutua tso lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem baa mli nu ni ahoo lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I protect my young maize crop from worms eating the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Check your crops regularly. Applying a small amount of clean dry sand or wood ash mixed with crushed neem seed powder into the center funnel of the young leaves can deter caterpillars like fall armyworms.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni egbi loo tso mli sũ ni he tse ni akɛ neem dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ efutu mli fioo ko wo baai bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ anaa.

english: How long will I have to wait before a new hybrid cocoa tree produces its first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani cacao tso hee ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ ajie eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually begin producing fruit within two to three years if they receive proper shade, sufficient water, and weed management during their early growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni sa, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: How do I stop insects from ruining my harvested grain before I take it to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ dani amɛya jara nɔ?

english: Make sure your grain is completely dry under the sun until it cracks sharply when bitten, then store it off the floor in airtight bags to keep insects out.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-rice ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi kɛyashi amɛbaatswa oya kɛji akɛ amɛye. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ vacuum kotokui amli koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why do my rice fields need to stay flooded with water while the crops are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ nu awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Rice plants grow best in standing water because it controls weeds, keeps the plant roots cool, and helps the soil release important nutrients that the rice needs to produce heavy grains.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ eyeɔ jwɛi anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ ŋmãa ni tsii aba lɛ kpo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni ehe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from intense heat. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to direct sunlight, the plant slows down water loss through evaporation during dry afternoon hours.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a few become pods. Flowers drop if the tree lacks water or nutrients, if there is too little shade, or if tiny beneficial insects (midges) are not present to pollinate them.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔii fioo pɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be fioo pɛ yɔɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves but yielding tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi ehiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows under heavy shade, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to store food in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛ niyenii ato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller plantain bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ plantain tso bibioo ko nɔ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every young sucker competes with the main plant for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning away excess suckers and leaving only one strong replacement allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi nɔ kome pɛ ni he wa ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomato fruits turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil switches between very dry and very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni tsakeɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa teŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so they can make food for the roots. It also keeps the leaves off damp ground, reducing disease and allowing airflow so the plant produces larger tubers.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa helai baa shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They crawl into the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime to eat the tender young leaves while hiding from heat, direct sun, and natural predators.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii yɛ be mli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid spreading dry fertilizer onto dry soil during hot, sunny weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer requires moisture to dissolve so plant roots can soak it in. Putting dry fertilizer on dry soil during extreme heat can burn the crop roots and cause nutrients to evaporate into the air before the plant can use them.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the middle vein down to the stem, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the primary food plants need to build strong, green leaves and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛtee shishigbɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the earth through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for heavy-eating crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives when rainy weather creates too much dampness and shade in the cocoa farm. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees helps airflow and prevents it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal helai ni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine ba kookoo ŋmɔji amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa hebuu.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted into the plant by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛbaa tsei amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam plants make food for their underground tubers through their leaves. Staking lifts leaves high into the sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil where fungal rot quickly spreads.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to heap up soil around the base of my cassava plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ muji toɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Mounding loose soil around cassava stems protects the expanding roots from direct sunlight—which causes them to turn green and woody—while giving the tubers soft space to grow large.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abua naa lɛ buɔ shishifãi ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ tsei. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get extremely high or when the plant lacks adequate water, causing heat stress that prevents the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa hulutsoo haomɔ ni tsiɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee aduawai baa.

english: Why does my maize crop fail to form full corn cobs if dry weather hits when the tassels appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ efeee ŋmei ni eyi obɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ná enɔ hewalɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: The flowering stage is when maize needs water most urgently to produce pollen and form kernels. Drought at this precise moment prevents successful pollination, resulting in empty or underfilled cobs.
ga: Be ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa he hiaa nu oya fe fɛɛ koni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui aba. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nɛkɛ be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ efolo loo he ko bɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers give smaller fruit bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plantain suckers are planted too close together, their root systems and large leaves compete fiercely for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ babaoo ahi shi koni akɛkwɛ kuu agbo ko nɔ.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava roots taste bitter while others taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally contains protective chemicals that cause bitterness, and the plant produces much higher amounts of these bitter compounds when exposed to prolonged drought or poor soil conditions.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ cassava mli. Ni tsei jieɔ nɛkɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ nɛɛ babaoo kwraa kɛji amɛkɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kpe.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains or shade timber provides cool air and protection from sun scorch until the cocoa trees mature and grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Tsei ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui loo hulutsoo tsei Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to capture energy and make big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot soil, prevents rotting diseases, and helps the plant produce a larger harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aha amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ gangrene naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of maize stalks usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-based fertilizer helps the crop regain its green color and grow healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa toi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the roots and leaves decay, they leave behind natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Abaashi Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know which direction to face cassava stem cuttings when planting them in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmei niji lɛ ahiɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds on the stem cutting; they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the new sprouts to grow awkwardly, reducing yield and delaying growth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ, esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ blɛoo. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni edalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Which type of plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and plant on my field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a strong, heavy bulb base—are best. They grow faster, produce stronger stems, and yield bigger plantain bunches compared to water suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni tsii ni tamɔ bulbous lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛ daa oya. Bɔɔ tso tsei ni wa ni eha plantains wuji kɛ akɛto tsei ashishifãi ni nuɔ nu ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why should I wait a bit instead of planting my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimɛɔ fioo moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill newly sprouted seeds. Waiting until the rainy season is fully established ensures there is steady moisture for the crops to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baafee mlɛo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa daa.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding lime or organic matter helps protect the tomatoes from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni abu tomato he koni ekafite.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat, prolonged drought, or pest attacks. Ensuring adequate watering during dry weather and keeping the plants healthy helps the flowers stay attached and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Clearing weeds early gives your young plants unimpeded access to food and water so they can grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. koni amɛnyɛ amɛdara oya

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during drought to reduce water loss and protect its roots. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil lacks moisture, which prevents the flowers from successfully forming tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Enɛ haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a clear sign that the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to build green leaves and grow strong cobs.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia koni aná baai eŋɔli ni aná ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why does my land dry out and harden so fast after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ ni ewaa oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic material like compost or dried leaves, which act like a sponge to hold water and keep the soil soft.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ blɛoo.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bibii.

english: Why do I still need to remove weeds even when my crops are much taller than them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe amɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have deep roots that steal water and fertilizers from the soil right under your crops, taking away the strength your crops need to produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ mli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus carried by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why are my yam leaves turning brown and dying long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam leaves is often caused by leaf spot diseases or root damage from soil pests, which block water from reaching the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato baai lɛ agbimɔ oya ji baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa nu ayashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my garden eggs taste very bitter when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become bitter when the plant experiences long periods of drought or heat stress while the fruit is growing on the bush.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ be mli ni aduawai miida yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my okra plants grow tall and bushy but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes okra focus all its energy on growing leafy stems instead of setting flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa fe nine lɛ haa okra kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii awo mli.

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava plants focus all their energy on growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of storing energy in the roots to make thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai kakadaji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ a pee bulb nɛ mi wa.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps nearby maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil, causing the plant to protect itself by aborting the flower.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The disease attacks the inside of the plant stems and blocks water from moving from the roots up to the leaves, causing the plant to wilt.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tutuaa tso lɛ mligbɛ ni ehaa nu jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to settle before sowing my cowpea seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu tsina ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Cowpea seeds need steady moisture to sprout properly. Sowing in dry soil or right after a single light rain can cause the seeds to rot underground or wither as soon as they shoot up.
ga: Cowpea dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi loo amɛgbi kɛji amɛpue pɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds around my yam mounds slow down the growth of the yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa mi-sweet potato wein tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from the yam plant, leaving the yam with too little energy to build long vines and big underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ sweet potato tso lɛ mli lɛ oya. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ náa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛfeɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see small green caterpillars eating holes in my cabbage leaves after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni miiye bu yɛ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm weather after rain causes pest eggs like the diamondback moth to hatch quickly. The young caterpillars feed on soft cabbage leaves to grow rapidly before pupating.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ diamondback ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. Kplukai bibii yeɔ kaabeji baai bibii koni amɛdara oya dani amɛfee bibii.

english: Why do my harvested plantains turn soft and rot faster when left under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya kɛ́ ashi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Heat from direct sunlight causes the plantain to breathe faster and release ethylene gas, a natural chemical that speeds up the ripening process and leads to early decay.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ muɔ oya ni amɛjieɔ ethylene gas lɛ kpo. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ oya ni ehaa egboɔ oya.

english: Why are my maize ears coming out small and light when I want to sell heavy grains at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ be mli ni miisumɔ ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni tsii lɛ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants need sufficient nutrients and water right when the ears begin to form. If the plants lack food or water at this stage, the kernels will not fill up completely, leaving you with small cobs that bring lower prices.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa tsei kɛji toi lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atsui enyɔɔɔ amɛmli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmei bibioo ko. ni haa jara lɛ baa shi

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve moisture and protect the roots underground. Adding mulch around the stem helps retain soil moisture so the plant can keep growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Stems lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: How can I make my tomatoes ripen evenly so buyers will take the whole basket at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha tomatoi lɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni jarayelɔi lɛ aŋɔ tsɛnsi muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Consistent watering and avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer late in the growth stage allow tomato plants to mature evenly, giving you uniform fruits that attract commercial buyers.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii po ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayeli mli lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why is my pepper farm producing plenty of green leaves but very few peppers to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants put all their energy into growing tall and bushy leaves instead of flowers. Switching to a balanced fertilizer encourages the plant to set fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my plantain leaves drying up with dark spots before the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka, which destroy the green parts of the leaf that feed the fruit. Treating the leaves early keeps the plant strong enough to yield large bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni fiteɔ baai lɛ amli hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni haa aduawai lɛ niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What causes my harvested yams to rot quickly in storage before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ?

english: Yams rot mainly when they suffer small cuts during digging or are kept in damp, hot rooms. Storing undamaged tubers in a dry, shady, and cool barn stops rot and extends their selling life.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ titri kɛji amɛyɛ pilamɔi bibii. yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ loo akɛtoɔ tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ muji lɛ to ŋmɔ ko ni mli egbi, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli, ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for my main crop if I plant beans in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for your main crop while giving you two different harvests to sell.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Okɛ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa otsei titrii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ haa ni ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cowpea plants before any pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called thrips feed on the flower buds and cause them to drop off prematurely. Protecting your crop with proper pest control at early flowering allows the flowers to turn into full seed pods.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bu onibii ahe yɛ fɔfɔii ni baa mra lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops reduce the quality of my harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When your crops have to fight weeds, they grow weak and yield smaller, lower-quality produce that is hard to sell for profit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi miiwu Amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ tsei fioo ni amɛhe ehiaaa ni ewa akɛ abaahɔ̃ɔ koni ana sɛɛnamɔ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so I don't waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo midumɔ nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii koni mikafite shika?

english: The best time is when the crops are actively growing and the soil is moist, usually 2 to 4 weeks after planting. Applying fertilizer in dry soil or right before heavy downpours wastes your input because plants cannot absorb it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ miida waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, bei pii lɛ, otsii 2 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu tsei lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ ejaakɛ tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and tall with very small corn ears or no ears at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo amɛbɛ toi kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpea or groundnuts before planting maize on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii dani madu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this natural plant food to grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ waa ni tsofa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest since the tubers grow under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is maturing when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, the main stem thickens, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking due to expanding tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei lɛ egbɔ kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ beni bulb lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my seed yams take several weeks to shoot up vines after I bury them in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ he otsii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ beni mifu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural resting period called dormancy after harvest. Even when buried in warm soil, the tuber will not sprout until this internal natural timing finishes.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ po lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ edaŋ kɛyashi adebɔɔ mli be ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbe naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that shade young cocoa trees from the harsh sun and keep the soil moist during the hot dry season.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers without forming small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop many if the soil is too dry, if temperature swings are high, or if tiny beneficial insects are not present to pollinate them.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi babaoo baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. hulutsoo tsakemɔi ni yaa hiɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baanyɛ afee pollination bɛ.

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a protective reaction. The pepper plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface exposed to the hot sun, preventing excess water loss.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ afee bibioo. Koni nu ni fa fe nine akafite

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off during very hot dry weather without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat dries out the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing proper fertilization. Without fertilization, the plant drops the flower to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crops wilt and look dead during dry spells even if I watered them recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni egboi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha tsei lɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ moŋ.

english: On extremely hot days, water evaporates from crop leaves faster than roots can drink from the soil. Plants droop to reduce their exposure to sunlight, but they usually recover overnight when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba shi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for green growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too intense or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water. High temperatures prevent pollen from working properly, so keeping the soil moist and cool helps the tree hold its blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba loo kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa pollen lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ fɛ̃i baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight because intense heat burns their delicate leaves and dries them out. Leaving tall shade trees or intercropping with plantains creates a cool shelter that holds moisture and helps the cocoa survive its early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ni ebaaha baai bibii lɛ agbi. abandoning tall trees Aloo, kɛ akɛ plantains ŋmɔɔ lɛ, ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small even though the leaves grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or remains continuously wet, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing branches and foliage instead of feeding the roots. Planting in well-draining soil without excessive nitrogen encourages the plant to store food in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nitrogen babaoo bɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny water mold that spreads rapidly in high moisture and darkness. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and wind flow through the farm to dry off the cocoa pods, stopping the rot from spreading.
ga: Nu mli ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii diji lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ duŋ mli lɛ Afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi. ni etsĩ dumɔwui ni egboi lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward to reduce their surface area and save water when the midday sun is too harsh. If the leaves relax in the evening, the plant is simply protecting itself; if they stay curled, it may need more irrigation or protection from sap-sucking insects.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe. Kɛji amɛkoto lɛ, ekolɛ ehe baahia ni afɔ amɛ nu kroko loo abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant during the next rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid maize will produce weaker plants with smaller cobs because hybrid seeds lose their special high-yielding traits after the first generation. Buying fresh certified hybrid seeds every planting season guarantees a heavy yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii ni ŋmãa bibii yɔɔ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year when I plant on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull minerals out of the dirt every season, so planting continuously on the same soil empties the land's food bank. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts feeds natural nutrients back into the ground so it stays fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ayaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ ahi shi babaoo.

english: Why do my plantain stems snap or fall over when heavy winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that struggle to support heavy bunches on their own. Supporting the main stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo forks gives them extra balance against strong wind gusts.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋmei fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are natural wild plants that are adapted to wake up and drink rain water much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents the weeds from stealing the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients your crops need to get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛnu nugbɔ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and fragile root systems that quickly burn and dry out under direct heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil moist, acting as a shelter while the young trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ abobaahe yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the energy it needs to turn green and form good cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma baai ni wa.
