Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: If I add extra fertilizer to my crops, will it make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha tsei lɛ adara oya fe shii enyɔ?

english: No, giving crops more fertilizer than they need can burn their roots and stunt their growth or kill them. Crops can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients at a time, so applying the correct amount at the right stage works best.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo onibii amli fe bɔ ni he hiaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni eha amɛdalɛ afee mlɛo loo ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afite. Tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai fioo ko pɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ yibɔ ni sa tsu nii yɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen from rich soil or improper fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of food underground. Balanced plant nutrition helps the cassava redirect its energy toward expanding the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei naa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo ŋmei ni esaaa mli. Ebaafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tso mli niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni etsakeɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural way for maize plants to protect themselves from hot weather. By curling their leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from escaping too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni ŋmãa tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil consistently watered and cool with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni oha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato.

english: Why do my garden pepper plants wilt in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In hot weather, plant leaves lose moisture faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting. Covering the soil around the roots with grass or dry leaves keeps the root area cool and conserves soil moisture throughout the day.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Tso baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a tiny fungus that multiplies rapidly in damp, dark, and wet conditions. Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the tree canopy, stopping the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji ni egbo baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, hei ni edɔ, kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tso niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ yitsoŋ gĩɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, weak plants. Giving each plant proper spacing allows roots and leaves to spread out and yield larger crops.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How does leaving dry leaves and old plant stems on my farmland help my soil?
ga: Te baai ni egboi kɛ tsei momo ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Old plant material decays over time and turns into organic matter that feeds useful soil organisms and retains moisture. Leaving crop residue on the field keeps the ground cool, prevents rain from washing away topsoil, and builds rich soil for future crops.
ga: Tsei amli nibii ni etsɛ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni efee shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are plant roots so important for my crops to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi he hiaa waa koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots act as the crop's anchor and food path. They secure the plant firmly in the ground so wind cannot blow it over, while drawing up water and nutrients from deep within the soil to feed the leaves and stems.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ ankɔ kɛ niyenii gbɛ. Amɛfiɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa lɛ kɛya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni ekɛha baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: How do newly planted crops establish their roots in the soil?
ga: Te tsei ni adu ehee lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds sprout or cuttings take hold, they send out small tender roots that search for moisture. As long as the soil has adequate water and softness, these roots push deeper to anchor the plant and begin feeding it.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwu lɛ kwɛ̃ loo ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaatsu shishifãi bibii kɛje kpo. Baje kpo koni oyatao ŋmɔtɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ nu kɛ blɛoofeemɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, Shishifãi nɛɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛkɛma tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛje shishi amɛha lɛ niyenii.

english: What should I do if my farmland soil is very hard and difficult to work?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ wa?

english: Hard or compact land prevents crop roots from spreading deep into the soil. Tilling or breaking up hard ground before planting loosens the earth, allowing water to sink in and roots to grow without struggling.
ga: He ni wa loo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni oootsu he nii loo ogbala mli dani odu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu lɛ abote mli ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada ni amɛkafee nɔ ko.

english: How does clearing and preparing my land properly make farming easier later in the season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni misaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha okwaayeli afee mlɛo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Proper land preparation removes underground obstacles and deep weed roots early on. This allows your crops to strike roots quickly and grow without competing against tough native vegetation for soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi gbɛtsii nibii kɛ jwɛi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli mra. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni wa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some weeds keep growing back even after I cut them down with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Many stubborn weeds store food in deep underground root systems. Simply cutting off the top leaves leaves the root alive underground, so you must completely uproot the entire root system to destroy the weed.
ga: Jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa babaoo toɔ niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofamɔ gbɛjianɔtoo muu lɛ fɛɛ koni okpata jwɛi lɛ ahiɛ.

english: What is the best way to remove deep-rooted weeds from my field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: To remove deep-rooted weeds permanently, wait until the soil is slightly moist after rainfall and use a hoe to dig around the base, pulling out the main root system entirely so leftover pieces cannot sprout again.
ga: Ani oosumɔ ni ojie jwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛya naanɔ? Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ shɔvel atsa shishitoo lɛ he. Gbalamɔ shishifã titri lɛ kwraa. Bɔni afee ni fãji ni eshwɛ lɛ akakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to be careful when uprooting crops like cassava or yams during harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ beni ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Root crops store their edible harvest underground. Careful uprooting prevents breaking or wounding the tubers, which protects them from rotting quickly and ensures they stay fresh for market or cooking.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ shishifãi wo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekagba loo eye awui. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni baa oya lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ehee koni ahɔ̃ɔ loo ahoo.

english: How can I tell if my root crops are growing well underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishishifãi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: Healthy root crop growth is shown above ground by thick green leaves and strong stems. As tubers swell underground, you will often notice the soil around the base of the plant cracking and raising slightly.
ga: Ajieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ adalɛ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsei ahe tsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei ni mli wa nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli gbala yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Bei pii lɛ obaana akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa ni ewo ŋwɛi fioo.

english: Why do crops with deep roots survive dry weather better than crops with shallow roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ?

english: During dry spells, surface soil loses water quickly. Crops with deep root systems can reach stored moisture deep beneath the ground surface, keeping the plant alive and green even when rains pause.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. Ha tsei ahi shi ni amɛfee eŋɔli kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ekpa po.

english: How does a strong root system help me get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shishifã ni mli wa yeɔ ebuaa mi ni minine shɛɔ ŋmaa kpakpa nɔ?

english: A strong root system absorbs more water and soil nutrients, supplying the plant with continuous energy. This extra energy translates into bigger stems, healthier leaves, and abundant fruit or tubered yields.
ga: Shishifã ni mli wa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ naa hewalɛ be fɛɛ be Hewalɛ kroko nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ tsei wuji. Baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong heat. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide shade to protect the young cocoa from direct sunlight and keep the soil moist during hot weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying fertilizer at the right time supplies this missing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ ni akɛbaawo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baatsu he nii.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my maize so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni nugbɔ akafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in two stages: a small amount when planting or two weeks after germination, and a second portion when the maize reaches knee-height when it grows fastest and feeds heavily.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Akɛ fioo ko awo mli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ loo otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. kɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ, be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ aaafee enaneshi, be mli ni edaa oya fe fɛɛ ni eyeɔ niyenii ni tsii.

english: Why am I seeing tiny holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like powder in the centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni powda ko ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the leaf whorls. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemicals protects the young growing points.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ahe ŋmeii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Root rot happens when too much water stays around the roots due to poor soil drainage or fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi that block the plant's water pipes. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like maize prevents these diseases from building up in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shwiemɔ trukaa nɛɛ baa. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ tsakpaa, tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa helai nɛɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems, poor yields, and makes it easy for diseases to spread between overlapping leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ helai baagbɛ ashwã baai ni tsɔɔ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under direct sun, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant groundnuts or beans together with my main crops like cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii titri, tamɔ ŋmei he?

english: Yes, planting legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas alongside main crops helps the soil because these plants pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, feeding the neighboring crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni akɛduɔ nibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛha tsei ni yeɔ hela lɛ niyenii.

english: It is best to wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough (about the length of your hand) over a few consecutive days so seeds do not germinate and then dry out if the rain stops for a week.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ofee ji ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. (aaafee nine kome kɛlɛ) gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: This happens when your soil is short on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay healthy. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from its old bottom leaves up to nourish the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut plants look full and green, but the pods underground are completely empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ eŋɔli lɛ? Shi ani shikpɔŋ shishi pod lɛ mli efee efolo kwraa?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when there is not enough calcium in the soil while the nuts are forming. Groundnuts absorb calcium directly through their underground pods to fill the seeds, so poor soil calcium leaves you with empty shells.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ. Peanuts shwieɔ calcium lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli koni ekɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ohiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally when dry weather hits to save water and keep from drying out completely. The plant goes into a resting state to survive the heat, and it will sprout fresh leaves quickly as soon as the rains start again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ ebɔɔ su mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ mli koni amɛhi wala mli yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over on their own as soon as the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji ená aduawai babaoo pɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the top of the soil and do not go deep into the ground. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the roots cannot hold the weight against wind or gravity, so you must prop up the stem with strong wooden Y-sticks.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tso ni wa ni tamɔ Y afi tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden inner funnel of the maize stem. It feeds on the young leaves before they open up, leaving ragged holes and waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmeii amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. Ebaaye baai bibii dani amɛkwɛ̃. Eshiɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ sũ ni tamɔ tsei ahe sũ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. They suck out the leaf juices, causing the leaves to grow twisted and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off the plant before producing any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔtɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop early mostly because tiny insects like flower thrips feed on the tender buds before pollination happens. When the flower tissues are damaged by these insects, the plant drops the flower instead of growing a pod.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi mra yɛ fã ko ni da mli ejaakɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛhe ŋmeii. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fite fɔfɔi ahe fãji lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This rotting is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering. When the soil swings between very dry and soaked, the roots cannot push calcium into the tip of the growing tomato.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni efɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ calcium kɛya tomatoi ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted, short, and bumpy instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eyɛ kuku, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil to push straight downward as they expand. If the soil is hard, compacted, or full of stones, the growing tuber gets blocked and is forced to bend into awkward shapes.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ekɛtsi kɛya shi be mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ, Atsiɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkoto amɛhe ni amɛfee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei.

english: Is it better for me to plant all my cocoa trees together on one large land or spread them across small scattered plots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ agbo kome nɔ loo magbɛ amɛ mashwã shikpɔji bibii anɔ? gbɛ?

english: Planting on one large, continuous land makes farm management much easier because you spend less time moving between plots, and it is easier to spray, weed, and harvest efficiently. Scattered plots can help protect you if disease strikes one area, but they require much more labor and transportation effort.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ hei wuji ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okɛ be fioo pɛ nyiɛɔ shikpɔji lɛ ateŋ. Ni ewaaa akɛ aaafɔse, aaakpa jwɛi ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔji ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu ohe kɛji hela ba he kome. Shi ebiɔ nitsumɔ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo koni akɛwo mli.

english: How do I know how many cocoa seedlings I should plant on one acre of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: For standard cocoa planting in Ghana, recommended spacing is 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet). Using this spacing, one acre of land will take roughly 435 cocoa seedlings, which gives each tree enough space to spread its roots and leaves without fighting for light and nutrients.
ga: Kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Kɛ akɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ nɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre 1 lɛ baafee nɔ ni baafee kookoo dumɔwui aaafee 435. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ eshwã ni ekɛ la kɛ niyenii he akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct heat and sunlight, which dries out their leaves and burns them. They require temporary shade crops like plantains and permanent shade trees to shelter them and keep the ground cool until they develop a full canopy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains kɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa daa koni amɛná he ko ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaaná ŋwɛi ŋta ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods grow directly out of the thick tree trunk instead of the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsei niji amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally exhibit a growth habit where flowers and pods emerge directly from the mature wood of the main trunk and heavy branches. This allows the tree to safely support the heavy weight of full cocoa pods, which would snap smaller, soft twigs.
ga: Cocoa tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli su ko ni haa amɛdaraa. he ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ tso ni eda ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli kɛ tsei niji ni tsii waa lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekwɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baaha niji bibii lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small extra stems growing at the bottom of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ shweremɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Those extra stems, called suckers or chupons, drain food, water, and energy away from the main trunk of the cocoa tree. Removing them keeps the tree strong and ensures all soil nutrients go toward growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo chupons. Ejieɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ebaawaje tso lɛ, ni ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ adara ni etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How many years must I wait after planting cocoa before the trees start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani aduɔ kookoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years with good care. Traditional cocoa varieties take longer, usually between 4 to 5 years before you get your first major harvest.
ga: Cocoa henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kusum nifeemɔi ni kɔɔ kookoo he lɛ heɔ be babaoo, bei pii lɛ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani onine shɛɔ oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but many of them dry up and drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi amɛteŋ babaoo gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally drops many of its flowers if it suffers from water stress, nutrient shortage, or excessive heat. The tree drops excess flowers to protect itself so it only carries the amount of pods its current energy levels can support.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi babaoo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. niyenii ni esaaa loo dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛbu ehe he. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ehiɛ pods ayibɔ ni hewalɛ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ pɛ.

english: Can I intercrop cassava with my young cocoa trees, or will it harm them?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ adu ŋmei? Aloo ebaaye kookoo tso lɛ awui loo ebaayeee lɛ awui?

english: Cassava is not recommended for intercropping with young cocoa because its heavy roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients and water, and its leafy shade can overpower cocoa seedlings. Plantain is a much better choice because it provides shade without choking the cocoa.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ kookoo bibii adu ŋmei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi ni tsii lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ni baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ baanyɛ aye kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kunim. Plantains ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo be ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwieee kookoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal organism that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded environments. During heavy rains, water droplets spread the fungus across pods, which is why pruning excess shade and clearing weeds helps air flow and reduces pod rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ ni ehaa pod lɛ mli fitemɔ baa shi lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees during the dry Harmattan season, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe?

english: During Harmattan, dry winds suck moisture from the soil and leaves, causing cocoa trees to drop leaves to conserve water. You can protect young trees by placing dry grass or crop leaves around their base as mulch to trap soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ amli. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he. Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛbaabɔle shishi lɛ he akɛ mulch koni ekɛha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves can be a sign that your tree is lacking essential nutrients in the soil, getting too much direct sunlight without enough shade, or suffering from root damage caused by waterlogged soil or pests.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ otso lɛ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. aloo ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark, and humid conditions. High moisture and poor airflow inside the farm allow the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, duŋ, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: If I cut a diseased pod off my tree, can it still infect my other healthy trees?
ga: Kɛji mifo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Ani ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba mitsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: Yes, if the sick pod is left lying on the farm floor, rain drops splashing on it or crawling ants can carry the disease spores onto nearby healthy trees. You should remove sick pods from the farm and bury or burn them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ashi helatsɛmɛi pods yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai awo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛfu loo oshã.

english: What signs should I look for when walking through my farm to catch crop sickness early?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ matao beni mitsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra?

english: Look out for dark spots on leaves or pods, wilting shoots, unusual white powdery growth, or small holes made by insects. Catching these signs early helps you remove infected parts before the sickness spreads to the whole farm.
ga: Taomɔ hei diji yɛ baai loo ŋmeii anɔ, ŋmeii ni egbo, kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo eyɛ bu bibioo ko ni kooloi kɛbaa Okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ mli mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ojie hei ni hela lɛ emɔ bo lɛ dani hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees exposed to excessive sun will show scorched, dry brown edges on their leaves, stunted growth, and pale or yellowish leaves because direct heat dries them out faster than their young roots can take up water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ babaoo lɛ baaná ŋmeii ni egbi yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. stunted growth Ni baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli baa lɛ baaha cacao tso lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Shade trees protect cocoa trees from harsh direct heat, help keep moisture in the soil, shield the trees from strong winds, and create a cooler climate that reduces overall plant stress.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe haomɔ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad if my cocoa tree branches grow too thick and overlap with each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mi-kookoo niji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni amɛkpã amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowded branches block sunlight and fresh air from moving through the farm. This creates a damp, dark environment where fungal diseases like Black Pod and pests thrive.
ga: Niji ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Does leaving heavy weeds around the base of my cocoa trees bring disease to the farm?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mli ewo muji ni ashiɔ yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ baaha hela aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, tall weeds steal nutrients and water from your cocoa trees while trapping damp air around the trunk, creating ideal conditions for pests and fungal diseases to survive and multiply.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni amɛbɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ ashihilɛ kɛ amɛfɔmɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects gather on the young green shoots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Insects such as mirids or capsids feed on the sap inside fresh shoots and young pods. Their feeding leaves small wounds on the bark, which can dry out shoots and create openings for infections.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids loo capsids yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Amɛ niyenii haa pilamɔi bibii yɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni eha helai aba.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: While a tree naturally produces more flowers than it can feed, excessive flower dropping occurs if the tree is stressed by drought, lacks nutrients in the soil, or if there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye moŋ, Shi fɔfɔi ni baa shi fe nine lɛ baaba kɛji hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing all the plants to remain small and weak instead of producing a good yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a corn plant usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil that helps leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or lack of water, as the plant tries to save energy to survive rather than produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to catch more sunlight and air, which helps the plant manufacture more food to build larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes little holes in my maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ni muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing shoot of the maize plant during the day and eats the leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why should I spread dry grass and leaves around the base of my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai mabɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool, trapping moisture so you water less, and preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Does pushing cassava stems upright into the ground produce better tubers than laying them flat?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei ni atsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba fe ni akɛ amɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems upright or at an angle forces roots to grow deeper into the soil, helping the plant find water during dry weather and produce stronger tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ shi ja loo yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa cassava tso lɛ ni enaa nu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ amli waa.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get eaten by tiny insects when I store them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mijie amɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils thrive if grains are stored while still holding moisture; thoroughly drying grains in the sun and storing them in airtight bags stops insects from breeding.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ adara kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to be mli ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto vacuum kotokui amli koni kooloi akafɔ.

english: Why do maize prices usually jump so high during certain times of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara yaa hiɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Crop prices rise when harvest season ends and grain becomes scarce. Right after the main harvest, markets are full of maize so prices drop, but during the lean dry season, less maize is available while people still need to eat, driving prices up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ajara yaa hiɛ kɛ́ kpamɔ be lɛ ba naagbee ni ŋmaa faaa. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Jara lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa. No hewɔ lɛ, jara lɛ ba shi. Shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, yibɔ lɛ faaa. Abɛi fioo pɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ be mli ni ehe hiaa ni gbɔmɛi aye nii lolo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: Where do traders take the maize that they buy from rural farming villages?
ga: Nɛgbɛ jarayelɔi kɛ ŋmãa ni amɛheɔ kɛjɛɔ akrowai amli okwaayeli akrowai amli lɛ yaa?

english: Traders aggregate maize from rural farms and transport it to large urban consumer markets like Kumasi, Accra, or Techiman, as well as to commercial poultry feed manufacturers and food processing factories.
ga: Jarayelɔi buaa ŋmãa naa kɛjɛɔ akrowai amli ŋmɔji amli ni amɛkɛyaa jarayelɔi ajarayelihei ni yɔɔ maji wuji tamɔ Kumasi, Accra loo Techiman, kɛ agbɛnɛ jarayeli kooloi aniyenii afeelɔi kɛ niyenii ahe nitsumɔhei.

english: Why does maize come into our local markets from different regions at different months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jɛɔ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ baa wɔ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ? Daa nyɔŋ nɔ?

english: Ghana has different rainfall belts. The southern regions harvest early in the year, while the northern regions harvest later, so markets receive fresh maize continuously from whichever region is currently harvesting.
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ baakpa nii yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli. Yɛ be mli ni kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ baakpa nii fiofio lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jara lɛ baaná ŋmãa hee ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested crops right on my farm or take them to a big town market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mikɛya jara nɔ yɛ maŋ wulu ko mli?

english: Selling on the farm saves you transport costs and effort, but local buyers offer lower prices. Taking your crop to a major town market gives you higher prices, provided the extra profit is more than your transport expenses.
ga: Okwaafoi ahɔ̃ɔmɔ haa okɛ shika baa shi yɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ he. Shi mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii tee jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji wuji amli lɛ, ebaaha oná jara ni nɔ kwɔ. Kɛji akɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni fata he lɛ baafee nɔ ni fe shika ni okɛmajeɔ lɛ.

english: How can I safely store my harvested maize so I can wait and sell it when prices go up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni mamɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ kɛji jara lɛ tee hiɛ?

english: To store maize safely without insects or rot destroying it, dry the grains thoroughly until they are very hard, store them in airtight (hermetic) bags or treated sacks, and keep them elevated off the floor in a cool, dry room.
ga: Koni akɛ ŋmãa ato shweshweeshwe ni kooloi bibii loo ŋmãa ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Kɛto kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) loo kotoku ni atsa mli lɛ mli. ni ewó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or grow mold so quickly if I bag it right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji mikɛwo baagi mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize contains moisture. If bagged wet, heat builds up inside the bag, creating the perfect condition for mold and dangerous toxins to grow, which ruins the grain quality for buyers.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ mli edɔ. Kɛji kotoku lɛ mli fũ lɛ, dɔlɛ baabua kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ baafite ŋmaa lɛ kpakpa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ.

english: How does the price of maize affect the cost of livestock and chicken feed?
ga: Te ŋmãa jara lɛ saa kooloi kɛ kooloi aniyenii ahe jara he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Maize is the main ingredient in animal feed. When maize is abundant and cheap after harvest, feed prices fall, but when maize is scarce and expensive, feed prices go up automatically.
ga: Abɛi ji nɔ titri ni akɛwoɔ kooloi aniyenii mli. Beni ŋmãa fa ni ejara waaa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ Kooloi aniyenii jara baa shi. Shi kɛ́ ŋmãa faaa ni ejara wa lɛ, kooloi aniyenii jara baaya hiɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How can I time my crop planting so I harvest when market prices are highest for major holidays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee be ni mikɛbaakpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ yɛ gbijurɔyelii wuji amli lɛ?

english: Calculate the exact growing period of your crop variety and plant so maturity aligns with peak demand periods, such as late December or Easter, when households and caterers buy large quantities of food.
ga: Buu be pɔtɛɛ ni otsei kɛ tsei lɛ daa lɛ he akɔntaa. Enɛ ji koni akwɛ akɛ dalɛ lɛ kɛ bei ni nibii babaoo taoɔ lɛ akpã gbee, tamɔ December naagbee loo Easter. he ni shiabii kɛ mɛi ni feɔ niyenii lɛ heɔ niyenii babaoo yɛ lɛ

english: Why do early-season rains help farmers get a much better price for their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa amɛ ŋmãa lɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting early with the first reliable rains allows you to harvest ahead of the majority of farmers, letting you sell your crop when market supply is low and buyers are willing to pay premium prices.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ haa onáa ŋmaa kpakpa fe okwaafoi babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do some farmers get many more bags of maize per acre than others in the same district?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi naa ŋmãa kotokui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Higher yields depend on using certified high-yielding seeds, planting at correct spacing, applying the right fertilizer at the right growth stages, and clearing weeds early so they do not steal nutrients from the crop.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I clear my farm without burning the bush first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni mikɛshãaa jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful soil organisms like earthworms. Clearing without burning leaves organic materials to decay naturally, keeping the soil fertile and moist for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does putting dried animal dung on my farm help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Animal dung works as a natural fertilizer. It slowly releases essential nutrients into the ground and improves the soil's structure so it can hold water better during dry spells.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in waterlogged ground. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks steady water, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like calcium. Keeping the moisture balanced helps fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu daa Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii titrii tamɔ calcium bɛ lɛ, nu ni mli edɔ ni sa ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ shi.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make food for the plant efficiently, which helps produce larger, healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that provide temporary shade and moisture to protect the tender cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant varieties is the best way to stop this.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ Ekɛ ŋmei mosaic hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛbaa ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ helai ahe lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpa enɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing funnels of maize. Spraying neem leaf extract or recommended biopesticides early can save your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni onibii akafite.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to take up water and nutrients quickly. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the food, light, and water your crops need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaaha amɛkaju niyenii, kane, kɛ nu ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds once the rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is safest to plant after the ground has received two or three heavy rains. This ensures the soil holds enough deep moisture so young seedlings will not dry out if the rain pauses.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii ji beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ egbiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ.

english: Why can't I just use my standard cutlass to collect rubber latex from my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ dagger ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ atsu nii kɛbua tsei amli nu lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Standard cutlasses are too thick and coarse, which can deep-wound the tree's wood. Rubber trees require special curved tapping knives to slice thin shavings of bark cleanly without damaging the inner growing layer.
ga: Daggers ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni baanyɛ abote tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ Rɔba tsei biɔ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛtswaa tsei lɛ koni akɛfo tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ. Ha ehe atse ni okafite ŋtayaa ni miida yɛ mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my young rubber trees are mature enough to start producing sap?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-rɔba tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi latɛs feemɔ?

english: Rubber trees are usually mature enough for tapping around 5 to 7 years after planting, when the trunk reaches about 50 centimeters in circumference at waist height.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atswa amɛ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ, beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ shɛɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 50 yɛ ebɔlemɔ he yɛ etsitsi nɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to tree crops when they grow too old to produce good yields?
ga: Mɛni baa tsei anɔ kɛ́ amɛdara tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: When mature trees like rubber reach 25 to 30 years old, their sap production drops significantly. At this stage, farmers harvest the timber to sell for wood and clear the land to plant new seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ni eda tamɔ tsei bibii lɛ ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ kpataa tsei lɛ koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkɛdu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why do my young trees stretch tall and thin instead of growing thick trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso bibioo lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tso ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, they compete for light and focus all their energy growing upward toward the sun rather than developing strong, thick trunks.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la mli akaŋ ni amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni teɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ hulu lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e wa nɛ e peeɔ tso nɛ he wa nɛ e mi wa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend cutting off lower branches from young tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei bibii lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches directs plant energy into developing a tall, solid main stem and healthy upper foliage, which makes harvesting trunk crops like rubber sap much easier.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛ tso titri ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ ŋwɛi baai ni wa aba. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ rɔba lɛ akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why don't farmers use large harvesting machines on tree plantations instead of working by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ tsɔnei wuji ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ tsuuu nii yɛ amɛ tsei aŋmɔji amli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ baatsu nitsumɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting products like rubber sap requires human precision to make delicate cuts that do not kill the tree, which heavy machinery cannot handle carefully enough.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa tamɔ rɔba lɛ biɔ adesa pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbeee tso lɛ mli. he ni anyɛɛɛ atsu tsɔnei ni tsii ahe nii jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa lɛ

english: Does cutting the bark of a tree continuously kill it over time?
ga: Ani tso lɛ yibii ni afoɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ gbeɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: If done correctly with special tools, removing thin bark layers does not harm the tree because bark naturally grows back and regenerates over several years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdadei krɛdɛɛi anɔ. Hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ jiemɔ Eyeŋ tso lɛ awui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaafee ehee yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava between my newly planted rubber trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei yɛ rɔbɔt tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first two to three years while tree seedlings are small, you can grow food crops between the rows to maximize land use and prevent weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii babaoo ni atsĩ jwɛi anaa.

english: Why do rubber trees shed all their leaves at the same time during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ shikome yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural survival response called leaf wintering where the tree drops leaves to conserve water during dry weather before sprouting fresh new foliage.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɛ̃i be mli shwiemɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ dani amɛbaaji heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Who is responsible for paying to clear and cut old tree stumps when starting a new farm?
ga: Namɔ ji mɔ ni kwɛɔ shika ni akɛjieɔ tsei momoi ni afoɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ aje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: The landowner or farmer usually bears the cost of clearing old trees and preparing the field, though selling the cut timber can help cover those expenses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋtsɛ loo okwaafonyo lɛ ji mɔ ni woɔ shika ni akɛjieɔ tsei momoi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ kɛha nidumɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso ni afo lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni awo nakai nyɔmɔwoo lɛ he nyɔmɔ moŋ.

english: Is it bad for me to plant my crop seeds immediately after a very heavy rain?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ waa waa sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away light seeds or compact the soil so tightly that young shoots cannot push through. It is best to wait until the topsoil is moist but not muddy so seeds get the air and water they need to germinate properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo ŋmaa bibii kɛya. Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔ he waa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akabote mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ shi efeee muji. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni he hia amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when there is no rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area exposed to the hot sun. This helps the plant conserve water and prevent drying out until it receives rainfall or irrigation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛba baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa amɛgbi kɛyashi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nu shwieɔ amɛnɔ.

english: If heavy rain falls while my crops are flowering, will it destroy my harvest?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ Ani ebaakpata miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Heavy downpours during flowering can wash pollen off the blossoms before wind or bees can spread it, which prevents fruits or seeds from forming properly and reduces your total yield.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani kɔɔyɔɔ loo ŋmeii baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haaa aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ afee jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: What happens to my crops if I irrigate them in the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hottest?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli shwane be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering under direct hot sun causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching root level, and hot surface water can shock tender crop roots. It is best to irrigate early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ la dani eshɛ shishifã lɛ he. Ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpokpo tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if my vegetables are getting too much water from irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-vegetables lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops get too much water, their roots suffocate from lack of air, causing leaves to turn pale yellow, soft, and droopy. Soil that stays constantly soaked will also cause the roots to rot.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hu baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and hard if the soil remains dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe wa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra food and moisture in its roots. When the soil stays dry for long periods, the plant uses up its stored food energy just to survive rather than expanding its tubers.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ Tsei kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo bulbs.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get excessively hot or when soil water levels change abruptly from very dry to soaked, causing stress that prevents fruit setup.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni haaa aduawai lɛ akpɛtɛ lɛ baa.

english: Is it safe for me to apply fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash fertilizer away from the farm into streams or push it too deep into the soil where crop roots cannot reach it. Fertilizer should be applied when soil is moist but not right before a downpour.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa faai amli. Aloo tsimɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ yɛ he ni tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee dani nugbɔ anɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow lots of tall green leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Bean plants that receive excess water or too much nitrogen fertilizer spend all their energy producing leafy green stems instead of developing blossoms and seed pods.
ga: Bean tsei ni nine shɛɔ nu babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Constant rain and wet weather create high humidity that encourages Black Pod fungal disease to spread quickly, especially on cocoa trees that do not get enough sunlight or air circulation.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa. Enɛ woɔ black pod fungal hela lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ kookoo tsei ni hulu la loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen feeds leaf growth, so when the plant runs low, it steals nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Excess water fills the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots. Without oxygen, fungal diseases thrive in the waterlogged dirt and rot the tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji oxygen bɛ Fungal helai daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa bulbs lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Curled yellow leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading viral diseases, or by severe heat stress when the plant is trying to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli haomɔ mli beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil place heavy stress on pepper plants. They drop their flowers to save water and energy just to survive, rather than spending that energy producing peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa pepper tsei anɔ. Amɛkɛ fɔfɔii woɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ jamɛ a he wami ɔ peeɔ chili peppers.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small shoots to grow around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many side shoots compete with the main stem for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Cutting back extra shoots leaves energy for the main stem to produce a big, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Side shoots babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso wulu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli koni ekɛfee plantains akui wuji ni he wa.

english: Why do so many of my cocoa flowers fall off without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ babaoo miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can feed. Many drop off because of dry spells, lack of soil nutrients, or because insects did not pollinate them in time.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Amɛteŋ mɛi pii gbee shi yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii lɛ efeee pollinate yɛ be ni sa mli hewɔ?

english: Why does weed grass come back so fast after I clear my farmland with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba oya beni mikɛ dade lɛ jie ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting grass at ground level leaves the roots alive inside the soil. To slow down weed growth, you need to turn the soil or remove the root systems completely.
ga: Jwɛi ni afoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni jwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo Ehe miihia ni otsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ojie shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it best for me to apply chemical fertilizer right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baafata he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Heavy rain downpours wash away fertilizer off the topsoil before plant roots can drink it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but not right before heavy rain.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa.

english: Why do some of my saved grain seeds fail to sprout when I plant them next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in warm or humid places lose their stored energy or develop mold inside. Seeds must be thoroughly dried and stored in sealed, cool containers to stay alive for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato yɛ hei ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ato lɛ loo ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsinsii ni mli ejɔ, ni atsĩ naa mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why are insects attacking my mangoes before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi mangoi lɛ dani amɛshwereɔ po lɛ?

english: Insects like fruit flies are attracted to the smell and softness of growing mangoes. They pierce the fruit skin to lay eggs inside, which causes the fruit to rot and drop early before ripening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango ni miida lɛ he muji kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbalaa koolooi, tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii. Amɛfoɔ aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli koni amɛwo wɔji yɛ mli. Enɛ ɔ haa nɛ yiblii ɔ puɛɔ nɛ e gbleeɔ oya loko e waa.

english: How do spray chemicals protect my crop from being ruined by bugs?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni kooloi akafite amɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crop protection chemicals act like a protective shield; some stay on the outside of the plant to drive insects away, while others are absorbed by the plant to kill pests when they try to bite the leaves or fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ tsei ahe. Mɛi komɛi hiɔ tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ koni amɛshwie kooloi bibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei shwieɔ ekrokomɛi anɔ koni amɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ́ amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye baai loo aduawai lɛ.

english: Why is it important to start protecting my fruit trees before I even see insects on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahebuu dani mana kooloi bibii yɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Many insect pests lay invisible eggs inside young fruits and flowers. If you wait until you see the damage, the insects are already inside the fruit and it is too late to save that harvest.
ga: Kooloi bibii babaoo woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ aduawai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi amli. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi ona nɔ ni efite lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloo lɛ ebote aduawai lɛ amli. Ni etsɛ tsɔ ni abaahere nakai nifeemɔ lɛ yiwala.

english: What does fertilizer actually do inside my crops to make them yield better?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe? kɛha nitsumɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: Fertilizer acts like food for the plant, supplying key minerals like nitrogen and potassium that the soil may lack. These nutrients help the crop build strong stems, healthy green leaves, and big, sweet fruits.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei aniyenii. Ehaa shika tsuru nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium ni ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ. Nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa. baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ aduawai wuji ni ŋɔɔ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding the right fertilizer helps the plant make green chlorophyll, which it uses to feed itself from sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil eŋɔli ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛjɛ hulu la mli.

english: Can I use the same type of fertilizer for my fruit trees as I use for my grain crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mi-cereal tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii?

english: Different crops have different needs; grains need high nitrogen early on for leaves, while fruit trees like mangoes need more potassium to form strong blossoms and heavy, sweet fruits.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ hiamɔ nii srɔtoi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa mra kɛha amɛbaai lɛ, yɛ be mli ni aduawai tsei tamɔ mango he hiaa potassium babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my mango trees produce plenty of flowers but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Mango trees often lose blossoms due to insect attacks, fungal diseases, or lack of water. Protecting the flowers from pests and stress helps them stay on the branch and turn into full-sized fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui, tsɛŋemɔ hela, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ haomɔi ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do some of my fruits look healthy on the outside but turn black and soft inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ kponɔgbɛ shi amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ mligbɛ lɛ?

english: This usually happens when tiny fly larvae hatch inside the fruit while it is still on the tree. The maggots feed on the flesh, causing the inside to rot even if the skin looks normal at first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwere. Kpɔ̃ɔ aduawai lɛ amli be mli ni oyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ loo lɛ, ni no haa emli lɛ fiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shishijee lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I leave weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; they steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants weak and unable to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Does putting extra effort into pruning and caring for young trees really make a difference years later?
ga: Mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishitsɔɔmɔ kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli. Ani ebaaha tsakemɔ aba diɛŋtsɛ yɛ afii komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Yes, caring for young trees builds a strong foundation. Pruning dead branches and controlling pests early creates a healthy trunk structure that can support much heavier fruit yields for many years.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei bibii akwɛmɔ. Ebaama shishitoo ni wa ema shi. Niji ni egboi lɛ afolɔmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui mra Ehaa tso lɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii babaoo afii babaoo.

english: How can I clear weeds around my fruit trees without damaging their roots?
ga: Majie jwɛi kɛjɛ he ni ebɔle he lɛ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akwɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ efiteee?

english: Use shallow weeding with a cutlass or apply mulching near the trunk rather than digging deep. Fruit trees have delicate feeding roots close to the surface that can be cut or stressed if the soil around them is disturbed deeply.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmeii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Aloo ha shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni oootsa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yibii tsei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yeɔ niyenii ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. ni abaanyɛ afo loo atswa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ gbala mli waa

english: Why does the ground under a large tree trunk stay soft and moist while the open field dries out quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli gbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: The wide canopy of leaves acts as a natural roof that blocks direct sunlight, lowering soil temperature and slowing down water evaporation so the soil beneath stays cool and moist.
ga: Kpoji ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli kpãa ni tsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahi shi ni edɔ ni edɔ.

english: How do I know if the roots of my young tree are growing well underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell by watching the upper part of the plant; when a young tree consistently sprouts fresh, healthy new leaves and strong stems, it means the root system below is established and absorbing water properly.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ tsei bibii lɛ, baai heei ni mli wa kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa lɛ dara pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ efee jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmɔɔ nu.

english: Why are my mango tree's new leaves reddish-brown instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is a natural stage of growth called flushing. The young reddish leaves contain protective compounds that shield the soft new growth from strong sunlight until the leaves mature and turn dark green.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dalɛ fã ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching. Nibii ni buɔ tso hee ni eda ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ baai tsuji bibii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my fruit trees drop many of their old leaves just before new shoots appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso yibii lɛ miiho baai momoi babaoo dani ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Trees naturally shed old or worn-out leaves to save energy and water, allowing the plant to direct its nutrients into growing fresh, healthy new foliage.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ loo ni efite lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ baa heei, ehee, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Should I prune old branches from my tree to help new leaves grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tso lɛ niji momoi lɛ koni baai heei akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, pruning away dead or overgrown branches allows sunlight and air to reach the inner canopy, encouraging the tree to sprout strong new leaves and fruiting branches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafolɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mligbɛ. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niji ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why is it helpful to leave a few big trees standing in my crop farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi tsei wuji fioo komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mature trees provide windbreaks, create protective shade for young shade-loving crops, and shed leaves that decompose into natural organic matter to nourish your soil.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo. kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii

english: Why shouldn't I plant small crops too close to the base of a giant tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ tsei wuji ashishi tsɔ lɛ?
