english: The thick root system of a large tree will pull most of the water and nutrients out of the surrounding soil, making it hard for small crops planted right under it to compete and grow well.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei bibii ni adu yɛ shishi lɛ akɛ amɛaaye akaŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it good to cover the soil around my tree trunks with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ akɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, protects surface roots from heat, traps moisture in the soil, and slowly rots into nutrient-rich compost.
ga: Hɛɛ, ale shikpɔŋ ni akɛ tsei ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt when people walk frequently over the soil near their bases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ gbɔmɛi nyiɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Constant heavy foot traffic packs the soil down tightly, squishing out air spaces and crushing the small surface roots that the plant needs to drink water and breathe.
ga: Gbɛfaa babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Mimɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli ni okɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ atswa. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei anu nu ni amɛmu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I cut down all the big forest trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni mifoɔ koo mli tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally thrive in forest environments. Big forest trees shade cocoa from hot direct sunlight, reduce heat stress, and help soil retain moisture so cocoa trees can focus energy on producing healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo mli shihilɛi amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight. Without taller trees to provide shade, direct sun causes sunburn on the leaves and dries up the water in the soil, causing leaves to turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei kakadaji ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Will my cocoa trees die sooner if I remove all the native wild trees from my farmland?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baagboi mra kɛji mijie maŋbii koo mli tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, unshaded cocoa trees grow fast initially but burn out quickly, often dying or losing productivity after 10 to 15 years. Cocoa grown under partial forest shade can live and produce pods for 30 to 40 years or more.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni bɛ hulutsoo lɛ daa oya yɛ shishijee mli, shi amɛgboiɔ oya, bei pii lɛ amɛgboiɔ loo amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 15 sɛɛ. Cocoa ni aduɔ yɛ koo lɛ fã ko shishi lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why does cocoa grow so much better on land that was recently dense forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni kooi babaoo yɔɔ mli nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: Forest soil is rich in organic matter from fallen leaves and decomposed plant material. This rich soil feeds cocoa roots naturally and acts like a sponge to hold water during dry periods.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ amli babaoo. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ nɛɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa kookoo shishifãi lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: How do large forest trees protect my crops during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ koo mli tsei wuji bu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Large trees create a cooler microclimate under their canopy. They block hot, dry Harmattan winds from drying out crop leaves and slow down water evaporation from the soil.
ga: Tsei wuji haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi. Amɛtsiɔ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekaha tsei ahe baai lɛ agbi, ni amɛhaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why are extension officers advising us to leave some big trees standing when clearing fresh land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashi tsei wuji beni asaa shikpɔŋ hee kɛha dumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Leaving selected shade trees preserves the natural forest structure that cocoa needs to thrive, prevents soil erosion, and maintains humidity essential for crop survival.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ehaa koo lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli nibii ni he hiaa ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɔ shi. Tsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni okwɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do bug pests seem to attack my cocoa farm more when there are no large forest trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei wuji bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Forest trees provide habitats for birds, ants, and beneficial insects that naturally eat crop pests like mirids (capsids). Completely clearing forest trees removes these natural pest controllers.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ ahiɔ. Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ koo lɛ mli kwraa lɛ baajie nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ kɛya.

english: How do forest shade trees help reduce weed growth on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni haa jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Thick shade from tall forest tree canopies blocks direct light from reaching the ground, which prevents light-loving weeds from sprouting quickly and competing with your crops.
ga: Shade ni mli tse ni jɛɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ tsiɔ la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi ni sumɔɔ la lɛ akakwɛ̃ oya ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaye akaŋ.

english: Why is it better for farmers in my village to work together when managing forest trees and clearing land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ baafee ekome kɛkwɛ koo mli tsei anɔ ni amɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Working together allows farmers to coordinate shade levels across neighboring farms, prevent widespread deforestation, and share heavy labor like pruning large forest branches safely.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ feɔ shade yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Tsi kooi ni afolɔ ashwie shi babaoo lɛ naa. ni amɛjara nitsumɔi ni tsii tamɔ tsei ni afoɔ yɛ kooi wuji amli lɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How does preserving forest cover on my farm benefit my neighboring farmers' crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mibuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ anibii lɛ?

english: Forest cover keeps local air cool and moist across an entire community. If every farmer cuts down all their trees, the surrounding region becomes hotter and drier, harming crops on nearby farms as well.
ga: Kooi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji okwaafoi fɛɛ fo amɛtsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ He ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ baafee dɔlɛ ni edɔ waa. Enɛ náa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hu anɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii.

english: How often should I water my newly transplanted fruit crops during their first few days?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi tso yibii ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Newly planted fruit crops need intensive care for the first two days, requiring water twice a day—once in the morning and once in the evening—to help them settle into the soil.
ga: Yibii tsei ni adu ehee lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni awo amɛ nu shii enyɔ daa gbi—ekoŋŋ leebi kɛ shikome gbɛkɛ—koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it recommended to water my crops in the morning and evening rather than the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Watering in the cool morning and late evening prevents the strong afternoon sun from evaporating the water quickly, ensuring the roots absorb enough moisture.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi kɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baatsi shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekafee nu lɛ oya. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will my fruit crops continue to need heavy watering twice a day once they get established?
ga: Ani ehe baahia ni afɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ nu waa lolo shii enyɔ daa gbi kɛji adu amɛ pɛ?

english: No, once the initial two-day establishment period passes, the crop's roots settle in and it no longer requires that much water to stay healthy.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ shishijee be lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ lɛ ho lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baahi shi ni ehe ehiaaa nu babaoo dɔŋŋ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I keep giving my fruit crops high amounts of water after the first few days?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ miha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Giving too much water after the early stage can rot the roots and waste effort, because the mature plant no longer needs high amounts of moisture to grow.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli fe nine yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite ni efite mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Akɛni tso lɛ edara hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni hulutsoo be babaoo ahi enɔ dɔŋŋ koni enyɛ eda.

english: Is evening watering as beneficial as morning watering for a young fruit crop?
ga: Ani gbɛkɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ bɔ ni leebi nu ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, evening watering gives the young plant a cool night to soak up moisture without heat stress, helping it recover faster during its initial days in the field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, gbɛkɛ nu ni akɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ haa amɛnáa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ haaa amɛná haomɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do young fruit crops need so much water in the first two days after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ ni aduɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first two days are critical because the plant is experiencing stress from moving into new soil, so frequent morning and evening watering helps the roots stabilize quickly.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ lɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ tso lɛ miina haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ni eyaa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nu shwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ. Yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi oya.

english: How can I tell that my fruit crop no longer needs frequent morning and evening watering?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni mikɛ nu awo mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ shii abɔ lɛ? leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Once the initial two days of establishment have passed, the crop transitions out of its critical stage, allowing you to reduce watering to a regular, lower frequency.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ ni ato shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ shihilɛ ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Ehaa okɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi kɛyaa nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni baa shi shii abɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is good management so important when starting out with fruit crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa he hiaa beni ajeɔ aduawai adumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Good management ensures you give the plant heavy attention when it is vulnerable—such as early double-daily watering—and then scale back appropriately so you do not waste resources.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa haa okwɛɔ otsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛyɛ oshara mli, tamɔ nu ni oooha amɛ shii enyɔ daa gbi dani be lɛ ashɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsakemɔ elɛɛmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa koni okafite nibii.

english: Can missing watering sessions in the first two days harm my newly planted fruit crop?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛhaaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná tso yibii ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Yes, young fruit plants have delicate roots right after planting. Skipping morning or evening care during those critical first two days can cause the plant to dry out and fail to take root.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, aduawai tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie leebi loo gbɛkɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii enyɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbi ni enyɛŋ ewo shishifãi.

english: Why does morning watering specifically help my fruit plants perform better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mihe leebi lɛ titri yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Morning watering hydrates the crop right before the heat of the day hits, giving the plant the strength it needs to endure sunshine without wilting.
ga: Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ leebi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani latsaa lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hulu la ni amɛgbooo.

english: Why do my rice plants grow well in standing water, but my maize plants rot if water stays on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani mi-abele tsei lɛ baagbo kɛji nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo?

english: Rice plants have special internal pathways that carry air from their leaves down to their roots underwater, while maize roots need oxygen directly from dry soil air pockets and will suffocate if submerged for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi biɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni egbi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli. ni ebaagbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ awo lɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: Is it okay for me to use water mixed with salt or chemicals to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mikɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofai baawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: No, crops need fresh water because salt pulls moisture out of the roots instead of feeding them, which burns the leaves and stops the plant from absorbing nutrients from the soil.
ga: Dabi, nu kpakpa he miihia tsei ejaakɛ ŋmei gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii. Enɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to build raised soil ridges or earthen walls across our fields before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔma shikpɔŋ ŋmɔji ni awó nɔ loo shikpɔŋ gbogboi yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli dani wɔdu nii lɛ?

english: Building raised soil embankments or ridges helps trap fresh rainwater for your crops to use while preventing heavy floodwaters from washing away your topsoil and drowning root systems.
ga: Berms loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ ni aaafee lɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ nu kpakpa ahi shi koni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu afua ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekashwie shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ akawo nu mli.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop most of its leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss, allowing the plant to rest and keep its tubers alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen; the plant is taking the small amount of nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the young green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ miitsu nii ni ekɛmiiha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy rather than trying to form fruit it cannot support.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ha tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Mohu ɔ, bɔ mɔde nɛ o pee yiblii nɛ e be nyɛe maa ye bua.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight, so they require larger trees to provide shade and maintain a humid environment until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená tsei wuji ni baaha ená hulutsoo ni eha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, wasting energy stretching tall to reach the sun instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni shɛɔ hulu lɛ he fɛɛ lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal essential plant food and fertilizer from the soil before your crops' roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ tso niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Removing small side branches forces the plant to send its food and water directly into growing bigger, healthier fruits rather than creating extra leaves you do not need.
ga: niji bibii amlijaa Side-out haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii kɛ nu gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa bo.

english: What actually causes the 'kube yiyare' disease that kills coconut trees in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ‘kube yiyare’ hela ni gbeɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ Ghana lɛ baa?

english: Kube yiyare' (Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease) is caused by microscopic organisms called phytoplasmas, which infect the inner transport system of coconut palms and block water and nutrients from reaching the top.
ga: Nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ phytoplasmas lɛ kɛ ‘Kube yiyare’ (Cape St. ni yeɔ hela yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni ehaa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shɛɛɛ ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: Where did the name Cape Saint Paul Wilt Disease come from for this coconut sickness?
ga: Nɛgbɛ gbɛi ni ji Cape Saint Paul Wilt Hela lɛ jɛ kɛha nɛkɛ ŋmei hela nɛɛ?

english: The disease was named after Cape Saint Paul near Woe in the Volta Region of Ghana, where agricultural officers first recorded and identified the sickness in coconut palms in 1932.
ga: Akɛ Cape Saint Paul ni bɛŋkɛ Woe yɛ Volta Kpokpaa ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ nɔ lɛ wo hela nɛɛ gbɛi. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he onukpai ŋma helai okadii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ amɛshwie shi ni amɛna klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ afi 1932 mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut tree turning yellow and drying up from the bottom upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When a coconut palm catches a wilt disease, the infection chokes its water pathways, causing the oldest bottom leaves to turn yellow and die off first as the tree tries to survive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ye wilt hela lɛ Hela lɛ tsiɔ nu gbɛi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why do my coconut trees suddenly drop all their young, immature nuts onto the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii fɛɛ ni eshɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Premature nut fall occurs when a palm is under severe stress or infected by disease, forcing the tree to drop its heavy fruits to save its remaining energy and water.
ga: Nut ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ haomɔ ni naa wa shishi loo hela ko emɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni tsii koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if my coconut tree is dying from dry weather or from 'kube yiyare' disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo hela miigbe ŋmei tso ko? 'Kubeyiya'?

english: Drought affects all trees on a farm at the same time and stops when rains return, whereas 'kube yiyare' attacks trees one by one, causing nut drop and yellowing leaves that never recover even after heavy rainfall.
ga: Hɔmɔ lɛ ye tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kome mli. ekomefeemɔ mli ni ebaakpa beni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa be mli ni ‘Kube Yiyare’ tutuaa tsei lɛ ekomekomei lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛŋ atsake kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How does 'kube yiyare' spread from my neighbour's infected farm to my healthy coconut trees?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ‘Kube Yiyare’ gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee mi ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: The disease is spread by small sap-sucking insects like planthoppers that feed on diseased coconut palms and then fly to healthy trees, transmitting the infection while feeding.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ planthoppers ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. no sɛɛ lɛ efo kɛtee tso ko ni mli wa nɔ Kɛtsɔ hela lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni eyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ

english: Can small insects really cause an entire coconut tree to dry up and die?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbe ŋmei tso diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, because insects act like mosquitoes carrying malaria; when they feed on tree sap, they inject tiny disease-causing germs into the tree's veins that multiply and block moisture flow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ kooloi bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ atiridii. Kɛ amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Amɛwoɔ helai bibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ amli. kɛyaa tso lɛ fãji amli Enɛ haa efalɛ yaa hiɛ ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa.

english: Is there any chemical spray or medicine I can use to cure a coconut tree infected with 'kube yiyare'?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛtsa ‘kube yiyare’ ŋmei tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: There is currently no chemical cure for an infected coconut palm; once a tree shows symptoms, it will die, so prompt removal of infected palms is necessary to protect nearby trees.
ga: Amrɔ nɛɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa ŋmei tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛ tso ko jie hela lɛ he okadii lɛ akpo lɛ, egboɔ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya koni akɛbu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Are there coconut varieties in Ghana that are safe from getting 'kube yiyare'?
ga: Ani ŋmeii srɔtoi yɛ Ghana ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ‘kube yiyare’ he?

english: Yes, agricultural research institutes in Ghana have bred disease-resistant coconut varieties, such as specific Malayan Dwarf hybrids, which can survive and fruit in areas affected by the disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, Okwaafoi Ahe Nibii Amli Taomɔ Nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ efɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ, tamɔ Malayan dwarf hybrid lɛ. ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii yɛ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ

english: If I cut down a diseased coconut palm, can I immediately plant a new seedling in the same hole?
ga: Kɛ́ afo akokoo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ, ani abaanyɛ adu tso hee yɛ nakai bu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is best to destroy the old root system completely and plant improved disease-resistant varieties rather than planting local varieties back into the exact spot where a tree just died.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpãtã shishifãi momo lɛ ahiɛ kwraa ni adu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du tso ɔ mi tso slɔɔtoslɔɔto ɔmɛ kɛ ya he nɛ tso ɔ gbo ngɛ ɔ nyɛsɛɛ nɛ ɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that lose moisture quickly in direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to protect them from heat stress while their roots establish deep in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe tsɔi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, their underground root systems compete directly for the same soil nutrients, water, and space. Spacing cassava properly allows each plant enough root volume to expand into thick, healthy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ he kome mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni kã cassava tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my maize crops and cause the leaves to turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-abele lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that absorb nitrogen and water from the soil much faster than crop plants can. When weeds crowd your maize, they starve the crop of nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi eyi o-abele lɛ mli obɔ lɛ Nitrogen hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it really necessary for me to walk through my farm every day if I already planted and weeded?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi kɛji midu ni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli?

english: Crop conditions change rapidly due to pests, diseases, and weather. Visiting your farm daily allows you to catch early signs of pest attacks or moisture stress before they spread and cause widespread damage to your yield.
ga: Tsei ashihilɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ hewɔ. Kɛ́ oya oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo hulutsoo be lɛ miiba bo mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defensive reaction to reduce its surface area and slow down water loss in extreme heat. Watering your crops consistently at the roots helps keep the stems firm and reduces heat stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsei feɔ koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni nu lɛ fiteɔ lɛ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ, ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea roots decay, they leave behind rich, natural nitrogen fertilizer that feeds heavy crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra bottom branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing lower branches prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the leaves during rain. It also redirects the plant's energy away from producing excessive leaves and into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ akashwie baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛjɛɔ baai babaoo ni ewoɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my bean plants before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pods lɛ?

english: Bean plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden dry spells, high heat, or an over-application of heavy fertilizers. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant retain its flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Bean tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can climbing weeds kill a large tree crop if I leave them alone?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni kwɔɔ lɛ agbe tso agbo ko kɛji mishi lɛ?

english: Climbing weeds and vines grow over the canopy of host trees, blocking sunlight so the tree can no longer produce its food through its leaves. Over time, the weight and shade of the vines weaken and strangle the tree.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ wein tsei kwɔɔ kɛyaa tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ashishi, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa, ni ehaa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, wain tsei lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ kɛ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ ha tsei lɛ fee blɛoo ni efolɔ amɛnaa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plantain stems with dry grass keep the ground moist for longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic mulch creates a protective barrier against direct sunlight and wind. This slows down water evaporation from the soil, keeping root zones cooler and moist for extended periods during dry spells.
ga: Organic mulching lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in wet, humid weather. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches lets sunlight in to dry out the farm and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: This curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and infected planting stems. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by local extension officers prevents this issue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii mosaic hela. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upwards like small cups and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo lɛ? Ni atsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking sap from young leaves. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and applying safe, recommended pesticides helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in my cowpea pods and leaves before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji kɛ baai lɛ amli dani akpaa.

english: These holes are made by caterpillars and pod borers that feed on the crop. Spraying recommended treatments during the early flowering stage prevents insects from ruining the pods.
ga: Buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ pod borers ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee be lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi akafite fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea early in the plant's growth fixes this yellowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ aba. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishijee be mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni asaa nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, during dry spells, or when soil water is irregular. Regular watering early in the morning and mulching soil around the roots keeps the plants cool enough to hold fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa leebi kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over when the fruits become large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ eyibii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, so heavy fruit bunches make the tree top-heavy and easy for wind to push over. Supporting the bearing stems with sturdy wooden props prevents them from breaking or uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ aduawai akui ni tsii miimɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee tsiimɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ bɔɔlu ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans between my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mi-corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil naturally. This enriches the soil and provides extra nutrients for neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ abele lɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why do we keep water standing in paddy rice fields instead of letting it drain away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ nu toɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔbaahã efo lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers weeds so they cannot grow and compete with the rice, while also giving the rice plants the constant moisture they need to produce high yields.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ jwɛi. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ eda ni ekɛ ŋmãa abɔ akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from sprouting and becoming soft while stored in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-sweet potato ni mikpa lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni efee blɛoo be mli ni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout quickly when exposed to heat and direct sunlight. Storing tubers on raised wooden racks inside a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated barn slows down sprouting and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to burn my farm land before planting, or should I clear the bush without burning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu nii loo esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛshãaa amɛ?

english: Burning may seem fast, but it destroys the natural plant food in the ground and kills beneficial soil organisms. Clearing the bush and leaving the weeds to rot naturally turns them into rich food for your crops.
ga: Ekolɛ ebaafee tamɔ nɔ ni shãa oya. Shi efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie tsei bibii ni oha jwɛi lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee niyenii babaoo kɛha onibii.

english: Should I cut down all the large trees on my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii dumɔ?

english: No, you should leave some trees on your farm. Large trees provide shade to protect young crops from scorching sun, protect topsoil from heavy rain washing it away, and keep moisture in the ground.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi tsei lɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni hoɔ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: What should I do with all the leaves and branches I cut down when clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee baai kɛ tsei niji fɛɛ ni mifo beni mijieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Instead of burning them, chop them up and spread them over the soil between your crops. This acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, traps moisture, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your plants.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, shwiemɔ ni okɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow well when my farm soil turns into heavy mud after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ muji waa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy muddy soil gets packed very tightly, making it hard for crop roots to breathe and stretch to find water and food. Mixing dry plant leaves or animal manure into the mud loosens it up so roots can grow easily.
ga: Muji lɛ mli tsii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi loo kooloo ŋmei futu muji lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha muji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Does burning dry mud or hard clay soil make it better for growing crops?
ga: Ani sũ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ashãa lɛ haa tsei daa jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, heating soil damages its natural structure and destroys the hidden nutrients your plants need. It leaves the soil hard and lifeless, making it harder for roots to pull up food and water.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni okɛwoɔ la mli lɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ, ni efiteɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. It makes the soil hard and lifeless. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbala niyenii kɛ nu kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: How can I tell if my farm ground is too wet and muddy for planting seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ muji tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if it stays like a sticky, hard lump of mud without crumbling when gently pressed, it is too wet. Planting seeds in overly soggy mud can cause them to rot before they sprout.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ehi shi tamɔ muji ni mli wa ni etseee kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ muji ni edɔ tsɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the soil under the top layer on my land is rich enough for crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Good soil is usually dark, crumbly, and smells like fresh earth. If you dig down and find hard, sticky yellow or red clay, it means roots will struggle, so you will need to add organic manure to improve it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eŋɔɔɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee. Kɛji otsa shi ni ona shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni ji ŋmɔŋ loo tsuru. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe baahia ni shishifãi lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni eha ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What can I do to stop rain water from standing like a pond on my farm and making mud?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni nugbɔ nu akate shi tamɔ nubu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha efee muji?

english: You can build raised earth mounds or ridges to plant your crops on, and dig shallow channels to lead excess rain away. This keeps crop roots above standing water so they do not drown.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni okɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii. ni efo gbɛ ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ koni ekɛjie nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ koni amɛkagbo.

english: Why does land that has been left to rest for a few years yield better crops than land I farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ afii fioo komɛi lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Just like a tired worker recovers after resting, soil gains back its strength when left alone. Falling leaves rot over time, restoring lost nutrients naturally so future crops can grow stronger.
ga: Tamɔ bɔ ni nitsulɔ ni etɔ lɛ lɛ he waaa beni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ ashi lɛ pɛ. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ waa po.

english: Why do weeds keep sprouting back so fast even after I cut them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ fɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Weed seeds stay hidden deep inside the soil waiting for sunlight and water to grow. Covering the cleared ground with dry grass or leaves blocks light from reaching the soil so weed seeds cannot sprout easily.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiimɛ hulu la kɛ nu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha hei ni egbele lɛ ahe koni la akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do older seed varieties seem to handle dry weather better than the newer seeds sold in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui ni egbɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional crop varieties have naturally adapted over many generations to withstand harsh local weather and poor soils, whereas many modern improved varieties are bred for high yields under ideal conditions and require steady water to perform well.
ga: Kusum tsei srɔtoi lɛ etsake amɛhe yɛ yinɔi ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛdamɔ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔji ni ehiii lɛ anaa. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni atsake amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ shihilɛi ni sa amli ni amɛbiɔ nu daa koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right crop variety if my farm dries out quickly during dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tso srɔtoi ni sa? Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: If your land does not retain water well, you should ask for drought-tolerant seed varieties or resilient traditional seeds rather than varieties that require flooded or constantly moist soil to survive.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ obi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli loo blema dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Mohu ɔ, bi nɛ a ha mo tso slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ biɔ nɛ nyu nɛ ngɛ mi loo zu nɛ mi nɛ ngɛ mi be fɛɛ be konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a hi si.

english: Why did the new rice variety I tried this year dry up so easily compared to my usual crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔ hee ni mika afi nɛɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni miduɔ daa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yielding rice varieties need continuous moisture or standing water to produce well; without a guaranteed water source, they dry out faster than traditional varieties bred for dry land.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa henɔi babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi daa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Kɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɛ lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya fe blema tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop dry out and fail to give a good yield on my highland farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi ni ewooo yibii kpakpai yɛ mi-ŋwɛi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice generally requires a large amount of moisture throughout its life cycle, so planting high-water-demanding varieties on high, dry land without extra irrigation prevents them from developing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu tsei srɔtoi ni he hiaa nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni egbi nɔ ni nu kroko fataaa he lɛ, ebaatsi shweremɔ ni sa naa.

english: Where is the best place on my farm to plant crops that need a lot of water?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nu babaoo lɛ?

english: Water-sensitive crops should be planted in low-lying valley bottoms, swampy areas, or places where rainwater naturally gathers and keeps the soil wet for long periods.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli. He ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ loo he ko ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes my crops to dry out quickly even when they looked healthy early in the season?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ?

english: When crops reach key growth stages, their water demand increases; if the soil dries up completely during this critical period, the plants lose moisture rapidly and dry out before maturing.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ shɛ dalɛ hei ni he hiaa waa lɛ Nu ni ataoɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do delicate crops fail to grow on the tougher and harder parts of my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ekwɛ̃ɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hei ni wa ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: Hard, dry land makes it difficult for roots to spread and hold moisture, which causes sensitive modern crop varieties to dry up unless hardy local varieties are planted instead.
ga: Hei ni wa ni egbi lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbiɔ. Ja amɛdu maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni wa moŋ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is suitable for growing rice successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko nɔ sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye loo daabi?

english: Look for land that holds water easily and does not drain away immediately, such as lowlands or clay-heavy soils, because rice performs best where moisture remains in the root zone.
ga: Taomɔ hei ni nu lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi oya ni ehooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ he lolo.

english: Why are crops on one side of my farm performing well while the ones on drier ground are failing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ehiii lɛ?

english: Farmlands often have uneven water distribution and varying soil types; areas that hold natural ground water allow crops to thrive, while drier spots cause water-hungry crops to dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni okwaayeli tsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ, nu lɛ mlijaa kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi babaoo bɛ. Hei ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ. yɛ be mli ni hei ni egbi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ agbi.

english: Can any crop survive on dry land that gets very little water during the season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, hardy native crops and drought-tolerant varieties are specially suited to grow in dry, tough soils where moisture-sensitive crops would dry out and perish.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋ tsei ni wa kɛ henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni kpɛtɛɔ nɔ. Tsei ni nuɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaafite.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow before the plants even start producing ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ po jeɔ toi feemɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow green and healthy. Adding well-timed nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure gives the crop the push it needs to stay green and produce large cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant hides its surface from the hot sun so it loses less water through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ kɛ ehiɛ teeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛfoɔ ehe lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu fioo pɛ laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my maize plants produce empty cobs without any grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty cobs usually happen when severe drought or extreme heat strikes right when the tassels and silks appear. Without sufficient water, the silks dry up and pollen cannot fertilize the cob to form grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo latsaa ni naa wa eba beni ŋmeii kɛ siliki jeɔ kpo. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Siliki lɛ mli lɛ, egbiɔ ni pollen lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmei lɛ ni ekɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over easily when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They waste energy stretching tall to reach light instead of building strong, thick stems.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa nɛ a mi wa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize when the early rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives two or three steady, heavy rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize is a heavy feeder that drains specific nutrients from the soil quickly. Planting it in the same spot continuously starves the soil and builds up crop-specific pests; rotating with beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye hɔmɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ebaaha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai aba. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small green or brown caterpillars to chew holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves feeding on the soft growing tips of young maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts controls them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii kɛkudɔ dani okpãtã he ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ hiɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my maize as soon as I plant the seeds or wait a few weeks?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmãa mli ŋmɔshi nii kɛji adu lɛ pɛ loo abaamɛ otsii fioo komɛi?

english: It is better to wait about two weeks after planting when the seedling has grown roots. Applying fertilizer at planting time wastes money because the tiny seed cannot absorb heavy nutrients yet.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔi shishifãi shweremɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsii lolo

english: Why does my harvested maize turn dusty and get eaten by small black insects in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo sũ ni kooloi bibii diji ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ yeɔ lɛ?

english: Small black insects called grain weevils attack stored maize if the grain is not dried completely or if the storage space is damp. Drying maize until it is bone-hard and storing it in airtight bags protects your harvest from insect damage.
ga: Kplukai diji bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa loo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Abɛi ni ooogbi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ wu ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I test if my harvested maize is dry enough to store without buying an expensive machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni miheee tsɔnei ni jara wa?

english: You can use the simple bottle salt test: mix a handful of dry salt with your maize in a clean, dry glass jar and shake it. If salt sticks to the inside of the jar after five minutes, your grain still has too much water and needs more sun drying.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ salt shaker kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Okɛ ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛ nine kome awo glase tsinsii ni mli tse ni egbi mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmei lɛ tsɔ tsɛnsi lɛ mli yɛ minitii enumɔ sɛɛ Oŋmaa lɛ yɛ nu babaoo lolo ni ehe miihia ni hulu lɛ ashɛ ehe babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the large trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Large shade trees act like protective umbrellas, shielding the cocoa from harsh heat and keeping the soil moist so the young roots do not dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa kwraa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Koni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi

english: How does breaking up hard soil with a tractor or hoe help my yam tubers grow bigger underground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akɛ trakta loo ŋmei shwieɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are underground stems that need soft, loose soil to expand freely. If the ground is hard and compacted, the tubers struggle to push through the dirt, resulting in short, thin, or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Yitso lɛ baaná naagbai ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kuku, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa baa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize make my maize crops grow healthier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ haa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special root systems that pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so the beans naturally fertilize the soil for the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii aha ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant loves from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, while also allowing crop-specific pests to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward trying to beat their neighbors for light instead of putting energy into growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ peeɔ tsehi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tso nguahi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide on the underside of leaves to suck out the plant's juices, or by viruses spread by these insects that cause the leaves to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination by insects, causing the plant to save its strength rather than carry fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni haaa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ hiɛɔ amɛhewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil for too long, it suffocates the roots and creates the perfect wet environment for fungal diseases to decay the tubers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii helai ni baanyɛ afite yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn pale yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When a crop lacks important nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, it automatically redirects the remaining food from its older bottom leaves up to the young top leaves to keep growing, causing the bottom leaves to starve and yellow.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ tsɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni eya nɔ eda. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops and make my crops turn weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are adapted to drink up water, fertilizer, and sunlight far more aggressively than cultivated crops, effectively stealing the food your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la mli waa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What is a hybrid seed, and how is it different from the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: A hybrid seed is produced by cross-breeding two different plant varieties to combine their best traits, like higher yields or pest resistance. Unlike saved seeds, hybrid seeds give stronger, more uniform crops in their first generation.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ feɔ kɛtsɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ afee ekome, tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome, ni tamɔɔɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ, woɔ yibii ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa fe klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ.

english: Are locally developed hybrid seeds as good as the imported seeds brought from abroad?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hi tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ?

english: Yes, locally produced hybrids are often better because they are specifically bred and tested to handle Ghana's local soil conditions, temperatures, and native pests, whereas foreign seeds are made for different environments.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ atsɔse amɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛtsu Ghana maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ, hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii. yɛ be mli ni abɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui kɛha shihilɛi srɔtoi.

english: Why do some of my fellow farmers hesitate to buy locally made hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minanemɛi okwaafoi lɛ ekomɛi sumɔɔɔ ni amɛheɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many farmers stick with traditional seeds because they are accustomed to them or assume imported seeds are better quality. However, local hybrids are proven through field trials to perform just as well or better under local conditions.
ga: Okwaafoi babaoo kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ blema dumɔwui ahe ejaakɛ amɛle loo amɛsusuɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ana odaseyeli yɛ ŋmɔ mli kaai amli akɛ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nakai nɔŋŋ. Nakai nɔŋŋ loo nɔ ni hi fe nakai yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shishi

english: What noticeable differences will I see in my farm if I switch from regular seeds to improved hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ srɔtofeemɔi ni kadiɔ mɔ mana yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mitsake kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ amli kɛtee dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ?

english: With improved hybrid seeds, your plants will grow much more evenly, flower at the same time, resist diseases better, and produce a significantly larger harvest.
ga: kɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ Otsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ha fɔfɔii yɛ be kome too mli Helai ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo ni kadiɔ mɔ

english: What does it mean when a crop variety is described as 'early maturing'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛ́ atsɔɔ tso henɔ ko mli akɛ ‘ekwɛɔ mra’?

english: An early-maturing variety grows faster than standard crops, reaching harvest readiness in a shorter timeframe—such as 120 days—so you can harvest sooner.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ gbii 120, no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa oya.

english: How can planting a 120-day crop variety protect my harvest if the rains stop early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbii 120 ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra?

english: A 120-day crop completes its growth cycle quickly, allowing it to mature and produce yield before late-season dry spells or droughts can ruin the farm.
ga: Gbii 120 ŋmɔshi nibii baagbe shweremɔ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii dani hɔmɔ be loo hɔmɔ ni baa naagbee be lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why does the time it takes for a crop to mature change depending on where my farm is located in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Crop maturity depends on local weather factors like temperature, rainfall, and daily sunlight. A crop that takes 120 days in one region might take slightly longer or shorter in another area with different climatic conditions.
ga: Tsei adalɛ damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nibii tamɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔnɛmɔ kɛ daa gbi hulu la nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni heɔ gbii 120 yɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahé be fioo loo kuku yɛ he kroko ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ yɔɔ srɔto yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of the same crop available for me to choose from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli ni manyɛ mahala mli lɛ?

english: Seed developers create different varieties—sometimes up to nine or more—so that farmers can choose seeds specifically tailored for early harvest, dry conditions, or specific soil types.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ srɔtoi - bei komɛi lɛ amɛyi fa fe nɛɛhu loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Enɛ haa okwaafoi halaa dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛha mra be mli ŋmaakpamɔ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi.

english: How do I know which seed variety will perform best in my specific district?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers and agricultural stations test different varieties across various regions to determine which maturity time and stress tolerance match your district's rainfall pattern and climate.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi kɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei lɛ baaka tsofai srɔtoi lɛ amɛkwɛ. yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ Koni ona kɛji akɛ dalɛ be kɛ haomɔ he tsuishitoo lɛ kɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpãa gbee.

english: How do researchers know for sure that a new crop variety works well before recommending it to farmers?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni niiamlitaolɔi ale kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko baatsu nii dani amɛkɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ?

english: Researchers run practical field trials directly on local land to observe how the plants grow, measure actual yields, and confirm their performance before releasing them to farmers.
ga: Nibii amlitaolɔi lɛ fee ŋmɔ mli kaai yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ daraa amɛhaa. Susumɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ he ni oma bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ nɔ mi dani ojie lɛ kpo otsɔɔ okwaafoi.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato plants in the early morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can drink water before the severe heat starts. Watering in the hot afternoon leads to fast water evaporation, and wet leaves in hot sun can burn or attract diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ dani hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ aje shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Ni baai ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbala helai.

english: How does proper irrigation help my crops during long dry spells without rain?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Irrigation delivers a steady supply of water directly to the plant roots when rain fails, allowing crops to keep growing, flowering, and producing yield without drying up or dying from drought stress.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Ehaa tsei daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛgbiee loo amɛgbooo yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do plantain plants need much more water to survive than cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi fe ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have huge leaves and soft stems that store water and lose moisture quickly through evaporation, whereas cassava plants are built for dry soil and drop their leaves to save water when rain is scarce.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai wuji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni amaa ŋmei tsei kɛha shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ashiɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni akɛbu nu he kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up like straws to protect themselves from intense sunlight and limit water loss. It is the plant's natural shield against heat stress until temperatures cool down.
ga: Akɛ abɛi baa lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ jwɛi koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dɔlɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or is getting too much or too little water, which stops the roots from absorbing key soil nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo loo nu fioo pɛ enine shɛɔ nɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cassava plants lose most of their leaves when the dry season sets in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during drought to conserve energy and water. The plant goes dormant under the soil and will quickly sprout fresh green leaves once rain returns.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Tsei lɛ ewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbaakwɛ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, like extreme daytime heat, irregular watering, or low soil nutrients, causing the plant to conserve energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open on the sides right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ sɛɛgbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting happens when a plant receives a sudden flush of water after a dry spell, causing the soft flesh inside the tomato to grow faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Yibii mligbalamɔ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nu ni hoɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa loo ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why would an expert or extension engineer need to inspect my farm land before setting up an irrigation channel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋaalɔi loo Extension Engineers lɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛto nu shwiemɔ gbɛi lɛ?

english: An inspection determines the slope of your field, the water source, and the soil type so water flows naturally across your crops without washing away topsoil or causing flooding.
ga: Kwɛmɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ehaa, nu jɛɛhe kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ efɔɔɔ shi loo ekɛ nu afua baaa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is holding too much water and choking my crop roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsi mihe?

english: If standing water remains on the surface for days, or if you dig down and find foul-smelling, soggy soil with soft, yellowing plant stems, your soil is waterlogged and lacks the oxygen roots need to breathe.
ga: Kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo Aloo kɛji otsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ona akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa oshishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the rain to soak deep into the soil before I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ lɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Planting in lightly moist soil can cause seeds to sprout and then die if the sun comes out and dries the topsoil before the roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgboi kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛnɔ. ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Yams become misshapen when the soil beneath them is too hard, compacted, or stony, which stops the tuber from pushing straight down into the earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make their food and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei koni amɛhoo niyenii ni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects to pollinate them; if there is no shade or moist organic leaf matter for these insects to live in, the flowers go unpollinated and drop.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ kooloi bibii koni amɛfee pollin. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni mli edɔ bɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná lɛ, no lɛ, kooloi bibii he miihia kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ pollination ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Small holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like beetles or caterpillars chewing on them, which weakens the plant's ability to produce healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to local conditions, so they quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops have a chance to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight and nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stems with small yields or no fruit at all.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo ewooo yibii kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why does cutting off some extra branches from my tomato plant help me get bigger tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo tomato tsei lɛ aniji krokomɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tomatoi wuji baa lɛ?

english: Removing unnecessary branches allows the plant to direct its energy, water, and nutrients into growing larger fruits instead of supporting extra foliage.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabi ni akɛ baai krokomɛi afata he lɛ

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, usually 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts next season on the field where I grew maize this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni midu ŋmeii yɛ mli afi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which restores fertility after heavy-feeding crops like maize have used up the nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ beni tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ eye amɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Does my plantain crop really need a lot of water to grow well?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia mi plantain lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantain trees consist mostly of water and have large leaves that lose moisture fast. They require consistently moist soil throughout the year to produce heavy, high-quality bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ji nɔ ni feɔ plantains lɛ babaoo, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛná ŋmeii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How much water do plantains need compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa plantains kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmei he?

english: Plantains require significantly more water than cassava. Cassava can survive long dry spells by storing energy in its tubers, whereas plantains will stunt in growth and produce small fruits if water is lacking.
ga: Plantains biɔ nu babaoo kwraa fe ŋmei. Cassava baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plantains lɛ baafee mlɛo yɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛbaawo yibii bibii kɛji nu bɛ amɛmli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn yellow when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drooping leaves are a defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to direct sunlight and slow down moisture loss. It is a clear sign that the plant is heat-stressed and needs moisture at its roots.
