ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ nɔ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ shi. Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ miiye latsaa he haomɔ ni ehe miihia ni nu ahi eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain stems lose their strength and fall over during dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and soft, water-filled stems. When the soil dries out, the stem loses its internal water pressure, causing the plant to weaken and easily fall over under its own weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: What causes my plantain tree to take a very long time to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii?

english: Delayed fruiting usually happens when the plant suffers from water shortages, poor soil nutrients, or heavy competition from weeds. Regular watering and soil enrichment speed up its growth cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nu ni faaa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akaŋshii ni naa wa ni jɛɔ jwɛi amli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: How can I keep my plantain farm moist if I don't have enough time to water every day?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ahi shi? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaafɔ nu daa gbi hu?

english: Applying a thick layer of organic mulch—such as dry grass, leaves, or cocoa husks—around the base of the plants traps moisture in the soil, keeping the root area damp for longer periods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni mli edɔ wo otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: How can I tell if the soil around my crops has enough moisture for them to survive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua wala?

english: Dig a few inches into the ground near the stem and squeeze a handful of soil. If the soil stays formed in a soft ball without crumbling or dripping water, it has adequate moisture.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni shɛɔ inchi 2-3 ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ko awo mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lolo ni nu ni mli ejɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ, Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will standing water on my farm harm my plantain plants?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye midumɔwui lɛ awui?

english: Yes, stagnant standing water rots plantain roots because roots require oxygen from the soil to breathe. Even though plantains love water, good farm drainage is needed to prevent waterlogging.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa plantain shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Eyɛ mli akɛ plantains sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi ŋmɔ mli nu kpakpa he miihia koni nu afua akafee.

english: How can I ensure my plantain farm gives me a good yield so I can make a reliable living?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai bɔni afee ni manyɛ maná shihilɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: To get profitable yields, supply your plantains with organic manure, clear weeds early, provide wind protection, and ensure adequate water during dry spells so the stems stay strong and yield large bunches.
ga: bɔni afee ni afee nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha plantains lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra, bu he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he, ni okwɛ koni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Koni eha tso lɛ mli awa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Which crops can I plant in Ghana that stay strong even when rainfall is low?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni yaa nɔ waa lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas are naturally drought-tolerant and can sustain growth on minimal rainfall, making them resilient options during dry weather.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli.

english: Can I mix two different farm chemicals together before spraying them on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afutu mli dani mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Mixing chemicals without guidance can burn your crops or destroy the effectiveness of the treatment. You should only combine chemicals if agricultural officers or product labels specifically state they can be mixed safely.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii loo efite bɔ ni tsofafeemɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai afutu pɛ kɛji okwaayeli he nitsulɔi loo tsofai lɛ ahe wolo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ehi akɛ abaanyɛ afutu.

english: Why do different crop chemicals come in different colors like red or white?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ etsuru loo eyɛŋ lɛ?

english: Chemical manufacturers color-code or distinctively label products so farmers can easily identify which ones target pests, diseases, or weeds, preventing dangerous mix-ups on the farm.
ga: Mɛi ni feɔ tsofai lɛ kɛ kɔlai tsuɔ nii loo amɛŋmalaa amɛnibii lɛ ahe saji yɛ faŋŋ mli. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi lɛ anyɛ ana nibii ni akɛmiikwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo jwɛi lɛ anɔ oya koni akɛtsi osharai ni akɛtoɔ he yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anaa.

english: What is the best time of day to spray liquid fertilizer or chemicals on my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ nu loo tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Early morning or late evening is best because lower heat prevents the liquid from evaporating quickly and stops the intense sun from scorching leaves that have wet chemicals on them.
ga: Leebi loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ la ni baa shi lɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ehaaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã baai ni tsofai ni mli efɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: When crops lack nutrients, they usually give warning signs such as yellowing leaves, slow growth, thin stems, or poor flower and fruit production.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Bei pii lɛ amɛjieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdalɛ blɛoo, amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, loo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ehiii lɛ kpo.

english: Is it okay to reduce the fertilizer dose so I can stretch my supply across the whole farm?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni manyɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Under-dosing gives plants insufficient food to grow strong, which leads to poor yields. It is better to give the full recommended dose to a smaller section of your field than to starve all your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fioo pɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni ehiii Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaha ŋmɔ ko mli he bibioo ko ni akɛhaa lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ fe ni aaaha hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves stay yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Leaves may stay yellow if heavy rains washed the fertilizer away before roots could absorb it, if the soil is too dry, or if the yellowing was caused by a pest or disease rather than nutrient deficiency.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa moŋ fe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ.

english: How long does it take to see results after applying fertilizer to my plants?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa beni awo tso ko mli fɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most crops show greener leaves and faster growth within one to two weeks after receiving fertilizer, provided there is enough moisture in the soil to help the roots take up the nutrients.
ga: Tsei babaoo baaná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaadara oya yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do insects keep returning to my farm even after I have sprayed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ spray shwie shi moŋ

english: Pests can return if the chemical only killed adult bugs while leaving eggs behind, if rain washed the spray off too soon, or if pests are migrating over from neighboring unsprayed farms.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ aba kɛji tsofai gbe kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ, ni amɛshi amɛwuji. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ oya tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efã kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni afɔɔɔ amɛ tsofa lɛ amli.

english: Why is it better to follow tested scientific advice rather than guessing how to use farm inputs?
ga: Mɛni he je nɛ e hi kaa wa maa nyɛɛ ga womi nɛ je mi si kpami ka a hyɛ ɔ se ɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii baatsu nii aha lɛ he.

english: Tested guidelines are based on trials that prove the exact amounts needed to get the highest yield safely, preventing you from wasting money or damaging your soil.
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ damɔ kaai ni tsɔɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni anyɛ ana yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika loo okafite shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops wither easily during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have small roots and thin leaves, causing them to lose water faster under hot sun than their roots can drink from the soil, making them droop until temperatures cool down.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai bibii, ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛlaajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eji nɔ ni fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ehi shi ni egbo kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes during the dry season if my farm is near an irrigation scheme?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ tomato yɛ fɛ̃i be mli kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu shwiemɔ nitsumɔ ko?

english: Yes, irrigation provides a controlled and steady supply of water when there is no rainfall. This allows crops to grow continuously throughout the dry season without drying out or suffering from water stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni akudɔɔ ni akɛhaa po baa kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei yaa nɔ amɛdaraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ ni amɛgbiŋ loo nu he haomɔ enaaa amɛnɔ hewalɛ.

english: Do crops grown with channeled dam water yield better than crops that rely only on rain?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops grown with managed irrigation often yield better because they receive a consistent amount of water right when they need it, unlike rainfed crops which can suffer whenever rains are delayed or irregular.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni akɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai ejaakɛ amɛnáa nu babaoo be fɛɛ be kɛ́ ehe miihia amɛ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni baanyɛ ana amanehulu be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baa sɛɛ loo ebaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when water sits around their roots for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When excess water collects around plant roots without draining, it pushes out oxygen from the soil. Without oxygen, the roots cannot breathe or absorb nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ tso shishifãi ahe ni ekɛ nu efooo Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my plant leaves curl up during the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni amɛfeee nakai lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. During hot afternoons, plants lose water quickly through transpiration, so they curl their leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why is it bad to irrigate my crops during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under strong midday heat causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots. Additionally, water droplets left on leaves can act like magnifying glasses in strong sunlight and scorch the leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu mli nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants when I flood the farm with too much water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ?

english: Too much water causes stress to the plant's root system. When a plant gets stressed during its flowering stage, it drops its flowers to save energy for survival rather than spending energy on producing fruit.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji tsei miihao yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Ebaafɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ekɛto hewalɛ ni ekɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do my crops rot at the base of the stem when water stays stagnant on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi be mli ni nu ekã ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Stagnant, unmanaged water creates a moist environment where soil-borne fungi and bacteria multiply quickly, attacking the soft base of the crop stem and causing it to rot.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Fuji kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya. Etutuaa tsei ashishifãi bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why should I water my crop field immediately after applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo mitsei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve into a liquid form. Only when dissolved can plant roots absorb the nutrients. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can also burn the plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ nu. Kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ, tso shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my crops whenever I apply irrigation water to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough plants that absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. When you irrigate, weeds take advantage of the water immediately unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni wa ni ŋmɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ nu shwie nɔ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaná nu lɛ he sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ja ojie fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ.

english: Why does rice grow well in flooded irrigation fields while other crops die in that same water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi gboiɔ yɛ nakai nu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems and roots that allow them to transport air from the atmosphere down to their roots underwater, unlike crops like maize or cassava whose roots drown in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛjieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ nu ni damɔ shi mli lɛ.

english: What is potassium, and why do my crops need it to grow well?
ga: Mɛni ji potaziɔm? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mitsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Potassium is an essential nutrient that crops need to stay healthy, often represented by the letter 'K' in fertilizers like NPK. It acts like a protective strength builder for plants, helping them grow strong stems, withstand dry weather, fight off diseases, and produce larger fruits and tubers like cassava and yam.
ga: Potassium ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. Bei pii lɛ, akɛ niŋmaakadi ‘K’ kadiɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ waa koni ebu tsei ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi Ekɛ helai srɔtoi wuɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Can I use the potassium or drip solutions from the hospital on my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ potassium loo helatsamɔhe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, medical potassium or hospital drip solutions are formulated specifically for human bodies, not soil. Using medical supplies on crops will not nourish plants, can harm the beneficial organisms in your soil, and is a waste of money compared to using actual agricultural fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofafeemɔ mli potassium loo helatsamɔhe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ aha adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. jeee kɛha shikpɔŋ Tsofafeemɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haŋ tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eye nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui. Ni eji shika fitemɔ kɛ akɛto okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he.

english: Is the potassium used in phone batteries the same substance I need for my farm fertilizer?
ga: Ani potassium ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tɛlifoŋ batrei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa mi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, they are completely different chemical forms. The materials used inside phone batteries are toxic industrial compounds designed to store electricity, while crop potassium is a safe, refined mineral salt meant to nourish plants through the soil.
ga: Dabi, amɛyɛ tsofafeemɔ su ko ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tɛlifoŋ batrei amli lɛ ji nitsumɔhei nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni akɛto srawa hewalɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, potassium ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ ji ŋmei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji ŋmei ni he tse ni afee koni ekɛha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe to mix strong local concoctions or tonic drinks with my crop fertilizers?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo hewalɛ nibii ni anuɔ lɛ baafutu miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: No, you should never mix non-agricultural liquids or concoctions with farm fertilizers. Mixing unknown substances can ruin the fertilizer's effectiveness, destroy your crop's roots, burn the leaves, or create dangerous chemical fumes that can harm your health.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ okɛ nu ni jeee okwaayeli loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futuɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Nibii ni aleee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. Efiteɔ otso lɛ shishifãi, eshãa baai lɛ, loo ehaa tsofa lasu ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ aye ohewalɛ awui baa.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are showing signs of lacking potassium?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ amɛmli?

english: When crops lack potassium, the outer edges of their older leaves start turning yellow and then brown, making them look like they have been scorched by fire. The leaves may curl, and the plant stems become weak and snap easily.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ potassium lɛ Baai ni egbɔ lɛ asɛɛgbɛ fãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ. Ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la miitswa. Baai lɛ baanyɛ abɔle. ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekumɔ oya.

english: Where is the best place around the plant to apply fertilizer?
ga: He ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Nɛgbɛ ji nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied to the soil around the plant's drip line—the circular area directly beneath the outer leaves—where the active roots grow. Never put fertilizer directly against the main stem, as it can burn the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ he, ni ji he ni yɔɔ kokroo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni shishifãi lɛ miida lolo yɛ. Kaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ.

english: What do the three numbers printed on a fertilizer bag, like 15-15-15, stand for?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yibɔi etɛ ni akala yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli, tamɔ 15-15-15 lɛ damɔ shi kɛha?

english: The three numbers represent the proportion of Nitrogen (for leaf growth), Phosphorus (for strong roots), and Potassium (for fruit size and health). A bag marked 15-15-15 gives an equal balance of all three key nutrients to your crop.
ga: Yibɔi etɛ lɛ damɔ shi kɛha nitrogen lɛ mlijaa. Nɔ ni fata he ji calcium (kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ), phosphorus (kɛha shishifãi ni wa), kɛ potassium (kɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ). (Kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ) Baagi ni akadi 15-15-15 lɛ baaha niyenii titrii etɛ fɛɛ ni sa kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Are there natural materials on my farm that can give potassium to my soil without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Ani adebɔɔ mli nibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aha sũ lɛ mli potassium ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ?

english: Yes, natural materials like cocoa pod husks, wood ash from your cooking fire, compost, and poultry manure contain good amounts of potassium. Spreading burnt wood ash or compost around your plants naturally feeds the soil over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kookoo pod ŋmeii. tso sũ ni jɛɔ la ni akɛhooɔ nii amli, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ashwishwɛi Eyɛ potassium babaoo jogbaŋŋ. Tso sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Where should I buy reliable fertilizers and crop products to ensure they are safe?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ koni mana akɛ amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Always buy fertilizers and crop inputs from certified agro-dealers registered with the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MOFA). Avoid buying unlabelled powders or mixed liquids from open market hawkers, as fake products can kill your crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MOFA) lɛ adɛŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ powda loo nu ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni aŋmalako nɔ ko nɔ lɛ hemɔ he yɛ jarayeli hei ni agbele naa lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, amale nibii baanyɛ agbe oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it dangerous to mix two different crop chemicals together without asking an extension officer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ baafutu ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni abiii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔ lɛ?

english: Combining different farm chemicals without proper guidance can cause unwanted reactions that burn crop leaves, leave toxic residues on food crops, or cancel out the beneficial effects of both products.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ ni akɛaafata he ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpakpa bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha nɔ ko ni ehiii aba ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ashiɔ yɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ loo ni afoɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ mli

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I cut down all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa from strong heat and helps the soil stay moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ebaafee ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is starving for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Nitrogen is what gives leaves their healthy green color so they can feed the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kpakpai bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Nitrogen ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni haa tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause water to pool without good drainage, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stalks and very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo ni elaaje baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience stress, such as intense heat waves or sudden dry spells. The plant sheds flowers to conserve energy and survive the harsh conditions.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ko, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ he. Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do I need to put up tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei kakadaji kɛha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward the sun so their leaves can capture maximum light. Lifting the vines off the ground allows the leaves to make more food, which builds bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii wuji baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain produce smaller bunches when many small suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: The small suckers growing at the base steal water and food from the main plant. Pruning away extra suckers ensures all the energy goes directly into growing a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Tso bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ni aaafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ haa hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa plantains tsei wuji ni tsii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: If I cut off the top tips of my pepper plants, will it kill them?
ga: Kɛ mifo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ naa lɛ, Ani ebaagbe amɛ?

english: Cutting the top tip actually signals the plant to branch out sideways instead of growing straight up. More side branches mean more flower spots and a larger harvest of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ baaje kpo kɛya afã moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Niji babaoo ni yɔɔ afã lɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔii babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni akpaa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients from the soil quickly. They grow aggressively to crowd out other crops before your planted seeds can fully establish.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ dani dumɔwui ni odu lɛ baanyɛ adara.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees react immediately to dry weather to protect themselves. When water becomes scarce, the tree drops its flowers so it doesn't waste precious moisture on new pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ akafite kɛya ŋmɔtɔ heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my neighbor's cocoa trees growing much faster than mine even though we planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo tso lɛ daa oya kwraa fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔfee ekome kɛdu moŋ?

english: Trees grow at different rates depending on soil nutrients, how much shade they get, and how well young plants are protected from weeds. Adding organic manure and managing shade properly helps slow-growing cocoa catch up.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ, ni enɛ damɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔ ni tso lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo kɛ bɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi ahe lɛ. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shade ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua kookoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ ni eshɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: What causes cocoa pods to grow slowly or take a very long time to ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa blɛoo loo amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ?

english: Slow pod development is usually caused by a lack of essential soil nutrients, insufficient water during dry spells, or sap-sucking insects like capsids. Proper pruning and timely fertilizing encourage healthy pod growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pod lɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids, ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: What can I do to help my weak young cocoa trees grow stronger branches?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛwo niji ni mli wa?

english: Regular weeding around the base, pruning off weak side shoots, and providing adequate shade with compost will give young trees the nutrients and strength they need to build sturdy branches.
ga: Ajie jwɛi ni bɔle shishi lɛ daa ni afolɔ afã tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii akakwɛ̃. Na niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni niji ni mli wa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I stop birds from coming to my farm and destroying my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi okpoi ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: Birds are attracted to visible fruits and seeds on exposed crops. You can deter them by hanging reflective shiny objects like foil strips, setting up scarecrows, or planting barrier crops around the farm perimeter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ anɔ lɛ gbalaa okpoi. Obaanyɛ otsi amɛ gbɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni haa hulu kpɛɔ, tamɔ foil ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ, ni okɛ tsɔne ni haa mɔ he feɔ gbeyei lɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ. loo odu gbɛtsii nii ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Are there simple ways to keep pest birds away without spending money on expensive chemicals?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni aaatsɔ nɔ ajie okpoi ni yeɔ mɛi awui lɛ ni afiteee shika yɛ tsofai ni jara wa ahe?

english: Yes, natural methods like installing noise-makers, using visual scarers, and trimming nearby tall wild trees where birds nest can significantly reduce bird visits without costly sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tamɔ gbee tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Projɛkta ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni ji hei ni okpoi feɔ amɛshĩai lɛ ni afoɔ. Abaanyɛ aba okpoi asaramɔ shi waa kɛji akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fataaa he.

english: Why do birds seem to attack my farm more than other farms nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni okpoi tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ fe ŋmɔi krokomɛi lɛ? Yɛ akutso lɛ mli?

english: Birds usually target farms that have easy access to exposed young fruit, open seedbeds, or farms that border dense wild bush where they roost. Clearing wild brush around your border makes your farm less attractive to them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okpoi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. dumɔwui aŋmɔ ni agbele naa loo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ koo mli jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ. Edges jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni oootsi lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni amɛsumɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings wither and die during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them protects them from burning and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shãa akafee nɔ ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Can having too much shade on my mature cocoa trees slow down their growth?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ha mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha edalɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, while young cocoa needs shade, mature trees require moderate sunlight to produce maximum pods. Excessive shade traps moisture, slowing down flowering and encouraging fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo moŋ. Shi tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings so they do not crowd each other out?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe?

english: Planting cocoa about 3 meters by 3 meters apart gives each tree enough space for roots and leaves to spread without competing with neighboring trees for water, soil nutrients, and light.
ga: Cocoa ni aduɔ aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ kɛ la

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are lagging behind because of poor soil or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ efo sɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: If slow growth affects all trees in an area uniformly, it is usually a sign of poor soil nutrients. If only isolated trees show yellowing leaves, dark spots, or dying tips, it is likely caused by a disease or pest attack.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo lɛ enaa tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli. Kɛji tso ko ni yɔɔ he kroko lɛ jieɔ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ, he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni miigboi lɛ kpo. Ekolɛ hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛbaa.

english: Why do many farmers burn their fields before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo shãa ŋmɔji dani amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ?

english: Burning clears heavy weeds, tall grass, and bush quickly so you can till and plant easily. The leftover ash also provides a quick boost of nutrients to the soil, though repeated burning damages the soil over time.
ga: Shãa jieɔ jwɛi ni tsii, jwɛi kakadaji, kɛ tsei bibii oya. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsu nii ni odu ŋmɔshi nibii mlɛo. Sũ ni eshwɛ lɛ hu kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ moŋ Ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What happens to my soil when a fire burns across my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ la shã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Fire burns away the top layer of organic matter, dry leaves, and small soil creatures that keep the soil fertile. It leaves the ground exposed to hot sun and heavy rains, which wash away rich topsoil.
ga: La shãa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, baai ni egboi, kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds sprout much faster than my planted crops after a field is burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mishã ŋmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many weed seeds have tough outer shells that survive heat underground. When fire clears away tall trees and shade, it leaves open soil with full sunlight, allowing weed seeds to germinate instantly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo yɛ kponɔgbɛ nibii ni wa ni baanyɛ adamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dɔlɛ naa. Beni la shwieɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ hulutsoo lɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I clear a bare strip of dirt around my crop farm before the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Okwaafoi aŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Clearing a wide strip of bare ground, known as a firebelt, removes dry grass and leaves that bushfires feed on. When a fire reaches this bare space, it runs out of fuel and stops before reaching your crops.
ga: He ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ale lɛ akɛ la fãi lɛ ahe saamɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi ni egboi kɛ baai ni koo mli la eye lɛ. Kɛ la lɛ shɛ he ni nɔ ko bɛ nɛɛ La lɛ baaho ni ebaakpa dani eshɛ onibii ahe.

english: Can my cassava or maize crops recover if a fire scorches my farm?
ga: Ani mi-cassava loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji la kpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ?

english: Maize plants will die completely once scorched. However, mature cassava plants may sprout fresh green leaves from underground roots when rains return, provided the heat did not cook the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Abɛi tsei gboiɔ kɛji ashã amɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛjɛ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba. Kɛji la ni tsoɔ lɛ shãaa ŋmeii lɛ,.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and turn yellow after I burn the same field for several years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mishã ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Repeated burning destroys natural plant compost and essential plant nutrients like nitrogen. Over time, the soil loses its richness, becomes hard, and can no longer hold water well, making crops pale and weak.
ga: shãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ Efiteɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi, ewaa, ni enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Does cattle manure left on my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei ni ashiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cattle manure acts as a rich natural fertilizer. It adds organic material back into the soil, improves water retention, and supplies key nutrients that help crops like maize and vegetables grow strong.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei babaoo. Ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eha nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ haa.

english: How does wood ash from burned vegetation affect young crop roots?
ga: Te tso sũ ni jɛ tsei ni ashã lɛ mli lɛ saa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A small amount of wood ash reduces soil acidity and supplies potassium. However, too much ash right around young seeds can burn delicate fresh roots and reduce germination.
ga: Tso mli sũ fioo ko haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa shi, ni ehaa potassium baa. Dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ ashã shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my plant leaves dry out so fast when the harmattan winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds carry extremely dry air that pulls moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can absorb water from dry soil, causing plants to wilt and leaves to turn brown.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa baa. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ asasu.

english: Why do my young tree crops die when large shade trees around them are cut or burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Ani afolɔ loo ashã?

english: Young tree crops like cocoa or shade-loving plants have thin leaves that easily get scorched by intense direct sunlight. Large shade trees keep the air cool and retain moisture in the ground for young crops.
ga: Tsei bibii tamɔ kookoo loo tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ yɛ baai bibii. ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shãa oya Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dry grass on top of the soil around my crops instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shãa najiaŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so your crops do not dry out quickly under the hot sun. As the grass rots, it also turns into rich natural food for the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii akagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ jwɛi lɛ fite lɛ Ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jara wa hu kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: If too many young shoots grow around the main stem, they steal water and nutrients from it. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the parent plant to produce bigger and heavier bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ nakai tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ ŋmei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ awo ŋmei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam plants need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to produce big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the sun and keeps them off the damp ground where leaves can easily rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ he ni baai lɛ baanyɛ afite oya lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft inner leaves of young maize. Catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii amli baai lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra kɛ tsamɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when the plant loses water faster than its roots can drink under high heat, or when tiny insects like whiteflies spread a virus to the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso ko nu fite oya fe bɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Aloo beni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei anɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them before pods can grow. If there is dry weather, intense heat, or a lack of shade, the flowers dry up and drop off before forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛfee pollination dani pods lɛ aba. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, latsaa ni naa wa, loo hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakumɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the ground right around the main stem starts to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ tso titri lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does using dried chicken droppings on my farm work better than using fresh manure straight from the coop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe ŋmei hee ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh manure produces high heat and contains strong compounds that can burn plant roots. Drying and resting the manure allows it to break down safely so crops can feed on it without damage.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ babaoo baa, ni nibii ni yɔɔ mli ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni aŋmɛ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, ehaa egboɔ shweshweeshwe. Bɔni afee ni aye nibii ni adu lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growing green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crop the nutrients it needs to regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni akɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa lɛ akwɛmɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛná amɛ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When grown alongside maize, they act as natural fertilizer producers, improving soil fertility for your main crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa-feemɔ nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ.

english: How does adding goat or cow manure to my field help my vegetables grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ too loo tsina ŋmei ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with nutrients, improves its ability to hold water during hot days, and makes the soil softer so plant roots can grow deeper and feed easily.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Ehaa nyɛmɔ ni oyɔɔ ni okɛbaahiɛ nu mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛyeɔ nii mlɛo.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but produce very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is grown in soil that is overly rich in leafy foliage nutrients, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tso baai amli niyenii babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Yam vines use stakes to spread their leaves high up where they can catch direct sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce food through photosynthesis, which travels down to build large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛgbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ lɛ. Baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to each other in the line?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin stems with small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my young tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. If the plant feels it does not have enough steady water, it drops its flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu ni fa lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni ehi shi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and dying on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, shaded conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning extra cocoa branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Kookoo tsei lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ baajie hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the young leaves. Spraying neem oil or recommended organic treatments helps clear the insects so leaves grow flat again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi bibii lɛ koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I feed my goats dry grass along with fresh green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha mitooi lɛ jwɛi kɛfata baai eŋɔlii heei ahe lɛ?

english: Feeding animals only lush, wet leaves can cause watery diarrhea and stomach problems. Dry grass provides fiber, which helps their stomachs digest food properly and stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni efɔ ni ehiɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ pɛ ha kooloi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu mli tsɛŋemɔ kɛ musu mli naagbai aba. Hay haa fiber, ni yeɔ ebuaa musu lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to use crop medicine to clear weeds around plantains instead of digging with a cutlass or knife?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsei ahe tsofai baagbe jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsɔ plantain nɔ moŋ fe ni okɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei baatsu nii.

english: Using weed medicine saves time and labor, especially on large farms with mature plantains. Digging manually with a cutlass takes much longer and can accidentally damage the shallow roots of the plantain tree.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haaa afite be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji ni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli lɛ amli. Ni akɛ dade tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo ni ebaanyɛ efite dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: How do weeds around the base of my plantain trees affect their growth?
ga: Te jwɛi ni bɔle mi plantains lɛ shishi lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil that your plantains need. When weeds crowd the base of the tree, the plantains will grow slowly and produce smaller, lighter bunches.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa odumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kɛ jwɛi eyi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, Plantains baakwɛ̃ fiofio. ni amɛdaraa bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: When is the best time to spray weed control medicine on my plantain farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaafɔ jwɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to spray when weeds are still small and green, usually early in the rainy season. Spraying early stops weeds before they grow thick and tough.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ beni jwɛi lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, eji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mra Ehaa jwɛi lɛ kpaa dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: After I finish spraying my plantain farm with medicine, what other work is left for me to do?
ga: Beni agbe plantain tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ Mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ atsu lolo?

english: Spraying only controls weeds or pests. You still need to cut off dry leaves, trim extra suckers, apply fertilizer, and check your crops regularly for diseases.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye jwɛi loo kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ. Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ baai ni egbi lɛ lolo. Fɔlɔmɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, shwiemɔ ni okwɛ tsei lɛ daa kɛji helai bɛ mli.

english: How many plantain trees can one farmer realistically manage on a field?
ga: Plantain enyiɛ okwaafonyo ko baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Using only manual tools like knives and cutlasses makes it hard to manage more than a small plot. By using proper farm medicines and methods, one farmer can easily maintain hundreds of plantain stands.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ fe shikpɔji bibii. Kɛtsɔ tsofai kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Okwaafonyo kome baanyɛ akwɛ plantains ohai abɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Can I rely only on crop medicine to run my plantain farm successfully?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ tsei ahe tsofai pɛ anɔ koni manyɛ matsu mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: No, medicine is only a tool to speed up weed or pest control. A good harvest still requires hand pruning, proper spacing, watering, and soil care.
ga: Dabi, tsofafeemɔ ji dɛŋdade ko kɛkɛ ni akɛbaagbe jwɛi loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ oya. Nikpamɔ kpakpa biɔ ni akɛ niji atsu nii lolo. Gbɛ ni sa, nu ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ

english: Why is it so difficult to dig out large plantain roots by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ akɛ nine baatsa plantain shishifãi wuji lɛ?

english: As plantains mature, they form a large, heavy underground base called a corm with many thick roots. Digging this out manually requires extreme physical effort, which is why targeted chemical treatments or specialized tools are used.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantains lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo agbo ko ni tsii ni atsɛɔ lɛ rhizome ni shishifãi babaoo ni mli tse yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ bo diɛŋtsɛ ofee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ, eheɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela loo nibii krɛdɛɛi atsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep producing small shoots around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce side shoots called suckers to multiply. If you leave all of them, they steal food from the main tree, so you must prune them and leave only one or two strong shoots.
ga: Plantains woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Kɛji oshɛrɛ amɛ fɛɛ oshwie lɛ Ebaaju niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tso lɛ niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oshi.

english: Why do mature plantain trees need a clean area kept around their base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui ni eda lɛ aná he ko ni he tse ni akɛto amɛshishitoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: A clean base prevents pests like weevils and stem borers from making homes in the trash, allowing sunlight and air to reach the roots so the plant remains healthy.
ga: Shishitoo ni he tse baatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ stem borers lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee shia yɛ jwɛi lɛ mli. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Will applying weed medicine near my plantain plants destroy the soil?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi plantains lɛ ahe lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: When used correctly according to instructions, agrochemicals break down safely without ruining the soil, allowing your plantain roots to continue growing healthy.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi anaa lɛ, Agrochemicals lɛ baafite shweshweeshwe ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ye obua oplantain shishifãi lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara waa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves, or that too much water is sitting around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-composted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. aloo nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply NPK fertilizer to my young crops after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔwui lɛ amli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The best time is usually 2 to 3 weeks after your seeds sprout or seedlings are transplanted. At this stage, the plant roots have spread enough to easily drink up the fertilizer nutrients without burning the young root tips.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ loo ajie dumɔwui lɛ awo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbɛ eshwa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ enu niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mlɛo ni eshãaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking the juices out of young leaves and passing a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛhaa hela lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ atsĩ curling naa.

english: What is eating holes into the growing center of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of young maize to feed, but catching them early and applying an extension-approved insecticide or botanical mixture direct into the leaf center stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Shi ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tso mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in full open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong heat, losing moisture faster than their small roots can drink. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava around them provides protection from direct sun and wind until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli jɔ ni etswaa oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves high into the sunlight, allowing the plant to capture maximum energy. This extra energy goes straight into making the underground yam tubers grow larger and heavier.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ená hulu la. Ehaa tsei toɔ hewalɛ babaoo. Akɛ hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛha shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛtsii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, if the plant does not get enough water, or if there are no insects around to shake the flowers to pollinate them. Regular watering and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps keep flowers attached.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii bɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ, Hosomɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ amɛ afee pollin. Nu ni oooha fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or if a fungal disease enters the plant through wet soil. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji ŋmeii helai bote tso lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How does leaving weeds in my farm reduce the final harvest of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha minaagbee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops all the resources they need to produce a big harvest.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ agbo.

english: How do I decide the best time to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Instead of relying strictly on traditional calendar dates, wait until the soil is consistently moist for several days in a row before planting, or consider using early-maturing seed varieties that need less time to harvest.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye blema kalanda gbii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani odu. Aloo kaa dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni heɔ be fioo pɛ kɛkpaa lɛ okwɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves turn green and produce strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to leave dry grass on top of my farm soil instead of burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli muji lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass on the soil, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, retains water during dry weather, and slowly breaks down into natural manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing small holes in my corn leaves and chewed-up centers in the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa baai lɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni atsɔ mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves (funnel) of the maize plant during the day, so you need to apply recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when they are active.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (cones) lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni etsuɔ ​​nii waa lɛ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and shaded environments. Pruning extra shade trees to let sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods immediately stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ baaha hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaatsi helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: If I plant my seeds closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani minɔ ni?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce maximum output.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Does leaving small weeds around my crops really lower the amount of food I harvest?
ga: Ani jwɛi bibii ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ haa niyenii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, even small weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a large harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi bibii po juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo nibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots under the ground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rain early on, the cassava plant puts its energy into leaves instead of roots. Avoiding heavy chemical fertilizers late in the season helps the plant focus on expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo mra. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe shishifãi lɛ. Tsofai ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress or sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and light shade helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli loo amɛgbi trukaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Must I always use tall sticks to support my yam vines, or can I let them grow on the ground?
ga: Esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ oha ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sunlight, allowing the plant to make more food for larger tubers while protecting the foliage from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa e-bulb agboi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for growing green leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ yeɔ lɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makwɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. It also gives pests and diseases that attack cassava a permanent place to multiply, so switching to a different crop like beans helps the soil recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmei lɛ hu yaa hiɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ.

english: How does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them stay healthy?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni egbi ni okɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle o-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil that traps moisture so water does not evaporate quickly in the hot sun. It also keeps the roots cool and prevents weeds from popping up to steal your plant's food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ mulch blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu shɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, efooo oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hu mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaje kpo koni amɛju tso lɛ niyenii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves catch full sunlight and stay safe from rot and ground insects.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni egboi kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahe.

english: If you leave too many suckers growing around the main plantain tree, they will drink up the water and nutrients needed for the fruit. Removing extra suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on producing a much bigger bunch.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii obɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa aduawai lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii wuji babaoo ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Removing and burning the infected plants early stops the sickness from spreading to healthy crops across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra kɛ amɛshãa Ehaa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by intense heat or dry soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why do small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Ko ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This often happens when the cocoa tree has more pods than it can feed, or because of a fungal attack like black pod disease. Pruning extra shade branches to let air and sunlight through the farm helps stop the fungi from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. aloo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni ji black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔi lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even when plenty of rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have very aggressive roots that drink water and absorb fertilizer faster than your crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the soil's food so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. koni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do my crops grow very well in the first year after I clear new land, but get weaker after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie he ko hee lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ani ebaagbɔjɔ yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ?

english: When land is newly cleared, the soil contains accumulated nutrients from fallen leaves and natural decay. Continuous farming extracts these nutrients with every harvest, depleting the soil unless organic matter or fertilizer is added to restore it.
ga: Beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebua naa kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbee shi kɛ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ mli. Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite. Ja akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does heavy rainfall carry away the top layer of dirt on my farm when I plant on a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tsei yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: bare soil on slopes has no roots or vegetation to hold it down, so fast-moving rainwater sweeps away the topmost layer of soil, which contains the most fertile nutrients for crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ shishifãi loo tsei ni baaye abua lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why is it good for my field if I plant groundnuts or beans before I plant maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani midu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally enriching the land with fertilizer for hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make greenery and food. It can also happen when soil is waterlogged and roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without making any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: High heat causes stress to tomato plants and dries up pollen inside the blossoms, preventing pollination from occurring so the flower falls off without forming a tomato.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. ni ehaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ Tsiɔ pollen ni baa lɛ naa. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow slow and bushy with small tubers when I plant them too close to tall maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miida blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ tsɔ hewɔ lɛ,.
