english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to create the energy required to feed its tubers. Tall maize blocks sunlight, forcing the cassava to spend energy reaching for light instead of growing food underground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛha eshishifãi lɛ niyenii. Abɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ haa ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ená la yɛ niyenii ni eeedu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stay green even when my crops are struggling from lack of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi naagba yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deeper, aggressive root systems that can search for and absorb small amounts of water hidden deep in the soil much better than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ basabasa. ni baanyɛ ana nu bibii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ni eŋɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller cassava roots when I plant stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii anɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wo mli lɛ?

english: Stem cuttings have natural internal channels for food and water flow. Planting upside down forces the new roots and shoots to bend around to find light and dirt, wasting energy that would normally grow big tubers.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni afo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni niyenii kɛ nu hoɔ yɛ mli. Dumɔ ni akɛ hiɛ tsɔɔ shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛtao la kɛ muji. Eji hewalɛ ni afiteɔ ni kɛ́ eji nakai lɛ, ebaaha yitso agbo aba.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I do not plant plaintains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji miduuu ŋmɔji yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from strong sun and preserving moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni okwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi

english: Why do seeds saved from my harvested hybrid maize yield much less grain than the original seed packet I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mi-hybrid corn lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are bred from specific parents to produce high yields in the first generation only. The seeds collected from that crop lose their vigor and uniform traits in the second generation, resulting in weaker plants.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on the same land where I am starting my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ eda waa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ aha su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli awa.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How long should I wait to harvest my vegetables after spraying chemical medicine on them?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa?

english: Every crop medicine has a safe waiting period printed on the bottle, usually between 3 to 14 days. Harvesting too early leaves chemical poison on the food, which can make consumers and your family sick.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛbaamɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akala yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 14 teŋ. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei shwieɔ niyenii lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ oweku lɛ aná hela.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juice out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early with proper sprays prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛji akɛ afɔse amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water sits around them for too long, preventing the roots from breathing. Planting cassava on top of raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the seeds I planted in the dry soil failing to sprout up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a good amount of water to wake up and start growing. If the soil is too dry, the seed remains dormant or dies right after sending out its first soft sprout because there is no moisture to sustain it.
ga: Nu falɛ ko he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. aloo egboɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baaye abua lɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage. Giving the plants consistent water during dry periods helps the flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi fiteɔ amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut tall sticks to support my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni maye mabua mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves up to catch maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and allows the plant to feed its growing tuber underneath.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: When is the most important time for me to remove weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The most critical time to clear weeds is within the first 3 to 6 weeks after planting. Young crops are too weak to fight with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during this period.
ga: Be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 6 mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ darako tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose moisture quickly. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing of the lower leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei jieɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers under the ground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or when stem cuttings are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the year is enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: The very first rain after a dry season usually only wets the top surface of the dry soil. You should wait until the soil is moist at least wrist-deep (about 10 to 15 centimeters) so your seeds have enough continuous water to germinate and survive if there is a short dry spell right after.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi onine mli (aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15) koni odumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhi shi yɛ be kukuoo fɛɛ ni hɔmɔ baa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What causes ragged holes and tiny brown dirt inside the center funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ cone lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the central growing point of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind dark green or brown waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ayeɔ baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into white powder and get full of holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ feɔ futafuta ni eyɛ ŋmeii beni mikɛtoɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by grain weevils and insects that lay eggs inside the seeds before or right after harvest. If the grain was not dried properly before storage, the moisture allows these insects to multiply fast and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui amli dani akpaa loo yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtoɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i baaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kponɔgbɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch maximum sunlight. Lifting the leaves away from the damp soil also prevents fungal diseases and allows the leaves to produce more energy to feed the growing yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of insect pollination. If the plant feels stressed or cannot be pollinated, it aborts the flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Kɛji tso lɛ miinu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ loo enyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli Ebaafo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees lean over and fall to the ground before the fruit stems mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can easily break under the heavy weight of a growing bunch, especially during strong winds. Farmers prop them up with sturdy wooden Y-fork sticks or manage pests like root nematodes that weaken the underground corm.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni fãa oya yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ni tsii lɛ shishi. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Okwaafoi kɛ fɔji ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tsei ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ. loo nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ root nematodes lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I clear the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil. Even small weeds growing close to young crops act like thieves, leaving very little food for your main crops to develop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi bibii po Mɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ po fee amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛha tsei titrii lɛ akwɛmɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and decay when heavy water sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu afua eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When excess water stays on the land for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil, causing the roots to drown and preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii.

english: Why does sticky mud in my valley farm dry into hard, cracked ground that damages my crop roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ mijɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbi ni etsɔ hei ni wa ni egbɛ eshwa ni miifite mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil swells when wet and shrinks tightly as it dries under the hot sun. Mixing dry organic matter like compost or crop leaves into the soil breaks up the clay and prevents it from cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ fũuɔ kɛji edɔ, ni egbɔjɔ waa kɛji egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni egbi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ahe baai futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbala shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbala.

english: Why does covering the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass keep them alive during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as a shade cover over the soil, stopping the hot sun from evaporating the ground moisture. This keeps the soil cool and wet so the plant roots can drink water longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu nu be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and cannot handle direct heat from the sun. Tall shade trees or quick-growing shade plants like plantains shield young cocoa from harsh sunlight until they are mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers without producing fruit during hot, dry winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the air is very dry and hot, the pepper plant loses water too quickly and drops its flowers to protect itself from drying out. Keeping the soil well-watered helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya tsɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin with small harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni ŋmaa fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Plants need space to stretch their roots and leaves. When planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough strength to produce a good harvest.
ga: He ko he miihia tsei koni amɛgbala amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛji adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops look weak and pale even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most farm crops. They steal the fertilizer and soil nutrients meant for your crops, starving the crop plants even if there is plenty of water.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my corn turn yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the corn is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its oldest bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves and ears at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai kɛ toi ni miida lolo yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmei shishifãi bibii beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil year after year. Rotating cassava with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore essential plant food back into the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Cassava kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first small rainfall of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often only wet the top layer of dry soil without going deep. If a long dry spell follows immediately, the newly sprouted seeds will run out of water beneath the surface and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ ni eyaaa shɔŋŋ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ hoɔ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why should I plant different types of crops together on the same farm instead of just planting corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa kɛkɛ

english: Planting different crops together protects your farm because if one crop suffers from pests or bad weather, the other crops can still produce food and income. Different plants also share soil nutrients in ways that help each other grow stronger.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni ooodu yɛ he kome lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he. Ejaakɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ ye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi baanyɛ awo niyenii kɛ shika lolo. Tso fɛɛ tso hu jaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know which crops grow well next to my maize without choking it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi ni ekɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Crops like beans or peanuts pair well with maize because they draw nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while low-growing crops shade the ground to prevent weeds from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni kwɛɛɛ shi fioo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How can raising tilapia fish help my crops grow better on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tilapia ni mikwɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Water from a tilapia pond is rich in natural waste from the fish, which acts as a powerful organic fertilizer. When you use this water on crops like corn and vegetables, it feeds the plants and saves you money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ tilapia ŋshɔi lɛ amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jɛɔ loo mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ okɛ nu nɛɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai anɔ. Nu nɛɛ baaha tsei lɛ aye nii, ni ebaaha shika akafite tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Do I need a big natural river on my land to start raising tilapia alongside my crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná adebɔɔ mli faa agbo ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mabɔi tilapia kwɛmɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe?

english: No, you do not need a river. You can dig small earthen ponds or use plastic tanks filled with stored rainwater to farm tilapia right next to your crop fields.
ga: Dabi, faa he ehiaaa bo. Obaanyɛ otsa muji bu bibioo ko. Aloo okɛ plastic baagi ni nugbɔ nu ni ato eyi mli obɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ tilapia yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to leave grass or plant ground cover on empty patches of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi jwɛi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cover crops and grass act like a protective blanket over the earth. They keep the soil cool during hot weather, hold moisture in the ground longer, and stop heavy rains from washing away fertile topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛ jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I clear all plants and leave the land bare before planting?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni mishi he ko dani midu?

english: Leaving soil completely bare exposes it to harsh sunlight and heavy rain, which dries out nutrients and hardens the ground. Keeping gentle vegetation or mulch on the land keeps the soil healthy and easy to farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa aba enɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Tsei akwɛmɔ blɛoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsu nii.

english: If I plant flowers near my food crops, won't they just attract harmful insects to destroy my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu fɔfɔi yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe Ani fɔfɔi lɛ gbalaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛbafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers actually attract good insects like bees, which help your food crops produce seeds and fruit, as well as friendly predator insects that hunt and eat the pests that destroy your crops.
ga: Fɔfɔi gbalaa kooloi kpakpai tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa oniyenii tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. Tamɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su ni taoɔ ni amɛyeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: How do flowers on a crop farm help improve the overall harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei aŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ?

english: Flowers invite pollinators that are necessary for crops to set fruit properly. They also help improve soil condition when their roots loosen hard earth and their leaves fall to decompose into natural manure.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔ̃ɔ pollinators ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii awo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nine. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ, ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What can I do to make sure my farmland stays fertile enough for my children to farm in the future?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mibii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nii yɛ mli wɔsɛɛ?

english: You can protect your soil for future generations by constantly adding organic compost, rotating your crops, and keeping cover plants on the land so the soil stays rich in nutrients instead of wearing out over time.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha wɔsɛɛ yinɔi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and look weak early in the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for soil nutrients like nitrogen or lacks steady moisture. Adding organic compost or rich pond water gives the plant the energy it needs to stay dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost loo nu ni fa babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: I sprayed a chemical booster I bought at the local market, but my crops are still weak and small. Why didn't it work?
ga: Mikɛ tsofa ko ni mihe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ shwie nɔ. Shi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛhe ehiaaa. Mɛni hewɔ etsuuu nii?

english: Yield boosters cannot replace basic plant care. If your soil lacks basic food or water, or if the product was fake or applied incorrectly, spraying it will not force the crops to grow.
ga: Nibii ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ jeee nɔ ni akɛyeɔ tsei akwɛmɔ shishijee lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa loo nu bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ ji amale loo akɛtsuuu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa tsei akwɛ̃.

english: My plant leaves suddenly developed dark spots and curled up overnight. Could someone have put a bad spell on my farm?
ga: Mibaai lɛ ná ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbɔle amɛhe nyɔɔŋ kome. Moko ngɔ shɛɛmi yaya. Ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by plant diseases like fungi or viruses, often spread by insects or wet weather. Using the correct agricultural spray or removing infected plants will protect the rest of your farm.
ga: Tse helai tamɔ fungi loo muawai kɛ enɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ okwaayeli mli tsofa ni sa tsu nii loo ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The plant is pulling nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miihe niyenii kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist so the young cocoa roots do not dry out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa Koni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them properly allows each plant to grow strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji shwereɔ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with thick green leaves, but why are the tubers under the ground tiny?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ daa waa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lɛ?

english: The soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium. Nitrogen makes plants spend all their energy building top leaves instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni potassium hu faaa. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmaa baai yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e kɛ pee tubers nɛ tsii.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, but why do the flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or inconsistent watering causes plant stress. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my land yield less food every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to look thin and pale even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds eat from the same plate as your crops. They steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and fertilizer before your crops can drink them, leaving your plants underfed.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani onibii lɛ nuɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why are caterpillars hiding inside the center leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm hide inside the tight leaf funnels because it keeps them cool and protects them from sunlight while they eat the softest part of the plant.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai ni mli wa lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves on my corn plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the corn is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and fade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is my harvest getting smaller every time I plant maize on the same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps put essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no trees above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso ko bɛ amɛyiteŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate foliage and tender roots that cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, cooling the air and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden poles to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach high off the ground so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. The sunlight allows the leaves to make the energy needed to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni bulbs agboi ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots for too long, the soil drowns the roots, leading to rot. Planting on raised mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛyashi amɛbaagboi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during the hot dry season without making fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making their flowers dry out and drop off before pollination can happen. Providing light shade and consistent watering helps the plant keep its flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni mli tse ha tso lɛ, ni aha lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee tsɔnei ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like mites or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus they spread. This damages the leaf tissue, causing it to distort and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. ni kɛ sɛɛkuu kɛ sɛɛkuu baa

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating large holes into the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars, often Fall Armyworms, hatch from eggs laid on the leaves by moths. They feed aggressively on young leaf tissue to grow rapidly, which damages the plant's ability to capture sunlight.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛtsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ baai anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji oya koni tso lɛ adara oya. Enɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil that your crops need to grow strong. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii kwraa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily when the fruit bunch becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, requiring wooden props to support the weight against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ tso nibii atsu nii koni akɛfi tsɔne ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatswa lɛ.

english: How long do I usually have to wait after planting cocoa before I can harvest my first crop?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ beni midu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ dani manyɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually begin bearing fruit between 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take about 5 years to yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii enumɔ dani ewoɔ yibii.

english: How do I know when my young cashew trees are mature enough to start bearing nuts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cashew tso lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Cashew trees typically start flowering and bearing nuts around 3 years after planting, showing small pinkish-white flowers that develop into cashew apples with nuts attached underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii aaafee afii 3 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Fɔfɔi bibii jeɔ kpo. Su ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ cashew apple ni ŋmeii ekpɛtɛɔ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect itself from hot weather; the leaves will sprout back once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, lack of water, or poor pollination, which stops the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii. ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii

english: Can I plant quick crops like peppers or beans between my tree crops while waiting for them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii oya yɛ mitsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping quick-growing food crops between young trees makes good use of land and provides food and income while you wait 3 years for your main tree crops to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni akɛ dumɔwui woɔ mli lɛ haa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii 3 koni otso titri lɛ ada.

english: What happens if I plant my maize stalks too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete for light, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stalks and small, poorly filled cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are left near their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni ashiɔ jwɛi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, which starves the crops and slows down their overall growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my plantain suckers are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Nutrient-deficient plantain plants display slow growth, pale or yellow leaves, weak stems, and produce small or poorly formed bunches at harvest time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo amɛhe bɛ fɛo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds after just the first small rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Early rains can be followed by a sudden dry spell, which causes newly germinated seeds and delicate roots to dry up and die in the hot soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ anyiɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing all over the leaves of my garden eggs and vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ekɛ ehe miiwo eggplant kɛ aduawai ahe baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: Small holes in leaves are usually caused by leaf-chewing insects or caterpillars feeding on the crop, which weakens the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni yeɔ baa loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant grain from my standard harvest instead of buying dedicated planting seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mikpamɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe tso dumɔwui pɔtɛɛ komɛi

english: Grain harvested for food is meant for consumption and often produces uneven, weaker crops with lower yields when replanted. Dedicated seed crops are grown under strict conditions to ensure genetic purity, high germination rates, and resistance to common pests and diseases.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛha niyenii lɛ koni akɛye ni bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ yibii ni ejaaa ni egbɔjɔ ni ebaa shi fe be mli ni adu ehee lɛ. Aduɔ dumɔwui tsei titri yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa shishi koni ana akɛ amɛhe tse. ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ waa kɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ.

english: Why do seed production plots need to be kept separate from regular food farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie dumɔwui akwɛmɔ ŋmɔji kɛjɛ niyenii ŋmɔji ni afeɔ daa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Seed plots are kept isolated so that wind or insects do not bring in pollen from other crop varieties nearby. Keeping them separate ensures the seeds stay pure and retain their high-yielding traits for the next season.
ga: Abaagbala dumɔwui lɛ amli bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii akaŋɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ amli gbalamɔ baaha amɛhe atse ni amɛhiɛ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I test if the seeds I have stored will actually grow before I spend money planting my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ dani mafite shika kɛdu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds inside a damp cloth, rolling it up, and keeping it moist for 5 days. If 8 or more seeds sprout, your seeds are strong and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛwo nɔ ni okɛwo mli gbii 5. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: If my farmland does not hold enough water for rice, what other staple crops can I grow reliably?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa Mɛɛ ŋmãa krokomɛi ni he hiaa waa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like maize, sorghum, millet, cassava, and cowpeas thrive in drier soils because their root systems are efficient at finding deep moisture and they require far less water than rice to mature.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ taomɔ mli. Ni ebiɔ nu fioo kwraa fe ŋmãa koni akɛhoo.

english: How do I calculate how much seed I need if I want to plant a large field like one hectare?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui ayibɔ ni he hiaa lɛ he akɔntaa kɛji miitao madu shikpɔŋ wulu tamɔ hectare 1?

english: Every crop has a standard seed requirement per hectare based on ideal plant spacing. For instance, planting one hectare of maize typically requires about 20 to 25 kilograms of certified seed.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni he hiaa yɛ hectare kome mli ni damɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa nɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmãa hectare 1 ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kilogram 20 kɛyashi 25.

english: Why is it helpful to prepare my land in planned stages rather than all at once right before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaasaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaasaa fɛɛ shikome dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Preparing land in stages helps manage weed buildup, improves soil moisture retention, and ensures you are ready to plant immediately after the first major rain without rushing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ he saamɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi ni abua naa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ofeɔ klalo akɛ obaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ oyaiyeli tsuuu nii.

english: How can I tell when my maize crop is changing from growing leaves to producing grain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-abele lɛ etsake kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛtee dumɔwui ni woɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will notice tassels developing at the top of the plant and soft silks appearing on the young cob. At this stage, the plant stops growing taller and directs its nutrients into forming and filling the grains.
ga: Obaana ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ kɛ siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni ekwɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee dumɔwui lɛ ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with small fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete intensely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces them to stretch upward for light rather than using their energy to develop thick stems and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe koni amɛna la moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ koni amɛná tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating your crops with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do my crops mature faster during hot, sunny weather compared to cool, cloudy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ? Kɛ akɛto gbɛkɛ kɛ atatu gbii lɛ ahe

english: Plants use sunlight and warmth to create energy for growth. Higher temperatures speed up their natural growth cycle, causing them to flower and mature seeds much faster than during overcast or cooler weather.
ga: Tsei kɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛdara. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dalɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ oya kwraa yɛ atatu loo fɛ̃i be mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen or the ground is waterlogged and choking the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea when the soil is moist will help the leaves turn green and build strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni ekɛmiimɔ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil pests to build up in that area. Rotating your farm with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and stops pests from taking over.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Fertilizer works best when root systems have developed and the soil is moist, usually about two to three weeks after the seeds sprout. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ etsɔ hiɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulutsoo be shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight and lose moisture faster than roots can take it up. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective umbrella that keeps the young cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aná lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants dropping off before any fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from severe heat, sudden drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps the plants retain their flowers to grow fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũɔ daa ni ehaa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling upward and twisting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites hiding under the leaves. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays prevents the foliage from twisting and slowing down plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ni eha tso lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds very close together just to fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Spacing plants properly ensures each crop gets enough light and food to produce larger, healthier yields rather than many weak plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves on top of the soil around their crop stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi buɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or straw—called mulching—keeps the sun from drying out the ground too fast and blocks weeds from growing. It helps crops survive short dry spells by keeping moisture trapped around the roots.
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to harvest, and what happens if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Ni mɛni baaba kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves begin to turn yellow and fall. Leaving tubers in the soil for too long makes them woody, reduces starch quality, and increases the risk of rot during rainy weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛtsɔ tsei. Ehaa ashikiŋsha lɛ nɔ baa shi ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: What is eating small ragged holes through the leaves of my young corn plants, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ he? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Ragged holes inside young corn leaf funnels are typically caused by Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender growth. Inspecting the middle whorl of the plants early and applying approved insecticides or clean sand/ash into the funnel kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo ŋã/ashwishwɛ ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋã lɛ mli lɛ baagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Officer, is it true that rubber trees can stay strong and produce for many years without dying easily?
ga: Official Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ rɔba tsei lɛ ahe wa lolo ni amɛwoɔ yibii afii babaoo ni amɛgbooo oya?

english: Yes, rubber trees are very resilient crop trees. Once established in good soil, a rubber plantation can stay healthy and remain productive for over 25 to 30 years with proper care.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, rɔbɔt tsei ji tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ nii waa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, Rɔba ŋmɔji baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii fe afii 25 kɛyashi 30 kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rain or standing water in the farm affect my rubber trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi rɔba tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mature rubber trees are quite tough and handle water well, but prolonged standing water around young seedlings can cause root rot. Good field drainage keeps the trees strong.
ga: Rɔba tsei ni eda lɛ wa waa ni amɛtsuɔ nu he nii jogbaŋŋ. Shi nu ni yɔɔ dioo ni bɔle Young tsei lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: How long can I continue tapping latex from a single rubber tree before it stops producing?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ matswa latɛs ni jɛ rɔbɔt tso kome mli lɛ dani nitsumɔ lɛ akpa?

english: If you tap the bark correctly without damaging the tree's inner layers, a single rubber tree can yield latex continuously for 20 to 30 years.
ga: Kɛji otswa tso lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee tso lɛ mli fãi lɛ, Rɔba tso kome pɛ baanyɛ ajie latɛs be fɛɛ be afii 20 kɛyashi 30.

english: If I use rubber or plastic sheets around my crop roots, will it help keep water in the soil longer?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ rɔba loo plastic ni akɛbɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, using plastic or rubber mulch covers the soil surface, preventing water from evaporating under the sun and keeping the roots moist for long periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ plastic loo rɔba ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ hulu la shishi. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava or plantain together with my young rubber trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ rɔbɔt tsei bibii?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when rubber saplings are small, you can intercrop with food crops like plantain or cassava to get food and income while the rubber trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava adu amɛ. Koni ana niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei lɛ edara kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do rubber trees survive heavy rainstorms better than some other tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔba tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Rubber trees grow deep taproots that anchor them firmly in the ground, and their wood is flexible enough to bend with strong winds without breaking easily.
ga: Rɔba tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ŋmɛɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ. Ni tso lɛ nyɛɔ efoɔ ehe bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ efoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli ni ekuuu lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do we keep young rubber seedlings in black plastic polybags before planting them in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔkɛ rɔba tsei bibii woɔ plastic kotokui diji amli dani wɔduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plastic polybags hold moisture around the young roots and protect the delicate saplings from weed competition and soil pests until they are strong enough for the field.
ga: Plastic poly kotokui lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hiɔ shi. Shishifãi lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ akaŋshii ni jɛɔ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi amli lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Will weeds still be a major problem once my rubber trees grow big and bushy?
ga: Ani jwɛi baafee naagba wulu lolo kɛji mi-gum tso lɛ da ni etsɔ jwɛi?

english: No, once the rubber trees grow tall and form a dense leaf canopy, they block sunlight from reaching the ground, naturally slowing down weed growth.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ rɔbɔt tso lɛ da ni efee baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Ebaatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How much water do my young rubber saplings need right after transplanting them into the field?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa mi rɔbɔt tso lɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young rubber saplings need steady moisture during their first few months so their roots can establish deeply. Planting at the start of the rainy season helps them get enough water.
ga: Rɔba dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu nii mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What kind of fertilizer should I give my rubber trees so their bark stays healthy and strong for tapping?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ akɛwo rɔbɔt tsei amli koni eha amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe awa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Applying balanced fertilizers rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium encourages thick bark growth and continuous latex production without weakening the tree structure.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse lɛ aya hiɛ ni ekɛ latɛs aya nɔ afee. ni ehaaa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant its own space allows roots to spread and stalks to grow thick and strong enough to bear big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii wuji anɔ.

english: Why do I need to make big earth mounds before planting my yams instead of putting them into flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni makɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick under the ground, so they need loose, soft soil to expand easily. High mounds create deep, soft soil and allow heavy rainwater to drain away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. ni oha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli koni ekagbo

english: Why do I need to keep plantain trees next to my young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantains woɔ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for food, especially nitrogen, or a sign of too little water. When the plant lacks food, it steals nutrients from its lower leaves to keep the upper leaves and growing cobs alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii he bolɔmɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii Ejuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baa lɛ kɛ ŋmei ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look droopy during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Curling up is the plant's natural defense to reduce sunlight exposure and conserve moisture until the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni ekɛbuɔ ehe koni ekɛba hulu la shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when plants experience extreme dryness, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tso lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my cassava produce smaller tubers even if the weeds are not touching the cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ? Ni jwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ kpaaa gbee?

english: Weed roots spread quickly underground and steal water and soil fertilizers long before their leaves touch the cassava. Removing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients available for the cassava roots to swell.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani baai lɛ taa ŋmei lɛ he. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot if I do not tie them to sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mikɛfiii tso nine nɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Heavy tomato branches bend toward wet soil where fungal diseases live. Tying stems to wooden stakes lifts the leaves and fruits off the ground, allowing air and light to circulate and keep the crop clean and healthy.
ga: Tomato niji ni tsii lɛ baakoto kɛya shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, ewoɔ baai kɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ mli. ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe atse ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see tiny holes and green dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ

english: Small holes and dirt inside the central leaves are signs of caterpillars like the fall armyworm feeding inside the heart of the plant. Treating the leaves early protects the shoot where new cobs develop.
ga: Buu bibii kɛ muji ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji ŋmeii, tamɔ asraafoi ni egbee shi ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe okadi. Baai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmeii ni feɔ ŋmeii heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested cowpeas turn into powder after sitting in a sack for two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ powder beni mita kotoku lɛ mli nyɔji enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay microscopic eggs inside the pods before harvest, which hatch inside stored sacks and eat the beans from the inside out. Storing dry beans in sealed, airtight bags starves these insects of air so the crop stays intact.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani akpaa amɛ. Efoɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni ato mli ni eyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi wo kotoku ko mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli lolo.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. When the plant doesn't get enough nitrogen from the soil, it steals it from older lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ejuɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow so short and weak when I plant it right under large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs direct sunlight all day to make food and grow strong. Big shade trees block the light and their roots steal water and plant food from the soil, leaving your maize weak and stunted.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmãa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni enyɛ efee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei wuji tsiɔ kane lɛ naa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow roots that stay close to the top of the soil, making it hard for them to hold up a heavy bunch of fruit. You can protect them by propping the main stem up with strong, wooden Y-shaped poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛaahiɛ aduawai ni tsii. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y ni ooowo nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear away the weeds around my cassava plants during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Cassava tsei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 2-3 lɛ mli?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal the water, light, and soil nutrients that cassava roots need to grow big tubers early in the season.
ga: Cassava tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmei shishifãi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Young cocoa pods drop off naturally when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil food, or insect damage. Giving the trees light shade and keeping the soil moist helps the tree keep its pods.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ Tso lɛ he hulutsoo kɛ sũ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii lɛ amli.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing many flowers, but the flowers drop off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Giving the plants steady water and light mulch around their roots keeps them cool so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my cassava tubers grow larger when I plant them on raised soil ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraa waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Loose, raised soil in ridges makes it easy for cassava roots to expand and grow fat without fighting hard soil. It also helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers do not stay soaked in water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ fɔ afata he ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ejieɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akabote nu mli.

english: Why do the stems of my cassava plants rot at the base after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot breathe if water sits on top of the soil for too long, which encourages harmful soil fungi to rot the stems. Planting on raised mounds allows heavy rain to run off quickly.
ga: Kasava shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ woɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do tiny flies gather under my tomato leaves and make the leaves curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi tomato baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiiha baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are whiteflies that suck the juice from tomato leaves and pass along leaf curl diseases. Spraying the underside of the leaves with neem water can keep whiteflies away.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tomato baai amli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ baa curl hela baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshwie ŋmeii yɛŋ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea plants mostly when the flowers first begin to show?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ babaoo beni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft young pods that attract insect pests looking for easy food. Protecting your plants with neem or recommended sprays right when buds open stops pests from ruining your harvest.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ woɔ nu mli nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni gbalaa kooloi ni taoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Buu otsei lɛ ahe kɛ neem loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he kɛji ŋmeii lɛ gbele pɛ. Ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshinii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and lose water faster than their small roots can pull from the soil. Providing shade from fast-growing plants like plantains keeps the ground moist and protects their delicate leaves until they grow stronger.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni amɛfiteɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shade ni jɛɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ ebaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop down during the afternoon heat even when the soil is not dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ shi shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water faster than roots can absorb it, so the plant wilts temporarily to conserve moisture. Once the air cools down in the evening, the plant will stand up straight again.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baadamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into tomatoes when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away pollen or physically break the fragile flowers off the stems before pollination happens. Without pollination, the plant cannot form fruit.
