ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe loo etswa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ dani abaanyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: What makes my vegetable seedlings look weak and droopy right after I move them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving a plant disturbs its small root system, causing root shock. The plant needs a few days in its new location to rebuild fine root hairs and adjust to the new soil.
ga: Tso ko ni ajieɔ lɛ gbalaa eshishifãi bibii lɛ amli, ni ehaa eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehe miihia ni tso lɛ ahi he hee ni eyɔɔ lɛ gbii fioo komɛi koni enyɛ efee shishifãi bibii. Ba ekoŋŋ ni okɛ ohe awo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant many maize seeds together in the exact same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too closely together fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa tsei lɛ bibii waa baa.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stem cutting should face up when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male fã ni esa akɛ mafo mi yucca niji lɛ anɔ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised leaf nodes along the stem. These nodes should point upwards toward the sky so the shoots grow properly above ground while roots sprout underneath.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. raised along the stem Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to reach high into the air to catch sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more energy the plant sends underground to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ eshɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔŋŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops make my cassava tubers smaller?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibii?

english: Weeds consume the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your cassava needs to grow. Less food for the cassava plant means smaller tuber roots at harvest time.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Niyenii fioo kɛha ŋmei tsei lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi bibii yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Stored seeds can lose their ability to grow if they were exposed to moisture, heat, or insect damage during storage, which kills the living embryo inside the seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ, dɔlɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɔmɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ fɛɛ agbo.

english: Why are my pawpaw plants flowering heavily but not producing any fruit for me to sell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Some pawpaw plants are purely male. Male plants produce flowers to supply pollen, but they will never grow fruit themselves. Keeping too many male plants in your farm wastes land and fertilizer without bringing you any money.
ga: Pawpaw tsei komɛi ji hii tsei pɛ. Tsei ni hii woɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ pollen. Shi ewoŋ yibii ko kwraa. Tsei hii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ fe nine lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ shika ko baaa kɛha bo.

english: How can I tell if a crop flower on my farm is male or female?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji hii loo yei?

english: Female flowers usually have a small swollen bump at their base that looks like a tiny fruit, while male flowers grow on thin stems without any bump. Learning to spot this helps you know which plants will actually yield food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi yei yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni efuu. Yɛ shishigbɛ, ni tamɔ tso yibii bibioo ko yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi hii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ. without any bumps Enɛ kwɛmɔ kasemɔ baaye abua bo ni ole tsei ni woɔ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Will keeping too many male plants on my farm lower the money I make at harvest?
ga: Ani tsei hii babaoo ni mikpaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, because male plants consume water, soil nutrients, and space without giving you crops to sell. You only need a small number of male plants to pollinate a large field of fruit-bearing female plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni hii lɛ nuɔ nu. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ haaa bo. Ohe miihia ni oná tsei hii fioo komɛi koni okɛwo tsei yei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko mli.

english: Should I cut down the plants on my farm that produce only male flowers?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ lɛ?

english: You should remove most of them, but leave a few (about 1 male plant for every 10 female plants). Removing excess male plants frees up land and nutrients for the female plants to give you a bigger, more profitable harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo kɛjɛ ohe. Shi ashi fãi komɛi. (Aaafee tso nuu 1 kɛha tsei yei 10 fɛɛ.) Kɛ́ ajie tsei hii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tsei yei lɛ aná shikpɔŋ kɛ niyenii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpa nibii babaoo ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: Why am I getting a very small harvest even though my field is full of green, flowering plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo pɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ fɔfɔii moŋ lɛ?

english: Your field may be filled with mostly male plants or male flowers. A crop field can look bushy and healthy, but if the majority of the plants are male, they cannot produce the fruits or seeds you need to sell.
ga: Ekolɛ tsei loo fɔfɔi ni ji hii babaoo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Ekolɛ ŋmɔji baanyɛ afee tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Shi kɛji tsei babaoo ji tsei hii Enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo dumɔwui ni otaoɔ ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my crop flowers drop off the stem without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Male flowers naturally drop off after releasing their pollen into the air or onto insects. Only female flowers stay on the plant and swell into fruits after receiving pollen.
ga: Fɔfɔi hii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni amɛjie pollen kɛtee kɔɔyɔɔ mli loo beni kooloo ko etswa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai beni amɛná pollen sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pumpkin vines produce so many early flowers before any pumpkins appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pumpkin wain tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi oya dani pumpkin lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pumpkin vines usually produce male flowers first to attract bees and pollinators to your farm. The actual pumpkins will only grow later when the vine begins producing female flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pumpkin wain tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛkɛgbala ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Anɔkwa pumpkins daa pɛ kɛji wain tso lɛ je shishi ewo fɔfɔi yei.

english: Do all crops need separate male and female plants to produce a yield?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ agbala tsei hii kɛ yei amli koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Not all crops work the same way. Crops like cocoa and tomatoes have both male and female parts inside the same flower, while crops like pawpaw or nutmeg often have completely separate male and female plants.
ga: Jeee ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ tomato Hii kɛ yei fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ pawpaw loo nutmeg Bei pii lɛ, tsei hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi kwraa yɛ.

english: How many male plants do I actually need to leave on my land for good pollination?
ga: Tsei hii enyiɛ ehe miihia ni mashi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa?

english: For most crops that have separate sexes, keeping 1 male plant for every 8 to 10 female plants is enough. Any extra male plants beyond that ratio take up space without adding value to your harvest.
ga: Kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ. Eshɛɔ he akɛ abaakpa tso nuu 1 kɛha tsei yei 8 kɛyashi 10 fɛɛ. Tsei hii ni fe nakai mlijaa lɛ baahe he ko ni amɛkɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko fataaa okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: What should I do if I plant seeds and end up with more male crops than female crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji midu dumɔwui ni miná tsei hii babaoo fe tsei yei?

english: You should identify the male plants early, pull out the extra ones, and replace them with new seedlings or female cuttings so your land is used mainly for fruit-producing plants.
ga: Esa akɛ oyɔse tsei hii mra. Gbalamɔ tso ni fa fe nine lɛ. ni akɛ dumɔwui heei loo yei ni afolɔ awo najiaŋ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii titri kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow on land where rain regularly washes away the surface dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain washes away the top layer of soil, it carries away all the vital nutrients your crops need to feed on. Without this rich topsoil, plants remain weak and produce very small harvests.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Ajieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ aye lɛ hu kɛyaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni egbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii fioo pɛ.

english: How can I tell if my land is too poor to grow a good crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ohia tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: If your soil turns hard like concrete when dry, washes away easily during heavy rains, or only grows thin, yellowish weeds, it lacks the organic food and structure needed to support strong crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit kɛji egbi Eshɛɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Aloo jwɛi ŋmɔŋ ko kɛkɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni he hiaa ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crops still fail even after I buy and apply expensive fertilizers on bad land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mihe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa wo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If the soil is severely washed out or too hard, rainwater carries the fertilizer away before roots can absorb it. You must fix the soil structure first so it can hold onto the plant food you apply.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ nu waa loo ewa tsɔ Nugbɔ nu lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ otsake bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ ohe akpɛtɛ tso niyenii ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to loosen and soften the soil before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafee lɛ blɛoo dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Softening the soil creates small air pockets and breaks up hard earth, allowing young crop roots to spread out easily, drink trapped water, and anchor the plant firmly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ blɛoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa Ehaa tsei bibii ashishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya Nuu nu ni ekã lɛ ni omɔ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ.

english: What happens to my plants if I plant directly into hard, unbroken ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ du shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etseee nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: When planted in hard ground, crop roots get trapped near the surface and cannot reach deep moisture. The plants easily starve, dry out during hot days, or get blown over by strong winds.
ga: Kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni enyɛŋ eshɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli shɔŋŋ. Hɔmɔ baaye tsei oya. Egbi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ

english: Why do my crop roots stay tightly clumped together instead of spreading through the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miikpɛtɛ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots get stuck when the surrounding soil is too tightly packed. Softening the ground during land preparation gives roots the freedom to stretch out and collect nutrients from a wider area.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni afeɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa heyeli ni amɛkɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛbua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa kɛjɛɔ he ko ni da.

english: How does soft soil help my crops survive when the rain stops falling for a few days?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Soft, loose soil acts like a sponge that absorbs rainwater deeply and holds onto moisture longer, giving crop roots access to water even during short dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni eŋɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa nu yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli po.

english: Why do crops on one part of my farm yield a lot while another part produces almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni fã kroko lɛ wooo nɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Soil quality varies across a farm. The high-yielding areas usually have deeper, softer soil that holds nutrients, while low-yielding areas often suffer from eroded topsoil or compacted ground.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Hei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛi hiɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa lɛ kɛ naagbai ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni shwieɔ shi loo sũ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Is it really worth spending money and time to prepare bad soil before planting?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ abaafite shika kɛ be ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu nii?

english: Yes, preparing bad soil prevents total crop failure. Investing in land preparation ensures that the money you spend on seeds, labor, and fertilizers turns into a large harvest that covers your costs.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni asaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kwraa lɛ naa. Shika ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shika ni ofiteɔ yɛ dumɔwui, nitsumɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni haa ohe nyɔmɔ.

english: Can rushing to plant without properly clearing and working the soil harm my final harvest?
ga: Ani oyaiyeli ni mikɛbaadu nii ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ he oshara mli?

english: Rushing into planting on unprepared ground leads to weak plants, lost seeds, and wasted money. Proper soil preparation protects your crop investment and gives you the best yield possible.
ga: Oya ni akɛyaaduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaaa nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. dumɔwui ni elaaje kɛ shika ni afiteɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ni eha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if a coconut variety will give me a heavy harvest before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmei srɔtoi ko baawo yibii babaoo dani adu?

english: High-producing coconut varieties are naturally bred for yield, but you need to buy certified seedlings from reliable agricultural nurseries to ensure the tree has the genetic potential for heavy fruiting.
ga: Atsɔ adebɔɔ nɔ akwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ ohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli he ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa fɔmɔ nii ni haa ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some coconut trees grow very short while others grow tall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei komɛi yɛ kuku waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kɛlɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different coconut varieties have different growth habits; dwarf varieties stay shorter and start fruiting earlier, while tall varieties take longer to produce but often live and bear fruit for a much longer time.
ga: Kokooi srɔtoi Amɛyɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Dwarf henɔi lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi mra. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii be babaoo fe nakai.

english: What physical signs should I look for in a coconut seedling to know it will grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadi esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ ŋmei tso mli koni male kɛji ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Choose seedlings that have thick sprouts, deep green leaves, and strong root bases from healthy parent palms, as these show the plant has high growth potential.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni tsei bibii ni mli wa yɔɔ mli. baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ shishitoo ni wa ni jɛ fɔlɔi adɛŋ ni wa lɛ mli Ejaakɛ nibii nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ dalɛ he nyɛmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: If I plant a high-yielding coconut seedling, why might it still produce very few fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmei tso ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ewoɔ yibii fioo lolo lɛ?

english: A good seedling gives your crop potential, but environmental factors like poor soil, lack of water, shade, and weed competition will prevent the tree from actually yielding well.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eshɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ he. Shi shihilɛ mli nibii tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, nu ni bɛ, hulutsoo, kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii baanyɛ atsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii kpakpai.

english: How does the weather during the dry season affect my coconut harvest?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ saa ŋmei kpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Coconut trees need constant water to turn flowers into fruits; severe drought creates environmental stress that causes young coconuts to drop off before maturing.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmei tsei daa koni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛwo aduawai. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, akokoi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛbaa.

english: Can adding fertilizer make a poor-quality coconut tree yield as much as a high-production variety?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo yibii tamɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Fertilizer improves the environment so a tree can grow its best, but if the plant naturally has low genetic potential, extra food alone cannot make it produce like a high-yield variety.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ tsei yɛ fɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, Niyenii krɛdɛɛi pɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni tamɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baaa.

english: What is the best type of soil environment for planting coconuts in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ Ghana?

english: Coconuts thrive best in deep, well-draining sandy loam soils where their roots can easily breathe and access underground water without getting waterlogged.
ga: Kokooi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu mlɛo ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my coconut trees shed their flowers before fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flower shedding usually happens when the tree faces environmental stress, such as poor soil nutrients, extreme heat, or sudden drought, which limits its ability to support full fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ naa baa shi.

english: Will watering my coconut trees during dry months increase the number of fruits I harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo miŋmei tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha miyibii ni mikpaa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, providing steady water keeps the soil environment moist, helping the tree maintain its production potential and yield fruits consistently throughout the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibiiwoo ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli ni ewoɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does my coconut farm yield fewer fruits now than when the trees were younger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii abɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo amrɔ nɛɛ fe be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Over time, trees absorb nutrients from the soil; without feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer, the growing environment degrades and crop production drops.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ. Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ efite ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree take so many years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong trunk and deep roots before they can support heavy pods, which usually takes about three to five years depending on the variety you plant.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ, ni enɛ damɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or when tiny insects called midges are not present to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ Nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ baa koni ebawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet weather when excess shade and poor airflow keep water sitting on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nu baa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I trim branches off my healthy cocoa trees when they are already growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli be mli ni amɛma shi jogbaŋŋ momo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree, which stops fungal diseases from growing and helps the tree put its energy into making larger pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Enɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or that heavy rain has flooded the roots and prevented them from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni eha shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl downwards during the dry harmattan afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miihoso yɛ Harmattan shwane ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl up in intense heat as a defense mechanism to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing vital water.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn as hard as a rock after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or manure, which act like sponges to keep the earth soft, loose, and able to hold moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, efee mlɛo ni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yes, because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving the cassava behind with plenty of space and time to swell its roots underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa hegbɛ kɛ be babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to your local soil, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize get full of holes and insects after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ kooloi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils multiply inside stored maize if the grain was not dried completely before storage, as remaining moisture creates the ideal environment for pests to hatch.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛtoɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ afɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow fast. It often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep for the roots to reach, or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. aloo be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the rainy season stays too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rains leave water sitting in the ground for days, it drowns the roots by cutting off oxygen, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the crop dies, that extra nitrogen stays in the earth to feed your next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as long dry spells, excessive sun heat, or a lack of shade trees. It can also mean there are not enough tiny midges (pollinating insects) around to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. hulu la ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo ni bɛ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ kooloi bibii (pollinators) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tsei awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves catch sunlight to manufacture food that gets stored in the ground as tubers. Staking spreads the leaves out wide so every leaf gets maximum sunshine, which results in much larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmeii. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa babaoo bɔni afee ni baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why does locally saved rice seed yield less than the modern seed varieties sold by agricultural officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi hɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from past harvests lose their vigor, purity, and disease resistance over time. Modern certified seed varieties are specifically bred to produce more grains per panicle and withstand local pests and dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. hetsemɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ be mli lɛ Akwɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo yɛ panicle kome mli. ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ.

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that enters the plant roots and clogs its internal water tubes, starving the leaves of water even if the ground is soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni shikpɔŋ ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa nu he hɔmɔ yeɔ baai lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ.

english: How do small weeds hurt my crops if there is enough rain and sunshine for all of us?
ga: Te jwɛi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha wɔ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and space from underground roots long before you notice them shading your crop above ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli oya dani oyɔseɔ akɛ eefo oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid spraying liquid pesticides on my crops in the middle of a hot sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ he?

english: Hot afternoon heat causes liquid chemicals to evaporate into the air before they can work, and water droplets on hot leaves can act like magnifying glasses that burn the plant. Pests also hide under leaves during hot hours to avoid direct heat.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkafee hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my grain seeds spoil or get eaten by insects when stored inside plastic sacks after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ kɛ́ akɛto plastic kotokui amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains stored with even a little moisture trap heat inside plastic sacks, causing mold to grow and attracting weevils. Grains must be dried thoroughly until they snap between your teeth and stored in airtight containers or treated sacks.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui lɛ toɔ plastic kotokui ni mli edɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmeii baa ni egbalaa ŋmeii. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaakumɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotokui ni atsa mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and die after water sits on my field for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe, just like humans need air. When heavy rainwater covers the ground for too long, it pushes out the air, causing the roots to drown and preventing the crop from taking up food, which turns the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kɛje kpo ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ aaawo nu mli Etsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nii Ekɛ kaadi ŋmɔŋ baa

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil and planted seeds on sloped land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eduɔ dumɔwui yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Fast-flowing rainwater gains speed moving downhill and grabs the light, nutrient-rich topsoil and loose seeds. Planting crops along ridges across the slope breaks the force of the water and keeps your soil and seeds in place.
ga: Nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ haa eyaa oya kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ la ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it important to dig small water channels through my farm before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atsa nubu bibioo ko? Ani ehe miihia ni matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Channels act like clear paths that guide excess rainwater safely off your field. This prevents water from pooling around crop roots, stopping root rot and protecting your farm from being washed away.
ga: Funnels tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ oyale mli. Enɛ haaa nu abɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ afite ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he koni ekaho.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to make mounds or ridges before planting cassava and yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afee gɔji dani adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so roots can expand easily into big tubers, while raising the crops above ground level so heavy rainfall does not collect around the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the soil during dry days, stops heavy rain from striking the dirt directly, and keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Which crops can I safely plant in low-lying land that stays wet during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔji ni nɔ edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Crops like rice and cocoyam thrive in very wet soil because their roots are adapted to water. Dryland crops like cassava or maize will rot if planted in low areas that flood easily.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ nu mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu shwieɔ shi oya lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when all the big trees on the field are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni afolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full sun. Large trees provide natural shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa from overheating until it grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei wuji haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainy storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit. When heavy rains soften the soil, the roots lose their grip, allowing strong storm winds to easily push the heavy plant over unless it is supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Shishifãi lɛ baafee mɛi ni nyɛŋ amɔmɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ahum ni tswaa lɛ tswaa waa aahu akɛ tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi oya. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: When crops lack water, their leaves wilt, curl, and dry up from the bottom up. When crops have too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, feel soft or slimy, and the soil around them stays muddy and smells sour.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ, amɛkpãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ shwiemɔ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli ewo muji ni eŋɔɔɔ.

english: Why do leaf spots and rots spread faster on my tomato plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases thrive in wet, damp conditions. Raindrops splash soil and fungal spores onto crop leaves, and the wet leaf surfaces give the fungi the moisture they need to enter and infect the plant.
ga: Fungal helai yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔshiimɔ shwieɔ sũ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa lɛ koni ebote tso lɛ mli ni ekɛ hela awo mli.

english: Why can some wild plants from the bush be grown on my farm while others die when I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei komɛi ni jɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi baanyɛ agboi kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Crops originally from wild bush environments can adapt to your farm if the soil, water, and sunlight conditions match what they are used to. Plants die when the new location is too dry, too sunny, or lacks the natural soil nutrients found in their bush habitat.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ koo mli shihilɛi amli lɛ kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la shihilɛi lɛ kɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ kpãa gbee. Tso lɛ baagbo kɛ́ he hee lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Hulu miitso tsɔ. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni anaa yɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashihilɛhe lɛ mli.

english: Can I successfully farm food crops in Accra even though the weather and land are different from the Ashanti region?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii yɛ Accra yɛ omanyeyeli mli eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Yes, many food crops can grow in Accra despite the climate differences. While soil and rainfall vary by region, using crop varieties suited for dry areas and ensuring proper watering allows crops to adapt and yield well outside their original home regions.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii babaoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Accra yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ kpokpai amli moŋ, shi Tsei srɔtoi ni sa kɛha hei ni nu bɛ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii kɛ nu ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ atsake amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛmaŋ kpokpaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very well in forest areas but struggle to produce in dry grassland areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooi amli shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛwo yibii yɛ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops react strongly to their environment. Forest areas offer rich, moist soil and high humidity, while grassland areas have hotter sun and drier soil. Crops suited for forest conditions need extra shade, organic matter, and irrigation to survive in drier places.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ henumɔi ni mli wa kɛha shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Kooi amli hei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, jwɛi shikpɔji lɛ yɛ hulu ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi. Tsei ni sa kɛha koo mli shihilɛi biɔ hulutsoo, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, kɛ nu babaoo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hei ni egbi.

english: How do officers determine which new areas or regions in Ghana are good for farming specific crops?
ga: Te onukpai lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛle hei loo kpokpai heei ni yɔɔ Ghana ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko dumɔ?

english: Agricultural researchers test crop varieties in different soils and climates across the country. By observing how well the crops grow and yield in each trial location, they can tell farmers exactly where those crops will succeed best.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kaa tsei srɔtoi amɛkwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛtsɔ bɔ ni tsei daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ shikpamɔ he fɛɛ he ni akwɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔɔ okwaafoi lɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye omanye fe fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a new piece of land in another region will support my crops before I move there to farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ hee ko ni yɔɔ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii dani mafã kɛyatsu okwaayeli yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: You can test the land by looking at what native plants grow naturally there, checking if the soil holds moisture without waterlogging, and starting with a small trial plot or consulting local extension officers to test the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka he ko okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔ ni ji maŋ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Ni oje shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔji bibii ni oooka okwɛ lɛ nɔ. Aloo yaa maŋ lɛ mli shweremɔ he nitsulɔ ko ŋɔɔ koni eka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ.

english: Does land cleared fresh from the virgin bush automatically make good soil for my crops?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee Ani jwɛi obalayoo fro lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Freshly cleared bush land is usually rich in natural plant nutrients from fallen leaves over time. However, it still needs proper clearing of roots and weeds so your crops do not have to compete for space and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii ni jɛɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ amli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia lolo ni ajie shishifãi kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ehe ehiaaa ni onibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe awo he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why do wild plants in the bush produce smaller fruits compared to the crops I cultivate on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Wild bush plants spend most of their energy competing with weeds and surviving naturally. Cultivated crops on a farm receive weeding, spacing, and care, allowing the plant to direct most of its energy into growing larger fruits and seeds.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛ jwɛi akaŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, akwɛɔ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui wuji ni amɛduɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it possible to grow good crops on small plots near big towns instead of deep inside rural forest areas?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ? ni bɛŋkɛ maŋtiase wulu Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ kooi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ akrowai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, urban and town farming is very practical, especially for fast-growing crops like vegetables and maize. As long as you have good soil, adequate water, and protection from urban waste, crops can thrive close to city markets.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋtiase kɛ maŋtiase mli okwaayeli he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛha tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ aduawai kɛ abele. Shii abɔ ni oyɔɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ maŋtiase mli jwɛi he. Nibii ni aduɔ hu baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei lɛ.

english: Why do my crops flower at a different time of year when I plant them in a different region of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli beni miduɔ yɛ Ghana kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Plants take cues from their environment. Changes in rainfall patterns, average temperatures, and daylight hours between regions signal to the plant when to shift from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsei nine shɛɔ okadi nɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ mli latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni yɔɔ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ lɛ Etsɔɔ tso lɛ be ni eshɛɔ ni etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ nɔ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops grow so fast during the first year after clearing a bush, but start performing poorly in later years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ebɔi nitsumɔ ni ehiii kwraa yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Clearing fresh bush leaves behind years of built-up natural compost (humus) that feeds the first crop. Over time, crops extract those nutrients from the soil, so without adding manure, fertilizer, or crop rotation, the soil fertility gradually drops.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sũ tsei lɛ, eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii (humus) ni ebua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ koni akɛye klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ baajie nakai niyenii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ afata he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi fiofio.

english: What actually happens to my maize if I leave too much space between the plants when planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi gbɛ babaoo yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ beni miduɔ lɛ?

english: When you leave too much space between maize plants, sunlight hits the exposed soil and causes weeds to grow rapidly. These weeds will compete with your maize for food and water, while also wasting valuable land you could have harvested from.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi gbɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ Hulu la lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa ni kulɛ obaanyɛ okpa nii lɛ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Not always. If crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer. This makes them grow tall and weak, resulting in small cobs or poor yields.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛkwɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii loo yibiiwoo ni ehiii.

english: How do I know if I am using my land efficiently when planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miitsu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Efficient land use means having the exact right number of plants on your field—not too few and not too many. If you see wide open spaces of bare soil after your crops grow, you are underusing the land and inviting weeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ oná tsei babaoo ni sa yɛ oyale mli. Jeee fioo tsɔ ni jeee babaoo tsɔ. Kɛji ona hei ni mli tse ni shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ nɔ beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ fioo ko pɛ miitsu nii ni ofĩ jwɛi nine.

english: Why shouldn't I just scatter my maize seeds freely on the field like I do with some small seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ heyeli mli tamɔ bɔ ni mafee ŋmãa bibii lɛ?

english: Scattering maize seeds leaves random uneven spaces where weeds can easily take over, and makes plants crowd each other. Planting in organized lines with proper spacing ensures every plant gets equal light and food.
ga: Abele ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni jwɛi baanyɛ aŋɔ he fɛɛ he oya. ni ehaa tsei feɔ ekome Dumɔ yɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ fɛo ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster in certain open parts of my farm than under the crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ hei komɛi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fe tsei ahe baai ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds need direct sunlight to germinate and grow fast. Where your crop leaves cover the ground, they block the sun and suppress weeds, but open empty spaces give weeds full light to take over.
ga: Jwɛi hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya. He ni otso lɛ baai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa ni egbe jwɛi lɛ. Shi he ni agbele lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ naa la babaoo.

english: How can proper plant spacing help me reduce the amount of time I spend clearing weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha be ni heɔ koni ajie jwɛi lɛ aba shi?

english: When you plant at the correct distance, your mature crop leaves form a continuous cover over the soil. This shade smothers young weeds naturally, so you spend less labor and money weeding.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ he ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baai ni eda lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baashwie jwɛi bibii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shika fioo ko pɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ he.

english: How many seeds of corn should I be putting into one hole when I am planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ adu?

english: Placing one or two seeds per hole at recommended line distances keeps the roots from choking each other. This gives each corn plant enough room to build a strong stem and produce large cobs.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ awo bu fɛɛ bu mli yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛto lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akakpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin with small cobs even though I used good land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ hiɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ po?

english: Thin plants with small cobs usually happen when plants are crowded or forced to share space with aggressive weeds that sprouted in wide gaps between rows.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni baa shi ni kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli babaoo loo anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛja he ko.

english: What is the danger of having too few plants on my farm plot?
ga: Mɛni ji osharai ni yɔɔ tsei fioo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Having too few plants leaves your field loose and exposed. You end up spending more time fighting weeds on bare soil while harvesting far less grain than your piece of land is capable of producing.
ga: Tsei fioo pɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Obaaye be babaoo ni okɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ awuu yɛ be mli ni okpaa dumɔwui fioo fe bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo lɛ.

english: How does the distance between my crop rows affect how well my maize grows?
ga: Te gbɛ ni kã midumɔ ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa mi ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Row spacing ensures plants don't block light from one another while allowing you to comfortably walk through to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the crops.
ga: He ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haaa amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ onyiɛɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli ni ofiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland turn into thick mud so quickly after just a little rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ muji oya lɛ?

english: Soil turns muddy fast when it has high clay content or poor drainage. Clay particles hold water on the surface instead of letting it sink deep into the ground, which can trap water around plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ muji oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni baanyɛ ahi nu ni bɔle tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ mli

english: How can I tell if my soil is holding too much water for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your soil stays muddy for several days after rain and your crops start developing yellow leaves or soft, rotting stems near the ground, it means the soil is waterlogged and plant roots are suffocating from a lack of air.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ efee muji gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ je shishi amɛná baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsei shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: What can I add to my land to stop water from gathering on top like mud?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata mishikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nu akabua ehe naa yɛ nɔ tamɔ muji?

english: Adding organic matter like well-rotted manure, compost, or dry plant leaves breaks up heavy soil. This creates small spaces in the ground so water can sink in like a sponge instead of standing as mud on top.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsei ahe baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaagbala sũ ni tsii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ bibioo ko baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni nu lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeedamɔ shi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ

english: How does heavy rain affect newly planted crop seeds and young seedlings?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa dumɔwui ni adu ehee kɛ tsei bibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall on bare soil can wash away small seeds, compact the ground so seedlings cannot break through, or cover young plants in thick mud that blocks sunlight and stops them from growing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui bibii, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha dumɔwui akabote mli. Aloo okɛ muji ni mli edɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa amɛdara lɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the condition of my land matter if I am already buying good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he hiaa kɛji akɛ miheɔ dumɔwui kpakpai momo lɛ?

english: Good seeds need healthy soil to grow well. If the land is too hard, waterlogged, or lacking nutrients, even high-quality seeds will struggle to sprout strong roots and produce a good harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai he miihia shikpɔŋ kpakpa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ, nu eyi mli obɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ po bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I prevent my soil from drying out and baking hard like a rock in the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mishikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi ni efee shiŋŋ tamɔ tɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: You can cover your soil with a layer of dry grass, straw, or leaves, which is called mulching. Mulch shades the ground from the direct sun, keeping the soil soft and locking in moisture longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops after planting on it for several years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ afii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting crops continuously drains essential plant food from the soil. Without giving the land a break, adding compost, or rotating crops, the soil becomes tired and loses its ability to feed new plants.
ga: Tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei heei ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi, loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeee.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon even when the soil was wet in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, crop leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture and usually recovers when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Can growing different crops together on the same land help protect my soil?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi ni mikɛbaadu yɛ he kome lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Yes, intercropping helps protect your land. For example, planting beans alongside maize covers the soil to prevent erosion, keeps the land moist, and adds natural nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsiɔ ŋmãa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ

english: Is rainwater better for my crops than getting water from a well or river?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe nu ni maná kɛjɛ nu bu loo faa mli?

english: Rainwater is usually better because it is soft, free of harmful salts or chemicals, and naturally absorbs tiny amounts of plant-nourishing nitrogen from the air as it falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ nu hi fe no ejaakɛ eyɛ blɛoo. Ebɛ ŋmei loo tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ejieɔ nitrogen fioo ko ni haa tsei hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ.

english: How can I estimate how many acres of land I have before starting my plantain farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ he akɔntaa dani mije plantain ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Knowing your acreage helps you buy the right quantity of plantain suckers and farm inputs; a common rough estimate is counting off approximately 70 paces by 70 paces for one acre.
ga: Oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ole lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oheɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni sa. Akɔntaabuu ni mli wa Enɛ ji nɔ ni miihe ashɛ steps 70 kɛ steps 70 yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my plantains in neat, straight rows rather than scattered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu plantains yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo, ni ja moŋ fe ni aaagbɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows makes it much easier to walk through the farm, manage weeds, apply fertilizers, and harvest heavy bunches without damaging surrounding plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ, awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa jwɛi babaoo. ni efiteee tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants look weak whenever weeds grow closely around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ be mli ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, light, and soil nutrients directly from the plantain roots beneath the ground, effectively draining the crop's strength and slowing its growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ plantain shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better to use chemical sprays or manual clearing to control weeds on a plantain farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ loo akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ plantain ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Using suitable weed chemicals saves significant labor and time on larger fields, keeping the ground under plantains clean without repeatedly disturbing the shallow root system with cutlasses.
ga: Tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ kɛ be babaoo akafite yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ plantains lɛ shishi lɛ mli atse ni okɛ dagger akafite shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: How does keeping the ground completely clear of weeds help my plantain yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi plantain ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When the soil beneath plantains is free of weeds, all available plant food goes straight into the crop, resulting in thicker stems and larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ jwɛi Tse niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni plantain tsei lɛ akui lɛ hu daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: If I spray weed control chemicals under my plantains, will it harm the crop?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ Ani ebaaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: As long as you spray carefully near the ground and avoid spraying the chemical directly onto young plantain leaves or leaves of low suckers, the crop will remain safe.
ga: Shii abɔ ni okɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ plantain baai bibii loo baai ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nibii ni adu lɛ baahi shi shweshweeshwe lolo.

english: How often should I carry out weed control on my plantain farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Weed control should be done regularly whenever young weeds begin to emerge beneath the crop, especially during the rainy season when weeds grow fastest.
ga: Esa akɛ atsu jwɛi ahe nii daa be fɛɛ be ni jwɛi bibii baabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be mli, be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: What primary work must I do continuously to keep an established plantain farm healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ nitsumɔi titrii esa akɛ matsu he nii daa koni makwɛ plantain ŋmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ?

english: The main ongoing task on an established plantain farm is keeping the ground free of competing weeds, along with removing old leaves and nurturing healthy replacement shoots.
ga: Nitsumɔ titri ni yaa nɔ yɛ plantain ŋmɔ ko ni ato ama shi lɛ mli ji ni aha jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ akaje jɛmɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, ajieɔ baai momo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ koni amɛhe awa.

english: Can a plantain farm stay productive on the same land for many years?
ga: Ani plantain ŋmɔ ko baanyɛ akwɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii babaoo?

english: Yes, plantains can continuously yield on the same land for decades if the soil health is maintained and weeds underneath are consistently controlled.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ daa.

english: Why are my neighbor's plantain stems so thick while mine remain thin and short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ plantain tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ waa yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Thick trunks grow when plantains get uninterrupted soil nutrients without competing against weeds underneath, whereas weeds underneath stunt trunk thickness and delay growth.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ daa kɛji plantains lɛ nine shɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yeee akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential food for plant growth. It can also happen when heavy rain saturates the soil and prevents the plant roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ ni eha tsei shishifãi lɛ akamu.

english: Why does my land produce less maize each season if I plant it on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli kɛji midu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize draws specific nutrients out of the soil every season. If you plant it repeatedly without resting the land, rotating with crops like beans, or adding manure, the soil becomes depleted and weak.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji odu shii abɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin, producing smaller heads, fruits, or tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni no haa bulb, aduawai, loo tuber lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide natural shade and cool moisture, helping young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more light and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enáa la babaoo ni ehaa helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: This is a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease damages the leaves and prevents the plant from growing large, healthy cassava roots underneath.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi.

english: This issue is called blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, which usually occurs when watering is irregular or after sudden hot dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ ni eba trukaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very hot temperatures, drought, or sudden overwatering. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli trukaa fe nine. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: A single light rain only wets the top layer of dry soil. If seeds germinate and a long dry spell follows, the tender roots will dry up and die in the hot soil below.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi fioo pɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ba. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off extra suckers growing at the base of plantain stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong shoots, allowing the main tree to focus its energy on producing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their delicate leaves from getting scorched by direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the cocoa establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni oooshi loo odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni enáa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Which suckers should I take from my old plantain trees to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mikɛje dumɔwui momoi amli kɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers' that have narrow, sword-like leaves and a thick base. They grow much faster and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers', which have broad leaves early on and tend to grow into weak plants.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ kui wuji fe ‘suckers’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ mra ni amɛfɔɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Does it matter which part of the cassava stem I use for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni akɛbaadu?

english: Yes, the middle portion of a mature stem is best because it contains healthy buds and enough stored food to sprout strongly. The green top tip rots easily in the dirt, and the bottom wood is too hard and slow to sprout.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ waa. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edaa fiofio.

english: Yams need their leaves lifted up into the sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off wet soil, which prevents rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potatoes lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient for green leaf growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmeii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets pests build up in the earth. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi baa shi ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seed immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry stretch before the true rainy season starts. If your seeds sprout during a brief rain and run out of moisture soon after, the fragile seedlings will dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli, ni hulutsoo bɛ yɛ be fioo ko sɛɛ Dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What is eating small holes inside the middle shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, a caterpillar that feeds on young leaf shoots. Applying neem-based treatments or approved pest controls directly into the central plant funnel controls them effectively.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ neem fee loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot, if the soil dries out unexpectedly, or if the plant gets too much nitrogen. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using balanced plant food helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baa shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Trukaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbi. aloo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ tso niyenii ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plants growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo hela ko ni ŋmeii yɛŋ kɛbaa Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ Ebaatsi baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: If too many suckers grow at once, they fight with the main plant for food and water. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough nutrients to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ tso lɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What is making holes in the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the top funnel of the plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended biological controls like neem oil or approved sprays can protect your corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do small insects bore tiny holes into my stored maize grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu bibii yɛ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are maize weevils, which attack dried grains if they contain moisture or are left exposed. Drying your corn very well under the sun and storing it in airtight bags will starve the insects of air and keep your grain safe.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmãa ŋmeii. ni tutuaa dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ kɛji amɛhe edɔ loo ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe in waterlogged soil. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Lifting the vines off the ground on tall stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and stay away from damp soil diseases, which helps the plant store more energy and make larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the leaves. Controlling these insects early with soapy water or appropriate sprays prevents them from damaging the plant and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ nu loo spray ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni amɛkagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni aha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your field.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for plant growth. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color and grow stronger.
