ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my commercial hybrid maize harvest for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jarayeli ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one strong harvest. If you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the new plants will produce much smaller yields, grow unevenly, and lose their resistance to diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha kpamɔ kome ni mli wa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baawo yibii fioo kwraa. dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why are small worms eating the inside of my young corn shoots after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ amli beni nugbɔ enɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which thrive during early rains and feed on fresh green shoots. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps protect your crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni shwereɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning excess canopy branches lets sunlight and air in, which keeps the pods dry and reduces the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping allows you to harvest maize quickly for early food and income within three months, while the slower-growing cassava stays in the ground to provide a major harvest later in the year.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa oya kɛha niyenii mra ni onáa shika yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha akpa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to conserve energy. Providing adequate water at the roots and light shade helps flowers stay on the stem and turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miibɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Crinkled or rolled leaves are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites. Spraying soapy water or suitable insect treatments controls these pests so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛ samla loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni sa baaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground right around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why does my harvested dried maize get full of small holes and powder when I store it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛ́ akɛto kotoku mli

english: Insects called weevils eat into stored maize if it was not dried completely or stored in pest-proof containers. Thoroughly drying your grain in the sun and using hermetic (airtight) storage bags prevents weevil damage.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ baaye ŋmãa ni ato kɛji akɛ egbiko kwraa loo akɛto nɔ ko ni ŋmãa nyɛŋ abote mli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu mli ni akɛ kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite amɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open, full-sun field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside them creates a living shelter that protects the young trees from heat and retains soil moisture until they are mature enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa he ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la ni fa babaoo.

english: Planting cassava too close together causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and resources to develop large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, leaving the land weak. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. gbɔjɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If your soil is light in color, dry, hard to dig, or if your previous crops had pale yellow leaves and slow growth, your soil is low on nutrients. Adding animal manure, compost, or chemical fertilizer restores the soil's capacity to nourish healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbi, ewa akɛ oootsu nii, loo kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi amli ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves with holes are usually a sign of insect pests, like the fall armyworm, feeding on the leaves, or a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Inspecting under the leaves for tiny caterpillars helps identify whether you need to apply pest control or add fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɔɔ mli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe okadi, tamɔ baai ni egbee shi, ni yeɔ baai lɛ, loo nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kɛji ehe miihia ni oye ŋmeii loo ŋmeii awo mli.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and will quickly steal the limited water, fertilizer, and sunlight available in the soil. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a fair chance to build strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei, ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during the hot season without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ekɛ pepper wooo lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes flower drop because the plant gets stressed and tries to conserve water. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass (mulching) and watering early in the morning keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛbu nu he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) shwie tso lɛ shishigbɛ, ni akɛ nu wo mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot hours is a survival mechanism to prevent water loss through the leaves. If the leaves bounce back in the evening, it is normal heat response, but if they stay curled, the plant needs more water or protection from pests.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ tomato mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala ni akɛtsiɔ baabii lɛ amli nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Kɛji baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli Enɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, shi kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, nu babaoo loo hebuu he miihia tso lɛ kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I save maize seeds from my current harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crop varieties lose their yield power and disease resistance in the next generation. Buying certified seeds every season guarantees uniform plant growth, stronger resistance to pests, and higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite yibiiwoo kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ada daa. Ehe wa jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nibii ni anáa babaoo

english: Why do insects destroy my stored maize and beans so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects thrive inside stored grain if it still contains moisture or is kept in permeable bags. Thoroughly drying your grain in the sun until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags or sealed containers prevents insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli kɛji amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli loo akɛto kotokui ni nu tsɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Gbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli koni kooloi akafɔ.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very sensitive roots and thin leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a natural umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do government seedlings come in black plastic bags instead of bare roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli lɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛwoɔ plastic kotokui diji amli yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: The soil inside the black plastic bag keeps the young roots moist, dark, and safe from damage while being moved to your farm. It prevents the seedling from going into shock and dying before it reaches your field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ plastic kotokui diji amli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akafee shoo ni amɛgboi dani amɛshɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I not plant my cassava sticks too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, and their roots fight for nutrients in the soil. Giving them enough space allows the underground tubers to expand and grow big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen, which is its main food for growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing that fertilizer or nutrient-rich soil is needed.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold or droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves droop on hot afternoons as a self-defense trick to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat. This helps the plant trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly during the hottest hours.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ he ni hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my cashew trees without turning into nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers fall off prematurely when the tree is attacked by tiny sucking pests or when it lacks enough moisture during the flowering phase. Spraying safely against pests and keeping the root zone healthy helps flowers set into nuts.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ tutua lɛ loo kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akwɛɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akatsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my young coffee trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-kɔfi tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming removes unnecessary branches that steal energy from the main trunk. Opening up the tree allows sunlight and air to reach all parts, which prevents diseases and encourages the plant to put its energy into producing heavier berries.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Tsei lɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo yibii ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest when I plant the exact same crop every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly without giving the ground time to heal. Rotating your main crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps put natural nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Tse kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsa Tsɔmɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do simple weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of soil for everything?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and space meant for your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get full access to all the food and moisture in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu kɛ he ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around young tree crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket over the soil. It stops the sun from drying out the ground too fast and keeps the roots cool during warm periods.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food plants need to grow green and strong, or the soil has too much standing water that is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nu ni ekã shi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many small flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower loss usually happens when the weather is too dry, when the soil lacks nutrients, or when tiny pests attack the flowers.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when water stays trapped in the soil around the roots for too long without draining, allowing ground fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni atswa lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up into tight shapes and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are often a defense response to heat, but in tomatoes, it usually means tiny insects like whiteflies have spread a leaf-curl virus into the plant while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ titri akɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies egbɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ mli beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ eshwã.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around the main mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajieɔ nyɛ tso titri lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots allows them to steal water and food away from the main plant, which results in much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves into the sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture enough energy to build big tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the sun gets extremely hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too hot, pepper plants shed their blossoms to save moisture and protect the main stem from dying of dehydration.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni ebu tso titri lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops actually harm them even if I give the crops fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer and water out of the soil before your crop's roots can reach them, leaving your crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ hɔmɔ aye ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni he hiaa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that heats up the soil, which can dry out and kill the delicate new sprouts before regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows soil pests that target that crop to build up in high numbers.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: Why is it important for me to measure exact distances between my trees instead of just planting them wherever there is open space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ masusu he pɔtɛɛ ni mi tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, nyɛɛ du tso ngɛ he tsuaa he nɛ he ko nɛ a ngɛ.

english: Measuring proper planting distances ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow. If trees are planted too close together, they fight for resources and spread diseases easily, but if they are planted too far apart, you waste land and allow weeds to overrun your farm.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛduɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ amli oya ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa. Shi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni kɛ ohe teŋ jɛkɛ tsɔ Obaafite shikpɔŋ ni oha jwɛi baaho oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting more economic trees on my piece of land automatically give me a bigger harvest at the end of the year?
ga: Ani cashew tsei babaoo ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, planting too many trees causes overcrowding. Overcrowded trees produce small, weak fruits because they are competing for light and soil food, which ultimately results in a lower total yield than a farm planted with recommended spacing.
ga: Dabi, tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ la kɛ shikpɔŋ he akaŋ kɛha niyenii lɛ. Enɛ baaha yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi yɛ naagbee fe ŋmɔji ni adu yɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛtoɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young tree crops struggle when I clear away all the big existing trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ momo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young tree crops are sensitive to harsh sunlight and strong dry winds. Keeping appropriate shade trees creates a cool microclimate that protects young leaves from scorching and helps the soil hold moisture during hot dry spells.
ga: Tsei bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa he waa. Tso ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in open areas of my farm compared to under the thick leaves of mature trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto tsei wuji ahe baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe

english: Weeds need direct sun to grow fast. Once mature crop trees expand their canopy and shade the ground, the heavy shade deprives weeds of sunlight, naturally slowing down weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da lɛ, ebaagbala eshishi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hɔnɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava together with my newly planted economic trees on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shika tso ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ama niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei?

english: Yes, but only during the first couple of years while the trees are young. Cassava can provide quick food, but because its roots feed aggressively, you must plant it far enough from the young trees so it does not steal their water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ pɛ mli. Cassava baanyɛ aha niyenii oya. Shi akɛni eshishifãi lɛ yeɔ tsei babaoo hewɔ lɛ, Ehe miihia ni Odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni ekaju enu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the lower branches of my trees stop bearing fruit when the top part of the tree gets very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ niji lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo beni tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaves need sunlight to produce energy for flowers and fruits. When the upper branches grow too thick, they block sunlight from reaching the lower branches, causing those lower parts to weaken and stop producing.
ga: Hulu la he miihia baai koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛ́ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli tsɔ tsɔ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ fã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why do flowers fall off my crop trees without turning into fruits during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Developing fruit requires a lot of water and energy. When a tree experiences severe water stress during a dry spell, it drops flowers to save moisture and protect itself from dying.
ga: Yibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Kɛ tsei na nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: My old economic trees produce very few fruits now; why do you recommend cutting them back instead of just adding more fertilizer?
ga: Mi shika helɛtemɔ tso momo lɛ miiwo yibii fioo ko pɛ amrɔ nɛɛ. Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ afo amɛ mli moŋ fe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafata he kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: As tree stems age, their internal pathways become inefficient at moving nutrients from roots to leaves. Cutting back old trees stimulates fresh, energetic shoots to grow, restoring high fruit yields faster than applying fertilizer to old wood.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda Tso lɛ mli gbɛi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya baai lɛ amli. Tsei momo ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni yibiiwoo lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya fe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei momo amli.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right against the main stem of my young tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: The active feeder roots that absorb water and nutrients spread outward around the tree under the edge of its leaf canopy, not right at the trunk base. Fertilizer placed directly against the stem can burn the bark and will be missed by the feeding roots.
ga: Niyenii shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ehe. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi Jeee tso lɛ shishi Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ masɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishi. ni shishifãi ni yeɔ lɛ lɛ hu baafo mli.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for long-term tree crops like cocoa, oil palm, or cashew?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ kookoo, ŋmei fɔ loo ŋmei?

english: Permanent tree crops need deep, well-drained soil where roots can grow deep to find water. If your land floods frequently or has hard rock close beneath the surface, tree roots will rot or fail to anchor properly.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu. Kɛji nu shwieɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ loo tɛi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbo loo amɛkpɛtɛŋ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why am I being advised to cut down my cocoa trees when some of them are still bearing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awo mi ŋaa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tsei lɛ be mli ni amɛteŋ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmeii lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees infected with Swollen Shoot Disease cannot be cured with chemical sprays. Cutting down the infected trees and surrounding host plants is the only way to destroy the virus completely and protect healthy trees nearby from getting infected.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei ni amɛshishifãi efuu lɛ atsa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpataa hela lɛ hiɛ kwraa. ni ebu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and rot before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess leaves and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm and keeps the pods dry so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fuji lɛ edaaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under direct tropical sun. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa gets established.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Will leaving large forest trees on my cocoa farm steal nutrients away from my crop?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei wuji ni mashi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: certain shade trees actually help cocoa trees grow better by blocking harsh winds and extreme sun heat. Their deep roots draw nutrients up to the surface, and their fallen leaves rot to create rich, natural fertilizer for your cocoa.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ ni etsĩɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Ni baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ koni ekɛfee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha o-cocoa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree if I want to get more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛji miisumɔ ni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning directs the tree's energy into making pods rather than growing extra foliage. Opening up the center of the tree also lets light and air inside, which prevents fungal diseases and makes room for flowers to form on the main trunk.
ga: Tso lɛ he ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii moŋ fe ni ebaakwɛ baai krokomɛi. Gbɛ ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ hu haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa fɔfɔii yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves naturally during long dry spells to conserve water and survive drought. Spreading dry grass or crop leaves around the base of the tree as mulch holds moisture in the ground and reduces leaf loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ lɛ mli. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai abɔle tso lɛ shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaa ni baafite lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do many tiny flowers appear on my cocoa trunk but drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ shi amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny beneficial insects like midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. If the weather is too dry or heavy chemical sprays kill these midges, the flowers remain unpollinated and drop off the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, anɔ koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi amli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni naa wa lɛ gbeɔ mɛi nɛɛ. No mli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ eshɛko amɛhe lolo ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my old farm getting smaller and fewer every harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ miifee bibii be fɛɛ be lɛ? Nikpamɔ be?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, they exhaust the natural nutrients in the soil, and their internal stems become less effective at moving food. Refreshing the soil with organic manure or specialized cocoa fertilizer gives the trees the energy to produce larger pods again.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafite. Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛ ko wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees very close together to fit more crops on my piece of land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces trees to compete with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. This results in tall, weak trees that yield fewer pods and allows diseases to jump easily from tree to tree.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai fioo pɛ baa. Ebaanyɛ etu kɛjɛ tso kome nɔ kɛya tso kroko nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so fast and thick right after I clear old trees to restart my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mijie tsei momoi lɛ koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Old tree branches create a dense canopy that blocks sunlight from hitting the ground, keeping weed seeds asleep. Once you cut those trees down, direct sunlight hits the bare ground and triggers weed seeds in the soil to germinate rapidly.
ga: Tsei momoi aniji lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ. ni ekɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ Kɛ́ ofo nakai tsei lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is waterlogged. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of green leaves, but give me very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani oooha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots to build large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei agboi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that provide vital shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How does placing dry grass around my pepper plants help them survive the dry season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te pepper tsei yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from stealing moisture from your pepper plants.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaju nu ni yɔɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and off the damp ground, which also prevents soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa mli kɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ hu anaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool with shade or mulch helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ shade loo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main tree. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni suckers (tso) babaoo ni miida yɛ tso kome he lɛ fa babaoo. Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Black Pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, damp conditions. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight in and air flow through, keeping pods dry and reducing rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Ragged holes in young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's funnel. Checking the crop early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem spray protects the plant from major damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ gbɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. Nitrogen is the main nutrient that keeps leaves green and healthy, so adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays flooded with excess water during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away quickly so the tubers remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by severe water stress during hot weather. Protecting the plants from insects and keeping the soil moist prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings necessary shade and soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Seeds should be planted after the soil receives two or three steady, deep rains so the ground holds enough moisture to help seeds germinate without drying out under the hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai anɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why does my yam crop need wooden stakes to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves upward toward sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, helping the plant catch more light to produce large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwa ŋwɛi koni enine ashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ naa la babaoo ni ekɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are armyworms attacking my maize stalks so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs that hatch rapidly into hungry caterpillars. They target young maize because the soft, juicy leaves inside the plant funnel provide ideal food for fast growth.
ga: Katerpilar ŋmei lɛ woɔ wɔji ohai abɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa bibii ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ adaraa oya.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local soil and harsh weather, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: I just acquired a new plot of farmland, which crop should I plant first to test if the soil is fertile?
ga: Miná shikpɔŋ hee ko kɛkɛ. Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu klɛŋklɛŋ koni maka kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts are ideal for newly acquired land because they fix nitrogen into the soil, improving fertility naturally while giving you a quick harvest to assess your soil's health.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas loo peanuts hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ hee ni anáa. Ejaakɛ eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa okpaa nii oya koni okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha.

english: If I buy my seeds late and miss the start of the rainy season, can I still plant my maize?
ga: Kɛji ohe dumɔwui sɛɛ ni oshɛɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee he lɛ Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa?

english: Yes, but you should choose fast-maturing or drought-tolerant maize varieties rather than full-season varieties, so the crop can mature before the rains stop completely.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ ohala ŋmãa henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Mohu ɔ, hla tso slɔɔtoslɔɔtohi nɛ a yeɔ be ɔ mi tsuo. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ adara dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa kwraa.

english: If I cannot afford to buy all my crop seeds at once, which ones should I prioritize buying and planting first?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ shikome hu? Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mikɛhemɔ kɛ dumɔ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ?

english: Prioritize buying long-duration crops like cassava or yam first, as they need the entire rainy season to grow, while short-duration crops like vegetables can be bought and planted later.
ga: Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ sino loo atomo klɛŋklɛŋ. Ejaakɛ esa akɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, abaanyɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ aduawai, ni adu sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do crops planted late in the season grow much slower than those planted right when the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops planted early benefit from the 'nitrogen flush'—a natural burst of nutrients released in warm soil at the first rain—whereas late-planted crops miss this boost and face declining soil moisture.
ga: Tsei ni adu lɛ náa ‘nitrogen leaching’, ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ amli lɛ he sɛɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ naaa nɛkɛ yifalɛ nɛɛ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni baa shi lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava together on the same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ be kome mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving sunlight and space for the slower cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la kɛ ŋwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ koni ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ akwɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen or is planted too close to other crops, forcing it to pull stored nutrients from old leaves to feed the growing top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo ekwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ. Anyɛɔ enɔ koni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato kɛjɛ baai momoi amli ni ekɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive chemical fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on leaf growth instead of fruit set.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe yibiiwoo.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even though the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This is typically caused by bacterial wilt, a soil pathogen that gets inside the plant stem and blocks water movement, causing the plant to collapse quickly during hot afternoons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu lɛ gbɛfaa naa. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi oya yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my previous harvest or buy certified seeds from the agro-dealer?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli loo ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for high yield, uniform growth, and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds often lose vigor and carry pests or diseases over from previous seasons.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. uniform growth and disease resistance Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa ni amɛwoɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and the branches swelling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eniji lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is a key sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It weakens the tree, reduces yield, and spreads through small insects called mealybugs, often requiring infected trees to be removed to protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi titri ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ mɔ ko yɛ Cocoa Swole Shoot Virus (CSSVD). Ehaa tsei gbɔjɔɔ, ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ biɔ ni ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Can a sick cocoa tree spread its sickness to healthy trees nearby?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases—especially viruses like Swollen Shoot and fungi like Black Pod—spread easily to nearby healthy trees through insects, rain splashing, or infected farm tools.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo helai, titri lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii diji, gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii, nugbɔshiimɔi loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What are those tiny bugs crawling on my cocoa stems, and are they bad for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛhiii kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Those insects are likely mealybugs or capsids. Mealybugs suck sap from the tree and carry viruses, while capsids bite young shoots and pods, causing them to dry up and die.
ga: Ekolɛ kooloi bibii lɛ ji mealybugs loo capsids. Mealybugs lɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ, ni amɛji mɛi ni hiɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni capsids lɛ ŋmɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii. ni haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet, cool, and humid conditions. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods helps keep it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and small pods during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees need consistent moisture to keep flowers and young pods alive. During severe dry spells, the tree drops them to save water and keep itself from dying.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbii bibii lɛ ahi shi. yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei baashwie amɛ shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce much less cocoa now than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo cacao fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees get older (usually past 20 to 25 years), their ability to absorb nutrients declines, and they become weaker against diseases. Old, low-yielding trees usually need to be cut down and replanted with new seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda Beni be hoɔ (bei pii lɛ, ehoɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25) lɛ, nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ baa shi. ni helai nyɛŋ eye amɛnɔ jogbaŋŋ Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni afo tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ ni adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Do my young cocoa trees grow better under full sunlight or under larger shade trees?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be wulu shishi?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from shade trees or food crops like plantains to protect their leaves from sunburn and heat stress. Mature cocoa trees can handle more light, but still need partial shade to stay healthy.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ hulutsoo tsei loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ la babaoo. Shi ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo ko lolo koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa tree if I want to harvest more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing air and sunlight to pass through the tree. This keeps fungal diseases away and lets the tree focus its energy on growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm has run out of nutrients for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa miduɔ nii?

english: When soil loses its nutrients, crop leaves turn pale or yellow, trees grow very slowly, and pod production drops significantly. Adding fertilizer or organic manure restores these lost nutrients.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii ni elaaje nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do weeds growing on the ground harm my tall cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ mi kakao tsei kakadaji lɛ awui?

english: Weeds compete with cocoa trees by stealing water and nutrients from the soil. They also trap moisture around the base of the trees, creating a damp environment where pests and fungal diseases can breed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛjuɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ hu shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afɔ́ yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to each other, the plants compete for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of putting energy into growing big cobs, they stretch upward to fight for light, resulting in weak stems and poor yield.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji Moŋ lɛ, amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛye la lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I rotate my cassava crop with groundnuts or cowpeas in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei atsake ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava takes up a lot of nutrients from the soil over its long growth cycle. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, naturally refreshing the land so your next crop grows stronger.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ edalɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ adebɔɔ naa Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted when the soil is hard and packed down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni efiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand underground by pushing through soft soil. If the ground is hard or heavy with clay, the tuber cannot expand easily, causing it to bend, split, or stop growing larger.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ Yitso lɛ hu nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo, ni no haa efoɔ, efoɔ, loo ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and easily burnt by intense heat. Direct sunlight dries out their leaves and soil moisture too quickly, which is why temporary shade crops like plantains are planted alongside them to act as natural shields.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji edɔ waa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni aduɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii lɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save moisture and energy. High temperatures can also dry out the flower pollen, preventing the plant from forming fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi. Tsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii

english: Cool, damp weather allows fungal spores to spread quickly through rainwater splashing from infected soil or surrounding trees onto healthy cocoa pods, causing black pod disease.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ nɔ loo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Kɛha kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ekɛ black pod hela baa

english: Why do fall armyworms hide and feed inside the center funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The central shoot or funnel contains the tenderest, most nutritious leaves. Armyworms hide inside this moist pocket because it protects them from direct sunlight, rain, and birds while giving them easy access to food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ loo cone lɛ mli. Asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ kotokui ni mli efɔ nɛɛ amli ejaakɛ ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ kɛ okpoi ahe, yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛnáa niyenii hu mlɛo.

english: Curled cassava leaves with yellow patches are a sign of cassava mosaic disease. This virus is spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on leaf sap, preventing the plant from making food properly.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. ni yeɔ baa mli nu Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce many flowers but very few nuts during some dry seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ hulutsoo bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Strong harmattan winds or extreme dry heat during flowering can dry out cashew blossoms or blow them off before bees and insects can pollinate them to form nuts.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo latsaa ni mli egbi waa yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha cashew fɔfɔi lɛ agbi loo etswa amɛ dani ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii anyɛ afee amɛ ŋmeii ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop flat black spots on the bottom right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ.

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium. This usually occurs when dry spells interrupt regular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔi ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ naa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize a few weeks after the first major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Planting late means missing the main growing window when soil moisture is at its best. Your crop may end up maturing during a dry spell, leading to weak plants and low yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔ samflɛ titri lɛ baaje mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Ekolɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I miss the early planting period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mifoɔ mra be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops rely on a specific window of good weather and soil moisture to establish roots quickly. If you miss this window, the soil dries up or loses nutrients, causing the plants to become stunted.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ samflɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee shishifãi oya. Kɛji otsi samflɛ nɛɛ naa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to finish clearing and preparing my land before the rain begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atse shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early ensures your soil is ready the moment the planting window opens. If you clear land after the rains start, you lose precious time and end up planting late.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo kɛji dumɔ samflɛ lɛ gbele pɛ. Kɛji otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ Obaafite be ni jara wa ni obaagbe naa ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How will buying better tools help my crops if I am using the same seeds as before?
ga: Te nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni miheɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛji mikɛ blema dumɔwui tsu nii?

english: Good tools help you complete tasks like land clearing and weeding quickly. Doing this work fast allows you to plant at the exact right time so your crops catch every rainy day.
ga: Dɛŋdade kpakpa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ogbe nitsumɔi tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ lɛ naa oya. Nɛkɛ nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ oya nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ ashɛre daa gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: What happens to my maize if I leave it in the field past the right harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛho kpamɔɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Missing the harvest window exposes matured crops to pests, mould, and bad weather in the field. This lowers the quality of your grain and reduces how much money you can sell it for.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ he tseee, ni shika ni obaanyɛ okɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more when I delay harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ?

english: When crops pass their peak maturity window, their natural skin or husks weaken and fruits soften, making them much easier targets for farm insects and diseases.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ho amɛdalɛ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛ adebɔɔ mli hewolo loo amɛhewolo lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni aduawai lɛ baafee blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaatsɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why can't I just plant my seeds anytime in the year as long as I use fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu dumɔwui afi muu lɛ fɛɛ, kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii?

english: Fertilizer only works when there is enough soil water for plant roots to drink it in. Planting outside the rainfall window means seeds won't germinate and fertilizer goes to waste.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii pɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ samflɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without making fruit when the weather turns very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need moderate heat and moisture during their flowering window. If late planting pushes flowering into a hot, dry window, heat stress forces the plant to drop its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei biɔ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔ sɛɛ tsɛ lɛ, fɔfɔii baaje kpo yɛ samflɛ ni mli edɔ ni egbi mli. Heat haomɔ baaha tso lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi.

english: What is the danger of transplanting my tomato seedlings into the field in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ ooodu tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli?

english: Transplanting during the hottest part of the day puts extreme stress on seedlings. Planting in the cooler morning or evening window gives young plants a better chance to anchor roots without drying out.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa tso bibioo lɛ naa hegbɛ kpakpa ni ekɛmaa eshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ egbiŋ.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops taller than mine even though we planted the same seed variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tso lɛ kwɔ fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu dumɔwui komekomei lɛ?

english: Planting even a week earlier allows crops to take advantage of early soil nitrogen released by the first rains. Missing that window means your crops miss that initial boost of plant food.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ otsi kome dani eshɛɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa sũ mli nitrogen ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ. Nakai samflɛ ni bɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná tsei aniyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ shishijee.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same field where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts add nitrogen to the soil naturally through their roots, which acts as free fertilizer for maize. Mixing them helps both crops grow better and gives you two different foods from one field.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni aheee nɔ ko Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli aba.

english: Can I plant tomatoes together with maize on my land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can, but tall maize plants create deep shade that blocks sunlight from tomatoes. It is best to space them out or plant tomatoes on the sunny edge so they get enough light to produce good fruit.
ga: obaanyɛ ofee Shi ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tomatoi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ loo ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ koni ona la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push little stems into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi etso bibioo lɛ kɛmiijɛ mli lɛ? kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts form their pods underground. After the flowers are pollinated, the stems bend down and push into the soil so the nuts can grow safely under the ground.
ga: Peanuts feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my corn plants turn yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip indicate that your corn is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer. Nitrogen helps the plant stay green and grow big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia o-ŋmei lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Can I plant rice on my dry upland farm, or does it always need flooded water?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ? Aloo ani esa akɛ nu atsɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not all rice needs flooded fields. There are special upland rice varieties designed to grow on dry land with normal rainfall, while lowland rice varieties require heavy soil moisture.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu afua. Don ŋmãa henɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni afee koni adu yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ waa.

english: Can I just plant the corn seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from modern hybrid corn will produce weaker plants and lower yields in the second year. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures strong growth and full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo ni baa shi aba yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ baaha amɛdara waa ni amɛná dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my corn seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When corn is planted too closely, the roots and leaves fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stems and small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii loo amɛlaaajeɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Staking tomato plants keeps the branches and leaves off the damp soil. This prevents fruit rot, protects the plant from ground insects, and allows fresh air to reduce diseases.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ niji anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ejieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akafite. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he koni helai aba shi.

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests and diseases multiply in the ground, lowering your yields over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is usually caused by irregular watering or a lack of calcium in the soil while the fruit is growing. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding organic compost helps stop it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing on my land instead of cutting them all down when clearing my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ beni mijieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving select trees provides shade that protects young crops from scorching sun, prevents heavy rain from washing away fertile topsoil, and drops leaves that naturally decay into nutrient-rich organic compost.
ga: Tsei ni ahala lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa anáa hulutsoo ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni etsɔɔ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly during short dry spells after I clear all vegetation off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ? Beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to heat and wind. Keeping scattered shade trees or ground cover helps retain soil moisture, creating a cool microclimate that keeps crop roots hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewɔ. Shade loo mulching ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why does my land yield fewer crops each year even though I plant the exact same crop on the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be po.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil faster than nature can replace them. Rotating crops—especially with legumes like groundnuts or beans—helps replenish nitrogen and restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ aha amɛye ekoŋŋ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, titri lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stop growing during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Heavy rains can wash away nutrients from the topsoil, leaving young plants starved of the food they need to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu eyi mli obɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers stay thin and tall with small fruit bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛlɛɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving none of the plants with enough energy to grow thick stems or large fruits.
