ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ mli wa Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii ni mli tse loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the soil without sprouting when I bury them deep underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as moisture to germinate. Planting them too deep in compact soil starves them of air, causing them to decay before shoots can break through to the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee nɔ ni bɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees produce far fewer pods than when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo kwraa fe shishijee lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their root systems lose efficiency in absorbing nutrients, and branches become prone to disease. Regular pruning, applying compost, and replacing non-productive older trees with fresh seedlings restores farm productivity.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ni niji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai oya. Tsei ni afoɔ daa Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni akɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛ dumɔwui heei baaye abua ni ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my yam grow better and produce bigger tubers when planted on high soil mounds rather than flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji akɛ adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: High soil mounds create loose, well-drained soil that allows roots to easily expand into full-sized tubers while preventing rainwater from soaking and rotting the growing roots.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni dalɛ fɛɛ yeɔ emuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi ni miida lɛ anɔ ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly appear in large numbers on my green maize leaves after a light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-abele baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ?

english: Pests like armyworm moths lay eggs on crops during dry weather, and the warm moisture after rain causes eggs to hatch simultaneously, leading to sudden caterpillar outbreaks feeding on fresh leaves.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ. Ni hulutsoo ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ be kome too mli. Ekɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai heei lɛ baa trukaa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my field with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mikɛ dade shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cutlasses remove weed tops but leave living roots buried under open sunlight. Covering exposed soil with mulch or shade crops blocks light from reaching weed seeds and slows down regrowth.
ga: Kakla ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baajie jwɛi lɛ ayitsei lɛ. Shi shi shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ ni afu yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ shishi. Kɛ akɛ mulch loo shade tsei ha hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their roots are still small. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and giving the young cocoa trees the cover they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi lɛ Tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called black pod disease, which spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Pruning thick branches and clearing weeds around the trees allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the pods and stop the rot.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Duɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aha ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi ni ekpa amɛ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have ragged holes and look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛye lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the central leaves of young maize. Checking your field early and using appropriate treatments like recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps kill the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni sa tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni agbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my maize after I harvest and bag it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-ŋma lɛ mli beni mikpa ni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Weevils infest stored maize if the grain still holds moisture or if the storage space isn't clean. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is completely hard and using clean, airtight bags keeps these insects from eating your stored harvest.
ga: Weevils baafite ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo loo kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he tseee. Okɛ ŋmãa agbi kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa Ni okɛ vacuum kotokui ni he tse atsu nii koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akaye onibii ni okɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when water stays on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water sits in the field without draining away, it suffocates the roots and creates the right environment for waterlogging rot to destroy the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ŋmɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ koni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: If your crop leaves turn light green or yellow instead of deep green, grow very slowly, or produce very small harvests even with rain, your soil is short on nutrients and needs manure or commercial fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my crop plants grow very tall and thin with small fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Giving plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and nutrients to grow strong stems and bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ shi ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Multiple extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing the extra shoots and leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plantain tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Suckers pɔtɛɛi babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when they lack consistent water and soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a hot, dry spell before the main rainy season actually starts. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die because the soil loses moisture too fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my local rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when the field gets dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ ŋmɔji lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Rice requires consistent water or very damp soil to absorb nitrogen and other nutrients. When the soil dries out, the roots can no longer take up food, which turns the leaves yellow and stops the plant from growing.
ga: Nu loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eŋɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa tso lɛ dalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my land is suitable for growing rice without doing expensive soil tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Land suitable for rice usually sits in valley bottoms or flat areas with heavy clay soil that holds water for long periods. If rain puddle water stays on top of the soil for days without sinking in quickly, the ground is good for holding water for rice.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli oya lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu ni akɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa nɔ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural defense mechanism to save water. Shedding leaves prevents the sun from drying out the plant, allowing the roots underground to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha tso lɛ agbi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: When crops lack nitrogen in the soil, they move the limited nitrogen from their older, lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top. This causes the bottom leaves to turn yellow first while the top stays green.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛjieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛha baai heei lɛ ahi ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha shishigbɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi nɔ lɛ baakã he ahi ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants curl up during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward when hot sun and strong dry winds cause the plant to lose water faster than its roots can drink. Curling reduces leaf surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli, ni no haa tso lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Curling haa baa lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in full, hot sunlight. Keeping taller shade plants like plantains or forest trees shields the young cocoa from direct sun and holds moisture in the air.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni ooofee amɛ shade lɛ baaye abua ni ebu cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition results in thin, weak plants with smaller yields compared to plants given proper space to grow freely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni aha amɛ he ko ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer onto my soil when there is no rain coming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ mli beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in moisture before plant roots can swallow it. Applying fertilizer to dry ground leaves it sitting on top where hot sun causes it to evaporate, or it can scorch the roots if no water is present.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi yɛ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ lɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã kɛji nu bɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same bed where I harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ saatso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpaa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the ground. Rotating them helps restore fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Amɛ ni oootsake lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my chicken coop straight onto my growing crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee ni jɛ tsina shĩa lɛ mli lɛ afata tsei ni miida lɛ ahe?

english: Fresh poultry manure generates strong heat and high ammonia gases as it breaks down, which can burn plant roots and kill the crop. It needs to be dried or mixed with leaves and rotted for several weeks before putting it near plants.
ga: Kooloi amli ŋmeii heei haa dɔlɛ kɛ ammonia gas ni fa babaoo baa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii Esa akɛ agbi loo akɛfutu baai ni egbo otsii babaoo dani akɛwo tso lɛ masɛi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops, like plantains or cassava, planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas that protect the young leaves from intense heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Aduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tse lɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, but leguminous crops like groundnuts and cowpeas can grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ agbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When heavy rains cause standing water around the roots, air cannot reach them, which causes the tubers to suffocate and rot underground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yam is a climbing plant, and lifting its leaves off the ground on tall stakes allows the leaves to trap more sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant sends underground to grow large yam tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ji tsei ni kwɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tsei tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? No gbá ni efo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli ni eshi muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Catching them early with appropriate bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ bio-insecticide loo neem mli nu ni sa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaabu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Mra Be ni Akɛyeɔ Succulent Pests lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers heat stress or irregular watering. When it is too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than spending food to form new fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baatsu nii kɛfee aduawai heei.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for me to sow my seeds at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rain has soaked the ground deeply at least two or three times. If you sow after just the first light rain, the hot sun can dry out the upper soil and destroy the seeds before they fully sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Kɛji odu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the heat of the afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon watering causes much of the water to evaporate quickly, wasting water and stressing the plant roots.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya. Nu ni afiteɔ ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei ashishifãi anɔ

english: Why should I clear the bush early before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ amli mra lɛ? Dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baanɛ?

english: Clearing early gives your land time to rest, allows cut weeds to rot into natural soil food, and ensures your crop seeds can catch the very first rainfall to build strong roots.
ga: Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii mra Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afoɔ jwɛi lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbatsɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa odumɔwui lɛ naa klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I leave some big shade trees on my farm when planting young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni miduɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct hot sun. Big shade trees act like large umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while protecting young plants from harsh winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hu he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin without making big cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight and soil food. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the light instead of developing thick stems and large corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ ngma agbohi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme hot weather, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its lower leaves during dry spells to save water and energy, keeping the main stem and underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better after I plant groundnuts or beans on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen food from the air and trap it in the soil, leaving rich natural fertilizer behind for your next crops to feed on.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ koni oye.

english: Why are my cassava roots remaining small even though the green leaves on top look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big foliage above ground instead of storing food in the tuber roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi dumɔwui lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the soil nutrients, space, and sunlight your crops need, while also hiding pests that eat young crop leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ teeɔ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant plantains alongside my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide fast shade for delicate cocoa seedlings, while also giving you food and income while you wait for cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ oya. Be nɛɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika haa bo yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open when heavy rains fall suddenly after a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ woɔ yibii beni nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ otsi ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry tomato plant suddenly gets a lot of water, the inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack open.
ga: Beni ahaa tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ nu babaoo lɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow big. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or drowns the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: What does fertilizer actually do to my crops, and why can't I just rely on dirt alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ shikpɔŋ pɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your plants. Over time, growing crops removes natural nutrients from the ground, so adding fertilizer or animal manure replaces those missing vitamins so your crops can yield heavily.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa otsei lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye vitamini ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Koni oha otsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Spacing them correctly ensures every single plant gets enough food to produce big, full cobs rather than many tiny, weak ones.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ tso bibioo najiaŋ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: It is best to plant cassava after the soil has received two or three heavy rains and is wet deep underground. Planting in dry or barely damp soil causes the cuttings to dry out and die before roots can form.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii 2-3 ni edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Leaving some large shade trees or planting plantains next to them protects the young leaves from heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Enɛ baabu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the leaves right in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides in the central funnel of maize. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed will save the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo amɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by drinking the water and stealing the soil nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your plants full access to the soil's food and sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with beans or groundnuts resets the soil and puts natural nitrogen back in.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out the earth. It keeps moisture in the soil longer during dry periods and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Is it better to buy certified seeds from an agro-dealer or just plant seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to yield more, resist common diseases, and handle dry spells better than saved seeds, which naturally lose their strength and yield less with every passing season.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni etsuɔ ​​hulutsoo be he nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ. Amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛfeɔ mɛi ni nyɛɛɛ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be fɛɛ be ni hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for plant growth. This often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of green leaves but not producing flowers or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When cowpea soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or organic food, the plant puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of reproduction. Cowpeas need balanced nutrients and sunny weather to trigger proper flowering and pod formation.
ga: Beni cowpea shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛaafɔ bii. Cowpeas biɔ niyenii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi ni sa kɛ pod feemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my cassava plants to twist, curl up, and develop yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni haa yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: This symptom is typical of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread between plants by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the leaves so they cannot convert sunlight into starchy roots efficiently.
ga: Okadi nɛɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nibii yaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa tsei ateŋ Virus lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ amɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ starch.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still attached to the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shaded environments. Pruning cocoa branches and removing weeds helps airflow and sunlight keep the pods dry.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Kookoo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their leaves and wilt quickly after heavy rains stay on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water around pepper roots cuts off their oxygen supply and encourages root rot fungi. When the roots rot and drown, they can no longer send water and food upward, causing the leaves to drop.
ga: nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Pepper shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ agbomɔ he hewalɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboi lɛ Nu kɛ niyenii nyɛŋ atsu kɛya ŋwɛi dɔŋŋ. haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry soil, or poor airflow. When stressed by environment, the plant sheds blossoms to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛ amɛnɔ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to make energy. Climbing stakes lift the vines high off the ground, maximizing sunlight capture which directly feeds and enlarges the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Tsoi ni akwɔɔ lɛ woɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni aaanyɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my harvested cassava roots thin and woody instead of big and starchy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛji tsei yɛ cassava shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ starch lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Thin cassava roots happen when plants are sown too close together, grown in hard soil that restricts root expansion, or harvested too early before the roots have stored enough starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ nɔ. loo akpa mra tsɔ, dani shishifãi lɛ ato ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily once the fruit bunch starts getting heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ bafee tsiimɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by stem borers or root pests like nematodes. Without a strong root anchorage, top-heavy plants easily fall over under the weight of heavy fruit or strong winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni stem borers loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ kɛji shishifãi ni wa lɛ fioo ko pɛ fiɔ sɛɛ. Tsei ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ aduawai ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Why does maize grow so slowly when weeds are left around the stems during the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ yɛ he lɛ? trunk yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Young maize seedlings grow slowly under weed pressure because weeds compete aggressively for soil nutrients, moisture, and root space during the plant's most critical development phase.
ga: Abele dumɔwui bibii lɛ daraa blɛoo. under weed pressure Enɛ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shishifãi ahe he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he akaŋ waa yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during extreme heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. Giving them enough water early in the morning helps reduce heat stress during the day.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛ́ ohiɛ nu mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be mli haomɔ aba shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops get white mold and rot faster when the weather feels very damp and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni egboɔ oya be mli ni shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity creates a moist environment where fungal diseases spread rapidly. Leaving enough space between plants allows fresh air to blow through and dry the leaves, which prevents rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli ni eha baai lɛ agbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite.

english: When daily temperatures get too high, plants become stressed and drop their flowers to save energy for survival. Providing shade or watering during heatwaves helps plants hold onto their blossoms.
ga: Kɛji daa gbi latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo loo nu ha tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after several days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain washes away nitrogen from the soil and fills air spaces around the roots, making it hard for plants to take up food. Adding fertilizer once the heavy rains slow down helps the crops regain their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ eyiɔ obɔ, ni no haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crop soil needs water even if the surface looks dry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia mi-potting sũ lɛ kɛji akɛ ehiɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi po?

english: Dig your finger about two inches into the ground; if the soil at that depth feels completely dry and crumbles easily without sticking to your skin, your crops need watering immediately.
ga: Okɛ oniji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi kwraa ni efoɔ oya ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni okɛ nu awo onibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I irrigate them with water from a salty well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei nu ŋshɔ mli nu shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Salty water leaves salt deposits in the soil, which makes it hard for plant roots to suck up clean water and nutrients. Using collected rainwater or fresh water sources helps roots drink properly.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ nugbɔ nu loo nu kpakpa ni abua naa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds take so long to sprout when planted in dry soil during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds require both moisture and moderate soil temperatures to wake up and germinate. If the soil is too hot and dry, seeds will either stay dormant or dry out before sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgbi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are some farmers building plastic shade structures to grow vegetables instead of planting in open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa plastic shade structures koni amɛkɛdu aduawai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses and shade nets shield delicate crops from extreme sun, heavy rainstorms, and insect pests, allowing farmers to grow healthy vegetables all year round.
ga: Greenhouses kɛ shade netting buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Ehaa okwaafoi duɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings die when I move them straight from the nursery to the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings raised in a cool, shaded nursery get shocked by sudden full sunlight. Moving them outdoors gradually over a few days helps them toughen up before final planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee naakpɛɛ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa kpo nɔ blɛoo Gbii fioo komɛi ni eho lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ dani aduɔ naagbee.

english: Is it worth spending money to set up drip irrigation instead of watering my crops with buckets?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ ooofite shika ni okɛto nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ moŋ fe ni okɛ baagi baashwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu?

english: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the plant roots with very little waste, saving labor time and water while helping crops grow uniformly, which covers the setup cost over time.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu yaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni jwɛi fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ mli. Ehaa nitsumɔ be kɛ nu baa shi, ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Tall shade trees keep the air humid and protect young plants until their root systems grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Which way should I push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil for them to grow best?
ga: Te esa akɛ ashɛre ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to turn its leaves upward, resulting in weak plants and fewer tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso lɛ Tsei lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Heavy rains often wash this nutrient away from the root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when the heat becomes too intense or when the plant does not get steady water. Without cool temperatures and consistent moisture, the blossoms cannot set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyɔɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni yaa nɔ daa bɛ lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear space and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei awo shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need their leaves high in the air and exposed to sunlight to manufacture food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground away from diseases and helps the plant send more energy down to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ hia baai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli shɔɔŋ ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni helai shɛɛɛ he, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoot suckers grow around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Suckers compete with the parent plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Leaving too many suckers causes the main tree to produce small, weak bunches of plantain instead of a heavy, healthy harvest.
ga: Tsobii lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ moŋ fe ŋmeii ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the dirt to feed the next crop, like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ globules bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juices. This damages the leaves and stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop's growth even when my crop is taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ

english: Even if weeds are short, their roots spread fast underground and steal food and moisture right out of the soil before your main crop's roots can take it in.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kuku moŋ Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ abote mli.

english: Why do black spots appear on my plant leaves during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud and moisture onto leaves, creating a wet environment where fungal diseases thrive. The moisture allows fungus spores to stick to the leaves, multiply, and cause rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Fɛ̃i haa fungal spores lɛ kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ahe, amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni amɛhaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do plantains grow so well when I plant them in cleared forest land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ?

english: Forest soils are rich in decomposed organic matter and retain moisture effectively, creating ideal nutrient conditions for young plantain roots to establish quickly.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa plantain shishifãi bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛma shi oya.

english: Why do plantains need open sunlight rather than heavy forest shade to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la he hiaa plantains fe koo mli hulutsoo koni ewo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight allows plantains to photosynthesize efficiently, producing the energy needed to grow thick stems and support heavy bunches of fruit, whereas dense forest shade makes them tall, weak, and unproductive.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ. Amɛhaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni aná tsei ni mli tse ni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ haa tsei lɛ akutsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: How many months does it take for a plantain crop to mature and be ready for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Plantains typically take about nine to twelve months from planting to full harvest, depending on soil quality, water supply, and the specific variety planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji nɛɛhu kɛyashi nyɔŋma kɛ enyɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli kɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I grow quick three-month crops on the same land while waiting for my plantains to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ nyɔji etɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni plantain lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Yes, intercropping short-duration crops like maize, beans, or vegetables between young plantain shoots provides early food and income during the nine months it takes for the plantains to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii ateŋ lɛ baaha aná niyenii kɛ shika oya yɛ nyɔji nɛɛhu ni heɔ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Why are plantains considered a reliable crop for long-term food supply on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ plantain akɛ tso ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha niyenii ni akɛbaatsu nii be kakadaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once established, a plantain mat continually produces replacement shoots (suckers) at different stages, allowing you to harvest repeatedly over multiple years without replanting every season.
ga: Kɛji akɛ agbe Plantain mats lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaya nɔ ekɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ aba yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Ehaa okpaa nii shii abɔ Obaanyɛ ofee afii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni odu ekoŋŋ daa be.

english: How do plantain plants multiply and spread across my farm field?
ga: Te dumɔwui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa miŋmɔji lɛ amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains propagate underground through corms that shoot up young suckers around the main stem; if these suckers are left unmanaged, they multiply and expand the crop stand naturally.
ga: Plantains gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔɔ rhizomes ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu nɛkɛ suckers nɛɛ ahe nii Ebaafee babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha egbɛhe ni edaa lɛ mli alɛɛ.

english: What can I do to ensure my plantain trees produce large, abundant bunches instead of small ones?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-plantains lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni fa babaoo moŋ fe ŋmeii bibii?

english: To get larger bunches, prune excess sucker shoots so the mother plant gets all the nutrients, maintain rich organic soil, and make sure the plant gets enough water during fruit formation.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ Kpãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ mli koni tso nyɛ lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ.

english: Will planting plantains continuously on the same land wear out my soil fertility over time?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ baaná mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Plantains draw a lot of nutrients from the ground. Without replenishing the soil through compost, animal manure, or balanced fertilizers, the soil will eventually lose its strength and produce smaller yields.
ga: Plantains jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ewooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, Yɛ naagbee lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni ebaafee nɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: How does the dry season towards the end of the year affect my plantain farm?
ga: Te hulutsoo be ni baa naagbee lɛ saa mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry weather reduces soil moisture, causing plantain leaves to yellow and dry up, which slows down fruit development; mulching around the stems helps trap ground moisture during these months.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ haa plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if yellowing leaves on my plantain plant are from old age or from disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛ onukpafeemɔ loo hela mli?

english: Natural aging causes only the lowest, oldest leaves to turn yellow and dry up one by one, whereas diseases usually cause rapid yellowing, wilting, or black spots across younger leaves.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dalɛ haa baai bibii kɛ onukpai pɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ komekomei. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ŋmɔŋ, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ diŋŋ baa baai bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant turn green and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal food and water from the main tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the mother plant gets enough energy to produce big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruits from growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi yibii lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Clearing surrounding weeds and spraying organic or safe insecticidal soaps helps control whiteflies and keep plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa tsei amli Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli Ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni eha tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of soil, which dries out quickly if dry weather returns. Waiting until the soil is thoroughly soaked deep down prevents seeds from sprouting and dying during a sudden dry spell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baagbi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baabote mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ baa trukaa lɛ.

english: Planting maize on the same plot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil and builds up crop diseases. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen naturally back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ helai baa tsei anɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to manufacture food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes allows maximum sunlight to reach leaves, encouraging the plant to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ená niyenii eha tso lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. Wo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep falling off without forming into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree experiences water stress or excessive direct heat. Maintaining light shade and soil moisture helps flowers set pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na nu babaoo loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ tɛ̃ɛ. La ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crops help them during dry hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu ni jɛ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni adu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, their roots compete with each other underground for nutrients, water, and space, preventing individual tubers from swelling up big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he akaŋ. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko akafu.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their young fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit due to stress caused by irregular watering, extreme heat, or sap-sucking insects. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during peak heat helps retain young peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii bibii yɛ haomɔ ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tsei yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akafite.

english: Can the dirty water from the river nearby harm my tomato plants?
ga: Ani nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye mi tomato tsei lɛ awui?

english: Yes, water that contains chemicals, heavy salt, or harmful germs can damage your crops just like it harms livestock. If water looks unusual or smells bad, it can cause diseases or burn the roots of delicate plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni tsofai, ŋmeii ni tsii, loo helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye onibii awui tamɔ bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye okooloi lɛ awui lɛ. Kɛji nu lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ejaaa loo ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba loo eshã tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ ashishifãi.

english: How do I know if the borehole water on my farm is safe to use for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni jɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nubu lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If water tastes salty, leaves a white powdery crust on leaves, or rusts metal quickly, it may carry too many minerals for crops. You can bring a small sample of the water to an agricultural extension office for testing.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ Eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. aloo dade lɛ shwieɔ oya Ekolɛ nu lɛ mli nibii babaoo yɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu bibioo ko awo mli. Obaanyɛ oya Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ koni aka bo okwɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the sides before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani etsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden, heavy burst of water after a long dry spell. The inside grows faster than the skin can stretch, so keeping soil moisture steady prevents cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu ni hoɔ trukaa ni tsii waa ba amɛnɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ haaa etse.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the plants cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow at the tips even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Heavy rains can wash away nutrients in the soil, so the plant shows its hunger through yellow leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisted with yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, spread by tiny whiteflies or infected cuttings. Planting healthy, disease-resistant stem cuttings prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees drying up and turning brown early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ oya lɛ?

english: Lower leaves dry up quickly when trees are planted too close together or lack sufficient air movement. Pruning dead leaves and spacing plants properly keeps air flowing and leaves healthier.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni egboi lɛ ni okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting suddenly while the leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho trukaa yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting usually happens when roots rot from standing water or bacterial wilt in the soil. Good land drainage prevents roots from suffocating, and infected plants should be removed right away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ shwie kɛjɛ nu ni ekã shi loo helai ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafo. Ni esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting inside the soil mounds before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ muji mli dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot occurs when excess water sits at the base of the mound without draining, creating a wet ground where rot organisms thrive. Building high, loose mounds helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Sweet potato rot baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ gɔŋ ko shishi ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa he ko ni efɔ ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: What should I do if my crops keep failing and I cannot figure out what is wrong?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii ni minyɛɛɛ mayɔse nɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Collect a sample of the affected leaves or stems along with a small pouch of soil from around the roots, and take them to your local agricultural extension officer or testing lab for advice.
ga: Bua tso lɛ baa loo tso lɛ hela lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kɛ sũ kotoku bibioo ko ni jɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ naa ni okɛya he ni oyɔɔ lɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe loo kaa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni amɛwo bo ŋaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or compost helps the plants regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the leaves and stems grow tall and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are spaced too closely, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize pests to build up in the field. Swapping maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are holes appearing in my corn leaves with small caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest, which eats the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides can protect your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Giving your tomatoes consistent water during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee tomato.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high into the air and keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing diseases from spreading.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Koni helai akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much if both are just growing in the soil together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa kɛji akɛ adu enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves in your farm; they drink the water and steal the soil nutrients intended for your crops, causing your crops to starve and produce poor yields.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaakwɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the earth too fast. It keeps moisture in the soil longer and prevents weeds from sprouting around your crops.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot sun, pepper plants lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Curling up is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing more water, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni efiteɔ lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: How do I know if a piece of land is good enough for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Corn needs well-drained, fertile soil that gets plenty of direct sunlight. Look for dark, rich soil where water doesn't pool after heavy rains, as wet roots will cause corn plants to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa. Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi mli. Shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I plow my land before planting corn instead of just clearing the weeds and planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani madu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni majie jwɛi lɛ kɛkɛ ni madu?

english: Plowing loosens hard soil so young corn roots can easily grow deep to find water and nutrients. It also turns over weeds and helps the soil absorb rainfall much better.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni etsɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I grow a good corn crop in a cleared forest area while keeping some large trees standing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ he ko ni ŋmãa bɛ, ni makwɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: You can, but you must be careful with shade. Corn needs full sunlight to build up energy for big cobs; if tall trees cast too much shade, your corn plants will produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Abaanyɛ afee, shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he. Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmãa wuji. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo babaoo lɛ Abele tsei lɛ baawo toi bibii. loo cob ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Should I plant my corn on flat cleared ground or build soil ridges first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ loo matswa ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Planting on ridges is often better because it keeps soil loose around the roots and prevents heavy rain from washing away seed rows or drowning young crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa sũ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli.

english: Why is it bad to scatter my corn seeds everywhere on the land instead of planting in straight rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: When seeds are scattered randomly, plants crowd each other and fight for sunlight and water. Planting in organized rows gives each crop room to grow and makes weeding and harvesting much easier.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aja dumɔwui lɛ amli trukaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa ŋwɛibɔfoi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko hegbɛ ni amɛdara. Ni ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: What basic steps should I follow when choosing the right spot on my farm to start planting?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ beni mihalaa he ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mije dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: First inspect the land for good soil quality, check how much sunlight reaches the ground throughout the day, and ensure the area is easy for you to access for weeding and carrying out your harvest.
ga: Nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni esa akɛ afee ji ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ana akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ lo. Kwɛmɔ ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni abaanyɛ aya jɛmɛ oya kɛha jwɛi ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nitsumɔi.

english: Why are my corn plants growing very tall and slender without producing any proper corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni ŋmãa ŋmeii ni sa bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Corn plants grow tall and thin when they are struggling to reach sunlight, often because they are shaded by nearby trees or planted too close together.
ga: Abɛi tsei baanyɛ adara ni amɛfee bibioo be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ.

english: How long does corn usually take from the day I plant it until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmãa heɔ kɛjɛɔ gbi ni miduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he?

english: Most common corn varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) from planting to reach full maturity for harvest.
ga: Abɛi henɔi ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara kɛha kpamɔ.

english: What simple things can I do to make sure I get a good harvest from my corn field?
ga: Mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. koni aná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli

english: Select good quality seed, prepare the soil by plowing, plant in measured rows, clear weeds early so they don't steal plant food, and make sure your crops get adequate sunlight and water.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Saamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni asusu mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Bɔni afee ni okaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli Ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hulu la kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will plowing my forest farm land every season hurt the soil over time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ koo lɛ mli daa be lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Repeated heavy plowing can break down soil texture and lead to erosion. To keep the soil healthy, mix in organic compost or leave crop residues to decay naturally after harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni tsii ni afɔɔ feemɔ Ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akumɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aba. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ Futumɔ yɛ organic compost mli loo ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is a foundation seed, and why shouldn't I just plant the rice grains I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwu shishitoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmaa ni ahere kɛjɛ naagbee nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foundation seed is high-purity seed grown under strict supervision to ensure it is healthy and free from diseases. Seeds saved from your previous harvest naturally lose their vigor over time, leading to lower yields and higher disease risks compared to fresh, high-quality seed.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni he tse waa ni aduɔ yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa shishi koni amɛná hewalɛ ni hela akamɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni helai hu baanyɛ aba kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell the difference between certified seeds and regular grain sold at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Certified seeds come in official sealed bags with government inspection tags that show germination rate and purity. Market grain is meant for eating, not planting, and often germinates poorly or carries seed-borne diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli baa yɛ kotokui ni maŋ lɛ kwɛmɔ okadi tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe tse ha. Nibii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji niyenii. eduuu nii ni bei pii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ loo eyɛ helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa

english: Why do my saved seeds fail to sprout after I store them in airtight plastic bags for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo plastic kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Airtight plastic bags trap moisture and heat inside, which rots the seeds or suffocates the living embryo inside them. Planting seeds need cool, dry, and breathable storage to stay alive until planting time.
