ga: Vacuum plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ yɛ mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo loo amɛha fɔmɔ kotokui ni eshwɛ lɛ agbɔjɔ. Dumɔwui adumɔ biɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni ehi shi kɛyashi dumɔ be mli.

english: Why do my rice plants turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much standing water in my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu babaoo hiɔ miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: While rice needs plenty of water, stagnant deep water deprives the roots of oxygen. Without oxygen, the roots cannot absorb nitrogen and other nutrients from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa moŋ, shi nu ni mli kwɔ ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my rice plants fall over right when the grains are almost ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shi beni eshwɛ fioo ni abaakpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: This falling over is called lodging. It usually happens when heavy rain or wind hits top-heavy plants, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer was used, which makes the plant tall but weakens its lower stems.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ shigbeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa tsei ni naa wa. aloo kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Enɛ haa tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ shi shishigbɛ shishigbɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do some improved rice varieties mature in three months while my local seed takes five months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli shi mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ nyɔji enumɔ lɛ?

english: Improved rice varieties are specifically bred to complete their growth cycle faster. This allows farmers to harvest before dry spells begin or even plant two crops in a single rainy season.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmãa henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛgbe dalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. aloo ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ po ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli

english: Why do my crops grow much faster when I plant them at the very start of the rainy season instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ lɛ?

english: Early rain causes a natural flush of nitrogen in the soil that gives young seedlings a huge burst of nutrition. Planting early helps crops establish deep roots before heavy rain or dry spells occur.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa niyenii babaoo. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ baa.

english: Why do my rice plants produce smaller heads when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crowded crops compete with one another for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough resources to grow thick stems and full, heavy seed heads.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ha gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa anaa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season bring more pests to my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests and soil diseases prefer specific host crops. Growing the same crop continuously gives these pests a permanent food source, allowing their numbers to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai sumɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ náa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ daa. Enɛ haa amɛyibɔ ​​buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How do national planting agendas and government crop initiatives actually help a smallholder farmer like me?
ga: Te maŋ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nɔyeli lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government agricultural initiatives work by giving smallholder farmers access to subsidized certified seeds, quality fertilizers, and expert advice from extension officers so you can produce higher yields and sell your crop more easily.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ okwaafoi bibii ni haa amɛnáa dumɔwui ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋaawoo ni he esa kɛjɛ extension officers adɛŋ No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aba ni ohɔ̃ɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer directly onto my crop leaves right before or during a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pouring fertilizer directly onto leaves can burn them, and heavy rain will quickly wash the nutrients away before the plant roots have a chance to absorb them from the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the middle of the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to protect themselves from intense heat and prevent precious water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni jara wa lɛ naa koni ekajɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to save energy and water in their roots, allowing the plant to survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when the plant does not get enough nutrients during its flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and yellow when weeds are growing close around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots, leaving your main crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: When cocoa trees are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight and air, creating dark, damp conditions that encourage diseases and prevent flower development.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai ahe hewalɛ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ akwɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it important for me to dig up and loosen the soil before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows young seed roots to spread out easily, helps air reach the roots, and allows rain water to soak deep down instead of running off the surface.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn bright green and grow so fast right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain releases trapped nitrogen gas from dry soil and warm rainwater carries these essential natural nutrients straight into the thirsty plant roots.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas ni amɔmɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ni nugbɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ baa tsei shishifãi ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do yam tubers need deeply dug soil mounds while leafy vegetables can grow in shallow soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams store their heavy energy underground in long roots that need deep, loose soil to expand, while vegetables have small roots that only search near the top of the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ hewalɛ ni tsii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi kakadaji amli, ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa. Shi aduawai lɛ, amɛyɛ shishifãi bibii ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ pɛ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts hidden under the soil are mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii ni mikɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the plant leaves begin turning yellow and dry, and when you open a sample pod and see dark markings on the inside shell.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ogbele sample pod lɛ ni ona okadii ni tsuɔ yɛ mligbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus. Inspecting under the leaves early and applying the right crop protection medicine prevents the infection from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ Amli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni sa ni buɔ tsei ahe lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is suffering from a disease or just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia amɛ?

english: A thirsty crop wilts during the hot afternoon sun but recovers in the cool evening after watering. A diseased crop shows permanent leaf spots, yellowing, or rotting that remains visible even after the plant gets enough water.
ga: Nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi ebaahe ejɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baajie baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ anaa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ ená nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po sɛɛ.

english: What is eating small holes into my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baa mli lɛ yeli ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. You can protect your cabbage by checking under leaves for insect eggs early, using neem leaf extracts, or spraying approved crop treatments before pests destroy the farm.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii loo ladybugs ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ obu o-cabbage lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ kɛji kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ mra. Neem baa mli nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai baafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: How can I keep my soil rich for my crops if chemical fertilizers become too expensive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jara wa tsɔ?

english: You can feed your soil without costly chemicals by adding animal manure, rotten plant compost, and rotating crops like maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, which naturally trap nitrogen in the soil to nourish future crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni jara wa aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ kooloi ashishifã ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Kompost ni jɛ tsei ni egbo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa woɔ mli. Enɛ kɛ nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Spacing your seeds correctly allows each plant to build strong stems and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná ŋmeii ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and start flowering early when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi shishi mra kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of rainfall cause maize plants to experience severe stress. To survive, the plant rushes its life cycle and flowers early to reproduce, which results in stunted stems and very small ears of corn.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa ŋmãa tsei anɔ. koni amɛhi shi Tsei haa amɛwala shihilɛ yaa oya ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi mra koni amɛfɔ bii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii waa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when water supply swings between too dry and too wet, or when flowers are not pollinated. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers stay on the plant and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ nu ni egbi tsɔ kɛ nɔ ni efɔ tsɔ teŋ loo be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ eshɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ehaa tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients from the soil faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your crops of sunlight and food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hulu la kɛ niyenii akaye amɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Why are some of the crop seeds I planted failing to sprout from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are old, stored in hot conditions, buried too deep in dry soil, or eaten by soil insects. Using fresh, certified seeds planted at the right depth in moist soil ensures healthy sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ. Kɛto he ko ni mli edɔ. Afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ tsɔ loo kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ waa.

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if harvested when fully soft, bruised during handling, or packed tightly in closed sacks without air. Picking tomatoes when they just begin to change color and storing them in ventilated crates keeps them fresh longer for sale.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ beni efee blɛoo kwraa lɛ. Epila yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kɛ́ aŋɔ tomato beni ebɔi su tsakemɔ ni akɛto adeka ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack key nutrients like nitrogen or are receiving too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer keeps leaves green so the corn ears grow full.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli bɔni afee ni ŋmei toi lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year when I plant the same crop repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally and refreshes the soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha sũ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do farmers plant plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moist climate it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans underneath their maize crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural food source for the nearby maize while covering the ground to block weed growth.
ga: Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ ŋmãa ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and turn brown during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baa lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose moisture rapidly through broad leaves during dry, windy weather. Covering the base of the plant with dry grass (mulching) traps moisture in the soil to protect the roots until rains return.
ga: Dumɔwui laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ amɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ be mli ni nu egbi, kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ koni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Extreme heat or irregular watering causes tomato plants stress, making them drop their flowers. Consistent morning watering and providing partial shade during peak hot seasons helps flowers stay on to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ fã ko yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are caterpillars eating the inside of my young maize plant funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing heart of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and placing approved control treatments inside the plant funnel protects the crop before major damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ atsuii anɔ. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ awoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani fitemɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: Cassava tolerates poor soils well but rots easily in standing water. If your field collects water during rain, planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess water drain away to protect the tubers.
ga: Cassava kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. Shi egboɔ oya yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli. Kɛji o-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ hiɛɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Kasava ni ooodu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa koni ebu ŋmɔji lɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow soybean on my farm to make animal feed, or does it require special conditions?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu soybeans yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii? Aloo ani shihilɛi krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ ni ataoɔ?

english: Soybean grows very well in warm climates with well-drained soil. It supplies high-protein seeds suitable for animal feed while simultaneously enriching your soil with nitrogen for future crops.
ga: Soybeans kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ protein babaoo ni sa kɛha kooloi aniyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ náa nitrogen babaoo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil or get insect holes soon after I bag them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ beni mikɛwo baagi mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil rapidly if bagged before they are completely dry. Thoroughly sun-drying grains until they crack cleanly between your teeth before storing them in airtight bags prevents mold and insect damage.
ga: Kɛ akɛwo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, ŋmaa fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛbaagbala jogbaŋŋ yɛ onyanyɔŋ mli dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Heavy rains can also wash this food deep into the ground where small roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ahoo niyenii nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil better for next season's corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny helpers on their roots that trap free plant food (nitrogen) from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that stored food remains in the ground to feed your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa fioo. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei aniyenii ni aheee nɔ ko (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpa niyenii ni ato lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii kɛha o-maise ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does mixing dried leaves and goat manure into my soil help crops stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni egbi kɛ too ŋmei ni mikɛfutuɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Organic matter like leaf mulch and animal manure works like a sponge in the soil. It traps rainwater deep down and holds onto moisture for a long time, keeping the soil cool and wet even when it does not rain for days.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Emɔɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo po.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum sun and stay safe from rot and fungal diseases living in wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha amɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: If too many small shoots grow around the main stem, they steal food and water from the mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only one strong replacement shoot, allowing the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ ni miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he tsɔ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baashwɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why is it risky to plant my corn immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot, dry period. If your seeds sprout right away and then hit a week of hot sun without rain, the delicate young seedlings will dry up and die before their roots grow deep.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ amɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsi kome. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aaada kɛya shɔŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant's juices, or by a plant virus spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular—such as when the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet—making it hard for roots to draw up nutrients smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Agbee shi ni afeee pod?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they are under stress from direct hot sun, dry winds, or lack of water. Providing shade trees helps keep the air humid and soil moist, which helps the flowers stay attached and turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo tsei.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if I leave them harvested too long after the rainy season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As the ground dries out and hardens after the rainy season, heat builds up in the soil. If pests have punctured the cassava tubers underground, bacteria and fungi quickly enter through the wounds and rot the mature roots in the warm soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni efee shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bote shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi amli Bacteria kɛ fungi boteɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛhaa shishifãi ni eda ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If I put extra fertilizer on my crops beyond the recommended amount, will they grow faster and yield more food?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ hu? Ani ebaada oya ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: No, giving crops too much fertilizer harms them in the same way overeating hurts humans. Excess fertilizer causes root burn, damages leaves, and makes the plant weak and susceptible to pests and diseases.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ tsei awui tamɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ adesai awui lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ shãa shishifãi, efiteɔ baai, ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Thinning plants out gives each crop enough space and resources to develop strong stems and large harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Tsei ni mli tseee lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Can I use the waste water from my tilapia fish pond to irrigate my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu fɔŋ ni jɛ mi tilapia nubu lɛ mli lɛ afɔ mi aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: Yes, water from a tilapia pond is full of rich organic nutrients from fish waste. Using it on crops acts as a natural fertilizer that nourishes vegetables like tomatoes and peppers without extra cost.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ tilapia ŋshɔi lɛ amli lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ loo mli nibii amli lɛ amli babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa aduawai tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why do some plants in the middle of my maize farm grow taller than the ones at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ daraa fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Crops look different across a farm because soil conditions vary. The middle of a field often retains moisture and organic nutrients better than the edges, which suffer more from soil erosion and wind.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi yɛ srɔtoi. Gbɛjegbɛ ko teŋgbɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe eshishigbɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ náa amɛnɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Too much water fills the air pockets in the soil, preventing root respiration. When roots cannot breathe, they fail to take up essential nutrients, leading to yellowing leaves and fruit drop.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkamu Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu Amɛnyɛŋ amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi.

english: If I cut off some branches from my tomato plant, won't that reduce the amount of fruit I get?
ga: Kɛ mifo tomato tso ko niji komɛi Ani no baaha yibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Removing non-essential branches directs the plant's energy and nutrients into growing larger, healthier fruits rather than spending energy maintaining extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil yield fewer crops every year even though I plant the same seed variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do weeds growing close to my cassava plants affect the tubers under the soil?
ga: Te jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe lɛ saa ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal food and water from the soil that the cassava plant needs. Clearing weeds allows the cassava roots to absorb all available nutrients and grow into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei tsei taoɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest produce uneven and weaker plants compared to new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their genetic vigor over generations, leading to unpredictable growth and disease vulnerability. Certified seeds are bred to grow uniformly and yield heavily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Ekɛ dalɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara be fɛɛ be ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorch and dry up when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees require partial shade from larger trees to protect their delicate leaves from severe direct sunlight, which scorches leaves and dries out soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be fioo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem weaker and fall over easily compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Over time, planting crops continuously on the same plot without resting the land depletes nutrients in the soil. Weak soil leads to poor root growth, which makes plants unstable and easily knocked down by wind.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs help?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni kɛji akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia mi?

english: If your crops are turning yellow, growing slowly, or yielding much smaller harvests than before, your soil is low on essential nutrients. Weak root systems and hard, compact soil are also signs that compost or fertilizer is needed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdara blɛoo, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: How do I choose the right cocoa seedlings to plant on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala kookoo dumɔwui ni sa ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Always source certified improved or hybrid seedlings from reliable nurseries. These varieties grow stronger roots, produce fruit much faster, and resist common diseases better than seeds saved from old farm trees.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, ná dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ loo hybrid kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ woɔ shishifãi ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa oya ni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ eshiɔ fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei momo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my crops too close together on my field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than properly spaced crops.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe be mli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Is it better to cut down my old, low-yielding trees or try to fix them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ loo aaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni asaa amɛ?

english: Very old trees with decaying roots and low yield rarely recover full production. Cutting them down and replanting with new, high-yielding seedlings gives you a much better harvest in the long run.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egbɔ waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ egboi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ amɛ ni okɛ dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo du amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmaa kpakpa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend leaving shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ ashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees scorch easily under direct hot sun. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas to keep the field cool, hold moisture in the soil, and protect young trees while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji koni amɛha shia lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni obu tsei bibii ahe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How can I keep my soil moist during hot spells when rain is sparse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your crops with dry leaves, grass, or crop stalks (mulching) traps moisture in the ground and shields the soil from direct heat.
ga: Mulching around Tso lɛ shishi ni baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo tso shishifãi (mulch) yɔɔ mli lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: When crops have shallow roots, they cannot reach water stored deeper in the earth. Improving soil texture with organic manure helps roots grow deeper to reach underground moisture.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛyashɛ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is the difference between organic manure and chemical fertilizer for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer provides a quick burst of nutrients directly to the plant, while organic manure slowly improves the physical health, water retention, and long-term structure of the soil.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aya hiɛ fiofio lɛ

english: How can I protect my cassava plants from leaves curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by viruses usually spread by insects like whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant stem cuttings provided by agricultural extension programs.
ga: Virus ko ni bei pii lɛ koolooi tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ gbɛjianɔtoi kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa ni obi cocoa lɛ he hiaa yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb upwards so their leaves can trap sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground exposes them to sunlight to build food for the underground tuber while preventing leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ akwɔ koni baai lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the leaf tips in a V-shape indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food maize needs to stay green, grow tall, and build strong leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli, ekwɛ ni ekɛ baai ni wa aba.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce poor yield when I sow the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground. It traps moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: What is causing small worms to hide inside the central leaves of my young corn and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the young central shoot (whorl) during the day to feed on leaves before the plant can tassel, which can severely ruin your harvest if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ tsei bibii (whorls) lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai lɛ dani tso lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ waa kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall and extreme humidity prevent bees and wind from moving pollen inside the flower, and high moisture can cause fungal rots on the flower stem, making the blossoms drop before fruit can form.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa tsɔ tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni amɛkajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii ahe tsei lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, signaled when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Ekɛ okadi ko tsuɔ nii kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tuber lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot drains the exact same soil nutrients every season and allows pests that feed on maize to build up in the soil. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi nakai nɔŋŋ daa be ni eyeɔ ebuaa abɛi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo miŋmɔji amli?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the evening when the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer on dry soil under a hot sun can burn plant roots and waste fertilizer through evaporation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dying suddenly even though they looked healthy last month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso lɛ gbo trukaa lɛ? Ni kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo nyɔŋ kome ni eho nɛ?

english: Cocoa trees often die from hidden infections like Swollen Shoot disease or root rot, which spread inside the tree long before the leaves turn yellow and drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ gbeɔ cacao tsei. Egbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Can I save a cocoa tree once its leaves start turning brown and dropping?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsa cacao tsei lɛ kɛ́ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbee shi?

english: If a viral disease or severe root damage has spread throughout the trunk, saving the tree is difficult; removing infected trees early is usually necessary to stop the spread to healthy neighboring plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa loo shishifãi ni efite waa lɛ egbɛ eshwa tso lɛ shishi fɛɛ Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ wa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra Bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa koni akɛkpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛmiiya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down diseased cocoa trees instead of giving us medicine to spray on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mɛi akɛ amɛfolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ tsofa ni amɛkɛwo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Certain cocoa diseases, like the Swollen Shoot virus, have no chemical cure, so cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to protect the rest of your farm from complete destruction.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi, tamɔ Swollen Shoot hela lɛ, bɛ tsofa ni akɛbaatsa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ kwraa.

english: Why is my cocoa farm producing fewer pods this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo pods fioo ko pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Declining cocoa yields are usually caused by aging trees, nutrient-depleted soil, hidden diseases, or lack of shade during dry periods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni eda lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii bɛ mli Hela ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ mli

english: How long does it take for newly planted cocoa trees to start giving good yields?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai awomɔ shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties take 3 to 5 years to start bearing pods, but newer hybrid varieties can begin producing within 2 to 3 years if well managed.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi amli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Shi hybrid henɔi heei Nibii ni afee lɛ baanyɛ aje shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers falling off before turning into real pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when stressed by pests, extreme drought, or poor soil nutrients, as they do not have enough energy to support pod growth.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai gba amɛnaa. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ bɛ.

english: What should I do with my land after all my cocoa trees have been destroyed by disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mishikpɔŋ lɛ beni helai efite kokoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: You need to clear the infected wood, let the soil rest or grow food crops for a season, and then replant using disease-tolerant seedling varieties with proper shade cover.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo ekwɛ niyenii kɛyashi be kome. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni sa lɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Where can I get reliable cocoa seedlings to replace my dead crops?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana kookoo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Improved, high-yielding, and disease-tolerant cocoa seedlings can be obtained through official Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) nurseries and authorized agricultural extension centers.
ga: Abaanyɛ ana kookoo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛjɛ Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ hei ni aha hegbɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I protect my cocoa farm so that it keeps producing well in the future?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he koni ewo yibii?

english: Regular pruning, maintaining shade trees, removing infected pods quickly, and feeding the soil with fertilizer protect your farm's health for decades.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ daa Ha tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo mli Jiemɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ni kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu oŋmɔ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees dry up during the dry season while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Farms with shade trees retain soil moisture and protect young cocoa from direct sun, whereas farms without shade lose moisture rapidly and dry out.
ga: Okwaafoi ni tsei yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food that creates strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the plant build food and turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei ni woɔ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ yeɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔ.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are naturally gifted plants that trap food from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize keeps the ground rich and fertile so your maize yields better without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji tsei ni yɔɔ nikeenii kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Emɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa baa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long, creating a home for tiny organisms that decay the plant. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to run off, keeping the roots safe and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ehaa bɔɔ nii bibii feɔ shihilɛhe. ni haa tsei fiteɔ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny, almost invisible insects sucking the sap out of soft young leaves and spreading plant sicknesses. Spraying your pepper plants with a mild soap-and-water mixture or natural neem extract helps drive these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni eshwɛ fioo ni anaaa amɛ ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the trees from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense, direct tropical sunlight. Leaving bigger trees or planting food crops like plantains nearby provides protective shade until the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni ajieɔ loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hulu lɛ naa kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear dry grass and weeds away from the stem of my cocoa trees during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni egbo kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds and dry grass close to the trunk can catch fire easily during dry spells, and they also hide pests that attack the trunk. Clearing around the base leaves a clean circle that keeps the tree safe from bushfires and stem-boring bugs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atswa la yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli oya. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu teeɔ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ni ajieɔ Shishitoo lɛ feɔ kooloo ni he tse. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ koo mli la kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves broad and high in the sunlight to produce food for the tubers below. Staking lifts the leaves off hot soil, catches maximum sunlight, and keeps leaves from decaying on wet ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli babaoo ni amɛya shɔŋŋ yɛ hulu lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Na hulu la babaoo ni etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when plants don't get steady water, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Watering regularly at the base of the plant keeps the temperature balanced so flowers can set into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ shishi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ tomato nɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around my crops help them survive when the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket on top of the earth, stopping the hot sun from evaporating moisture out of the soil. This keeps the root area cool and damp so crops can draw water even during short droughts.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ agbala nu yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops grow right next to each other, their roots fight over the same soil food and water, making every plant thin and weak. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light, water, and nutrients to give you big fruits or grains.
ga: Beni tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha oná aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth, or when the soil is too waterlogged, which suffocates the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: My cocoa trees used to give me many pods, but now that they are old, the yield is dropping every year. Why does this happen?
ga: Kulɛ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ ni egbɔ lɛ, nɔ ni afeɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural internal systems slow down, they become more vulnerable to diseases like swollen shoot, and their roots cannot absorb soil nutrients as effectively as young trees.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ helai tamɔ tsei ni efuu lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ tsei bibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading the cassava mosaic virus, or by mealybugs sucking the sap out of the leaves, causing the leaves to deform as they try to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when a strong wind blows, even before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ? Dani nugbɔ baanɛ waa po?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the ground. If microscopic worms called nematodes attack the roots, the roots rot and break, leaving the heavy plant with no firm anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaakumɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat stresses the plant and destroys the pollen, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why do my yams sometimes crack open under the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ tswaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when heavy rains come suddenly after a dry period. The inside of the tuber drinks water and grows very fast, causing it to swell quicker than the outer skin can expand.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ba trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Tuber lɛ mli nuɔ nu ni edaa oya waa. Enɛ haa fuumɔ baa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ alɛɛ mli.

english: My pepper plants look very healthy in the morning, but by afternoon they wilt completely and die. What is causing this?
ga: Mi pepper tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ waa leebi. Shi beni shɛɔ shwane lɛ, amɛbaagbi kwraa ni amɛbaagboi. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: This sudden collapse is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that multiplies inside the plant's stem and blocks the internal water tubes, cutting off water to the leaves during the hot afternoon.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei amli ni etsĩɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over hundreds of years to survive tough conditions. They quickly send out strong roots to grab water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crop seeds can even sprout.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛtsuɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni gbalaa nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani odumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and prevents weed seeds from getting light to grow.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la koni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so that I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with weak, thin plants that produce small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield more.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If crops grown on the land in previous seasons were short, yellowish, or gave very low yields, the soil is likely low in nutrients. Testing the soil or looking for poor plant growth tells you if compost, manure, or chemical fertilizer is needed.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ kuku, amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa Tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo otao tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and leaves on top of the soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi toɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass, called mulching, protects the soil from the hot sun. It keeps the ground cool, helps the soil hold water longer after it rains, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are missing a key soil nutrient called nitrogen, or the soil is too waterlogged or dry. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Flowers often fall off when the weather is too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or if insects aren't visiting to pollinate them. Keeping the soil moist and letting beneficial insects visit can help the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi baaa ni amɛbafee pollination Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ abasara lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural way of saving water, and it will usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do people advise planting plantains next to young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the air humid, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to stand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots drown and fungus grows, causing rot. Planting cassava on mounds or raised ridges helps water drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyashiɔ amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo saatso ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapted to survive poor conditions. They quickly steal water, light, and nutrients meant for your crops, which is why clearing them early is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛjuɔ nu, kane, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia.

english: Why didn't the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest grow as well as the store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Many store-bought seeds are special hybrids bred for high performance in a single season. Seeds saved from those crops lose their strength in the next generation, producing weaker plants with smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akɛfee ekome ni akwɛɔ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kome mli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I stop all my maize from getting ready at the same time so I don't have to sell everything at once?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa ŋmãa ni efee klalo shikome? No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome?

english: You can use staggered planting, which means planting small sections of your farm a few weeks apart so your crop matures in batches over time rather than all on the same day.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaadu fã bibioo ko. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ kui amli yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so much faster than my cassava tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ miifite oya fe mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have thin skin and high water content, making them decompose quickly once picked, while cassava tubers have dense starch and protective bark that allow them to last longer.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfiteɔ oya kɛ́ abua amɛnaa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi yɛ ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmei ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I leave my cassava in the soil for a few months if I am not ready to harvest it yet?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji fioo komɛi? Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ makpa nii lolo hu?

english: Yes, mature cassava roots can safely remain stored underground in the living plant for several months until you are ready to harvest and take them to market.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe yɛ tso ko ni hiɛ ka mli nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛya jara nɔ.

english: Why should I harvest my plantains while they are green instead of waiting for them to turn yellow on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa plantains be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ,.

english: Plantains continue to ripen after being harvested, so picking them green gives you extra days to transport and sell them before they become soft and overripe.
ga: Plantains yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haa onáa be kroko ni okɛbaafã gbɛ ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ dani amɛfee blɛoo tsɔ ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables wilt and rot quickly when I harvest them in the middle of the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ akpa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Crops lose moisture rapidly under intense afternoon sun, causing them to wilt instantly and break down faster compared to crops harvested in the cool early morning.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛfiteɔ oya fe tsei ni akpaa yɛ fɛ̃i mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ.

english: Why does drying my hot peppers in the sun make them stay fresh for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ agbiɔ mi-hot peppers lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Sunlight removes water from the peppers, and without moisture, the bacteria and fungi that cause rot cannot survive, allowing the peppers to be stored safely.
ga: Hulu la lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Bacteria kɛ fungi ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ hu nyɛŋ ahi shi. Ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ chili baato

english: Are there specific yam varieties that can stay in storage longer without rotting?
ga: Ani ŋmeii srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee?

english: Yes, yam varieties like Water Yam or Laboko have thicker skins and lower moisture loss, allowing them to remain fresh in storage for months compared to fast-sprouting varieties like Pona.
ga: Hɛɛ, ayɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmeii loo laboko. Eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ shi ehee yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ nyɔji babaoo. Kɛ akɛto henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ Pona lɛ ahe.

english: What happens to my harvested onions if I do not dry them in the shade before storing them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-onii ni mikpa lɛ nɔ? Kɛji migbiko yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛtoɔ lɛ,.

english: Drying or curing onions hardens their outer skin and seals the top neck, preventing fungal spores and moisture from getting inside and rotting the onion bulb.
ga: Sabolai ni agbiɔ loo atsaa lɛ haa hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ mli waa ni ehaa tsitsi lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabote mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my fresh peppers heat up and turn soft when I pack them tightly into large sacks for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-chili hee lɛ mli edɔɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo beni mikɛwoɔ kotokui wuji amli koni mikɛmaje lɛ?

english: Harvested crops continue to breathe; tightly packing them traps the heat and moisture they release, creating warm conditions that cause rapid spoilage inside the bag.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔɔ, ni ehaa kotoku lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my garden eggs spoil faster if I harvest them during heavy rainy season days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mibua amɛnaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain makes the crop absorb high amounts of water and carries fungi spores from the soil onto the skin, causing the fruit to decay rapidly after harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ nu babaoo ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hewolo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa amɛ.

english: Cassava stems have small growth buds or 'eyes' where leaves sprout. You must plant the stem with these buds pointing upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for the plant to shoot up and reduces your harvest.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni baai lɛ jɛɔ mli baa. Esa akɛ okɛ tso lɛ adu ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃, ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow big. This happens when the soil is weak or when heavy rains wash away the soil nutrients.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why did my crop stems burn and wither after I gave them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is strong like medicine. If you place it directly against the plant stem or apply too much at once, it draws water out of the roots and scorches the plant. It should always be placed a few inches away from the stem in moist soil.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ mli wa tamɔ tsofa. Kɛ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛwo nɔ babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, Egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni eshãa tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ he inchii fioo komɛi.

english: Why are holes appearing in my corn leaves with small caterpillars eating deep inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji miije kpo yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii miiye nii kɛmiiya tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The parent moths lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl inside the growing funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and moist to chew up the fresh leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛi ni miida lɛ amli. ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli edɔ ni akɛyeɔ baai heei

english: This rot, called Black Pod disease, is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Heavy rain splashes the fungus from the dirt onto the lower pods, and high moisture helps it spread quickly across the farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ akɛ blackpod hela. Fungi bibii ni kɛbaa Ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ muji lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans helps the soil recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing very small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other under the dirt for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant proper space allows it to feed well and grow larger fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even if there is plenty of rain for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive invaders that grow faster than your crops. They steal the soil's food, water, and root space, hiding your crops from the sunlight and leaving them weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni daa oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato hulu lɛ he. ni eha amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe efee shoo
