english: It is safer to wait until the ground gets a few steady, heavy rains. The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or dry spell, which will dry out the soil and kill newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná nugbɔshiimɔ bibioo ko ni yaa nɔ daa. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ekpata dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How long can a single pineapple plant stay on my farm and keep producing good fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ pineapple tso kome baanyɛ ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: A pineapple plant can live for many years, but it usually produces its best and biggest fruit in the first harvest. After that, it produces smaller fruits called ratoon crops. Most farmers replant after 3 to 4 years to maintain high quality.
ga: Pineapple tsei baanyɛ ahi shi afii babaoo. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni dara fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ be lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ratoon tsei. Okwaafoi babaoo duɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ koni amɛhe afee fɛo.

english: After I harvest a pineapple fruit, do I need to destroy the plant or can I get new planting materials from it?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo ananas ko sɛɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ makpãtã tso lɛ hiɛ loo matao nibii heei ni akɛduɔ nii?

english: You do not need to destroy it. The old plant produces small shoots called suckers, slips, and crowns. You can carefully remove these side shoots and plant them in the soil to grow brand-new pineapple plants.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofite lɛ. Tsei ni edara lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii. Ale amɛ akɛ suckers, shoots, kɛ shoots, ni obaanyɛ ojie nɛkɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni odu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ona ŋmei tso hee ko kwraa.

english: What happens to my pineapple crop when the sun is very hot and there is no rain for weeks?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-anana tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo?

english: Pineapples are tough and can survive with little water, but severe drought and intense heat will slow down their growth, make the fruits much smaller, and cause sunburn on the skin, which lowers their market value.
ga: Pineapple wa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛ nu fioo pɛ. Shi hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni naa wa haa shweremɔ baa shi. Ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa ni ekɛ hulutsoo baa hewolo nɔ ni haa jara nɔ jara baa shi.

english: How can I protect my soil from drying out when the rains stop during the farming season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: You can practice mulching, which means spreading dry grass, crop leaves, or straw over the bare soil around your plants. This layer shades the soil, keeps it cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mulching akase nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afɔ jwɛi, tso baai, loo jwɛi afɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my pineapple plants turning yellow and rolling inwards during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is the plant's natural way of saving water. When it is too hot and dry, the leaves turn lighter and curl inward to reduce sunlight exposure and trap moisture inside the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛji edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Can pineapples grow in full sunlight, or do I need to plant shade trees over them?
ga: Ani ŋmeii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo ehe miihia ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ nɔ?

english: Pineapples grow best in full, direct sunlight because they need lots of sun to make sweet fruits. However, during extreme heat spells, you may need to cover ripening fruits with dry straw to prevent sunburn.
ga: Pineapple kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛwo aduawai ni ŋɔɔ. Shi, yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe koni hulu akatswa bo.

english: Why are my pineapple plants producing very small fruits that ripen early this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa ni shwereɔ mra yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops face extreme heat stress and lack of water early in their growth, they feel threatened and force themselves to flower and ripen early to survive, resulting in tiny fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ mli lɛ kpe yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ, Amɛnuɔ he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛdara mra koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai bibii.

english: How do I know the exact time to harvest my pineapples so they do not spoil before I get them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni anaa koni akafite dani akɛwo jara nɔ?

english: Harvest your pineapples when the base of the fruit turns green-yellow. If you wait until the whole fruit turns bright yellow on the farm, it will become soft and rot quickly while being transported to buyers.
ga: Kpãa o-pineapple lɛ mli beni shishigbɛ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi aduawai lɛ fɛɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ebaafee blɛoo ni ebaagbo oya be mli ni etsɔɔ gbɛ kɛyaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to handle harvested fruits so they stay fresh while I travel to sell them in another town?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu mikpamɔ lɛ he nii koni ehi shi ehee be mli ni mifãa gbɛ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Harvest early in the morning when it is cool, keep the fruits in a shaded spot away from direct sun, and pack them neatly in crates without squeezing them so they do not get bruised during transport.
ga: Kpaa nii lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ha aduawai lɛ ahi he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni akɛwoɔ adeka lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛmiimɔɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ akafee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa lɛ.

english: Which types of crops are best for me to plant if my area experiences long dry periods without regular rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji akɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ naa hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ daa?

english: Crops like pineapple, cassava, sorghum, and cowpea are very drought-tolerant. They have strong root systems or leaf structures that help them survive long dry periods better than crops like maize or vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ anana, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa waa. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa loo baa ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to build green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from old leaves to new ones to survive, so adding NPK fertilizer or animal manure restores the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no big plantain trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui wuji bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn and dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides broad leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo bibioo lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: What is eating holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown dirt inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant to feed on young leaves. Clearing weeds early and applying targeted insecticide or neem extract in the funnel helps control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmei mli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛjegbɛi anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help the soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmã duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds the neighboring maize plants.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin roots when I plant the stems very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo beni miduɔ shishifãi lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too close, the roots fight underground for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper distance allows each plant to spread its roots and swell into big tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, ekwɛɔ shishifãi ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads in cold, wet conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight reach the farm and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nu mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli kɛbaa. Shade ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaafata he koni hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry out so the flowers cannot form seeds or fruit. Covering the soil around the plant stem with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and retains water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui loo aduawai. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha tso lɛ he (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why is my farm soil producing smaller crop yields each year even though I clear the field well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihe esa waa yɛ jɛmɛ shwiemɔ mli moŋ.

english: Harvesting crops removes nutrients from the ground every year without putting anything back, leaving the soil tired and weak. Rotating your crops or adding compost and decomposed poultry manure brings life and nutrients back to the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi ni ekɛ nɔ ko wooo mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa etɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ashishifãi ni egboi fata he lɛ, ebaaha wala kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your plants, leaving your crops starved even when water is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ waa. Ha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready for harvesting under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akuuu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and cracks begin to appear on the surface soil around the stem base as the growing tubers push the earth upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni bulb ni miida lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why should I nurse my crop seeds in a special bed first instead of planting them directly into my main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young seeds are very delicate and need a protected space with soft soil, shade, and regular water. Nursing them gives them a safe environment to grow strong roots and healthy stems before facing the harsher weather and pests of the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he waaa waa ni amɛbiɔ he ko ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, hulutsoo kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɔɔ. Amɛtsɔsemɔ baaha amɛná shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa. Dani ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baakpe

english: How much water do my crop seeds need while they are still in the nursery stage?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa midumɔwui lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Seeds and young sprouts need light, steady moisture to grow. You should water them gently so the soil stays damp like a squeezed sponge, but avoid putting too much water so the seeds do not rot in muddy soil.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ tsei bibii hia la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni mli edɔ koni amɛdara. Esa akɛ okɛ nu awo mli fioo. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛmiimɔ nii. Shi kaaha nu fe nine koni dumɔwui lɛ akafite yɛ muji lɛ mli.

english: Why do some seeds in my nursery bed sprout very fast while others take a long time to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds develop at different rates depending on their outer shell thickness, how deep they were planted, and how much moisture they receive. Even seeds from the same batch can awaken at slightly different times based on their individual strength.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Edamɔ bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli wa ha lɛ nɔ. dumɔ mlibotemɔ Ni hulutsoo be enyiɛ enáa? Dumɔwui ni jɛ kuu kome mli lɛ po baanyɛ ateshi yɛ bei srɔtoi fioo amli, ni enɛ damɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do pests and insects attack my small seedlings more than the older plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ? Mi nɔ lɛ fa fe tsei momo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young seedlings have very tender, sweet leaves and stems that are easy for insects to chew and digest. Older plants develop tougher leaves and stronger natural defenses that make them harder for tiny pests to eat.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni ŋɔɔ. ni kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ ni amɛye mlɛo Tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli wa kɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii ni mli wa. ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baa Ewa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my seedbed is ready and good enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ efee klalo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Good seedbed soil should feel soft, loose, and crumbly in your hands, free from large stones, heavy clay lumps, or deep weeds. This allows delicate seedling roots to push through easily and find air and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ashishi shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ni etse ehe, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ onine mli. Ebɛ tɛi wuji shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii loo jwɛi ni mli kwɔ Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛnaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii.

english: Should I apply heavy chemical fertilizer directly to my crop seeds when setting up the nursery?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo awo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ miito ŋmɔ ko ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔ?

english: No, strong chemical fertilizers can easily burn tender seeds and destroy young roots. It is safer to mix rich, well-rotted manure or compost into the soil, which feeds the seeds gently without scorching them.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ mlɛo ni efite shishifãi bibii. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii blɛoo ni eshãŋ amɛ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wither and die when exposed to full, hot sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants have small roots that cannot pull water fast enough from the ground to replace what the strong sun dries out from their thin leaves. Shade shields them until their roots grow deep enough to drink more water.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya bɔ ni sa koni ekɛye hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baai bibii lɛ najiaŋ Shade lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnu nu babaoo.

english: Why do I need to separate crowded seedlings and space them out into a second bed before final planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijaraa dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli ni mikɛwoɔ saatso ni ji enyɔ nɔ dani miduɔ naagbee lɛ?

english: When seedlings grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, becoming tall, thin, and weak. Giving them extra space allows each plant to grow a thick stem and strong branch structure.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni amɛhe waaa. He kroko ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ tso ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa.

english: Why is it recommended to slowly reduce the shade cover over my nursery a few days before transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ajie hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ nɔ lɛ shi fiofio gbii fioo komɛi dani atsake lɛ.

english: Removing the shade bit by bit helps the seedlings get used to direct sunlight and wind. This process toughens the plant up so it does not go into shock when planted out in the open field.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie shade lɛ fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛle hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa. No hewɔ lɛ, shoofeemɔ ko bɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to move my crop seedlings from the nursery into the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to move seedlings late in the afternoon or early in the morning when the sun is cool. Transplanting during the cool hours reduces heat stress on the plant and gives the roots time to settle in overnight.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane mli loo leebi maŋkpa be mli ni hulu lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai amli lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaahi shi nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava usually mean sap-sucking pests like whiteflies are attacking the plant, or the crop has contracted cassava mosaic disease. Inspecting under the leaves helps identify insects early before the disease spreads across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ miitutua tso lɛ. loo tsei ni cassava mosaic hela lɛ emɔ amɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ana kooloi bibii mra. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: What should I do if I find a strange insect eating my crop that I have never seen in my area before?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni miiye ŋmɔshi nibii ni minako amɛ dã yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: If you spot an unknown insect causing damage, capture a sample in a clean container or take photos, and immediately notify your local agricultural extension officer or report it to research institutions like CSIR so experts can identify the pest and stop it from spreading.
ga: Kɛji okɛ kooloi bibii ni aleee ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ kpe Buamɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ naa yɛ tsɛnsi ni mli tse mli loo ofo mfoniri. ni oha okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ale amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo obɔ he amaniɛ otsɔɔ niiamlitaomɔ he ko tamɔ CSIR koni ŋaalɔi lɛ ana tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ni amɛkpa egbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny pests like thrips feeding on the blossom stems before pollination occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination.

english: Why is my maize growing tall and thin without producing full cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo shi eyimɔ obɔbɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants grow tall and weak when planted too close together or when the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, causing the plants to stretch for sunlight instead of putting energy into filling cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo ŋmãa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn soft and rot while they are still underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by waterlogging in poorly drained soil, or fungal and bacterial infections carried in contaminated seed yams or soil nematodes.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. loo fungal kɛ bacteria helai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji loo nematodes ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough water for planting tomatoes without using expensive tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato ni mikɛ nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a handful into a ball at root depth; if it holds its shape without dripping excess water and crumbles easily when poked, it has ideal moisture for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka shikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nine ni okɛaawo bɔɔlu mli yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛha shweremɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani eyibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall easily because their roots are shallow, especially if soil pests like nematodes or stem borers have damaged the root system, or if heavy bunches lack support poles.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers fite shishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso agbo ko bɛ tso ni fiɔ esɛɛ

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpea plants to grow lush foliage instead of flowers, or insect pests called pod borers might be destroying the young flower buds before pods form.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ cowpea tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pod borer lɛ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi bibii lɛ dani pod lɛ afee.

english: Where can a farmer like me get official help when a crop disease starts spreading fast in our village?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafonyo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ ana yelikɛbuamɔ kɛjɛ maŋ onukpai adɛŋ beni tso hela ko jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a disease spreads quickly, you should inform your district Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) extension officer or contact national agricultural bodies like CSIR, who collect samples to diagnose the problem and provide control measures.
ga: Kɛji hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa oya Esa akɛ oha okpokpaa lɛ Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) Extension Officer lɛ ale loo okɛ omaŋ lɛ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe tamɔ CSIR lɛ abɔ, ni amɛbaabua nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa koni amɛkwɛ naagba lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ aha.

english: Young cocoa leaves scorch when exposed to direct sunlight and dry winds without enough shade canopy, which is why planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young trees until they mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost to the base of the plant will help restore its green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ fãji titrii lɛ ahe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and attracts pests that adapt to that plant. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns vital nutrients like nitrogen to the soil and stops pest buildup.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa kooloi ni etsɔ nakai tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantains to shelter them and retain soil moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛná wɔɔhe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the leaves and central stems of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young maize leaves. Inspecting plants early and applying proper pest control measures before the worms get into the central whorl helps save your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni sa ni oootsɔ nɔ okɛbu tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ abote teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha okpamɔ be lɛ akafite.

english: Cassava roots rot when excessive water sits around them in poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to run off and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu babaoo atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to develop strong stems and higher yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress or irregular water supply. Consistent watering and protecting the soil with organic matter helps keep the root zone cool and encourages fruit to set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ daa ni abuɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ewoɔ aduawai hewalɛ koni amɛwo shi.

english: Why is it important to remove the tiny side shoots growing out of my tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato nine lɛ mli lɛ he miihia.

english: Removing these extra shoots, known as suckers, focuses the plant's energy and nutrients into producing larger, higher-quality fruits rather than growing useless leafy stems.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni ajieɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ Ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ tso yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crop stems with dried grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried plant materials, called mulching, blocks harsh sunlight, traps ground moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better to water my crops in the morning or in the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering in the early morning gives plants the moisture they need to handle daytime heat while allowing wet leaves to dry quickly, which reduces the chance of fungal diseases developing on wet leaves overnight.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnáa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsu hulutsoo be mli dɔlɛ he nii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it best for me to harvest my maize early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makpa ŋmãa leebi lɛ?

english: Harvesting early in the morning keeps the crop cool and fresh, reducing heat stress and water loss, which prevents grains from spoiling quickly right after harvest.
ga: Nikpamɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haaa ŋmaa lɛ afite oya yɛ nikpamɔ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn before it spoils on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa dani efite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Your corn is ready when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the kernels become hard, and a small dark spot appears at the base of each kernel.
ga: O-corn lɛ efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ mli wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi.

english: What will happen if I delay harvesting my corn and leave it on the field past its harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kpamɔ be sɛɛ ni mishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi ŋmãakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature corn in the field exposes it to pests like weevils and birds, and unexpected rain can cause mold to grow, ruining your yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni eda lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ okpoi yeɔ lɛ, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to walk through my farm to inspect crops regularly before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa dani ŋmaakpamɔ aba lɛ?

english: Checking your field frequently helps you spot pest damage, plant diseases, or maturity early so you can plan the right day to harvest before losses occur.
ga: He ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ shii abɔ Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii, tso helai, loo bɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oto gbi ni sa ni okɛbaakpa nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ dani nibii ni elaaje lɛ aba.

english: Does breeze or wind help my crops grow better, or does it harm them?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ loo eyeɔ amɛ awui?

english: A gentle breeze cools plants and dries up extra leaf moisture to prevent diseases, but very strong winds can break stems and dry out soil moisture too fast.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa fioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gĩɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ. Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants fall down whenever a strong wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over during winds when its roots are shallow, the soil is overly wet, or the stems are weak due to lack of space or nutrients.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Aloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ he ko loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need good air movement around my maize when drying it after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle mihe lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ magbi mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Moving air carries away moisture from harvested corn quickly, preventing harmful mold and fungal rot from growing on the grains.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ ehe oya lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ yaa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Is early morning the right time for me to apply chemical sprays or liquid fertilizers to my crops?
ga: Ani leebi ji be kpakpa ni mikɛ tsofai loo nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Early morning is ideal because wind is usually calm and temperatures are cool, but you must wait for heavy morning dew to dry so the water does not wash away the spray.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ dioo ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu mli ejɔ. Shi esa akɛ omɛ ni leebi lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa lɛ agbi koni nu lɛ akafɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant my corn very close to my house, or will the building affect how it grows?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mishia? Aloo tsu lɛ baaná dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Buildings block natural sunlight and alter air movement; crops planted too close to walls may grow thin and tall trying to reach sunlight, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Tsuji tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ. Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ gbogbo tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee bibioo ni amɛfee shɔŋŋ kɛ́ amɛmiitao ni amɛná hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do some farmers plant a row of tall trees around the edge of their crop fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsei kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Rows of tall trees act as windbreaks to slow down heavy gusts, preventing strong winds from knocking over delicate crops like maize and keeping topsoil from blowing away.
ga: Tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ ŋmãa ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ akatswa.

english: Why does cassava grow so well in regions like Bono and Ashanti compared to other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai tamɔ Bono kɛ Ashanti nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava thrives in warmer climates with rich, well-drained loam soil and moderate rainfall, which regions like Bono and Ashanti offer naturally. Its roots dig deep to draw nutrients, making it more resilient than many other sensitive food crops.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni kpokpai tamɔ Bono kɛ Ashanti yɛ adebɔɔ naa Eshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi fe niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: What kind of soil should I look for if I want my cassava tubers to grow big?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni o-cassava shishifãi lɛ adara lɛ, mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ otao?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained sandy or loamy soil. Clay soil that holds too much water will cause the tubers to rot underground, while hard soil prevents the tubers from expanding.
ga: Cassava he miihia ŋã loo ŋã ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni ji shikpɔŋ ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ bulb lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava sticks to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should pick stems from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Select thick cuttings from the middle portion of the stem that have visible, healthy buds rather than the soft top ends.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ ashishifãi. Halamɔ tsei niji ni mli tse kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni fɔfɔii ni mli wa ni anaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, hla nɔ nɛ ngɛ hiɔ nɔ nɛ ngɛ blɛoo.

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana?

english: The best time to plant is at the start of the main rainy season, usually around April or May. This gives the cuttings enough soil moisture to sprout strong roots and leaves before any dry spell begins.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ baai ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Can I grow maize on the same piece of land where I plant cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with maize works very well. Maize grows fast and is harvested early within 3 to 4 months, leaving room for the slower-growing cassava plants to spread out later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ haa ŋmeii tsei ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and the ground around the stem may start to crack as the tubers push up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Ekolɛ tso lɛ shishitso lɛ baaje shishi efo be mli ni yitso lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants curling up and showing light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. You can protect your farm by planting improved, disease-resistant stem varieties provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni okwaayeli nitsulɔi efee ni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava tubers contain a lot of water and start reacting with air immediately after harvest, causing them to rot fast. To stop this, you must process them into food like gari or flour quickly, or keep them covered in wet soil until use.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli ni kɛ́ akpa amɛ lɛ, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya Bɔni afee ni akpa enɛ Ehe miihia ni okɛfee niyenii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ oya. Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ awo mli kɛyashi akɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why is cassava considered such a reliable food crop for households across Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ ŋmei akɛ niyenii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha shiabii ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava can stay stored safely underground in the soil for months until you need to eat it. In addition to using the heavy starch tubers for dishes like fufu and banku, the green leaves can also be cooked into nutritious soups.
ga: Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ato shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shweshweeshwe nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi ehe baahia ni oye. Kɛfata ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii tamɔ fufu kɛ banku lɛ he lɛ, abaanyɛ ahoo baai eŋɔli lɛ hu ni afee shwiili ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Why is it easier for cassava farmers who live near major highways to make a good profit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii okwaafoi ni hiɔ gbɛjegbɛi wuji ahe lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Because fresh cassava spoils very quickly after harvest, farms near main transport routes allow buyers and trucks to collect tubers quickly and reach major market towns before the crop goes bad.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmei hee lɛ, fiteɔ oya waa. Bɔ ni ŋmɔji lɛ bɛŋkɛ gbɛjegbɛi wuji ni akɛyaa jɛmɛ lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ lɔlei buaa ŋmeii anaa oya ni amɛyashɛɔ jarayeli maji ni he hiaa lɛ amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ.

english: Why do many farmers plant plantain trees alongside young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Leaving proper space—usually about two feet between rows and one foot between plants—ensures each maize stalk gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors.
ga: He ni sa—bei pii lɛ, aaafee ninetalɔi 2 yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ kɛ ninetalɔi 1 yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ—haa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: How long does it take for cassava to be fully mature and ready for harvesting after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most cassava varieties take between 9 to 12 months to mature, which gives the roots enough time to swell up and store starch underneath the soil.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛdaraa, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that helps plants stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛmaa tsei ni wa.

english: What causes my tomatoes to rot from the bottom while they are still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium, often caused by irregular watering or sudden dry spells while fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato mli lɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo trukaa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How do I pick the best cassava stems to use for my next planting stock?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ midumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Choose mature, hard stem cuttings from healthy plants that are 8 to 12 months old, making sure the stems show no signs of disease or insect damage.
ga: Halamɔ tsei niji ni wa ni eda kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ ni hela loo kooloi ni efite tso lɛ he okadi ko akafee.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is severe drought, as heat stress prevents the flowers from pollinating properly.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba waa. Yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to let weeds grow close to my young yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ mibibii sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from young yam plants, which weakens the vines and prevents big tubers from growing underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ sweet potato tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni ehaaa bulb wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my field is getting too much water during the heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔji lɛ miihe nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: If water collects on the surface for days and crop leaves turn pale and soft, the roots are suffocating from a lack of air in the waterlogged soil.
ga: Kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ŋwɛi gbii babaoo ni tso lɛ baai lɛ bafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to dry my harvested maize thoroughly before putting it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Drying maize removes moisture that molds need to grow and stops destructive pests like weevils from multiplying inside your stored grain.
ga: Abɛi ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔtɔ adara lɛ kɛyaa. ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my green mangoes keep dropping to the ground and rotting before they are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi ni eŋɔli lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree experiences stress from irregular rain, poor nutrients, or fruit fly attacks. The tree sheds excess fruit it cannot support so it can save energy for the remaining crop.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. niyenii ni ehiii loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa lɛ Tso lɛ baawo aduawai ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yams rot inside the soil if I do not harvest them as soon as the leaves dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikpaaa amɛ kɛji baai lɛ egbi pɛ?

english: When the yam vine dries, the tuber stops growing. Leaving tubers in hot, damp soil leaves them vulnerable to soil bacteria, fungi, and insects that feed on and rot the unharvested tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa sũ mli helai, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni akpaaa lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes start rotting from the bottom while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛmiida lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant lacks calcium, often caused by inconsistent watering where the soil goes from extremely dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ calcium. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge bushy leaves above ground but very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy foliage above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn yellow and dry up while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt. It is a natural process where young cocoa trees thin out excess pods they cannot feed, though severe wilting can also be caused by lack of water or fungal diseases.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherel ni shwieɔ shi. Eji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni faaa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela hu baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ hela ni naa wa aba moŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow flowers at the top before any corn ears show up on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋwɛi dani abele toi lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top flowers, called tassels, release pollen that needs to drop down onto the silks of the lower ears. This pollination is what allows the individual corn grains to develop inside the ear.
ga: Atsɛɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akɛ tassel. Ejieɔ pollen ni esa akɛ etsɔ siliki ni bɔle toi lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ pollination nɛɛ ji nɔ ni haa ŋmãa ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ toi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my dried oil palm seeds take so many months to sprout even when I keep the soil wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have a thick outer shell and go into a natural deep sleep called dormancy. They require heat treatment to break the shell's defense before water can get inside to start germination.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli tse ni amɛboteɔ wɔɔhe ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛmiitao dɔlɛ koni amɛfite ŋshɔŋloo lɛ hebuu lɛ dani nu abote mli ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why do I need to build a palm leaf shed over my young pepper seedlings in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young pepper seedlings have fragile roots and tender leaves that dry out quickly in direct sun. A shade structure creates a soft environment that protects them until they are strong enough to be transplanted into open fields.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni waaa kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni baabu amɛhe lɛ baa kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfã kɛya ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli.

english: Why does my plantain stem produce smaller bunches when I allow all the shoots to grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ bibii beni mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? mi plantain lɛ

english: Multiple side shoots, or suckers, steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the main stem. Pruning extra suckers ensures all food goes into one main plant, producing larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yitsei lɛ, loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi babaoo lɛ, juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa niyenii lɛ fɛɛ hiɔ tso titri kome nɔ. Ehaa plantain tsei ni dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ baa.

english: How does planting a thick line of lemongrass around my vegetable field protect my main crops?
ga: Lemongrass tsei ni mli tse ni aduɔ Te aduawai ŋmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Lemongrass acts as a natural physical and scented barrier. Its strong aroma repels many crop-damaging insects, and its dense growth prevents soil erosion and blocks stray farm animals from entering your vegetable plot.
ga: Lemongrass tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɔmɔtsoŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ he gbɛtsii nii. Ehe muji ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni bɔ ni edaa waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni elaaje lɛ akabote o-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves food from old lower leaves to feed the young upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites hiding on the underside of the leaves and sucking out the plant juices. Treating the plants early with neem oil or appropriate sprays removes these pests and allows healthy leaves to unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa tsu nii lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it. Shade trees or fast-growing plantains act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from harsh heat until its roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam plants naturally climb to catch sunlight, which powers the plant to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground where they get maximum light and stays safe from ground heat and rotting fungi.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ ni amɛnáa la babaoo yɛ lɛ. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools around them without draining, cutting off oxygen to the roots and encouraging rot-causing organisms. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. nu bɛ mli Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa. ni ekanyaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do groundnut flowers need loose, soft soil around the base of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers drop, the plant grows long stems called pegs that must push down into the earth to grow the nuts underground. Soft, well-tilled soil allows these pegs to bury easily into the ground to produce pods.
ga: Beni ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni esa akɛ ashɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛdu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baafu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or sudden dry conditions, which stops the flowers from pollinating properly. Keeping soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots keeps the plant cool enough to turn flowers into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my mature plantain plants fall over easily during wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily untether under heavy bunches, especially if tiny soil worms or root rot have damaged them. Propping the heavy stem with a strong wooden pole supports the weight and prevents wind from knocking it over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ ajɛ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ ashishi oya. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ kpata amɛhiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, efiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ he.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to drink water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food, light, and water your main crop needs to get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii, kane, kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why does my rainfed rice stunt and look pale during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice requires a steady supply of root moisture to move minerals up into its leaves and stems. During short droughts, the plant stops growing to conserve water, but keeping organic compost in the soil helps hold moisture around the roots longer.
ga: Omɔ he miihia nu ni yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ minerals aya baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli Tsei baakpa amɛdalɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi kɛ́ akɛ organic compost wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen when the ground stays flooded for too long, which prevents the plant roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to grow good crops before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dani madu?

english: Healthy soil feels dark, crumbly, and holds moisture well without turning into hard mud. If you see earthworms and decaying leaves in the soil, it means the ground is alive and full of nutrients for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ, egbɔjɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni efeee nɔ ni wa ni efeee muji. Kɛji ona shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ No tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ wala mli ni eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa onibii.

english: What causes small holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa tso bibioo ko teŋ?

english: Small holes inside the leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm, which hide in the growing center of the plant and eat the tender leaf tissue before it opens up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ cutworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ tso lɛ dalɛ teŋgbɛ ni eyeɔ baai bibii amli fãji dani egbeleɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller tubers and fewer grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bulbs bibii ni dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by taking away the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your main crops need to grow big, leaving your crops with less energy to make food.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaahoo nii.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Tall trees provide shade and keep the air cool and moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize eats the same specific nutrients out of the ground every season. If you plant it in the same place repeatedly, the soil loses those nutrients completely and pests that love maize will build up in that soil.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kwraa. Ni kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does covering the dirt around my dry-season vegetables with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-dry be mli aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a hat for the soil. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out the ground, keeping the soil cool and moist for a longer time after you water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ hood Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni awo mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting after the first rainy days begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked into the soil deep enough to wet your whole hand when pushed into the ground, usually after two or three strong rains, so seeds do not dry out and die.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ onine muu lɛ fɛɛ afɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛre bo kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ gbii ni amɛgboii.

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves of the plant turn yellow and fall off, usually around 9 to 12 months after planting. You can test by carefully digging up one plant to check if the roots are thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso ko ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ona shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I just plant the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strength and produce lower yields than their parents. Buying certified seeds ensures you get strong plants that resist diseases and produce maximum grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi fe amɛfɔlɔi. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ haa onine shɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die if I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that get burnt easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees provide shade that protects the young cocoa from harsh heat and retains humidity in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves out to catch sunlight. Staking gets the leaves off the damp ground where they can rot or get diseased, allowing the leaves to make more food to grow large tubers under the earth.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Staking jieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo hela aba amɛnɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When a plantain tree produces too many small shoots (suckers), they all fight with the main tree for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which leads to larger stems and bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ná ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni wa, ni no baaha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni plantain jwɛi lɛ hu agbo.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to stay green and grow. The plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make my next corn crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on this stored nitrogen, growing stronger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa baaye nɛkɛ nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ. Ni ebaada waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo lɛ fɔ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce tiny yields even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and steal the soil's nutrients, water, and sunlight before your plants can reach them. Even with plenty of rain, your crops go hungry because the weeds are consuming all the food in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii po miiye hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right after the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ pɛ?

english: Black pod is a water-loving fungal disease. High rainfall creates moist conditions that allow the fungus to spread easily through water droplets, especially if the air cannot circulate through thick cocoa foliage.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ nu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baatsɔ nu mli ŋmɔtɔi amli egbɛ eshwa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ amli.

english: Why are tiny worms eating holes in the middle whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide deep inside the tender center leaves of corn plants during the day to avoid heat, emerging to feed on the leaf tissue and damage the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛjo hulutsoo lɛ naa foi. Ejeɔ kpo ni eyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperature levels get extremely hot, tomato pollen becomes dry and sticky, preventing the flowers from self-pollinating. Unpollinated flowers cannot produce tomatoes and simply drop off the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ Fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee tomato ni amɛshiɔ tsei kɛkɛ.

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil at the base of the stem begins to crack upward due to the swelling tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Bare trunk left Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ efuu yɛ shishi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they naturally feed the soil and help the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the underground roots cannot get oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ pepper tsei ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, stopping heat from the sun from drying out water quickly and keeping the roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekpaa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ koni ekaha nu lɛ agbi oya. ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat or don't get enough water. Keeping the soil consistently damp and providing light shade helps the flowers stay on and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛmaa shi akɛ tomato.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients while their leaves block sunlight, leaving less energy for the plant to grow big fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haaa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes into the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to eat the soft growing leaf tips inside the corn stalk. Spraying an organic neem seed solution or approved pesticide early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ ashishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem dumɔwui loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Raising the leaves off the damp ground stops leaf rot diseases and gives the plant maximum sunlight to grow bigger yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa koni eye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ ni edara.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the large shade trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting plantains or leaving scattered tall trees gives young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do seeds saved from my high-yielding corn harvest produce weaker crops the following year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yield seeds are hybrids created for a single generation. Saving seeds from your harvest breaks down those strong genetic traits, leading to uneven growth and lower yields in the next season.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee aha yinɔ kome. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nakai fɔmɔ nii ni mli wa lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Is it true that I can make more money growing rubber trees instead of cocoa on my land?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ maná shika babaoo kɛtsɔ rɔbɔt tsei ni maduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ kookoo najiaŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rubber can provide a regular, year-round income once mature because tapping happens frequently, whereas cocoa income is seasonal. However, rubber requires a larger upfront investment and takes about 6 to 7 years before you can start harvesting.
ga: Rɔba tsei baanyɛ aha shika ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ ejaakɛ tapping baa shii abɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ be mli ni shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ kookoo mli lɛ ji be mli nibii ni anáa lɛ, rɔba biɔ ni akɛ shika babaoo awo mli kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni eheɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani ajeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ shishi.

english: Can I plant cocoa trees and rubber trees together on the same field?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu kookoo tsei kɛ rɔba tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is generally not recommended to mix rubber and cocoa closely. Mature rubber trees grow very tall, create dense shade, and have extensive root systems that draw heavy amounts of water and nutrients away from cocoa trees.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ akɛ rɔba afutu kookoo jogbaŋŋ. Rɔba tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ adara waa. Create dense shade Ni eyɛ shishifãi babaoo ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli.

english: How long will I have to wait for a rubber tree to start yielding income after planting?
ga: Kɛ́ midu migbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni rɔbɔt tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 5 to 7 years to grow thick enough for latex tapping. During these early years, you will need to invest in maintenance without getting direct returns from the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atswa amɛ. Yɛ shishijee afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, obaawo shika yɛ tso lɛ saamɔ mli ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɛɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: If I cut down my old cocoa trees to plant a new crop, will the soil still be healthy?
ga: Kɛji ofo kookoo tso momo ko ni odu ehee. Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi lolo?

english: Old cocoa land often loses nutrients after decades of farming. Before planting a new crop like rubber or fresh cocoa, you should clear dead roots to prevent disease spread and enrich the soil with organic matter or fertilizers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ momo nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dani obaadu ŋmɔshi nibii heei tamɔ rɔba loo kookoo hee Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni egboi lɛ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally decline in productivity after 25 to 30 years due to tree aging, soil nutrient exhaustion, and increased vulnerability to diseases like Swollen Shoot or Black Pod.
