ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ayibii baa shi yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etã. ni ehaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu loo ŋmeii ni efee diŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Do rubber trees dry out the soil more than cocoa trees do?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ fe cacao tsei?

english: Yes, rubber trees have deep and aggressive root systems that absorb large amounts of underground water, which can reduce moisture in the topsoil for surrounding smaller plants during dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, rɔba tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛduɔ tsei bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing rubber trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha rɔbɔt tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Rubber trees thrive best in deep, well-drained, slightly acidic soils in regions with high rainfall and warm weather. Flat or gently sloping lands prevent waterlogging, which helps rubber roots grow deep.
ga: Rɔba tsei daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyɛ acid fioo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ kɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ. He ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo he ni etse fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa rɔba shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Does managing a rubber farm require more daily work than managing a cocoa farm?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ biɔ daa gbi nitsumɔ babaoo fe kookoo ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ?

english: Once mature, rubber requires steady, skilled labor almost daily or every few days for latex tapping. Cocoa labor, on the other hand, comes in heavy seasonal spikes during weeding, spraying, and harvesting periods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ rɔbɔt lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Rɔba biɔ nitsumɔ ni he esa yɛ be fɛɛ mli nɔ ni miihe ashɛ daa gbi loo daa gbi kroko. Gbii fioo komɛi ni akɛbaatswa late lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo nitsumɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ.

english: Why are some farmers in my district replacing their cocoa farms with rubber plantations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsake kookoo ŋmɔji amɛmiifee rɔbɔt ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Farmers often convert to rubber when old cocoa trees succumb to diseases like Swollen Shoot, or when they want a more continuous monthly income stream rather than relying on seasonal cocoa harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi tsakeɔ kɛyaa rɔbɔt dumɔ nɔ kɛ́ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbe kookoo tsei momoi lɛ, loo kɛ́ ehe miihia ni amɛná shika ni yaa nɔ babaoo daa nyɔɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ kookoo ni afeɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do rubber trees grow so much faster and taller than cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔba tsei daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Rubber trees are naturally fast-growing canopy trees designed to reach high into the sunlight quickly, while cocoa trees naturally prefer growing under moderate shade or filtered light in lower forest layers.
ga: Rɔba tsei ji tsei bibii ni daa oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni afee koni amɛyashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli loo la ni mli tse yɛ koo lɛ shishigbɛ fãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, a key nutrient maize needs to build green leaves and strong stalks. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season fixes this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow quickly and produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in overly wet and shady conditions. Pruning unnecessary farm foliage to let sunlight and fresh air through helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Baai ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni he ehiaaa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant leaves during the day and feed at night. Catching them early and treating them with proper control measures prevents major crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa seedlings acts as a living shield, keeping them cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ahe lɛ baatsu nii akɛ tsɔne ni hiɛ ka. Ha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make energy for the underground tubers. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents fungal diseases and leads to larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ekɛ sweet potatoes ni dara baa.

english: Planting too close together actually reduces your yield because individual plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows every ear of corn to grow full and heavy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo aba shi ejaakɛ tso fɛɛ tso kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa toi fɛɛ toi adara kɛyashɛ elɛɛmɔ kɛ etsitsinɔnii fɛɛ he.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from last season's hybrid maize grow as well as the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields for one generation only. Seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities, resulting in smaller, weaker crops in the second year.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha yinɔ kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time of year ensures the flowers successfully turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ aye omanye.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and watery instead of big and starchy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tapioca lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ nu yɛ agbo ni eyɛ starch najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small if planted in hard, compacted soil or harvested before reaching full maturity. Planting in loose, well-drained soil lets the roots easily expand and store starch.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ loo akpa dani amɛdara kwraa. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmeii amli.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to grow cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ cacao tsei?

english: Healthy soil for cocoa is usually dark in color, feels moist, crumbles easily in your hand, and is rich in decayed leaves. If the soil is very sandy, hard like rock, or stays flooded with water for days, cocoa roots will struggle to grow and absorb nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Feeling moisturized Egbeeɔ shi mlɛo yɛ nine mli ni eyɛ baai ni fiteɔ babaoo Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋã babaoo Ewa tamɔ tɛ loo nu ni ekɛ ehe ewo mli gbii babaoo Cocoa shishifãi lɛ naa wa akɛ amɛaadara ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker when I plant on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Plants pull specific food and nutrients out of the earth as they grow. When you grow the same crop continuously in one spot, it completely drains those specific nutrients from the soil, leaving the land tired and making plants weak unless the soil is rested or fed.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Beni oduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ he kome lɛ. Ebaajie nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwraa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ja hejɔɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate, thin leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle direct, intense heat. Without taller shade plants like banana or plantain to shield them, the hot sun dries out their water supply faster than their roots can drink it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni yeɔ hulutsoo nɔ tamɔ banana loo plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu jɛɛhei lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu amɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial insects to move pollen from flower to flower so fruit can form. If the weather is too dry, if the tree lacks nutrients, or if chemical sprays kill these helpful insects, the flowers cannot turn into pods and will fall off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi fioo komɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ bɔni afee ni aduawai aba. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Aloo kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do cocoa trees shed many of their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way of protecting itself from drying out. Leaves lose water into the dry air, so by shedding them during dry weather, the cocoa tree conserves precious moisture inside its trunk and roots to survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ. Cacao tsei lɛ buɔ nu ni jara wa yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some of my green cocoa pods turn black and rot while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal disease called black pod, which spreads through water droplets during heavy rains and humid weather. Excess shade, trapped moisture, and lack of airflow create the ideal warm, wet conditions for the disease to attack pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa koni akɛtutua ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for the same water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from each other above ground. Giving each tree enough space allows it to grow full, healthy branches and produce more pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe baai tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha ená niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ebaawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal food, nitrogen, and nutrients directly from the soil before your crops can reach them. Even with enough water, a crop without soil nutrients cannot produce green chlorophyll, causing its leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ niyenii, nitrogen, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po lɛ Tsei ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil ni ji eŋɔli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why is it helpful to trim off extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming or pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree does not waste energy feeding them. It also lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the center of the tree, which keeps the tree dry and reduces fungal diseases.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ yɛ niyenii yeli mli Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do cassava plants produce smaller tubers when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei bulbs lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs strong, direct sunlight on its leaves to manufacture the energy required to swell its roots into large tubers. When big trees block the sunlight, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach the light instead of growing heavy tubers underground.
ga: Yucca he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Beni tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu bulbs ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to produce healthy foliage. Applying animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea can replenish the soil and restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji ŋmɔji lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on the same plot where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize consumes large amounts of nutrients from the soil, while legumes like beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops restores soil fertility naturally without relying heavily on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ waa.

english: What causes ragged holes in my young corn leaves with tiny caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest common across West Africa that feeds heavily on corn foliage. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract sprays into the whorl of the leaf can control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ Afrika Anaigbɛ fɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai babaoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves during the rainy season, causing the whole plant to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is tomato blight, a fungal disease that thrives in warm, wet weather when leaves stay wet for long periods. Staking tomato plants off the ground and spacing them wider apart improves airflow, which helps leaves dry quickly and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji tomato hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ baai lɛ mli edɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ odu tomato tsei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ amɛ abɔ he babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do I need to grow plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide broad, leafy shade that acts as an umbrella, protecting young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a sudden dry spell. Ensuring consistent soil moisture during hot periods helps the plant retain its flowers so they can mature into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. loo trukaa shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away the small extra stems growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fata he lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra stems, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around roots in soil that drains poorly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off, preventing waterlogging around the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsi ehe kɛbɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for underground root growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, maximizing sunlight absorption, reducing leaf diseases, and resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulu la ni shɛɔ mɔ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ehaa tsei amli helai baa shi, ni ehaa sweet potato tsei wuji baa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi shwieɔ shi No hewɔ lɛ mi tso shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation and keeping the roots cool. Over time, the grass breaks down and adds organic matter to enrich the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ shi ni oha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i Beni be hoɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ fãa ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows its roots to spread and feed well, resulting in thicker stalks and bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know which small suckers to cut away from my plantain tree so that I get bigger bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafolɔ mi plantain tso lɛ mli tsei bibii koni maná tsei niji wuji?

english: Plantain suckers draw food away from the main fruiting tree. Leaving only one strong follower sucker alongside the mother tree ensures that all the soil nutrients and water go directly into developing a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwui shwieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome ni he wa yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii fɛɛ yaa plantain akui wuji ni tsii lɛ ashweremɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do people tell me that planting cowpeas or peanuts makes the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and peanuts belong to a family of plants that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies and rots, this stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts fata tsei ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already damp and the crop is growing fast, but not right before a heavy rainstorm. Applying it a few inches away from the stem and covering it lightly with soil protects it from being carried away by surface water.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni tsei lɛ miida oya lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ owoɔ dani ahum ni naa wa ko baa. Okɛ inchi fioo komɛi awo tso lɛ shishi ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ fioo. Koni akaŋɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛya.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat because their roots are shallow and lose water faster than they can absorb it. Shade trees or plantains act as living shields, keeping the cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi kɛha wala. Ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers using sunlight caught by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves into the air and sunlight while keeping them off the damp ground, which prevents leaves from rotting and helps the tuber grow bigger underneath.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tswaa baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ agbo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my mature tomato fruits crack open on the bush after a sudden heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ mi jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa trukaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When tomato plants go through a dry period and suddenly receive a lot of water, the inside of the fruit grows faster than the outer skin can stretch. This sudden pressure causes the skin to split open.
ga: Beni tomato tsei tsɔɔ be mli ni nu hulu enyɔ shi trukaa lɛ, amɛnáa nu babaoo. Yibii lɛ amli fã lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard and woody to cook if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava stays past its maturity period, the plant turns its food reserves into tough, woody fibers instead of soft starch. Harvesting at the right age keeps the tubers soft and good for cooking.
ga: Ejaakɛ ŋmei lɛ eye fe afii pɔtɛɛ ko. Kɛkɛ ni nitsumɔhe lɛ tsake niyenii ni ato lɛ efee tso mli tsɔi ni wa yɛ ashikishaŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the bush from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi jwɛi lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant sicknesses. Clearing weeds around the farm and using safe insect treatments helps keep leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ni ajieɔ Okwaayeli kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from the high-yielding maize I bought and harvested last season to plant again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mihe ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Special store-bought seeds (hybrids) are bred from specific parent plants to yield high in their first year. If you plant the seeds harvested from that crop, the next generation loses that vigor, resulting in uneven growth and smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapoi krɛdɛɛi amli (hybrid) lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: Can I use crushed neem leaves and local herbs to protect my maize from armyworms?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ neem baai ni atswa kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai abu ŋmãa he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ahe?

english: Yes, neem leaves contain natural bitter compounds that repel insects and stop them from feeding. Extracting juice from crushed neem leaves and spraying it on young maize works as an affordable botanical insecticide.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ko ni yɔɔ neem baai lɛ amli ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni ehaaa amɛye nii. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ neem baai ni atswa lɛ mli ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jara waaa ni jɛɔ tsei amli.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The virus weakens the plant, making it unable to produce large tubers.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Virus haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afee yitsei wuji.

english: How do leaves from local trees help improve my soil quality naturally?
ga: Te baai ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: When leaves fall and decay, they turn into organic matter called humus. This acts like a sponge to hold moisture during dry spells and slowly releases natural nutrients into the soil for crop roots to absorb.
ga: Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ humus. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio koni tsei shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from too much direct heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor pollination. Maintaining a moderate tree canopy provides necessary shade to keep flowers healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni fe nine ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni ehiii Tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are there safe organic spray remedies I can prepare at home for black spots on my pepper plant leaves?
ga: Ani tsofa ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni ji tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni manyɛ masaa yɛ shia kɛha ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ pepper tso lɛ baai anɔ lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, spraying a mild solution of soapy water mixed with wood ash or baking soda helps suppress fungal leaf spots by creating an alkaline environment where fungi cannot easily grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ tso mli ashwishwɛ loo baking soda efutu mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛtsi fungal leaf spot lɛ naa kɛtsɔ alkaline shihilɛ ni fungus nyɛŋ adara yɛ mli lɛ ni eeefee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds and herbs grow much faster on my farmland than my planted crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild plants are native to the local soil and climate, making them tough and fast to adapt. Their seeds lie dormant in the soil waiting for water and can capture sunlight and nutrients much quicker than domesticated crops.
ga: Koo mli tsei ji shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe oya. Amɛ dumɔwui lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛmiimɛ nu. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛto hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ahe oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shia mli lɛ.

english: Will planting large trees near my vegetable farm take away food from my crops?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni madu yɛ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ baaha niyenii ni jɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaje mli?

english: Yes, large tree roots spread out wide to draw water and fertilizer from the upper soil layers, while their thick leaves block light, causing sun-loving vegetables underneath to grow thin and weak.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei wuji ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa koni amɛgbala nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa Enɛ haa aduawai ni sumɔɔ hulu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: What makes my harvested yams rot quickly while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungal or bacterial spores entering small cuts made during harvesting. Storing yams in hot, unventilated barns speeds up this decay, whereas cool air flow keeps them firm.
ga: Fungal spores loo bacteria ni shwieɔ shi bibii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni egbo baa. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ baaha nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ oya. yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ bɔleɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow starting from the leaf tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip and moving down the center in a V-shape is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the main nutrient responsible for strong green leaves and fast plant growth.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa kɛ tsei adalɛ oya.

english: This is usually caused by Bacterial Wilt, a soil disease where harmful bacteria clog the plant's internal water pipes. Even if the ground is full of water, the plant cannot draw it up to the stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsiɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ Shi tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I inspect my farmland closely before buying seeds to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mahe dumɔwui ni mikɛdu lɛ?

english: Different crops require specific soil conditions and moisture levels. Checking your land first prevents you from wasting money and labor on seeds that cannot thrive in that specific spot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ha. Kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛ nitsumɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni baakwɛ̃ŋ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my land gets enough rain for growing maize successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Maize needs steady rainfall, especially when flowering. If your area has very short or unreliable rainy periods, the corn stalks will dry up before producing full cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. titri lɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii baa Kɛji he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo loo anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ baa.

english: What signs on my land show that I should NOT plant crops there?
ga: Ani okadii komɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Standing pools of water that do not drain, heavily cracked dry soil, or rocky ground mean crops will struggle to grow deep roots or breathe, leading to poor yield or total failure.
ga: Nubu ni ekã shi ni nu hoɔɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni egbɛ eshwa waa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo shishifãi loo amɛfo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ loo etsuuu nii kwraa.

english: Can I plant maize on any type of soil in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi fɛɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: No, maize grows best in deep, well-drained soil with good organic matter. It performs poorly in waterlogged swamps or very sandy soils that cannot hold moisture.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Amɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to corn plants if the rains stop too early in the season?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmãa tsei anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra tsɔ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: If rain stops early, corn plants suffer severe water stress, causing leaves to curl and dry up, which results in empty or poorly filled corn cobs.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ baaná nu he haomɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: If the rain is light this year, should I still plant my usual water-loving crops?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ afi nɛɛ Ani esa akɛ makwɛ tsei ni sumɔɔ nu ni sa?

english: It is risky to plant water-demanding crops during a low-rain season. It is better to switch to drought-tolerant crops like cassava or cowpeas, or hold off on planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni nu faaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ yɛ oshara. Ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ oootsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei nɔ. loo amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ dumɔ he

english: How can I tell if my land holds too much water for corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa tsɔ kɛha ŋmãa?

english: If rainwater sits on top of the soil for days without soaking in, the land is waterlogged. Corn roots in this environment will rot because they cannot get oxygen.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni etsɔɔɔ mli lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ baagboi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look healthy when young but die before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa beni amɛdara shi amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Crops often fail late in the season if the water supply drops during their flowering stage or if the soil lacks enough nutrients to support the plant as it forms fruits or seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fiteɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ kɛji nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ba shi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ beni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Is it safe to assume this year's rain will start at the same time as last year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaasusu akɛ afi nɛɛ nugbɔ lɛ baaje shishi yɛ be kome too mli kɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Rainfall timing changes from year to year. Relying only on past weather can lead to planting too early in dry soil or too late in heavy rains, which harms seed germination.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ bei tsakeɔ daa afi. Kɛ́ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni eho lɛ pɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha adu nii mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo adu sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni yeɔ dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ awui lɛ

english: What should I do if I realize my land is not suitable for growing corn?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa?

english: Instead of forcing corn on unsuitable land, you can pick crops that match your land's conditions, such as growing cassava on poorer soil or rice in low-lying, wet areas.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyɛ ŋmãa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni esaaa nɔ Obaanyɛ ohala ŋmãa ni sa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the maize regain its deep green color and grow bigger ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ toi wuji.

english: Why does planting beans alongside my maize make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas work with beneficial microbes in the ground to capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food. This enriches the soil and leaves nutrients behind for maize and other crops.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eshiɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛhaa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil because waterlogged ground suffocates the roots, preventing them from breathing and allowing fungal diseases to rot them underground. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii helai fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my sorghum crop survive long dry spells much better than my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deep root system that can reach water far underground, and its leaves can roll up tight during extreme heat to stop moisture from evaporating, allowing it to survive until rains return.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akaho. Ha ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce plenty of flowers but fail to form any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called thrips feed on cowpea blossoms before pods can form, causing the flowers to drop off. Spraying the crop with recommended organic or chemical controls at the start of flowering protects the blossoms so they can produce beans.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ thrips lɛ yeɔ cowpea fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ. haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tight and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and spreading viruses. Treating the plants early with neem oil spray helps kill these pests and allows flat, healthy leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ daa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die in the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by soil-borne bacteria or fungi that block the water-carrying tubes inside the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or sorghum helps clear these harmful organisms from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helatsɛmɛi loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛfaa paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up wooden stakes to give me large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture food, which is then stored in the root as a tuber. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight and stay free from leaf diseases, resulting in much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tamɔ tuber Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni foliar hela akaye amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ bafee wuji babaoo.

english: How do my groundnut plants produce nuts underground when the flowers bloom above the soil?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni mi-peanut tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated in the air, it forms a small stem called a peg that grows downward and burrows itself into the soil, where the nut develops safely away from sun and pests.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli sɛɛ lɛ Ebaafee ŋmei bibioo ko. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the roots of my soybean plants have small round bumps on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Those small bumps on soybean roots are called nodules, and they house friendly bacteria that trap nitrogen from the air to feed the plant naturally without needing costly chemical fertilizers.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ soybean shishifãi anɔ lɛ akɛ nodules. Ni amɛji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛkɛha tsei niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Can I plant cashew trees on the same farm where I grow my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cashew tsei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ cocoa tsei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, but you must space them carefully. Cashew trees grow very large and need full sunlight, so if planted too close, they will block the light and steal nutrients from your cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Cashew tsei lɛ dara waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ adu lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatsi la naa ni ebaaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli.

english: Will mixing different crops on my farm cause them to fight for nutrients in the soil?
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ani enɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If crops are planted too close together, they will compete for water and food. However, proper spacing and combining crops with different root depths allows them to share the land without harming each other.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛhaa nu kɛ niyenii. Shi kɛlɛ, sɛɛkuu ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi srɔtoi yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaato he lɛ haa amɛjaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛyeee amɛhe awui.

english: What is the benefit of planting quick-growing crops alongside my main tree crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni mikɛ mi tsei titrii lɛ masɛi lɛ he?

english: Quick-growing crops provide shade for delicate young trees and give you food or cash income to live on while you wait years for main crops like cocoa or cashew to start producing harvest.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa hulutsoo. ni eha bo niyenii loo shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ kookoo loo cashew ŋmeii. je kpamɔ shishi

english: Why are my old cocoa trees still producing pods while people are telling me to replace them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ cacao tso lɛ ato najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Older cocoa trees have deep root systems that help them survive and yield pods, but as they age further, their total output slowly drops and they become more likely to catch diseases.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ Amɛ nibii fɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ fiofio. lɛ baa shi ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hela

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight without protective shade trees or temporary crops like plantain keeping the area cool and moist.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ ni tsei loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni haa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees need deep, soft soil that drains water easily so the roots do not rot, along with balanced rainfall and shade from taller trees.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia kokoo tsei. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ amli lɛ fata he.

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree usually yields peak harvests for about 25 to 30 years, after which the harvest starts to decline significantly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ he aaafee afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi waa.

english: Can cashew trees survive on land where cocoa is struggling to grow?
ga: Ani cashew tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kookoo miitao ni ekwɛ̃ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cashew trees are very tough and can survive in drier climates and poorer soil conditions that would normally cause cocoa trees to dry up and fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, cashew tsei lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do I know when cashews are ready to harvest on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni cashew ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cashews are fully ripe when the cashew apple turns bright yellow or red and the entire fruit naturally falls off the tree onto the ground.
ga: Cashews lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ aduawai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsuru ni mli tse. Ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ fɛɛ baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Which crop will start making me money faster between cashew and cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baaje shika shishi aha mi oya: cashew nuts loo cocoa?

english: Cashew trees generally start bearing fruit in three to four years, while improved cocoa varieties also take around three to four years, making both good medium-term investments.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ. Abuɔ lɛ akɛ eji shikawoo kpakpa yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is very hot, plants lose water quickly through tiny pores in their leaves. Curling up helps them reduce surface exposure, trap moisture, and protect themselves until the heat passes.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. Curling haa nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ebuɔ ehe he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why does the soil around my plants dry out so quickly during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Direct hot sunlight causes water in the topsoil to evaporate rapidly into the air. Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves (mulch) shades the ground and traps moisture for your plant roots.
ga: Hulu la ni mli edɔ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (Mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it harmful to water my crops in the middle of a very hot day?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ oooha ŋmɔshi nibii nu yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Yes, watering during hot sunlight causes quick evaporation before roots absorb it, and water droplets left on leaves can focus sunlight, causing mild leaf burns.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ. Ni nu bibii ni eshwɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii ashã.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables lose their quality and market value when I pick them under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ jarayeli sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baa shi kɛ́ mikɛto hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Harvesting in high heat causes crops to lose moisture instantly and wilt, making them decay much faster before reaching buyers. Harvesting early in the morning keeps them firm and fresh.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kwraa dani amɛshɛɔ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ. Kɛ́ akpa loo lɛ leebi lɛ, ehaa loo lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant young seedlings to my main field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui bibii kɛya miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli?

english: Transplanting early in the morning or late in the afternoon gives fragile young roots cooler soil and time to settle before facing harsh midday heat.
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ leebi loo shwane mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛ be ni amɛkɛhiɔ shi dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my harvested grains and tubers spoil faster when left out under direct sunlight after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui kɛ bulbs ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Direct sun heat speeds up internal crop spoilage and creates warm, inviting environments for pests. Storing fresh harvests under shade keeps them cooler and preserves their quality longer.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii heei ni anáa lɛ to hulutsoo be shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Extreme atmospheric heat can ruin a plant's pollen, causing severe stress that forces the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy rather than set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata tso ko mli muji lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa aahu akɛ ehe bahiaa ni tsei lɛ ajie fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my farm on a very hot, sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve properly. Applying them in high heat without water can cause concentrated salts to burn plant roots and ruin the crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsu nii ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can planting taller crops next to shorter ones protect my farm from heat stress?
ga: Te tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ tsei kukuji ahe lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Taller crops act as natural sun shields, creating cooling shade for delicate short crops below and keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔnei ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do young crops grown under partial shade look greener than those left in open heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ feɔ eŋɔli fe dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat damages plant green pigments (chlorophyll) and stresses leaves, whereas gentle shade protects leaves, helping them stay green and produce food efficiently.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli tsofa ni ji eŋɔli (chlorophyll) lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ haoɔ. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli jɔ buɔ baai lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green foliage. This often happens when heavy rain washes away nutrients or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with tiny yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of using energy to build thick stems and large fruits, the plants stretch upward rapidly just to reach light.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai wuji. Tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni enyɛ emɔ la lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply dry fertilizer around my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsuɔ nii kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants can only drink nutrients that are dissolved in water; they cannot take in dry fertilizer. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the crop cannot absorb it until it rains.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. Amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ lɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct sunlight and to keep the soil cool and moist. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense heat dries out the seedlings faster than their young roots can absorb water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do I need to put up stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food that builds the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes ensures the leaves get full sunlight and prevents them from rotting on wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni ehaaa efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep inside the leaf whorl during the hot part of the day to feed on soft new leaves, leaving behind chewed holes and insect waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni shwieɔ baai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be lɛ mli koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Shi bu ni atsɔ mli kɛ kooloi bibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and twisting into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects as they feed on the plant sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing flowers, but the blossoms keep falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime heat gets too high or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly between wet and dry. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed the unused flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni akɛtsuuu nii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil if heavy rains continue for too long near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa tee nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave soil continuously waterlogged, water fills all the air spaces, suffocating the roots and causing soil fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that spread sideways rather than deep into the ground. When the heavy bunch forms at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to uproot it from wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa amɛsɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmeii ni tsii fee yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baagbala shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Rice plants thrive in shallow standing water because the water suppresses weeds and keeps the roots continuously moist, whereas maize roots will rot if left underwater.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu shishi.

english: Why is it better to buy certified rice seeds instead of planting seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist common local diseases, germinate evenly, and give you a much higher yield than saved seeds that lose their strength over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsaa amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato, ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a signal that your plants are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer or that excess water is preventing the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa fe nine lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer on the field right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani ahum baatswa?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer away into streams or deep into the soil before your crops' roots have a chance to drink it up, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛnuɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Which direction should I point cassava stem cuttings when I push them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei nine lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: You must plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to grow and reduces your yield.
ga: Ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ ni baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why is it important to remove weeds in the first few weeks after my crops come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eje kpo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and easily choked out by fast-growing weeds; clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the water and food they need to grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do small insects get into my harvested grain bags when I store them in the room?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli kotokui lɛ amli kɛ́ mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli?

english: Weevils and pests often come from eggs laid on the grain before harvest or from dirty old sacks; drying grain properly and using clean, airtight bags keeps them out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmaa nɔ dani akpaa loo kɛjɛɔ kotokui momo ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ vacuum kotokui ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up; changing crops each season keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without turning into vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage, leaving the plant without enough strength to form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ náaa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that act as natural sunshades, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while it grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to get maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I drop three or four maize seeds together into the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planted too closely together, the seeds will compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and tiny corn cobs instead of strong plants with big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Yɛ tso ni wa ni ŋmei agbo yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and turning wrinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap under the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. Treating the plants for pests stops new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Pest treatment koni akɛtsi baai heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anaa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Consistent watering and keeping the root area cool helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni aaaha efee fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive sitting in stagnant water for too long because the soil loses all its air. Waterlogged soil causes the roots to drown and decompose before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ efo mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛfiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, the soil is enriched with free fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni okpaa nii lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the sun from drying out the soil quickly. It holds in moisture, keeps root temperature low, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ha shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ aba shi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my young crops wither away even if I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The first rain of the year is often a false start, followed by dry, hot weather before the true rainy season begins. If the seeds germinate during this dry gap, the tender seedlings dry out and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ateŋ Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during dry spells to conserve water, acting like they are resting to survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛto nu. Kɛtsɔ amɛnifeemɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiihe hejɔɔmɔ koni amɛye amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my yam set take a very long time to sprout after I plant it in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni adu yɛ gɔji anɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural rest period called dormancy after harvest. If you plant them while they are still resting, they will remain inside the warm soil until their internal body clock wakes them up to sprout.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu amɛ be mli ni amɛwɔ lolo lɛ, Amɛbaahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛmli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa lɛ baate amɛ shi koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and slender with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. They waste their energy stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of building strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni shɛɔ hulu lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei akui ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my plantain sucker take almost a year before I see a bunch coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain sucker lɛ he nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani ena ŋmeii ni fãa lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk must grow around 30 to 40 broad leaves first to store enough food energy. Only after gathering enough energy can it push out the flower from inside the stem to form a full bunch of plantains.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tso lɛ aná baai ni mli kwɔ 30 kɛyashi 40 dani enyɛ ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato. Beni abua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa pɛ kɛkɛ ni abaanyɛ ajie fɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli koni efee plantains kuu ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives leaves their rich green color and helps plants grow fast. Applying fertilizer rich in nitrogen will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo amɛmli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the edges of my pepper plant leaves look like they are scorched or burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi tamɔ nɔ ni eshã loo eshã lɛ?

english: Burnt leaf edges can mean the soil lacks potassium, which helps plants manage water, or it could mean too much fertilizer was applied at once, which burns the root system.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishi ni eshã lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ nu nɔ. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baafata he shikome. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: If I spray weedicide on my farm, how does it destroy weeds without killing my maize?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ egbe jwɛi ni egbeee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Selective weedicides are designed to only affect specific plant types, such as broad-leaved weeds, while leaving grass-family crops like maize untouched. However, non-selective weedicides will kill any plant they touch, so you must always check the bottle label.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei komɛi pɛ anɔ, tamɔ jwɛi ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ jwɛi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baagbe tsei ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Can spraying strong agrochemicals during hot afternoons damage my crop leaves?
ga: Ani okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa ni mikɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai?

english: Yes, spraying chemicals under hot direct sunlight causes liquid droplets on leaves to heat up quickly and evaporate, leaving concentrated chemical spots that can scorch and burn leaf tissue. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ adɔ oya ni etsɔ la. Eshiɔ tsofa ko ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã ni ashã baa lɛ mli fãji. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Why do my young tomato flowers drop off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attack by tiny pests like thrips. Ensuring the soil stays moist and protecting the flowers from insects helps them turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips tutua tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni obu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal sickness that thrives in high humidity and deep shade. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight into the farm, which dries the tree canopy and stops the fungus from spreading.
