ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ yitso lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwã.

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential living shade, protecting the young cocoa plants from heat stress and helping the soil hold moisture during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha wala. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize draws a lot of nitrogen out of the soil to grow. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs maximum sunlight on its leaves to produce big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where they can get sunlight easily and stays safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulu la baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya, ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: If too many young shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain stem, they steal water and food from the main plant. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest one or two, allowing the main tree to produce much bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) ni miida yɛ he lɛ Plantain tsei wuji babaoo tsɔ Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso niji ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome loo enyɔ pɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haa tso titri lɛ shwereɔ niji wuji waa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the soil is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage usually fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough regular water. Keeping the soil moist and cool helps the plant keep its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the central shoots of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These pests hide inside the central growing tip of the plant and must be managed early so they do not destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ni esa akɛ atsu he nii mra. bɔni afee ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops suffer so much even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ awui waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that grow faster than crops. They act like thieves, stealing the fertilizers, sunlight, and water meant for your crops, which starves the main plants even during good rain.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli.

english: Cassava roots store soft starch as they mature, but once they pass their ideal harvest age, the plant turns that soft starch into tough woody fibers, making the roots hard to cook and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo toɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi kɛ́ kpamɔɔ be ni sa lɛ ho Tso lɛ baatsake ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahoomɔ wa, ni eyeli hu wa.

english: Why do some farmers attach a branch from a high-yielding tree onto a different stem, and will it ruin my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ aniji fĩɔ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ? Ni ani ebaakpãtã midumɔ nii lɛ ahiɛ?

english: This practice is called grafting. It is a safe and proven technique where a branch from a fast-producing tree is joined to a strong rootstock. It helps crops fruit much faster and stay resistant to diseases without using any harmful chemicals.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ grafting. Eji ŋaa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ana he odaseyeli. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ aniji ni ajieɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shishifã ni wa he lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa, ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. It is not caused by bad weather or spiritual bad luck, and planting disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents it.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Jeee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ gbonyo loo mumɔŋ haomɔ hewɔ. Ni ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai akamɔ mɔ.

english: If I get crop seeds brought from another country, will they grow well on my farm here in Ghana?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui anɔ kɛjɛ maŋ kroko nɔ Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Foreign seeds may struggle to grow because they are not adapted to Ghana's specific soil, temperature, and rainy seasons. It is safer to plant certified seeds approved for your local region.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ ana naagba yɛ dalɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana shikpɔŋ, latsaa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooodu dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can getting text messages on my mobile phone help me know when to plant my maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shɛɛ saji ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ mi-mobail foŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni male be ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa?

english: Agricultural text alerts use weather forecast data to tell you the exact time rains will start. Planting according to these alerts stops your seeds from drying up in hot soil during dry spells.
ga: Okwaayeli he kɔkɔbɔɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsɔɔ bo be ni nugbɔ baabɔi nɛmɔ. Kɛ́ odu yɛ kɔkɔbɔɔi nɛɛ anaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate harsh, direct sun exposure. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa keeps the soil moist and protects the young plants from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and dark green but produces very small corn cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen makes leaves grow large but leaves the plant without enough phosphorus and potassium, which are the nutrients required to fill out strong, heavy grain cobs.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ wuji shi ehaa tso lɛ bɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛwo dumɔwui ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ amli

english: What makes my yam tubers rot underground in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa?

english: Yam rot is caused by microscopic soil pests and fungi when water stays trapped around the roots. Planting on raised soil mounds allows proper water drainage and keeps tubers healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa kɛji nu tsi ehe kɛbɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni bulb lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers onto the ground instead of forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stress and irregular watering cause tomato plants to drop flowers before fruiting. Watering consistently in the early morning protects the blossoms so fruit can form.
ga: Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli baa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa leebi lɛ, ebaabu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce larger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to extract soil nutrients and water very quickly. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing food and water from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli oya waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with wide leaves, acting like living umbrellas that shade the cocoa and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of maize stalks mean the plant lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves on top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants growing lots of big green leaves but producing no flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of spending energy on flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo he lɛ

english: What will happen to my crop if I plant my corn seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, tall stalks and very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why does my maize harvest get smaller every year when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop on the same land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, leading to weak plants over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience high heat stress or inconsistent watering, as a mechanism to save water and protect their own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he ni abuɔ amɛwala he.

english: Why is my cassava plant producing flowers, and does it mean the roots are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Ni ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava flowers naturally to produce seeds as part of its normal growth. Flowering does not mean the root tubers are ready; harvest readiness depends on the months planted and variety.
ga: Cassava fɔfɔii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ dumɔwui aba akɛ dalɛ ni sa lɛ fã. Fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ shishifã lɛ efee klalo. Nikpamɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ damɔ dumɔ nyɔŋ kɛ henɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Afternoon wilting in wet soil often means the roots are damaged by disease or root rot, which prevents them from pumping water up to the leaves fast enough when the sun is hot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shwane mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow faster than my planted crops when rain is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep root systems naturally adapted to harsh conditions, allowing them to steal scarce water and nutrients faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni etsɔ ehe ewo shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni anaaa lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why should I cut off the top growing tip of my garden egg plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ?

english: Cutting the main top tip stops the plant from growing straight up and forces it to sprout side branches, creating a bushier plant that bears far more fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ, ni enyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ niji jeɔ kpo yɛ esɛɛgbɛ. Enɛ haa tso bibioo ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are sitting in too much water and cannot breathe properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get heat-stressed or do not get consistent water, causing the plant to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ dɔlɛ hao amɛ loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu daa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ baa amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and thin without producing many tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo tomato babaoo lɛ?

english: When tomato plants do not get enough direct sunlight, they stretch out seeking light instead of using energy to grow thick stems and heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Tomato baagbala ehe koni ena la moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: How do I know if my farmland is good enough for growing big cassava roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmei shishifãi wuji akwɛmɔ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-draining soil so the roots can expand easily; heavy clay soil holds too much water and causes the tubers to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia cassava bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces maize plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and tiny cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my cowpeas right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The early rains provide warm, moist soil that helps seeds sprout quickly and grow strong roots before any dry spells hit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni edɔɔ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhaa shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ be lɛ baa.

english: How do chemical sprays actually protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Insecticides work either by coating the leaves so insects die when they take a bite, or by getting absorbed into the plant to stop sap-sucking pests.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni kooloi lɛ agbo kɛji amɛye amɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekpa kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm make my main crops grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like nutrient thieves, stealing the water, sunlight, and soil food that your main crop needs to grow healthy and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the extra leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming unnecessary lower leaves directs the plant's food straight into growing fruit while improving airflow to stop leaves from rotting.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ koni baai lɛ akafite.

english: How does adding fertilizer to the soil help my crops give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer gives crops essential plant nutrients like nitrogen and potassium that power root growth, flower production, and larger fruit development.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa, fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ aduawai wuji ni baa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Flowers fall off when they are not pollinated by tiny insects or by hand. Without pollination, the flower cannot complete fertilization, so the tree drops the unfertilized flower instead of growing a fruit or pod.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii loo niji kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ afee fɔmɔ nii kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ni ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmɔtɔ moŋ.

english: What is hand pollination, and why would I need to do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee enɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hand pollination means manually transferring pollen from male flower parts to female flower parts using a tool or tiny brush. Farmers do this when there are not enough natural insects around to ensure flowers successfully turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ dɛŋdade bibioo ko loo brɔsh nɔ. Okwaafoi feɔ enɛ kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee kookoo ŋmeii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How do small insects help my crop trees produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Insects like midges and bees carry pollen from one flower to another while feeding. This movement of pollen fertilizes the flowers, allowing your crops to form fruits, cocoa pods, and seeds.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii woɔ fɔfɔi fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Nɛkɛ pollen lɛ nyiɛmɔ nɛɛ haa fɔfɔi ni woɔ yibii baa. Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo aduawai, kookoo ŋmɔji, kɛ dumɔwui.

english: What harm do weeds actually do to my crops if I leave them on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need to grow strong. Leaving weeds unattended starves your crops, slows down their growth, and creates places for insect pests and snakes to hide.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ anɔ. shwieɔ dalɛ nɔ fioo ni efeɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ onufui baanyɛ ahi

english: How often do I need to weed around my cocoa trees for them to grow well?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa trees usually need clearing every 2 to 3 months because fast-growing weeds can choke them and block sunlight. Older, bushy cocoa trees need weeding at least 3 to 4 times a year to keep the farm clean and easy to inspect.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 ejaakɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ amɛ ni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa. Kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ anɔ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni akwɛ mli oya.

english: Can weeds cause diseases to spread among my crops?
ga: Ani jwɛi baanyɛ aha helai ni baa miŋmɔshi nibii amli aba?

english: Yes, tall weeds trap damp moisture around the stems of your crops, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases like black pod thrive. Weeds also harbor harmful pests that bite crops and pass along viruses.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kakadaji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni mli efɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. tso shishifã Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baanyɛ adara. Jwɛi hu hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ helai baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when tall weeds grow too close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ jwɛi kakadaji lɛ bɛŋkɛ mi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds shade out your crops from sunlight and steal key soil nutrients like nitrogen. When crop roots cannot get enough food and light, their leaves lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ́ tsei shishifãi lɛ náaa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Baai lɛ hu baafite amɛ su eŋɔli ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my crop yields lower this year even though the rains were good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eba shi afi nɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Good rain is only one part of crop growth. If your farm is overgrown with weeds or flowers are not being pollinated properly, the plants cannot convert that rainwater into healthy, full crop yields.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ fã kome pɛ. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi eyi oŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ loo fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei nyɛŋ atsake nugbɔ nu lɛ afee nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does heavy mud and muddy water from nearby land digging affect my farm soil?
ga: Te muji ni tsii kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Thick mud coats the topsoil and blocks air and water from reaching your crop roots. Over time, this chokes the roots, causes them to rot, and prevents crops from absorbing food from the ground.
ga: Muji ni mli edɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu naa koni ekashɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaa amɛgboɔ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to cocoa pods if a farm is left unweeded for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ajieee jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Unweeded cocoa farms develop high humidity, which causes fungal pod rot to spread rapidly. Additionally, overgrown bushes allow rodents and insects to damage and eat the cocoa pods before harvest.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ amli hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa pod rot tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ ni amɛyeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Doc, if my crop yield is dropping every year, will adding fertilizer make my farm produce well again?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, kɛji mi nibii ni mifeɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mikɛbaafata he lɛ baaha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Over time, crops remove essential nutrients from the ground. Adding the right fertilizer or manure restores these nutrients (like nitrogen and phosphorus), helping your soil regain its strength so your farm yield can go back up.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ (tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus) aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ.

english: Doc, why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the crops are getting too much water, missing specific nutrients like nitrogen, or that fertilizer was applied too close to the stem, which burns the roots instead of feeding the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Niyenii mli nibii komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he tsɔ ni bɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shãa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Doc, how does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help my soil stay rich for my next maize crop?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmei kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and leave it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize uses that natural food to grow strong without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa kɛ nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Doc, if I mix different chemicals together to spray my farm, will it make my crops grow faster?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, kɛji mikɛ tsofai srɔtoi futu mli koni mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Ani ebaaha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya?

english: Mixing unapproved chemicals can burn your crop leaves, kill good insects, and ruin your harvest. It is safer to apply each chemical according to recommended guidelines rather than mixing them yourself.
ga: Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai, egbe kooloi kpakpai, ni efite onibii. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ okɛ tsofa fɛɛ tsofa baatsu nii yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa moŋ fe ni bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛbaafutu.

english: Doc, what steps should I follow if I want to clear a new piece of land to grow cassava successfully?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, miisumɔ ni majie he hee ko koni manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Clear the bush and loosen the soil so cassava roots can grow deep and wide. Plant healthy stem cuttings at a slight angle right at the start of the rainy season, and keep the field clean of weeds for the first three months.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛshwere. Dumɔ tsei niji ni mli wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. ni oha jwɛi akafee nɔ ni he tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli.

english: Doc, why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers can grow?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they suffer from too much heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and watering regularly helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni fe nine, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Doc, why does my maize farm produce small cobs with missing grains?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? He ni dumɔwui bɛ lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when maize plants lack water or nutrients during the flowering stage, preventing proper pollination. Planting seeds in neat blocks rather than single long rows helps pollen travel better from plant to plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ blɔkii ni yɔɔ fɛo mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kakadaŋŋ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni pollen lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Doc, is it better to plant cocoa trees alone or mix them with food crops when starting a farm?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, ani ehi akɛ ooodu kookoo tsei pɛ loo okɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ afutu mli kɛ́ ooje ŋmɔ shishi?

english: Planting young cocoa trees alongside plantains or cassava provides the cocoa with needed shade from the hot sun while giving you food and income while you wait for the cocoa trees to mature.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ plantains loo cassava masɛi lɛ, ebaaha kookoo lɛ aná hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he hulutsoo be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Doc, how can I tell if the insects on my farm are harming my crops or helping them?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua amɛ?

english: Insects that chew holes in leaves, suck plant juice, or damage fruits are pests. Beneficial insects, like bees and ladybugs, do not eat the plant; instead, they help flowers turn into fruit or eat bad pests.
ga: Abuɔ koolooi ni shwieɔ baai, amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu, loo amɛfiteɔ aduawai lɛ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Koolooi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Kaaye tso nɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ bua fɔfɔi ɔmɛ nɛ a peeɔ yiblii aloo a yeɔ koolohi yayahi.

english: Doc, why do my tomato fruits develop black, rotten spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Datrɛfonyo, mɛni hewɔ tomatoi lɛ shishigbɛ tsɔji diji ni egboi yɔɔ mli dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when watering is irregular—switching between very dry and very wet soil prevents the roots from taking up calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛji akɛ afɔɔ amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ nɔ tsakemɔ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ calcium.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. This often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when the soil has been overused.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kɛji akɛ sũ babaoo wo mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Maize takes the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot without rotating crops drains the soil, leaving it poor and unable to support healthy plant growth.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni atsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ adalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big stems but have tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much shade or excess nitrogen, it spends its energy growing tall stems and heavy leaves toward sunlight instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni tsii koni ená hulu la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot endure full, direct sunlight or harsh harmattan winds. They need temporary shade plants like plantains to shelter them while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruits when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants require direct sunlight to make the energy needed for quick growth and fruiting. Heavy shade from big trees slows down their development significantly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii. Shade ni mli tse ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants give me smaller peppers when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ pepper bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots and leaves compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all produce smaller fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ejaakɛ tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ woɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than the crops I planted after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Local weeds are naturally adapted to the soil and weather conditions. They wake up quickly with rain and absorb water and nutrients faster than newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Amɛteɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or water supply is irregular. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to protect itself from stress.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tso lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of leaves but very few pods during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baa babaoo shi eshishifãi fioo pɛ yɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cowpeas receive abundant water, the plant focuses on vegetative growth, making leaves and vines instead of stress-induced flowering that produces seed pods.
ga: Kɛji cowpea nine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ baama tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Ewoɔ baai kɛ wain tsei yɛ fɔfɔi ni haomɔ kɛbaa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting quickly in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they suffer cuts during harvest or are stored in hot, closed spaces. Wounds allow fungi to enter, while high temperatures cause moisture buildup that speeds up decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã. Pilamɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli. yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa oya.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help feed the plants and keep them green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni eha amɛhi shi ŋmɔji.

english: Can I start a cassava farm with just a few stem cuttings if I do not have much money?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ niji fioo komɛi pɛ aje ŋmei ŋmɔ shishi kɛji mibɛ shika babaoo?

english: Yes, you can start small with just a few healthy cassava stems. As those plants grow, you can cut their branches to plant a larger farm the following season without spending money on new stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo kɛ ŋmei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ nakai tsei lɛ dara lɛ Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni okɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ofite shika yɛ tsei heei ahe.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried grass keep them alive during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the dirt from direct sunlight. This stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps the root area cool and wet.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ.

english: Why does planting beans in the same farm as my maize make the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are special crops that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When those roots decay, they release natural fertilizer directly into the soil for the maize to feed on.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ nakai shishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that shield the cocoa seedlings from hot sunlight and help keep the surrounding ground moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eye ebua ni eha he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high into the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more food the plant makes to build large tubers underground.
ga: Shishitoo mla ni ji amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tso lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, babaoo ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ bulbs wuji aba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden heat stress and water shortage. The plant panics and drops the flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ baa. Tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes inside the young leaves of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli?

english: Ragged holes inside the center funnel of young maize plants are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms, which hide inside the stem and feed on the soft growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ asraafoi ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ tso lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and getting smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by very small insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves. This damages the young leaves and distorts their growth.
ga: Kooloi bibii waa tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baai bibii ni efiteɔ amɛdalɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and thin even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal the water, plant food, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. If weeds are left in the field, your crops will starve even if there is plenty of rain.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ kɛji nugbɔ babaoo nɛ po.

english: What is harrowing, and how does it help my crop seeds germinate better?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni woɔ mɔ he gbeyei? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harrowing breaks up big soil clods after plowing to create a smooth, fine soil bed. This helps small seeds make close contact with the soil so they can absorb moisture and sprout quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ agboi amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui bibii Ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ kpaakpa No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: How does using a tractor to prepare my land help my crops grow better than using just a hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛsaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii pɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A tractor can loosen the soil deeper and faster than a manual hoe. Deeply loosened soil allows crop roots to grow deep into the earth to find water and nutrients easily.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ ni etsu nii oya fe tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to add fertilizer to my land when plants already get food from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miiná niyenii kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time as crops feed on it season after season. Fertilizer restores those missing nutrients so your current crops have enough strength to grow large and produce high yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ yɛ jwɛi ni ayeɔ yɛ be mli lɛ hewɔ. Fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei ni oyɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so my crops get the most benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing—usually shortly after sprouting and during early growth stages—so the roots can easily absorb the nutrients without burning.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ—bei pii lɛ, beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ kɛ be mli ni edara mra lɛ—koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãaa.

english: Why do my crops stay stunted and weak when the ground is very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil prevents plant roots from spreading out to search for water and nutrients. It also stops air from reaching the roots, which smothers the plant's growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɛɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ

english: How can I get my crops to grow bigger and produce more harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ni makpa nii babaoo?

english: Crops grow big when they have healthy soil, proper spacing so they don't fight for light and food, adequate water, and protection from weeds and pests.
ga: Tsei daa kɛji amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa. Gbɛ ni sa ni esa akɛ akafee akaŋshii kɛha kane kɛ niyenii, nu ni sa, kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe.

english: How do I plan the distance between plants when sowing my fields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato gbɛ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbor, allowing each crop to reach its maximum size.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso shɛɔ elɛɛmɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he.

english: How do I calculate how much seed and fertilizer I need for my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Measure your land size first, then use the recommended rates per acre provided by officers. Applying too little reduces crop growth, while applying too much wastes money and can burn your plants.
ga: Susumɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ shika ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni onukpai lɛ eto yɛ acre kome mli lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aba shi. yɛ be mli ni efiteɔ shika babaoo ni ehaa tsei lɛ shãa.

english: What is satellite farming, and how can it help me monitor my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji satelait okwaayeli? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi koni makwɛ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Satellite farming uses photos taken from space to check the health of your field. It can show you which areas of your crops are thirsty, lacking nutrients, or suffering from pests before you notice with your eyes.
ga: Satelait okwaayeli kɛ mfonirii ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo hei ni kumai yeɔ, niyenii ni esaaa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai miipiŋ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani okɛ ohiŋmɛii po yɔseɔ.

english: Why do crops grown with modern techniques seem to yield much more than traditional methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe blema gbɛi lɛ?

english: Modern techniques combine early land preparation, balanced plant nutrition, improved seed varieties, and precise pest management so crops grow without stress throughout their life cycle.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ mra feɔ ekome. balanced plant nutrients Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Bɔni afee ni tsei adara ni haomɔ ko bɛ he yɛ amɛshihilɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my oil palm fruit bunches grow very heavy while others stay light?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm yibii lɛ ekomɛi tsii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu waaa lɛ?

english: Heavy palm fruit bunches come from trees that receive good nutrients, regular rain, and proper sunlight. The variety of the palm tree also matters, as improved varieties naturally grow larger fruits with thicker flesh.
ga: Palm tsei ni tsii lɛ jɛɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. kɛ hulu la ni sa Tsɛi srɔtoi lɛ hu he miihia. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baawo yibii ni dara ni mli wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes the total weight of my palm fruit harvest to drop during certain seasons?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-palm yibii ni mikpaa lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi yɛ bei komɛi amli?

english: Oil palm trees need consistent water to fill out their fruits. During dry periods, the trees struggle to feed the developing bunches, resulting in smaller, lighter fruits and a lower overall harvest weight.
ga: Nu he miihia oil palm tsei lɛ daa koni amɛyibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena niyenii eha eniji ni miida lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii, ni amɛhe waaa, ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: How can I encourage my oil palm trees to produce larger and heavier fruit bunches?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-oil palm tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii?

english: You can increase bunch weight by applying the right fertilizer around the tree's drip line, clearing weeds that steal soil nutrients, and regularly pruning dead fronds so the tree puts its energy into fruit growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha o-bunch lɛ tsiimɔ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni okɛbaabɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. tso mli nu ni shwieɔ shi Jiemɔ jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ni ŋmɔmɔ baai ni egboi lɛ daa koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii kɛha yibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: How much fresh palm fruit do I usually need to harvest to produce one full drum of palm oil?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, FFB enyiɛ ehe hiaa ni makpa koni maná ŋmei fɔ tanki ni eyi obɔ?

english: Generally, it takes about 1 to 1.3 tons of good-quality fresh palm fruit bunches to extract one standard drum (about 200 liters) of red palm oil, depending on how efficient your pressing method is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee tɔn 1 kɛyashi 1.3 ni ji tsofa-kɛ-ŋma hee ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni akɛjie tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsuru ni ji tso kome (aaafee lita 200), ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ ojieɔ lɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I get less palm oil when I process the fruits myself by hand compared to using a mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmei fɔ nɔ fioo kɛ́ mikɛ nine miitsu aduawai ahe nii kɛ akɛto ŋmei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he lɛ?

english: Manual processing leaves a lot of oil trapped inside the fruit flesh and fiber. Mechanical presses in processing mills apply much higher pressure, squeezing out almost every drop of oil from the fruits.
ga: Nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mu babaoo shwieɔ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsɔji lɛ amli. Mɛkanikal presses ni yɔɔ nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei lɛ kɛ presses ni nɔ kwɔ waa tsuɔ nii. Kɛtsɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔ fɛɛ fɔ ni jɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ni ekɛmiimiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does the weight of the palm fruit bunch directly tell me how much oil I will get?
ga: Ani ŋmei yibii akuu lɛ tsiimɔ tsɔɔ bo fɔ enyiɛ obaaná tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Usually yes, because heavier bunches tend to have fully developed, oily fruit flesh. However, if the weight comes from thick inner shells or water rather than oily flesh, the oil yield might still be low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ aduawai ni kpɛɔ ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Shi, kɛji akɛ muji lɛ jɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe loo ni kpɛɔ lɛ, ekolɛ Mu ni ajieɔ lɛ baafee bibioo lolo.

english: Why should I filter or screen my harvested palm fruits before putting them into the oil press?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ mli loo makwɛ mli dani mikɛwo mu tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Screening removes dirt, stones, empty fruit stalks, and debris. This prevents your oil extraction equipment from getting damaged and ensures you extract clean oil without wasted energy.
ga: Screening jieɔ muji, tɛi, aduawai tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛ jwɛi. Enɛ baaha nibii ni okɛjieɔ mu lɛ akafite. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ mu ni he tse ni ofiteee hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell when my palm fruit bunches are mature enough to give the best oil yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-palm yibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ mu ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ baawo?

english: A bunch is ready when its fruits turn bright reddish-orange and a few loose fruits naturally detach and fall to the ground when you gently test the bunch.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ efee klalo beni eyibii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse lɛ. kɛ aduawai ni etse amɛhe lɛ Fioo komɛi baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ beni okaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli blɛoo lɛ okwɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why does harvesting palm fruit bunches too early reduce my final oil quantity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei yibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa minaagbee fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Unripe palm fruits have hard flesh that has not yet accumulated oil. Harvesting early means you end up with low oil recovery, even if the bunch itself looks large.
ga: Palm yibii ni ahoo lɛ yɛ loo ni wa ni ebuaaa fɔ naa lolo. Kɛ́ okpa mra lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaaná mu fioo ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni da po.

english: Does separating small or damaged palm fruits from the healthy ones help my oil production?
ga: Ani ŋmei yibii bibii loo ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha mu ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, sorting out damaged or rotten fruits improves the overall quality and taste of your oil, and prevents bad fats from lowering the market value of your entire oil batch.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni efite loo ni egbo lɛ mligbalamɔ baaha ofɔ lɛ fɛɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ. ni otsi muji fɔji lɛ anaa koni ekaha o-batch muu lɛ fɛɛ jara ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive harsh direct sun. Tall shade trees or fast-growing plantains protect the young cocoa from intense sun heat and help retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits can grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering during hot spells helps the flowers stay healthy and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants look fresh in the morning but wilt down completely during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ehee leebi shi egboɔ kwraa yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: This happens when the plant loses water through its leaves faster than its roots can draw moisture from dry soil. If the soil is wet and it still wilts, it may be caused by soil-borne germs that block the plant's internal water transport.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ shwie nu kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi egbɔjɔ lolo Ekolɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass or decomposed leaves around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛbɔleɔ he Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It prevents the hot sun from drying out the ground, keeps roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and rots into rich plant food.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Tsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Tsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni amɛkafite ni amɛfee tsei aniyenii

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground when heavy rain stays on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, it starves the roots of air and allows rot fungus to multiply and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni amɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my maize plant and eat holes in them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by moths. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant because the tender new leaves are soft and easy to eat.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small bunches when I leave many young stems growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ashɛrɛ tsei bibii ashwie lɛ Akɛ babaoo bɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one mother plant, they all fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only the strongest ones, giving the main tree enough food to grow a large bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, niji ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni etsɔ kuu agbo.

english: Why is it necessary for me to stake my yam vines on tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso nine ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for building big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Okɛwo la mli ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I harvest my vegetables early in the morning instead of in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa mi-aduawai lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Early in the morning, plant tissues are fully charged with water absorbed overnight. Harvesting before the sun gets hot keeps the produce fresh and crisp, stopping it from wilting quickly on the way to the market.
ga: Yɛ leebi lɛ, nu shwieɔ tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli kwraa nyɔɔŋ kome. Kɛ́ okpa nikpamɔ dani hulu lɛ tso lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ afee ehee ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my mango trees close together so I can fit more trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mango tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When mango trees are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each tree enough room to spread its roots and branches, which leads to healthier trees and a bigger harvest overall.
ga: Kɛji adu mango ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from around the base of my young fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients away from your young fruit trees. Keeping the ground clean around the trunk ensures the tree gets all the food it needs and prevents pests from hiding nearby.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni he tse yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ, ni ehaaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akatee he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How often should I water my newly planted mango seedlings during the dry season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ afɔ mango dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Young mango seedlings need watering two to three times a week during the dry season because their roots are still near the surface. Once their roots grow deep into the ground after a couple of years, they can withstand dry weather much better.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ mango tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lolo. Beni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young fruit trees turning brown and burnt at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young fruit tree leaves turn brown from harsh sun exposure or a lack of moisture in the soil. Giving young trees partial shade and keeping the soil moist protects delicate leaves from scorching during intense heat.
ga: Tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ feɔ asarasu kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ akashã yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my mango trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mango tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra or overcrowded branches, known as pruning, allows light and air to pass through the center of the tree. This stops moisture from trapping fungal diseases and encourages the tree to grow bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ afolɔmɔ. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ akamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my mango trees so they grow well?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ okɛ tsofa awo omango tso lɛ mli koni ekwɛ koni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the beginning of the rainy season when the ground is moist, and right before the tree flowers. Moist soil helps the roots absorb the nutrients quickly to build strong flowers and fruits.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Ni dani tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ niyenii mli nibii oya koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my mango trees dropping their flowers before any fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden water stress or when tiny insects like thrips attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering and controlling pests helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: What causes black sticky spots on my mango leaves and how does it affect my trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni shwieɔ mango baai anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te enáa mango tso lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Black sticky spots are caused by sap-sucking insects that leave behind a sugary fluid where black mold grows. This mold blocks sunlight from reaching the leaves, which weakens the tree and reduces the amount of fruit it can produce.
ga: Kplukai ni nuɔ nu ni shwiɔ nu ni mli edɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibii ni abaanyɛ awo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some farmers cover their growing mangoes with paper bags while they are still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ woji kotokui haa amɛ mango lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Covering growing fruits with paper bags shields them from fruit flies, birds, and harsh sunlight. It keeps the fruit skin smooth and clean, helping you sell high-quality fruit at a better price.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ wolo kotoku ha aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ aduawai ahe ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ anɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe atse. Ye obua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: How can I stop my harvested mangoes from getting soft and rotting so quickly after picking?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa mango ni akpa lɛ koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite oya beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mangoes rot quickly if they are bruised during picking or left sitting in hot sunlight. Harvesting fruits carefully with a small piece of stem attached and keeping them in a cool, shaded place preserves their freshness much longer.
ga: Mango baafite oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ loo ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oootse aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tso bibioo ko ekpɛtɛ he ni okɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living shade and holds soil moisture during the young trees' first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ tsei bibii lɛ aklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen, a key food it needs to build leaf strength. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plants helps bring back their dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛma baai lɛ ahewalɛ nɔ Ni akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing yellow patches all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects and infected stem cuttings. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and removing infected plants early prevents the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ akɛ nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ Adumɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dust inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides in the funnel of the plant and eats young leaves. Inspecting your field regularly and applying recommended pest treatments early stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ daa ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ awo mli mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni onibii akafite.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato flowers keep falling off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying compost helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni enyɛ ewo yibii.

english: How can I keep the soil in my vegetable beds from drying out so fast under the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, straw, or clear leaf litter—a practice called mulching—traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly.
ga: He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni oooha Okɛ jwɛi, jwɛi, loo baai ni mli tse ni afo lɛ aha onibii ahe—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ni haa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ato he lɛ? Sweet potato wain tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach full sunlight, which the leaves use to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground where they could rot or get exposed to soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulutsoo be fɛɛ. Akɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akatara hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi loo helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spreading chemical fertilizer on completely dry soil during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so the roots can drink it in. Placing fertilizer on hot, dry ground without water can burn the crop's roots and waste your money since the plant cannot digest it.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni edɔ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpea or groundnuts on land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the earth, but leguminous plants like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally renewing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni ekɛfee hei heei kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to come up when I bury them deep down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth, air, and a small amount of moisture close to the surface to break open and push upwards. Planting them too deep buries them where they run out of energy before the shoot can reach sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia hulutsoo, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛgbele amɛhe ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehi he ko ni ehewalɛ baaho dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves lose water faster than their young roots can absorb it from the soil. Planting shade trees or plantains around them creates a protected environment that keeps the air moist and prevents leaf burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ehaa shihilɛ ni abuɔ he lɛ baa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my plantain stems fall over so easily when a strong rain wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, and if you allow too many suckers to grow around one mother plant, they compete for root space and loosen the soil anchor. Trimming away extra suckers leaves fewer plants to share the root base, making the main stem much stronger against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ni kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, tso ni ji nyɛ kome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ akafee nɔ ni afɔɔ namɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɔ etswaa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize turn yellow from the center tips outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naa kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its oldest lower leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baa ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni ekɛye baa heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my maize crop get full of chewed leaves and ragged holes inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ eyi kɛ baai ni atsɔ mli kɛ bu ni etse yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide deep inside the soft central leaves where rain and predators cannot reach them. They feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold, leaving holes as the leaves grow outward.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. ni nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. Shi bu ko kɛji baai lɛ dara kɛtee kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil instead of shooting up fresh green leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?
