english: Cassava stem cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, taken from weak or dry stems, or planted in waterlogged soil. The small growth buds must point upward so energy flows naturally into roots and shoots rather than trapping moisture inside the stem wood.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ shishi tsei ni afo lɛ baagbo kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Okɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔjɔ loo egbi lɛ amli. Aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni hewalɛ atsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛbote shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeemɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay very small if I do not stake the vines off the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii nɛkɛ kɛji mikɛ wain tso lɛ etswaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows the underground tuber. When vines lie flat on the ground, leaves overlap, get shaded by weeds, and become prone to fungal diseases, leaving the plant with too little energy to build big tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baatsɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni haa hulutsoo yɛ. ni amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why are my green tomatoes getting black, soft patches on their bottoms before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil while building fruit. Irregular watering causes the fruit tissue at the bottom to collapse and turn black because calcium only moves through the plant with a steady stream of water.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haa aduawai lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni hoɔ daa lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni calcium tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plant before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme stress from severe heat, dry soil, or excessive shade. Dropping flowers is the plant's defense mechanism to save energy and survive rather than trying to feed new fruit during hard conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo ni fa fe nine mli lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ji tso hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ aduawai heei aha niyenii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out and crack open so fast when I scrape all weeds away down to the bare dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya beni mifoɔ jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ lɛ eshwɛɔ mi lɛ?

english: Bare dirt is exposed directly to hot sunlight and wind, which bakes the surface and pulls moisture out of the ground very quickly. Leaving dead grass, dry leaves, or crop residues as a cover acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool and locks water in.
ga: Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashɛ muji ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ he. Enɛ baaha ŋwɛi lɛ ashã oya ni ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egboi, baai ni egboi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why does mixing dry cow manure into the ground help my crops stay green longer during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil, holding onto rainwater much longer than plain dirt can. It slowly releases both trapped moisture and essential plant nutrients directly to the roots, keeping crops fed and hydrated during dry periods.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe muji folo, ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli kɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain bunches become extremely heavy as they mature. Because the plant's trunk is soft and not made of hard wood, the top-heavy plantain tree easily gets pulled down by gravity or blown over by wind if it isn't supported with a wooden pole.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ tsii waa kɛji amɛdara kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni akɛ tso ni wa fee. Ewaaa akɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa tsei ni amɛyiteŋ tsii lɛ kɛyaa shi loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ kɛyaa kɛji akɛ tsei ni akɛfee ŋtayaai efiii amɛsɛɛ.

english: When is the right time to put a support pole under my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni fiɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ awo shi?

english: You should place a support pole under your plantain tree as soon as the fruit bunch begins to form and grow heavy, before strong winds or the sheer weight of the fruit cause the stem to bend or snap.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso ko ni fiɔ sɛɛ awo plantain tso lɛ shishi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛfee ni amɛfee tsiimɔ pɛ. Dani kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo tso lɛ yibii lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ atsɔ loo efo.

english: What kind of pole should I use to hold up my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛɛ tso esa akɛ mikɛfi midumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Use strong wooden poles or thick bamboo sticks that have a 'Y' shape or fork at the top. The fork holds the neck of the heavy plantain stem securely without cutting into the plant.
ga: Kɛ tso ni wa loo ŋmei tso ni mli wa ni ‘Y’ su loo fɔk yɔɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Fɔk lɛ mɔ̃ɔ plantain tso ni tsii lɛ kuɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efooo tso lɛ mli.

english: Where exactly should I position the support pole on a plantain plant?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ sɛɛfimɔ tso lɛ ama dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ?

english: Place the top fork of the pole firmly under the upper stem right where the heavy bunch hangs, and sink the bottom end deep into the soil on the side the plant is leaning toward so it pushes back against the weight.
ga: Okɛ tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ awo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋta ni tsii lɛ ŋmɛɔ lɛ. ni okɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ afuu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tso lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi lɛ sɛɛ kɛshi etsitsinɔnii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my plantain farm from being destroyed by strong winds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafite lɛ?

english: You can protect your plantain farm by propping up heavy fruiting plants with sturdy poles and by planting tall windbreak trees along the edges of your farm to reduce the force of strong winds.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii ni tsii ni okɛ tsei ni wa baadamɔ shi lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ tsei kakadaji ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa lɛ ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ hewalɛ aba shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does heavy wind affect the yield of my plantain crop?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ saa mi plantain lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Strong wind tears plantain leaves, which reduces the plant's ability to make food, and it can knock down trees carrying immature fruits, causing you to lose the entire harvest before it is ready.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbálaa plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei ni amɛyibii ekwɛko lolo lɛ agbee shi. Enɛ haa onibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani efeɔ klalo.

english: How can I tell if a plantain plant is in danger of falling over soon?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi plantains lɛ baagbee shi etsɛŋ?

english: Look for signs like the trunk leaning sharply to one side, cracks appearing along the stem, or roots lifting out of the soil around the base under the heavy weight of the fruit.
ga: Taomɔ okadii tamɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsi ehe waa kɛtee he kome. Gbɛjegbɛi je kpo yɛ tsɔne lɛ tsɔne lɛ he. aloo shishifãi ni woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ mli yɛ aduawai lɛ tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ shishi.

english: Why are plantain stems so soft compared to other trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo waa kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Plantain trees are not true woody trees; their trunks are made of tightly wrapped leaf sheaths filled with water. This soft structure makes them flexible, but it also means they need extra support when carrying heavy bunches.
ga: Plantains jeee anɔkwa tsei ni yeɔ ŋmɔŋ daa. Akɛ baai ni akɛ nu ewo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ fee tso lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ haa enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe. Shi etsɔɔ hu akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko he miihia amɛ kɛ́ amɛtere jatsui ni tsii.

english: What makes plantain fruit bunches get so heavy as they grow?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains lɛ tsiimɔ waa kɛ́ amɛdara?

english: As plantain fruits develop, they fill up with large amounts of starch and water stored by the leaves. This natural filling process makes the bunch very heavy compared to the soft trunk supporting it.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ wo yibii lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nu babaoo ni ato yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ woɔ amɛmli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli nɛɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Do I need to put a support pole under every single plantain tree on my farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ awo dumɔwui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi?

english: No, you only need to support the trees that are currently bearing heavy fruit bunches, especially those growing in open areas where strong winds blow directly across your field.
ga: Dabi, ehe miihia ni ofi tso ko ni miiwo aduawai ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ kɛkɛ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛha tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant my yams on raised soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the topsoil so young yam tubers can expand downward smoothly without hitting hard earth. It also keeps rainwater from pooling around the tubers and causing them to rot.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii bibii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ. Agbɛnɛ hu, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ bɔɔ bulb lɛ he ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: Why do some seed yams fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams fail to sprout if they were bruised during cutting, infected with rot fungi before planting, or buried in dry soil without enough moisture to activate their dormant growth buds.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni afoɔ lɛ. Akɛ fungal rot hela lɛ emɔ lɛ dani adu loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Yam vines naturally reach upward to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which is sent underground to build large, healthy tubers instead of trailing on damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee bulbs agboi ni mli wa Moŋ lɛ, efoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to be careful when tying yam vines to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines carry water and essential nutrients between the roots and leaves. Tying them too tightly or snapping the stems cuts off this food flow, causing the vine to wither and stopping tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei hiɛɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ ofĩ lɛ waa tsɔ loo ofo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi niyenii lɛ naa koni ekaho. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa bulbs lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my yams turn out small or out of shape in heavy clay or waterlogged land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ji bibii loo amɛhe esaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, well-drained soil to expand naturally underground. Heavy clay compresses the growing tubers into distorted shapes, while excess water starves the roots of air and rots the crop.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ miimɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ amli ni efee nɔ ni efite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant yams on the exact same piece of land two years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams heavily consume specific nutrients from the soil during a growing season. Replanting in the same spot exhausts these nutrients and leaves behind pests and soil diseases that will attack the new crop.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ afite, ni ebaashi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baatutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Why does my yam plant grow long vines and leafy leaves before any tubers form underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji kɛ baai dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: The yam plant uses its early growth stage to build a strong leafy canopy. Once the leaves are fully developed, they capture sunlight to manufacture energy, which is then redirected downward to swell and build the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ mra be mli dalɛ be tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni baai ni mli wa yɔɔ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ dara kwraa Baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Kɛkɛ lɛ, etsɔɔ gbɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shi koni efuu ni efee yitso.

english: How do I know that my yams under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: When yams reach full maturity, the vines and leaves above ground naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up. This signals that the plant has finished feeding the tuber and it is safe to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Wein tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakpa shweremɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eshishifãi lɛ niyenii naa ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam plants turning yellow and getting dark spots before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Dark spots and early yellowing are usually caused by fungal leaf diseases like anthracnose. These diseases destroy leaf tissue, preventing the plant from making food and reducing the final harvest size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ mra be mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Helai nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii ni ehaa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting or getting soft inside the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ loo miifee blɛoo yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yams remain alive after harvest and react to heat and humidity. High temperatures or moisture in storage trick the tuber into thinking it is time to grow again, causing it to use up its stored food energy to produce new shoots.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ hiɔ shi lolo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Dɔlɛ ni mli wa loo hulutsoo ni yɔɔ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ lakaa bulb lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ akɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ atsu nii koni akɛfee ŋmeii heei.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow, curling up, and making the plants stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ miifee bibioo waa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to stop it and keep your harvest strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi etsɔɔ mli lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them with little caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ani okɛ ohe ewo mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars eat the growing leaves of the crop, but applying the recommended spray early in the morning or late in the evening when they come out to feed will protect your maize.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe baai. Shi kɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni amɛje kpo kɛmiitao niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmã lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that blocks water from moving up inside the plant stem. Rotating your farm with crops like maize or cassava helps starve the bacteria so future tomato crops stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake oŋmɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa muawai koni wɔsɛɛ tomato tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough space and resources to produce a much bigger yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Naagbee lɛ, amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: It is best to wait until the rain wets the soil down to the depth of your hand. Planting after just one short rainfall can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ oniji amli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ kuku ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ ba.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans on the same land with their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take natural food from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This works as a free fertilizer that helps nearby maize grow stronger and greener.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: This yellowing is a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make healthy green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they don't get enough shade, moisture, or soil nutrients, or if tiny pollinating insects aren't present. Keeping moderate shade trees like plantains and maintaining good soil helps the flowers set into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ lɛ, kɛ́ aha tsei tamɔ plantains lɛ hulutsoo be ni sa, ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so fast after I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam rot is usually caused by fungi entering through small cuts made during harvesting, or from heat and dampness in the barn. Storing only uninjured yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn stops the rot from starting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni tsɔɔ ŋmei bibioo ko mli ni eboteɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli loo kɛjɛ latsaa kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii ni pilaaa pɛ ato ŋmɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaje shishi amɛgboi.

english: Why should I clear away old crop remains and rotten fruits after harvest instead of leaving them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ ni eshwɛ kɛ aduawai ni egboi lɛ ashwie beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving old plant remains on the field gives pests and plant diseases a place to hide and multiply over the dry season. Clearing them cleans the field so your next crop starts in a safe environment.
ga: Tso momo ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai naa he ko ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mli ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Look at the color change on the skin. Green cocoa pods turn bright yellow when ripe, and reddish pods turn orange-yellow. Ripe pods also make a hollow sound when you tap them lightly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ hewolo nɔ su mli lɛ. Kookoo tsei eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii tsuru lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu feɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ otswa amɛ fioo.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather and thick shade. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and clearing affected pods helps stop it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji krokomɛi ni abaakpa koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sun. Planting shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside cocoa protects the young seedlings until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain loo cassava yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my cassava so it boils well for soup?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei kɛha shwiili kpakpa?

english: Most local cassava varieties are mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. Harvesting too early leaves you with tiny tubers, while waiting too long makes the roots woody and hard to cook.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ŋmeii bibii ahi ohe. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tso ni ehoomɔ wa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is missing nitrogen from the soil. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the crops are young will bring back the green color and help form healthy ears.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ, ebaaha eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni toi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster than my crops after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal food and water from the soil before your main crops can reach it. You must clear all weeds from around your plants before applying fertilizer so your crops get all the food.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aba. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ otso lɛ mli nu lɛ kwraa dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii lɛ fɛɛ

english: Is it safe to spray chemical medicine on food crops like maize that I harvest to make kenkey?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ niyenii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa koni mikɛfee Kenkey gbee lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must respect the waiting period written on the chemical label before harvesting. Always wash harvested food thoroughly with clean water to make sure no chemical residue remains.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ obu mɛmɔ be ni aŋma yɛ tsofa lɛ he wolo lɛ nɔ dani okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ nu ni mli tse afɔ niyenii ni akpa lɛ he jogbaŋŋ koni tsofa ko akashwɛ yɛ mli.

english: Why do I feel weak or dizzy after spraying farm chemicals on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minuɔ he akɛ migbɔjɔ loo mihe feɔ mi shoo beni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai eshwie mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical vapors enter your body through your skin, eyes, or breathing when you spray without protection. Always wear protective clothing like boots, long sleeves, gloves, and a nose mask during spraying.
ga: Tsofai amli lasu boteɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ ohewolo, ohiŋmɛii, loo omumɔ mli kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ ni okɛbuuu ohe. Wo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ atadei, atadei ni hiɛ nine kakadaŋŋ agboi, glɔvs, kɛ hiɛ he mask be fɛɛ be beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Will putting more chemical than recommended into my spraying machine kill crop pests faster?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛfataa tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ baagbe kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ oya?

english: No, using too much chemical can burn and damage your crops instead of protecting them. Following the exact mixing measurements on the bottle label works best and saves you money.
ga: Dabi, tsofai babaoo ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite onibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobu amɛhe lɛ, nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ahe susumɔi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha okɛ shika akafite.

english: How do small insect pests destroy my crop leaves without me seeing them early?
ga: tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpãtã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai oya ni minaaa amɛ?

english: Many pests hide on the undersides of leaves or inside stems where direct sunlight cannot reach them. Regularly inspecting underneath crop leaves helps you catch and treat insect infestations early.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi loo tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shɛɛɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra ni otsa amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves, and when there is not enough, the plant pulls it from older leaves to feed the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ anɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer in two stages: first, about two weeks after sprouting when the roots are ready to feed, and second, when the plants reach knee height to support strong stem and cob formation.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo kɛha niyenii. kɛ gbɛ ni ji enyɔ lɛ Beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛkuɛ he koni amɛfi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ asɛɛ

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworm caterpillars are destroying my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ miifite mi-abele lɛ?

english: Look closely into the central funnel of the maize leaves. If you see ragged holes, caterpillar droppings that look like wet sawdust, and small striped worms feeding inside, your farm has Fall Armyworm.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa baa ko teŋgbɛ faa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji ona buji ni etse, ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shi yɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ Fall Armyworm.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and growing tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. As they feed on leaf juice, they spread viruses and cause the leaves to wrinkle and stunt fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Be ni amɛyeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Excess rain fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, drowning the cassava roots. Without air, soil fungi grow quickly and attack the roots, causing them to rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems that cannot pull water fast enough. Strong sunlight burns their foliage and dries up the surrounding topsoil, causing the plant to wither.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã ebaai lɛ ni ebaaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ ni egboɔ.

english: Yam plants store energy in tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, maximizing foliage growth and preventing soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ bulbs lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ baai ni nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ lɛ anɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ daa babaoo. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Plantain suckers should be spaced about 3 meters apart so their broad leaves do not block sunlight from each other and their roots do not compete for soil food and moisture.
ga: Esa akɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 bɔni afee ni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ akatsi hulu la lɛ naa ni shishifãi lɛ akatswa niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like boron, causing the blossom to dry up instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ boron ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I cover the base of my garden plants with dried grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ aha abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants (mulching) keeps the roots cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, keeps weeds from growing, and decomposes over time to feed the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nutrients to build strong leaves, so when nitrogen runs out, the plant pulls it from the older leaves to feed the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii nibii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh sunlight and heat. They require shade trees or temporary nurse crops like plantains to protect their leaves from sunburn and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛbii anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil better for planting maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they work with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, seedlings compete heavily for sunlight and soil nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to reach light, making stems thin, weak, and prone to falling over.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛyaa oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: When soil becomes waterlogged from heavy rain, standing water replaces air in the soil. Without oxygen, cassava roots suffocate and become vulnerable to fungal infections that cause root rot.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baaná amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms instead of forming fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai najiaŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress or sudden dry conditions. The heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ ahe. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my yam crop produce larger tubers when I use wooden stakes to lift the vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ naa tubers wuji beni mikɛ tso tso tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach sunlight. Staking spreads the leaves out so they catch more light to make energy for tuber growth, while keeping leaves off the wet ground prevents disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni la babaoo abote mli ni ekɛ hewalɛ aha bulb lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ ahe koni helai akamɔ bo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a viral disease spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less harvest even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They quickly absorb the fertilizer and water from the soil before your crops can reach them, starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller fruit bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii beni mikɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers forces the main plantain tree to share its nutrients and water. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, directing maximum energy into producing a large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ aha. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha hewalɛ babaoo aba ni akɛfee tso lɛ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and dying when I clear all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out their roots. Traditional practice of leaving select forest trees creates a cool canopy that protects young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Kusum nifeemɔ ni ji tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ kooi ni ahala mli lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ.

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need to survive their early months.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though I applied chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks organic matter to hold nutrients. Without compost or old crop remains mixed into the dirt, heavy rain washes chemical fertilizer away before the maize roots can feed on it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ahi mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii momo ni akɛfutu mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dani ŋmɔ mli shishifãi yeɔ amɛ.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mikɛ cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa du yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize helps the soil naturally. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves harvest yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cowpeas ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my soil drying out so quickly now compared to when we used to leave crop stalks on the ground after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto be mli ni wɔshiɔ tsei ashishifãi yɛ wɔsɛɛ beni wɔkpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving old plant stalks on the soil acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sunlight from baking the ground, keeps moisture trapped in the soil, and helps beneficial earthworms break down organic food for your next crops.
ga: Tsoi momo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he Etsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashã shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni amɛgbalaa niyenii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land without giving it a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull the same nutrients out of the earth every season. Without resting the land or rotating crops, the soil becomes exhausted and loses its natural power to support healthy crop growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔɔɔ loo otsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do insects return in bigger numbers after I spray my farm with strong chemical pest killers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi akuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa babaoo beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ efɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays often kill both the destructive pests and the helpful insects that natural eat them. When the good insects are gone, surviving pests reproduce much faster without natural predators to stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ fɛɛ. Beni kooloi kpakpai lɛ etee lɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ wala lɛ fɔɔ oya kwraa ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields for only one planting. The seeds produced from that harvest lose their special traits, leading to uneven growth, smaller cobs, and weaker plants in the second season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shikome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ baafite amɛsui lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ŋmeii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss. This is a natural survival defense that keeps the root tubers alive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala hebuu ni haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by hot, dry days that scorch the damp ground. The seeds absorb initial moisture to start growing, but get trapped in hot, wet soil and rot before they can burst through the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni shãa hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa nu ni yɔɔ shishijee lɛ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ zu nɛ mi edɔ nɛ e ngɛ nu ɔ mi, nɛ e puɛɔ loko e nyɛɔ nɛ e sɛɔ zugba a mi.

english: How much maize am I supposed to harvest from my one hectare of land if my farm does well?
ga: Abele enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa kɛjɛ hectare kome mli kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Under basic farming methods in Ghana, farmers typically get around 2.2 metric tons per hectare, but using improved seeds, fertilizer, and good farm management can significantly increase that harvest.
ga: Yɛ okwaayeli gbɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ shishi lɛ, okwaafoi lɛ naa aaafee mɛtrik tɔn 2.2 yɛ hectare kome mli. Shi dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why is my maize field yielding very low harvest even though I work hard on the land every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ faaa nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa gbi?

english: Low harvests usually happen when the soil is depleted of nutrients or when older seed varieties are planted without fertilizer, limiting crop production to low baseline yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni etsɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi kɛtee shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ anɔ.

english: Will my maize output improve right away if I start using improved seed varieties?
ga: Ani mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mibɔi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, improved seed varieties are bred specifically to resist pests, utilize soil nutrients better, and produce larger ears, helping you surpass the low yields of standard seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui henɔi ni atsake amɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni afee toi wuji Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ofeɔ nɔ ni fe dumɔwui ni baa shi lɛ ayibii.

english: What is this 'Planting for Food and Jobs' program I keep hearing about in my village?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘niyenii kɛ nitsumɔi’ nitsumɔi ni minu he yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Planting for Food and Jobs is a government initiative that helps smallholder farmers get subsidized high-yielding seeds, fertilizers, and agricultural guidance to boost overall crop production.
ga: Okwaayeli kɛha Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi ji nɔyeli nifeemɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii ni amɛnáa yelikɛbuamɔ kɛha dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ okwaayeli he ŋaawoi koni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How did government programs help increase total maize production across Ghana in recent years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi eye ebua ni ŋmãa ni ajieɔ lɛ fɛɛ etee hiɛ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afii nɛɛ amli?

english: By distributing certified seeds and subsidized fertilizers to thousands of farmers at once, these programs improved soil productivity and enabled fields across the country to produce much higher yields than before.
ga: Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa lɛ ni ajaa ahaa okwaafoi akpei abɔ shikome lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ nitsumɔi nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do I need a government permit if I want to sell my harvested maize in a neighboring country?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná nɔyeli lɛ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo kɛji miitao mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: The government controls crop exports through permits to make sure enough grain stays inside Ghana so local families have food before any surplus crop leaves the country.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ kudɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ kɛtsɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ woji anɔ koni ekwɛ akɛ ŋmaa ni fa bɔ ni sa eshwɛ yɛ Ghana. Enɛ ji koni wekui ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ aná niyenii dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ashi maŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I freely load my maize onto a truck and take it across the border whenever prices are higher over there?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ awo lɔle mli yɛ heyeli mli ni mikɛfo husu lɛ be fɛɛ be ni jara lɛ baaya ŋwɛi?

english: No, you cannot transport food crops across the border without an export permit, because the ministry checks national grain supply levels first to prevent food shortages at home.
ga: Dabi, onyɛɛɛ okɛ niyenii ni adu lɛ aya husu lɛ naa kɛji obɛ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nitsumɔhe lɛ baakwɛ bɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ fa ha klɛŋklɛŋ koni niyenii akashɛ shia.

english: When is the government likely to allow farmers to export maize to foreign markets?
ga: Mɛɛ be nɔyeli lɛ baaŋmɛ okwaafoi gbɛ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa aya maŋsɛɛ jarayeli hei?

english: Export permits are usually granted only when domestic harvests are bumper and there is clear proof that there is plenty of surplus maize available in Ghanaian markets.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ahaa gbɛŋmɛɛ woji ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ pɛ kɛji akɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ tsi enaa ni odaseyeli ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni fa fe nine yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why does maize suddenly become scarce and expensive in Ghanaian local markets in some years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa namɔ wa ni ejara wa waa yɛ Ghana maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei yɛ afii komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Grain shortages occur when bad weather, rainfall delays, or pest outbreaks reduce total harvests, causing local supply to drop before the next harvest season comes.
ga: Ŋmaa ni faaa lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ehiii. nugbɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni haa nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ baa shi Enɛ haa nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi dani ŋmaakpamɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: What happens to food security in our towns when there is a critical drop in national maize production?
ga: Mɛni baaba niyenii ni yɔɔ wɔ maji lɛ amli lɛ nɔ? Mɛɛ be maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ ba shi kwraa?

english: When overall production falls critically low, local prices rise quickly, making it difficult for consumers to afford basic food staples, which is why national crop monitoring is critical.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi waa lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli jara baaya ŋwɛi oya. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ akɛ amɛbaahe niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni maŋ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is a key nutrient in the soil needed for leaves to stay green and healthy. It can also happen if heavy rains wash nutrients away or if water sits around the roots for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni baa lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers always tell me to plant beans or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the ground. Legume crops like beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which puts nutrients back into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo, titri lɛ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally make thousands of flowers, but only a tiny fraction are visited by very small insects that pollinate them. Flowers that are not pollinated naturally drop off, and the tree will also shed extra flowers if it is stressed by drought or lack of soil food.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji mɛi ni kooloi ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ saraa. Fɔfɔi ni jeee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ baagbee shi. Ni tso lɛ hu baawo fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, the tubers stop growing useful starch and continue taking in water from wet ground. Too much moisture in mature roots creates a favorable condition for soil fungi and bacteria to enter and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ ŋmei lɛ baakpa ŋmei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ shweremɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ejie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ shishifãi ni eda lɛ amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abote mli ni ekɛ tuber rot baa.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually a reaction to tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or from a plant virus carried by insects. It can also happen when plants suffer from extreme heat and lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ji kooloi ni kɛ kooloi baa lɛ amli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit. It usually happens when watering is inconsistent, such as long dry spells followed by heavy rains, which prevents the plant from pulling calcium from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough resources to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by hot, dry weather before the main rainy period fully begins. Sowing too early risks burning your young seedlings in the dry soil if the rain disappears for several weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa. Dumɔwui ni ooodu mra tsɔ lɛ kɛ oshara baaha odumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that have adapted to quickly swallow water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before domestic crops can. If you do not remove weeds early, they will steal the fertilizer and water meant for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛmi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani shia tsei lɛ baanyɛ. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, Amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛha onibii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my young crops with dry grass or husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Mi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jwɛi loo ŋmeii?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or husks, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the hot sun. It stops water from evaporating quickly out of the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am putting cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔji yɛ shikpɔŋ Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava stems with the small leaf buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant the stem upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow straight up and root growth will be weak and slow.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tso lɛ shishi lɛ Ewa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ, ni shishifãi lɛ hu daa blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil so the tubers can expand into large shapes. Creating mounds loosens hard soil, improves water drainage so the tubers do not rot, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni ooofee lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Koni yitso lɛ akafite Ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help bring back the deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any small fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or having too much leafy growth from excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo baa ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ mli baa lɛ yɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying the plants with a natural neem oil solution or insecticidal soap gets rid of these insects so fresh leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small cobs when I plant the seeds close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each maize plant enough space allows its roots and leaves to get the food needed to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu Kɛ́ aha ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the dirt. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching your soil for the next farming season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha okwaayeli be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal sickness that spreads quickly in damp, dark environments. Pruning overcrowded cocoa branches to let in sunlight and wind helps dry out the trees and stops the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. Kookoo niji ni mli eyi obɔ fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii agbɛ ashwã.

english: It is best to water early in the morning. If you water in the hot afternoon, much of the moisture evaporates into the air before the roots can drink it, wasting water and leaving the plants thirsty.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Fɛ̃i babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ haa nu fiteɔ ni ehaa kumai yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. This can happen if the soil lacks organic matter or if heavy rains have washed the nutrients deep down beyond the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni mli kwɔ fe shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot sun even when the ground feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During extreme heat, tomato leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil. If the soil is too wet, the roots can also get suffocated and stop taking up water properly.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing the central funnels of my young corn plants to look ragged with ragged holes and small black drops inside?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli ŋmeii ni etse kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's funnel. They hide in the leaves during the day and chew on the young growing leaf tissue, leaving behind ragged holes and droppings.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni miida lɛ. Amɛshiɔ bu kɛ ŋmeii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as lack of water during dry periods, poor soil nutrition, or attacks by tiny sap-sucking insects like capsids. Proper shade and soil moisture help the tree hold its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ nu ni bɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutuamɔ. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when we get too much rain late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave standing water in the farm, oxygen cannot reach the tubers, allowing soft rot fungi to attack and rot the roots underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ yitso lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them handle the heat?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ latsaa lɛ naa?

english: Spreading dry grass creates mulch, which acts like a blanket over the dirt. It blocks sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps the soil cool, and slows down water evaporation so plant roots stay moist longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi lɛ fɔ shi lɛ, ehaa sũ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la naa ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo Koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant beans or cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have tiny root nodes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. This naturally feeds the soil and helps neighboring maize crops grow stronger without using as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo awo mli tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over before the fruit is ripe for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tso lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy bunches of fruit, especially during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden or bamboo poles keeps the plant balanced until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early when my crop plants are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even if weeds look smaller than your crops, their roots are aggressively stealing water, fertilizers, and root space underneath the soil. Clearing them early removes this subterranean competition so your crops get full nourishment.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji bibii fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po lɛ, Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ yiwalɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaajie teemɔŋ akaŋshii kɛya. No hewɔ lɛ, onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow better tubers when I build tall wooden stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mima tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants make energy through their leaves exposed to sunlight. Staking gets the vines off the wet ground where diseases spread and exposes maximum leaf area to the sun, allowing the plant to pump more energy down into growing a bigger tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei feɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking jieɔ wain tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ, ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak root systems. Direct sunlight burns their foliage and dries the topsoil quickly, which is why they require shade crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa amɛ shade tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant maize on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize repeatedly draws the same key nutrients out of the soil. Planting crops like beans or groundnuts in alternating seasons replaces those lost nutrients naturally, keeping the land healthy for long-term production.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii titri kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ be ni tsakeɔ mli lɛ baaye niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha nitsumɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant cassava and maize together on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested early, while cassava grows slower and stays in the ground longer. Intercropping allows you to maximize soil space and harvest maize early without disturbing the growing cassava tubers.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yaa hiɛ ni okpaa ŋmãa oya ni okɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do weeds around my cassava plants cause the roots to grow small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni bɔle mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from the cassava roots. Clearing weeds ensures the plant can direct all its energy into growing full, heavy tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni tsiimɔ fa babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Pruning allows sunlight and air to move freely through the canopy, which prevents black pod disease and ensures the tree spends its energy developing big, healthy pods rather than unnecessary leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ pod agbo ni mli wa yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops stay green longer during dry weather when I place dead leaves around their bases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, beni mikɛ baai ni egboi fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried plant leaves or grass creates a protective layer called mulch. Mulch traps moisture in the ground, shields root zones from direct heat, and slowly rots into rich plant food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch lɛ baa. Mulch mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ shishifã lɛ he kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa.

english: Why does it take a few years for oil palm trees to start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii fioo komɛi dani oil palm tsei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees focus their first few years on building strong trunk foundations and deep root networks. This structural growth ensures the tree can support heavy fruit bunches continuously for decades.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ anɔ yɛ shishitoo ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ maa nɔ. Nɛkɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ daa lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ewoɔ aduawai ni tsii be fɛɛ be afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices and spreading diseases, which deprives the leaves of nutrients needed to grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm make my vegetables grow better than untreated soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Animal manure enriches the soil with vital organic matter that slowly releases nutrients over time while helping the soil absorb and hold onto water much better.
ga: Koolooi aŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he hiaa ni yaa hiɛ fiofio. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii fiofio Beni be hoɔ lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When planted too close, seedlings must fight each other for limited sunlight, root space, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough resources to produce thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops use to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing tall with lots of big leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni baai lɛ dara shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing leaves towards the sun instead of storing food in their underground roots.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ baai ni amɛtsɔ amɛhe amɛkwɛ hulu lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting them under fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects them from extreme heat and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains shishi lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Extra shoots compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Tsobii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji ni tsii.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass and dead leaves around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwieɔ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egboi amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants, called mulching, shields the ground from hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ mulching ni bɔleɔ Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why are holes appearing in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaves. If they damage the central growing point of the plant, it cannot produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa kɛji amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enyɛŋ ewo toi kpakpai.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or lack of soil food. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy and keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my maize make my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen food out of the air and fix it into the soil. When grown next to maize, they act as a natural fertilizer for your main crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji adu yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa kɛha otsei titrii lɛ.

english: Weeds grow rapidly and steal the water, sunlight, and soil food that your crops need. When crops are forced to compete with weeds, they cannot form full, healthy fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Beni anyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛkɛ jwɛi akaŋ lɛ Nakai tsei lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii loo ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from drought or too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ loo nu babaoo miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When crops lack water, their leaves roll up and wilt to save moisture. When soil has too much water, leaves turn soft and pale yellow, and the roots begin to rot because they cannot breathe.
ga: Kɛ nu bɛ tsei lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any big trees around?
