ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective cover that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during high winds right when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni jwɛi lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the top of the soil rather than going deep. When the plant grows a heavy fruit bunch, it becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden or bamboo pole prevents the roots from pulling out of wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛmli kwɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ aduawai akuu ni tsii Ebaaná ŋwɛi tsiimɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn ears are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil runs low, the plant moves what little it has to the top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie nibii fioo komɛi kɛya baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain causes water to sit in the soil without draining away, it starves the roots of oxygen and allows destructive soil fungi to cause root rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehooo. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akpata amɛ hiɛ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and put long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make the food that grows the big tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows the leaves to catch more light and keeps them away from soil dampness, which causes leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la babaoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. ni ji nɔ ni kɛ baa hela baa lɛ

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems instead of turning into green fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when the ambient heat becomes too high or when they experience water stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant retain its flowers so they can form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji hulutsoo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ tomato lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight like small tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ tsɔnei bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As these pests suck out the plant's juices, they cause the leaves to distort and can also spread harmful plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei amli helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui hu eshwã.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests that feed on that crop a permanent place to live. Alternating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas helps rebuild soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa. Akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: Why do some of the seeds I bury deep in the soil fail to sprout and come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mifuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a limited amount of stored energy to sprout and push through the soil. If buried too deep, the seedling runs out of energy before it reaches the surface to get sunlight, causing it to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛtsɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does leaving tall weeds around my crops reduce the total amount of food I harvest?
ga: ŋmɛɔ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔleɔ he Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that compete directly with your crops for water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal the resources your crops need to develop full, healthy fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, Jwɛi nɛɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii kɛ ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient found in fertilizers or good compost, or that weeds are stealing food from the crop's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai amli. Aloo jwɛi miiju niyenii kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull natural plant food out of the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, acting like a natural fertilizer for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa adebɔɔ mli tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight while their roots establish; without shade trees or plantains nearby, intense sun and heat dry them out and scorch their leaves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwaa lɛ. Shade loo dumɔwui ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ. Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ haa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Why do my crops dry out and wither so fast during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds are dry and suck moisture out of crop leaves quickly, so covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps hold water in the ground.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ shwieɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni oookɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulch) aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of pushing them straight into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle gives roots more space to spread out, resulting in more tubers forming close to the surface, which makes harvesting easier.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, bulb lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. ni haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why do my pepper fruits stay very small even though the plant leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: When pepper plants grow too many dense branches, they spread their food energy too thin, so pinching off extra side shoots allows the plant to focus energy on making bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ dara ni amɛhe tse tsɔ lɛ, Ebaagbɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ lɛ eshwa tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama yibii wuji ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain stalks falling over easily during heavy winds and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain stems fall over easily if small worms called nematodes or stem-boring insects damage the roots underground, weakening the plant's hold on the soil.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo kooloi ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato bushes fall off before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil becomes too dry, or when lack of insect visits prevents flowers from being pollinated.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii bɛ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to be dug up from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellowish and dry up, and when you open a few test pods and see dark spots on the inside shell around the nuts.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele test pods fioo komɛi ni ona ŋmeii diji yɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii ni bɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly after I stack them in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fite oya beni mikɛto ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot fast if they get bruised during digging or if they are piled together without air flowing freely around them to keep them cool and dry.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ amɛ loo akɛto he kome ni kɔɔyɔɔ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Koni eha edɔ ni egbi

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. This happens when the soil is poor, after heavy rain washes away nutrients, or when fertilizer has not been applied in time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehiii. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laajeɔ. aloo be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and twist together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or recommended pest treatments early protects the new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo gbɛi krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ dalɛ hee naa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers without growing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shiɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers and drop many to save energy, but dropping nearly all of them usually means the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or has poor pollination from small insects in the farm.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛteŋ babaoo koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nɔ ni laajeɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efeee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits splitting open while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when their water supply changes suddenly, such as heavy rain after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit fills with water faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Nu yiɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits in the field without draining properly. Excess standing water starves the roots of air and allows soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aye shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die before the yams are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is commonly caused by fungal diseases like leaf spot or root damage from microscopic worms called nematodes. When roots or stems get damaged, the plant cannot transport water, causing the vine to wither early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Kɛji shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ nu aya. Ehaa wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya

english: What is making small holes and leaving dirt inside the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? ni eshiɔ muji yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing center of the corn plant to eat fresh leaves. The dirt left behind is their waste, and treating the center of the plant early helps stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Muji ni ashi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji jwɛi. kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akpa muji dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds stop growing under my cowpea plants after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kpaɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants spread quickly and create a thick cover of big leaves over the soil. This shade blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, preventing buried weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni mli tse ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shade nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haaa jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ anaa la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the soil, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Supporting them with bamboo or wood stakes prevents the weight and wind from pulling them out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii baaha efee nɔ ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ehaaa muji kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ agbala amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my oil palm tree turning brown and drying up first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn brown while top leaves stay green, the oil palm is usually suffering from drought or a lack of potassium in the soil. The tree naturally draws food and water from older lower leaves to keep its new top leaves alive.
ga: Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mu tsei anɔ amanehulu. Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from harsh sun and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa canopy matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava plant grow very tall with many leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing stem and leaf vegetation above ground rather than swelling its storage roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e haa nɛ sisifãhi nɛ a bua a he nya ngɛ sisi ɔ puɛɔ.

english: Why are my green tomatoes dropping off the stems and rotting on the ground before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ dani amɛmiitsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often fall early due to fruit fly pests puncturing the skin to lay eggs or blossom-end rot caused by irregular watering and lack of calcium in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɔɔ hewolo lɛ mli koni amɛwo amɛwui. loo fɔfɔii ashishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller with every new shoot that grows around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii heei baakwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a mother plantain tree, they compete for the same soil nutrients, light, and water. Pruning excess suckers allows the plant to focus its nutrients into producing a larger, healthier fruit bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ni bɔle dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, la, kɛ nu mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ yɛ aduawai akui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look tired and wilted during the afternoon sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etɔ lɛ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. Adding dry grass or mulch around the root base keeps soil moisture from evaporating quickly.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Hay loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekafo oya.

english: Instead of planting after the very first light rain, wait until the ground gets a deep, soaked rain that penetrates hand-deep into the soil so seeds do not dry out and die after germinating.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to feed the root system. Lifting vines off the wet ground also prevents humid soil fungi from damaging leaves and stem tissue.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni efɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ akafite baai kɛ tso lɛ shishi fãji lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested corn get covered in tiny holes and white powder while stored in my shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ powda yɛŋ beni akɛtoɔ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into harvested maize to feed and multiply if the corn is not dried properly before storage. Thorough drying and storing in sealed containers keeps pest infestation low.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛshwere kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Maize crops heavy-feed on soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Legume crops like groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and return it into the soil, restoring farm fertility naturally for future harvests.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni aku sɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔ mli fɔmɔ aba kɛha wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ

english: Why do almost all the small green fruits drop off my mango tree shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mango tsei lɛ anɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree experiences sudden dry spells without soil moisture or when blossom-damaging pests like thrips attack the flowers, forcing the tree to shed excess fruit it cannot support.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi, tamɔ thrips lɛ tutua fɔfɔi, ni no haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops need regular water even after they have already grown tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa eyɛ mli akɛ ekwɛ̃ momo moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops need water throughout their entire life cycle to carry nutrients from the soil into their leaves and fruits. Even after growing tall, continuous water is required for the plant to fully mature and produce healthy yields.
ga: Tsei hia nu yɛ amɛ wala be fɛɛ mli koni amɛ ŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛ baai kɛ amɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ. Beni amɛdara po lɛ, Tsei lɛ hu he miihia nu ni yaa nɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is irrigation, and how can it help my crops during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji nu shwiemɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Irrigation is the practice of supplying water to crops using pipes, pumps, or sprinklers instead of relying only on rain. It ensures your crops get enough water during dry spells so they can keep growing to full maturity.
ga: Nu shwiemɔ ji nifeemɔ ni akɛ paipii, pɔmpii, loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Koni enyɛ eda kwraa

english: Why do my maize plants dry up before making big cobs when the rain stops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra lɛ?

english: Maize requires a steady supply of moisture when forming cobs. If rain stops early, the plant suffers water stress, causing it to stop feeding the cobs and dry up prematurely.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ eefee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra Tsei lɛ baaná nu he haomɔ. Enɛ haa amɛkpaa cob kɛ niyenii ni egbi lɛ yeli mra.

english: Can crops still mature normally during the dry harmattan season in Ghana?
ga: Ani tsei baanyɛ ada lolo bɔ ni sa yɛ harmattan be ni nu egbi yɛ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: During harmattan, dry winds and high temperatures dry out the soil quickly. Crops cannot mature normally during this period unless you provide an artificial water source through irrigation.
ga: Yɛ Harmatta Dry beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa ni naa wa baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Tsei nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli. Ja okɛ nu jɛɛhe ko ni afee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ha kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does giving my crops too much water at once make them mature faster?
ga: Ani kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo ha ŋmɔshi nibii shikome lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: No, flooding crops with excessive water can suffocate their roots and stop them from absorbing nutrients. Crops mature best with a steady, controlled amount of water given consistently over time.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ nu wo onibii amli fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛkaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa, ni akudɔɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: How can a single farmer manage to care for a very large piece of land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafonyo kome pɛ anyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ?

english: Large farms are managed using agricultural machinery such as tractors, boom sprayers, and motorized pumps. These machines allow one person to plant, spray, and water vast areas of land quickly without heavy manual labor.
ga: Akɛ okwaayeli tsɔnei tamɔ trakta kɛ boom sprayer tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔji wuji anɔ. kɛ pɔmpii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii Nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ haa mɔ kome nyɛɔ eduɔ nii oya, ekɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ nu woɔ hei wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ eniji atsu nii waa.

english: How do large farms spread water and fertilizers evenly across many acres?
ga: Te ŋmɔji wuji baanyɛ aja nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli?

english: Large farms use mechanical systems like overhead sprinkler networks, drip lines, or tractor-mounted sprayers. These tools distribute liquids uniformly so every crop receives the exact amount of moisture and nutrients it needs.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji kɛ tsɔnei tamɔ tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ, tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ, loo tsɔnei ni akɛshwieɔ trakta nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nibii nɛɛ jaa nu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some large commercial farms run smoothly even when the owners are not physically working on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji wuji komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛnuŋtsɔmɛi lɛ kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ko kwraa wooo ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Commercial farms rely on automated equipment, clear work schedules, and trained supervisors. Mechanization allows farm operations like irrigation and land spraying to happen automatically or under minimal supervision.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmɔji kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ anɔ. nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli ka shi faŋŋ kɛ nitsumɔ nɔkwɛlɔi ni ená tsɔsemɔ Mechanization haa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shwiemɔ baa mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni kwɛɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I use a water pump machine instead of watering my vegetable farm by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu pɔmp atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baafɔ mibɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ?

english: A water pump delivers a strong, consistent flow of water directly from a stream or well to your field through hoses. This saves time, reduces physical exhaustion, and ensures deep root watering that hand-watering cannot achieve.
ga: Nu pɔmp lɛ kɛ nu ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ faa loo ŋshɔnaa kɛyaa oyale mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ paipii anɔ. ni haa be baa shi Ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ baa shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu ni mli kwɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he kɛtsɔ nine ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when my crops have officially reached full maturity?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ shi yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves changing color from green to yellow or brown, stalks drying up, or fruits reaching full size and firmness. At this point, the crop stops growing and is ready for harvest.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛshishifãi ni gbɛ́ɔ, loo aduawai ni shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he kɛ loo ni mli wa. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baakpa shweremɔ ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Fertilizer should be applied when soil is moist and roots are ready to absorb nutrients—usually a few weeks after germination and during early vegetative growth. Applying too early or during intense heat wastes fertilizer and can harm the crops.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii mli nibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ tso lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ kɛ be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ shishijee mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli mra tsɔ loo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Applying too much fertilizer can 'burn' the plant's roots and leaves, turn the leaves yellow or brown, stunt growth, and potentially kill the crop, while also wasting your money.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ‘eshã’ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. ehaa shweremɔ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ efite ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji shika fitemɔ hu.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve and activate so the plant roots can take it in. Applying it to dry ground keeps the nutrients trapped and useless until water is added.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli ni ekanya ni ebote tsei shishifãi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni efee nɔ ni he ehiaaa kɛyashi be mli ni akɛ nu baafata he.

english: Can I mix my weedkiller chemical with my fertilizer to save time when spraying?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Some farm chemicals can react poorly when mixed together, which can destroy their effectiveness or damage your crops. Always ask an extension officer or check product labels before combining different agricultural chemicals.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni nitsumɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ loo efite oŋmɔshi nibii. Esa akɛ obi extension official lɛ loo okwɛ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ dani okɛ okwaayeli tsofai srɔtoi afutu mli.

english: Why do I need a special permit or training before buying certain farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maná gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo krɛdɛɛ ko loo tsɔsemɔ dani mahe tsofai komɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certain agricultural substances are strong and can be dangerous if mismanaged. Regulations and permits ensure farmers receive proper safety training to protect themselves, their soil, and consumer health.
ga: Okwaayeli mli nibii komɛi eyi mli obɔ, ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efee oshara. Mlai kɛ gbɛŋmɛɛ woji haa okwaafoi lɛ naa shweshweeshwefeemɔ he tsɔsemɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe, amɛshikpɔŋ kɛ amɛ jarayelɔi lɛ ahewalɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to inspect my maize field during every growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Crops have different nutritional and protection needs at each stage of growth. Inspecting them regularly allows you to detect pests, diseases, or nutrient shortages early before they destroy your harvest.
ga: Tsei yɛ niyenii kɛ hebuu he hiamɔ nii srɔtoi yɛ amɛdalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nibii amlipɛimɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa onaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa mra. dani okpãtã onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale and yellow even though I planted them in rich soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ?

english: Maize requires active nutrient support, especially nitrogen, to stay dark green and strong. Pale leaves usually mean the soil lacks available nutrients or the roots cannot access them properly.
ga: Abɛi biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo. titri lɛ nitrogen Bɔni afee ni efee eŋɔli ni mli wa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does all fertilizer work the same way for every crop I grow on my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: No, different crops require different combinations of nutrients. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen for leaf and stalk development, whereas other crops like root vegetables or fruit trees require different nutrient balances.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii aba. Yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ shishifãi loo aduawai tsei biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can an extension officer help me measure the right amount of fertilizer for my farm size?
ga: Te extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni masusu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ he?

english: Extension officers can teach you practical measurement techniques based on your total plot size and crop count, ensuring every plant gets enough nutrients without over-fertilizing.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ bo susumɔi ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii. Enɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ayibɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli fe nine.

english: How do I calculate how many maize plants I should have on my land so they do not crowd each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmãa tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ maná yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akɔntaa? Koni amɛkafee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Officers use guidelines based on land size to help you determine the ideal number of plants for maximum yield.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni eye ebua bo ni oyoo tsei ayibɔ ni sa ni baaha oná yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Mɛɛ be nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains because direct sun and dry Harmattan winds quickly dry out their delicate leaves and roots before they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ haa baai kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gĩɔ oya dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need plenty of sunlight to build large tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil where diseases spread and exposes them to daylight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni fata staking he ji ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ nɔ, ni akɛwo hulu la mli.

english: This leaf damage is commonly caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant and feed on young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Root rot occurs when too much water stays around the roots in heavy soils during heavy rainfall. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face stress from prolonged dry weather, nutrient shortages in the soil, or attacks from insect pests like capsids.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli haomɔ he. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves typically indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen or that the soil is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight one another for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and ground water, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkpaaa nii babaoo.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even after I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po?

english: Weeds grow quickly and steal the added fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crops, leaving less nourishment for your plants to grow.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni fa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ fioo.

english: Early morning is the best time to water because it gives plants moisture before the afternoon heat and allows wet leaves to dry quickly, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ naa nu dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa baai ni efɔ lɛ egbiɔ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to support good crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark, crumbles easily in your hand, retains moisture without staying muddy, and contains living organisms like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ muji baaa. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from temporary crops like plantains because direct heat scorches their tender leaves and dries up soil moisture before their roots develop fully.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central whorl of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves, leaving behind small ragged holes and waste.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Eshiɔ bu bibii kɛ jwɛi yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after leaving them in the soil for a full year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi muu fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is too hard or poor in nutrients, or if you planted stem cuttings taken from weak, diseased plants.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ okwɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees turn yellow and droop around the trunk before flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drooping in plantain leaves are often caused by root rot from overly wet soil or fungal diseases like Panama disease that block water movement inside the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Panama hela ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without producing any pepper fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry winds cause stress to pepper plants, making the blossoms drop off because high temperatures interfere with proper flower pollination.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa.

english: How does leaving dead leaves on top of my soil help my crops during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dead leaves acts as a mulch that traps moisture, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing easily.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egboi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies feeding on the plant and spreading leaf curl viruses that disturb normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. kɛ helai ni haa baai shwieɔ shi lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. ni tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni makwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground, and staking keeps their leaves elevated away from ground dampness and diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni staking hereɔ ehe tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my main crop grow greener?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize plants grow taller and greener.
ga: Peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa, ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Planting seeds too close forces young plants to compete for sunlight and soil nutrients, making them stretch tall for light instead of using energy to produce thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛmɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a better harvest than me even though we bought the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔhé dumɔwui kome pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ?

english: Crop yield depends heavily on how well you prepare your land before planting and how carefully you carry out your daily farm management practices, such as clearing weeds and maintaining soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ bɔ ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ohaa dani oduɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Ni te otsuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi nitsumɔi, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ ohaa tɛŋŋ?

english: How does proper land clearing affect how my crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ he?

english: Preparing your soil properly helps roots penetrate deeper, allows the ground to hold moisture longer, and removes pest habitats so young crops can grow strong without competing for nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni ajie hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anyɛ adara waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Can improper weeding and clearing cause my crops to dry out faster?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi oya?

english: Yes, clearing land improperly or removing too much soil cover exposes the ground to direct heat, which quickly burns off soil moisture and stresses crop roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ ni ejaaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do crops naturally seem to grow better in regions like Ashanti or Brong-Ahafo compared to drier places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei tamɔ Ashanti loo Brong-Ahafo kɛ akɛto hei ni nu bɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Different regions have different natural environments, including higher rainfall levels, richer soil, and favorable temperatures that naturally support better crop growth in places like Brong-Ahafo and the Ashanti Region.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛi srɔtoi. nɔ ni fata he ji nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa babaoo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni hi ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei tamɔ Brong-Ahafo kɛ Ashanti kpokpaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted in the same month perform differently in different parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ kome mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ Ghana hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Local climate conditions like temperature variations, humidity, and rainfall timing vary across regions, causing the exact same crop to grow faster or slower depending on where it is planted.
ga: Akutsoŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ tsakemɔi, latsaa, kɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa oya loo edaa blɛoo yɛ he ni adu lɛ yɛ lɛ naa.

english: Is it true that certain farming towns like Dormaa are better suited for farming than other areas?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ okwaayeli maji komɛi tamɔ Dorma hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaayeli fe ekrokomɛi?

english: Yes, specific areas like Dormaa have favorable microclimates and soil conditions that allow large clusters of farms to thrive more easily than in less fertile locations.
ga: Hɛɛ, hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ Dormaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ ni hi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa okwaayeli kui wuji akɛ amɛaashwere yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baaa nii babaoo lɛ nɔ.

english: How does the surrounding environment affect how my crops handle heat during the dry season?
ga: Te shihilɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ tsuɔ dɔlɛ he nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Environmental factors like natural windbreaks, nearby trees, and surrounding vegetation help protect crops from extreme heat by reducing evaporation and keeping air moisture higher around your farm.
ga: Shihilɛ mli nibii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli hulutsoo baa lɛ nɔ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ aya ŋwɛi

english: How much of my crop's failure or success depends on my own actions versus the weather?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni eyeee omanye loo eyeee omanye lɛ damɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ minifeemɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: While weather creates the baseline environment, your personal farm activities—such as planting on time, preparing land correctly, and weeding—dictate whether your crops can survive difficult weather conditions.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ feɔ shishijee shihilɛ lɛ moŋ O diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi tamɔ dumɔ yɛ be naa Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsɔɔ kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli.

english: Does leaving trees on my farmland help or hurt my crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Leaving selected shade trees creates a milder local environment for your crops, preserving soil moisture and shading delicate plants from severe sun damage.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni ahala ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ, ebaaha shihilɛ ni mli edɔ aba kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni oha tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe shade kɛjɛ hulu ni fiteɔ nii waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops look healthy at first but weaken right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shishijee mli shi egbɔjɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Crops often fail late in the season if the land was not prepared with enough nutrients to support full growth, or if environmental stresses like soil drying out catch the plants when they need water most.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ haaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ni amɛdara kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ ahiɛ nu fe fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crops I planted are growing well and staying healthy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsei ni miduɔ lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Healthy crops usually have bright green leaves, sturdy stems, and steady growth. Regularly walking through your field helps you spot early signs of nutrient deficiency, disease, or insect damage before it spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. strong trunk and stable growth Kɛji onyiɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa, hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ mra dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and stop growing before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or the crop is getting either too much or too little water. Adding compost or well-rotted animal manure can replenish the soil and help the leaves stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops so they do not rot in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops give clear signs when ready, such as leaves drying, color shifting from green to yellow/brown, or seed heads hardening. Harvesting at the right time stops mold, insects, and rain from destroying your yield.
ga: Tsei baaha okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛji amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni egbi, ni amɛsu tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ/ŋmɔŋ. aloo dumɔwui lɛ ayitso lɛ mli waɔ Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: How does unexpected rain during the harvest season affect my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ baasa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Excess rain during harvest can cause ripe grains to sprout prematurely or rot on the plant. Harvesting on clear dry days and drying crops thoroughly in the sun before storage prevents post-harvest losses.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ nikpamɔ be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akwɛ̃ mra loo egbo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa nɔ ni agbiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛtoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nibii ni baafite yɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Farming feels very overwhelming and tiring for me. What simple methods can make my daily field work easier?
ga: Okwaayeli haa minuɔ he akɛ eji nɔ ni tsii fe nine ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Mɛɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo baanyɛ aha mi daa gbi shiɛmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ afee mlɛo?

english: Planting in straight rows makes weeding faster, while applying mulch (dry grass or leaves) around crops suppresses weed growth and holds water, greatly reducing the amount of manual labor required.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ ayeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni mulching (Dry grass loo leaves) ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe lɛ baatsi jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehiɛ nu mli. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do my crops keep failing or producing very small yields even on a small farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko po mli lɛ?

english: Low yields on small plots usually come from poor seed quality, exhausted soil, or incorrect spacing. Using certified seeds and rotating different crops every season restores soil power and boosts yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni ehiii, shikpɔŋ ni efite, loo gbɛ ni esaaa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Be fɛɛ be yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: I keep a few cattle on my farm; how can I use them to help my crops grow better?
ga: Mikwɛɔ tsinai fioo komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛtsu nii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cattle dung is a rich natural fertilizer that improves soil nutrients and water retention, while leftover crop leaves and stalks can be fed back to your cattle, saving money on fertilizer and feed.
ga: Tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aha tsinai lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shika toɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii he.

english: How can I protect the crops I planted from being eaten or damaged by my livestock?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe koni kooloi akaye loo akafite?

english: Creating living fences out of thorny local plants or building simple bamboo borders around your crop plots keeps animals restricted while allowing them to graze safely in designated areas.
ga: Afee gbogbo ni hiɛ ka kɛjɛ maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli loo afeɔ ŋmei husu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ebɔle oŋmɔji lɛ ahe Enɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ahi shi yɛ be mli ni ehaa amɛyeɔ kooloi shweshweeshwe yɛ hei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ.

english: I want to start growing crops for the first time in Ghana. Which crop is easiest for a beginner to succeed with?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ Ghana. Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ akɛ amɛaaye omanye yɛ mli?

english: Crops like cassava and maize are ideal for beginners because they are hardy, adapt well to local soil and rainfall patterns, and have a steady local market demand.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni jeɔ shishi lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ hewɔ. Ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee jogbaŋŋ kɛha he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ. ni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Insects are destroying the few crops I planted. What is a cheap and simple way to protect them?
ga: Kplukai miifite ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni miduɔ lɛ. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni jara waaa ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe?

english: You can prepare simple natural sprays using neem tree leaves or sprinkle wood ash on affected crops to repel pests without spending money on expensive chemical insecticides.
ga: Obaanyɛ osaa adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ okɛ neem baai loo tso sũ afɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ koni okɛshwie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ehe ehiaaa ni ofite tsofai ni jara wa ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the growing stalks fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in weak stems and small corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii baa.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in the green leaves of my young maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni etse ehe lɛ miije kpo yɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar eating the leaf tissue, which can weaken the plant and destroy the growing point if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ cutworms ni eye baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni efite hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ kɛji akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves during dry spells to save water, but severe leaf drop usually means the trees lack adequate shade coverage or soil moisture to protect them from extreme heat.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai ni fiteɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baabu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ he.

english: Why does my oil palm tree produce plenty of flowers but fails to form fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi ewooo aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need successful pollination by insects or wind to turn flowers into fruits; if the farm lacks pollinating weevils or if the tree is suffering from severe water stress, the flowers will wither without producing palm fruit.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ ni kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa lɛ bɛ loo kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa he. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛwooo ŋmei yibii.

english: How do I choose the best part of a cassava stem to cut and plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The middle section of a mature stem is best for planting because it has well-developed buds and enough stored energy to sprout strong roots quickly, unlike the soft top stem or the hard base.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii ni edara jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ oya. Jeee akɛ tsɔne lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishi ni wa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for growing heavy underground tubers, and staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from heat, rot, and shade caused by weeds.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. ni okɛ ohe awo shi koni owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulutsoo lɛ akafee nɔ ko. fitemɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni jwɛi kɛbaa

english: Which type of plantain sucker is the best one for me to transplant into a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi kɛha ŋmɔ hee mli dumɔ?

english: Sword suckers—which have a broad base and thin, blade-like leaves—are the best to plant because they have strong underground buds that produce healthy roots faster than suckers with wide leaves.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli wa ni woɔ shishifãi ni mli wa oya fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like phosphorus during the flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Why does adding dried animal manure make my crops grow better than just planting in plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Animal manure releases nutrients like nitrogen slowly into the soil over time and improves the soil's ability to hold moisture around plant roots during dry days.
ga: Koolooi agbo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli fiofio. Beni be hoɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up heavily in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that shield the young cocoa plants from heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow well. Applying fertilizer or well-rotted manure fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply top-dressing fertilizer to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The best time is about 4 to 6 weeks after planting, when the maize is knee-high. This is when the plant enters a fast growth stage and needs extra nutrients the most.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe. Enɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ boteɔ edalɛ oyaiyeli be lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa niyenii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he fe fɛɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains all the nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility and kills pests naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with my corn help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This acts as a free, natural fertilizer for your corn.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stem to plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that show no signs of disease. Use the hard middle section of the stem—about thumb thickness—with clearly visible, healthy buds.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hela he okadi ko lɛ amli. Kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni wa lɛ atsu nii. (aaafee tsɔne bibioo ko dalɛ) ni ŋmeii ni mli wa ni anaa jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need as much sunlight as possible to produce food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun, leading to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is making ragged holes in my corn leaves with small brown dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abele baai lɛ amli ewo muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛmli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They eat the central growing leaves of maize, but you can control them early by applying approved insecticides or dropping clean sand into the plant funnel.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni adu yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai. Shi obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ mra. Kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ ŋã ni he tse awo dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: It is best to water early in the morning. This allows the roots to absorb moisture before the sun gets hot, whereas afternoon watering causes moisture to evaporate quickly and can shock the leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ oya, ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ akpokpo.

english: Why do my stored beans get tiny holes and turn into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Tiny holes are caused by bean weevils, which lay eggs inside the seeds. Properly drying your beans and storing them in airtight containers or PICS bags suffocates the insects and protects your crop.
ga: Bean weevils ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ogbi kɔfi yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo PICS kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant needs to grow green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or animal manure around the base will feed the crop and turn the leaves green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Cones lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down will slow down growth or prevent roots from forming properly. You must make sure the tiny buds on the stem point upward toward the sky before pushing the stick into the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akwɛ̃ɔ ŋmei tsei ni tsɔɔ amɛhe nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ okwɛ koni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akafite. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani ekɛ tso lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ

english: You should wait until you get two or three steady, heavy rains that soak deep into the soil before planting. Planting right after the very first light shower can cause your seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani odu. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and saw-dust dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baa mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant and eat the soft leaves, so you need to apply recommended treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ lɛ awo faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden poles in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves exposed to sunlight so the plant can make energy to grow big tubers underground, while also keeping leaves off wet ground where diseases live.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ ahi lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer as soon as I bury the seed or wait until it sprouts?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ loo aaamɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait until the seed sprouts and shows its first green leaves, usually one to two weeks after planting. Putting fertilizer directly on unsprouted seeds can burn them or get washed away by rain before the plant has roots to absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛjie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ baai eŋɔli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui ni ekwɛko lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo nugbɔ ahoɔ amɛ dani tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How does leaving weeds in my farm affect the growth of my cassava roots?
ga: Te jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your cassava crop. Clearing weeds early gives your cassava room and full access to soil nutrients so the roots can swell into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa o-cassava tsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei tsu lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom end rot, and it happens when tomato plants do not get regular water or lack calcium in the soil. Watering your tomato plants consistently and avoiding letting the soil get completely dry prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu daa loo calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha egbi lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil moisture quickly, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make green leaves and build food. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee baai eŋɔli ni ekɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the center leaf whorl of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hide inside the leaves at the center of the plant to feed, but early spraying with recommended bio-pesticides or neem oil can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ afɔse tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ mra. Ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots break down in the ground, they release natural fertilizer that feeds nearby maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before any small pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought and poor soil nutrients. Maintaining partial shade and moisture helps midges survive and keeps flowers on the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ko mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dwarf lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when the ground is soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can easily be damaged by soil pests like nematodes and stem borers. Pruning away excess suckers and keeping the base clean strengthens the main tree's root system.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes kɛ stem borers baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oha shishigbɛ lɛ he atse lɛ, ebaawaje tso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, the plant stops storing fresh starch in the roots and begins forming tough wood fibers. Harvesting on time ensures the tubers stay soft, starchy, and good for eating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei hee ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ni ebɔi tso mli tsɔi ni mli wa lɛ feemɔ. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni esa akɛ aye.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die in the afternoon heat even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that gets inside the roots and blocks the plant's internal tubes, stopping water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does covering the soil with dry grass around my crop stems keep the ground wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield against direct sunlight, reducing water evaporation from the soil and keeping the root zone cool.
ga: Baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. kɛ shishifã lɛ he ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my crops produce tiny yields if I plant four or five seeds together in the same small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ to he kome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too closely together compete against each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak stems and smaller harvests compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.
