english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops after a big rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with aggressive root systems that absorb water and nutrients instantly, whereas farm crops take longer to establish their roots and require early weeding to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi shwieɔ shi, ni ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli mra. koni eda

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and dry up before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow prematurely when the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or when the soil gets too waterlogged. Keeping the field well-drained and applying fertilizer at the right time keeps leaves green so they can feed the growing cobs.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ mra kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ oha he ni nu hoɔ yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli koni eye ebua ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does standing water kill my maize crop, but my rice crop grows well in flooded fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni damɔ shi miigbe mi ŋmãa lɛ? Shi ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their roots that allow them to breathe underwater. Maize roots lack these channels, so sitting in water suffocates the roots and causes the crop to rot and die.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko wo nu mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with green leaves but end up producing tiny cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen causes them to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of fruiting. Maize needs a balanced diet, including phosphorus and potassium, to convert foliage growth into big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tso ko lɛ, ehaa ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he moŋ fe aduawai ni baa lɛ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia ŋmãa. ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he Koni etsake baai lɛ adalɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does my rice crop fall over flat on the ground right before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Rice falls over (lodges) when its stems are thin or when too much fertilizer makes the head heavy. Giving the crop adequate potassium helps strengthen the stems, while proper planting distance gives roots room to hold the crop firmly in the soil.
ga: Omɔ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bafee mlɛo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ha otsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni amɛkɛfiɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some cobs in my maize farm have missing grains with empty patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii ni bɛ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Maize relies on wind to carry pollen from the top tassels to the silks below. If the weather is extremely hot and dry when flowers open, the pollen dries up, leaving unfilled spots where grains failed to form.
ga: Abele kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ejie pollen kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli kɛya siliki ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ beni fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Ashiɔ hei ni eyiko ni nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui.

english: How do I know the exact right time that my rice is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn a clear golden-yellow color. Harvesting too early leaves you with soft, chalky grains, while waiting too long makes the ripe grains drop onto the ground and waste.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 batsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbee shikpɔŋ ni etsɔ jwɛi.

english: Why do buyers pay me less for my harvested grain if I leave it to dry in the sun too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo yɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ahe lɛ? Ni kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ hulu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ hu?

english: Over-drying grains makes them brittle and prone to cracking when threshed or milled. Buyers reduce prices for cracked grains because they break easily into powder during processing, reducing total usable food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni egbi tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaakumɔ oya kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli loo atsɔ mli. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baa ŋmaa ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ jara nɔ ejaakɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni etsɔɔ powda beni atsuɔ he nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Will using a harvesting machine break or ruin my grain compared to cutting it by hand?
ga: Ani ŋmaakpamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baakumɔ loo ebaafite miŋmaa lɛ kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛfoɔ lɛ he?

english: Harvesting machines are set to gently strip and clean mature grain without crushing it. When used correctly on well-dried crops, a machine reduces grain breakage and separates dirt better than manual beating.
ga: Ato nikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ dumɔwui ni eda lɛ atsu nii fiofio ni ekɛtsuuu nii ni ekɛ amɛ etswaaa. Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Mshinii haa ŋmaa ni etseɔ lɛ baa shi ni ejaraa muji mli jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni akɛ niji tswaa.

english: How can a flying drone tell if my crops are sick or struggling before I can see it myself?
ga: Te drone ni foɔ lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔ dani mi diɛŋtsɛ mana?

english: Drones take photos using special sensors that measure light reflection off leaves. Leaves that are thirsty or suffering from hidden disease change how they reflect light long before human eyes can notice the damage.
ga: Drone lɛ kɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi ni susuɔ la ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ mfoniri. Baai ni kumai yeɔ amɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baatsake bɔ ni amɛjieɔ la kpo amɛhaa lɛ dani adesa hiŋmɛi lɛ ana nɔ ni efite lɛ.

english: Will spraying liquid fertilizer with a drone burn or damage the leaves of my crops?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛ drone shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baashã loo ebaafite mitsei lɛ ahe baai?

english: Drones release chemical mixtures as an extremely fine, controlled mist that coats leaves evenly. Because the spray is light and uniform, leaves absorb the nutrients quickly without liquid gathering into burning pools on the leaf surface.
ga: Drone lɛ jieɔ tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni anyɛɔ akudɔɔ mli. ni haa baai lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ waaa ni ehiɔ shi daa. Baai lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni nu lɛ buaaa ehe naa yɛ nubui ni eshã yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping some shade trees protects them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaha abu ohe yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem. Make sure the buds are pointing upwards toward the sky before pushing the stem into the ground, otherwise the crop will grow upside down and weak.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni okwɛ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ŋmɔshi nii lɛ baatsɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can scorch germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular so the young roots have constant moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ daa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ nii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during dry spells when there are weeds all around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni jwɛi ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that drink up all the underground water and nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds regularly leaves more water in the soil for your crops to survive.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do people cover the soil around their vegetable roots with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ashishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Dry leaves keep the soil cool, stop moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and slow down weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔi lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central leaves and eat the plant. Catching them early with recommended control measures saves your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaahere onitsumɔ lɛ yiwala.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when the plant lacks water. Regular watering and partial protection during extreme heat helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hebuu ko yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Without temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them, the leaves burn, curl up, and turn yellow to cope with heat stress and water loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, amɛbaakpãtã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkɛkpee dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajie nibii krokomɛi ni fata he ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all compete for the same soil water and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to leave only two or three strong ones allows the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, tso kome Tsobii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ amli babaoo koni eshi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants shade each other and fight for nutrients in the soil. This forces them to stretch thin toward sunlight instead of building strong stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛya hulu la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm make the soil richer for next season's maize?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the crop leaves and roots decay after harvest, they release this natural fertilizer back into the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdu wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and soft if I leave them in the ground after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains begin, mature cassava plants take energy out of their underground tubers to grow fresh green leaves above ground, which makes the roots lose starch content and become watery.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ, Cassava tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli starch lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛfeɔ nu.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to make food for the plant. Staking holds the leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which sends nutrients down to swell the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: La tɛ̃ɛ he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi koni ená hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii baa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress or poor pollination. High afternoon temperatures prevent the pollen from fertilizing the flower, causing the plant to drop the blossom.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa ji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo pollination ni ehiii. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. haa tsei shwieɔ shi

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into cups and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or viruses they spread. As they feed on the underside of young leaves, the leaves distort and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa beni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato nursery seedlings suddenly collapse and die right at the soil line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This collapse is caused by fungal diseases known as 'damping-off,' which thrive in overwatered or crowded seedbeds where moisture remains trapped near the soil surface.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ shigbeemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damping’, ni shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli he ni nu ni mli edɔ etsi ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry fertilizer on top of the soil right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the topsoil before the roots can absorb it. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or buried near the crop root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. loo afu yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why do I need to place wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the damp soil, maximizing sunlight exposure and preventing ground fungal diseases from infecting the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo Ni otsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight because their foliage is sensitive. Planting them under fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a cool microclimate and protects young cocoa from sun scorch during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ nuɔ la he waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ baa, ni ebuɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize typically indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for leafy growth, so adding compost, animal manure, or a balanced nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color and grain development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil grow better crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a natural fertilizer in the ground. When planted alongside maize or rotated with it, legumes feed nitrogen directly to the soil, reducing the need for chemical fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Gbalamɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni otsake lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo akɛ ŋmãa tsu nii kɛdu Legumes lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does my plot produce much smaller harvests when I grow cassava in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ faaa kwraa kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that crop feeds on and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating crops helps rest the soil and break disease cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni tso lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni efoɔ helai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots go soft and rot underground after heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged, poorly drained soil because oxygen cannot reach the roots. Plant cassava on raised mounds or ridges so surplus rainwater drains away naturally from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why is it beneficial to spread dry grass or leaves around the roots of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-vegetable shishifãi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering soil with organic materials, known as mulching, prevents rainwater from evaporating quickly, keeps the soil cool during dry spells, and stops weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni ekaha obɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do small holes appear in the leaves of my young maize plants in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai anɔ yɛ be ni amɛdaraa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaf funnels are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the foliage. Detecting them early allows you to use neem oil solutions or recommended targeted treatments to save the central growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Enɛ baaha okɛ neem fɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ atsu nii ni okɛtsa shweremɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when plants experience severe heat stress, dry spells, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and keeping the root zone cool with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. shihilɛi ni mli egbi Aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and turning crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curled, twisted pepper leaves are caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating the insects early with mild insecticidal soaps stops further foliage damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa lɛ. Koolooi ahe tsamɔ mra Samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa baai lɛ afitemɔ kroko.

english: What should I do to save my cassava crops if my field gets flooded after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikɛhere mi-cassava tsei lɛ ayiwala kɛji nugbɔ ba miŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot quickly when left in standing water for more than a few days. You should dig drainage channels around your field to let the excess water flow away, or plant on raised soil mounds during the wet season to keep the roots dry.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli fe gbii fioo komɛi. Esa akɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ he. ŋmãa ŋmɔji koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli Aloo adu yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni shishifãi lɛ akagbi.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow after continuous rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them, and too much water starves roots of air. Digging simple water paths to drain the farm and applying a bit of nitrogen fertilizer once the soil dries will help them green up again.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ni nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Nu ni atsaa lɛ mlɛo Kɛji akɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo afata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell when it is safe to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because a sudden dry spell can kill young seeds. Wait until the rain falls consistently enough that the top layer of soil stays moist for three consecutive days.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ be fɛɛ be bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across my yam leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by leaf spot disease, which spreads rapidly in warm, humid weather when leaves stay wet. You can prevent it by giving plants enough space for air to flow through and removing infected leaves early before it spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ enɛ baa, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni baa lɛ mli efɔ lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni oooha otsei lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa

english: Will using chemical fertilizers damage my land over time compared to animal manure?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ akɛto kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Relying only on chemical fertilizers without organic matter can make the soil acidic and hard over time. Mixing modern fertilizers with natural manure or compost keeps the soil rich, moist, and healthy for years to come.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ tsu nii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee acidic ni ewa yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: Is it better for my soil if I spray weed killer or clear weeds by hand with a hoe?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ loo mikɛ minine shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ?

english: Spraying weed killer saves time, but overuse can damage beneficial soil microbes and nearby crops. Combining weed chemicals for heavy areas with hoeing around delicate crop stems protects your plants and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa be afite. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛfutuɔ hei ni tsii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Black pod disease thrives when cocoa trees are too shaded and air cannot dry the damp pods. Pruning tall shade trees and clearing lower branches lets sunshine in and lowers the humidity around the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ daa kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha ŋmeii ni mli efɔ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ajieɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni eha hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest grow smaller cobs than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce strong crops in their first generation, but their saved offspring lose vigor and produce smaller yields. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa aba. Shi seshibii ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni mli wa baa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat causes tomato plants to drop flowers to save their water and energy. Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the roots cool and helps the plant hold onto its blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to reduce water loss from direct sunlight and heat. If they uncurl in the evening, the plant is fine, but giving them regular water will help reduce their stress.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba nu ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baa lɛ shi. Kɛ amɛkpɛ amɛyiŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo nu mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eba haomɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs sunlight to make food for big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why will planting my seeds too close together make my final harvest smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ baaha minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ aba shi lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other underground for soil food and water, while their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in thin plants and small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply before the hot sun causes the water to evaporate into the air.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when too much rain collects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped in the soil, the roots suffocate and soil fungi cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Planting maize on the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize-specific pests build up in the ground. Switching to beans or groundnuts refreshes the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmeii loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under the hot sun. Plantain trees grow fast and broad, acting as natural shade umbrellas to protect the delicate cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛfeɔ wuji. Amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the plant lacks steady water, because extreme heat and dry conditions prevent the flower from turning into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ tsakeee aduawai.

english: How do wild weeds hurt my crops even if there seems to be enough open land around them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye midumɔ nii lɛ awui? Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛhe moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, water, and soil food before your crops can reach them, effectively starving your crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my soil so hard that it is difficult to dig and plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa akɛ ewa akɛ abaatsũ ni akwɛ tsei lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter, is over-farmed, or gets dried out by direct sunlight. Adding compost, leaves, or animal manure helps break up hard soil so roots can grow easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. niyenii ni ayeɔ fe nine loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni haa egbiɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai, loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: What practical steps can I take to soften hard land before planting my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni hei ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo dani madu kookoo?

english: You can soften hard land by digging planting holes early, adding manure or compost into the holes, and spreading a layer of dry grass or leaves (mulch) over the soil to hold moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha hei ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo kɛtsɔ dumɔ bu ni oootsu mra lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo bu lɛ mli. ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛ ashwã (mulch) lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops remain small and stunted when the ground below the topsoil is very hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli wa waa lɛ?

english: When the deeper soil is hard or compacted, plant roots cannot push downwards to reach underground moisture and nutrients, which stops the plant from growing big and strong.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ shi koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haaa tsei adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Is it better to plant my young crops early in the rainy season instead of waiting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni aaamɛ?

english: Yes, planting early gives young plants enough rain and time to build strong root systems before the harsh dry season arrives, helping them survive tough conditions.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying after I transplant them onto my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni mifã kɛtee koni miyadu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings often die if they receive too much hot sunlight, if the soil is too hard for their roots to spread, or if they do not get enough water during their first few weeks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo dumɔwui gboiɔ kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ loo kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to keep shade trees around young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔdu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn in direct sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the air cool and the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves and grass help my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around seedlings with dry leaves, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil, retains water, and turns into plant food as it rots.
ga: Mulching ni bɔleɔ Dumɔwui ni baai egbi lɛ akɛ mulching. Ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii be mli ni egboɔ lɛ.

english: How can I know if a piece of land is suitable for cocoa before I clear the bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Good cocoa land should have deep, soft, dark soil that drains water easily without flooding, and it should have enough big trees to provide gentle shade for young plants.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ. Nu lɛ hoɔ oya, nu afua ko bɛ, ni esa akɛ tsei wuji ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo.

english: If a portion of my land is too hard for cocoa, can I plant a different crop there?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko mli wa tsɔ akɛ abaanyɛ adu kookoo Ani manyɛ madu tsei krokomɛi yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Yes, crops like cassava, yam, or legumes are tougher and can tolerate harder or poorer soils better than sensitive crops like cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cassava, sweet potatoes loo legumes wa waa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ shikpɔji ni wa loo ohiafoi anɔ fe tsei ni waaa tamɔ cocoa.

english: How can I plan my land preparation so that farm work does not overwhelm me later in the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato mishikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ he gbɛjianɔ koni ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ akaye minɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Preparing your land in smaller, manageable sections and planting in phases allows you to clear, weed, and care for your crops properly without running out of time or money.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ fãi bibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii amli, ni oduɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ ojieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni okwɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee be loo shika.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally feeds the maize plants, improves soil fertility, and gives you two different crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aye nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ aya hiɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ aba kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain, as the soil underneath is often still dry. Dig down into the soil with your hand or a cutlass; if the top 10 to 15 centimeters of soil stays moist and holds together when squeezed, it is safe to sow your seeds.
ga: Kaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Okɛ oniji loo dade atsu nii kɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ji sɛntimitai 10 kɛyashi 15 lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning yellow because the soil lacks nutrients or because of too much rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo?

english: If the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, the lower, older leaves turn yellow first while the upper leaves stay green. If it is due to waterlogging, all leaves across the plant droop and yellow together because saturated soil smothers the roots and prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, baai bibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ. Kɛji nu afua lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ nɔ baai fɛɛ baagbo ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛmu.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees protect cocoa seedlings from harsh sun heat, keep the surrounding air humid, and prevent the soil from drying out too fast.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward into the sunlight to catch light and produce energy. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing the plant to grow bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛha hewalɛ aba. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I leave dry plantain leaves on the soil around the base of the plant instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi plantain baai ni egbi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Leaving organic materials like dried leaves on the soil acts as mulch. Mulching traps soil moisture during dry spells, suppresses weeds from growing, and breaks down over time into rich fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulching lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What is eating holes in the leaves inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing point of the maize plant during the daytime and feed on the soft, young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni darako lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling tightly upwards and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiiya ŋwɛi shiŋŋ ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on sap and spreading leaf curl virus. Controlling these small insects early prevents the leaf curl disease from crippling the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ leaf curl virus lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni leaf curl hela lɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains flood the farm for long periods, standing water starves roots of oxygen, causing bacteria and fungi to attack and decompose mature cassava tubers in the waterlogged soil.
ga: Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni eda ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants lose all their flowers without producing any fruit during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ fɛɛ laajeɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When daytime temperatures get extremely hot, tomato pollen dries out and becomes inactive, causing unpollinated flowers to drop off the stem before fruit can start forming.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsuuu nii. Ha fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai aje shishi amɛwo.

english: How long does it usually take for a rice crop to grow from planting until it is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most common rice varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) from planting to reach full maturity, allowing farmers to plan their planting according to the rainy season.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani edaa kɛyashɛɔ shweremɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛtoɔ dumɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naa.

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80% to 85% of the grains on the stalks turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the grains feel hard when you bite into them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ateŋ aaafee 80% kɛyashi 85% tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ okɛ ohe wo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why does rice need so much water in the field compared to maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in wet conditions because water helps transport nutrients efficiently to the plant while naturally choking out weeds that cannot survive under flooded soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the tips of my crop leaves drying up and turning brown during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf tips turn brown when the plant is losing moisture into the hot air faster than its roots can drink water from the soil, which is a sign that the crop is suffering from heat stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɔfo kɛji tso lɛ mli nu lɛ fite kɛtee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miina dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves lose their deep green color and turn pale yellow, usually starting from the bottom leaves, and the plant stops growing tall.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni tso lɛ baakpa shweremɔ.

english: Young crops are weak and easily choked by fast-growing weeds; removing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the soil nutrients, water, and sunlight to grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ shwieɔ amɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, air, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks and a smaller overall yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: What is the difference between buying certified seeds and using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahemɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ teŋ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to resist diseases and produce high yields uniformly, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their strength and yield less crop over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo be fɛɛ be. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What can I do after harvest to stop insects from destroying my stored grain over the year?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ koni kooloi akafite dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: To safely store grain for long periods, dry it thoroughly under the sun until it is completely hard, then keep it in clean, airtight bags in a dry store room to keep moisture and bugs out.
ga: Koni akɛ dumɔwui ato shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ Ha egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo vacuum bag ni mli tse mli yɛ he ko ni egbi koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why does my harvested rice break into tiny pieces when it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Beni oootsɔ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains break during milling if the crop was harvested when it was already too dry, or if it was dried too quickly under intense direct sunlight, making the grains brittle.
ga: Ŋmaa baakumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni egbi tsɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same piece of land as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mi-kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ duɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct heat from the sun. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide broad leaf cover that shades cocoa plants and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaves and promotes strong stem growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tso lɛ yibii lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure straight onto my crop soil right after clearing out my poultry house?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo tsɛnsi sũ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie tsina ŋmɔtɔ shĩa lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure generates strong heat and ammonia as it decomposes, which can scorch tender roots and kill crops. It should be left to rot and dry in a compost heap for a few weeks before applying it to land.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ feɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ammonia beni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Esa akɛ aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi ni amɛgbi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their vegetable crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass, known as mulching, stops hot sunlight from drying out the earth, keeps root zones cool, and blocks weeds from growing and stealing crop nutrients.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ebɔle Tsei ahe, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju tsei amli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot inside the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing rainwater stays trapped in the soil around them for too long without adequate drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away freely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme fluctuations between very wet and very dry soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during peak midday heat helps plants set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli egbi waa teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ la ni ahiɔ shi daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and slowing plant growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha tso lɛ dalɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Spraying plants with neem oil or appropriate insecticidal soap helps suppress these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same plot every farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil consumes the same nutrients year after year and lets maize-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii afi fɛɛ afi. kɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni akɛhaa ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose maximum leaf area to direct sunlight. When leaves catch enough light, they produce the energy needed to build bigger, heavier yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba.

english: Will planting my crops very close together produce a larger total harvest?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ni mikɛduɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to compete intensely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants with small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce maximum yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water and survive the heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume normal growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support. Shedding unfertilized or excess flowers is a normal way for the tree to save its energy for the few pods it can successfully grow.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi ni bɛ fɔmɔ loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tsei fɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he kɛha fɔfɔi fioo ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize plants have small holes in the leaves and white dust inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni sũ yɛŋ yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars or fall armyworms feeding on the tender inner leaves and stems, which weakens the maize plant and reduces your final harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers loo cutworms ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa naagbee ŋmaa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves at the top of my pepper plants curling up tightly into a ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by plant viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular amounts of water while the fruits are forming, rather than being caused by an infectious plant disease.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ calcium loo enine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei ahe helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same soil where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a free natural fertilizer for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around lɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa mi-vegetables lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (called mulching) keeps the hot sun from drying out the water in the dirt, keeps crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from springing up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the extra small shoots growing at the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nɔ krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Too many shoot suckers steal water and soil nutrients from the main plant. Removing extra suckers leaves maximum energy for the main stem to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch full sunlight on their leaves, which allows the plant to produce the energy needed to grow large tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa kɛjɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and stay small even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal fertilizer, water, and root space directly from your crops underneath the soil, essentially starving your crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people say a crop seed is an F1 hybrid?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛɛ tso ko dumɔwu ji F1 hybrid lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: An F1 hybrid seed is produced by crossing two different plant varieties. This cross gives the crop special strength and vigor, helping it grow fast and produce a heavy harvest of good fruit.
ga: Akɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ F1 hybrid dumɔwui. Nɛkɛ krɔs nɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ nibii kpakpai babaoo.

english: Can I collect and plant the seeds from the high-yielding fruits I harvest this season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui anaa ni madu kɛjɛ aduawai ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni mikpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: If your harvest came from F1 hybrid seeds, saving those seeds for next season is not recommended. The seeds from the harvested fruit will not grow into the same strong plants and will result in uneven, lower-quality fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ lɛ jɛ F1 hybrid dumɔwui amli lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ato kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ edaŋ ni amɛtsɔŋ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni ebaaha yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee aba.

english: What happens when two different varieties of the same crop are crossed together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ tso kome mli henɔi enyɔ tsɔ mli?

english: Crossing two different plant varieties creates a hybrid. The first generation of plants from this cross usually grows stronger, bears fruit faster, and produces better yields than traditional direct seeds.
ga: Tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni afɔɔ lɛ haa anáa tsofa ni akɛfee tsofa kroko. Bei pii lɛ, tsei klɛŋklɛŋ ni jɛ krɔs nɛɛ mli lɛ daa waa. Ehaa yibii oya ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni hi fe blema dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ

english: Is it better for me to buy hybrid seeds or stick with local traditional seeds for my farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome loo makɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni ji shishijee dumɔwui lɛ akpɛtɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: Both types have their place. F1 hybrid seeds give very high yields and uniform ripening but require buying fresh seeds each season, whereas local seeds allow you to save your own seed even if the yields are somewhat lower.
ga: Henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ amɛ gbɛhe. F1 hybrid dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo waa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Shi esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui lɛ toɔ, eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi fioo moŋ.

english: Why do seeds bought from the agro-dealer grow with so much power compared to seeds I saved myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ daa waa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mibuaa naa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Agro-dealer hybrid seeds are specially bred to have high energy and vigor, which allows the plant to grow strongly, set abundant fruit, and ripen evenly when given proper care.
ga: Akwɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa. Ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I have to buy new hybrid seeds every single planting season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, if you want to maintain the same high yield and fruit quality every year, you must buy fresh F1 seeds each season because saved hybrid seeds lose their strength in the next generation.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji oosumɔ ni ohiɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Esa akɛ ohe F1 dumɔwui heei yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops ripening faster and bearing larger fruit than mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ yibii wuji fe mi nɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using F1 hybrid seeds, which are bred to have high vigor and quick development, allowing fruits to mature and ripen faster than non-hybrid crops.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ F1 hybrid dumɔwui, ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara oya lɛ miitsu nii. Ehaa aduawai lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya fe tsei ni jeee tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ.

english: Why did the crops I grew from my saved hybrid seeds turn out so weak and uneven?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu kɛjɛ hybrid dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Seeds taken from an F1 hybrid harvest split their genetic traits in the second generation, causing the new plants to lose their combined vigor and produce unpredictable fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ F1 hybrid ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jaa su yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei heei lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛfee ekome lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: How can I tell if a seed variety will give me a heavy fruit harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni sa? Ani ebaaha miná naagbai ni tsii?

english: Seeds labeled as F1 hybrids are designed for high productivity, meaning once they take root, they reliably bear high volumes of uniform fruit that ripen well for harvest.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni aŋmala nɔ akɛ F1 hybrids lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ, Ewoɔ yibii ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔɔ.

english: Will planting hybrid crops force me to change the way I care for my land?
ga: Ani tsei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ baaha matsake bɔ ni mikwɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mihaa lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Hybrid seeds work on your regular farmland, but because they bear more fruit and grow faster, they perform best when given sufficient water and nutrients.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Hybrid dumɔwui tsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli ŋmɔji ni okɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ amli. Shi akɛni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ hewɔ. Amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key soil nutrient that keeps leaves green and helps the plant grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the plant juice, or by a virus transmitted by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, improper watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ haomɔ, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni esaaa. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my bean plants try to climb and wrap themselves around nearby corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ miitao ekwɔ ni ekɛ ehe abɔle ŋmãa tso ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Climbing bean varieties have weak stems and naturally look for taller structures to reach higher into the air for more sunlight.
ga: Bean henɔi ni kwɔɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛtaoɔ nibii ni kwɔlɔ ni amɛshɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: Why does my yam vine dry up and die off right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi ni egbo dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally turn brown and dry up when the plant matures because it has finished sending all its energy and nutrients down into the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baatsɔ blɔfo ni amɛbaagbi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ewo shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Excessive water fills up the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots and allowing water-loving fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha hydrophilic fungi lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunshine. Without larger trees to provide shade and trap humidity, the sun burns their young leaves and dries them out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and tall with small cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops have to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to grow weak instead of producing big yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Esa akɛ Dumɔwui lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ daaa fioo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does growing groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛ nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after a rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep or spreading root systems that allow them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than domesticated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ loo amɛgbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe shia tsei.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and grow tall. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure restores their green color and health.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my crops make my soil richer?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni shwereɔ?

english: Cowpeas and other beans have special roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil as natural plant food, which feeds neighboring crops for free.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away off the top of the soil before your crop's roots can drink it in, wasting your investment and washing useful nutrients out of your field.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ. Eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ ni efɔseɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso mli moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows leaves to catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to pump food underground and produce larger tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛpomp niyenii awo shikpɔŋ shishi ni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba.

english: When too many suckers grow around one stem, they compete for water and nutrients, resulting in small bunches; leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Suckers kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa ji nɔ ni eshwɛ koni ekwɛ koni jwɛi agbo ni tsii aba.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so quickly even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that drink water and absorb fertilizer much faster than your crops, stealing light and essential nutrients your plants need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ejuɔ la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, the roots cannot breathe air, which creates ideal conditions for soil fungi and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets extremely stressed by excessive heat or uneven watering, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa waa. Enɛ haaa pollination ni sa aba.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up when the weather becomes damp and cold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that multiplies in cold, humid, and shaded conditions; pruning trees to let sunlight through helps keep pods dry and healthy.
