ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni fɔɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings die when I pour a lot of water on them once a day instead of watering them lightly multiple times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu babaoo wo mli shikome daa gbi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mawo amɛ nu blɛoo shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Young crops have tiny, shallow roots that can only drink a little bit of water at a time. Flooding them with too much water at once drowns the roots and rots them, whereas light watering at shorter intervals keeps the soil constantly moist without suffocating the plant.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni baanyɛ anu nu fioo pɛ yɛ be kome mli Nu ni awoɔ lɛ babaoo shikome lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fioo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Is it better for me to give all the fertilizer to my maize crop at once, or should I split it into small doses over time?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ awo mli shikome? Aloo esa akɛ majara ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii bibii? Beni be hoɔ lɛ

english: Crops absorb nutrients gradually as they grow. Applying fertilizer in smaller, frequent doses ensures the plant gets fed whenever it is hungry, and it prevents heavy rains from washing away excess fertilizer before the roots can use it.
ga: Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fiofio be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli fioo ni ekɛwoɔ mli shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii be fɛɛ be ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Does it matter if I use salty or dirty water from the gutter to water my tomato plants during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ mi-gutter lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛwo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, water quality is very important for crop health. Dirty or salty water can burn delicate roots, block the plant from taking up food, and introduce diseases that will stunt the growth of your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahewalɛ. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo nu ni mli ewo muji baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni ekɛ helai ni baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ naa lɛ baa.

english: Why do young pepper seedlings in the nursery need so much more attention and frequent care than fully grown plants in the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings are very delicate and dry out quickly under the hot sun because their roots are small. Just like young babies, they need small, regular care with water and shade until their roots grow deep enough to survive tougher field conditions.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ waaa waa ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ daraaa. Tamɔ abifao pɛpɛɛpɛ Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ fioo daa kɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo. Kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do I need to apply chicken manure more frequently when I am farming on sandy soil compared to clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsina ŋmei afata he shii abɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ miitsu nii fe shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces that let water and plant nutrients drain away very quickly. Because sandy soil cannot hold onto food for long, you must feed your crops smaller amounts of manure more often.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ hei wuji ni nu kɛ tsei aniyenii baanyɛ atsɔ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ato niyenii be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii aha onibii lɛ shii abɔ.

english: How does using drip irrigation help my crops grow better than pouring buckets of water on them?
ga: Te drip irrigation ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni mikɛwoɔ baagi mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Drip irrigation delivers tiny amounts of water directly to the plant roots continuously throughout the day. This gentle, frequent supply ensures the plant never gets too dry or flooded, allowing it to grow continuously without stress.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa nu fioo ko baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ agbi tsɔ loo nu akahoo lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaa be fɛɛ be ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Can I spray liquid fertilizer directly onto the leaves of my vegetables, and how does it help them?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa?

english: Yes, spraying liquid fertilizer on leaves allows plants to absorb nutrients directly through tiny pores on their surface. Applying light sprays at regular intervals gives crops a quick energy boost when their roots are still small or struggling.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ oya be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo loo amɛkã shi lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keep my crops from drying out so fast?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya nɛkɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which shades the ground from the harsh sun. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, helping small crop roots stay moist for longer periods between waterings.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage plants wilt and drop leaves right after I move them from the nursery bed to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moving plants damages their tiny root hairs, making it hard for them to drink water immediately after transplanting. Giving them small amounts of water right away and shading them temporarily helps them recover without dying from shock.
ga: Tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ he kroko lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ, ni no haa ewaa akɛ aaanu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu fioo amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ ni amɛgboii kɛjɛɛɛ shoofeemɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are asking for water before they start wilting and dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miibi nu dani amɛje shishi amɛgboi ni amɛgboi?

english: You can check by pushing your finger about two inches into the soil near the base of the plant. If the soil feels dry and warm at that depth, the roots are thirsty and need a light watering right away, even if the leaves have not started wilting yet.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ aaafee 2 inches ni ooonyɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni edɔ yɛ nakai shishigbɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye shishifãi lɛ, ni ehe miihia ni awo amɛ nu fioo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ ejeko shishi egbo moŋ.

english: Why does the soil on one side of my farm look dark red while the other side is light and sandy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni fã kroko lɛ mli tse ni ŋã yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Farmland often has different soil types caused by how the land was formed over time. Darker soil usually holds more nutrients and moisture, while sandy soil drains water quickly, meaning each section of your farm may need different crops or fertilizers to grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli hei lɛ yɛ sũi srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Shi shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, nu hoɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ekolɛ oŋmɔ lɛ fãi srɔtoi lɛ baabi ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a soil survey or test, and how does it help me manage my land?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ he niiamlipɛimɔ loo kaa? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni makwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A soil test is like a doctor's checkup for your land. It identifies what nutrients your soil already has, what it lacks, and what treatments or fertilizers you need so you can feed your crops correctly without wasting money.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa tamɔ datrɛfonyo ko ni baakwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, nɔ ni ebɛ mli, kɛ tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ okwɛ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee shika.

english: Water ponding happens when the soil has heavy clay or a compacted layer beneath the surface that blocks drainage. Identifying this soil type helps you build simple drainage ditches or loosen the ground so crop roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shishigbɛ ni tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ henɔ nɛɛ ni oooyɔse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ofee nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ he tsɔne ni yɔɔ mlɛo. loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ ji koni tsei shishifãi akafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting oil palm trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmei fɔ ŋmɔ?

english: Oil palms need deep soil that holds moisture well but does not remain flooded. Checking your soil depth and drainage before planting ensures your trees grow strong roots and yield heavy fruit bunches in the future.
ga: Mu tso biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ shi nu shwieee nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ dani adu lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa ni ewo yibii babaoo wɔsɛɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my young oil palm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting quick food crops between young palms during their first two years is a good practice. It helps suppress weeds, keeps the soil covered, and provides you with food and income while waiting for the palms to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni ayeɔ oya tsei ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni emɛɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Are all plant diseases dangerous enough to destroy my entire crop harvest?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai fɛɛ yɛ oshara bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akpata miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Not all crop diseases are fatal; many plants, especially mature palms, can easily tolerate mild spots or leaf damage without losing harvest yield. Knowing which diseases are minor saves you from spending money on unnecessary chemical sprays.
ga: Jeee tsei ahe helai fɛɛ woɔ mɔ wala he gbeyei. Tsei babaoo, titri lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni eda lɛ, baanyɛ akpɛlɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo baai ni fiteɔ fioo lɛ nɔ oya ni yibiiwoo lɛ fiteee. Kɛ́ ole helai ni ji nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okafite shika yɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What causes brown spots on my palm leaves, and should I be worried about them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ baa? Ni ani esa akɛ mahao yɛ enɛ he?

english: Brown spots on leaves are usually caused by minor fungal infections or a lack of specific nutrients in the soil. On mature trees, they are rarely fatal, but checking the soil can help you fix the issue before it affects growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ anɔ Amɛfɔɔɔ gbele baa. Shi shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni osaa naagbai dani amɛná odalɛ nɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young oil palm trees spend their early years building a strong root system, trunk, and large leaves to gather energy. Once the tree reaches a mature size, it naturally shifts its energy toward producing fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei bibii yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi, tsei ashishifãi, kɛ baai agbo ni mli wa ni baabua hewalɛ naa. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ naa hewalɛ nɔ etsɔ aduawai akuu.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are missing essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is so waterlogged that the roots cannot breathe. Rain provides water, but plants still need proper soil nutrition to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which specific fertilizer my crops need?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mitsei lɛ?

english: Different crops and soil types require different plant foods. Testing your soil or looking at leaf signs allows you to choose the exact fertilizer blend—such as extra nitrogen for leaves or potassium for fruit—that your farm needs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo baai okadii lɛ akwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa, tamɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛha baai loo potassium kɛha aduawai. taakɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa lɛ

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each stalk enough room to grow strong and produce large, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa toi agboi ni tsii.

english: Too many suckers steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough strength to bear large bunches of plantain.
ga: Suckers babaoo tsɔ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ mli waa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Yam tubers grow deep underground. Making loose soil mounds makes it easy for the yam root to expand smoothly while preventing water from gathering around the tuber and causing it to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ nu ni tsiɔ naa koni ekabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboi lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They need living shade, like young plantain trees, to protect them until their roots and leaves are strong enough to withstand full heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui bibii. Koni ebu he kɛyashi shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with tiny caterpillars hiding in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. These caterpillars feed on the growing centers of maize plants, but early treatment with approved sprays or neem extracts can protect your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji. Shi tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔ lɛ he

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with yellowish-green patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties from agricultural officers keeps the farm healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni duɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why are my maize plants looking pale green and light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Light yellow leaves usually show that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crop regain its dark green color and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny roots that naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When harvested, they leave this rich soil food behind for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji akpa Amɛshiɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, often due to uneven watering during dry spells. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the fruit grow healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In hot weather, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant wilts slightly to conserve water, but usually recovers once the heat drops in the evening.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ baagbi fioo koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my crops still failing even after I spent a lot of money buying expensive fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mifite shika babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he moŋ?

english: Spending money on fertilizers alone does not guarantee a good harvest; if fertilizer is applied at the wrong time, in the wrong amounts, or during bad weather, crops cannot absorb it and the investment is wasted.
ga: Shika ni afiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ pɛ haaa ana nɔmimaa akɛ abaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, bɔ ni sa, loo kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ kɛkɛ ni shika ni akɛwo mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to buy so I do not waste my farm money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe? Bɔni afee ni okafite ŋmɔ mli shika?

english: Determining fertilizer needs depends on your soil type and crop choice; following recommended spacing and split-application guidelines ensures your crops get just enough nutrients without excess running off into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe hiamɔ nii ni atsɔɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ahalaa lɛ nɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akɛha akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ afee nɔ ko aha kɛ bɔ ni akɛbaatsu nii aha lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛjooo foi babaoo kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How does writing down my daily farm expenses help my crops perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli daa gbi lɛ ŋmalamɔ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Keeping simple records of what you buy and spend helps you plan and afford essential farm activities like weeding and pest treatment on time, preventing crop damage caused by delayed care.
ga: Nibii ni aŋmala ashwie shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Nɔ ni kɔɔ nɔ ni oheɔ kɛ nɔ ni ofiteɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua bo ni oto ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ be naa. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava yields so poor even though I spent money clearing a very large piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kwraa lɛ? Ni mikɛ shika lɛ tsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ ko ni da waa lɛ nɔ?

english: Farm size matters less than proper management; overcrowding plants, planting weak stems, or failing to weed during the first three months reduces root size regardless of land area.
ga: Okwaafoi lɛ dalɛ he ehiaaa tsɔ fe bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ tsɔ. tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni aduɔ Kɛji ajie jwɛi loo ajieee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ekɔɔɔ he eko shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods in some seasons even when I treat them the same way every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ lɛ yeɔ nakai nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Cocoa trees respond heavily to changing rainfall patterns and natural soil nutrient loss over time, requiring regular pruning and adjusted feeding to maintain consistent pod production.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni tsakeɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni fiteɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ he nii waa. Ebiɔ ni afolɔ tsei lɛ amli daa ni afee tsakemɔi yɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ mli koni pod lɛ afee nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: Why are my crop yields lower than my neighbor's farm when we both planted the same seed at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi fe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔduɔ dumɔwui komekomei yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to soil fertility variations, how deeply seeds were planted, weed competition, and how well moisture was retained in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi anɔ. Te dumɔwui ni adu lɛ mli kwɔ ha tɛŋŋ? Jwɛi ahe akaŋshii kɛ bɔ ni atoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ahaa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow after heavy rains even though I added manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can flood the roots and wash away essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach them, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afee nu ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by underground pests like nematodes or waterlogged soil, making the heavy plants easily fall under strong winds unless propped up with bamboo or wooden stakes.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Ehaa tsei ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. ja ŋmei loo tsei ahe tsei fiɔ sɛɛ

english: How can I tell if spending money on pest control sprays is actually helping my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Checking leaves regularly for reduced insect holes and comparing harvest weights from treated areas versus untreated areas shows if the chemical spray is protecting your yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ amli daa koni kooloi amli ŋmeii lɛ aba shi. kɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli tsiimɔi ni jɛ hei ni atsa kɛ hei ni atsako lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he. Etsɔɔ kɛji tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ buɔ onibii ahe.

english: How do I stop my harvested vegetables from spoiling quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ anaa koni ekafite oya dani mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Harvesting during cooler morning hours, keeping produce under shade instead of direct sunlight, and gentle handling prevent heat buildup and bruising that cause fast rotting.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli Nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ najiaŋ. Ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii blɛoo lɛ, etsĩɔ dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa oya lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and intense heat. They need shade trees or tall food crops like plantain to protect them from drying out until their root systems are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow fast. It can also happen when the soil is waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the nitrogen from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps put food back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie nitrogen fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni ekuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is wet before putting solid fertilizer on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa awo miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that crop roots can drink it up. If applied to dry soil during hot weather, the fertilizer stays concentrated and can actually burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the light and keeps them off the damp ground where rots and fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit when the daytime temperature gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes it produce only leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ haa baai pɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms. These caterpillars crawl into the central funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and moist, feeding on the new leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni eyɔɔ blɛoo ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai heei ni ayeɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that inject a virus or damage the leaves as they feed on the plant juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo efiteɔ baai beni amɛnuɔ tso mli nu lɛ

english: How do I choose the right plantain shoot to dig up and plant on new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain ni sa kɛha shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ŋmɔ kɛ dumɔ?

english: Look for a 'sword sucker'—a young shoot with narrow, sword-shaped leaves and a thick base. These establish roots much faster and grow stronger than shoots that already have wide, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘sword suckers’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ klante kɛ shishi ni mli tse. Enɛɛmɛi feɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli kwɔ momo lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil right around the base of the main stem starts to crack open from the tubers swelling beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso wulu lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni efuu ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big bushy leaves but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excess water, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, creating natural food that helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves look like someone shot small holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ mɔ ko ni etsɔ bu bibii amli lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the center funnel of the plant and chew through the leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ amli dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a germ in the soil that clogs the stem so water cannot reach the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa, ni ehaa nu shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens either because the plant is trying to save water in hot weather, or because tiny insects like thrips are sucking sap from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ejaakɛ tsei lɛ miitao ni amɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when tiny insects do not pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor nutrients, or lack of shade.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli loo kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. niyenii ni esaaa loo hulutsoo ni bɛ

english: Why do my yam vines stay weak and produce small tubers if I do not stake them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ bulbs bibii kɛji mikɛ shishifãi etswaaa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up to catch direct sunlight. Higher leaves catch more light, which gives the plant the energy needed to swell the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaná la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaving too many young shoots makes them compete with the main plantain for food and water, which results in smaller bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ plantains titrii lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops small even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds steal crop food from the soil and block sunlight, causing your crops to starve even when water is available.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nu yɛ po.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving tall trees or planting plantains around young cocoa provides living shade and moisture to help them survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo adu amɛ yɛ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baaye abua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce small harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni eji ŋmaa bibioo beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow strong and yield larger crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Is it really necessary to cut tall sticks to stake up my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni afo tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes helps them capture more sunlight to make food. It also keeps the leaves away from damp soil and pests, which leads to bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛha nihoomɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaa lɛ koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni kooloi akabote mli. Enɛ baaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right stage supplies nitrogen to keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aya hiɛ koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on my farm after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the dirt, but beans and cowpeas naturally put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating these crops keeps your soil healthy without spending as much money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it bad for me to scatter fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baashwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani ahum aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash loose fertilizer off the top of the soil into gutters and streams before your crops can absorb it. It is best to place fertilizer near the base of the plant and cover it lightly with soil when rain is mild.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni okɛha nɔ fioo kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around them for too long because the soil cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from uneven watering or sudden extreme heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo latsaa ni naa wa ni baa trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do weeds growing around my maize reduce the total amount of corn I harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi ŋmãa lɛ haa ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act like crop thieves—they steal water, light, and soil nutrients meant for your corn. Clearing weeds early gives your maize full access to those nutrients so it can produce full ears of corn.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii julɔi, amɛjuɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa o-ŋmãa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ aná nakai niyenii lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛɔ ewoɔ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are small worms eating the inside leaves of my young maize, and how do I protect my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of maize plants. Checking your farm frequently and applying recommended biological or chemical treatments early stops them before they destroy your whole crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii abɔ ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ atsu nii mra. Kpa ŋmɔji nɛɛ dani amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: How long does a grafted mango tree take before it starts giving fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango tso ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start producing fruit within 3 to 4 years, whereas trees planted directly from seed can take anywhere from 7 to 10 years to yield fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé he fɛɛ he kɛjɛ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do fruit trees like mango need so much space between them when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii tamɔ mango lɛ he hiaa ni gbɛ babaoo ahi amɛteŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Mango trees grow large root systems and wide branch canopies over time. Planting them far apart ensures they do not fight each other for underground water, soil nutrients, and sunlight.
ga: Mango tsei daa kɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ niji ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la

english: Why are the leaves on my young mango tree turning yellow and dropping off during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yellow dropping leaves are usually a sign of heat stress and lack of water. Young trees need regular watering during dry periods because their roots are not yet deep enough to search for groundwater on their own.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Ehe miihia ni afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lolo bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Is well water good for watering my farm crops during the dry months?
ga: Ani nu bu mli nu lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, well water is excellent for crops because it is full of natural ground minerals and free from industrial chemicals like chlorine, helping plants stay healthy during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo, ni tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei tamɔ chlorine bɛ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning or late in the afternoon. Cool temperatures allow plant roots to absorb the water before the hot sun evaporates it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi loo shwane. He ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep moisture in my soil longer so I don't have to water every day?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ? No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni mikɛ nu awo mli daa gbi?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or straw (a method called mulching) acts like a protective cover that slows down water evaporation from the sun.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi (gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching) shwie shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ nɔ ko ni haa nu ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why do my young crops dry up and die quickly when the rains stop for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots that stay close to the top of the ground. When the sun dries out the top surface of the soil, the roots cannot reach deeper moisture without hand watering or irrigation.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Beni hulu la lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ gĩɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ he kɛji akɛ awooo amɛ nu loo akɛ niji awooo amɛ nu.

english: How many months does it take for standard grain crops like maize to mature for harvest?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ ni akɛkpaa ŋmaa ni afɔɔ feemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Most standard maize varieties in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (about 90 to 120 days) from the day of planting to full maturity for harvest.
ga: Abɛi henɔi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edara kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make food for growth. When planted under heavy shade, they stretch upward searching for light, making them thin and easy to fall over.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha amɛdalɛ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaakpã mli kɛya ŋwɛi koni ena la. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbeeɔ shi oya

english: Why do I need to add fertilizer to my land if the soil already looks dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo?

english: Dark soil can still lack vital plant nutrients that get used up by previous crops over time. Fertilizer restores essential foods like nitrogen and phosphorus so your plants grow strong and produce well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ lolo. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around its roots. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to smaller harvests over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa yibii bibii baa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it necessary to space out my crops properly instead of planting seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aja he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong stems without competing against neighboring crops for resources.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ dalɛ ni mli wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ yɛ nibii ahe

english: How deep should I bury cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted about 5 to 10 centimeters deep in the ground, slanted or flat, so roots can spread easily and form thick tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛntimita 5 kɛyashi 10, ni ehiɛ afee ŋmei loo ŋmei. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei ni mli tse.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot afternoons is a natural defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent moisture from evaporating too quickly under severe heat.
ga: Tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu he, ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct direct sunlight. Faster-growing crops like plantains provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa plants mature.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and partial shade during very hot weather help the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow thick stems underground instead of producing seeds on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava uses underground roots as its primary storage bank to hold starch and water, allowing the crop to survive dry weather conditions and nutrient-poor soils.
ga: Cassava kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi tsuɔ nii akɛ etoohe titri ni ekɛ ŋmeii kɛ nu toɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding manure or compost help my crops survive dry hot weather better?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Compost and manure act like a sponge inside the soil, holding onto rainwater and organic nutrients so plant roots can keep feeding even when rainfall stops for a while.
ga: Kompost kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ahiɛ mli lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aya nɔ ana niyenii kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ekpa be fioo po.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting in the barn even before I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛdu shikpɔŋ po lɛ?

english: Seed yams have a natural internal cycle that wakes them up from resting when the warm season returns, signalling that conditions are right to start growing again.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni teɔ amɛ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Etsɔɔ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ ja koni eje shishi eda ekoŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off because of poor insect pollination, lack of nutrients in the soil, or water stress caused by dry weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu mli haomɔ ni shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my tiny cocoa pods turn black and dry up while they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ No hewɔ ni minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: This is often cherelle wilt, a natural process where the tree drops excess young pods it cannot feed, but it can also be caused by insect bites from pests like mirids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji cherel ŋmei. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ ashwieɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ ejɛ koolooi amɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni jɛ kooloi tamɔ pollen mli hu kɛba.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn dark brown and rot right on the trunk during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads quickly in cold, wet, damp, and overly shady farm conditions.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ tsɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do new leafy shoots keep growing out from the bottom of my cocoa tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei No hewɔ lɛ etee nɔ eda kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi.

english: These shoots are called chupons or suckers. The tree pushes them out when it seeks new growth, but they drain vital energy and nutrients away from pod production.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ chupons loo suckers. Tso lɛ tsiɔ amɛ kɛyaa he kroko kɛ́ ehe bahia ni amɛkwɛ̃ ehee. Shi amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During harmattan, dry air and hot sun dry out the soil. The cocoa tree sheds leaves on purpose to reduce water loss and survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmatta beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves look pale green instead of deep dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse shi jeee eŋɔli ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Pale leaves usually mean the soil is low on essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, or the young trees are receiving too much direct sunlight without enough shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen ni faaa, loo akɛ tso lɛ ji bibioo. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface and the top heavy fruit bunch makes the plant top-heavy, so strong winds easily uproot them if they are not staked.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee tsiimɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie shishifãi lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ tso etswaaa amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when the rainy season is too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to drown and decay underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ji oxygen lɛ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei kɛji hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a self-defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, helping the plant save moisture during the hottest hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛba he ni dɔlɛ baa lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my cocoa seedlings after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in the soil and sprout rapidly as soon as clearing exposes the soil to direct sunlight and moisture.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu la kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crops need different types of plant food instead of just one fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei niyenii srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Just like humans need a balanced diet of different foods to stay healthy, crops need a mix of nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. Giving them only one type of plant food can cause nutrient deficiencies, leaving the crop weak and producing poor yields.
ga: Taakɛ niyenii ni ja ni jɛ niyenii srɔtoi amli lɛ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛha hewalɛ kpakpa Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium hu he miihia Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ. Tso niyenii henɔ kome pɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What happens to my plants if I give them too much fertilizer at one time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli shikome?

english: Rushing to feed crops too much fertilizer at once can burn their roots and damage them. Crops grow best when fed steady, balanced amounts of nutrients over time so they can absorb what they need without getting stressed.
ga: Oya ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aha onibii lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite. Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni haomɔ ko akafee amɛ.

english: How does proper plant nutrition affect the crop after I harvest it?
ga: Te tsei aniyenii ni sa lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plants that receive balanced nutrition build stronger cell walls and store essential nutrients. This makes the harvested produce firmer, better tasting, and less likely to rot quickly during transport to buyers.
ga: Tsei ni naa niyenii ni sa lɛ maa wala yibii lɛ ahe gbogboi ni mli wa, ni amɛhiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ lɛ mli waa. E ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ ebaafite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa mɔ ni heɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do plants in the wild grow without fertilizer while my planted crops struggle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ daa ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa lɛ?

english: Wild plants grow naturally spaced out over long periods and feed on deep, undisturbed soil rich in decomposing organic matter. Planted crops grow close together and are expected to produce higher yields, which drains nutrients from the soil much faster.
ga: Koo mli tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa enaa ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egboi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaawo yibii babaoo. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya kwraa.

english: Can I use wild plants and leaves from the bush to feed my farm crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ koo mli tsei kɛ baai ni jɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ atsu nii kɛye mi okwaayeli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, leaving wild bush vegetation to decompose or turning it into compost creates natural organic matter. Adding this to your soil slowly feeds your crops balanced nutrients and helps the soil retain water naturally.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni koo mli tsei lɛ fite loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ enɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa fiofio. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do some buyers pay higher prices for crops grown using traditional, natural methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ blema kɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ lɛ jara babaoo lɛ?

english: Many specialized processors and foreign buyers prefer crops grown with natural soil management and fewer chemicals because consumers consider them healthier, safer, and better for processing.
ga: Mɛi babaoo ni feɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi kɛ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsofai fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ buɔ tsei nɛɛ akɛ amɛhe wa, amɛhi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: Why do processing companies care so much about how I treat my crops on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ susuɔ bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii mihaa lɛ he waa lɛ?

english: Factory owners and processors need crops that are consistent in size, firmness, and quality so their processing machines work smoothly and the final product lasts longer on store shelves.
ga: Mill nuŋtsɔmɛi kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ miitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni dalɛ, shifimɔ, kɛ kpakpafeemɔ yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni naagbee nibii lɛ ahi shwapoi amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to rush and harvest my crops before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ oyaiyeli baakpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops too quickly before they reach full maturity means the plant has not finished storing its natural sugars and nutrients. This results in smaller produce that spoils quickly and gets rejected by major buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii mra tsɔ, dani eshɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbeko ebɔɔ su kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa nibii bibii ni fiteɔ oya ni mɛi ni heɔ nibii wuji lɛ kpooɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I prepare my harvested crops so foreign buyers and factories will buy from me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa minikpamɔ lɛ koni majimaji ateŋ jarayelɔi kɛ nitsumɔhei ahe nii kɛjɛ midɛŋ?

english: Buyers look for clean, well-sorted produce without damage or diseases. Sorting your crops by size and removing spoiled ones ensures that processors receive high-quality raw materials suitable for processing.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ nibii ni he tse. Ahala jogbaŋŋ Ebɛ nɔ ko ni fiteɔ loo hela bɛ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amlijaa yɛ amɛdalɛ naa kɛ tsei ni efite lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ naa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: Why do crops grown in rich, natural soil stay fresh longer after harvest than crops grown quickly in weak soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni adebɔɔ mli nii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe tsei ni adu mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops grown slowly in healthy, nutrient-rich soil absorb minerals that make their outer skins and fibers stronger. This protects the harvested food from rotting quickly when stored or transported to market.
ga: tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ, ejieɔ mineral ni haa hewolo lɛ kɛ kponɔgbɛ tsɔji lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ buɔ niyenii ni akpa lɛ he koni ekafite oya kɛ́ akɛto loo akɛtee jara nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which acts like essential food for green leaf growth, or that heavy rains have washed the nutrients out of reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomatoes get dark, soft rotten spots on the bottom while still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It is caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered when soil moisture goes from very dry to very wet suddenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛtee nɔ ni mli edɔ waa nɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main crop help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and trap it in small bumps on their roots, which leaves natural fertilizer in the soil for neighboring plants to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli, ni no haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ aye.

english: Which direction should the little buds point when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The small nodes or buds on the cassava stem cutting must point upward toward the sky so the shoots can easily grow straight up while roots form underneath.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii Yɛ ŋmei nine lɛ nɔ lɛ esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ. mlɛo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shishi lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete fiercely for sunlight and stretch upward, creating thin, flimsy stems that break easily and yield smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni fãa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines to climb on tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe bahia ni maye mabua sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking raises the yam leaves toward the sun, allowing the plant to make maximum energy from sunlight which goes directly into growing large tuber roots underground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni haa shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shwereɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves, suck out the plant juices, and transmit viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi, ni amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my plantain trees turning yellow and collapsing against the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is a common sign of Panama disease or damage from stem borers (weevils) eating through the root stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Panama hela loo nɔ ni jɛɔ stem borers (ŋmei) ni yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ mli baa lɛ he okadi, ni no tsiɔ nu naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their blossoms before any small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers under stress from long dry spells, excessive heat, or when there are no tiny midges present in the soil litter to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, latsaa ni naa wa, loo be mli ni ŋmeii bibii bɛ lɛ shishi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ fɔfɔii lɛ awo mli

english: Why do my seeds rot in the soil without sprouting when I plant during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil smothers seeds by blocking oxygen, causing soil fungi to attack and decay the seeds before they have a chance to germinate.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛnaa hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Can I plant tomatoes on the same piece of land where my pepper plants are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, but you need to be careful because peppers and tomatoes belong to the same plant family. They attract the same pests and soil diseases, so if one gets sick, it can easily spread to the other. Giving them proper spacing and monitoring for pests helps them grow well together.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato jɛ tso kome mli. Amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hela mɔ mɔ kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa mɔ kroko nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛ amɛhe ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries out the pollen, preventing pollination. When a plant gets too heat-stressed, it drops its flowers to conserve energy. Providing adequate water and light shade during severe hot spells can prevent flower drop.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Tsi pollination naa Kɛji tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni fa fe nine mli lɛ Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ni akɛaaha yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: Can garden egg plants keep producing good yields if I leave them on the farm for many years?
ga: Ani ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afii babaoo?

english: Garden egg plants can survive for years, but their fruit production drops heavily after the first 1 to 2 years. As the woody stems age, the plant produces smaller, lower-quality fruits, so replanting fresh seeds every couple of seasons gives much better yields.
ga: Egg tsei ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi afii babaoo. Shi eyibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 1 kɛyashi 2 lɛ sɛɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ daa lɛ. Tso lɛ baawo yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ daa be 2-3 lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my older garden egg bushes turning small and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ eggplant tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: As crop plants age, their roots become less efficient at pulling nutrients like nitrogen out of the soil. Over time, the soil also gets depleted of plant food. Adding compost or manure around the base and pruning old branches can help, but planting new seedlings is often best.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Tsei aniyenii baaho yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baabɔle Niji momo lɛ ashishi kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and fresh air into the tree canopy helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and wilting during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots that cannot reach water deep underground, and their young leaves burn easily in full sun. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains near young cocoa protects them from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Ni ebaa bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees produce many flowers but very few actual pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between flowers. If the farm environment is too dry, or if all ground cover is cleared, midges lose their breeding ground, resulting in unpollinated flowers that drop off without forming pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei yeɔ kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli shihilɛ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ. Midge baafite he ni efɔɔ bii yɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I safely use manure from my goats and chickens on my crop fields?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ too kɛ wuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fresh animal manure is very strong and produces heat as it breaks down, which can burn crop roots. You should dry and compost the manure by mixing it with dry leaves and letting it rot for a few weeks before spreading it near your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa kɛji efite. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Esa akɛ ogbi ni okɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ nɔ ni oha egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛgbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one section of my land but poorly on another plot nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko nɔ shi ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kroko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient content change from place to place. One plot might hold water better or have more decayed leaves from past vegetation, while another plot might be stony or exhausted from previous farming.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome kɛyaa he kroko. Shikpɔŋ kome baanyɛ ahiɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Aloo baai ni miigboi ni jɛ tsei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ yɛ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ kroko baanyɛ ahi tɛi loo egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Why is crop rotation important instead of planting the same vegetable in the same soil every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni aaadu aduawai komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Changing crop types breaks pest cycles and keeps the soil balanced.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ahenɔi ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: If I plant my maize very close together, will I get a bigger harvest because there are more plants on the farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa Ani maná yibii babaoo ejaakɛ tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak plants with small or empty ears. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and light to produce full, healthy yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact stage when my pepper plants will start producing flowers after transplanting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he pɔtɛɛ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most sweet and hot pepper varieties in Ghana begin flowering between 60 to 75 days after transplanting, provided they receive adequate water and soil nutrients during their vegetative stage.
ga: Peppers ni ŋɔɔ kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 75 teŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning light yellow and staying short instead of growing tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efee kuku moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves and slow growth usually signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil or root damage from waterlogging. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color and growth vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ amɛdaramɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ efite kɛjɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli tse ni amɛdara waa.

english: Should I buy certified seed varieties from the agro-dealer or just plant the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ loo madu dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Certified hybrid or improved seeds are bred to mature faster, resist local diseases, and produce higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations, leading to uneven growth and lower harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofa ebɔ he loo ni asaa amɛhe koni amɛshwere oya. helai ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my vegetable crops even though I cleared the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe mi-aduawai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to quickly snatch available water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing early and weeding regularly during the crop's first 3 to 4 weeks prevents weeds from choking your vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛjie nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ni jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi lɛ akatsi o-vegetables lɛ naa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to trim off the lower leaves and side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai kɛ amɛsɛɛ niji lɛ?
