english: Trimming lower leaves improves airflow around the base of the plant, which keeps fungal diseases from spreading from wet soil onto leaves. It also directs the plant's food towards developing larger fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii lɛ hu gbɛ koni ewo yibii wuji yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day when the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection mechanism maize uses to prevent water loss through its leaves during high heat. If the leaves unroll in the cool evening, the plant is managing heat stress, but if they stay rolled, the soil needs irrigation or rain.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ naa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miikpe. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo lɛ Ehe miihia ni afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu loo nugbɔ anɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. Signs of maturity include lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, the main stem turning woody, and the ground around the stem base cracking as tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbɔ lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbalaa kɛji bulb lɛ mli fũu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without any shade crops around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Intercropping them with fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects the cocoa seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains du lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la babaoo.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops every time I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility by adding natural nitrogen.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tree crops so important in the history of farming here in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hiaa yɛ okwaayeli he yinɔsane mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Tree crops like cocoa and cashew have a rich history in Ghana because they act as long-term investments. Unlike seasonal crops, tree crops stabilize the soil and provide farmers with steady income for decades once mature.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ kookoo kɛ cashew nuts yɛ yinɔsane kakadaŋŋ yɛ Ghana akɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika mli. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ náa shika ni yaa nɔ daa afii nyɔŋmai abɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do tree crops behave differently from regular food crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ niyenii ni afɔɔ dumɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe?

english: Seasonal crops grow and yield within a few months, but tree crops take several years to mature. However, once a tree crop is established, it lives for decades and yields repeatedly every season without needing to be replanted.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ be mli lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi tsei aheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa. Shi, kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ, Ebaahi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ. Be fɛɛ be ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What is a greenhouse, and is it considered a new technology or just a different way of planting?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋwɛitsu? Ni ani enɛ ji ŋaalee hee loo eji gbɛ kroko kɛkɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ adaraa?

english: A greenhouse is a modern farming technology. It is a structure made with special plastic and netting that creates a protected environment for growing crops away from harsh outdoor elements.
ga: Greenhouses ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaalee. Eji nɔ ko ni akɛ plastic kɛ ŋmei krɛdɛɛ ko fee ni haa shihilɛ ni buɔ he kɛha tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ he jɛkɛɔ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ nibii ni mli wa lɛ ahe.

english: How does growing crops inside a greenhouse change the way the plants behave and grow?
ga: Te tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ tsei lɛ asu kɛ amɛdalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops inside a greenhouse grow faster and produce higher yields because they are protected from strong winds, scorching sun, heavy downpours, and destructive insect pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo yibii babaoo ejaakɛ abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: Is greenhouse farming a new practice in Ghana, or have local farmers been doing it for a long time?
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli ji nifeemɔ hee ko yɛ Ghana. Aloo okwaafoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ efee nakai be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Greenhouse farming is a relatively new modern practice in Ghana, even though it has been used for many years in other parts of the world.
ga: Greenhouse okwaayeli ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔ hee ko yɛ Ghana. Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ je lɛŋ hei krokomɛi afii babaoo moŋ.

english: Can I grow long-term tree crops like cocoa or citrus inside a greenhouse?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu afi mli tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo citrus yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli?

english: No, tree crops grow too large and deep-rooted for greenhouses. Greenhouses are best suited for fast-growing, high-value vegetables like tomatoes, sweet peppers, and cucumbers.
ga: Dabi, tso lɛ daa tsɔ ni eyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛha ŋtayaa. Greenhouses ji hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni jara wa tamɔ tomato, bell pepper, kɛ kukumba.

english: Where did greenhouse technology originally come from before reaching Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni tsɔne ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ lɛ je shishi dani eshɛ Ghana?

english: Modern greenhouse farming in dry areas originated in Israel to save water and protect crops, and it later spread to places like Australia and South Africa before being introduced to Ghana.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ je shishi yɛ Israel koni akɛbu nu he ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Sɛɛ mli lɛ, egbɛ eshwa hei tamɔ Australia kɛ South Africa. dani akɛtsu nii yɛ Ghana

english: How does a greenhouse help crops survive extreme heat and dry sun?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ greenhouses yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu ni egbiɔ lɛ mli?

english: The covering material shades the crops from harsh direct sunlight and keeps moisture around the plant, preventing the leaves from burning or drying out quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, tɛ̃ɛ he. ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso lɛ he, ni no haaa baai lɛ ashã loo amɛkagbi oya.

english: Why are modern farming practices like greenhouses becoming popular in hot countries like South Africa and Australia?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli nifeemɔi tamɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ehe gbɛi waa yɛ maji ni mli edɔ tamɔ South Africa kɛ Australia lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Farmers in hot countries use greenhouses because they allow complete control over water and temperature, enabling crops to thrive even in regions with poor rainfall or severe heat.
ga: Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ maji ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛ greenhouses tsuɔ nii ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ nu lɛ kɛ latsaa lɛ nɔ kwraa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɔɔ po.

english: How do I know if my crops would benefit more from modern greenhouse farming or traditional outdoor farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kusum nifeemɔi ni afeɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ babaoo?

english: Delicate crops like tomatoes and peppers benefit greatly from greenhouses because they are sensitive to pests and rain damage, while tough crops like cassava, yam, and tree crops grow better outdoors.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ Baaná greenhouses he sɛɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nibii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow well. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I leave dead leaves and stems on my farmland instead of burning them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai kɛ tsei ni egboi yɛ midumɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ dani madu?

english: Leaving crop residues on the land feeds the soil as it decays, retains soil moisture during dry days, and prevents heavy rains from washing away your fertile topsoil.
ga: Nibii ni adu mli nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your cassava grow better without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out to catch direct sunlight to produce food. Climbing stakes allows the leaves to get maximum light, leading to larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ naa la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on tender maize whorls. Inspecting your field early and applying ash, botanical sprays like neem, or appropriate insect treatments keeps them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ sũ lɛ atsu nii Botanical spray tamɔ neem loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Leaf curl is usually spread by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap from the plant. Controlling these pests early prevents the virus from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ eshwaa. Ni oooye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Ebaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when rainwater sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain stays trapped in the soil without draining away, the roots drown and fungal diseases take over, causing root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ekpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efooo. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it better for my garden vegetables if I water them early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the plants drink before the heat sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly before roots absorb it and can scald hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi lɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ ni amɛshã baai ni edɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant before producing any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani miwo tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets too hot, when plants suffer from irregular watering, or when bees are not available to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei naa nu ni amɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he naagbai Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in full sunlight without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that easily dry out and burn in harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates living umbrellas that shade the delicate seedlings.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hulutsoo aba ni baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ yitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tips on older bottom leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green leaves and large cobs, so applying urea or NPK fertilizer near the plant roots helps restore its green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ baa ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ ekwɛ baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ urea loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show light green or yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or through infected stem cuttings. It stops the plant from making enough food, leading to smaller tubers underground. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting helps prevent this.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa loo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Etsĩɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight and dry air. Plantains grow quickly and have wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the air moist until the young cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like waste inside the middle leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the day to feed on new leaves. Detecting them early and applying recommended pesticides or neem oil prevents them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tsei ni miida lɛ.

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot. It happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually because the soil is too dry or watering is uneven. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps stop it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Why is my harvest smaller when I plant my crops very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing them correctly gives each plant enough room and resources to produce thick stalks and large yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ato tso lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei ni mli tse ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yam vines are climbing plants that need maximum leaf surface exposed to sunlight to produce large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, reducing disease and ensuring the plant gets enough light to feed its growing tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ ni hulutsoo tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa helai baa shi ni ekwɛɔ koni tsei lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua bulbs ni miida lɛ.

english: How does putting dried animal manure on my field help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Decomposed animal manure adds organic matter to the soil, which works like a sponge to hold water during dry spells. It also slowly feeds essential nutrients to your crops without burning their roots.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛtoɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa hu haa onibii lɛ fiofio. ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ ashãaa

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out completely, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Watering your crops regularly during flowering and avoiding heavy nitrogen chemical fertilizers stops the flowers from falling.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli babaoo lɛ ahe lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients and water from the soil before your plants can reach them. Removing weeds early ensures that the water and soil food go directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otsei lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same piece of land where I am growing young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and can easily dry out under strong sunshine. Fast-growing plants like plantain provide critical shade to protect the young cocoa while also giving you food and cash harvest while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ agbɔ lɛ.

english: Does a young cocoa plant grow better in full open sunlight or under shade crops?
ga: Ani cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo shishi?

english: Young cocoa grows much better under shade crops like plantain because full sunlight overheats the plant and dries up soil moisture. Once cocoa trees mature, they require less shade and more controlled sunlight to produce abundant pods.
ga: Kookoo bibioo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ ashishi, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli dɔɔ fe nine. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli gbɛ́ɔ Beni kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa Ehe miihia ni hulutsoo be fioo kɛ hulu la ni akudɔ lɛ babaoo aba koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa babaoo aba.

english: Will planting plantains too close to my cocoa seedlings steal all the soil nutrients from the cocoa?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ mi-kokoo dumɔwui lɛ tsɔ lɛ baaju shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If you follow proper farm spacing recommendations, plantains and cocoa share soil nutrients well without fighting each other. The plantain fallen leaves actually decompose into rich organic matter that feeds the cocoa roots.
ga: Kɛji onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ gbɛ ni sa lɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ plantains kɛ cocoa baajara niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni amɛwuuuu. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: What are plantain suckers, and how do I use them to grow more crops?
ga: Mɛni ji plantain ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ amɛ atsu nii koni mikɛdu tsei babaoo?

english: Plantain suckers are small shoots that grow naturally out of the base of a mother plantain tree. You can dig them up carefully without buying new seeds and replant them elsewhere to expand your farm.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ji tsei bibii. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ shishi Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii ni okɛ dumɔwui heei aheee ni okɛdu yɛ he kroko koni okɛgbala oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do small plant shoots keep popping up around my plantain stems after I harvest the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii feɔ No hewɔ lɛ epue kɛbɔle he fɛɛ. Mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikpa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ.

english: That is the plantain plant's natural way of reproducing. After the main stem bears fruit and is harvested, the stem dies back and transfers its energy to those bottom shoots so new plantain stems can grow in its place.
ga: Nakai ji bɔ ni plantains fɔɔ bii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni tso titri lɛ wo yibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baagbo ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baaya tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ koni plantain tso heei akwɛ̃ yɛ egbɛhe.

english: How do I know when it is time to cut down old cocoa trees and replant new ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafo kookoo tso momo ni madu ehee?

english: When cocoa trees become very old, produce few pods, or suffer from heavy disease attacks, their yield drops drastically. Replanting those old sections with fresh seedlings restores high productivity to your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ egbɔ waa, ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo, loo hela ko ni naa wa mɔ lɛ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa. Dumɔwui heei ni ooodu yɛ nakai fãi momo lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take to start yielding pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Depending on the variety you plant, modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing pods in 2 to 3 years, whereas traditional varieties can take around 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni enɛ damɔ tso ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ.

english: How can I feed my family during the years before my newly planted cocoa trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ afii ni baatsɔ kookoo tsei heei ni adu lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi lɛ amli?

english: You can plant short-term food crops like plantain, cassava, or cocoyam between the young cocoa lines. These food crops mature quickly, ensuring your family has food and daily income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni heɔ be kuku tamɔ plantains, cassava loo cocoa yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ateŋ. Niyenii tsei nɛɛ daa oya. Eha oweku lɛ ná niyenii kɛ daa gbi shika dani abɔi kookoo feemɔ.

english: Can I use income from selling food crops like plantains to build a new cocoa farm without taking loans?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shika ni mináa kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ mli lɛ ama kookoo ŋmɔ hee ni mikɛ shika ko akafa?

english: Yes, intercropping allows you to sell surplus crops like plantain to cover initial costs for land preparation, nursery buying, and farm maintenance for your new cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine tamɔ plantains koni okɛwo shishijee shika ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he nyɔmɔ. Hemɔ he ni akɛkwɛɔ tsei kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ kɛha o-cacao tsei heei lɛ.

english: What makes cocoa farming a good agricultural business for me to encourage my family to join?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ agribusiness kpakpa kɛha mi koni mawo miweku lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo mli?

english: Cocoa is a reliable long-term crop that produces yearly harvests for decades once established, giving your family sustained financial security and a valuable property to pass on to younger generations.
ga: Cocoa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ewo yibii afi fɛɛ afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ kɛjɛ be mli ni ato shishi lɛ. Ehaa oweku lɛ náa shika he shweshweeshwe shihilɛ ni hiɔ shi daa, ni eji nibii ni jara wa ni esa akɛ okɛha yinɔbii ni darako lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need plantains planted next to them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are fragile and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains provide vital shade and hold moisture in the soil, acting as natural protection for young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii koni ebu cacao tso bibioo lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize plants are running out of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has left to its newer, top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya baai heei anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, it starves the roots of oxygen. Without air, the roots suffocate and become vulnerable to fungal infections that cause them to decay underground.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients repeatedly and allows pests that target maize to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas replenishes nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my harvest even if I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than your crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. If weeds are left in the field, they consume most of the crop nutrients before your plants can get to them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha otsei lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli Amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii babaoo dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants look weak and wilted during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In the heat of the day, pepper plant leaves lose water through evaporation faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing water and usually recovers as the weather cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Pepper tsei ahe baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni elaaje lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air gets too hot, water is inconsistent, or nutrients are missing. High heat prevents proper pollination inside the flower, causing the plant to drop the useless blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii bɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni baa fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Ha tsei ni fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa lɛ agbee shi

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to capture as much sunlight as possible to build large tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off damp ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni fungal helai gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ, Minɔ lɛ etee ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hatch on the leaves and feed inside the growing tip of the plant, which can stunt the stalk's growth and reduce your final yield if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ naa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ dalɛ aba shi ni eba naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up and feeling sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji mita he lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky cowpea leaves are a sign of aphids—tiny insects that cluster under leaves to suck the plant's sap. The sticky layer is liquid waste excreted by these pests, which can stunt the plant and spread plant diseases.
ga: Cowpea baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni wa lɛ ji aphids he okadi. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nu mli jwɛi ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ jieɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɛ tsei ahe helai ashwã.

english: If my farmland has been left idle and overgrown for years, why do my new crops struggle to grow right after I clear it?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ efee efolo ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ afii babaoo Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Land left untended for a long time often gets compacted and full of deep weed seeds. Simply clearing the top leaves the soil hard and deficient in quick nutrients, so crops struggle until you properly break up the soil and add compost or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ashi ni atsuuu he nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jwɛi dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ eyiɔ mli obɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa oya ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ogbalaa sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli.

english: Why do crops planted on neglected family land often turn yellow and stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ weku shikpɔŋ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves and stunted growth usually mean the soil is starved of nitrogen. Neglected land covered in wild brush consumes nitrogen quickly, leaving very little food in the ground for your new crops until you replenish it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni aku hiɛ ashwie nɔ ni koo mli tsei ehà nɔ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen oya. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo ko pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ kɛyashi obaawo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa crops need protection from strong heat and sunlight when they are small. Without larger shade trees or plantains nearby to block the direct sun, their leaves dry out and burn before their roots can establish.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la he beni amɛji bibii lɛ. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ. Amɛbaai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa dani shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural defence mechanism for maize plants. By curling their leaves during the hottest part of the day, they reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to hold on to their internal water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛha abɛi tsei. Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ahi baa lɛ mli.

english: If I plant many crops very close together on my land, will I harvest more food?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: No, planting too close causes crops to fight over water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if they had proper breathing space.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi fe kɛji akɛ he ko ni sa yɛ ni akɛmuɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive tough conditions with very deep roots. They aggressively absorb available water and fertilizers faster than cultivated crops, which is why crops need early protection through weeding.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni ama koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ waa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni abu tsei ahe mra kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow so much better on land where I previously planted beans or groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in root nodules. When the roots decay, they leave free nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without making any peppers when it gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat stress or lack of water, they shed their flowers to save energy and protect themselves from dying, sacrificing fruit production for survival.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Ehe bahia ni amɛkɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ ashã afɔle bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: This leaf curling is usually caused by cassava mosaic virus, spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant leaves from making energy, leading to small and woody tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei ahe baai anaa koni amɛkafee hewalɛ. Ewoɔ bulbs bibii ni eji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the middle of the day even when the soil still feels slightly moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ fioo lolo po.

english: On very hot days, crops lose water from their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the soil. They droop temporarily to protect themselves, but usually bounce back by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkoto shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Shi bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow even after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer is like food for plants, but applying the wrong type or putting it at the wrong time can burn the roots instead of helping. Yellow leaves can also mean the soil has too much water, which prevents the plant from breathing and taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei. Shi kɛ́ okɛwo gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo yɛ be ni ejaaa mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ amu ni amɛnáaa niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the base of the plant instead of scattering it all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe ni makɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the crop's root zone ensures the roots absorb most of the nutrients directly. Scattering it everywhere feeds unwanted weeds and wastes your money on empty soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ ateŋ babaoo tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he lɛ haa jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ náa niyenii, ni efiteɔ shika yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I spray pest chemicals in the afternoon when the sun is strong?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli?

english: Spraying chemicals in hot afternoon sun can burn the plant leaves because intense heat causes the liquid to dry too quickly and scorch the delicate tissues. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening when the weather is cooler.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ ni eshãa fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why can't I use the same chemical spray for killing weeds to also control insects on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii koni mikɛkudɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Weed killers are designed to stop plant growth, so spraying them on your crops will destroy the crop along with the weeds. Insecticides are specially made to target bugs and worms without harming the green plant tissue.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ koni ekpa tsei adalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ. Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛgbe kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni eyeee tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ awui.

english: Why does rice grow well in wet, flooded land where other crops rot and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa shwereɔ yɛ hei ni nu efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ, he ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that act like air pipes, bringing oxygen from above ground down to their submerged roots. Most other crops do not have this system, so their roots drown when left in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shishifãi ni ebote nu shishi lɛ anɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why do I need to clear and level low-lying land properly before planting rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ ni wɔfee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ jogbaŋŋ dani wɔdu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Leveling low-lying land ensures that water spreads evenly across the whole field so every rice plant gets the same amount of moisture. If the field is uneven, water pools too deep in low spots and leaves high spots completely dry.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ mlijaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Faa lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ehaa hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best suited for the soil on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops require specific soil types and moisture levels to yield well. Agricultural crop directories and extension officers help match your land's specific soil type with seed varieties bred to produce high yields in your specific area.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni anyɛ adu nibii kpakpai. Okwaayeli mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe woji kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Plants grown too close together act like children sharing a single small bowl of food. They fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving all of them weak and producing smaller harvests.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii. Beni amɛjaa niyenii yɛ tsɛnsi bibioo kome mli lɛ, amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulutsoo be lɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear and plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshinii lɛ beni mijie amɛ ni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants whose seeds lie hidden in the soil waiting for sun and rain. Because they adapt faster to rough soil conditions than farm seeds, they will quickly steal food and sunlight from young crops unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa. Dumɔwui yɛ ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni miimɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli ja ajie amɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops look weak and stunted during the dry season even if I give them light water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ miha amɛ nu ni mli jɔ po

english: Light surface watering evaporates quickly in dry heat before reaching deep roots. Without deep soil moisture, roots cannot expand to pull nutrients upward, causing the plant growth to slow down.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni mli tse lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ la ni mli egbi mli dani eshɛɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii kɛya ŋwɛi. Ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. Nitrogen helps leaves grow green and strong, phosphorus builds healthy roots, and potassium helps the plant produce flowers, fruit, and fight off diseases.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Fosforo haa shishifãi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai.

english: Why shouldn't I give my crops all their fertilizer at once right after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-fertilizer lɛ fɛɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Giving all the fertilizer at once can burn the tender plant roots or get washed away by heavy rains before the crops can use it. Feeding them in stages over several months ensures nutrients are available when the plants need them most.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ahoɔ amɛ dani tso lɛ kɛtsu nii. Niyenii ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli Yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli lɛ, enɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa amɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops need extra potassium when they are older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ potassium babaoo he hiaa mi tsei lɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Potassium is essential for the later stages of plant growth. It helps transport sugars and water into developing fruits, making them larger, sweeter, and heavier before harvest.
ga: Potassium he miihia waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ sugar kɛ nu yaa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ. Ha amɛfee wuji, amɛhe afee fɛo, ni amɛhe afee shwiili dani okpa amɛ.

english: How far away from the main stem should I place fertilizer when applying it to my crop?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem near the edge of the plant's leaf canopy. Putting it directly against the main stem can burn the plant tissue, while placing it slightly away reaches the active feeding roots.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee inchi 2-3, ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, okɛto he ko ni kɛ tso ni akɛhaa lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: How long will I have to wait from the day I plant pineapple suckers until harvest time?
ga: Kɛjɛ gbi ni aduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Pineapples grow very slowly compared to crops like maize or vegetables. It usually takes about 12 to 14 months (around a full year) for a pineapple plant to grow, flower, and fully mature a fruit.
ga: Pineapple daa blɛoo waa kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 14 (aaafee afi muu fɛɛ) dani ŋmei tso ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why does a pineapple plant take a whole year to grow just one fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afi muu fɛɛ dani ŋmei kome pɛ baakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pineapples have thick, tough leaves designed to save water. They build up energy very slowly in their stem over many months before they have enough stored food to produce a single heavy, sweet fruit.
ga: Pineapple yɛ baai ni mli tse ni wa ni afee koni ekɛbu nu he. Amɛbua hewalɛ naa fiofio waa yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli nyɔji babaoo dani niyenii ni ato ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai kome ni ŋɔɔ ni tsii aba.

english: Why do pineapple farmers spray chemicals on their crops several months after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii okwaafoi lɛ shwieɔ tsofai amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ beni amɛdu lɛ?

english: Pineapples are often sprayed with special hormone chemicals several months after planting to force all the plants in the field to flower at the exact same time, allowing the farmer to harvest everything together later.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei nɔ nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ koni enyɛ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli, ni enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkpaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: What happens if I apply chemical fertilizers or sprays when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo shwie nɔ lɛ fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so roots can take them in. Applying them to dry soil can cause the concentrated chemicals to sit on the roots and burn them instead of helping the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ata shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛshã amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaye amɛbua tso lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my plants are missing important food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When plants lack essential nutrients, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, their growth slows down, or their leaves get dark spots and dry edges.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo Aloo baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi.

english: Why do some of my crops drop their flowers before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plants drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, attacked by small pests, or lacking key nutrients like potassium and boron that give the plant strength to hold onto developing fruits.
ga: Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutuaa amɛ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ boron ni bɛ mli lɛ No haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and heat. Without temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees, the leaves scorch, lose water quickly, and turn yellow due to solar stress.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, Baai lɛ baashã. nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I drop four or five maize seeds inside the same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole creates fierce competition among the seedlings for soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stems and very small or poorly filled cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa dumɔwui ateŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛhiɛɛɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves inside the center whorl of my young maize plants torn and full of holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli etse ni eyɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: This ragged leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl deep into the central growing tip of the maize plant and eat the tender unrolled leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni jieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass and lift up wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ ni mawo tsei anɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb upward to spread their leaves to capture sunlight, which supplies energy to swell the tuber underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp soil to prevent leaf rotting diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. ni ji hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa lɛ akafite.

english: Which specific part of a cassava stem should I choose to cut into stakes for planting?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã esa akɛ mafolɔ miwo tsei amli koni madu?

english: You should use the mature middle portion of a healthy stem that is about as thick as a finger with visible, healthy buds. The soft green top breaks down easily, while the very base is too woody and slow to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee inchi kome ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni wa ni anaa lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda lɛ atsu nii. Tsobii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fãa oya. Shishitoo lɛ ji tso tsɔ ni edaa fiofio.

english: Why do the lower, older leaves of my maize turn yellow from the leaf tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ baa lɛ mligbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts on older leaves usually signals a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant starves for nitrogen and pulls whatever is left from its bottom leaves to support new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli ni egbalaa nɔ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛfi ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the ground around vegetable stems with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It keeps the topsoil cool under hot sun, stops water from evaporating quickly out of the dirt, reduces weed growth, and gradually breaks down into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good for my farm if I plant groundnuts or beans in between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has beneficial soil bacteria on its roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer that feeds both the legumes and nearby crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cut away the small young shoots popping up around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii bibii lɛ? ni daa kɛbɔleɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) creates too much competition for water and soil nutrients. Trimming them off leaves energy concentrated in the main mother plant so it can form a large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii ni fe nine aba kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Tso ni afoɔ lɛ haa hewalɛ baa tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Koni ebatsɔ plantains akuu agbo ni tsii

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants drying up and falling off before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant undergoes environmental stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil conditions, or a sudden lack of water during flowering, which triggers the plant to shed flowers to protect itself.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni faaa trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that protects them from harsh heat and preserves moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii woɔ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow from the middle outward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni midu lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, so applying nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure near the roots helps the leaves turn green again and support grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when I plant them in the ground?
ga: Kɛji oodu shikpɔŋ lɛ, gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei niji lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should usually be planted about one meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space ensures their underground roots have plenty of soil room to expand into large tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ, amɛnáa shikpɔŋ babaoo ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the dirt from direct heat so water doesn't evaporate quickly. It keeps root systems cool and moist, prevents weed seeds from growing, and slowly breaks down into rich manure for the crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nu lɛ shwieee oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to breathe just like human lungs need oxygen. When floodwater sits on a field for days, it smothers the roots, causing cassava tubers to drown and rot underground.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Taakɛ bɔ ni adesa fɛ̃i he hiaa oxygen lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Be ni nu afua lɛ mli nui lɛ hi ŋmɔji lɛ amli gbii babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ nu. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside maize is very beneficial. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize while allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, obaanyɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Continuous planting of maize on the same spot consumes the same key nutrients over and over until the soil becomes exhausted. Rotating maize with crops like legumes or cassava allows the soil to rest and replenish different nutrient reserves naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii titri kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii shii abɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in the leaves and center funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Small holes and ragged damage on young corn leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These insects hide inside the central leaves of the plant during the day and eat the soft growing leaves, which can stunt crop growth if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni miida Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso lɛ dalɛ naa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant feels stressed by severe heat, lack of consistent watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining regular watering schedules and using balanced plant food helps the flowers stay on the stem and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tso niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi tso lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ tomatoi lɛ ama shi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the tiny side shoots from my tomato stems while they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Eko jɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Removing side shoots, called suckers, prevents the tomato plant from wasting energy on growing excess leaves and small branches. Trimming them directs the plant's water and food toward developing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, no haaa tomato tso lɛ afite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa ni fa fe nine kɛ niji bibii lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa tso lɛ yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when they get too much direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛɔ ohe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like young human babies—their leaves burn easily under full sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantain or shade trees around them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and soil moist while the cocoa establishes root systems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei krokomɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kookoo feɔ shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ko.

english: Why is covering the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves good for them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hi kɛha tsei lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, works like a blanket for the soil. It stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. When soil lacks nutrients or becomes waterlogged from heavy rain, the plant cannot feed properly, causing its lower leaves to turn yellow from the tips inward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji niyenii he foomɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha nu eyi mli obɔ. Tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. They act like natural fertilizer factories, feeding the soil so that your maize can grow stronger without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔhe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni o-abele lɛ ada waa ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know which direction to put cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole he ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds or raised bumps along the cassava stick; these are the eyes. Always plant the stick with these eyes pointing upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight up easily without wasting energy trying to turn around.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii, loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ ni yɔɔ yucca tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛɛmɛi ji hiŋmɛii lɛ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tso nine lɛ ama shi ni ohiŋmɛii akwɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ oya ni amɛfiteee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsake amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall sticks and build stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ amli ni matswa tso kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food that feeds the tubers growing under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet soil into the sunlight, which prevents leaf rot and helps the plant build large, healthy yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ afite ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: If too many young shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, allowing the main stem to grow large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ, single main trunk Nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu baatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ ŋmeii akuu agbo ko ni he wa.

english: Why are there small holes and caterpillar waste inside the center funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of the maize plant where it is safe from sun and birds. Finding them early allows you to spray or apply ash directly into the funnel before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Eji he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe. Taomɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ sũ afɔ loo okɛ sũ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ dani efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted like dried tea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ tii baai ni egbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves and passing small plant viruses. Controlling these tiny insects early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai bibii amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. kooloi bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but then the flowers drop off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant gets stressed from irregular watering. When heat or dry spells shock the plant, it drops flowers to save its strength until growing conditions get better.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be lɛ ha tso lɛ he fee lɛ yaa lɛ, ashwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing in the lower leaves of maize usually indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is a mobile nutrient, so the plant moves available nitrogen from older leaves to feed newer top growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow from the tip inward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmei baa lɛ shishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaagbee mli kɛyaa mli.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing large green leaves but failing to form tight heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head mainly due to excess nitrogen fertilizer or high temperatures. Too much nitrogen forces the plant to focus purely on leaf expansion rather than wrapping into a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji nyɛŋ afee yitso, titri lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine loo hulutsoo ni naa wa hewɔ. Nitrogen babaoo baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ pɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo yitso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but most of them drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed a large percentage of their flowers to manage energy. However, excessive drop is caused by dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of natural pollinators like midges in the farm.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛkwɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, hɔmɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ shwiemɔ ni fe nine baa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ midges ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ bɛ.

english: If my cassava plants start flowering, does that mean the tubers underneath are ready for harvest?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Flowering in cassava is part of its natural stem growth cycle and does not indicate tuber maturity. Tubers mature based on the variety's age timeline—usually between 9 to 12 months—regardless of when flowers appear.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cassava mli lɛ fata adebɔɔ mli tso lɛ dalɛ he. ni etsɔɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ daraa amɛhaa. Bulb lɛ daa be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ daraa lɛ—bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ—ni be ni fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers and small fruits right after they form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ miifite lɛ? Beni ato lɛ sɛɛ

english: Pepper plants shed flowers and young fruit when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to push foliage growth over fruit retention.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛha amɛyibii lɛ afee blɛoo kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha amɛhao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli fe bɔ ni ekwɛɔ aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: My tomato leaves are curling upwards and twisting tightly. What is happening to my crop?
ga: Akɛ mi tomato baai lɛ shwie shi ni atsɔ mli shiŋŋ. Mɛni ba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by whiteflies. It can also be a reaction to heat stress and low soil moisture as the plant tries to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. Ekolɛ ebaafee nɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni baa shi lɛ mli baa hu beni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up and dying early before the rainy season is even over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ?

english: Premature drying of yam vines is usually caused by yam anthracnose, a fungal disease favored by wet conditions, or by root knot nematodes damaging the underground root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ loo kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does a purple-flowered weed keep growing right next to my maize stalks and making the maize weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ko ni fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miikwɛ̃ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Mi ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ?

english: That weed is Striga (witchweed). It is a parasitic plant that attaches its roots directly to your maize roots, stealing water and vital nutrients before it even emerges above the soil.
ga: Nakai jwɛi lɛ, ni ji striga (abɛi jwɛi) lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa dani amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why does my plantain mat produce so many suckers, and should I leave all of them to grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ maha amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee ekome kɛdara?

english: Plantains naturally shoot up multiple suckers to propagate. You should not leave them all, as they will compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, leading to smaller bunches. It is best to prune and leave only 2 or 3 suckers of different ages.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantains lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii babaoo koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Esaaa akɛ oshiɔ amɛ fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa ni oshi ŋmeii 2 loo 3 pɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi.

english: Why do my maize plants easily fall over during heavy rains or wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo ahum ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falling over (lodging) happens when root systems are weak or shallow, when plants are sown too close together, or when stem borers hollow out the base of the stalk.
