ga: Abɛi ni shwieɔ shi (lodging) lɛ baa kɛji shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. Beni adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo be mli ni stem borer worms lɛ tswa tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every year even though I plant the exact same crop on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops take specific nutrients out of the soil every season to grow. When you plant the same crop repeatedly without resting the land, rotating crops, or adding manure, the soil runs out of those key nutrients, making the crops weak and lowering your harvest.
ga: Tsei heɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsakeee, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, nakai niyenii titrii lɛ faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehaa onibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to make green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes the food away from the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha niyenii je tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt left inside the top of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by leaf-eating caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the central funnel of the plant, eating the soft young leaves and leaving behind their droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do heavy weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal food, sunlight, and water directly from your crops. When weeds surround a young crop, they choke its growth and leave very little nutrients in the soil for the crop.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ Amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa ni amɛshiɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, hot sun. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, overhead to protect them from the harsh heat until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch sunlight, which feeds the growing tuber beneath the soil. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet ground, preventing rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ ŋmei du ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very helpful. Groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, which feeds the soil and helps the maize grow better.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the early rains are unpredictable?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ?

english: It is safest to wait until the soil stays continuously moist for a few days after a heavy rain before planting. Sowing after just one light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ dani odu. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo ko pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting under the ground if I do not harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mikpaaa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains soak the soil for too long, water fills all the air spaces around the roots. Without air, the cassava roots suffocate and become vulnerable to waterlogged soil rot caused by fungi and bacteria.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyɔɔ oshara mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔle he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of beneficial insects like bees needed to shake the pollen inside the flower to form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kɛji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I keep tall shade trees on my cocoa farm instead of clearing all of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni mafo tsei lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Tall shade trees shield young and mature cocoa from harsh direct sunshine and hot winds, keeping the farm cooler and helping the soil hold onto moisture so the cocoa plants do not dry out.
ga: Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii kɛ mɛi ni eda lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni kookoo tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: What is an 'Indian tree' and how does planting it help my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘India tso’ ni te edumɔ yeɔ ebuaa mi kokoo lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Indian tree' is a local name often used for fast-growing shade trees like Gliricidia. Planting them provides quick, soft shade to protect cocoa leaves from sun damage while improving soil health.
ga: India tso’ ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni bei pii lɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ glicidia. Nibii ni adu lɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa oya, ni ebuɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ hu yaa hiɛ.

english: How much shade do my cocoa plants actually need to stay healthy?
ga: Mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hulutsoo be enyiɛ he hiaa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa plants need moderate shade—about 40% to 50% cover—to protect them from sunburn, but too much heavy shade can block sunlight needed for pod production and encourage fungal diseases.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be ni sa (aaafee 40% kɛyashi 50% ni haa hulu lɛ tsoɔ amɛ). Shi hulutsoo babaoo baanyɛ atsĩ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha pod feemɔ lɛ naa ni ewo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ.

english: Can I plant any type of tree on my farm to shade my cocoa, or are some trees harmful?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ? Aloo tsei henɔi komɛi yɛ ni yɔɔ oshara?

english: Not all trees are good; some compete heavily with cocoa for water and nutrients or attract pests. It is best to use recommended shade trees like leguminous species that drop leafy mulch and enrich the soil.
ga: Jeee tso fɛɛ tso hi. Kookoo henɔi komɛi kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai loo koni amɛgbala kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo mli, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that cannot handle full sunlight, causing them to lose water faster than they can absorb it from the ground.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are receiving too much direct sunshine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ?

english: Cocoa getting too much sun usually has yellowish or scorched brown leaves, drops its leaves prematurely, and shows slow growth due to heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ waa lɛ baa yɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni eshã. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛdaraa blɛoo yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Does shade from trees protect my cocoa plants completely during the dry season?
ga: Ani tsei ahe hulutsoo buɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Shade helps reduce heat stress and keeps the soil cool, but it cannot do everything; cocoa trees may still need proper weed control, mulching, and care to survive long dry spells.
ga: Shade haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shi enyɛŋ efee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ, awo amɛmli ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lolo koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: If I have good shade trees protecting my cocoa, do I still need to spray for diseases?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛbaabu kookoo lɛ he. Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ hela nɔ lolo?

english: Yes, because shade trees only protect against sun exposure; they do not prevent pests or fungal problems like black pod disease, which actually thrive if moisture is trapped under the canopy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa pɛ. Amɛbuuu he kɛjɛɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela, ni baanyɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ he.

english: Besides protecting my crop from the sun, what else do shade trees do for my soil?
ga: Kɛfata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ebuɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ he lɛ, Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Shade trees drop leaves that rot and turn into rich organic fertilizer, and their roots help pull water and nutrients from deep in the ground up to where cocoa roots can reach.
ga: Shade tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai ni egboi lɛ amɛshwieɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo. Ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ kɛyaa he ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Will planting shade trees reduce the total amount of cocoa pods my farm can produce?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ aba shi?

english: Properly managed shade trees improve overall cocoa plant health and lifespan, but if shade becomes too thick, you must prune tree branches so sunlight can still reach the cocoa flowers and pods.
ga: Shade tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha kookoo tso lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ koni hulu la lɛ anyɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lolo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the bigger trees on my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, sensitive leaves and shallow roots. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to protect them from the harsh sun and to keep the soil moist until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Amɛmiitao hɔnɔ kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ aaawa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around them for too long in heavy rain. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay firm.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni eha yitso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds in dry ground weeks before the main rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ otsii komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Seeds left in dry soil for a long time can get eaten by insects and birds or get damaged by ground heat. Waiting until the first major rains arrive ensures the seeds sprout quickly and evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, kooloi kɛ okpoi baanyɛ aye amɛ loo dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Kɛ́ wɔmɛ kɛyashi klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu lɛ baaba lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant three or four maize seeds together in the same single hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and small, poorly filled ears of corn.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmãa toi ni ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants droop down during hot afternoons but look normal in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shi etamɔ nɔ ni eji nɔ ni sa leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Drooping is their natural way of reducing water loss, and they recover once the sun cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or when bees are not available to pollinate them. Consistent watering and partial shade during extreme heat helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to survive easily in local soil. They quickly steal sunlight, water, and nutrients away from your crops, which is why early weeding gives your crops the advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe oya koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji anɔ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called black pod disease, which spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Pruning excess tree branches lets sun and air flow through the farm to dry out moisture and protect the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli Afolɔ tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ebu ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main parent plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It stops the plant from making food properly, leading to very small roots. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems and pulling up affected young plants.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa kwraa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu kɛ tsei bibii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the small cocoa pods on my trees turning black and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in damp, dark conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra branches to let air and sunlight reach the trunk and removing infected pods helps keep the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Afoɔ tso lɛ mli nibii krokomɛi koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do I stop caterpillars from eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmeii ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the growing center of the plant. Applying ash, clean sand, or recommended neem-based pesticides into the central leaves early in the morning destroys the worms before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ sũ, ŋã ni mli tse, loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛ neem fee lɛ awo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ baakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to save water when the sun is too hot. Shrinking their leaf size prevents water from evaporating into the air, helping the plant stay alive until cooler evening temperatures arrive.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he kɛji hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ baashɛɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much chemical fertilizer. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during peak afternoon heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily before the bananas are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani banana lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by tiny worms in the soil called nematodes or by stem borers. Supporting your fruiting plantain trees with strong wooden poles prevents the wind from knocking them over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fi dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa amɛ shi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess rain floods the soil and pushes out all the air roots need to breathe. Heavy rains also wash essential plant nutrients deep into the ground where root systems cannot reach them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ ni he hiaa shishifãi lɛ koni amɛmu lɛ ashwieɔ shi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive in harsh conditions, so they absorb water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food your crops need to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I tell under the soil if my yams are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaya shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell yams are ready to harvest when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow and dry out. This shows that the plant has finished sending energy down into the tuber.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ sweet potato efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsɔɔ akɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa yitso lɛ naa.

english: Why does changing the type of crop I plant on my plot each season give me better yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ ahenɔi ni mitsakeɔ lɛ haa yibii kpakpai baa lɛ?

english: Planting different crops breaks the life cycle of soil pests and diseases that target only one crop type. It also balances soil nutrients, as some plants consume nitrogen while others, like beans, put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kwɛɔ tso henɔ kome pɛ nɔ lɛ ashihilɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei komɛi kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear my land several months before I actually start planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo dani mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing land early gives the cut bush and vegetation enough time to dry out and break down, which adds nutrients back into the soil and prevents old weeds from immediately choking your young crops.
ga: He lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei ni afo lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbi ni amɛkumɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi jwɛi momoi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ trukaa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant immediately after cutting down fresh trees and bush on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo sũ tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting too quickly can harm your crops because decaying green plants draw nitrogen out of the soil to break down, leaving your new seedlings weak, yellow, and starved of food.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei eŋɔli ni miifite lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfite. Enɛ haa dumɔwui heei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: How long should I leave cut grass and brush to dry on the field before tilling or planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni afo ni atsɔ mli lɛ ni egbi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani matsu nii loo madu?

english: Leaving cut bush to dry for about two to three consecutive months allows it to rot or burn completely, which kills pests and weed seeds hiding in the foliage before your crop goes into the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ koni amɛgbi nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi loo amɛshã kwraa. Egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ dani onibii lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ.

english: Why must I wait for the soil to rest after clearing thick bush before planting cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ beni ajie jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ dani adu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Waiting allows the underground root systems of old weeds to die off completely, making the soil softer and cleaner so your crop roots can spread easily without competition.
ga: Mɛɛmɔ baaha jwɛi momo lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbo kwraa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehe tseɔ. Enɛ haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: What is the reason for wrapping a piece of plastic or rubber tightly around a tree stem after joining two branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ plastic loo rɔba abɔle tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ beni akɛ niji enyɔ lɛ ebɔ he lɛ?

english: The rubber wrapping holds the two plant parts tightly together so they can heal into one tree, while keeping moisture inside and preventing rain or pests from rotting the fresh cut.
ga: Rɔba ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ekome. tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni akɛfee ekome jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni anyɛ akwɛ amɛ tamɔ tso kome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli, ni ehaa nugbɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ aniji heei lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tie a plastic bag filled with moist soil around a living branch on a fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi fĩɔ plastic kotokui ni sũ ni mli edɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛbɔleɔ tsei niji ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ aduawai tsei anɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: This practice, called air-layering or marcotting, tricks the branch into growing roots inside the wet soil while still on the tree, giving you a new strong seedling to cut off and plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli loo marcotting. Enɛ ji koni akɛlaka tsei niji lɛ koni amɛwo shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni obaanyɛ ofolɔ ni odu.

english: Why do farmers put clear rubber or plastic sheets over small nursery seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ rɔba loo plastic ni mli tse woɔ dumɔwui bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: The rubber or plastic traps heat and moisture around the young plant like a mini-greenhouse, protecting delicate seedlings from drying out in the harsh sun.
ga: Rɔba loo plastic tsɔnei ni bɔleɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Tso bibioo lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli.

english: How does wrapping black rubber tape around budded branches help cocoa or mango trees grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ akɛ rɔbɔt diŋ fĩ tso nine he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua cacao loo mango tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: The rubber tape seals the delicate new bud against hot air and rain, ensuring the high-yielding branch fuses properly with the root stem so the tree produces fruit much faster.
ga: Rɔba tɛp tsiɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei niji ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ kɛ shishifã lɛ feɔ ekome jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ woɔ yibii oya kwraa.

english: Why is wet dirt or moss wrapped inside plastic when trying to make a tree branch grow roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ plastic fɔ̃ɔ muji loo ŋmɔtɔ nɔ kɛ́ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni aha tso nine ko akwɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: The plastic wrapper prevents the sun from drying out the dirt, giving the branch the continuous moisture it needs over several weeks to sprout healthy new roots.
ga: Plastic ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa hulu lɛ haaa muji lɛ agbi. Ha niji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo koni ewo shishifãi heei hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why can't I just tie a grafted branch with regular cloth or rope instead of using rubber or plastic wrap?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ anyɛɛɛ akɛ mama loo kpã folo akpɛtɛ tso niji ni akɛwo mli lɛ he yɛ rɔba loo plastic najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cloth and rope let air in and allow water to evaporate, which dries out the cut stem and kills the graft before the two plant parts have time to join together.
ga: Mama lɛ kɛ kpãa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso ni afo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ dani tso lɛ fãi enyɔ lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛtsaa amɛhe.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizer ruin or poison my soil in the long run?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baafite loo ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Fertilizers are not poison; they are simply concentrated food for plants. Soil only gets damaged when fertilizer is overused or applied incorrectly over many years without adding organic matter.
ga: Fertilizer jeee poison. Eji niyenii ni mli wa kɛha tsei kɛkɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ pɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine loo yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ afii babaoo ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he.

english: Why do my crop leaves look burnt after I spray them with pest chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Chemicals burn leaves when the mixture is too strong, applied in direct hot sunlight, or used incorrectly. Following exact measurement guidelines prevents crop injury.
ga: Tsofai lɛ baashã baai lɛ kɛ́ nɔ ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ Susumɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni akapila ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it safe for my family to eat crops right after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Every chemical needs a specific waiting period after spraying so the crop can break down the medicine safely before harvest. Eating crops too soon after spraying causes health risks.
ga: Tsofai fɛɛ biɔ be krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛbaamɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akumɔ tsofa lɛ mli shweshweeshwe dani akpa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ayeɔ mra tsɔ beni afɔse tsofa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he osharai baa.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to give my crops so I don't kill them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mikɛbaahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikagbe lɛ?

english: Crops need exact portions just like people. Measuring fertilizer with standardized cups or caps rather than guessing ensures plants get fed without getting burned.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia nibii komɛi tamɔ gbɔmɛi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kɔɔpoo loo nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ susu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe moŋ fe ni ooosusu he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛye nii ni amɛshãaa.

english: Can I mix different farm chemicals together in one spray tank to save time?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli lɛ afutu. afee ekome yɛ spray tanki kome mli koni akɛ be akafite?

english: Not all chemicals work well together. Combining wrong chemicals can ruin their power, clog your sprayer, or create a mixture that damages your crops.
ga: Jeee tsofai fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsofa lɛ hewalɛ naa. Sprayer lɛ efo. Aloo feemɔ nibii ni baanyɛ afite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Applying fertilizer early in the morning or late afternoon when temperatures are cool helps plants absorb nutrients better without heat stress.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ leebi loo shwane mli Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ ni hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my farm right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from plant roots into rivers and gutters before crops can feed on it, wasting your money.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa faai kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: How does fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and healthier?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Fertilizer refills the soil with essential nutrients that crops consume as they grow, helping them build strong roots, healthy leaves, and bigger fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyiɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni wa, kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even after I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves happen when crops receive the wrong type of fertilizer, when fertilizer is placed too close to roots, or when soil is too dry for roots to take up nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baa kɛji tsei lɛ nine shɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa nɔ. Beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Is fertilizer really necessary if my crops are already growing fine on their own?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia diɛŋtsɛ kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ miida jogbaŋŋ momo?

english: Even good soil loses its strength over time as crops harvest nutrients. Adding fertilizer keeps soil fertile so crop yields stay high season after season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ po hewalɛ baaje edɛŋ yɛ be ni sa mli, ejaakɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow very well in some parts of Ghana but struggle in other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana hei komɛi lɛ? Shi yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need specific environmental conditions to thrive, including deep rich soil, high humidity, warm temperatures, and steady rainfall. Regions that are too dry or have thin, sandy soil cannot support healthy cocoa growth.
ga: Cacao tsei biɔ shihilɛ pɔtɛɛ ko dani amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ fata he. kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa Hei ni egbi tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni mli tse Enyɛŋ eye ebua kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Can I plant cocoa on land where I previously farmed cassava or maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, but heavy feeding crops like cassava exhaust the soil. You should replenish nutrients with organic manure or compost and plant shade trees before putting your cocoa seedlings into the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi tsei ni awoɔ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afata he. ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ dani akɛ kookoo dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: If cocoa grows well in a nearby district, does that mean it will automatically perform well on my farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not always. Microclimates and soil conditions change quickly. Soil depth, water drainage, shade cover, and rainfall timing can vary even over short distances.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi tsakeɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, shade, kɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake yɛ gbɛ kukuji po amli.

english: Why does the price I get for my cocoa beans change from time to time even when my yield is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ jara tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi moŋ?

english: Cocoa prices fluctuate based on global market supply, world demand, local buying policies, and currency changes rather than just the amount of cocoa you harvest on your own farm.
ga: Cocoa jara tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni akɛhaa yɛ jeŋ jarayelihe lɛ naa. je lɛŋ nibii ni ataoɔ Kuu lɛ mli nihɔɔmɔ he mla kɛ shika tsakemɔi Jeee kookoo abɔ ni okpaa yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ pɛ.

english: How can I protect my income when global cocoa prices go down during the harvest season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishika he kɛji jeŋ muu fɛɛ kookoo jara ba shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: You can plant food crops like plantains, cassava, or fruit trees alongside your cocoa. Diversifying your farm ensures you have other produce to sell when cocoa market prices fall.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava loo aduawai tsei yɛ kookoo masɛi. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii srɔtoi ni ooofee lɛ haa onáa nibii babaoo ni okɛbaatsu nii. Hɔɔ be mli ni kookoo jara lɛ ba shi lɛ.

english: How long will it take after planting a young cocoa seedling before I harvest my first pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties begin bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties take around 4 to 5 years to start producing.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How many years can one cocoa tree keep bearing fruit for me if I take good care of it?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kookoo tso kome baawo yibii eha mi kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A cocoa tree can remain productive for 25 to 30 years or more with proper pruning, weed management, and soil fertilization.
ga: Kookoo tsei baanyɛ awo yibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ. jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa

english: Why is cocoa considered a long-term investment compared to growing vegetables or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ akɛtoɔ aduawai loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Unlike vegetables that must be planted every season, cocoa is a perennial tree crop. Once established, it provides a recurring annual harvest for decades without the cost of replanting every year.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ aduawai ni ehe hiaa ni adu daa be lɛ he. Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Kɛji ato shishi pɛ lɛ Abaakpa lɛ daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni shika ni akɛbaadu ekoŋŋ daa afi lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The hot, dry Harmattan winds pull moisture from the plant. Cocoa trees naturally drop some of their leaves to save water and protect their trunk and roots until the rainy season returns.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifã lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, or overgrown shade conditions. Pruning extra shade branches lets in sunlight and prevents the fungus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, hei ni edɔ, loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ babaoo lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli ni aaafolɔ babaoo lɛ baaha amɛná hulu la ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do I have to put wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso tso fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high up into sunlight to make food. Leaving vines on the hot ground exposes them to soil diseases and reduces the size of the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha sũ mli helai aba amɛnɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and grow tall. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do people say planting cowpea or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving free natural plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ sɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains drown the soil without proper drainage, the roots suffocate, allowing waterlogged bacteria to cause decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ nu mli lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets too hot or when the soil lacks water. The plant sheds flowers to save energy so it can survive the dry heat.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ shwane mli tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be ni mli egbi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop in the afternoon but stand up fresh in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi fresh yɛ leebi?

english: In hot heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the dry ground. The plant droops on purpose to hide from the sun and conserve moisture until the cool night allows it to refill.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei gboiɔ kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ amɛbaatee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ baaha nu lɛ aba mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that drink the plant's juices and spread plant viruses, stopping leaf growth and fruit production.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Ehaa baai lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: A seed carries only a tiny amount of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its food trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ baaye niyenii lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ waa lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani hulu la lɛ baashɛ amɛhe.

english: Weeds act as greedy neighbors; their aggressive roots steal water, sunlight, and soil food directly away from your crops, leaving your plants starving and weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Eshishifãi ni boteɔ mli lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or go moldy when I stack the sacks inside my spare room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛ kotokui to shĩa ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize carries hidden moisture inside its kernels. When packed tightly inside a room without proper airflow, the trapped heat and dampness create an ideal environment for mold to spread and insects to multiply rapidly.
ga: Abele ni akpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko mli jogbaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baafa oya.

english: How can I tell if my corn is dry enough to store without it rotting later?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni sɛɛ mli lɛ efiteee?

english: You can test maize by pressing a kernel with your thumbnail or biting it; if it feels hard, makes a sharp cracking sound, and leaves no dent, the water content is low enough for safe long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni ooonyɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmãa bibioo lɛ nɔ loo okɛ ŋmãa lɛ atswa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji enuɔ he waa Gbee ko ni tswaa. ni ŋmeii bɛ mli Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee bibioo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are tiny beetles eating my stored corn even though the grain looked completely clean when I put it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse kwraa beni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, invisible eggs inside the maize kernels while the crop is still in the field. Once you harvest and bag the warm corn, those eggs hatch into beetles that eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. ni anyɛɛɛ ana yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa ni mli edɔ lɛ ni okɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do some farmers use special airtight bags instead of regular woven sacks to store their harvested grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ vacuum kotokui krɛdɛɛi tsuɔ nii yɛ kotokui ni akpɛɔ daa lɛ najiaŋ kɛtoɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Airtight bags seal out air completely, which suffocates any insects or eggs hidden in the grain and prevents mold from growing, protecting your harvest without using chemical powders.
ga: Vacuum bag lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa kwraa. Enɛ baaha kooloi bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni otsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ Buu onibii ahe ni okɛ tsofa powda tsuuu nii.

english: Why does my maize produce huge, overflowing yields in some seasons but very small ears in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ bei komɛi amli shi ewoɔ toi bibii kwraa yɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Maize is very sensitive to water and soil food right when it flowers. Good rains and proper nutrients during that critical week produce full, heavy ears, while dry weather causes the plant to produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Abɛi nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he waa kɛji ewo fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ nakai otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ ayi obɔ ni etsii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: If I save seeds from my best corn harvest and plant them next season, why do the new plants grow weaker?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to ni mikɛdu kɛha be ni baa lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Many modern crop varieties lose their strength and disease resistance after the first harvest. Planting seeds saved from a previous crop often leads to weaker plants and much lower yields than buying fresh seed.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu ni ajie kɛjɛ tsutsu dumɔ mli lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni aheɔ lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my corn crop if I leave it on the stalks in the field for too long after it is ripe?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving dry corn in the field exposes it to rain, birds, and insects, which rots the cobs, weakens the stems until the plants fall over, and increases field losses before you even harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaagbala nugbɔ, okpoi kɛ kooloi, ni no baaha ŋmãa lɛ agbo. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbɔjɔ aahu akɛ tso lɛ gbee shi. Ni ehaa nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ dani okpaa nii po.

english: What causes my corn to turn dark and moldy when I transport it over long distances to sell in neighboring countries like Burkina Faso?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-ŋmã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛtee he ko shɔŋŋ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ mi tamɔ Burkina Faso lɛ amli?

english: Long journeys in closed trucks build up intense heat. If the corn has even a little leftover moisture when loaded, that heat causes the grain to sweat and grow destructive molds during travel.
ga: Gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni akɛyaa lɔlei wuji amli lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa baa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli beni awoɔ mli lɛ, Nakai dɔlɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does fresh maize lose so much weight and shrink after I dry it in the sun for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni afɔ lɛ ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ waa kɛ́ akɛwo hulu mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested corn is full of water weight. Sun-drying removes that excess water, shrinking the kernel slightly but leaving behind a dry, hard seed that weighs less and stays preserved.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ eyi kɛ nu shwiili. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo shi eshiɔ dumɔwui ni egbi ni wa ni tsiimɔ waaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does some stored corn develop a whitish or greenish dust on the kernels, and is it safe to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa komɛi ni ato lɛ yɛ sũ yɛŋ loo eŋɔli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani ehi akɛ ayeɔ?

english: That dust is a dangerous mold caused by damp storage conditions. It produces invisible poisons called aflatoxins, making the grain unsafe for both human consumption and animal feed.
ga: Muji ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli baa. Ehaa tsofa ko ni anaaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa ŋmaa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai aniyenii kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Why do some of the fruits on my oil palm bunch start falling to the ground on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi miije shishi amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When palm fruits reach full maturity, the stalks connecting them to the bunch naturally weaken and loosen. Fallen fruits on the ground are the tree's natural signal that the entire bunch has reached peak oil content and is ready for harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ tso ni kɛ tso lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ baafee blɛoo ni ekɛ ehe aaajɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yibii ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ eshɛ mu ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he, ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to cut down an oil palm fruit bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mu tsei akui?

english: Look closely at the base of the tree for loose fruits. When about 2 to 5 fruits have naturally dropped from the bunch onto the ground, the bunch is fully ripe and contains the highest amount of oil.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona yibii ni etse ehe. Beni aduawai aaafee 2 kɛyashi 5 shwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛmli mu fe fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I leave ripe palm fruit bunches on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmei yibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe bunches on the tree causes the oil quality to spoil by increasing acidity. The fruits will also start rotting or be eaten by pests, leading to a loss in farm income.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaafite fɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ acidity ni ebaaya hiɛ lɛ nɔ. Yibii lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye amɛ. Enɛ haa shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce heavy fruit in some months but very little in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ ekrokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees react directly to rainfall patterns. During dry seasons, the trees save water and slow down fruiting, but when the rainy season comes, it triggers heavy flowering that leads to high fruit yields months later.
ga: Mu tsei kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi yeɔ tsakpaa tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaha nu akafite ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo. Shi kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ ba lɛ Tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi babaoo, ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower fronds on my oil palm turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a natural aging process of the tree. Older fronds at the bottom naturally turn yellow and die as the tree sends water and nutrients upwards to support new growth and developing fruit bunches.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ naa bɔ ni tsei daa lɛ. Baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee kɛ aduawai akui ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do palm trees planted close together grow very tall but produce small fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tɛŋ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, their leaves block each other from sunlight. The trees compete by growing tall and thin to reach the light, using up energy that should have gone into making big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Abuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa la lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ efee aduawai agbo ni tsii.

english: Why is my young oil palm tree taking so many years before it starts producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Young palms need plenty of sunlight, clean weeded areas, and soil nutrients to mature. If weeds or tall crops grow too close, they steal food and shade the young palm, delaying its ability to start flowering.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia tsei bibii. Tsumɔ he ni jwɛi shwieɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ Kɛji jwɛi loo tsei kakadaji kwɛ̃ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaaju niyenii ni eha etsitsi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why is it so hard to separate fresh palm nuts from the bunch right after cutting it down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaagbala ŋmei yibii heei amli kɛjɛ ŋmei lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afo lɛ?

english: Freshly cut palm bunches have tough, fibrous tissues holding the fruits tightly inside the stalk. Over a few days, these tissues naturally dry out and break down, allowing the fruits to loosen.
ga: Palm tsei ni afo ehee lɛ yɛ fãji ni wa ni hiɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli Nɛkɛ fãji nɛɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Does letting harvested palm bunches rest for a few days make it easier to remove the nuts?
ga: Ani kɛ́ ashi tsei ni akpa lɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo akɛ abaajie ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yes, leaving cut bunches in a cool spot for 2 to 3 days allows natural fermentation to soften the thick stalks, making the fruits drop off easily without heavy manual effort.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei niji ni afo lɛ yɛ he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ afee blɛoo. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo fataaa he.

english: Why do palm fruit bunches heat up and start smelling sour when left in a pile after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei yibii lɛ mli woɔ la ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cut fruits are still living tissues that generate heat as they breathe. When packed in a pile, natural yeasts cause rapid fermentation, which heats up the pile and can spoil the oil if left too long before processing.
ga: Yibii ni afo lɛ shwɛɔ fãji ni hiɛ ka ni feɔ dɔlɛ beni emuɔ lɛ. Kɛ akɛwo ŋtayaa mli lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli ŋtayaa kɛ ŋtayaa baa oya. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efite fɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani atsu he nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants curling up and turning pale yellow during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water when heat is high and soil moisture is low. Yellowing usually shows that the crop is suffering from water stress or lacking key nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite kɛji dɔlɛ fa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hu faaa. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually getting enough water down at their roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: You can dig a small hole about a hand-length deep near the plant's root zone; if the soil can be squeezed into a loose ball without falling apart or dripping wet, the roots have adequate water.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa bu bibioo ko. Aaafee tso kome ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifã he lɛ. Kɛji akɛ abaanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni etseee loo efee ŋmɔtɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or inconsistent watering, as the plant tries to conserve water and energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni naa wa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii heei.

english: Why are my cassava stems growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the roots underneath remain tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa lolo.

english: Cassava puts its energy into growing tall leafy tops when there is too much nitrogen or excess water in the soil, leaving very little energy to develop thick tubers underneath.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji amli kɛji nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná yitso ni mli wa yɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning reddish-purple?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple-red lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize plants usually mean the roots cannot access enough phosphorus from the soil, often because the soil is too cool, wet, or compacted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my crop help my soil perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots, which enriches the soil and acts as natural fertilizer for neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die during the day even when there is moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes can wilt in wet soil if soil-borne bacteria or fungi have attacked the root system, preventing the roots from absorbing water regardless of how wet the ground is.
ga: Tomato baanyɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ helai loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather, especially when cocoa trees are planted too closely together or have too much shade.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ayɛ hulutsoo tsɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily right when the bunches start to get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni jwɛi lɛ mli miiwo wu lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that need soil heaped around the base (mounding) and wooden support stakes to keep heavy bunches from pulling the tree out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni biɔ ni ato shikpɔŋ kɛbɔle shishigbɛ (mound) kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ shi lɛ ahe koni niji ni tsii akagbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my watermelons rotting on the bottom side before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Bottom rot happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly, usually caused by irregular watering patterns in the field.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant my maize in straight rows instead of scattering the seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines with proper spacing ensures each maize plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors, making weeding easier and producing larger cobs.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi lɛ ni anáa ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect damage from tiny pests like whiteflies that spread diseases or suck out the plant's sap, starving the plant of vital nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni gbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa loo amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ efite amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: Under intense afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, usually recovering by evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ni baa shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes too drastically. When stressed by heat or drought, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ kpe Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to grow properly. If the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, the growing tuber cannot push through easily, resulting in stunted, misshapen roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Anyɛɛɛ atsɔ bulb ni adu lɛ mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhe bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Weeds act like extra mouths at a small food table. They quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving your main plants hungry and weak.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni yɔɔ niyelihe okpɔlɔ bibioo lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ oya. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei titrii lɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruits start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ?

english: Plantain roots stay close to the surface and cannot easily support heavy bunches when wet soil gets soft or strong winds blow. Using wooden prop sticks helps support the heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mlɛo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni naa wa kpe. Tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, overly shady, and wet environments. It spreads quickly through rain splashes if there is poor airflow in the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ, egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii.

english: Why do my stored beans get full of small holes and turn to dust after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Eyi obɔ kɛ sũ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay hidden eggs inside the seeds before or right after harvest. Once inside your storage bags, the eggs hatch into larvae that eat the beans from the inside out.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui ni amɛkɛteeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli dani akpaa loo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ eshɛ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli pɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo.

english: Why do plantain plants produce harvest so much faster than cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui woɔ yibii oya fe kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing herbaceous plants that can mature and yield a heavy bunch within 9 to 12 months, whereas cocoa is a woody tree that needs 3 to 5 years of growth before it starts producing cocoa pods.
ga: Plantain ji jwɛi tso ko ni daa oya ni baanyɛ adara ni ewo yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, yɛ be mli ni kookoo ji tso ni yeɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani ebɔi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii feemɔ.

english: If I am not sure how long I can keep using a piece of land, should I plant cocoa or plantains?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mileee be abɔ ni manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii hu? Ani esa akɛ madu kookoo loo plantains?

english: Plantains are ideal for short-term land use because they mature within a year and allow you to harvest quickly, while cocoa is a long-term investment that requires guaranteed land access for many years to be profitable.
ga: Plantains hi kɛha shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be kukuoo mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ afi kome mli, ni ebaaye ebua bo ni oná ŋmaa oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji shika ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni biɔ ni mɔ ko aná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ afii babaoo dani enyɛ ená sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Can I harvest plantains from the exact same tree stem again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa plantains kɛjɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: No, a plantain stem dies after it produces a single bunch of fruit. However, the plant naturally grows small new shoots called suckers around its base, which grow up to give you the next harvest.
ga: Dabi, plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ baagbo beni ewo yibii kuu kome pɛ sɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei bibii. Nibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni amɛbaakwɛ koni okpa be kroko.

english: Why do a lot of small side shoots grow around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ Mi plantain shishitoo lɛ he?

english: Those side shoots are called suckers. It is the plantain's natural way of multiplying itself underground so that new plants can replace the main stem after it is harvested.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni plantains tsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi bɔni afee ni tsei heei abaye tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ najiaŋ beni akpa amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh heat. They naturally need shade from taller plants, like plantains or shade trees, to keep them cool and moist during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why do plantain plants fall over easily during strong winds and heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unlike deep-rooted trees like cocoa, plantains have shallow, fibrous root systems near the topsoil. When the fruit bunch gets heavy and the soil becomes soft from rain, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ fiber ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni esoro no kwraa yɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ kookoo he. Beni aduawai akui lɛ amli tsii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee blɛoo kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooojɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Plantains have soft stems and huge leaves that lose water very quickly in hot, dry air. Dropping their outer leaves is the plant's survival trick to reduce water loss and protect the main stem during dry spells.
ga: Plantains yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa tso lɛ yiwalaheremɔ koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Will growing plantains on my land exhaust the soil for future crops?
ga: Ani plantains ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui?

english: Plantains consume a lot of soil nutrients to build fruit, but their large leaves shade the ground and eventually rot into organic mulch, which helps keep the soil moist and fertile if managed well.
ga: Plantains kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ aduawai. Shi amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there fewer weeds growing under a mature plantain farm compared to an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛɛɛ shii abɔ yɛ plantain ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ amli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Mature plantains form a thick canopy with their large leaves, blocking sunlight from reaching the ground. Most weeds need direct sunlight to germinate and grow, so the shade naturally slows them down.
ga: Plantains ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli tse ni eyɛ baai wuji. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ. Jwɛi babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo haa jwɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is my plantain bunch very small even though the plant leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ni tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa?

english: Large leaves mean the plant got enough water and nitrogen to grow tall, but forming a heavy fruit bunch requires extra soil nutrients like potassium. Without enough potassium during fruiting, the bunch remains small.
ga: Baai wuji tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nu kɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃. Shi aduawai akui ni tsii ni afee lɛ biɔ niyenii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium. Kɛji akɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ yibiiwoo be mli lɛ, Kuu lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha efo kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make food that feeds the tubers under the dirt. Staking lifts the leaves into the air where they get sunshine and stays away from rotting soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ ahi kɔɔyɔɔ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la yɛ lɛ, ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is an important food in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the farm and prevent the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not right before a heavy downpour. Burying or covering the fertilizer with a little dirt near the base of the stem keeps it safe until the plant drinks it up.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi kaafee nakai dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ fioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fu loo ehà nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi tso lɛ baanu nu lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. It also makes pests and diseases that love maize build up in that ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai he lɛ.

english: What is causing these tiny green worms to eat holes in the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli nɛɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hatches from eggs laid by small moths. They hide inside the central part of the corn stalk and feed heavily on young leaves if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii babaoo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus carried by very small white insects called whiteflies, or it can be a sign that the plants are under extreme heat and drought stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Aloo ebaanyɛ efee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miina dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the hot sun will dry out the soil and kill the delicate new sprouts before the real rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui heei dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the stem near the ground grows thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni tso lɛ shishi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my young pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-baby pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds are like thieves—they steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer away from your pepper plants. They also serve as hiding spots for insects that carry diseases.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ julɔi. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ o-pepper tsei lɛ amli. Etsuɔ nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi ni kɛ helai baa lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ.

english: Why do my plantains rot so quickly after harvest, and how can I stop this from destroying my profits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enɛ naa koni ekafite mishishijee shishitoo mla lɛ?

english: Fresh plantains naturally ripen and spoil within a few days due to ethylene gas release. Processing fresh plantains into dried plantain powder removes moisture, extending their shelf life from a few days to several months without spoilage.
ga: Plantains heei baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ ethylene kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ hewɔ. Plantain hee ni akɛfeɔ plantain pauda ni egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ehaa be ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛjɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛyaa nyɔji babaoo mli ni efiteee

english: What can I actually make out of my harvested plantains besides selling them fresh at the local market?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛ plantains ni akpa? Kɛfata he lɛ, amɛhɔ̃ɔ nibii heei yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.
