english: You can process plantains into high-value items like plantain powder for fufu, dried chips, or starch. Value-added products last much longer and sell for higher prices than raw, perishable bunches.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain afee nibii ni jara wa waa, tamɔ plantain powda ni akɛfeɔ fufu. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni egbi, loo ashikiŋsha, ni jara wa waa lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe ŋmɔtɔi ni fiteɔ oya lɛ.

english: Should I use ripe or unripe plantains if I want to process them into plantain powder?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ plantains ni ekwɛ̃ loo ni eshɛko atsu nii kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee amɛ plantain powder?

english: Unripe plantains are ideal for making plantain powder because they contain high starch and low sugar content, making them easy to slice, dry, and mill into a smooth flour.
ga: Plantains ni eshɛko lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha plantain powder feemɔ yɛ starch ni fa babaoo kɛ sugar ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaafolɔ, agbi, ni agbɛlɛ ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Do I need expensive industrial machines to start turning my plantain harvest into powder?
ga: Ani nitsumɔhei tsɔnei ni jara wa he miihia mi koni mabɔi plantains ni akpa lɛ tsakemɔ kɛmiifee powda?

english: No, you can start on a small scale by manually peeling, thinly slicing, sun-drying the slices on clean raised platforms, and using a local community mill to grind them into flour.
ga: Dabi, obaanyɛ oje shishi bibioo kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ooogbi yɛ kpoku ni nɔ tse ni awo nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ akutso lɛ mli ŋmɔ ko atsu nii ni okɛshwie nɔ ni efee ashikishaŋ.

english: How does turning my plantains into powder help me make more money than selling raw bunches?
ga: Te plantain powder ni mikɛbaafee powder lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo fe ŋmeii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Selling raw plantains during peak harvest leads to low prices due to market gluts. Plantain powder is a processed product that can be stored until prices rise, reducing waste and commanding higher profit margins.
ga: Plantains ni ahoko ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ haa jara baa shi ejaakɛ jara lɛ fa babaoo. Plantain powder ji nɔ ko ni afee ni abaanyɛ akɛto kɛyashi jara lɛ baaya hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fitemɔ baa shi ni ehaa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo baa.

english: I hear traders cross the border from Togo to buy plantains in Ghana; how can my farm benefit from cross-border trade?
ga: Minu jarayelɔi ni foɔ husu lɛ kɛjɛɔ Togo koni amɛyahe plantains yɛ Ghana lɛ he. Te miŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana husui asɛɛ jarayeli he sɛɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Neighboring countries like Togo have high demand for Ghanaian staple foods. By producing uniform, high-quality plantains or processed plantain powder, you can attract cross-border traders who buy in larger quantities.
ga: Maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Togo lɛ taoɔ Ghana niyenii titri waa. Kɛtsɔ plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo plantain powda ni atsu he nii ni afeɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ogbala husui asɛɛ jarayelɔi ni heɔ nii babaoo lɛ.

english: Why do plantain prices drop drastically during certain months of the year in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain jara baa shi waa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Prices drop during peak harvest season because many farmers harvest at the same time, creating a market surplus. Since fresh plantains spoil quickly, farmers panic-sell at cheap prices to clear their stock.
ga: Jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be ni fa fe fɛɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okwaafoi pii kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli. ni kɛ nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ Ejaakɛ plantains heei lɛ fiteɔ oya Okwaafoi lɛ sheɔ gbeyei ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ koni amɛkɛjie nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the fruit bunch fully develops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Premature leaf yellowing is usually caused by water stress during the dry season, lack of soil nutrients like potassium, or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka, which reduce the plant's ability to feed the growing bunch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni tsiɔ mɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ sigatoka diŋ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛ niyenii haa kuu ni miida lɛ baa shi.

english: How long does a plantain sucker take from the day I plant it to when I can harvest the first bunch?
ga: Be enyiɛ plantain sucker heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni miduɔ kɛyashi be mli ni manyɛ makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: A healthy plantain sucker typically takes between 9 to 12 months to yield a full bunch, depending on water availability, soil fertility, and proper sucker management.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe. Edamɔ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ suction he gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa

english: Why do my plantains get bruised and turn soft so easily when I carry them over long distances to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mikɛtee he ko shɔŋŋ koni miyahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh plantains contain high water content and soft flesh that damages easily under weight and friction during transport. Converting plantains into dried powder makes transportation much easier and prevents physical damage.
ga: Plantains heei lɛ yɛ nu babaoo kɛ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni efiteɔ oya yɛ muji kɛ ŋmɔlɔ shishi yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Kɛ́ atsɔ plantain nɔ afee powda ni egbi lɛ, ehaa gbɛfaa feɔ mlɛo kwraa, ni ehaaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ afite.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade during their early growth stage because intense direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture before their root systems are strong enough to support them.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo yɛ amɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: Why do plantain leaves split into ribbons during high winds, and does it hurt the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ? Ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa ŋmɔshinii lɛ anɔ loo ekɛbaaa?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins during strong winds to prevent the entire stem from snapping; while it looks damaged, it actually protects the plant from falling over.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baagbala amɛhe yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli koni amɛkakumɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite po Shi ebaanyɛ ebu tso lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ koni ekagbee shi.

english: If I plant my maize very close together, will I harvest more corn from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he ko Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting maize too close together creates heavy competition for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny ears of corn, which reduces your overall harvest weight.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii baa. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts between my rows of cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, providing a natural fertilizer that feeds the nutrient-hungry cassava plants growing beside them.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and drop off during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during extreme heat to conserve water loss, but severe curling combined with leaf drop usually signals water stress or sap-sucking insects like thrips and whiteflies spreading viruses.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ akafite. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa ni fata baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over easily right before the bananas are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo dani bananai lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when microscopic pests called nematodes or fungal rot attack the roots under the soil, weakening the plant's foundation so it cannot support the heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo rot fungi lɛ tutua shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly, which stresses the plant and stops pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛkpaa pollination.

english: Why does putting too much chemical fertilizer burn the stems of my vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa aduawai shãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts; using too much draws moisture out of the plant roots and stems instead of feeding them, causing chemical burning and tissue damage.
ga: Fertilizer ji ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Ekɛ tsofa shãa kɛ fãji ni fiteɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength and vigor in the second generation, leading to uneven crop growth, weak plants, and much smaller harvests compared to buying certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kwraa fe be mli ni aheɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when stored in a closed room after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested yams continue to breathe and produce heat; storing them in closed, unventilated rooms creates humidity that traps heat and encourages fungal rot to spread quickly across the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo tsu ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mɔɔ dɔlɛ baa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa bulb lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen food from the soil, or the soil has too much water, which suffocates the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa niyenii yeli.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, so none of them get enough energy to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwu ko bɛ ni náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnut on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but crops like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix good food back into the soil through their roots, making the land fertile for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii kpakpa toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp wet ground where diseases like to spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii. Staking hu haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai fɔɔ baa lɛ. sumɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa

english: Roots need air to breathe. When rain stays on the farm without draining, water fills all the air gaps in the soil, drowning the roots and allowing soil rot germs to destroy them.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu homɔ bɛ mli lɛ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel heat stress or do not get enough water. The plant discards the flowers to conserve its strength and stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa amɛnáaa. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are fall armyworms. They hide inside the funnel because the young inner leaves are tender, moist, and protected from the hot sun while they feed.
ga: Amɛji asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ? Ani eji nɔ fɔŋ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Plants drink fertilizer dissolved in soil water. Putting fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the crop cannot swallow it without water.
ga: Tsei nuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ nu mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ atsu nii kɛji nu bɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my groundnut plants turn yellow and dry up when the nuts are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he lɛ?

english: As groundnuts finish their life cycle, the plant stops feeding its leaves and sends all remaining food into the pods underground, signaling that it is harvest time.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii gbe amɛwala shihilɛ naa lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nikpamɔ be eshɛ.

english: How can I treat sickness in my crops if I cannot find or afford chemical sprays in my market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsa helai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mana tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ loo mahe yɛ jara nɔ hu?

english: When manufactured chemicals are unavailable, you can manage crop sicknesses using natural solutions like spraying water mixed with crushed neem leaves or wood ash, and by cutting away infected leaves so the sickness does not spread.
ga: Beni tsofai komɛi bɛ ni afee lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa loo tso sũ efutu mli lɛ atsa tsei ahe helai. kɛtsɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod is a plant sickness caused by excess moisture and fungi; it spreads when rain drops bounce off wet soil onto low pods or when the farm tree canopy is too thick to allow airflow.
ga: Black pod ji tso hela ko ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛba ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn watery and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water for too long or when tiny soil pests bore holes into the roots, allowing disease to enter.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ bu yɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba

english: Yellow leaves usually show that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia oŋmɔshi nii lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: How can I tell if my land's soil has lost its power to feed my crops properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ?

english: If your crops stay small, produce pale leaves, or yield very small harvests despite good rain, your soil has run out of organic food and needs manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin but fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ shi amɛfeee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer without balanced minerals like phosphorus, or when planted too close together, they spend all their energy growing tall leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo tsei amli ni minerals tamɔ phosphorus ni sa bɛ mli, loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kakadaji yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my crop leaves overnight and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi tso lɛ baai amli nyɔɔŋ kome Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Night pests like armyworms or beetles feed on tender leaves while it is cool; putting a little clean sand or dry ash into the growing tips of young plants can stop them from feeding.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kooloi tamɔ cutworms loo ladybugs yeɔ baai bibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni mli tse loo sũ ni egbi fioo ko fata tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkaye nii.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when heat becomes too high, when water is given unevenly, or when insects fail to visit the flowers to help them set fruit.
ga: Tomato baakwɛ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Ha nu ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara fɔfɔi koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and short roots that lose water quickly in dry harmattan winds, which is why planting temporary shade plants like plantains nearby keeps them alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow so weakly when I plant them very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and plant food in the ground, causing every plant to remain weak and small.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu mli ni amɛduɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize farm turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: This usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow green and strong. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant steals food from its older bottom leaves to feed the young leaves at the top, making the lower ones turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny pests like mites or thrips sucking the juices out of young leaves. As the damaged leaves try to grow, they twist and wrinkle, which stops the plant from making food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji baai ni efite lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When temperatures get too hot or the air is very dry, tomato pollen becomes dry and useless. If the flowers are not fertilized, the plant drops them to save its energy rather than keeping flowers that cannot produce fruit.
ga: Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Tomato pollen lɛ baagbi ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ Tsei lɛ baashi fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛgbele koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpa fɔfɔi ni nyɛŋ awo yibii lɛ

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and open instead of forming a hard round ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ hiɔ shi blɛoo ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bɔɔlu kokroo ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbage needs steady water and cool soil to form a tight head. If the soil dries out frequently or the heat is too strong, the leaves spread outwards instead of wrapping tightly over one another.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ he miihia cabbage koni ekɛfee yitsei ni mli wa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ shii abɔ loo latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã kponɔgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ he shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the green pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, which is a fungus that spreads fast in high moisture and shade. Damp conditions help fungus spores jump from the soil onto the pods and quickly ruin them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my young sweet orange trees drop a lot of small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? Babaoo dani ebatsɔ agbo?

english: Citrus trees naturally shed small fruits if they do not have enough water or soil nutrients to support all of them. Dropping some fruit is the tree's way of making sure the remaining fruit gets enough food to mature.
ga: Orange tsei baawo yibii bibii. Taakɛ eji lɛ, kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ, Yibii ni ashwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ekwɛɔ koni yibii ni eshwɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains waterlog the ground for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot in the soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves produce food for the underground tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so leaves can catch maximum sunlight without touching wet soil where diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ anyɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni etaaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Too many suckers growing around one mother plant compete for the same food, light, and water. Removing extra suckers allows the mother plant to focus all its strength into producing a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Ayɛ tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ ebɔle ehe. Tso ni ji fɔlɔ kome lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ plantains ŋmeii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ afeemɔ he nii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my farm land better for maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have friendly natural bacteria on their roots that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni haa mɔ feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. beni okpaa lɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I decide whether planting maize or planting rice on my land will bring me a better income?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha maná shika kpakpa?

english: Rice thrives in wet, swampy lowlands or areas with plenty of water, while maize grows better in well-drained highland soils. Rice usually requires higher setup costs for land preparation and water management, but can yield high profits if water is reliable, whereas maize has lower input costs and a steady market.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efɔ loo hei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ gɔŋ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, Rice biɔ shika babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛha shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kɛ nu he nitsumɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo aba kɛji akɛ anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa yɛ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe jara ni baa shi kɛ jarayeli ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: How can I calculate all my farming costs before planting so I do not run out of money before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu okwaayeli he nyɔmɔwoo fɛɛ he akɔntaa dani madu nii? Bɔni afee ni shika akaho nyɛ dani nyɛkpaa?

english: Add up the costs of land clearing, seeds, fertilizers, chemical sprays, and paid labor from planting through harvest. Listing these basic components early allows you to choose a crop that fits your budget and prevents your crop from failing due to lack of money mid-season.
ga: Nɔ ni fata he ji shika ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ, dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ. kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ mli Shishijee nibii nɛɛ ayɔsemɔ mra Ehaa ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ oshika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ kpãa gbee. ni atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ shika ni bɛ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my soil is better suited for root crops like cassava or grain crops like maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tuber ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa?

english: Loose, well-drained sandy soil allows root crops like cassava to expand underground easily without rotting. Heavy soils that hold moisture are better for grain crops like maize or rice, which need steady water to feed their stalks and seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli, tamɔ ŋmei, shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni amɛgbooo. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni mli edɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Enɛ biɔ nu daa koni eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why can I not use the exact same type and amount of fertilizer for both my maize and my vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ bɔ ni falɛ ji lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa kɛ mi-aduawai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops feed on different nutrients. Leafy crops and heavy grains like maize require more Nitrogen to grow tall and strong, while root crops and fruit vegetables need more Phosphorus and Potassium to develop roots and fruits. Using one feed for everything wastes money and reduces your yield.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ srɔtoi. Nibii ni yɔɔ baai kɛ ŋmaa ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, he miihia nitrogen babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shishifãi kɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai biɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo koni shishifãi kɛ aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii kome tsu nii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, efiteɔ shika ni ehaa shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ baa shi.

english: If I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season, will they yield as well as fresh store-bought seeds?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani dumɔwui ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baaha yibiiwoo tamɔ dumɔwui heei ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crop harvests lose their strength and uniformity over time, leading to lower yields and weaker plants in the next season. Purchasing fresh certified seeds ensures consistent crop growth, better pest resistance, and maximum yield potential.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ akpamɔ mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛ nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli hemɔ haa tsei lɛ daa daa. Eheɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nibii babaoo baa

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more plants on my small farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli hu?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak plants and smaller harvests; proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to produce bigger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields every year if I plant maize on the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year until the ground becomes exhausted. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil, keeping the farm fertile without extra cost.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaho. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni woɔ yibii ni okɛ shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to survive on tough soil and gather light fast. Your food crops need early weeding within the first few weeks after sprouting so the weeds do not steal the water and nutrients meant for your crop's early growth.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔji ni wa nɔ ni amɛbua la naa oya. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ oniyenii tsei lɛ amli oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni jwɛi lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni tso lɛ adara mra lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during a dry spell even if I give them a little water every evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ gboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo daa gbɛkɛ moŋ.

english: Shallow watering only wets the top of the soil, causing roots to stay near the surface where the hot sun quickly dries them out. Giving your farm a deep soaking less frequently encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where it stays cool and moist longer.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbi oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ wo nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ mli lɛ, ebaawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni baahi shi ni edɔ ni edɔ be babaoo

english: Why do insect pests show up on my farm right after the first major rains of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The heat and moisture from early rains trigger dormant insect eggs in the soil to hatch and wild weeds to sprout, creating food for pests. Scouting your farm early lets you spot these insects while their numbers are small before they damage your main crops.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ̃ɔ. ni koo mli jwɛi baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee niyenii amɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua bo ni ona kooloi bibii nɛɛ be mli ni amɛyi fa fioo dani amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant on land that my family has farmed for generations?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miweku lɛ etsu nii yɛ nɔ kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo ni eho lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Over time, plants draw nutrients out of the earth. When land is farmed continuously for decades without resting or adding organic manure and fertilizers, the soil loses its natural food supply, resulting in lower harvest yields.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite e-adebɔɔ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Does cocoa grow better on fresh forest land or on land that was previously used for farming?
ga: Ani kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ atsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fresh forest land has rich, undisturbed soil packed with natural plant foods from decaying leaves. Old farmland can still grow good cocoa, but it often needs soil testing, compost, or fertilizer to restore lost nutrients.
ga: Kooi heei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa. Eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni jɛ baai ni egboi amli. Gbɛjianɔtoo momoi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ kookoo kpakpa lolo. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni aka shikpɔŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ akwɛ koni akɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How many bags of cocoa can I realistic harvest from a well-managed acre of land?
ga: Cocoa kotokui enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ he ko ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: While traditional farming methods might yield 3 to 5 bags per acre, using modern high-yielding cocoa varieties alongside good weed control and fertilizer can produce 15 to 20 bags per acre.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ blema okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha aná baagi 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ acre kome mli moŋ. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, abaanyɛ aná kotokui 15 kɛyashi 20 yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why do some cocoa trees start bearing fruit in two years while others take five years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei komɛi jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi heɔ afii enumɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties grow at different speeds. Hybrid and grafted cocoa seedlings are specifically bred to mature faster and bear fruit early, whereas traditional or wild cocoa varieties naturally take much longer to mature.
ga: Srɔtoi srɔtoi daa oya yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Akwɛɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome kɛ nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo yibii mra. Yɛ be mli ni blema loo koo mli kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa pods on one farm to grow large and healthy while another farm yields small pods?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ daraa ni amɛhe waa? yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ kroko hu woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Pod size depends on soil fertility, sunlight access, water supply, and crop variety. Trees that are properly pruned and fed produce larger, healthier pods than overcrowded or nutrient-starved trees.
ga: Pod lɛ dalɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Hulu la, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ tsei ni anáa. Tsei ni afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ niyenii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni eyi obɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does the bottom stem of a grafted crop look modified or cut near the roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛwo amɛmli lɛ ashishigbɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni atsake loo afolɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Grafting joins a top shoot from a high-producing parent plant to the root stock of a strong, hardy plant. The visible join mark at the base shows where these two parts were united to create a faster-growing, disease-resistant tree.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ he ji ni akɛ tso ni ji nyɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afata tso ni he wa ni wa lɛ shishifã lɛ he. Weld okadii ni anaa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ fãi enyɔ lɛ fata he koni afee tso ko ni daa oya, ni helai nyɛŋ emɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Ani abaanyɛ akɛfata kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantains provides helpful shade for young cocoa seedlings and gives you food and income while waiting for the cocoa to mature. However, avoid heavy roots like cassava too close to seedlings so they do not steal soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ shika aha bo be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ shishifãi ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni akaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Should I cut off shoots and extra stems growing around the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ani ajie kookoo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, removing lower shoots—called chupons—is essential. Cutting them allows the tree to direct its water and nutrients to the main trunk and branches where cocoa pods grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ ajiemɔ he miihia. Nɔ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji titri ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: What should I do if my old cocoa trees have stopped producing good pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-cacao tso momo lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ?

english: You can rehabilitate old trees through 'stumping'—cutting the trunk low to the ground so a fresh, strong stem can sprout—or you can clear and replant the area with modern, fast-bearing cocoa varieties.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha tsei momo lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ‘amɛ ni oootsi’ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifã lɛ ni ooofo shi koni tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni woɔ yibii oya lɛ atsu nii ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is the base of my tree stem peeling or showing damage near the ground line?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsɔne lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miiho loo efite yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Damage at the stem base can be caused by accidental cuts from weeding cutlasses, pest attacks, or fungal diseases from water pooling at the root level. Keeping the base clear of heavy weeds helps protect the tree's bark.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishi lɛ afite kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ Kɛ́ jwɛi ni tsii bɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and cool moisture, helping young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it bad if my mature cocoa farm has too many large trees shading it?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei wuji babaoo tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa?

english: Yes, while young cocoa needs strong shade, mature cocoa needs balanced sunlight to flower and yield well. Too much dark shade creates high humidity, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo ni mli tse lɛ he miihia ŋmɔlɔ ni mli ewo duŋ. Shi hulu la ni sa he miihia kookoo ni eda lɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai. Shade ni mli ewo duŋ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ baa

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This can happen due to cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally drops pods it cannot feed, or black pod disease caused by fungi in overly wet conditions.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ cherelle lɛ ni egbo lɛ hewɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni enyɛŋ eye nii yɛ. loo black pod hela ni ŋmei ko kɛbaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine mli

english: What is causing dark patches and dried leaves on my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛni kɛ okadii diji kɛ baai ni egbi baa mi-kokoo niji lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests called capsids or mirids. They suck sap from stems and leaves, creating wounds that dry out branches and weaken the whole tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo myrids lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi baa ni haa tso lɛ niji lɛ egbiɔ ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why should I cut off the straight shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ cacao tso shishi lɛ?

english: Those shoots are called chupons. They grow fast and consume water and nutrients without producing pods, stealing energy away from the main fruiting branches.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ chupons. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni amɛjuɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei niji wuji lɛ amli.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the main trunk of my cocoa tree instead of just the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eniji lɛ anɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally flower on old wood and main trunks so that the heavy mature pods have strong support and do not snap small twigs.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei momoi kɛ tsei wuji anɔ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe awa, ni amɛkakumɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ.

english: During the dry Harmattan, the soil and air lose moisture quickly. The cocoa tree sheds leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself until rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm's soil is running out of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ?

english: Signs of poor soil include pale or yellow leaves, slow tree growth, and trees dropping their flowers instead of setting pods.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ ahe ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ daaa blɛoo, ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from around the root base of my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizers, and soil nutrients directly from cocoa roots. They also trap unwanted moisture and shelter insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo lɛ hu ni amɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aboɔhe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to pluck a cocoa pod from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: A pod is ripe when its color fully changes—green pods turn bright yellow, and red pods turn orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside have proper sweet pulp for fermenting.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ haa kɔfi yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow so much faster when the heavy rains start in May and June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa je shishi yɛ May kɛ June mli lɛ?

english: May and June mark the main rainy season in southern Ghana, providing soil with consistent moisture and high atmospheric humidity, which helps plants absorb nutrients rapidly and photosynthesize efficiently.
ga: May kɛ June ji nugbɔnɛmɔ be titri yɛ Ghana wuoyigbɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ hu yaa hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛfeɔ fotosintɛsis jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it best for me to sow my maize seeds right before the main rains in May or after the first heavy downpour?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ May mli loo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: It is best to plant immediately after the first consistent rains begin in early May so the soil is adequately moist for germination, preventing seeds from drying out in hot dirt or being washed away by torrential downpours.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ May shishijee gbɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛkwɛ̃. Tsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akatswa amɛ kɛya.

english: Why do gentle, steady rains help my crops produce better yields than violent rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa ni ehaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Gentle rains soak deeply into the soil without destroying soil structure or knocking off flowers, whereas heavy rainstorms erode topsoil, break stems, and disrupt pollination.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii loo ehaa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, efoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and the roots spoil when it rains heavily through July and August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ July kɛ August mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills soil air pockets with water, suffocating root systems. Without oxygen, cassava tubers rot rapidly under waterlogged soil conditions, leading to leaf yellowing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji kaadi ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do spots appear on my tomato leaves whenever we get continuous rain during the wet months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal spores to bloom and spread across wet foliage, causing leaf spots and blight.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal spores ni amɛfɔlɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What causes my seeds to rot in the ground instead of sprouting after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain compacts soil and seals off oxygen from the seed. Deprived of air and sitting in wet mud, seeds decay or get destroyed by soil fungal organisms before sprouting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ kɛ muji ni mli efɔ mli ni etaa Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants looking weak and pale even though they receive plenty of rain in August?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ August mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Excess rainfall causes nutrient leaching, where key plant nutrients like nitrogen are washed deep below the root zone, leaving crop roots unable to feed even with ample water.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii shwieɔ shi. he ni tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hoɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi shɔŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ.

english: What primary farm management activities should I focus on during the wet months from May to August?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi esa akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama nɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛjɛ May kɛyashi August?

english: During peak rains, focus on maintaining proper field drainage to prevent root rot, performing frequent weeding to stop nutrient competition, and scouting for fungal crop diseases.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ shii abɔ. Koni akpa niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii kɛ tsei ahelai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ataomɔ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after heavy rain falls on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds possess wild, resilient root systems adapted to capitalize instantly on sudden water and nutrient flushes, allowing them to outpace domestic seedlings during rainy weather.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli. Afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni fa babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe shia dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why does my topsoil wash away so easily when heavy mid-year rains fall on my cleared farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ hoɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ afi teŋgbɛ lɛ tswa miŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Bare, unploughed soil lacks roots to bind dirt particles together and crop foliage to break the falling rain's force, allowing heavy runoff water to carry away rich topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni atsuuu he nii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni baaha sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ afee ekome, ni ebɛ baai ni baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ lɛ akumɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ babaoo lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rain damage my cocoa beans after I have already harvested them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ lɛ fiteɔ mi-kookoo yibii lɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain introduces unwanted moisture to harvested cocoa beans, which causes mold and fungi to grow. Excess moisture makes the beans spoil quickly during storage, ruining their natural flavor and reducing their value.
ga: Nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ataooo baa kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ. Fɛ̃i babaoo haa kɔfi yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya beni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni ehaa kɔfe yibii lɛ ahe jara baa shi.

english: What happens to cocoa beans when we heap them under plantain leaves for a few days?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii anɔ kɛ́ wɔto amɛ yɛ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Covering cocoa beans under plantain leaves creates natural heat, starting a process called fermentation. This heat kills the bean germ so it cannot sprout, and it creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa plantain baai ashishi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ baa. Ejeɔ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔtɔ shishi. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ nɛɛ baagbe bean mli helai lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa beans turn black inside while drying on the mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ mli beni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans turn black inside if they stay wet for too long, lack proper air circulation, or get wet from rain. The black color is caused by mold growth inside the bean shell.
ga: Beans lɛ mli baatsɔ ediŋŋ kɛji amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ bɛ loo nugbɔ lɛ mli efɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ su diŋ lɛ baa.

english: What makes a cocoa bean 'good quality' when buyers inspect it?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ‘hi jogbaŋŋ’ kɛ́ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kwɛ mli?

english: Good quality cocoa beans are fully fermented, thoroughly dried so they crack easily, dark brown inside rather than grey or slate, and completely free from mold, insect holes, or flat empty shells.
ga: Akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ewo mli kwraa. Gbimɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkakumɔ oya. Mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo slate najiaŋ. ni ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do buyers use a tool to check how wet or dry my harvested crops are?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ nibii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ bɔ ni mikpamɔ lɛ mli efɔ loo egbi ha lɛ?

english: Buyers test moisture because wet crops rot quickly during storage and shipping. Well-dried crops last much longer and weigh properly without water weight, which ensures processors get usable produce.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kaa hulutsoo lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ejaakɛ tsei ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ. Nibii ni adu ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɔ shi be babaoo ni amɛtsiimɔ ji nɔ ni sa kɛji akɛ nu tsiimɔ fataaa he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ náa nɔ ko ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when they turn from green/red to a solid yellow or orange color. Harvesting too early means underdeveloped beans, while harvesting too late causes beans to sprout inside the pod.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji amɛtsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli/tsuru mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa mli. Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii edarako jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity, shade, and wet weather. Splashing rain carries the fungus from the soil and infected branches onto healthy pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do heavy rains cause my crops to shed their flowers before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa midumɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Heavy rain physically knocks flowers off stems and washes away pollen needed for fertilization. Cold, waterlogged soil from excessive rain also stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔi ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ hu kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ashwie koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa pods grow directly on the main tree trunk instead of the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers and heavy pods on their thick main trunk and main branches so the wood is strong enough to support the weight of the heavy pods without breaking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni tsii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ amɛtso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ amɛniji wuji ni mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ tsɔne ni tsii lɛ mli ni ekuuu.

english: Why does the condition of my crop right after harvest affect the price I am offered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa jara ni mikɛhaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Crops that are wet, moldy, or poorly fermented require extra work to restore or must be discarded entirely. Buyers pay full price only for clean, dry crops that can be stored immediately without spoiling.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni efɔ, ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ni edɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kroko koni akɛsaa loo esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ashwie kwraa. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he tse ni egbi ni abaanyɛ akɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efiteee lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulu lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, long periods without rain, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during dry spells and adding well-rotted manure helps the plant retain its flowers so they can produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are forming big tubers underground without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ efoŋ?

english: When cassava roots begin to expand into heavy tubers underground, they push the soil outward, causing visible cracks around the base of the stem. Additionally, the plant naturally sheds its lower leaves as it shifts its energy into storing starch in the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii. Ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baa. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a maximum harvest only for the first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength, resulting in uneven plant growth, smaller cobs, and higher weakness to diseases in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni hela lɛ baa oya yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for soil nutrients and water. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce large, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather natural nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the crops decay after harvest, that fixed nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops look thin and pale even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like bullies underground, stealing fertilizer, water, and space away from your crops before the crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yiwalɔi, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves full of small holes even though I do not see any insects on them during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabii baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii eyɛ mli akɛ anaaa kooloi bibii yɛ gbi lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Many leaf-eating pests, like caterpillars and beetles, hide under leaves or in the soil during the hot day and come out to feed during the cool night. Checking under the leaves early in the morning helps spot these pests early.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi ni yeɔ baai babaoo ahe ji ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Ekɛ ehe woɔ baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛje kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onaa nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This black rotting on the bottom of tomatoes is caused by irregular watering, which prevents the plant from moving calcium from the soil into the developing fruit. Covering the soil with dried grass mulch keeps the ground moist and prevents this rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist until it gets strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibioo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my maize grow very thin and tall without big cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tse ni ekwɛɔ ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize is crowded, each plant fights its neighbors for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall for light instead of producing big cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni emɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmãa wuji.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves in dry weather to save water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and keep growing tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni bulb lɛ baaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do the leaves and vines on my yam plant turn brown and die before I dig up the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally yellow and wither when the tubers underground have finished growing. This is a natural sign that the yams are mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ atomoi eda ni esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can nourish. Dropping excess flowers helps the tree save energy to grow a healthy batch of actual pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha amɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni ekwɛ̃ hewalɛ, anɔkwa fɔfɔi.

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the flower stems bend down and push into the soil so the actual groundnuts can grow safely underground.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ ashɛre pollination lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers when the soil stays soggy for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates pepper plant roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up food, which causes the plant to drop its flowers in distress.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ baaha pepper tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Etsiɔ mumɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ haomɔ mli lɛ naa

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, rotten bottoms while they are growing on the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ ni egbo be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering during warm weather.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Continuous rain creates wet conditions that encourage Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly through water droplets splashing on the pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my orange trees turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale leaves usually show that the tree is lacking nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are struggling to absorb nutrients due to poor soil conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ ni ehiii lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants look weak and yellow even though I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Just like a human child needs proper food and not just water, young maize seedlings need essential soil nutrients like nitrogen early on. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nutrients or is too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni niyenii ni sa he hiaa adesai, shi jeee nu pɛ lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ ŋmãa bibii hu he miihia sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen mra. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer right next to the stem of a small crop plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii ashishigbɛ he lɛ?

english: Young crop stems and roots are very sensitive, much like soft skin on a young child. Placing strong fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant; it should be placed a few inches away in a circle or pocket so the roots can reach for it safely.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ waaa kwraa. Tamɔ gbekɛ fioo ko hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ kooyigbɛ loo kotoku mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it important for me to check my crops every day even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa gbi kɛji akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ po lɛ?

english: Crops require continuous attention throughout their growth. Pests and diseases often start small under leaves or inside stems before major damage shows, so inspecting your field daily helps you catch and solve problems early.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai jeɔ shishi bibioo. yɛ baai ashishi loo tsei lɛ amli dani nɔ ko wulu baafite No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni odu lɛ daa gbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni osaa amɛ mra.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants curling up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll inward to protect themselves from intense sunlight and to slow down water loss. It is the plant's natural way of protecting itself when it is thirsty or experiencing heat stress.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu ni hoɔ blɛoo lɛ he. Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he kɛji kumai miiye lɛ loo ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miikpe.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks fall over easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Corn stalks fall over when their roots are shallow, planted too close together, or weakened by underground pests. Planting seeds at the proper depth and giving plants enough space helps roots grip the soil firmly.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa ni ahaa tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are some cobs on my corn plant missing seeds or only half-full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ amli lɛ ekomɛi ehiɛ efolo loo fã pɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Missing seeds on a corn cob usually happen when the plant experiences drought or stress while it is flowering and producing silks. Without enough water during pollination, some kernels fail to form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni elaaje yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ loo haomɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ siliki lɛ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ pollination be mli lɛ Dumɔwui komɛi nyɛŋ afee.

english: How do I know if my land is better suited for growing rice instead of maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi ŋmãa najiaŋ?

english: Rice thrives in heavy clay soils or lowland areas that hold water for long periods, whereas maize needs well-drained soil where roots won't sit in water. Land that stays muddy during the rainy season is ideal for rice.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni tsii loo yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young rice crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally aggressive and compete strongly for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives young rice plants the head start they need to grow strong and shade out future weed growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ basabasa yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ yitso ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi ni baakwɛ̃ wɔsɛɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the tips of my young rice leaves turn brown early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby rice lɛ miitsɔ blɔfo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Brown leaf tips on young rice plants often indicate that the soil is drying out too quickly or lacks specific minerals like potassium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plants early prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miigbi oya tsɔ loo nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi tamɔ potassium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni oha tsei lɛ niyenii mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell, which can dry out the soil and cause your newly germinated seeds to die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba.

english: Why does adding fertilizer actually help my crops yield more bags at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kotokui babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops need food to grow, just like humans. Fertilizer supplies essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil loses over time, enabling plants to produce stronger roots, healthier leaves, and significantly more fruit or grain.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni ehoɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa. Baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui babaoo

english: How do I know if my maize leaves are turning yellow because the plant is hungry for fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When yellowing starts at the tip of older bottom leaves and moves down the central leaf vein, it usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. The plant is moving stored nitrogen from old leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Beni ŋmɔŋ jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni edara lɛ anaagbɛ ni eyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ fãji lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Tsei miitsi nitrogen ni ato kɛmiijɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it better to apply all my fertilizer at planting or split it into different applications as the crop grows?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ baafata dumɔwui ahe loo majara ŋmei lɛ mli kɛha nitsumɔi srɔtoi? Beni tso lɛ daa?

english: Splitting fertilizer applications is usually better because young plants cannot consume large amounts at once. Applying a portion early and the rest during active growth prevents heavy rain from washing expensive fertilizer away before roots can drink it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei bibii nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be kome mli. Fã ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ dalɛ be mli lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa lɛ ahe dani shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: How does putting dried animal manure in my soil help chemical fertilizer work better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Manure builds soil organic matter, acting like a natural sponge that holds water and nutrients near plant roots. This prevents chemical fertilizer from draining away quickly in sandy or poor soil.
ga: Manure feɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji koni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ akaho oya kɛya shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense against heat stress. By rolling its leaves, the crop reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight to conserve internal water until the air cools down.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni nu ahi emli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: What makes my cassava plant grow huge leafy bushes above ground but give me very thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi yucca tso lɛ náa baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?
