english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, or receives excessive rain, cassava puts its energy into growing green leaves rather than storing starch in underground tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tuber sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds and rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its underground anchor roots are weak or shallow. This happens due to shallow land preparation, insect attack on roots, or planting seeds too close to the soil surface.
ga: Abɛi baashwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ he eko. Enɛ baa mli yɛ he ni asaa he lɛ jogbaŋŋ, kooloi ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ, loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why does planting beans together with my maize help the soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and convert it into a form in the soil that maize plants can easily drink, acting as a natural fertilizer provider for companion crops.
ga: Beans ji ŋmãa ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmãa tsei baanyɛ anu mlɛo. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha nanemɛi tsei.

english: Why do some crops take several months longer to mature than others grown on the exact same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fe ekrokomɛi ni akwɛ̃ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Each crop species has a distinct genetic life cycle. Short-season crops like maize rapidly complete flowering and grain production, whereas root crops like cassava need months to steadily accumulate starch in underground tubers.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ wala yibii sɔrɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ ŋmãa, fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ, heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛyaa nɔ amɛbua ŋmeii anaa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why does putting wet or un-dried harvested grain inside storage bags cause them to spoil so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akpa ni efɔ loo egbi ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ haa amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Damp grain trapped in bags creates a warm, moist environment where mold, fungi, and insects thrive quickly, causing decay, discoloration, and total destruction of the harvested crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ ni akɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli efɔ ni ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ koolooi shwereɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ, ehiɛ su tsakeɔ, ni efiteɔ kwraa.

english: If I plant cocoa on my entire land, can I still grow food crops between the trees?
ga: Kɛji midu kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lolo?

english: When cocoa trees are young, you can grow food crops like plantain or cocoyam between them for the first few years. However, as the cocoa trees grow bigger, their leaves form a dense ceiling that blocks sunlight, which means most food crops will no longer grow well underneath.
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ Obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains loo kookoo tsei yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shi, beni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, Amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwereŋ jogbaŋŋ yɛ eshishi dɔŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava or vegetables under my young coconut trees while they are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo aduawai yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ashishi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, while coconut trees are small and their leaf branches have not spread wide, you can safely intercrop them with fast-growing crops like cassava or vegetables without hurting the coconut seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ji bibioo ni eniji lɛ egbɛ eshwaaa moŋ, shi Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai adu lɛ shweshweeshwe. ni eyeee ŋmei tso lɛ awui

english: What will happen if I plant coconut trees too close to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei tso ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tso tsɔ?

english: Coconut trees grow very tall and broad roots, while cocoa needs specific shade and space. Planting them too close creates fierce competition for soil nutrients and water, causing both crops to give fewer fruits.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni kɛlɛ waa ni mli kwɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei biɔ hulutsoo kɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii fioo.

english: Do coconut trees take up all the water in the soil and stop nearby plants from growing?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei miimu nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛmiitsi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Coconut trees have extensive root systems that draw a lot of moisture from the topsoil. If you plant sensitive crops right next to their base, those crops will struggle to get enough water during dry spells.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi babaoo ni gbalaa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu tsei ni waaa ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ Nakai tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant too many different types of trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tsei srɔtoi babaoo yɛ he kome?

english: Mixing too many tree varieties closely together causes them to crowd each other out for light and nutrients, making the farm difficult to manage and reducing the overall harvest of each crop.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tsei babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ amɛhe koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, the hot sun scorches their leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ, Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do experienced farmers keep shade trees like kunkum on their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ kankum toɔ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees like kunkum act as natural shields for cocoa, filtering harsh sunlight, keeping the soil cool and moist, and protecting the farm from strong winds.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ kungum lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛbuɔ kookoo he. Efoɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ. ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: How do I know if my coconut trees are getting enough sunlight when planted near other tall trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tso ko miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Coconut trees love full sunshine; if they do not get enough light, their stems grow thin and weak, bending toward the sun, and they will produce very few or no coconuts.
ga: Kokoo tsei sumɔɔ hulu ni eyi obɔ. Kɛji la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ŋmɛɔ hulu lɛ he ni ebaawo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo ebaawo eko kwraa.

english: Why do cocoa trees spread their branches so wide and cover all the land as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa babaoo ni amɛhaa he ko muu fɛɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees mature, they naturally expand their branch canopy to capture as much light as possible, eventually joining together to create a dark cover that suppresses weeds on the ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Niji lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔ la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni naagbee lɛ amɛbua amɛhe naa koni amɛfee shĩa ko ni mli ewo duŋ koni amɛkɛtsi jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How many years does a coconut tree usually take after planting before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Depending on the variety, dwarf coconut trees can start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while taller traditional varieties usually take 6 to 8 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛji srɔtoi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kusum mli tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do many of my yam setts die underground before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ babaoo miigboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam setts often rot in the ground due to soil-borne fungi, insects, or excess water; treating setts before planting protects them so almost every piece survives and sprouts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, loo nu ni fa fe nine ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fãi lɛ fɛɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops wither and die in the middle of the growing season even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ moŋ?

english: Crops often wither during the season because hidden underground pests or root diseases damage the stem and roots, preventing the plant from absorbing water and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii gboɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo shishifãi ahe helai fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What causes some yams to stay small while others grow very large on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii komɛi feɔ bibii ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ wuji yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow large when the soil is loose enough for expansion, receives sufficient water and nutrients, and is free from competition by weeds or pests.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse bɔ ni sa ni egbɛ eshwa. Na nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni jwɛi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ amɛhe akaŋ bɛ mli

english: How does planting my crops too close together affect the size of my harvest?
ga: Te tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in smaller tubers and lower overall yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye akaŋ kɛha hulu la Nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa shi ni yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do modern planting methods give a higher survival rate compared to our traditional ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ haa mɔ hiɔ shi babaoo kɛ akɛto wɔ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Modern methods focus on correct spacing, proper soil preparation, and seed treatments, which protect young crops from disease and give them ideal growing conditions.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔ Enɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds on my farm reduce the total amount of food I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii fɛɛ ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops, causing young plants to grow weak or die before harvest time.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ shɛɔ.

english: Why is making proper mounds or ridges important for tubers like yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni sa ni aaafee lɛ he hia kɛha ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the soil so tubers can easily expand underground while also improving water drainage to keep the crop roots from rotting.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi koni tsei shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: How does feeding the soil help my crops produce higher quantities at harvest time?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛyeɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Soil nutrients provide essential energy for plants; when crops receive proper nourishment early on, they build strong roots that support more and bigger tubers.
ga: Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei hewalɛ ni he hiaa. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni sa mra Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ ŋmeii babaoo sɛɛ.

english: Does using healthy, disease-free seed yams really make a big difference in my total yield?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, using clean and healthy planting material ensures nearly every sett planted will sprout and grow strongly, giving you a full farm with bigger tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ dumɔ nii ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ saatso fɛɛ saatso ni adu lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni eda waa. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ yitso ni da.

english: How does treating my planting seeds before putting them in the ground stop them from dying early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ atsa dumɔwui ni adu lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkagboi oya?

english: Treating seeds creates a protective shield against soil insects and fungal decay, ensuring that almost all your planted crops survive their early growth stage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ baahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dalɛ fã lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight and direct heat. Leaving tall shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains keeps the soil moist and prevents the delicate young cocoa leaves from scorching while the trees are young.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo loo adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi kookoo baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to grow green leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the soil, it suffocates the roots and creates the wet conditions that rot-causing fungi need to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when soil water is uneven. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing the blossom from turning into a tomato fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. Tsi fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tomato aduawai.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if they are just growing in the soil next to my maize?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds act like thief crops by taking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly away from your maize roots, leaving your crop weak, thin, and unable to form big ears of corn.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi kɛtsɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ, amɛhe feɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants compete fiercely for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing strong stems. Giving plants proper space allows each one to get enough air, light, and nutrients to build big fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baaná tso ni mli wa lɛ, ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni eha ehe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he ko ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa kɔɔyɔɔ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do small worms chew holes in my crop leaves early in the morning but disappear during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ŋmɔɔ mibaai lɛ leebi lɛ? Shi ebaalaaje yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli?

english: Many leaf-eating caterpillars hide in the cool soil or under leaves during the hot midday sun to keep from drying out. They come out to feed in the cool morning and evening hours when leaves are soft and fresh.
ga: Kplukai babaoo ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ mli loo baai ashishi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli koni baai lɛ akagbi. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛfee ehee lɛ.

english: Why does mixing dry leaves and poultry manure into my soil help my crops survive dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi otsii babaoo ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Decayed leaves and manure add organic matter, which acts like a sponge in the dirt. It holds onto rainwater underground longer so plant roots can keep drinking even when it hasn't rained for days.
ga: Baai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa he, ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ekɛ nugbɔ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ anu nu kɛji nugbɔ enɛko gbii babaoo po.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny natural helpers on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, leaving behind free nitrogen fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbualɔi bibii yɛ amɛshishifãi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the middle of the afternoon but wake up again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli shi amɛteɔ shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun to shrink their surface area and slow down water loss. Once the air cools down in the evening, the roots catch up on pumping water and the leaves stand back up.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni ekɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee bibioo ni ekɛha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ nu lɛ mli kɛya ŋwɛi ni baai lɛ baadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when I plant them in an open field without any big plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a living shelter that protects the saplings from intense sun rays and keeps moisture in the soil until the trees mature.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa anáa he ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures that every stalk gets enough light and nutrients to grow thick and produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year when I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously on the same soil consumes specific nutrients faster than the soil can naturally replace them. Rotating cassava with nitrogen-fixing leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil nutrients naturally and improves future harvest yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi tsuɔ nii oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ amɛ awo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni akɛ ŋmeii ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ cowpea lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do crops like beans and groundnuts help improve the soil for other crops planted after them?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decompose after harvest, this stored nitrogen acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival mechanism that maize uses to cope with extreme heat. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and limits the amount of water lost through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛkpee dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛhaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any fruit actually starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience high environmental stress, such as irregular watering, intense heat, or pest damage. Keeping the soil consistently moist and cool reduces plant stress and helps the blossoms develop into healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ni mli wa, tamɔ nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ kpe. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ anɔ haomɔ aba shi, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off the extra shoots growing from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, often called chupons or suckers, drain valuable water and food away from the main trunk of the cocoa tree. Removing them directs the tree's energy towards producing healthy flowers and developing full cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ chupon loo tsei lɛ, jieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi ni mli wa ni ewoɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become tough and woody if I leave them in the ground for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants pass their mature stage, the roots stop storing soft starch and begin forming hard wood fibers to support the plant. Harvesting at the recommended maturity time ensures the tubers stay tender and ideal for cooking or processing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ho dalɛ be lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛtoɔ ni amɛjeɔ tso mli tsɔi ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ feemɔ shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ lɛ naa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi kɛha nihoomɔ loo nitsumɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted vegetable seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe aduawai dumɔwui ni midu yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants that have adapted to spread rapidly and absorb surface water and nutrients quickly. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing light, water, and food from your young vegetable seedlings.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ o-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I place dry grass or fallen leaves on the soil surface around my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egboi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic materials like dry grass, known as mulching, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over the garden bed.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ jwɛi hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekaha abɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How do I select the best quality seeds to plant so I can get a strong harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni maná yibii kpakpai?

english: Good seeds should be plump, dry, uniform in size, and free from insect holes or mold. Choosing certified seeds from reliable source suppliers ensures higher germination rates and healthier crops.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbi, amɛdalɛ po, ni bu loo ŋmeii ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ akafee nɔ ko. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni ahalaa kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni amɛduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crops dry up so fast even when it rains occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ bei komɛi amli po lɛ?

english: Young plants have small, shallow root systems that cannot reach deep groundwater. When rainfall is irregular, the topsoil dries out quickly, meaning young crops need consistent manual watering until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ niji afɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu daa kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: How should I decide which crop to plant so I can easily sell it for a good price?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni mikɛbaahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara kpakpa nɔ?

english: Before planting, talk to local market women and buyers to find out which crops are in high demand and short supply during harvest season. Planting based on market demand ensures you have ready buyers when your produce is ready.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, okɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ agba sane koni ona tsei ni ataoɔ waa ni amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ. Ni oooya hiɛ yɛ bɔ ni jarayeli nibii lɛ taoɔ lɛ naa lɛ haa onáa mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ ni efee klalo beni onibii lɛ efee klalo lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear and loosen the soil before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil makes it soft, allowing tender plant roots to push through easily and absorb water and air. Soft soil also helps seed sprouts push up to the sunlight without breaking.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha efee blɛoo. Enɛ haa tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ mli oya ni amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ hu haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli ni amɛkuuu.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. This makes the plants tall, thin, and weak, resulting in smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Beni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa lɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is standing around the roots for too long. Feeding the soil with manure or fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli lɛ daalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my crops in the afternoon under the hot sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu shwane mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Watering under the hot afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate quickly before the soil absorbs it, and hot wet soil can stress the plant roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ eŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii.

english: Why should I seek advice from agricultural officers before trying a new crop variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ŋaa dani maka tso hee ko makwɛ?

english: Agricultural officers understand local soil conditions, weather patterns, and proper planting techniques. Learning from them helps you avoid costly mistakes like planting the wrong variety at the wrong time of year.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi nuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shishi. kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ dumɔ gbɛ̀i ni sa Ni okaseɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni heɔ shika babaoo tamɔ tso ni ejaaa ni ooodu yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant the same crop on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests specific to that crop to build up in the soil. Changing crops each season gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa ehe.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my crops so they don't spoil quickly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite oya.

english: Each crop shows clear maturity signs, such as leaves drying, color shifting, or fruit reaching a firm texture. Harvesting at full maturity ensures the produce stays fresh longer while being transported to the market.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko jieɔ dalɛ he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo, tamɔ baai ni egbi, su tsakemɔ, loo aduawai ni wa. Nikpamɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom in a V-shape, it means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps the crop stay green and form healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, amɛfeɔ V su. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tsei. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why are the bottoms of my pepper fruits turning black and rotten before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Black spots on the bottom of peppers are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the fruit due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents this from happening.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai lɛ amli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi enɛ naa koni ekafee nakai.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight and heat. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act as umbrellas that cool the soil and retain moisture until the cocoa trees are strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he, tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very thin and tall with small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwilafoi bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to build thick stalks and grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when temperatures become too hot or when water supply drops suddenly. Heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why does my cassava produce lots of big green leaves above ground but only small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or heavy manure, cassava puts all its energy into growing lush leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Balanced feeding allows the plant to send nutrients down into the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo ŋmeii babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei baato hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmei kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves drop and curl during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than roots can drink it up. The plant temporarily wilts to conserve moisture, but it will recover as the day cools down as long as the root zone has water.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi ebaaku esɛɛ kɛya bɔ ni eyɔɔ tsutsu lɛ mli kɛ́ edɔ lɛ, be fɛɛ be ni nu yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after planting in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen as well as water to wake up and sprout. If the soil is too heavy, waterlogged, or buried too deep, the seeds struggle to breathe and take much longer to break through the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ nu koni amɛte shi ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsii tsɔ, nu eyi mli obɔ loo efu lɛ mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ naa mumɔ ni wa ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are growing well without digging up the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi miida jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ŋmei tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava tubers swell underground, they push the soil outward, causing visible cracks in the earth around the base of the stem while the main stem thickens and leaves remain healthy.
ga: Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi Ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli fãi ni kadiɔ mɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up and covered in a sticky substance?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves mean tiny insects called aphids are feeding on the sap of your crop and leaving behind a sugary liquid. Applying organic solutions like neem seed oil spray gets rid of these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids lɛ miiye ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛmiishi nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ wala mli tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are hungry for nutrients like nitrogen, which rain alone cannot provide. Applying the right fertilizer gives the crops the food they need to stay green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nugbɔ pɛ nyɛŋ aha lɛ he miihia otso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil actually needs fertilizer to grow better crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Koni adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield smaller harvests than they used to, your soil is likely tired and lacking the essential nutrients that fertilizer restores.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu egbɔjɔ ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aku sɛɛ aba lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Flowers often drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients, which prevents the plant from having enough energy to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ haaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin instead of strong and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Planting your seeds too close together forces the maize plants to fight each other for sunlight, causing them to stretch upward thin and weak instead of growing sturdy stalks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni wa.

english: In intense sunlight, leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up to keep cool. They usually recover in the evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects or viruses transmitted by insects, which damage the leaves and prevent the plant from producing healthy tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ afee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is enough space in the soil for everything?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Weeds act like food thieves. Their roots spread quickly to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from your crops, leaving your crops weak.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛjuɔ niyenii. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that love that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will removing some leaves or stems from my crops reduce my final harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mijie baai loo tsei komɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaha minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: No, removing extra or dead leaves actually helps the plant save its food and energy to feed the main fruits, making them larger and healthier.
ga: Dabi, baai ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ haa koni ekɛye eyibii titri lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot if I water them every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli daa gbi lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the tiny air holes in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe, which causes them to decay and rot.
ga: Nu babaoo yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing very small while my neighbor gets big ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tubers lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers stay small when planted too close together or in hard soil where roots cannot expand. Spacing plants well and loosening the soil lets the roots swell into large tubers.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwa lɛ. Gbalamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings burning and turning brown in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need shade from nurse plants like plantains to protect their tender leaves while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛkɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: What makes my maize leaves turn yellow with brown spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Yellow leaves with brown spots are often caused by fungal diseases that thrive in excess moisture, or by a lack of nitrogen washed away from the soil by heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Aloo nitrogen ni bɛ ni shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: What will happen if I plant my pepper crops very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This makes them grow thin and weak, producing fewer and smaller fruits overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Ha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ fɛɛ afee bibioo kɛ bibioo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is mature enough to cut for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛya jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are mature when the individual fingers swell and lose their sharp angles, turning rounded, and the dry flower ends at the tip of the fruit rub off easily.
ga: Plantains lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni enineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fũuɔ ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ naagbee yɛ eshishigbɛ ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture. By folding its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to stop water evaporation.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛbu nu mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akpa shwiemɔ.

english: Why does stubborn grass slow down the growth of my young yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ miiha mi sweet potato tsei lɛ miida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Grass has shallow, fast-spreading roots that drink up water and fertilizer before the yam plant can reach them. Clearing weeds early gives young yam shoots full access to soil food.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya. ni baanu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani sweet potato tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping small green fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they suffer from irregular watering or a lack of key soil nutrients like potassium and calcium needed to support heavy fruit loads.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium ni he hiaa koni akɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when their natural resting period ends, especially if stored in warm, dark, humid places. Keeping yams in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated barn helps delay sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji amɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ atomɔ to he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ blɛoo.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot so fast on the farm if I leave them on the plant for a few extra days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Once tomatoes ripen fully on the vine, their skin softens, making them weak against heat, bacteria, and insects. Harvesting them early when they turn light pink allows them to ripen safely off the plant without rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ tomatoi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Ehewolo lɛ baafee blɛoo. Enɛ haa amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha hulutsoo, helatsɛmɛi kɛ kooloi bibii. Kpamɔ mra. Kɛ́ amɛtsɔ pinki ni mli tse lɛ, amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfiteee.

english: What causes my harvested cassava to turn black and spoil inside after just two days?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots continue to react with air after being cut from the stem, causing rapid internal damage. Processing or eating cassava within 24 to 48 hours of digging it up prevents this spoilage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi yaa nɔ amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome beni afo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Ekɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa oya Kɛ́ atsuɔ ŋmei he nii loo ayeɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli yɛ ŋmei ni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmei nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do wild animals and rodents attack my maize farm just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli kooloi kɛ ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: As maize matures, the cobs sweeten and dry out, producing a strong scent that attracts nearby animals looking for an easy meal. Harvesting your crop as soon as the husks turn brown prevents animals from destroying it.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋmãa lɛ ŋɔɔ ni egbi. Ehaa tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ko ni gbalaa koolooi ni bɛŋkɛ ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkafite lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your corn plants are lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient they need to grow strong. Adding manure or fertilizer to the soil helps restore their green color and healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil moist around the root area helps the plant retain its flowers so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ koni enyɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do some farmers plant cassava around the edges of their vegetable farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei yɛ amɛ aduawai ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava grows tall and sturdy, acting as a natural windbreak and barrier that protects delicate vegetables from strong winds, scorching sun, and roaming animals.
ga: Cassava daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ he tsɔne kɛ tsɔne ni buɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ

english: Why do my dried cocoa beans get moldy when I store them inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni egbi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ akɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: If cocoa beans are not dried fully in the sun, trapped water inside allows mold to grow during storage. Drying them thoroughly until they snap cleanly when pressed protects them from mold.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu lɛ egbiko kookoo yibii lɛ kwraa lɛ, Nu ni akɛwo mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ aahu kɛyashi amɛbaakumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ anyɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why does my land produce less food every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Alternating with crops like beans or peanuts restores nutrients and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: How do I know when my yam is fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni sweet potatoes lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely. This shows the plant has finished sending all its energy into growing the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for leaf growth. It often happens when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the soil or when fertilizer has not been applied yet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility naturally and helps keep weeds from overcrowding your crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele ni ooodu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi akayimɔ onibii amli fe nine.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer about two to three weeks after germination when the crops have grown roots, and when the soil is damp so the plants can easily drink in the nutrients.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ eje shishi lɛ. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo

english: Why do I see small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves of my maize plants and eating tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi tsei lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on tender maize leaves. Early spraying with recommended organic or safe chemical treatments protects your field before severe damage occurs.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oyale lɛ he dani nɔ ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and stopping the plants from producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy so fruit can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ mli Kudɔmɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ mra Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil moist and protecting them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, giving them maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ mɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers dropping off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by long dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of pollination by tiny insects. Ensuring proper shade and soil moisture helps flowers convert into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ pollination He ni akɛhaa hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant move calcium smoothly into the tomatoes.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa calcium lɛ yaa tomato lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and extreme heat. Without shade trees or plantains growing beside them to block the harsh sun, the intense heat burns the young leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ bɛ lɛ, Koni ekɛtsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize stalks turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts from the lower leaves and moves up the stalk is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newer top leaves, leaving the older bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ ni eyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil and starves the cassava roots of oxygen. Soil that stays soggy for too long creates ideal conditions for water rot and harmful fungi to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ naa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha nu mli fitemɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper and tomato leaves curling upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes and peppers is often caused by leaf-curl viruses transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies. The virus disrupts the plant's normal growth, causing the leaves to twist, curl, and stunt overall crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji hela ko ni haa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa. Virus gbalaa tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ, amɛkɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why does my plantain shoot produce very small bunches when I let all the suckers grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa bibii nɛkɛ beni mihaa tsei lɛ fɛɛ daraa yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Removing excess suckers allows the parent plant to direct all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛbaatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes instead of just crawling across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create food for tuber development. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to full sunlight while preventing leaf rot diseases caused by soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha tuber lɛ shweremɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni eŋmɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ ehe hu kɛjɛɔ baai ni fiteɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ekɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help the soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in their roots that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays behind as free fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ baaya nɔ ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my pepper plant flowers falling off before any peppers form on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as sudden hot spells, lack of soil moisture, or getting too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ko he, tamɔ hulutsoo ni baa trukaa fe nine. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry heat spell that can last for weeks. If the seeds germinate after that single rain, the young roots will dry up and die before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ dɔlɛ be ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ ahi shi otsii babaoo sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ, Shishifãi bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops stay stunted even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miigba midumɔwui lɛ anaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb fertilizer and water much faster than young crops can. If weeds are not cleared before fertilizing, you are mostly feeding the weeds instead of your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baanyɛ afee. Kɛji ajieee jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii Ekolɛ obaaha jwɛi niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the roots standing in water for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ ashi shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdamɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the roots under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure or fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to build tall stems and green leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are ready to start bearing pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo ŋmeii?

english: You will know your cocoa tree is mature enough when you see small pink and white flowers opening directly on the main trunk and thick branches. These first flowers signal that the tree is ready to produce pods.
ga: Obaale akɛ o-cacao tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ona fɔfɔi bibii. Fɔlɔi ni ji pinki kɛ eyɛŋ feɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ. Nɛkɛ mra be mli fɔfɔi nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaawo ŋmɔtɔ.

english: My tomato plants are producing plenty of flowers, but why are the flowers falling off without making any tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from dry soil. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, causing it to fall off before a tomato can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ miipiŋ tso lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomatoi lɛ feɔ.

english: Seeds carry only a small amount of stored food energy to help them sprout. If you bury them too deep, the shoot runs out of energy before it can break through the soil into the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛji ofu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mfonirifeemɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani enyɛɔ eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa hulu la mli.

english: Should I cut off the small extra branches growing at the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ani ajie nakai shweremɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, removing those extra side shoots—called suckers—helps the main plant direct all its food and water toward making bigger and healthier tomato fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, ajieɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii. ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ eniyenii kɛ enu fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that hide under the leaves and suck out the plant sap, or by a sickness carried from plant to plant by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ mli

english: Why do my young vegetable crops droop in the afternoon heat even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Nɛgbɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli leebi?

english: Hot midday weather makes water evaporate from the leaves faster than young roots can pull water up from the soil. Once the sun goes down and temperatures cool, the plant will stand tall again.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baadamɔ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants grow slow and weak when I plant them directly under big shady trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants need direct sunlight to make food for themselves. Big forest trees block sunlight, leaving the plantain weak, thin, and unable to produce heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo niji babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow poorly if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your main crops. Clearing them early ensures that all the goodness in the soil goes directly to your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa nibii kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ náa onibii anɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen. Heavy rains often wash nutrients deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach them, or waterlogged soil prevents roots from absorbing food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing leaves and drop their flowers when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat causes pepper plants to experience stress, so they shed flowers and slow down leaf growth to save water and protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ adalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛkagbi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees build strength during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ woɔ hewalɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting directly on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, highly humid conditions, especially when air cannot flow freely through overcrowded branches.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli oya.

english: Yams become misshapen when the soil is hard and compacted, making it difficult for the tuber to expand freely, or when tiny root pests called nematodes attack the growing tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa yitso lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa ehe. aloo beni shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava early in the rainy season instead of waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli moŋ fe ni ooomɛ lɛ?

english: Planting early gives cassava roots enough wet soil to build a strong root network, allowing the crop to store energy and survive later dry spells without losing yield.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi akuu ni mli wa ama. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtoɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ sɛɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli ni nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there are too few pollinating insects like bees visiting the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni foɔ koni amɛyakwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe lɛ faaa tsɔ.

english: Why do my garden eggs get small brown holes on the skin before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ dani efee klalo akɛ akɛbaato?

english: Small holes in garden eggs are caused by fruit borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid on the flowers and chew their way inside the growing vegetable.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii amli lɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛyeɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up and feel sticky when I touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ he kɛji mita he lɛ?

english: Curling, sticky leaves are caused by sap-sucking insects called aphids that feed on the leaves and leave behind a sugary substance that makes the surface sticky.
ga: Koolooi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ aphids lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle, ni wa baa. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ nɔ ko ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋwɛi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and open instead of forming a tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbele yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, suffer from erratic watering, or experience severe heat during the head-forming stage.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ejaaa loo naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ be mli ni afee yitso lɛ.

english: Why is April a good time for me to start applying fertilizer or treatment to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ April ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofafeemɔ lɛ?

english: April marks the beginning of the major rainy season in Ghana. Applying treatments early in this period ensures the soil is moist enough for the roots to easily absorb nutrients, boosting flower and pod growth.
ga: April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai tsu nii mra yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: What will happen to my cocoa yield if I apply treatments too late in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: If you apply treatments late, the trees miss their primary growth phase during the rains, resulting in fewer cocoa pods, smaller bean sizes, and higher vulnerability to pests.
