ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsu nii Tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛdalɛ be titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo ko pɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraaa. ni amɛyɔɔ oshara babaoo kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees start flowering and growing new leaves when the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni amɛjieɔ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Early rains signal to the cocoa tree that moisture is available again after the dry season, prompting it to break dormancy, put out new leaves, and form flowers that turn into pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ji okadi kɛha kookoo tsei lɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baaba ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ fãa, ewoɔ baai heei, ni efeɔ fɔfɔi ni tsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Will heavy rain wash away the treatment if I apply it to my cocoa trees during the rainy month?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie tsofa lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ amli?

english: If applied right before a downpour, heavy rain can wash away chemical treatments. It is best to apply when light rain is expected so the moisture helps sink the nutrients into the root zone.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsofai. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ baanɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ boteɔ shishifã lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear or brush the weeds around my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie loo mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Kakao ni afeɔ daa

english: Weeds compete with cocoa trees for water, light, and soil nutrients. Regular brushing keeps the tree base clean, reduces pest hideouts, and lowers the risk of black pod disease.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ brɔshi tsu nii daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishi he tseɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni okɛ black pod hela lɛ aba shi

english: Should I clear the bush on my cocoa farm before or after applying fertilizer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli loo beni miwo mli sɛɛ?

english: Always clear weeds before applying fertilizer. If you apply fertilizer while weeds are still present, the weeds will absorb the nutrients instead of your cocoa trees.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni jwɛi yɛ lolo lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if a new brushing tool or weed cutter is safe to use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɔne hee ni akɛfoɔ ŋmeii loo jwɛi ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A safe brushing tool should clear weeds quickly without cutting into the trunk or damaging the delicate feeder roots of the cocoa tree near the surface.
ga: Esa akɛ brɔshi dɛŋdade ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ajie jwɛi lɛ oya ni ekɛfooo tso lɛ shishi loo efiteee kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: If my neighbor treats their cocoa farm early and I wait, will my trees suffer?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kwɛ ekoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ mra ni mimɛ lɛ, ani mitsei lɛ baaná he sɛɛ?

english: Yes, pests and diseases from neighboring untreated farms can migrate to yours. Treating your trees early along with neighboring farms creates a shield that protects the whole area.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni atsaaa amɛ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ afã kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ otsei lɛ mra. Ekɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ jɛmɛ fɛɛ he.

english: While I am waiting to receive spraying chemicals or fertilizer, is there anything I should do on my farm?
ga: Be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛná tsofai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Mɛni esa akɛ afee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can prune dead branches, clear weeds, and remove diseased pods so that your farm is clean and ready to benefit immediately once inputs arrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ, jwɛi ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaná he sɛɛ kɛji nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bashɛ pɛ.

english: How long does it take for cocoa trees to show improvements after early season treatment?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani cacao tsei lɛ ajie hiɛyaa kpo yɛ be mli ni atsa amɛ mra lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Trees usually show visible improvements like greener leaves within 2 to 3 weeks, followed by healthier flower formation over the following month if water is available.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei jieɔ hiɛyaa ni anaa tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ nyɔŋ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli kɛji nu yɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the ground is overly soaked with water, which prevents the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my corn cobs have missing kernels and empty spots when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ ekomɛi amli ŋmeii lɛ elaaje kɛ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty spots on corn cobs happen when pollination fails during hot, dry weather or when stalks are planted too far apart for the wind to carry pollen effectively from one plant to another.
ga: He ko ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. aloo be mli ni tsei ashishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ aŋɔ pollen kɛjɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to save corn seeds from my harvest to plant next season, or should I buy fresh seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahere ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Saved seeds from harvested hybrid corn gradually lose their strength and produce lower yields each season, whereas buying fresh certified seeds ensures uniform growth, higher yield, and better disease resistance.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ fiofio. Ehewalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha amɛdara daa lɛ. Ha nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rain pattern keeps changing every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Akɛni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi hewɔ lɛ

english: Instead of planting on a fixed date, wait until the soil receives two or three good, steady rains and stays moist down to the depth of your finger before sowing your seeds.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kpakpai 2-3 ni nɛɔ daa ni ehaa edɔ kɛyashɛɔ oniji amli dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over easily whenever a small wind blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when roots are shallow due to hard soil, when seeds are planted too close together, or when insect pests damage the lower stem and roots.
ga: Tsoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa hewɔ. Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food. Under big shade trees, plants stretch upwards trying to reach light, leaving them weak, thin, and unable to produce good yield.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ shishi Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni emɔ la lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops look weak and small even though I give them enough water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crop growth. Plants also need essential plant foods like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium from manure or fertilizer to build strong stems and healthy leaves.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa kɛha tsei adalɛ. Tsei hu he miihia tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni wa.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable crops curl up and feel sticky during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled and sticky leaves are caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves, drink the plant's sap, and leave behind a sweet, sticky waste.
ga: Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ baa. nu tso mli nu ni eshiɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before the flowers can turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the soil causing green leaves to grow instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa baai eŋɔlii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests to build up; rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or tree cover to protect them and keep the surrounding soil moist during their first few years of growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛdaraa lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nitrogen boost they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen babaoo ni baaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots drown from a lack of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do small caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants and chew holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft growing center of maize plants. Spraying early in the morning or late afternoon when the caterpillars come out to feed helps protect the plant before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi loo shwane mli Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ, amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa kɛbuɔ tso lɛ he dani amɛfiteɔ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the moisture steady in the soil helps the plant retain its flowers so they can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ba daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing big harvests when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and large fruits, they stretch upward for light and stay weak.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nguahi. Mohu ɔ, e ngmɛɛ e he konɛ la nɛ ba mi, nɛ e ya nɔ nɛ e he gbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy winds right when the fruit bunch gets large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛ be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a full fruit bunch, especially in wet soil. Supporting the trunk with bamboo or wooden props prevents wind from uprooting the tree.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ajie tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the branches during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow into the farm, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crop seeds after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and climate, so their seeds wake up instantly when rain falls. Clearing weeds early gives your sown crops a fair chance to establish their roots first.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ lɛ mli tsei ni atsɔ adebɔɔ nɔ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tsei ni odu lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from my harvested hybrid maize for the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield only once. If you save and replant those harvested seeds, the new crop will grow unevenly and yield much less grain than the original parent seed.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo shikome pɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ dumɔwui fioo pɛ baaba fe shishijee fɔlɔ dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when the sun is too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily and lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it. They require shade trees like plantains during their early years to filter harsh sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains he miihia amɛ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. koni ekɛjie hulu la ni naa wa lɛ

english: Is full direct sunlight good or bad for a mature cocoa farm?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda?

english: While full sunlight can increase short-term yield if fertilizers and water are abundant, excessive unshaded sun stresses the trees, dries out the soil, and significantly shortens the lifespan of the cocoa farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ. Shi hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ awala feɔ kuku waa.

english: Why are tiny, young cocoa pods shriveling up and turning black on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This natural response is called cherelle wilt. When the tree experiences stress from nutrient shortage, water lack, or sudden sunlight changes, it rejects surplus young pods to conserve energy for the rest of the tree.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli hetoo nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Beni tsei naa haomɔ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo hulu la ni tsakeɔ trukaa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ kpooɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects called midges for pollination. If weather conditions are too dry, if heavy shade blocks insect movement, or if the tree is stressed, unpollinated flowers naturally fall off without producing pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Kɛji hulutsoo be ni tsii tsiɔ kooloi agbɛfaa naa loo kɛji tso lɛ miihao Fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and drop during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The Harmattan brings low humidity and dry winds that rapidly strip water from leaves. The cocoa tree sheds its leaves as a survival mechanism to minimize water loss from its branches and trunk.
ga: Harmattan kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya baa. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni jɛɔ amɛniji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do black spots spread so quickly on my cocoa pods during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture and heavy rainfall create the ideal environment for fungal spores that cause Black Pod disease. Excess moisture on pod surfaces allows the fungus to enter and destroy the pod quickly.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni kɛ blackpod hela baa lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ pod lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli ni efiteɔ pod lɛ oya.

english: Can I plant cassava right next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe?

english: It is not recommended because cassava is an aggressive feeder that competes heavily with young cocoa for soil nutrients and moisture, often stunting the growth of the cocoa trees.
ga: Akɛ enɛ haaa ejaakɛ ŋmei ji ŋmei ni yeɔ nii waa ni ekɛ ŋmei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsiɔ kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow better under large forest trees than on completely cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ kooi amli fe hei ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ?

english: Forest trees create a humid microclimate, protect cocoa from harsh winds, drop leaf litter that enriches the soil, and shield the farm from extreme temperature spikes.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ baa. Buu kookoo he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Shĩ baai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashwie. ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he

english: Why do I need to cut off dead or excess branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive branches that waste energy, allows filtered sunlight and air to circulate through the canopy, and encourages the tree to direct nutrients toward healthy flower and pod development.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii ni fiteɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni atsɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. ni ekanyaa tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ amaje fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni he wa lɛ adalɛ

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If cocoa trees grow very tall and thin with few leaves at the bottom, or if flowers fail to blossom due to damp, dark conditions, the canopy above is likely too dense and needs thinning.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da waa ni efee mlɛo ni baai fioo pɛ yɔɔ shishigbɛ. aloo kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ efɔɔɔ yɛ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ duŋ hewɔ lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hu fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni ehe hiaa ni afee lɛ bibioo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or urea fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is causing holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa kaaba baa mli? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by tiny caterpillars eating the leaves. You can protect your crop by spraying natural neem leaf extracts or recommended insecticides, and keeping the farm free of weeds where pests hide.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. ye cabbage baai Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oha jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I space my cassava stems far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbala mi-cassava tsei lɛ amli yɛ he kome moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Cassava roots need room underground to swell up and grow big tubers. If you plant them too close, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfu. Kɛji odu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil gets too dry, or when bees aren't visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering and keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii baaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up. This sign shows that the plant has finished growing and stored all its food energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe edalɛ naa ni ekɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ewo eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the moisture goes straight to the roots before the hot sun dries it up. Afternoon watering causes water to evaporate too quickly and can stress wet leaves in high heat.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha amɛgbi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha baai ni efɔ lɛ ashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nutrients from the soil. Cowpeas and groundnuts are special plants that put fresh nitrogen back into the soil naturally, making the land rich again for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ nitrogen hee baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the second generation. If you plant saved hybrid seeds, the crop will grow unevenly and produce smaller cob yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ cob fioo pɛ baaha kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my crops even during short dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that steal food, water, and light away from your farm crops very quickly. Removing weeds early gives your crops the strength to outgrow them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa, ni amɛshishifãi mli kwɔ ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii amli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya fe amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa tree's early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this nutrient.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep soil to expand smoothly. If the soil is too hard, stony, or clay-heavy, the tubers struggle to push through and end up bent, short, or small.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eji shikpɔŋ lɛ Tubers lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaagbe naa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛfee kuku, loo amɛfee bibioo.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the plant from growing properly and reduces tuber size.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: What causes small holes to appear all over my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves of the plant and eat the tender green tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ baai teŋgbɛ ni amɛ yeɔ fãji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during heavy rains when air cannot flow freely around the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle tsei lɛ ahe oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil gets too dry. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves dry up and fall off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni yitso lɛ fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air as well as water. When heavy rains leave water sitting in the soil, the roots drown and cannot absorb nutrients until the soil drains.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia pepper shishifãi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwɛɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyashi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu baaho.

english: If I cut a stem from a sick cassava plant to grow a new one, will the new plant be sick too?
ga: Kɛji ofo ŋmei tso ni hela mɔ lɛ ni odu ehee. Ani tso hee lɛ hu baaná hela?

english: Yes, because the new stem cutting is part of the parent plant's body. Any disease or virus inside the sap of the parent plant moves directly into the new stem and grows along with it.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ tso lɛ yitso hee ni afo lɛ fata tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he. hela loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ Yɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã hee lɛ mli ni ekɛ lɛ daa.

english: Can disease travel from one plantain tree to another through my harvesting cutlass?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ atsɔ mikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ dumɔwu kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, when you cut a diseased tree, infected sap sticks to your blade. When you cut a healthy tree afterwards, those disease germs enter through the open cut, infecting the healthy plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofo tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ Latex ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ baakpɛtɛ otsɔne lɛ he. Beni ofo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ sɛɛ Nakai helai lɛ baatsɔ tsei niji ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ amɛbote mli. ni ekɛ hela baa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: If one yam tuber gets rot in a mound, why does it quickly spread to the other tubers nearby?
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmei ko fite yɛ muji lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Tubers sharing the same mound are connected through the moist soil and close root space. Water in the soil carries disease germs straight from the rotten tuber into the cuts or skins of nearby tubers.
ga: Tubers ni jaa sũ lɛ tsaa kɛtsɔɔ sũ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa. Nu ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egboi amli kɛyaa pilamɔi loo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahewolo nɔ.

english: Why do plantain suckers grow so much faster than crops planted from seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui daa oya fe tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: A sucker stays connected to the mother plant's roots and food store early on, drawing direct nourishment from the mother while developing its own leaves.
ga: Suckers lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ shishifãi kɛ niyenii atoohei lɛ kpaa gbee mra. Egbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ.

english: Extra suckers drink sap and nutrients away from the main mother tree. Removing them ensures all the plant's food goes into developing one big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi lɛ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ feɔ plantains ŋmɔ agbo kome ni tsii.

english: How does grafting a branch from a mature fruit tree onto a young seedling make it bear fruit faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ni woɔ yibii ni egbɔ lɛ ni akɛaawo tso bibioo ko mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ewo yibii oya?

english: Grafting fuses the water channels of the stem and rootstock together. The young stem receives nutrients instantly from established roots, skipping years of slow youthful growth.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Tsoi bibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni etswa ama shi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ehe ehiaaa ni etsɔ oblahiiaŋ ŋmɔnɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ mli afii babaoo

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and weak when I plant four seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Plants growing in the exact same spot share a small area of soil. They end up competing for the same food and water, leaving every plant malnourished.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ jaa shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ. Amɛgbeɔ naa kɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. ni haa tsei fɛɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the bigger trees from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like delicate seedlings that cannot handle strong direct sunlight. Larger canopy trees act as protective mother trees, filtering heat and keeping moisture in the air.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ dumɔwui bibii ni nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei agbo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nyɛ tso ni buɔ mɔ he. Efoɔ dɔlɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to collect seeds only from the healthiest cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔbua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Seeds inherit life traits from the parent plant. Seeds taken from strong, disease-resistant trees are much more likely to produce healthy plants with abundant pods.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ wala sui kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do nursery seeds need a palm-frond shade canopy before they are transplanted into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ hulutsoo dani adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tender young sprouts lose water very quickly in open heat. A shade canopy creates a gentle, humid environment that protects fragile young shoots until their stems are strong enough for the sun.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ. Shade lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Enɛ buɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I collect seeds from my own harvested palm nuts to plant a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-palm tso lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Most commercial palm nuts are hybrids bred from two specific parent trees. Seeds collected from a hybrid tree will not produce the same high yield as the parent plant, often resulting in lower oil content or trees that produce mostly male flowers.
ga: Palm tsei ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji tsofai ni akɛfee tsei pɔtɛɛ enyɔ ni afɔɔ amɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa fɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi loo tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo lɛ baa shi.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says a palm seedling is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Kɛji extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ palm dumɔwui ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid crop is created by controlled breeding between two different parent varieties to combine their best traits—such as high oil yield, thin shells, and disease resistance. Because of this mix, hybrid plants grow strong, but their own seeds cannot be saved for replanting.
ga: Afeɔ tsei ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi srɔtoi enyɔ ni akudɔ amɛ ni akɛ amɛ feɔ ekome lɛ nɔ koni akɛ sui ni hi fe fɛɛ, tamɔ fɔ ni fa babaoo, amɛhewolo ni mli tseee, kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ afata he. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ daa waa. Shi anyɛɛɛ ahere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ayiwala koni akɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: My neighbor offered me extra palm seedlings from his farm. How can I know if they will produce good fruit?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ ŋmei tsei krokomɛi ni jɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ha mi. Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ebaawo yibii kpakpai?

english: You cannot tell a seedling's quality just by looking at its leaves. Unless the seedlings come from certified germinated seeds bought from an approved research center like OPRI, they may be wild varieties that yield very little oil and take longer to fruit.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni dumɔwu ko hi ha kɛtsɔ baai lɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ kɛkɛ. Ja dumɔwui lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ OPRI lɛ mli, no lɛ ekolɛ amɛji koo mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ mu fioo ko pɛ ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do some of my oil palm trees only produce flowers but never grow fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ekomɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi pɛ shi amɛkwɛɛɛ ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce both male and female flowers. Only female flowers can develop into palm nut bunches, while male flowers only provide pollen. If a tree is stressed or comes from uncertified seed, it may produce mostly male flowers.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei fɛɛ. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ baanyɛ atsɔ panicles. yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi hii lɛ woɔ pollen pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ he ejɔ loo ejɛ dumɔwui ni atsɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ ewo fɔfɔi hii babaoo.

english: Can an oil palm tree change from producing male flowers to producing female flowers?
ga: Ani mu tsei baanyɛ atsake kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛya fɔfɔi yei amli?

english: Yes, an oil palm tree produces male and female flowers in cycles. Providing your trees with enough water, fertilizer, and good sunlight encourages them to produce more female flowers, which turn into fruit bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei yɛ sɛɛkuu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kpakpa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ha tso lɛ, ebaawo lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi yei babaoo. ni tsɔ aduawai akuu ko

english: How do male and female palm flowers work together to give me a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: The male flower produces pollen, which is carried by the wind and small insects to fertilize the female flower. Once fertilized, the female flower grows into a full bunch of palm nuts rich in oil.
ga: Fɔfɔi hii feɔ pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ kooloi bibii kɛyaa. Ba ni okɛ fɔfɔi yei abafɔ. Kɛji akɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi yei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei tsei ni mu eyi mli obɔ.

english: If I buy palm nuts in large quantities during the harvest season, can I put them directly in the soil to grow?
ga: Kɛ mihe ŋmei ŋmeii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni madu?

english: No, raw palm nuts have very hard outer shells and natural dormancy. If you put them directly into the ground, very few will sprout. They require special heat treatment and controlled nursery conditions before they can germinate properly.
ga: Dabi, palm nuts ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa waa, ni eji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni wɔɔ. Kɛ adu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nɔ fioo ko pɛ baakwɛ̃. Amɛbiɔ hulutsoo krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of the year to transplant my young palm trees into the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu mi-palm tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant your palm seedlings at the beginning of the main rainy season, usually around April or May in Ghana. This allows the young roots to absorb enough moisture and settle firmly before the dry season begins.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ yaa nɔ yɛ April loo May mli yɛ Ghana. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛmaa shi shiŋŋ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why do the palm fruits from commercial farms have thin shells while my local palm nuts have thick shells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yibii ni jɛɔ jarayeli ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-palm aduawai ni yɔɔ shia lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Commercial farms use an improved hybrid variety called Tenera, which has thin shells and thick oil flesh. Local or wild varieties, known as Dura, have very thick shells and less oil flesh, giving lower yields per bunch.
ga: Jarayeli ŋmɔji kɛ tso ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni atsɛɔ lɛ Tenera lɛ tsuɔ nii. ni yɔɔ ŋmei bibioo kɛ fɔ ni mli edɔ Atsɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli loo koo mli ŋmei lɛ dura. Eyɛ ŋmei ni mli tse waa kɛ loo fioo ni mli ewo mu. ni haa yibiiwoo ni anáa kɛjɛɔ kuu kome mli lɛ baa shi

english: How close together should I plant my oil palm trees so they don't fight for light?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-oil palm tsei lɛ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni amɛkatswa la he akaŋ?

english: Oil palm trees need plenty of sunlight to produce female flowers. Planting them about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern gives each tree enough space for its leaves to spread without blocking light from neighboring trees.
ga: Mu tsei he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi yei. Kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋtɛi etɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa lɛ baagbɛ eshwaa ni etsĩii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akane lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by the harsh sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist while your cocoa trees are establishing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between my crops instead of planting them close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other, resulting in weak plants and small fruits. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food for green growth, or when water has settled around the roots for too long. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer brings back the healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii daa loo be mli ni nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in between my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and improves the growth of your main crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my maize plants and leaving tiny holes and dirt?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii? kɛ muji?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that feeds inside the growing point of maize plants. Spraying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ nii yɛ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa yɛ lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ŋaawoo haa leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: This sudden drying is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, which lives in the soil and blocks water from moving up the stem. Rotating your tomato farm with non-vegetable crops like maize helps clear the disease from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho tso lɛ nɔ. Tomato ŋmɔji ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jeee aduawai, tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi haa he ni amɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from drying up quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and quickly suck up the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ, ni amɛmuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather is too hot and dry or when they don't get steady water. Mulching around the base and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni amɛnáaa nu daa Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready to dig up from the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can also gently dig around one stem to check if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo hu abɔle tso kome he koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and turn brown when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their young roots cannot absorb water fast enough to replace what the hot sun evaporates from their leaves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye nɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ efo kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their small flowers before pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers to save energy so they can focus their water and nutrients on growing only the pods they can support.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ ahi ŋmeii ni cacao tso lɛ baanyɛ aye abua lɛ pɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ni akpa ehee lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Covering cocoa beans ferments them, which stops them from germinating, develops the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for, and turns the inside of the bean brown.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni akɛhaa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa. ni otsake dumɔwui lɛ amli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize plants need to build strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmã tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot and turn dark just two days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni amɛfee diŋŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to react with air as soon as they are dug up from the soil, causing rapid decay because they lack a thick protective skin.
ga: Kasava shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ekome kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛ. Enɛ haa egboɔ oya yɛ hewolo ni mli tse ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main trunk, which reduces the number of cocoa pods the tree can produce.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsɔne wulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: How does leaving dead plantain leaves around the base of my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Plantain baai ni egboi ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dead leaves act like a protective blanket over the soil, trapping groundwater underneath and stopping the hot sun from drying out the root zone.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu toɔ shishi, ni ehaaa hulu lɛ adɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ fe nine.

english: Why do my yam plants grow bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso ha wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for the tubers while keeping the leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛha bulb lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akashɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the farm stays dark and wet during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ lolo ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that thrives in wet, damp shade where air cannot blow through freely to dry out the trees.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli oya ni eha tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I keep planting the exact same crop on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ naaa niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously consumes the same specific nutrients from the soil every season until the ground becomes completely exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be daa be mli kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground toward the sun, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it good practice for me to plant cowpeas inside my maize farm at the same time?
ga: Cowpeas ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ be kome mli Ani enɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa kɛha mi?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for your maize while also shading the ground to stop weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tsina ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akpa.

english: Why must I nurse my pepper seeds in a small bed first instead of planting them directly on the main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikwɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and produce fragile sprouts that can easily be washed away by rain or eaten by pests. Nursing them allows you to protect and care for the tender seedlings until they grow strong enough for transplanting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni waaa ni nugbɔ baanyɛ ahoo loo ŋmeii baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ amɛhe ni okwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss caused by hot, dry winds. Providing shade trees and spreading dry mulch around the roots helps the soil keep moisture during Harmattan.
ga: Cocoa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ koni nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni egbi ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ harmattan beaŋ.

english: Why does cassava manage to survive on my farm even when rainfall stops for many months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nyɔji babaoo po lɛ?

english: Cassava is naturally drought-resistant; when water is scarce, it drops its upper leaves to save moisture and survives on the water and food energy stored inside its underground tubers.
ga: Cassava ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Kɛ nu faaa Ekɛ eŋwɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ nu kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato yɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a strong rainstorm blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that stay near the top soil, making them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Mounding dirt around the base and propping them up with wooden bamboo forks gives them extra support against wind.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Ha amɛfee nɔ ni tsii beni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he ni akɛ ŋmei fɔk fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa abuɔ he babaoo kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, preventing it from forming a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen lɛ. ni etsĩɔ tomato feemɔ naa.

english: What happens to my soil when I place dry bush grass around the roots of my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: Placing dry grass around crop roots is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under hot weather, stops moisture from evaporating, and eventually rots into rich compost for your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso shishifãi ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaagbo ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Small holes in young maize shoots are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating the leaf tissue. Catching them early allows you to spray organic remedies like neem oil or appropriate treatments before they destroy the plant's growing center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni sa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ. dani amɛbaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: How can I look at my crops and tell if my soil lacks proper plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni sa?

english: Crops show signs through their leaves: pale or yellowing leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, leaves turning purple or reddish point to low phosphorus, and leaves with brown, burnt edges mean the soil lacks potassium.
ga: Tsei jieɔ okadii kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ: bei pii lɛ, baa ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Baai ni tsɔɔ purple loo etsuru lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ phosphorus faaa. Ni baai ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Does a cocoa tree keep growing year after year, or do I have to replant it every season?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei daa afi loo esa akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ daa afi?

english: Cocoa grows continuously every year as a perennial tree, but because it stays in the ground long-term, it can be attacked by diseases throughout its lifetime.
ga: Cocoa yaa nɔ edaa afi fɛɛ afi akɛ tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo. Shi akɛni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, helai baanyɛ atutua amɛ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: If I plant brand new cocoa seedlings on my farm today, are they safe from diseases?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛ midu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ahe?

english: New cocoa seedlings are not automatically safe; disease can affect any cocoa plant regardless of age, even ones planted today.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui heei bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɛɛ amɛhe. Helai baanyɛ aná kookoo tsei anɔ hewalɛ ekɔɔɔ afii ni amɛye lɛ he. Tsei ni adu amrɔ nɛɛ po

english: Is it possible for cocoa disease to spread to every single farm in our village?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ kookoo hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ wɔ akrowa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa diseases can affect any farm you go to because the insects that carry the infection move easily across farm boundaries.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo hela baanyɛ aná ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ ni oyasaraa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ, ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni hiɛ hela lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: What actually causes my cocoa trees to become sick?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ hela diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Many serious cocoa diseases are caused by viruses that live inside the tree and disrupt its growth.
ga: Virus ni hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa lɛ kɛ cocoo helai babaoo ni naa wa baa.

english: How does cocoa disease move from one tree to another across my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: The disease is moved by transmission agencies or vectors, which are small insects that carry the virus from an infected plant to a healthy one.
ga: Helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ loo nibii ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What are mealybugs, and why should I worry about them on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmeii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahao yɛ amɛhe yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Mealybugs are tiny insects that act as vectors; they suck sap from sick plants and spread the disease virus to healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Mealybugs ji kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can big forest trees like Onyina or Odwama on my land affect my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei wuji tamɔ Onyina loo Odwama ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, shade and forest trees like Onyina and Odwama can shelter the insects and viruses that cause cocoa disease, allowing infection to jump to your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kooi tamɔ Onina kɛ Odwama baanyɛ ahi kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni kɛ kookoo hela baa lɛ amli. ni eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Are there other wild plants near my bush that can harbour pests that attack cocoa?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei krokomɛi yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ mi koo lɛ ni baanyɛ ahi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa kookoo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, wild plants like Coccids can harbor disease-carrying mealybugs and serve as a source of infection for nearby cocoa farms.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei tamɔ Coccids baanyɛ ahi mealybugs ni hiɛ helai lɛ amli ni amɛha hela aba kookoo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell farmers to cut down sick cocoa trees instead of treating them with chemical sprays?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɛ okwaafoi lɛ akɛ amɛfolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Viral diseases inside cocoa trees cannot be cured with medicine; cutting down the sick tree is necessary to stop the virus from spreading to surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛ tsofa atsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni yɔɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ. Ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli.

english: What is the best action to take if an officer spots a diseased tree on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji onukpai lɛ na tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The infected cocoa tree must be uprooted or cut down completely to eliminate the virus and stop mealybugs from spreading it further.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie cacao tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ loo afolɔ amɛ kwraa koni ajie hela lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni atsĩ mealybugs lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa babaoo.

english: How often do I need to water my cabbage and tomato crops so they don't dry out?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo kaabii kɛ tomato nu koni amɛkagbi?

english: Vegetables like cabbage and green tomatoes have high water needs and require watering every single day to ensure continuous growth and keep the soil consistently moist.
ga: Nu he hiamɔ nii babaoo yɛ aduawai tamɔ cabbage kɛ green tomato mli ni esa akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ daa gbi koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens to my vegetable plants if I miss watering them for a couple of days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu shwieee nɔ gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Skipping water for sensitive crops like cabbage or tomatoes can slow down their growth, cause leaves to wilt, and reduce the overall quality and size of your yield at harvest.
ga: Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛhaa tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ kaabe loo tomato lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nɔ ni afee lɛ fɛɛ mli hilɛ kɛ elɛɛmɔ baa shi kɛ́ akpa.

english: Why do leafy crops like cabbage need more regular watering than some other field crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabe biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Leafy green vegetables expand rapidly and contain high water content in their tissues, making them dependent on daily moisture to build healthy, large leaves.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya ni nu babaoo yɔɔ amɛmli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ biɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa gbi koni amɛná baai agboi ni mli wa.

english: I just acquired a new plot of land to start farming, what basic steps should I plan for?
ga: Etsɛko tsɔ ni mihe shikpɔŋ hee koni mikɛje okwaayeli shishi. Mɛɛ shishijee nibii esa akɛ ato he gbɛjianɔ?

english: Starting a farm involves clearing the land, determining the financial costs for tools and seeds, choosing necessary soil inputs, and establishing a regular routine to manage your daily farm tasks.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɔ shishijee he ji shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Shika he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha nitsumɔ dadei kɛ dumɔwui ahe tsɔɔmɔ Shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ halamɔ kɛ daa gbi nifeemɔ ni okɛbaatsu odaa ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi ahe nii.

english: How can I figure out the total cost of starting crop farming on my new farm land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male shika fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ashishijee yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: To estimate total costs, you must calculate the price of land preparation, buying seed or seedlings, essential fertilizers or additives, daily labor, and maintenance until harvest.
ga: Kɛji ootao obu shika fɛɛ ni he baahia lɛ he akɔntaa Esa akɛ obu shika ni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he akɔntaa. Dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ahemɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo nibii ni akɛfataa he ni he hiaa Daa gbi nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛ ekwɛmɔ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ

english: How do I know what extra materials or fertilizers to add to my newly planted farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ ni midu ehee lɛ he?

english: The inputs you add depend on your soil condition and crop choice; adding well-rotted manure or balanced crop nutrients early on helps supply essential food for steady plant development.
ga: Nibii ni okɛfataa he lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shihilɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ohalaa lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo tsei amli niyenii ni sa fataa he mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ aya nɔ aya hiɛ.

english: My crops have been in the ground for two weeks and are growing quickly, how should I care for them now?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii enyɔ nɛ ni amɛmiida oya. Te esa akɛ makwɛ amɛ aha tɛŋŋ bianɛ?

english: At the two-week mark, young plants enter a fast growth phase where they need consistent daily water, protection from early pests, and clear soil around them free of competing weeds.
ga: Otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baabote dalɛ be lɛ mli oya. Nu he miihia amɛ daa gbi. Ayɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni bɔle Tsei ni jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ

english: How should I structure my daily farm activities to ensure my crops grow big and healthy?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mato mi daa gbi ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: A good daily routine involves checking your crops early in the morning, watering them consistently, inspecting for damage or disease, and applying necessary nutrients at the right stages.
ga: Nɔ ni hi ni ofeɔ daa gbi ji ni okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi. Nu daa Kwɛmɔ kɛji nɔ ko efite loo hela ko bɛ mli. ni okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ atsu nii yɛ he ni sa

english: Why do sensitive crops like tomatoes demand so much of my time when it is near harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato he hiaa mibe babaoo beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ miibɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: As crops approach harvest, they need close daily monitoring to ensure they receive steady water, remain healthy, and are picked right at peak maturity to avoid spoilage.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ kpakpa mli ni ahalaa amɛ kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa koni amɛkafite.

english: How much time do I need to commit to my vegetable farm during the growing period?
ga: Be enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mikɛdu aduawai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Vegetable farming requires a daily time commitment; setting aside dedicated time every single day for tasks like irrigation and field checks is necessary to secure a successful harvest.
ga: Aduawai abɔɔ mli nitsumɔ heɔ be daa gbi. Be ni akɛhaa daa gbi kɛha nitsumɔi tamɔ nu shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ. Ehe miihia kɛha nikpamɔ ni yeɔ omanye.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaasaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stay short and stunted even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ lɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted growth often happens when the soil is too hard for roots to spread, or when tiny worms called nematodes are attacking the roots. Mixing compost into the soil before planting loosens it up and feeds the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo beni ŋmei bibioo ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes lɛ miitutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee mlɛo ni eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look twisted during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up to reduce the amount of water they lose in the hot sun. While it is a natural self-defense against heat, severe curling can also be a sign of whiteflies carrying the cassava mosaic virus.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ laajeɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ eji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he moŋ. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ afee ŋmeii yɛŋ, ni ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ he okadi.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea plants fold up in the late afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants naturally fold their leaves late in the day to preserve moisture and protect themselves from cool evening air. This is normal plant behavior and means the plant is healthy and responding to its environment.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ he. Enɛ ji tso subaŋ ni sa ni etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​eshihilɛhe lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep dropping off instead of growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Providing light shade and watering regularly during hot dry spells helps fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade ni akɛhaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛmaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ etsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods wilt and dry up either because the tree has more pods than it can feed, or due to black pod disease caused by excessive shade and dampness. Pruning shade trees allows sunlight and air to keep the pod healthy.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbi ejaakɛ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. Aloo black pod hela ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: High soil mounds give yam tubers loose, soft earth so they can expand easily without resistance. Mounds also protect the roots from rotting in standing water during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe feɔ blɛoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa mlɛo ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Gɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops immediately after the first major rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first major rain triggers a natural release of nutrients trapped in dry soil, known as a nitrogen flush. Planting immediately gives seeds a head start to grow deep roots before any temporary dry spell hits.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ jeɔ kpo. Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ nitrogen flɔsh. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ baaye abua ni amɛje shishifãi ni mli kwɔ shishi dani be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi aba.

english: Why are there so many small holes appearing in the leaves of my cabbages?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Mɛi babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ mi kaabaji baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, eating the leaves. Spraying neem leaf extract or intercropping with onions helps drive these pests away naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo ni akɛ sabolai baadu lɛ baashwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Plantain suckers grow slowly if too many secondary suckers are competing with them for food and water. Cutting away extra suckers leaves all the soil nutrients for the main plant to fruit quickly.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛji akɛ tsei ni ji enyɔ lɛ fa babaoo ni kɛ amɛ miitswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo koni eye ebua tso titri lɛ ni ewo yibii oya.

english: Why do my crops get sick when I leave rotten fruits and weeds around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela kɛ́ mishi aduawai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rotting plants and weeds harbor pests, bacteria, and fungi that easily spread to healthy crops. Keeping your farm clean prevents disease outbreaks and protects your yield.
ga: Tsei kɛ jwɛi ni egboi lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaba, ni ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to space my maize plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ abɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small ears. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during the dry season?
