ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl during dry periods to reduce water loss from sunlight. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water and survive drought.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni ekɛbuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Consistent watering helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa loo pollination ni bɛ Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Cowpeas and beans capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for your maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting tomatoes in the exact same plot where I harvested them last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tomato dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting tomatoes repeatedly in the same spot allows soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like corn or beans starves those pests and restores soil balance.
ga: Tomato ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable crops during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mikɛhaa mitsei lɛ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ehiii kɛhaaa mi lɛ?

english: Watering under bright sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can absorb it, and wet leaves in high heat can suffer sun scorch or fungal growth.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni baai ni efɔ ni akɛwoɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo loo ŋmeii ada.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants start turning yellow and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves show that the yam plant has finished growing above ground and is transferring its remaining energy into swelling the tuber underground for harvest.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ naa. Ni eetsɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do holes keep appearing in the leaves of my cabbage crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by insects like diamondback moth caterpillars eating the plant. Clearing weeds and catching pests early prevents leaf loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi, tamɔ diamondback caterpillars, ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa cabbage baai amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amɔmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil or isn't getting enough water. Applying fertilizers like NPK or animal manure at the right stage helps the plant stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why does my land produce very few crops even though farming land in Ghana is naturally fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nii fioo nɛkɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ moŋ, shi.

english: Farming on the same piece of land year after year without replacing nutrients drains the soil of its natural strength. Adding organic compost, rotating crops, or planting beans can rebuild the soil's fertility naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni atsakeee niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he, ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ, loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout properly after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds require consistent moisture and loose soil to germinate. Planting in dry soil, planting too deep, or using seeds damaged by heat or insects will prevent the seeds from sprouting.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dumɔ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ loo kɛ dumɔwui ni latsaa loo kooloi efite lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why are my corn cobs coming out very small with many missing grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo bibii waa ni ŋmeii babaoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Incomplete cobs usually happen when the plant lacks water or nutrients while flowering, or when wind pollination is poor due to planting seeds too far apart from each other.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni amɛmiifɔlɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ tsɔ.

english: What other crops can I grow in Ghana to feed my farm animals when maize is scarce or expensive?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana koni mikɛye kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ be mli ni ŋmãa faaa loo ejara wa lɛ?

english: Cassava, sorghum, and sweet potatoes are great alternative feed crops. Processed cassava root meal and sorghum grains offer high energy for livestock when maize is hard to find.
ga: Cassava, sorghum kɛ sweet potato ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii krokomɛi. Cassava ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni atsu he nii lɛ haa kooloi hewalɛ babaoo kɛ́ ŋmãa faaa.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts or beans makes the ground better for next season's crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving free plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the center leaves of my young corn plants before they grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. Checking your fields early and applying recommended pest treatments when the plants are small protects the growing tip from being destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves twist up and show pale spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies or infected planting stems. Using disease-resistant stem varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ́ akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die faster than my neighbor's crops when the dry spell begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya fe mikutsoŋbii lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Crops with shallow roots or soil with low organic matter lose water very quickly during dry periods. Adding compost or organic mulch holds water in the soil like a sponge and helps plant roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ sponji. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: How can I store my harvested maize so that small insects do not turn it into dust?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato? Koni kooloi bibii akatsɔ sũ?

english: Insects need air and moisture to destroy stored grain. Thoroughly drying your maize in the sun and storing it in airtight (hermetic) storage bags starves pests of oxygen and keeps the grain safe without heavy chemicals.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia kooloi koni amɛfite ŋmaa ni ato lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii akabote kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli, ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii tsuuu nii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers alongside my young cocoa seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii ahe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and moist until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize crops grow better when I plant cowpea in the same soil after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with food that maize plants need for strong leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or heavy rains washing away nutrients. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot make chlorophyll, which gives leaves their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ efo mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa

english: Why does my cassava crop produce giant leaves above ground but very small tubers inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves and branches on top instead of storing starch in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji wuji yɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ ngmlɛfia ɔ kɛ woɔ tso ɔ sisi fã ɔmɛ a mi ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown, rot, and dry up right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and dark shade. When high rain levels keep the farm constantly wet, fungal spores spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i fe nine kɛ duŋ mli ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ahaa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and shrinking in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and drought stress that forces the plant to curl its leaves to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛfolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu nu he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my garden egg plants look wilted and weak in the afternoon hot sun even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the soil. The temporary wilting is a defense mechanism to reduce leaf exposure to the hot sun.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ ehe.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden drought or excess water. Stress causes the plant to drop blossoms to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba trukaa loo nu babaoo ba. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, space, and soil food. They stretch upward as high as possible to reach light, leaving little energy to develop thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, he ko, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee shɔŋŋ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná koni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: If stem cuttings are planted in waterlogged soil with poor drainage, oxygen cannot reach the cut end. This creates ideal conditions for soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the stem before roots can grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Oxygen nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni amɛfite tsei lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the early rains are steady enough for me to start planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ ehi shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Early rains can be deceiving. It is best to wait until the soil stays moist a few inches deep for three consecutive days, rather than planting after just one heavy rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ afee amale. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛyashɛ inchi fioo komɛi gbii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ hiɔmi nɛ nya wa si kake pɛ se.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which leads to thin, weak stalks and very small corn ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii waa baa.

english: Why are my corn plants forming small ears with missing grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ toi bibii ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains usually happen because of poor pollination during dry heat or because insects damaged the tassels and silk before pollination could finish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ. aloo akɛni kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmeii kɛ siliki lɛ dani pollination lɛ gbeɔ naa hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even when I planted them on time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Adu yɛ be naa?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients out of reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall and leafy but fail to produce big ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai shi ekɛ toi wuji baaa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems instead of developing the grain.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee dumɔwui

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that suck sap from the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ni ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or a shortage of specific soil nutrients like phosphorus during the blooming stage.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, hao amɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves dry up and get dark spots during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates high humidity that spreads fungal diseases like blight, which forms dark spots on leaves and quickly dries them out.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni mli wa baa ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa, ni no haa baa lɛ nɔ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egbiɔ oya.

english: Why is witchweed killing my maize even when I clear and weed my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ witchweed miigbe mi ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ?

english: Witchweed, also known as Striga, attaches itself directly to the roots of maize underground and steals food and water before it even appears above the soil.
ga: Witchweed, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ Striga lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu dani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: How do I stop insects from eating my harvested corn after putting it in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ naa beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Corn must be dried completely until the grains are hard before storage, and stored in airtight bags or treated with safe, recommended grain dust to keep insects out.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kwraa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ afee shiŋŋ dani akɛto. Ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ dumɔwui amli sũ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi akɛ awo mli lɛ awo nɔ koni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why should I clear and cut weeds on my field before I start digging the soil to plant my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds first removes competition for sunlight and nutrients, makes digging soil mounds much easier, and allows cut weeds to break down into useful organic matter for your crops.
ga: Shishijee jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛha hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli taomɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ mli lɛ mli ewoɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha onibii amli.

english: Can I leave the cut weeds lying on the soil after clearing my land, or will they spoil my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi jwɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Aloo ebaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on top of the soil helps protect the ground from burning in the sun, retains soil moisture, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I start digging planting mounds immediately, or must I finish cleaning up the field first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo esa akɛ magbe ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ naa klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to complete clearing and cleaning the ground first so you can see the field clearly, remove hard obstacles, and create clean, high-quality mounds for your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni otsumɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni ona ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Jiemɔ gbɛtsii nibii ni wa ni ofee shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do yams require soft, deeply dug soil or mounds instead of being planted directly in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo gɔji ahe hiaa sweet potato yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by expanding downwards into the earth; soft, deep soil gives the tuber space to swell easily, resulting in larger and smoother yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tuber he lɛ baagbɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens if I do not plant my seed yams properly in the ground after preparing the mounds?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ miduuu sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni misaa gɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: If seed yams are planted too shallow or exposed to direct heat, they can dry out, rot, or produce weak shoot buds instead of developing strong roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo akɛwo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ egbi, egbo loo ekɛ ŋmeii bibii aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená shishifãi ni mli wa

english: Why do some of my planted seed yams fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams may fail to sprout due to excess soil heat, poor seed quality, pest attack underground, or being planted in soil that is too dry.
ga: Ekolɛ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ hewɔ. dumɔwui ni ehiii lɛ Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa shikpɔŋ shishi loo aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ

english: If I buy and apply fertilizer to my yam farm, will that automatically make all my yams grow very large?
ga: Kɛ mihe mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛwo mli lɛ Ani mi-sweet potato lɛ baatsɔ agbo waa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Fertilizer supplies helpful plant food, but big yams also depend on soft soil depth, adequate rainfall, healthy planting material, and good soil management.
ga: Fertilizer haa tsei niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi ŋmeii wuji hu biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa

english: Is it possible for my yams to grow very big without using chemical fertilizers?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu sweet potatoes ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, if the soil is naturally rich in nutrients, soft, well-drained, and receives good rainfall, yams can yield very large tubers without added chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ eyi mli obɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛnáa nugbɔ nu kpakpa Sweet potatoes baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji waa ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do yams in one section of my farm grow much larger than yams in another section of the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ daa babaoo fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko mli lɛ?

english: Soil depth and nutrient content vary across a field; areas with deeper, richer soil and better moisture retention allow yam tubers to grow bigger.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ nii babaoo ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know when it is the exact right time to start digging mounds and planting my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: The best time to dig and plant is at the onset of the rain season when the soil becomes moist enough to dig easily and soft enough for seed yams to break dormancy.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsa ni adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akumɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni haa ŋmeii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Can I plant quick-growing vegetables like peppers and onions on the same farm plot as my young plantains?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sabolai. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-plantains bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop peppers and onions with young plantains. Because young plantains take several months to grow tall and create shade, planting short-term vegetable crops in between them makes good use of the open land, water, and sunlight before the plantain canopy closes.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ plantains bibii adu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ hulutsoo. Be kukuoo mli dumɔwui ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ateŋ lɛ heɔ he ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ dani plantain ŋwɛitsu lɛ ŋmɛɔ.

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots that have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong, heavy bulb at the bottom. These grow much faster, produce stronger plants, and give better yields than suckers with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai lɛ mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii yɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa. Ha tso lɛ mli awa ni ewo yibii kpakpai fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain plants turn yellow and dry up during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly in hot weather. When soil moisture drops, the plant sheds its lower leaves to survive. Adding a thick layer of dry grass or mulch around the base helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ba shi lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ baafata he. Kɛ́ abɔle shishitoo lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: How do I know when my pepper seedlings are ready to be moved from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaajɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Pepper seedlings are usually ready for transplanting about 4 to 6 weeks after sowing, once they are as tall as your index finger and have developed 4 to 6 strong green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha dumɔwui aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ. Beni dumɔwu lɛ kɛlɛ tamɔ onine ni tsɔɔ nɔ ko lɛ ni eyɛ baai 4 kɛyashi 6 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Keeping the field clear of weeds and using insecticidal soap or recommended remedies early on prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. He ni jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa he lɛ atsu nii mra lɛ he miihia waa. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What type of land is best for growing onions in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha sabala ŋmɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Onions grow best in loose, well-drained sandy loam soil that is rich in decayed organic matter or manure. Heavy clay soil makes it difficult for onion bulbs to expand and often leads to rotting.
ga: Sabolai kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii haa ewaa ahaa sabala akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa, ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell when my onions are fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-onions lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Onions are ready to harvest when the green tops naturally fall over and begin to dry up at the neck. Once about half to two-thirds of the crop leaves fall over, it is time to gently pull them up.
ga: Sabolai efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛtsitsi nɔ lɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ aaafee fã kɛyashi mlijaa enyɔ mli ekome gbee shi lɛ, Be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ agbala lɛ fiofio kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds around my crops on a regular monthly schedule?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ gbɛjianɔtoo naa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. Regular monthly clearing keeps weeds manageable before they choke crop roots and attract pests to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nyɔji amli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ dani amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli ni amɛgbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi awui lɛ kɛbaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I grow pepper in the exact same spot where I harvested pepper or tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he ni mifo ŋmeii loo tomato yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Growing crops from the same family in the same soil back-to-back causes soil-borne pests and diseases to build up. Rotating peppers with crops like maize, beans, or onions starves those pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nakai ŋmãa lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent my harvested green plantains from ripening too quickly before I take them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi green plantains lɛ anaa koni akakpa amɛ mra tsɔ dani mikɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Harvest plantain bunches when they are fully formed but still deep green. Store them in a cool, well-ventilated, shaded area away from direct sunlight, and keep them away from ripe fruits like papayas or bananas that emit ripening gases.
ga: Kpaa plantains beni jwɛi lɛ edara kwraa shi amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Kɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ jɛmɛ. Ekɛ ehe akabɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he Ni okɛto aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ tamɔ papaya loo banana ni jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and die when water stays on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water covers the ground for days, it drowns the roots, preventing them from taking up food and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni no haaa amɛye nii, ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Excess water staying in the soil creates a wet environment where tiny fungi and rot germs thrive, eating into the underground tubers before they can be harvested.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni eshwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ baa. he ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing poorly in the area where heavy tractors drove through my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni traktɔi wuji tsɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Heavy tractor wheels press the soil particles tightly together and squash the air holes. This makes the ground too hard for young plant roots to spread out and find water.
ga: Trakta shwiili ni tsii lɛ nyɛɔ sũ mli nibii bibii anɔ ni amɛkuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni tsei bibii ashishifãi nyɛŋ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna nu.

english: Why do weeds make my young crop plants grow slowly and look pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔwui lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops, stealing the fertilizer, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crop gets a chance to feed.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa trees the shade they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei lɛ náa hɔɔŋ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: When crops get too much shade or focus on leafy growth, they spend all their energy growing tall towards the sun instead of storing food in the tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo amɛsusu baai lɛ adalɛ he lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my maize plants give small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, leaving each plant with too little energy to build big maize cobs.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hewalɛ fioo tsɔ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without making any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress or dry soil, or when insects fail to visit the blossoms to carry pollen between them.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ ayasara fɔfɔi koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔtɔ

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up, so the plant curls its leaves to shield itself and reduce water loss until evening.
ga: Yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce mostly leaves in heavy rain, but start making pods when the rain decreases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi je pods feemɔ shishi beni nugbɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ?

english: Continuous heavy rain signals to the bean plant to focus on growing stems and leaves. When rainfall slows down, the plant senses a change and shifts its energy into making flowers and pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ nuɔ tsakemɔ lɛ he ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ mli ni ekɛfeɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves. It can also happen when too much rain sits around the roots, preventing them from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing big stems and leaves above ground instead of sending energy down to build heavy, starch-filled roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei agboi kɛ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ kɛba shi koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct heat from the sun. They need shade from temporary crops like plantains or shade trees to keep the soil cool and retain air moisture until their roots grow deep enough to survive on their own.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on in order to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ koni ewo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for tuber growth. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes also keeps the leaves dry and clean from soil-borne diseases that rot the leaves.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni haa baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I find small holes in my maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni Ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant to feed on the tender young leaves where sun and birds cannot reach them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii ni hulu la kɛ okpoi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, mites, or aphids hiding on the undersides of leaves. As they drink the leaf sap, they damage the leaf structure and can transmit viruses that distort plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ Amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ amɛshwã.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to save its own life when it does not have enough resources to feed developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. Yɛ hɔmɔ loo nu ni bɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala beni nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds right after the very first rainfall of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the top layer of soil and is followed by a hot dry spell. Seeds that sprout in this brief moisture will quickly dry out and die before the main rains establish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. ni nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji be ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli. Egbiɔ ni egboɔ oya dani nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my farm when the soil is moist instead of when it is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plant roots cannot eat dry fertilizer powder; they can only drink nutrients dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil in high heat can concentrate salts around roots and burn them.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋoo abua shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã amɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same patch of land every single season give me a smaller harvest each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize draws the exact same nutrients from the soil every year, eventually leaving the dirt empty of specific food. Continuous planting also allows pests and soil diseases that attack maize to multiply in that spot over time.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, enɛ haa niyenii komɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ hu haa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ nakai he lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are certified seeds bought from registered agro-dealers better than the seeds I save from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred and tested to resist common local pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce uniform crops with higher yields, whereas saved seeds lose these strong traits over time and produce weaker yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ su kome kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni baa shi.

english: Why does my hybrid maize yield so poorly if I take the seeds from my harvest and plant them again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid corn lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ nɛkɛ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds get their high yields from a special one-time cross between parent plants. When you replant seeds saved from a hybrid crop, that special vigor breaks down, resulting in uneven growth, small cobs, and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni ji fɔlɔi lɛ ateŋ tsakpaa krɛdɛɛ kome mli. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ. Nakai hewalɛ ni fa lɛ baafite. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Kob bibioo ko yɛ jɛmɛ. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: How can I test if a bag of groundnut seeds will sprout well before I spend time planting my whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji ŋmei dumɔwui kotoku kome baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani mafite be kɛdu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by placing ten sample seeds in a wet cloth or bowl of moist soil for a few days; if eight or more sprout healthy roots, the seed lot is good quality.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui nɔkwɛmɔnɔ 10 ni akɛaawo mama ni mli efɔ loo sũ ni mli ewo tsɛnsi mli gbii 2-3 nɔ, kɛji shishifãi kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai mli wa. Etsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow and dry up while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil is running out of nitrogen, so the plant is pulling nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the younger growing leaves and developing cobs at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ baa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato plants produce long, thick green leaves but very tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure, the plant uses all its energy to grow lush foliage above ground instead of storing sugars below ground to build big tuber roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ sugar baato shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee tuber shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, preventing any of them from growing strong enough to produce full cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do some of my cowpea seeds rot in the ground without sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to breathe as they sprout; if the soil remains waterlogged or the seeds are buried too deep, they suffocate and rot before they can break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo loo afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do cassava leaves curl up and develop yellow patches during the warm dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are typically signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that multiply quickly during warm weather and suck sap from the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the stem without producing any fruit when the hot season sets in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni ewooo yibii beni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Extremely hot weather damages tomato pollen, preventing the blossoms from fertilizing, so the plant sheds the useless flowers to conserve its energy and moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ tomato ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa amɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my cassava help make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for nearby crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very soft leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool ground moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to make green leaves. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains wash it away, the plant moves food from its lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ amɛbaai eŋɔlii lɛ Beni nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha nɔ hee ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot under the ground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater sits in heavy soil without draining away, it drowns the roots and allows rotting fungi to enter and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any small pods begin to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii bibii feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they are under stress, especially during short dry spells or when tiny insects like mirids attack the delicate flower stems. It is the tree's way of saving energy when conditions are not right to nurture growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛyɛ haomɔ mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ iris lɛ tutua fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he beni shihilɛi lɛ esaaa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Curling tomato leaves are usually a sign of leaf curl virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the sap. The virus changes how the leaf grows, causing it to twist and shrink, which stops the plant from making food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji leaf curl hela lɛ he okadi. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni etsakeɔ baai lɛ adalɛ. ni haa etsɔɔ ehe ni egbɔjɔɔ Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop down and dry out quickly during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan, hot dry winds pull water out of plant leaves very fast. Plantain leaves fold downwards and brown at the edges as a self-defense mechanism to reduce leaf surface area and slow down water loss.
ga: Yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli oya. Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo yɛ amɛnaagbɛ akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ he ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their tiny fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji efɔ fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when they experience water stress, very high heat, or a lack of calcium in the soil. If the plant feels it does not have enough water or nutrients to grow the pepper to full size, it discards the extra fruit early.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛyashɛ eshishijee he lɛ, mashɛrɛ aduawai ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why does my maize cob come out with missing or empty spaces instead of full rows of corn kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔji lɛ bɛ loo efee efolo yɛ abele ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Empty spots on a maize cob happen when hot, dry weather damages the pollen on top of the plant before it can reach the sticky silks on the ear. Every single silk must catch a grain of pollen for a corn kernel to grow.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ kpata ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ hiɛ dani enyɛ eshɛ siliki ni shwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ toi lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Esa akɛ siliki lɛ fɛɛ amɔmɔ pollen bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay small if I do not weed around the climbing vines early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ bibii lolo kɛji mikɛ jwɛi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Wein tsei akwɔɔ mra?

english: Yams build giant underground tubers using energy gathered by their leaves high up on stakes. If weeds grow thick around the base, they steal soil water and nutrients, leaving the yam vine too weak to send food down to build heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ hewalɛ ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ niyenii baa shi koni efee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my tall rice stalks fall over flat onto the mud right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, minɔ lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over—a problem called lodging—when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer. Excess fertilizer makes the stems grow tall, soft, and thin, so they become top-heavy and break easily under wind or heavy grain heads.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi—naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ wɔɔhe—kɛji amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe afee mlɛo, ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ amɛ oya.

english: Is it better for me to plant mango seeds from fruit I ate, or should I buy grafted seedlings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ mango dumɔwui kɛjɛ aduawai ni miyeɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Grafted seedlings are much better because they bear fruit in just 3 to 4 years, stay shorter for easy harvesting, and guarantee sweet fruit, whereas trees grown directly from seeds grow extremely tall and can take up to 8 years to produce.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 pɛ mli, ni amɛwala be kukuoo kɛha nikpamɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ akɛ ebaawo yibii ni ŋɔɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ daraa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehe afii 8 dani ewo yibii.

english: Can crop varieties or fruit trees imported from foreign countries grow successfully in our local weather and soil?
ga: Ani tsei srɔtoi loo aduawai tsei ni akɛba maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, many foreign tree varieties can thrive in Ghana if our temperature and rainfall match their needs, though extension officers often recommend grafted local varieties that naturally withstand local pests and dry seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋsɛɛ tsei babaoo baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ Ghana kɛji wɔ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ yeɔ wɔ taomɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ maŋ lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni akɛwo mli ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ anɔ lɛ he ŋaa moŋ, shi

english: Can I plant a mango tree near my house or compound, or does it strictly need to be out in a big farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu mango tso yɛ shia lɛ masɛi loo ebɔle he? Aloo esa akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko nɔ?

english: You can plant a mango tree near your compound as long as it gets full sunlight and has plenty of space around it, because mango trees grow very large over time and spread wide roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu mango tso yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ enine shɛ hulu ni fa nɔ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ edaa waa yɛ be ni sa mli ni egbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa babaoo.

english: How much space should I leave between my mango trees so they do not fight each other when they grow big?
ga: Te esa akɛ mango tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ahi teŋ bɔni afee ni nɔmɔ akafee kɛji tsei lɛ dara?

english: You should space permanent mango trees about 8 to 10 meters apart so their large branch canopies and root systems have plenty of room to expand without shading each other out.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ mango tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi, amɛniji wuji kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ aná he babaoo ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsiii amɛhe gbɛ.

english: Can I keep growing my usual cassava and maize on the same land while my new mango trees are still young and small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be mli ni mango tsei heei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop seasonal food crops like maize or vegetables between young mango trees during their first two to three years to earn food and income while waiting for the trees to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni akɛwoɔ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Mango tsei bibii ateŋ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ shika be mli ni amɛmɛɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right type of soil for long-term tree crops like mangoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ mango?

english: Mango trees need deep, loose, and well-drained soil where water does not sit for long periods, because standing water rots their deep taproots.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni nu lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shi be kakadaŋŋ Ejaakɛ nu ni ehi shi lɛ baaha taproot ni mli kwɔ lɛ agbo.

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting before my mango tree starts giving me fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii ogbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani mango lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango trees usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years after planting, while non-grafted trees take around 7 to 10 years to mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli beni adu amɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni mango tsei ni akɛwooo mli lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he.

english: Why is my young tree growing straight up like a tall pole instead of developing wide branches with lots of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso bibioo lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ tamɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona tsei niji ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai babaoo lɛ?

english: Trees grow straight up when they are reaching for sunlight or planted too close to shade; cutting or trimming the top tip of a young tree encourages it to grow side branches that carry fruit.
ga: Tsei lɛ daa shi shiŋŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ loo amɛbɛŋkɛ hulutsoo be tsɔ. Tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni afolɔ loo afolɔ amɛnaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ niji ni woɔ yibii.

english: Why does my mango tree flower heavily, but then almost all the tiny young fruits fall off before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo, shi eshwɛ fioo ni aduawai bibii lɛ baagbee shi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Tiny fruits drop mainly due to dry spells without enough soil moisture, pest attacks, or natural self-thinning where the tree sheds extra fruit it cannot physically support.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi titri yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Pest attack loo tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli ni egbɔjɔɔ, he ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii krokomɛi ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to pick my mangoes so they ripen sweet instead of spoiling early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛɛ bo be ni sa ni esa akɛ okɛkpa mango koni ehi jogbaŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni eeefite oya?

english: Harvest mangoes when they reach full size, their shoulders broaden at the stem end, and the dark green skin lightens to a yellowish or pale green tone.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ mangoi kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛɛ fe ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ naagbee. ni hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are shallow and their leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep the soil cool and retain moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize plants lack nitrogen fertilizer. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to newer upper leaves to survive, leaving the bottom leaves yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ o-abele tso lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice lower leaves naturally falling off and the soil around the base of the stem cracking open as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli gbálaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like something chewed holes in them while they were still rolled up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni atsɔ mli awo bu mli be mli ni ashɛreɔ amɛ lolo lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like Fall Armyworms that crawl into the central leaves before they open up. Applying approved pest treatments inside the central funnel of the plant early in the morning kills the caterpillars.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ dani egbeleɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weak when weeds are growing close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ jwɛi bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves in your farm. They compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, leaving your main crops starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, hulu la, kɛ nu mli, ni no haa hɔmɔ yeɔ bo ni oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves droop temporarily to protect the plant from losing too much water, and they usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why is it wrong for me to apply chemical fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ? Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ejaaa kɛha mi?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so that roots can drink it in. Placing dry chemical fertilizer on dry roots can burn and destroy the root system of your crops.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Tsofai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi ni egbi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pepper ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, uneven watering, or attacks by tiny insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the plants from high heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does covering the bare soil with dry grass or leaves help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground, also known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the heat, suppresses weeds, and breaks down into organic food for the soil.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear the climbing vines off my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie wain tsei ni kwɔɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Climbing vines wrap tightly around young cocoa trees, competing with them for sunlight and suffocating branches, which slows down growth and reduces overall pod yield.
ga: Wein tsei lɛ bɔle cacao tso bibioo lɛ he waa. Hulu la he tawuu kɛ tsei niji ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa pod yibiiwoo lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How often should I clear weeds and brush around the base of my crops?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni mafolɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ he?

english: Weed clearing should be done every 4 to 6 weeks during the rainy season because fast-growing weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that your main crop needs.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ daa otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa onibii titrii lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to trim the excess branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Trimming excess branches allows sunlight to penetrate the canopy and improves airflow, which keeps humidity low and prevents fungal diseases like Black Pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. ni etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: What happens if I leave shade trees on my farm without cutting back their branches?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mifolɔɔɔ eniji lɛ?

english: Overly dense shade tree branches block too much sunlight from reaching your crops, causing weak growth, poor flowering, and a lower harvest yield.
ga: Tso niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fɔfɔi ni ehiii kɛ kpamɔ yibiiwoo ba shi

english: When is the best time for me to prune and trim trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni mafolɔ amɛhe?

english: Pruning is best done immediately after the main harvest during the dry season, as this gives the trees time to recover and shoot fresh branches before the next rains.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná be ni ekɛtsake ehe ni ekwɛ̃ niji heei dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: How does using a sharp cutlass for trimming help keep my crops healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfoɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: A sharp cutlass makes clean, smooth cuts on stems and branches, which heal rapidly and prevent disease-causing fungi and insects from entering open plant wounds.
ga: Kakla ni naa wa baashi ŋmeii ni he tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tsei akui kɛ tsei aniji anɔ. Enɛ tsaa oya ni ehaaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni kɛ hela baa lɛ abote tso lɛ mli pilamɔi ni agbele mli lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe to use the same farm tools for clearing bush and trimming crop branches?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii kɛjie brɔshi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, but you should clean and wipe down your tools after clearing general bush to avoid accidentally transferring crop diseases from wild plants to your healthy farm trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe ni otsumɔ shi beni ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni akagbɛ tso helai ni jɛ koo mli tsei amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the farm becomes overcrowded with wild growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Wild trees and thick undergrowth swallow nutrients from the ground and create excessive shade, forcing cocoa trees to spend energy reaching for light instead of developing pods.
ga: Koo mli tsei kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni etaoɔ la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee pod lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa plants require shade trees while mature trees need more sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ? Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ, hulu la babaoo he miihia lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under intense heat, requiring shade to survive; mature trees need direct sunlight to fuel flowering and pod formation.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. ni biɔ hulutsoo koni enyɛ ehi shi Tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekanya fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ.

english: How does removing low-hanging branches from my crop trees help improve my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni shwieɔ shi ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Removing low branches keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing soil-borne pests and mold from easily crawling up into the main stem and fruit pods.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Cocoa pods change color as they ripen, usually turning from green or red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them when they are fully yellow ensures the beans inside are fully mature and ready for fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa pods turn yellow while others stay green on the same tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods develop at different times depending on when the flowers were pollinated. Green pods are still growing and maturing, while yellow pods have completed their growth cycle and are ready to be picked.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli, ni enɛ damɔ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Pods eŋɔlii lɛ miida lolo ni amɛmiidara. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ egbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Is it fine if I pick green cocoa pods early and let them ripen in my house?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mifolɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ mra? Ni aha ekwɛ̃ yɛ shĩa lɛ mli?

english: No, cocoa pods do not ripen properly after being picked from the tree. Harvesting green pods results in underdeveloped beans with low sugar content, leading to poor fermentation and low-quality cocoa that buyers will reject.
ga: Dabi, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ. Pods eŋɔli ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni sugar faaa yɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa kookoo lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo.

english: What happens if I leave the yellow cocoa pods on the tree for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: If yellow pods remain on the tree past maturity, the seeds inside will start to sprout or rot. Overripe pods are also much more vulnerable to diseases and animal attacks, which ruins your bean yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛdara kwraa lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ loo amɛbaafite. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ tsɔ lɛ hu helai kɛ kooloi baanyɛ atutua amɛ waa. Enɛ baafite o-bean ni ofeɔ lɛ.

english: What is the main cocoa season in Ghana, and why does my harvest slow down during certain months?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji kookoo be titri yɛ Ghana? Ni mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: In Ghana, the main cocoa season runs from October to February because rainfall patterns earlier in the year support pod growth. The harvest slows down during dry months because trees conserve water and stop producing new pods.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, kookoo be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ Alemle kɛyashi Oflɔŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ dalɛ. Nikpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli ejaakɛ tsei lɛ buɔ nu he ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii heei ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce fewer pods during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During extended dry spells, cocoa trees suffer water stress. To protect themselves from drying out, trees will naturally shed flowers and tiny pods, leading to smaller harvests during those times.
ga: yɛ hɔmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ Cocoa tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he Tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, ni no baaha ŋmaa bibioo aba yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: Why are some of my young cocoa pods turning black and dying before they turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young pods turning black is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet and humid conditions, or by natural thinning where the tree drops pods it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pod bibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many of the white flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii yɛŋ babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of tiny flowers, but only a small percentage are pollinated by tiny insects called midges. It is normal for unpollinated flowers to fall off, though heavy shade or drought can worsen flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ, shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛ pollen lɛ baagbee shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be loo hɔmɔ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii agbo moŋ.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans right after cutting open the yellow pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijara ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans, kills the embryo inside to prevent sprouting, and releases the rich chocolate flavor and brown color required by cocoa buyers.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ. Gbemɔ fɔmɔ kotoku ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni ekɛtsi fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ naa. ni ejieɔ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ kpo.

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under larger forest trees. Shade protects delicate cocoa leaves from burning under intense sunlight and helps keep moisture in the soil during dry periods.
