ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Shade buɔ cocoa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf yellowing and curling in cassava is often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus prevents leaves from capturing sunlight properly, which stops the cassava roots underneath from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ adara.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet weather and heavy shade. Pruning overhead tree branches to let light in and clearing out rotten pods stops the fungi from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afolɔ koni la abote mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over so easily when a small wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over when their root systems are weak or shallow. This usually happens if seeds were planted too close to the surface, if the soil lacks nutrients, or if the plants were crowded too tightly together.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ abua tsei lɛ anaa tsɔ

english: Why does my rice crop look light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves mean your rice plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Giving the soil nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves darken and produce stronger food for the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-rice tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni mli wa baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain suckers growing very slowly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa blɛoo beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers grow slowly if microscopic soil worms (nematodes) or banana weevils damage their roots. Cleaning the roots properly before planting and keeping the base mulched helps them establish fast.
ga: Plantain tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. (Nematodes) loo banana ŋmeii fiteɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ atsumɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ dani adu ni akɛ sũ ha nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmaa shi oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before making any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛfee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Without steady moisture and moderate temperatures, the plant drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni tamɔ ekome kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my watermelon vines spread out everywhere but produce very few watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ miigbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he shi ewoɔ watermelon yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons need bees to move pollen from male flowers to female flowers. If there are few bees around, or if you use too much fertilizer that causes leaf growth instead of flower growth, few fruits will form.
ga: Watermelon he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi yei lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsu nii ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi. Nɔ ko fioo pɛ ebaaná.

english: Why are my hot pepper fruits growing small and wrinkled instead of full and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hot pepper aduawai lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Small and wrinkled pepper fruits happen when the plant does not get enough regular water while the peppers are forming. Irregular watering starves the fruit of the fluid it needs to expand properly.
ga: Pepper yibii bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa be mli ni pepper lɛ miifee lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha nu lɛ aye hɔmɔ koni egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize plants so aggressively compared to mature ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ tutuaa mi-corn tsei bibii lɛ waa fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer young maize because the leaves are soft, tender, and easy to chew. The young leaves are also full of concentrated sugars that the caterpillars need to grow quickly.
ga: Autumn cutworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa bibii ejaakɛ baai lɛ ji bibii, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛyeɔ oya. Sugars ni mli wa ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ hu eyi baai bibii lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my yam vines dry up before the yam tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: As yam tubers grow bigger under the ground, the plant redirects its nutrients away from the lower, older leaves and feeds the tuber instead. If it happens too early, however, it could be a fungal leaf disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛ niyenii haa ŋmeii lɛ moŋ. Kɛji eba oya tsɔ Ekolɛ eji fungal leaf hela.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings burning and dying when the sun is very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade crops, like plantains, planted next to them to act as living umbrellas and protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on the growing parts of maize. Detecting them early allows you to use recommended sprays or natural extracts before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa fãi ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or mites. They suck the plant's sap and spread viruses, which stunts plant growth and reduces fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ ada, ni ehaa yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants have plenty of big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or high-nitrogen fertilizer is applied late, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing stems and foliage instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli sɛɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tsei kɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ baai amli.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger yams when I train them to grow up tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ sweet potato agbo fe tsutsu lɛ beni mitsɔseɔ lɛ koni eda ni etsɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce more energy, which the plant stores underground as larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Baai ni hulu la babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo. Tso lɛ kɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei ni da fe no.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, leaving valuable nutrients behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop yield even if my crops are already much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo moŋ.

english: Even small weeds steal water, fertilizer, and root space from your crops underneath the soil, while also serving as hiding places for harmful insects and diseases.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii hu akɛ he ni kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering during the time the fruit is setting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest yield less grain than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Improved and hybrid seeds lose their strength and uniformity after one harvest. Planting saved seeds leads to weaker plants and lower yields compared to purchasing fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ kɛ nɔ ni afee amɛ ekome lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kome sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ he yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when they start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers attached to one plantain stem weakens the root base. Removing excess suckers and mounting soil around the stem base strengthens the roots to support heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ sũ fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ.

english: Why do my mangoes become very soft and spoil quickly on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ji gbekɛbii bibii ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When mangoes become unnaturally soft or spoil early, it is often a sign of nutrient deficiency, especially a lack of calcium or potassium. Feeding the tree the right fertilizers builds strong cell walls so the fruit stays firm and lasts longer.
ga: Kɛji mango lɛ mli efee bɔdɔɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo efiteɔ oya lɛ Bei pii lɛ eji niyenii ni esaaa he okadi. titri lɛ, kɛji akɛ calcium loo potassium faaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo otsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbogboi ni wa baa koni aduawai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some parts of my fruit feel soft and weak while other parts stay hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ fãi komɛi nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ be mli ni fãi krokomɛi hu kã he amɛfee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Uneven softening usually happens when the plant lacks a balanced supply of soil nutrients while the fruit is growing. Ensuring your crop gets the proper soil food allows the fruit to develop evenly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa aha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I tell if my fruit is poor quality just by touching or squeezing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-fruit lɛ ehiii kɛtsɔ mi nine ni mikɛtaa he loo ni mikɛmimɔ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: A healthy fruit should feel firm and yield only slightly to gentle pressure. If squeezing it reveals soft or watery patches, the crop is likely suffering from nutrient deficiencies or pest damage.
ga: Esa akɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni ekɛ nɔnyɛɛ fioo pɛ aha. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ kpo lɛ, ejieɔ hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo nu lɛ kpo. Ekolɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite.

english: How can I prevent my fruits from developing soft spots before I take them to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi yibii lɛ anaa koni ekagbɔjɔ dani mikɛba jara nɔ?

english: Soft spots can be prevented by applying balanced fertilizers during the flowering and fruiting stages, keeping up regular watering, and handling harvested fruits gently.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsĩ bɔjɔmɔ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Okɛ nu awo mli daa ni okwɛ aduawai ni akpa lɛ anɔ blɛoo

english: How do I know if my fruit crops are suffering from a lack of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi aduawai tsei lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Crops show fertilizer hunger through weak leaves, slow growth, small fruits, or fruit that turns soft and rots easily. Seeing these symptoms on the fruit tells you the tree needs specific soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei jieɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpo kɛtsɔ baai bibii, amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, aduawai bibii, loo aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni fiteɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ona okadii nɛɛ yɛ aduawai anɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo akɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi he miihia tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does applying fertilizer really change how firm my harvested crop will be?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni tsei ni akpa lɛ mli wa ha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, nutrients like calcium and potassium act as the structural building blocks for crop fruit. Without them, the harvested produce turns out watery, soft, and spoils quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium kɛ potassium tsuɔ nii akɛ nibii ni haa tsei ayibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛ amɛbɛ Nibii ni akpa lɛ bafeɔ nu oya, efeɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I do not follow the recommended steps when feeding my crops fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ tsuuu nii beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer without following the proper process, correct amount, or timing can burn plant roots or leave the crop hungry when it needs food most. Following the process ensures the plant can use the nutrients to grow good fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni akɛ gbɛ ni sa, bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii, loo be ni sa tsuuu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi loo eha tsei lɛ aye hɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ. Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaha tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can giving my crops the wrong fertilizer cause them to yield poor-quality harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii aba?

english: Yes, using the wrong type or too much of one fertilizer—like nitrogen alone—makes plants produce soft, weak fruit that spoils fast. Balanced fertilizers match the specific fruit-building needs of the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni fa fe nine, tamɔ nitrogen pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ oya. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ baatsu oŋmɔshi nii lɛ aduawai pɔtɛɛi ahe hiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Why do my fruit trees need specific fertilizers instead of just basic compost?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: While compost improves the soil structure, fruit-bearing crops need higher amounts of specific minerals like potassium and calcium during fruiting to produce high-quality, firm yields that buyers prefer.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo moŋ, shi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ biɔ mineral pɔtɛɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ calcium babaoo yɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Bɔni afee ni afee nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my fruit crop if I skip applying fertilizer during the fruiting stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mifo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ yibiiwoo be mli?

english: If crops lack key nutrients while fruits are forming, the tree cannot build strong fruit tissue, leading to weak produce with soft spots, poor flavor, and a short shelf life.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee aduawai amli fãji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kɛ shihilɛ kuku ni akɛtoɔ shĩa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorching and turning brown during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their tender leaves lose moisture too quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, shielding them from heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the small coconuts dropping off my trees before they get a chance to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Ani egbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Early fruit drop in coconuts is often caused by sudden dry spells, insect damage, or a lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil. Giving the trees extra water during hot seasons and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ oya lɛ mli baa ji ni amɛgbi trukaa, kooloi ni fiteɔ amɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ yibii amli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high afternoon heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and providing light shade during peak heat helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛhao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves on top but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing thick stems and leaves above ground instead of feeding the roots below. Balanced plant nutrients encourage strong tuber growth.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tuber dalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism tomato plants use to reduce surface area and stop water from evaporating out of their leaves during hot periods. If they recover in the evening, the plant is safe, but mulching the soil helps keep the roots cool.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi, ni amɛtsi nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji ohe wa bo gbɛkɛ Tso lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper field spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and food to build strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my crops look weak and yellow when heavy rains leave standing water around them for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shiɔ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ? gbii babaoo

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air to breathe. When excess water sits around the base of the crop, it drowns the root system, preventing the plant from taking up food and causing root rot and leaf yellowing.
ga: Tse shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi lɛ awo nu mli. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaye nii ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve the growth of my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the ground for whatever main crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaya nɔ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wuji fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass around my plants help them handle the dry season?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Te mitso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekpeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naa ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct sun rays from drying out the dirt, traps soil moisture longer, and prevents weeds from popping up to steal nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekagbi muji. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaje kpo ni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize right at the break of the rainy season rather than waiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee fe ni aaamɛ lɛ?

english: The first seasonal rains trigger a natural release of rich nitrogen stored in the soil. Planting early lets your crops soak up this high surge of nutrients immediately, giving them a fast, strong start before late-season dry spells arrive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ haa nitrogen ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei jeɔ shishi oya, ni amɛhe wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: How long can I keep harvesting from the same crop before I need to pull it out and plant new ones?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ dani ehe baahia ni majie kɛjɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Different crops have different production lifespans. Short-term crops like tomatoes or pepper produce for a few months, while perennial crops like cocoa or citrus can continue producing for several years before their yield naturally declines and requires replanting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe bei srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ Ewoɔ yibii nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ kookoo loo citrus baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii babaoo. dani yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe baahia ni adu ekoŋŋ

english: Why do some crops mature and finish quickly while others stay in the farm producing for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi daa ni amɛgbeɔ naa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛwo yibii afii babaoo lɛ?

english: Annual crops complete their lifecycle in a single season to give fast returns, whereas perennial or long-term crops invest energy into building strong stems and roots, allowing them to yield continuously over multiple years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ gbeɔ amɛshihilɛ naa yɛ be kome mli koni ekɛ yibiiwoo aba oya. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo loo tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ woɔ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa amamɔ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ efee nibii ni yaa nɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: Why do my older crops produce smaller harvests compared to when they were young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ?

english: As plants age beyond their peak production years, their internal transport system slows down and soil nutrients around them deplete, leading to smaller yields and requiring replacement with fresh seedlings.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eho amɛ afii ni amɛwoɔ nii babaoo lɛ he lɛ Amɛmli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ baa shi, ni no haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni ehe bahiaa ni akɛ dumɔwui heei atsake.

english: If I try a new chemical treatment or practice on my crops, will the food still be safe for my family to eat?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mika tsofa loo nifeemɔ hee ko mikwɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hu? Ani niyenii lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo ni miweku lɛ baaye?

english: New farm inputs or treatments are safe as long as you follow the correct dosage and respect the waiting period (pre-harvest interval) before harvesting so that chemicals break down properly.
ga: Nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli loo tsofafeemɔi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ onyiɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ sɛɛ ni obu mɛmɔ be lɛ he. (be ni tsɔ ŋmaa lɛ hiɛ) dani akpa koni tsofai lɛ afite jogbaŋŋ

english: Can people safely eat crops that were harvested at the end of their long production lifecycle?
ga: Ani gbɔmɛi baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afeemɔ be kakadaŋŋ naagbee lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, produce harvested from older plants is generally safe to eat, though the texture or taste might change slightly compared to young crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni egbɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ayeɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsake fioo kɛ akɛto tsei bibii ahe moŋ.

english: Will using new organic manures or liquid fertilizers change the taste of my crop soup?
ga: Ani organic loo nu mli ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsake miŋmɔshi nibii ahe shwiili lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ?

english: New organic inputs improve soil nutrition and healthy plant growth without harming the food's taste or safety, provided they are well-composted and applied correctly.
ga: Nibii heei ni akɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ mli niyenii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni enaaa niyenii lɛ ŋɔɔmɔ loo shweshweeshwefeemɔ nɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which short-term crops can I plant if I need fast cash to buy new farm supplies?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo manyɛ madu kɛji shika he miihia mi oya koni mikɛhe okwaayeli he nibii heei?

english: Vegetables like spinach, okra, and garden eggs grow rapidly within weeks to a few months, allowing quick sales and fast cash turn-around to fund other farm activities.
ga: aduawai tamɔ spinach Okra Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya yɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahɔ̃ɔ nii oya, ni shika hu baa oya ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi krokomɛi amli.

english: How often should I replace old crop varieties with new seedlings to maintain good harvests?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui heei atsake tsei momoi lɛ koni amɛná yibii kpakpai?

english: Vegetables are replaced every planting season, while long-term cash crops are typically replaced or rejuvenated every 15 to 20 years when yields drop significantly.
ga: Akɛ aduawai tsakeɔ daa be mli ni amɛdaraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, atsakeɔ shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ loo atsakeɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ daa afii 15 kɛyashi 20 kɛ́ nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi waa.

english: When a crop finishes its main yield, can the rest of the plant still be useful for food or feeding farm animals?
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ená amɛ nibii titrii lɛ fɛɛ Ani abaanyɛ akɛ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii lolo akɛ niyenii loo akɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi niyenii?

english: Yes, many mature crop residues like maize stalks, cassava peels, and legume vines can be used as livestock feed or worked back into the soil as compost.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa tsei, ŋmãa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii akɛ kooloi aniyenii loo aku sɛɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa.

english: Is it better to keep selling small fast-growing crops continuously or invest in long-producing crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaaya nɔ ahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo akɛ shika awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ amli?

english: A mix of both works best: short-term crops provide quick, regular income for daily upkeep, while long-term crops offer larger, stable wealth over several years.
ga: Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ: ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa anáa shika oya ni yaa nɔ daa kɛha daa gbi nibii akwɛmɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ haa ninamɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to place fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem can chemically burn the plant's tissue and damage its root crown. It is best to apply fertilizer in a circle a few inches away from the stem where the roots can safely reach it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa ashã tso lɛ fãji lɛ ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ kokroo nɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overly shady environments. Pruning excess canopy trees to let in sunlight and clearing infected pods regularly helps keep the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la babaoo aba mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do small holes keep appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are typically caused by pests like caterpillars eating the plant. Spraying safe, natural treatments like diluted neem oil or recommended insecticides will control the pests and protect your leaf harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ ni atsɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ baaye kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ anɔ ni ebu obaa ni okpa lɛ he.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch sunlight. Staking exposes leaves to light for better growth while keeping them off damp soil to reduce fungal diseases, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ la mli koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: Why should I plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing necessary shade and conserving soil moisture while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la fiteɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as intense heat waves, erratic watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay attached and develop into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni bɛ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified maize seeds instead of planting seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their vigor and yield capacity over successive generations. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local pests, tolerate weather stresses, and produce significantly higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaawo yibii yɛ wɔsɛɛ yinɔi amli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo baa

english: It is risky to plant after the very first rainfall, as a dry spell may follow and kill young seedlings. Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays moist for several days in a row before planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ eha tsei bibii lɛ agboi. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ dani odu.

english: How can I stop insects from eating holes into my harvested cowpeas while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-cowpea ni akpa lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ he ko ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Storage insects like weevils target moist beans. Drying your beans thoroughly in the sun until they are hard and storing them in sealed, airtight bags (such as PICS bags) prevents insects from breathing and multiplying.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmeii ni mli efɔ. Kɛ́ agbi kɔfi ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli (tamɔ PICS kotokui) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akamu ni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates living umbrellas that keep the air cool and soil moist so the cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ kã ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect themselves. As long as the stem remains green and healthy, the plant will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the stalks to grow thick and produce full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes in them like something ate them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli ewo muji tamɔ nɔ ko ni eye amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf shoot. Catching them early and applying safe pest treatments inside the central funnel saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme afternoon heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right time helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies spreading viruses. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap early keeps these pests away and protects new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he ni ebaatsi shweremɔ hee naa.

english: Why is my yam vine turning brown and dying long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo be saŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by leaf spot diseases or root rot from waterlogged soil. Planting yams on raised mounds ensures good drainage and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya ji baai ni etse loo shishifãi ni egbo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni shishifãi ni wa hu baa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden prop stakes prevents them from blowing down before harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekatswa shi dani akpa.

english: Why do my garden eggs get dark rotten spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni egbo yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of garden eggs are caused by blossom-end rot, which occurs when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Consistent watering prevents this fruit damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji fɔfɔii ni egbo lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tso yibii nɛɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil. Cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ babaoo aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: What is the main difference between chemical fertilizer and manure for my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizers give your crops a quick boost of nutrient food right away, while organic manure builds up the soil health over time so it holds water and nutrients better for future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Is chemical fertilizer safe to use on my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, approved chemical fertilizers are completely safe for food crops as long as you follow the correct application amounts and safety guidelines.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii. Shii abɔ ni obaanyiɛ tsofa lɛ falɛ ni ja kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the chemical fertilizer I am buying from the local market is approved and genuine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ ji nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni eji anɔkwale?

english: Look for official government license seals and manufacturer labels on the bag, and purchase directly from certified agricultural input dealers.
ga: Taomɔ maŋ nɔyeli hegbɛ he stamp kɛ mɔ ni fee lɛ niŋmaa yɛ kotoku lɛ nɔ. ni amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ajalɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ

english: Will adding extra chemical fertilizer make my maize grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, using more fertilizer than recommended can burn the roots and ruin the soil. Crops only need a specific limit, and applying too much will actually damage or kill your plants.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Husu pɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni kɛ okɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite otsei lɛ loo egbe amɛ.

english: Should I drop chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: No, you should place fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away from the stem. Putting chemical fertilizer directly on the stem will cause root and plant burning.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ fɔmɔ nii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Inchi fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ kɛ tso lɛ.

english: When is the best time during the rainy season to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours, because heavy rains will wash the nutrients away before your crops can absorb them.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow and dry after I applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kɛji akɛ awo mli ŋmei lɛ?

english: Yellow or scorched leaves usually mean too much chemical fertilizer was applied or it was placed too close to the plant, causing 'fertilizer burn' which prevents the roots from taking in water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni eshã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ babaoo ewo mli loo akɛwo tso lɛ he tsɔ, ni no haa ‘ŋmei shãa’ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every year when I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops repeatedly takes nutrients out of the earth. Without adding back nutrients through manure or chemical fertilizer, the soil becomes tired and exhausted.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ afata he ekoŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure on my crop roots right after clearing out the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee afata tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie tsina ŋmei lɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is too strong and hot for young plant roots. You should let it sit and decompose into compost for a few weeks first so it does not burn your crops.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi. Esa akɛ oha eta shi ni efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi klɛŋklɛŋ koni ekashã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I tell whether my farmland needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: If your soil is hard, sandy, and loses water quickly, organic manure helps rebuild the soil structure. If your crops are already planted and showing quick nutrient shortages like pale leaves, chemical fertilizer acts faster to correct it.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ŋã yɔɔ mli ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Organic fertilizers yeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ekoŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu otso lɛ momo ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa trukaa, tamɔ baai bibii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so that I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If you plant seeds too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This results in tall, thin stalks that produce small ears instead of healthy plants with big, full harvests.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe tseee, ni no haa toi bibii baa yɛ tso agbo ni he wa, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants start turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋfeemɔ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. Heavy rains often wash this food out of the soil, meaning you need to add compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ su eŋɔli lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ niyenii nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and weak roots that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas to keep them cool and moist until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra side branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra branches forces the plant to send all its water and nutrients directly into growing big, healthy tomatoes rather than wasting energy on growing excess leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni abaakpa tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ akudɔ emli nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ koni etsɔ tomatoi wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts pull good nutrients from the air and store them in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they feed the soil naturally and act like free fertilizer for your maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts gbalaa niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaafee tamɔ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmãa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or attacks by tiny pests. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its strength just to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tutua amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛbu amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why does the maize I saved from my last harvest yield less than the fresh seed I buy from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpa kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred to give strong yields for only one planting. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their parent strength and yield smaller crops if planted a second time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shikome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛfɔlɔi ahewalɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shii enyɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass or palm leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket. It stops the sun from drying out the water in the ground, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot when left in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ shwie shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, the cassava roots cannot breathe. The excess water causes the roots to drown and rot right inside the soil before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce small yields even after I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibii babaoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ewo ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach it. If you don't clear the weeds early, you end up feeding the weeds instead of your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ aye niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does the main cocoa harvest season usually end around January just after Christmas in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, kookoo kpamɔ be titri lɛ baa naagbee yɛ January mli, yɛ Blonya sɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow rainy and dry weather cycles. In Ghana, the main pod production finishes around Christmas because the dry Harmattan season begins, causing the trees to stop producing flowers and rest until the rains return.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, pod feemɔ titri lɛ gbeɔ naa yɛ Blonya beaŋ ejaakɛ Harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi, ni no haa tsei lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop leaves and look weak during the dry season early in the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick for cocoa trees during dry periods. By shedding leaves, the tree reduces water loss through evaporation to keep its main stem and roots alive until rainfall resumes.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli teemɔŋ sane ni haa ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Koni akɛbu tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa trees take several years after planting before they produce their first pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu cacao tsei lɛ sɛɛ dani efeɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees spend their first three to five years building strong root systems, sturdy trunks, and broad leaf canopies. They need this mature structure to store enough energy to support heavy pods.
ga: Cacao tso bibioo ko heɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa baa. tso ni mli wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ Amɛhe miihia ni amɛfee ekome kɛto hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sun. Fast-growing plantains provide big leaves that act as natural umbrellas, supplying the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa trees yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afolɔ ashwieɔ shi krokomɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak or unnecessary branches that steal food from the rest of the plant. Opening up the canopy also lets air and sunlight reach the trunk, which encourages flowering and prevents fungal dampness.
ga: Niji ni egbɔjɔ loo ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Kɛ́ agbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hu shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ fɛo, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ he.

english: Why do many small, young cocoa pods turn dark and shrivel up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii babaoo feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The tree intentionally discards extra young pods it cannot feed due to limited nutrients or water, concentrating its energy on developing the healthiest remaining pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii yɛ niyenii loo nu ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni akɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji pods ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ afeemɔ.

english: Why do flowers grow directly out of the main trunk of a cocoa tree instead of on leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii jɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers on the thick bark of the trunk and older branches so the heavy mature pods have strong support to hang safely without snapping small stems.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akui kɛ tsei niji ni egbɔ lɛ ahe tsɔi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfo shweshweeshwe ni amɛkuuu ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when a cocoa pod on the tree is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A cocoa pod shows it is ripe by changing color. Green pods turn bright yellow, and reddish pods turn orange-yellow, indicating that the seeds inside are fully grown and ready.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwere kɛtsɔ su ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo.

english: What causes healthy green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ diŋ trukaa ni egboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp conditions. Raindrops splash the fungal spores onto pods, quickly turning them black if the farm stays too humid.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores nɔ yɛ pods lɛ anɔ. ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ fa tsɔ.

english: Why do some branches on my cocoa trees die off with dried brown leaves hanging on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi egboi ni baai ni egbi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ efolɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by insect pests like mirids (capsids) that bite tender stems to drink sap, releasing toxic saliva that dries out and kills that branch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni ŋmɔɔ tsei bibii koni amɛnu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Jiemɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni haa tsei niji gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants showing small holes with powdery brown dirt inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ efutu ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Treating the shoot early with recommended organic or chemical controls stops them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Tsamɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi kɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Enɛ baatsi shishifã lɛ naa koni ekafite he ni edara yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food. When the vines climb tall stakes, their leaves capture more sunlight, which helps the plant send energy down to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ Ebaai lɛ baaná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow and instead rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ekomɛi edaaa ni amɛgbooo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems rot if they are planted upside down, taken from weak or diseased stems, or buried in waterlogged soil. Stems planted right-side up with healthy buds in well-drained soil sprout quickly and root properly.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ŋwɛi. Okɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. loo afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Tsoi ni adu yɛ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛ ŋwɛi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaashishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen between them. Without enough shade, leaf litter, and moisture for midges to live in, unpollinated flowers simply dry up and fall off the tree.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen aya amɛteŋ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be, baai amli jwɛi, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni dwarf lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli lɛ, fɔfɔi ni Unpollinated lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain sucker from an existing farm to plant in my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for a maiden sucker, which has narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a wide, solid base. Avoid suckers with wide, broad leaves because they come from older roots, take longer to fruit, and yield smaller bunches.
ga: Taomɔ oblayei bibii ni nuɔ nu, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni etsɛ mli. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same farm with my maize help the maize grow greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have natural root nodules capable of trapping nitrogen from the air and putting it into the soil. The nearby maize plants absorb this extra nitrogen, which makes their leaves darker green and healthier.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛbaai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before the fruit gets ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, happens when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil. It is usually triggered by irregular watering or dry soil spells while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around pepper stems with dry grass and crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, called mulching, shades the ground from hot sun, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from growing and competing with your crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why do the leaf tips of my lowland rice start turning yellow when dry weather lasts for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lowland rice grits lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ otsii enyɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice has shallow roots that require consistent soil moisture to absorb nutrients. When the surface soil dries out, the plant cannot feed properly and lets its leaf tips turn yellow to save water.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni ha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔŋ koni nu akafite.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees dropping small green fruits onto the ground long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ miiho aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop young fruit when they suffer from sudden changes in soil water levels, attacks by fruit flies, or when the tree sets more fruit than its stem and roots can support.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ fiteɔ amɛyibii bibii lɛ kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsake trukaa. Yibii amli ŋmeii tutuaa Aloo kɛ́ tso ko wo yibii babaoo fe bɔ ni eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow fast. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer early gives them the food they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara oya. Nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra. Enɛ baaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my land is ready for planting cassava?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmei?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil so its roots can expand easily into big tubers. If the soil is soft enough to dig easily and does not hold standing water after a rain, your land is ready for planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia Cassava. Bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulb agboi oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii oya ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Checking under the leaves for small insects and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten by caterpillars or beetles. You can control them by picking them off by hand early in the morning or spraying the leaves with natural neem leaf water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabe baa lɛ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ oniji ni okɛbaakpa lɛ nɔ leebi loo kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu ni okɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if they do not get enough water, if the soil lacks nutrients, or if tiny insects called mirids attack them. Proper shade management and protecting trees from bugs help flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ myrids lɛ tutua amɛ. He ni akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce a lot of flowers but very few nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Cashew trees need insects like bees to carry pollen from flower to flower so nuts can form. Heavy rains during flowering or attacks from sap-sucking bugs can damage the flowers before nuts develop.
ga: Cashew tsei he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ baanyɛ afite fɔfɔii dani ŋmeii aba.

english: Why is it bad to plant my pepper seedlings very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded, they fight for sunlight, air, and soil food, making them tall and weak. Giving them proper space lets air flow freely, which prevents diseases and helps each plant bear more fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very good because beans capture nitrogen food from the air and feed it into the soil. This helps the maize grow stronger while letting you harvest two crops from one field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ejaakɛ obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get eaten by tiny black insects after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii diji eyi mi-abele ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli lɛ? Niyenii yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Those tiny black insects are weevils, which hatch inside grains that still contain moisture. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard and dry before storing it in sealed bags stops weevils from surviving.
ga: small black insect Nomɛi ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ebaawa ni egbi kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akahi shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground if I leave them too long after the leaves turn brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn brown and dry up, the plant has stopped growing and no longer drinks water from the soil. Leaving the tubers in wet ground after this stage causes bacteria and water to enter and rot them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni enuuu nu kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha helatsɛmɛi kɛ nu abote mli ni amɛgboi.

english: If I bring seeds or seedlings from a nursery in Accra, will they automatically grow well in my farm's soil?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui loo dumɔwui bibii kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni yɔɔ Accra lɛ ba. Ani dumɔwui loo dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Crops raised in controlled nursery conditions are used to mild environments and constant care. When moved to open farm land, they experience shock and need time, proper watering, and soil preparation to adapt to the harsher field conditions.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa. Kɛji akɛ amɛmiiya dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ Amɛnaa shoofeemɔ ni eheɔ be. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wa waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die when I plant them directly in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants do not have deep root systems yet to draw water from the soil. Placing them in direct sun causes them to lose moisture faster than their roots can supply, so they need initial shade or planting at the onset of rains to survive.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni amɛná shishijee hulutsoo loo amɛdumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishijee mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow fast and green when I apply fertilizer, but weaken quickly once the fertilizer runs out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ? Shi ani ebaagbɔjɔ oya kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite?

english: Fertilizer provides immediate food for plants, but if the underlying soil lacks natural organic matter, it cannot hold onto those nutrients for long. Adding manure or compost helps the soil store nutrients so plants remain fed over time.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ, shi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ nakai niyenii lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ niyenii kpakpai amli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná niyenii daa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but producing small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ani eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei bibioo ko?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the plant spends all its energy developing branches and leaves instead of food storage. Cassava requires balanced nutrients, especially potassium, to feed tuber growth rather than just top leaves.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei niji kɛ baai yɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛtoɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja he miihia cassava. titri lɛ potassium Koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ mli hewalɛ moŋ fe baai lɛ anɔ pɛ.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency. When nutrients in the soil are low, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Beni niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops after the first rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the soil waiting for moisture. Because wild weeds are naturally adapted to the local environment, they react faster to rain than cultivated crops and will steal food and water unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi waa ni amɛwɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛmɛ ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛtsuɔ nii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. ni ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu ja ajie lɛ mra.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the bush around them is allowed to grow thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ? Ani aŋmɛ gbɛ ni eda babaoo?

english: Overgrown weeds and shade trees compete with cocoa trees for soil food and block sunlight. Thick vegetation also traps excessive damp air, encouraging fungal diseases like black pod to rot the flowers and pods.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hulutsoo tsei. Tsoi ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ fe nine lɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baa, ni ehaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: If I keep planting maize on the exact same plot every year, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: The same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil. Repeated planting on one spot also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil from year to year.
ga: Tsei nɛɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ hu haa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing any peppers during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo pepper yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant suffers from high heat and lack of water, it enters survival mode. It deliberately sheds its flowers to conserve water rather than spending energy growing fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ na piŋmɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ejɛɔ etsuiŋ eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu aduawai.

english: Why do insect pests suddenly attack my vegetable farm right at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The flush of soft, new leaves that grow right after the rains start provides ideal food for insects waking up from dry season dormancy, causing rapid pest outbreaks.
ga: Baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ. Ehaa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa kooloi ni jɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa oya.

english: How do I know if the first few rains of the season are enough for me to start planting my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?
