english: Light, scattered rains over the first few days usually only wet the surface. Planting too early can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if a short dry spell follows before deep soil moisture builds up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu pɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ko ba. dani shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ abua naa

english: Why do my crops still look thirsty even after we get two or three light rains in a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye wɔ lolo yɛ be mli ni wɔnine shɛ nugbɔ fioo ko nɔ po lɛ? Shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Light rains often evaporate quickly off the hot soil surface without sinking deep enough to reach the lower roots where the crop actually drinks.
ga: Drizzle lɛ sumɔɔ ni efo oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni eboteee shishi kɛyashɛ shishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe he ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ nu diɛŋtsɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do if the rainy season starts much later in the year than normal?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi sɛɛ fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa yɛ afi nɛɛ mli?

english: When the rains arrive late, it is best to plant fast-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties so they can fully grow before the short rainy period finishes.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba sɛɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ adu tsei ni daa oya loo tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ koni amɛshɛ shweremɔ he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why is light rainfall sometimes better for my farm than a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ nugbɔ fioo ko hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ fe nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Gentle rain slowly soaks into the earth without washing away topsoil, exposing roots, or carrying away the fertilizer you placed around your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fiofio lɛ Efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ ajiemɔ kpo Aloo jiemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: How can heavy, intense rain damage my young crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni naa wa waa lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy downpours pack strong physical force that can snap soft young stems, wash away seeds, and compact the soil so roots cannot breathe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei bibii. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Can heavy rain right after planting destroy my farm investment for the whole season?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔ mli shika ni mikɛwo mli lɛ be muu fɛɛ?

english: Yes, torrential rain early on can rot seeds in flooded soil or wash them out of the ridges completely, forcing you to buy new seeds and spend extra labor replanting.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ nɛ waa mra. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ loo efɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kwraa. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni ohé dumɔwui heei ni okɛ nitsumɔ kroko atsu nii ni okɛdu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my maize yield if the rains stop earlier in the month than expected?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If the rain cuts short while maize is filling its cobs, the plant will not get enough water to complete grain growth, leaving you with light, small, or dry kernels.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miiyi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ Tso lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui adalɛ. Enɛ haa onáa dumɔwui ni tsiimɔ waaa, bibii loo egbi.

english: How does rain continuing late into the month affect when I should finish my major field work?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ naagbee lɛ saa be ni esa akɛ magbe mishiɛmɔ nitsumɔ titri lɛ naa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended rainfall keeps the ground wet, which extends the growing window for late crops but delays field clearing, drying, and land preparation for the next cycle.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ adalɛ be lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi ekɛ jɛmɛ sɛɛ tsɛ, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni esaa kɛha kpokpaa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is continuous rain bad when my crops are already mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ehiii be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Rain during harvest keeps mature crops wet on the field, which leads to mold, fungal diseases, grain rotting, or seeds sprouting while still on the plant.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, kɛ dumɔwui ni fiteɔ baa. aloo dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: How can I tell that the rainy season is finally coming to an end for the year?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ naagbee lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: As the season wraps up, rainfall becomes lighter and days between rains grow wider, signaling that it is time to harvest, dry your produce, and clear the field.
ga: Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nugbɔ lɛ baafee mlɛo ni gbii ni kã nugbɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ baafee babaoo. Okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni abaakpa nii Gbi onibii lɛ ni ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or is sitting in too much water. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo eyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects can cause tomato flowers to dry up and fall off before fruit can start growing.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo pollinators ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi dani aduawai lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their small young pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop when the tree suffers from environmental stress like prolonged dry heat, water shortage, or nutrient deficiency as the tree tries to conserve its energy.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ he amanehulu. nu ni faaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ ji akɛ tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How do I know when it is safe to start planting my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil several times, rather than planting after the very first light shower, so seeds have enough deep soil moisture to survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ shii abɔ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water trapped around the roots without proper drainage, the roots suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kã he fɛɛ he lolo. shishifãi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Shifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing down into the earth. If the soil is hard, compact, or full of stones, the tuber cannot expand easily and ends up small or deformed.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Tubers nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli oya ni amɛfee bibii loo amɛfite.

english: Why is it harmful to plant the same crop on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ abaadu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to the soil, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from the base of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from crop roots, which starves the young plants and slows down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my plantain tree bear bigger fruit bunches when I cut away extra shoots around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ yibii wuji beni mifoɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and nutrients from the main mother tree. Removing excess shoots ensures all energy goes into producing a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa anyɛɔ atsuɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ he nii koni akɛwo ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to start working on my land right from the beginning of the year if harvest is months away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli kɛji akɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ eshwɛ ni kpamɔ lɛ baashɛ?

english: Crops require continuous care—such as land preparation, weeding, and soil management—throughout their entire growth cycle. Work done early in the season builds the foundation for crops to mature properly and produce a maximum yield at harvest time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ saamɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ yɛ shweremɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ Nitsumɔ ni agbeɔ naa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ feɔ shishitoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: If I plant my crops and leave them without daily attention, will they still yield well at the end of the season?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ emaaa nɔ daa gbi Ani ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lolo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: No, crop behavior depends on consistent effort. Without regular weeding, pest control, and monitoring throughout the year, crops become weak and produce very little, whereas consistent work leads to a successful harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ subaŋ damɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ bɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nitsumɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ kɛ nikpamɔ ni yeɔ omanye baa.

english: What causes my crops to produce a sudden heavy yield all at the same time?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo trukaa yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive consistent maintenance and mature under favorable weather conditions, they reach full peak development together. This results in a heavy, simultaneous yield often called a bumper harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsei anɔ daa ni amɛdara yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ amli lɛ, Tsei lɛ baafee ekome kɛda kwraa. Enɛ haa anáa nibii babaoo shikome, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ bump harvest.

english: How do I know when it is the exact right time to harvest my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Crops show clear physical behavior when mature, such as changes in fruit color, drying out of leaves, or firm pod development. Harvesting at this exact peak ensures your produce is at full weight and highest quality for market.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ subaŋ sɔrɔtoi kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ aduawai lɛ ahe su tsakemɔi, baai ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni wa ni baa lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa onibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha jara nɔ.

english: Why do produce buyers only start visiting our farming community at specific harvest times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ jeɔ wɔ okwaayeli akutsei lɛ amli saramɔ shishi yɛ kpamɔɔ bei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Buyers track crop seasonality across regions and travel to farming communities only when crops reach peak maturity, as this guarantees large quantities of fresh produce are ready for immediate purchase.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ nyiɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei asɛɛ yɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ fɛɛ ni amɛyaa okwaayeli akutsei amli pɛ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etee hiɛ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ abaaná nibii heei babaoo ni abaanyɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Should I contact crop buyers before my harvest is ready or after I finish harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mɔ ko ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abɔ dani mikpamɔ lɛ aba loo beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to make arrangements with buyers shortly before harvest begins. Early notice allows buyers to arrange transport in advance so they arrive as soon as the crop is bagged, reducing post-harvest losses.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ baato be dani nikpamɔ lɛ aje shishi. Kaadi ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ toɔ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbashɛ shi kɛji akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo kotoku mli pɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can small-scale farmers like me attract big crop buyers to come directly to our farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi lɛ agbala ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jarayelɔi wuji kɛba wɔŋmɔji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Buyers prefer visiting farms or communities where crops are well-maintained and produced in high volume. Planning your season well so your crop yields heavily gives buyers a reason to bring trucks straight to your farm gate.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛyasara ŋmɔji loo akutsei ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ nii babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oto obe lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni onine ashɛ onibii babaoo nɔ lɛ, ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ naa yiŋtoo ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛkɛ amɛtsɔnei lɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do crop buyers prefer to purchase produce in large quantities like 20 bags at a time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, tamɔ kotokui 20 yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Traders incur high transport and fuel costs to reach farms, so buying in bulk—such as 20 bags per vehicle—makes their trip profitable and allows them to move large volumes quickly to urban markets.
ga: Esa akɛ jarayelɔi awo gbɛfaa kɛ fuɛl he nyɔmɔ babaoo dani amɛyashɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii babaoo ni amɛheɔ, tamɔ kotokui 20 yɛ tsɔne kome mli lɛ haa amɛ gbɛfaa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. ni ehaa amɛfãa nibii babaoo kɛyaa maŋtiasei amli jarayeli hei oya.

english: Why is it important to sell my harvested produce quickly to the first buyer who arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahɔ̃ɔ mikpamɔ lɛ oya maha klɛŋklɛŋ jarayelɔi ni baa lɛ?

english: Harvested produce starts losing moisture, weight, and freshness immediately. Selling quickly to the first available buyer protects your profit and prevents produce from spoiling on the farm.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛmli nu, amɛtsiimɔ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ohɔ̃ɔ oya oha mɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni heɔ nii lɛ, ebuɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa nibii ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afite.

english: Why should I pack my harvested crop into standard sacks or bags before the buyers arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ awo kotokui loo kotokui ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ amli dani mɔ ni heɔ lɛ aba?

english: Bagging crops standardizes measurement for quick pricing, protects harvested crops from sun and dirt exposure, and allows rapid loading when buyer vehicles arrive on the farm.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ kɛ susumɔi feɔ ekome kɛha jara ni awoɔ oya. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ muji he. ni ehaa anyɛɔ awoɔ mli oya kɛ́ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ tsɔne lɛ bashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my cocoa beans are high quality before I take them to the buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛmaje mɔ ni heɔ lɛ?

english: High-quality cocoa beans are properly fermented and thoroughly dried. They should have a deep reddish-brown color, rustle like dry leaves when handled, and be free from mold, flat beans, or smoky smells.
ga: Akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ efee su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa gbee ni tswaa tamɔ baai ni egbi kɛji akɛ ashɛ he. ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo lasu he ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp and cool conditions. You can reduce it by pruning overgrown branches to let light in and picking ripe pods regularly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Obaanyɛ oba enɛ shi kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ooofolɔ koni la babaoo abote mli lɛ nɔ, ni ooofolɔ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ daa.

english: What basic steps can I take on my farm to help my cocoa trees produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: To increase yield, keep weeds under control so they don't steal plant nutrients, prune excess shoots to open up the canopy, and apply the right fertilizer at the start of the rainy season.
ga: koni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ Ha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi koni amɛkaju tsei lɛ amli niyenii. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ogbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Flowers drop when they aren't pollinated by tiny insects like midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought or poor soil nutrients. Keeping organic leaf mulch on the ground helps protect these natural pollinators.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe, loo kɛji hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ahe.

english: Can I grow food crops like plantain or cassava alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Ani abaanyɛ adu yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantains with young cocoa is helpful because the plantains provide vital shade to shield tender seedlings from harsh sunlight while giving you food to harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain ni akɛ kookoo bibii eduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii ni obaakpa.

english: Should I cut down all the big trees on my farm before planting new cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo hee?

english: No, you should leave a few good shade trees. Moderate tree shade protects your cocoa from harsh heat, keeps moisture in the soil, and helps trees survive during the dry Harmattan season.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi tsei fioo komɛi ni haa hulutsoo. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be ni sa mli lɛ buɔ o-cocoa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean young cocoa plants are getting too much direct sunlight, lack nitrogen in the soil, or have roots soaked in waterlogged soil that cannot drain properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ etsɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I prevent tiny insects from destroying the young shoots on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are likely mirids (capsids) that suck sap and create dry patches on stems. You can manage them by removing damaged pods and spraying approved treatments at the right time of year.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji myrids (capsids) ni nuɔ nu lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hei ni egbi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ ni ooojie kɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni oooshwie nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land is good for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil is rich, dark brown or reddish, soft to dig into, and drains water easily so the roots don't rot after heavy rains.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli eyi obɔ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsuru. Ebaanyɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ egbooo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: How many years will I wait after planting before my cocoa trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ midu migbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani kookoo tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties can start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years under good care.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong foliage. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I plant legumes like beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and feeds crops like maize that need lots of nitrogen to grow well.
ga: Legumes yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa tsei tamɔ ŋmãa ni he hiaa nitrogen babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my seeds take a very long time to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to trigger germination—the process where the seed wakes up and shoots out roots. Without enough soil moisture, the seed remains dormant to avoid dying after sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu koni amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ amɛteɔ shi ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Koni shweremɔ akagbo yɛ shweremɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge leaves above ground but very small tuber roots beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi lɛ ji bibioo kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant directs all its food energy into growing tall stems and leafy green foliage instead of building thick starch roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi ni mli tse ni mli edɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during intense afternoon heat is a plant's natural defense to reduce sunlight exposure and cut down on water loss through transpiration, though persistent curling can also indicate insect pests like thrips or mites.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa be mli lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shi kɛ nu ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ latsaa ni baa shi lɛ he. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips loo mites moŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow so tall, thin, and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, plants shade each other and compete aggressively for sunlight. This causes them to stretch rapidly upward into thin, spindly stalks that fall over easily in strong winds.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei bibii ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong wind blows during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, superficial root systems rather than deep taproots. When the heavy fruit bunch develops and wet soil softens around the shallow roots, strong winds easily tip the heavy plant over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ mli tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni ebɔle shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ ahe lɛ bagbɔjɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ ashwie shi oya.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when daytime temperatures are extremely high or when the plant experiences sudden water stress, both of which prevent successful pollination inside the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. aloo beni tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpeɔ trukaa lɛ. Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do dark brown spots spread quickly across my yam leaves during continuous rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves during wet periods are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. Rain droplets splash fungal spores from leaf to leaf, and the damp conditions allow the fungus to multiply quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sweet potato baa lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa kroko nɔ. Ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Cocoa pods are fully mature when their outer skin color changes distinctly from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange-yellow color, showing that the sugary pulp inside has reached full ripeness.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eda kɛji hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ su tsake kwraa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ loo ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ edɔ kwraa.

english: Good soil for maize feels crumbly, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and is rich in organic matter. If your soil is hard like rock or very sandy, adding compost or animal manure helps improve its structure and gives the plants nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa lɛ mli etse. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli ni eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ loo ŋã babaoo Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, or the roots are suffering from too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer helps bring back the green leaf color and healthy growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai eŋɔli lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba shihilɛ kpakpa mli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and giving them light shade during very hot days helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How does planting my crops right at the start of the rains help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early planting allows young roots to capture the initial surge of nitrogen released in the soil by the first rains. It also ensures the crop reaches full maturity before the dry season sets in.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii ni amɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekwɛɔ hu koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sun. They naturally require shade trees or plantain plants grown beside them to act as physical barriers against hot sunlight and harsh winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibi ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Should I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant next season or buy fresh seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui heei?

english: Buying fresh certified seeds from approved dealers gives you strong plants that resist diseases and produce high yields. Saved seeds, especially from hybrid varieties, lose their strength and produce much lower yields in the next generation.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha tsei ni wa ni helai nyɛŋ atswa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ aba. Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ titri kɛjɛ hybrid henɔi amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii ni baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my pepper seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds need a balanced blend of warmth, air, and soft moisture to sprout. If planted too deep, watered excessively, or placed in hard, dry dirt, the seeds will either rot or remain dormant.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ hia dɔlɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nu ni mli edɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji adu mli tsɔ Nu babaoo Aloo okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni egbi nɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi loo amɛbaaya wɔɔ.

english: Why do small caterpillars keep eating the centers of my corn leaves every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ daa afi lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, which are born from moths that fly into fields and lay eggs on young corn. Regularly checking the funnels of young plants early in the morning lets you catch and destroy them before they wreck the whole crop.
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei bibii lɛ agbɛi lɛ amli daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: How can I prevent my yam tubers from rotting under the dirt before I dig them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite dani mafo amɛ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi and tiny worms called nematodes thriving in wet, poorly drained soil. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers so they stay dry and safe.
ga: Fung kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato ni egbo baa. Atsɛɔ enɛɛmɛi akɛ nematodes ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens if I put fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it safely. Applying chemical fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the salts around the roots, burning and damaging the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ haa ŋmei feɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eshãa ni efiteɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly when the rain stops for just a couple of weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need a constant supply of soil moisture to carry food and nutrients from the earth up into their leaves. When rain stops, the hot sun dries out the soil, forcing the plant to lose more water than its roots can pull in, which makes the leaves wilt to save energy.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛnyɛ amɛwo niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ afite nu babaoo fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ, ni enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Must I always wait for the rainy season before I can plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ be fɛɛ be dani madu dumɔwui?

english: You do not have to wait for the rain if you have a way to irrigate your land, such as carrying water from a nearby river or using a groundwater pump. Irrigation lets you plant anytime so you can harvest and sell crops even during dry seasons when market prices are higher.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ nugbɔ kɛji oyɛ gbɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okɛ nu awo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nu ni okɛbaajɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ mli. loo okɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu pɔmp atsu nii Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tsei be fɛɛ be. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okpa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ.

english: You should check if the rain has soaked deep into the earth—at least to the depth of your hand. Planting after just a light surface drizzle is risky because dry soil underneath will trap the seed in heat and dry it out before it sprouts.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ—kɛ hoo lɛ, ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ tamɔ onine. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baamɔmɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ latsaa mli ni eha amɛgbi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's clever way of defending itself against heat stress. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the burning sun, which cuts down on how much water evaporates from its leaves.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Do all crops need the same amount of water to yield a good harvest?
ga: Ani nu falɛ kome he hiaa tsei fɛɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: No, crops have different water needs based on their roots and biology. Moisture-loving crops like rice need plenty of water, while crops like cassava and sorghum have deep root systems that help them survive longer periods without rain.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ nu he hiamɔ nii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ bɔ ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli amɛha lɛ naa. Tsei ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, he miihia nu babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: How does using a tractor to plow my field help my crops grow better than using a hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ trakta ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A tractor plows deeper and breaks up hard earth far more evenly than hand tools can. Deep, loose soil makes it much easier for young plant roots to push downward, spread out, and drink trapped moisture and nutrients.
ga: Trakta baanyɛ atsu nii kɛya shɔŋŋ ni efo shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli nakai nɔŋŋ. fe nɔ ni nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ baanyɛ afee Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya shi, amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, ni amɛnu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ.

english: Can driving heavy machinery on my farm harm the way my crops grow later?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akudɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, if heavy machines move over wet ground, they squash the soil particles tightly together, a problem called soil compaction. Compacted soil leaves no air pockets for roots to breathe, making it hard for crops to grow properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsɔnei ni tsii nyiɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Naagba ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ eshiii kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku ko ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛakwɛ̃

english: Why does planting my crops in straight rows using a mechanical seeder give a better harvest than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ du mitsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa yibii kpakpai baa fe ni mikɛ nine baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every seed gets equal space, sunlight, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. It also leaves clear pathways that make it easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and care for the crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui fɛɛ dumɔwui naa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ awui. Ehaa onáa gbɛ ni mli ka shi faŋŋ hu ni haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okwɛ onibii anɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow and stop growing when heavy rain floods the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Roots need oxygen to breathe and absorb nutrients; without air, the roots start to drown and fail to feed the plant, turning the leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi gbee shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How can I keep water in my soil for my crops when the rains become irregular?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahiɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around the base of your crops with dry leaves, straw, or cut grass, a method called mulching. This organic blanket shades the ground from the hot sun and stops moisture from evaporating away too quickly.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Base tsei kɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo jwɛi ni afo, gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he tseee. ni etsĩ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ

english: How does adding chicken manure to my farm soil actually help my cocoa trees grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and essential nutrients that feed both soil organisms and plants. It improves the soil structure, helping it hold onto moisture longer so crop roots stay nourished and healthy.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei fɛɛ yeɔ nii babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Can I put fresh livestock manure directly around my young seedlings, or will it harm them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee abɔle he. Ani abaanyɛ adu mi dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: Fresh manure is too strong and produces high heat and gas as it breaks down, which can burn delicate crop roots. It should always be dried or composted first before putting it near young plants.
ga: Manɔ hee mli wa tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo baa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ agbi loo afee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be dani akɛwo tsei bibii ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct, harsh heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to shield them from burning while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa tɛ̃ɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ la he beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has poor drainage and is drowning the roots, which stops the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to keep chickens inside my cocoa farm, or will they destroy the crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ kooloi yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: A small number of chickens can help by eating insects and leaving behind manure, but too many chickens will scratch up shallow cocoa roots and damage tender young shoots.
ga: Kooloi fioo komɛi baanyɛ aye abua kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛyeɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Shi tsina ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa ŋmeii bibii anɔ.

english: How do I prevent my soil from getting completely ruined after farming the same piece of land for years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mishikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite kwraa beni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving crop residues on the field to rot naturally, applying organic manure, and avoiding complete bush burning keep organic matter in the soil so it stays fertile over time.
ga: Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ organic fertilizer atsu nii Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ shãa he kwraa. Koni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if the tree lacks water or soil nutrients, or if there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Cocoa tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in dark, overly wet, and crowded farms. Pruning extra branches allows air and sunlight to pass through and keep the pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ ni eyi obɔ, ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ agbi

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil waiting for sunlight. When you clear the land, sunlight wakes them up, and because weeds are very tough, they quickly consume available nutrients faster than young crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ taraa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛmɛɔ hulu la. Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu lɛ baate amɛ shi. Ni akɛni jwɛi lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ hewɔ lɛ, eyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe tsei bibii.

english: Why does my crop produce plenty of big green leaves but very little actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi aduawai diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: An excess of nitrogen in the soil pushes plants to grow leaves instead of flowers. Balancing the soil with other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kwɛɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into dust and get full of tiny black insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ mli sũ kɛ kooloi bibii diji lɛ? Ani eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils lay eggs inside the grain. If the maize is not dried thoroughly or stored in airtight containers like PICS bags, the eggs hatch and the beetles eat the grain from the inside out, turning it into powder.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa mli. Kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ kwraa loo akɛtooo nɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, tamɔ PICS kotoku mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛ mli kɛya kpo. ni etsɔ powda

english: How does drying my harvested rice properly prevent it from spoiling in the storeroom?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aaatsi enaa koni ekafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Fungi and bacteria need moisture to grow and cause rot. Drying rice to a safe moisture level removes this water, putting the grain into a sleeping state where mold and microbes cannot grow.
ga: Mold kɛ bacteria he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛgboi. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ, ejieɔ nu nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa ŋmaa lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ko ni mli ejɔ mli ni ŋmeii kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ nyɛŋ adara.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing green shoots even when I keep them inside a dark storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ tsũ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers have a natural biological clock. After a period of rest after harvest, the tuber automatically prepares for new growth by sprouting shoots, regardless of light, because it is using its stored energy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Beni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be fioo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bulbs lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa dalɛ hee he kɛtsɔ shweremɔ ni la kɔɔɔ he eko lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the crop moves the available nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed the young growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and difficult to cook if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ahoomɔ wa lɛ?

english: As cassava plants get older, they stop storing soft starch in the tubers and begin converting it into tough, woody fiber to support the growing plant above ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛtoɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tso ŋmeii ni wa koni amɛkɛye amɛbua tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off without producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, which prevents the flowers from successfully forming fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ kpe. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet potato tubers rot inside the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Too much rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, fungal diseases quickly attack and decay the waterlogged tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Fungal helai tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmatta ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds are dry and hot, sucking water out of large plantain leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry soil. The plant drops its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself from dying.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ. Ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai agboi amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why are tomato prices very low when everyone is harvesting, but extremely expensive a few months later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ miikpa nii lɛ? Shi ejara wa waa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: When every farmer harvests at once, the market gets flooded with tomatoes, forcing prices down. Months later, fresh tomatoes become scarce because fewer people can grow them off-season, pushing prices up.
ga: Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛkpaa nii lɛ Jarayeli lɛ eyi kɛ tomatoi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ajara ni baa shi. Nyɔji komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Tomatoi heei faaa ejaakɛ mɛi fioo ko pɛ duɔ amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji jara ni yaa hiɛ.

english: What is the reason behind keeping grain reserves in government warehouses after a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji jwɛŋmɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ nɔyeli nitoohei yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ agbo ko sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Storing surplus grain during good harvests keeps market prices stable for farmers, and releasing those stored grains during dry seasons prevents food shortages and high prices for consumers.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine ni akɛtoɔ yɛ kpamɔ kpakpa be mli lɛ haa jarayeli jara lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa okwaafoi lɛ. Ni ŋmaa ni ato lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni faaa kɛ jara ni yaa hiɛ kɛhaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ naa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillar droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to feed, which requires early detection and targeted application of approved pest control treatments.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ biɔ ni ana mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii.

english: High afternoon temperatures, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients can cause blossom drop. When the plant experiences stress from heat or water shortages, it sheds its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with lots of green leaves, but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ehaa chili fioo ko pɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus all its energy on growing stem and leafy foliage instead of setting fruit. Using a balanced fertilizer containing phosphorus encourages flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni fɔsfɔs yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases targeting that crop to multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yields even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that steal essential soil nutrients, fertilizer, and root space away from your crops, effectively starving the plants underground.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves as a protective defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which minimizes water loss through evaporation during hot weather.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo baa lɛ shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Is borehole water good to use directly for my vegetable farm during the dry season?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ sa akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, borehole water provides a reliable water source during dry periods, but it is best applied early in the morning or late in the evening near the root base to prevent thermal shock and excess evaporation.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ ji nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Shi esa akɛ akɛwo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishitoo lɛ koni tsakemɔi ni jɛɔ la ni mli edɔ fe nine kɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Cassava roots rot when water remains trapped around them in poorly drained soil, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as temporary sunshades, providing the young cocoa trees with essential shade and moisture needed during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ be kukuoo mli shade. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it important to support my yam vines with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei lɛ afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves off the damp ground toward sunlight, allowing them to capture energy more efficiently to feed the growing tubers underground while preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. abandoning tall trees Akɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains wo amɛhe shade mli loo adu amɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the upper growing leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when I plant them on flat land during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, well-drained soil to grow. Planting on flat ground causes rainwater to pool around the roots, drowning them and causing rot; planting on raised mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu mli gbee kɛ fitemɔ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ oya.

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows the leaves to spread out and capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight helps the plant make food, which is stored in the soil to form larger, healthier yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. Akɛ enɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans together with my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil food. This naturally fertilizes the soil for the neighboring maize plants without depleting the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteee jɛmɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but the flowers drop off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from water stress during very hot weather or when flowers are not properly pollinated by wind or insects. Regular watering and mulching the soil can prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dirt that looks like sawdust inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides deep inside the growing tip (funnel) of the maize plant and eats the delicate young leaves before they open up.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ naa (cone) ni miida lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni eyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and produce very small harvests even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa nɛɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive competitors on your farm. They steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops, leaving the main plants starved and weak.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ mɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers to plant so my new farm grows fast?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni madu koni miŋmɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ oya?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base. They establish stronger root systems and grow into healthier, more productive plantain trees than suckers with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘Sword Bud,’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse lɛ. Amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously in the same soil allows pests and soil diseases specific to peppers to multiply, while also exhausting the specific soil nutrients that pepper plants need to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmeii anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa ni pepper tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ hu.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves, showing it needs fertilizer like urea or NPK.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Beni tsei lɛ daraa Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo NPK awo mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my soil for next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plants harvest, that extra nitrogen stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa tsei lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all surrounding bush and trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei bibii kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and sensitive to strong, direct sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted nearby to shield them from intense heat and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods, starving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain off safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better for me to water my garden vegetables early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ mibɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows plants to absorb water before the hot sun evaporates it. Watering in the hot afternoon wastes water and can scorch stressed leaf leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ leebi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafite nu lɛ, ni ebaanyɛ eshã baai lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding on the leaf sap. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and viral diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with tiny dark brown spots inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the maize plant to eat soft inner leaves. Treating the plant early stops the worm from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsei ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on all their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and giving them full access to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ he fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when wind blows while bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow shallow, and a heavy bunch makes the plant top-heavy. Pests like root nematodes or weevils can also weaken the roots, so supporting the stem with bamboo poles keeps it upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni tsii tsii tso lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo weevils lɛ hu baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei tsu nii kɛfi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when temperatures get excessively high, when soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks sufficient water during the critical flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni yibii bɛ mli kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and rotting before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy seasons. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning shade branches helps air flow through the farm, keeping pods dry and healthy so they don't rot before harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ waa kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkafite dani akpa.

english: What causes small insects to bite my young cocoa pods and make them dry up on the branch?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii ŋmɔɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: These insects are mirids (capsids), which suck sap from young pods and stems, killing them. Applying approved treatments at the right time protects the growing pods so they stay on the tree until they mature.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji mirids (capsids), ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ amɛ. Tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be naa lɛ baabu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. So they stay on the tree until they mature.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees develop swollen stems and stop producing healthy pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi ashishifãi efuu ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ feemɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny mealybug insects. Affected trees slowly die and yield fewer pods, so removing infected trees protects the healthy ones nearby.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baagboi fiofio ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does protecting my cocoa pods from damage help me make more profit at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: When every pod on your tree reaches full maturity without rot or insect damage, you harvest heavier, higher-quality beans. More healthy pods directly increase your total harvest weight and farm income.
ga: Beni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ otso lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ edara kwraa ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ. Obaakpa ŋmeii ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo baaha okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli shika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it bad to leave overripe or infected cocoa pods hanging on my trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving bad pods on the tree creates a breeding ground for diseases and pests that spread to healthy pods. Harvesting every ripe and diseased pod regularly keeps your farm clean and protects future yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii gbohii yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa helai kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni ebaabu wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods so I don't lose bean quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ akafite.

english: Cocoa pods are ready when they change color completely, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or reddish-brown to orange. Harvesting at full ripeness ensures maximum bean weight and oil content.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛtsake amɛhe su kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. loo red-brown kɛyashi orange Nikpamɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tsiimɔ kɛ fɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches from my cocoa trees if I want them to bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ mli kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes useless branches that consume water and nutrients. It directs the tree's energy into growing strong flowers and healthy pods, while letting sunlight reach the main trunk.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛaatsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishitoo wulu lɛ he.

english: How does clearing tall grass and weeds around my cocoa trees protect my pods?
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te cacao tsei buɔ mi-pods lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that your cocoa trees need to build big pods. Weeds also trap damp air that causes pod rot, so keeping the farm floor clean keeps pods safe.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni pods lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Flowers fall off when trees lack nutrients or when natural pollinators like tiny midges are absent. Avoiding harsh chemicals that kill friendly insects and keeping soil fertile helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli loo kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ tamɔ midges lɛ bɛ. Tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, ni ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the forest trees above them are too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso ni eda lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: While young cocoa trees need shade, mature cocoa trees need sunlight to make flowers and mature their pods. Thinning overhead tree branches lets in light, encouraging higher pod production.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo he miihia kokoo tsei bibii. Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Niji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa la boteɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pod ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong green leaves. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the plants gives them the food they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ abɔle he. Tsei baaye abua tsei ni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in my farm than the crops I actually planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and very good at stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early gives your crops a fair chance to grow big enough so their own leaves shade the ground and stop new weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaai lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, heavy insect attacks like mirids (capsids), or poor soil nutrients. Providing enough shade during dry weather and managing pests early helps the trees hold onto their flowers until pods develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ hao amɛ. Kplukai ni tsii ni tutuaa mɛi tamɔ capsids loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Ni akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa baaha yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when the weather is too hot and dry, or when the soil lacks moisture and plant food like phosphorus. Watering regularly at the roots and putting grass mulch around the base keeps the root area cool so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ tsei ahe nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs bɛ lɛ, ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni okɛ sũ awo amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. koni fɔfɔii lɛ afee aduawai

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects called whiteflies that spread a virus, or by extreme sun heat and unpredictable watering. Using nursery nets for seedlings and controlling small insects keeps your tomato leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly lɛ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa. aloo kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ dumɔwui ni akudɔɔ kooloi bibii lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to put tall sticks next to my yam vines while they are growing?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama emasɛi? Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines allows the leaves to spread out high in the air to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers the plant to manufacture food, which flows down into the ground to make larger, heavier yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ babaoo. Hulu la haa tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.
