english: How do I know which suckers to cut off from my plantain stool?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ mi plantain ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli?

english: To get big plantain bunches, keep only one main producing stem, one medium follower sucker, and one small shoot on a single stool. Prune away all extra shoots so they do not steal food and water from the main bearing stem.
ga: Bɔni afee ni onine ashɛ plantains akuu agbo ko nɔ lɛ, Ha tso titri kome pɛ ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahi ohe. 1 sucker ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ kɛ sucker bibioo 1 ni yɔɔ sɛi kome nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli.

english: What makes my cassava tubers rot in the ground before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to run off, keeping the roots dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ babaoo. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during the Harmattan dry season even when I water them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ minine shwieɔ amɛnɔ nu moŋ?

english: During the Harmattan, the dry wind and intense heat pull water out of plant leaves faster than roots can soak it up. Plants naturally slow down their growth to protect themselves from drying out until cooler, rainier conditions return.
ga: Yɛ harmattan beaŋ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo.

english: If you planted high-yielding hybrid seeds, saving and planting those seeds will result in uneven, weak plants with smaller yields next season. It is best to purchase fresh certified hybrid seeds every season, or use open-pollinated varieties if you plan to save seeds.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ ni odu lɛ baaha tsei ni bɛ hejɔɔmɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli. Aloo okɛ ŋmeii ni agbele naa lɛ atsu nii kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahere dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why are my food crops growing so poorly under these big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Big trees block sunlight and compete aggressively for water and nutrients in the ground. When trees get too large, they can suppress and overtake nearby food crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni amɛkɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ da tsɔ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ atsu nii ni eye nɔ.

english: Why do tree roots seem to stop my food crops from growing well nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Tree roots spread very deep and wide, drawing heavily on soil moisture and plant nutrients. This leaves very little water and food for the smaller crop roots growing close to them.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ lɛɛ waa ni amɛmli kwɔ. Ejieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa tso bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. ni miida yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ

english: How do trees interact with food crops planted right next to them?
ga: Te tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ ahe?

english: Trees and food crops share the same space for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When trees are small, they can offer beneficial protection, but as they grow, they can overwhelm smaller crops if left unmanaged.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii tsei fɛɛ yeɔ he kome kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛha hebuu ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I stop shade trees from completely taking over my food farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ni haa shade lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi niyenii ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can regularly prune and trim the upper branches of shade trees. This reduces the canopy size, allowing enough direct sunlight to reach your food crops while still keeping necessary shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ daa ni ofolɔ amɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ aba shi. Ha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ ashɛ oniyenii tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ohiɛɔ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting too much shade from trees on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo kɛmiijɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: If your crop plants look thin, unusually tall, pale green, or fail to produce healthy fruits and tubers, they are likely receiving too much heavy shade from surrounding trees.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo, elɛɛmɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ, eyɛ su ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ewooo aduawai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Etamɔ nɔ ni ebaaná hulutsoo babaoo kɛjɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli.

english: What should I do when my food crops are being crowded out by tall trees?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ tsei ni kwɔlɔ eyi mi niyenii tsei lɛ amli obɔ?

english: You should thin out unnecessary trees or cut back overgrown limbs so your main crops get enough air circulation, light, and soil space to survive and yield well.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ afee bibioo loo ofolɔ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ koni oha otsei titrii lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa, la kɛ shikpɔŋ he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops bend towards one side when they grow under large tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa he kome kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei niji wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops naturally bend and stretch toward any available open sunlight. When tree branches block light from directly above, the crop tilts toward the nearest patch of open sky.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa hulu la ni yɔɔ lɛ he. Kɛ tsei aniji tsi la ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my food crops dying after the trees in my field grew very tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eda tsɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As trees mature, their leaves form a thick canopy that blocks out the sunlight food crops need to make energy. Without enough sunlight, sunlight-loving food crops eventually weaken and die.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaai lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu la naa, ni no ji niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ Niyenii tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu la lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ naagbee ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Is it good to leave tall trees in my field while growing food crops underneath?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi tsei kakadaji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni miduɔ niyenii yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: It depends on the number and size of the trees. While a few trees can protect soil from heat, too many tall trees create dense shade that prevents food crops from growing properly.
ga: Edamɔ tsei lɛ ayibɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei fioo ko pɛ baanyɛ abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa he moŋ, shi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ Fa tsɔ lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni mli wa ni haaa niyenii tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava and maize in a field full of growing trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni tsei ni miida eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant them when the trees are still small. However, as the trees grow larger and fill the field, you will need to give food crops more open space away from tree shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu amɛ beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ. Shi, beni tso lɛ daa ni eyiɔ he lɛ, Ebaabi ni oha oniyenii tsei lɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ babaoo ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifã lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives them the nitrogen needed to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil better for other crops later?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi aha tsei krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots with friendly bacteria that pull nitrogen food from the air and leave it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ ni helai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɔɔ mli ni gbalaa nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛshiɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to yield big fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the air humid so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi. Ha hulutsoo ni okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: How do I know which direction to push a cassava stem into the soil when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni esa akɛ matsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' along the cassava stem where old leaves grew out. Always plant the stem with these buds pointing upwards toward the sky so the shoots can grow properly above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he he ni baai ni edara lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ ni fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Spraying the plants with neem oil solution or insecticidal soap helps control these pests before they stunt your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shoo.

english: Why are there small holes and saw-dust like waste inside the central shoot of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ni ŋmeii ni tamɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This is a clear sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing point of the maize. Early application of registered bio-pesticides or local controls like clean wood ash in the funnel can protect your crop.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli. Biopesticides ni aŋmala awo wolo nɔ momo loo ni akudɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tamɔ tso sũ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ cones mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop even if they are growing a small distance away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmiida yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have very aggressive roots that quickly drink up soil moisture and absorb fertilizer nutrients before your crop roots can reach them, leaving your main crop weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ oya ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa otso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight. Using tall stakes raises the leaves off the wet ground where diseases spread, allowing them to catch maximum sunlight to feed the tubers growing deep underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tso kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewóɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Enɛ haa enáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfi bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant lacks water, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Regular watering during hot afternoons helps keep the blossoms on the vine.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua wain tso lɛ ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my hard crop seeds need to be soaked in hot water before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ midumɔwui ni wa lɛ ekomɛi awo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani adu lɛ?

english: Some crop seeds have very hard outer shells that stop water from getting inside. Soaking them briefly in warm or hot water breaks down that tough outer coat, helping the seed wake up and sprout much faster in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa waa ni haaa nu abote mli. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo nu ni mli edɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko Enɛ baaha yitsɔi kponɔgbɛ fã ni mli wa lɛ akumɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya.

english: Why does my compost heap need to get hot on the inside before it is ready for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-compost pile lɛ awo mli la mli dani efee klalo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The heat built up inside a compost pile is generated by tiny beneficial organisms breaking down plant waste. This high heat is necessary to kill harmful plant diseases, pests, and weed seeds so your final manure is safe to apply.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛfiteɔ tsei amli jwɛi. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɛɛ he miihia koni akɛgbe tsei ahe helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui. Bɔni afee ni okɛ onaagbee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I dump all my fertilizer in one big pile right at the root of my plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-fertilizer lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ ŋtayaa agbo kome mli kɛkɛ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Placing all your fertilizer in one spot makes it too strong for that one area, which can burn the plant's roots. Spreading it around the root zone helps the plant absorb nutrients evenly without destroying its roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ wo he kome lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee babaoo tsɔ kɛha nakai he lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. spread around Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ ni efiteee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up and turn yellow during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl during hot hours to protect themselves from losing too much water. The yellowing happens when the soil is too dry for the plant to draw up nutrients like nitrogen from the ground.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Yellowing baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to ferment and heat-dry my cocoa beans in the sun after harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-kokoo yibii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fermentation and sun-drying use natural heat to stop the bean from germinating, dry out moisture so mold cannot grow, and unleash the rich chocolate flavor required by cocoa buyers.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ egbiɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Fɛ̃i tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekakwɛ̃. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my freshly dug cassava roots rot so quickly if I leave them out in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi ni atsa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots lose water very fast and react to strong heat by damaging their internal tissues. This causes dark streaks and quick decay unless they are processed or kept in a cool place.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛtsuɔ he nii kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba kɛtsɔ mligbɛ fãji ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efiteɔ oya. ja atsu he nii loo akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing good yields when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of putting energy into producing big pods or ears.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛfee ŋmɔtɔi wuji loo toi.

english: Why do tomato flowers fall off my plants without forming fruit when the weather becomes too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, making it impossible for the flower to become fertilized. When fertilization fails, the plant drops the flower to save its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Kɛji fɔmɔ nii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehewalɛ he.

english: Why do leaf diseases spread faster across my farm when the weather is both warm and humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Fungi and crop diseases thrive in warm, moist conditions. High heat combined with humidity creates the perfect environment for disease spores to multiply and spread across your leaves quickly.
ga: Fungal helai kɛ dumɔwui shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni hulutsoo fata he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya yɛ obaai lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to dig such a deep hole when planting a young tree on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo bu ni mli kwɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ beni miduɔ tsei bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Digging a deep hole, up to a meter, allows the main roots to reach underground moisture deep in the soil, which helps the tree stay firm and survive dry seasons as it matures.
ga: Bu ni mli kwɔ fe mita kome ni atsa lɛ haa shishifãi titrii lɛ náa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli beni edara lɛ.

english: Why is it important to press the soil down firmly with my hands or feet after covering a seedling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛ oniji loo onaji atswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni okɛha dumɔwui lɛ ahe sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pressing the soil removes air pockets around the roots. If air stays trapped underneath, it dries out the soft roots, which can cause the young tree to die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooonyɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ehi shishi lolo. baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso bibioo lɛ agbo.

english: How high should I pack the soil around the stem when transplanting a seedling into the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mawo sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui miiwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should fill the hole completely to cover the entire root area, pressing the dirt down firmly to seal out air and protect the root stem from drying up.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ bu lɛ awo mli kwraa bɔni afee ni shishifã lɛ fɛɛ aha. Nyɛɛ muji lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli ni eha shishifã lɛ akagbi.

english: What causes a young tree seedling to suddenly die a few weeks after planting it?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui bibii gboiɔ trukaa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: A common cause is leaving loose soil with air pockets around the roots during planting. Trapped air prevents the roots from taking up water, leading to root rot or drying.
ga: Nɔ ni fɔɔ baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ebɔleɔ he. shishifãi yɛ dumɔ be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgbiɔ.

english: Is it bad for my crop if the soil right next to the planted stem stays very loose?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ mli etse waa?

english: Yes, loose soil allows heat and dry air to penetrate underground to the roots, which stops the roots from gripping the earth and damages the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi boteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛfite tso lɛ.

english: Is it safe to cut or trim some of the roots off a seedling before I put it in the ground?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaafo loo aaafolɔ shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ?

english: Yes, trimming long, damaged, or tangled root ends helps the plant focus on growing clean new roots into the fresh soil once planted.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishifãi ni kɛlɛ, ni efite, loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi heei ni he tse ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ kɛji adu lɛ pɛ.

english: How do farm chemicals like weedkillers affect the underground roots of my crops?
ga: Te ŋmɔ mli tsofai tamɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Harsh chemicals applied too close to plants can soak into the soil and burn sensitive roots, slowing down plant growth or causing root tip decay.
ga: Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ashã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo loo ha shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What should I do to a seedling's roots if I suspect they were exposed to bad chemicals in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛji misusuɔ akɛ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ amɛhe?

english: You can carefully trim off the outer affected root tips before planting so the damaged parts do not continue to decay under the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo shishifãi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni ena hela lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛdu. Bɔni afee ni fãi ni efite lɛ akaya nɔ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I protect my young tree roots if I hear that chemical fertilizers are causing problems in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ahe kɛji minu akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ naagbai miiba he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Ensure good planting practices by keeping chemical applications away from direct root contact and removing damaged root tips prior to transplanting into clean earth.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni adu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛbaashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ni jiemɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ.

english: Maize leaves roll up to reduce their exposure to the sun and conserve moisture. It is the plant's natural defense against heat stress when water is low.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛji nu faaa.

english: Is it okay for me to channel stream water across my farm to share with my neighbor's land?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ maha nu atsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ agba he sane?

english: Yes, but you must ensure the water channel is kept clean and not over-diverted so both farms get sufficient, clean water without causing soil erosion or water shortages downstream.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni nu lɛ gbɛ lɛ mli atse ni etsakeee gbɛ tsɔ. koni ŋmɔji enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná nu ni mli tse ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwiemɔ loo nu ni faaa yɛ faa lɛ shishigbɛ hei lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Early morning is best because the soil absorbs the water before the sun gets hot, allowing roots to soak up moisture without losing water to heat evaporation.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu ni nu ni jɛɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and rot after heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiifite beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air as well as water. When water sits on the field for too long, the roots drown, start to rot, and can no longer feed the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu he miihia pepper shishifãi. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛha tsei lɛ niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I do not separate my cassava plants from my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji migbalaaa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: If cassava and yam are planted too close without proper spacing, their roots and leaves will fight each other for nutrients, sunlight, and soil moisture, leading to smaller tubers for both crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni gbɛ ni sa bɛ amɛteŋ lɛ, Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ bulb bibii.

english: Why should I pull out some healthy seedlings if too many sprout together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji amɛdara tsɔ yɛ he kome?

english: Removing excess seedlings—called thinning—gives the remaining plants enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to grow strong and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ thinning. Enɛ baaha tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops turn yellow and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni edara blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your maize plants, leaving the crop undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei amli. ni haa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall and thin without producing any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee mlɛo ni fɔfɔi loo aduawai bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Tomato plants stretch upward when they are blocked from direct sunlight. They use all their energy searching for light instead of making flowers and fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ eshɛ amɛhe. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtaoɔ la moŋ fe ni amɛaafee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain trees turning brown and drying up while new leaves grow on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is normal aging. The plant transfers nutrients from old lower leaves to feed new growth and fruits, causing the older leaves to naturally dry up.
ga: Enɛ ji dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha shweremɔ hee kɛ aduawai. Ha baai momoi lɛ agbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves get eaten by insects more when I leave tall wild bushes around the edges of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi yeɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ babaoo beni mishiɔ jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔleɔ miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Wild bushes act as breeding grounds for farm pests. Keeping a clean border around your field stops insects from easily moving from the bushes onto your crops.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji he ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ oha ŋshɔ lɛ naa he tse yɛ Oŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkajɛ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii amli oya.

english: Why do buyers pay me less when my harvested crop is still wet or fresh out of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo kɛ́ mikpamɔ lɛ mli edɔ loo nu efo mli lɛ?

english: Wet crops weigh more due to water, not actual produce. Excess water also makes crops rot quickly during transport and storage, so buyers deduct money to cover the cost of drying and potential crop loss.
ga: Tsei ni efɔ lɛ tsii yɛ nu hewɔ. Jeee nɔ ni anáa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ Nu babaoo hu haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ jieɔ shika kɛjɛɔ mli koni ekɛwo shika ni ekɛgbiɔ nii lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ afite lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ.

english: Why do my plant leaves turn yellow and rot when water stays around the roots for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just as much as they need water. When soil stays soaked, the roots drown, rot, and cannot send nutrients up to the leaves, causing them to yellow and drop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni tso shishifãi hu he hiaa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ nu he hiamɔ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya baa lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high sunshine is a plant's defense mechanism to protect itself from drying out. By curling, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to conserve water until the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekagbi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haa amɛhe ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shwane mli latsaa lɛ baa shi.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing outwards. This wastes energy on tall stems rather than producing big tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe baawo ŋwɛi moŋ fe kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: Why do my crops look pale and weak even after heavy rain has fallen on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall gives water but can wash away nutrients in the topsoil. Water alone is not food for plants, so adding compost or fertilizer is necessary to feed the crops after heavy rains.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu baa shi ebaanyɛ ejie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nu pɛ jeee niyenii kɛha tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on my land before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stop growing fast even when the soil is fertile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miikpa shweremɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse moŋ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil nutrients, fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought or extreme heat, or when tiny insects that pollinate the flowers are missing. Keeping shade trees helps maintain soil moisture and beneficial insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji hɔmɔ loo latsaa ni naa wa ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo beni kooloi bibii Pollinators lɛ laaje lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are ready to harvest without pulling up all the crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikpaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Watch the leaves above ground; when they turn yellow and begin to drop, dig up two test plants. If the inner pods have dark brown or black spots, the whole field is ready to harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi gbee lɛ, ŋmɔ tsei enyɔ ni akɛkaa mɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ pod lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the young leaves of my maize plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like fall armyworms feeding on them. Checking early and applying organic or approved sprays protects the growing heart of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ cutworms, ni egbee shi ni eye amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni akɛ organic loo certified sprays ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ he.

english: Should I cut off some branches from my tomato plants or let all of them grow?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato niji lɛ ekomɛi loo maha amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Pruning extra side branches helps tomato plants direct their energy and nutrients toward producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than spending energy on excess leafy growth that blocks sunlight.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní ngɛ tsohi nɛ a daa pe nine nɛ tsiɔ hulu la nya ɔ he.

english: What happens if I do not trim the extra side shoots growing on my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifolɔɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving extra side shoots, often called water shoots or chupons, allows them to steal nutrients from the main tree stem. This creates a overcrowded tree that produces fewer pods and harbors pests like capsids.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni fata he ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ lɛ Nod Nam loo Chu Pong. Enɛ baaha amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi ni amɛhiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids.

english: How do I decide how many main branches to keep on my young mango tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ niji wuji enyiɛ ni esa akɛ mahi mi mango tso bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: Selecting 3 to 5 well-spaced, strong main branches early on creates an open structure that allows sunlight and air to reach all parts of the tree, helping it bear heavy fruit loads without snapping.
ga: Niji wuji 3 kɛyashi 5 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ halamɔ mra. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii ni tsii ni efoŋ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties branch out close to the ground while others grow straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava branching behavior depends on the specific variety; low-branching types quickly cover the soil to shade out weeds, while upright tall varieties leave ground space, making them ideal for intercropping with maize or beans.
ga: Bɔ ni ŋmãa niji lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ damɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsofai ni niji yɔɔ shishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya koni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni kɛlɛ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ shiɔ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa masɛi.

english: Why do the lower branches on my sweet pepper plants turn yellow and stop fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: As pepper plants grow taller, upper leaves shade the bottom branches from sunlight. Since these shaded leaves no longer produce food efficiently, the plant stops supporting them, making early removal of low branches helpful.
ga: Beni pepper tso lɛ da lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ buɔ shishigbɛ niji lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ kpa esɛɛfimɔ. Enɛ haa niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he.

english: Does a crop with more branches always give me a bigger harvest than one with fewer branches?
ga: Ani tsei ni yɔɔ niji babaoo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni yɔɔ niji fioo lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. When a plant has too many branches, it spends its food supply maintaining those branches instead of developing fruits or tubers, often resulting in smaller, poorer-quality yields.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Beni tso lɛ yɛ niji babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ nakai niji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee aduawai loo ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa anáa yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why should I stake and support all the main vines of my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-sweet potato tso lɛ mli wain tsei titrii lɛ fɛɛ shi ni mafi amɛsɛɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Keeping all main vines up off the wet ground prevents fungal rots and maximizes light absorption for bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ wein tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ tsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi fungal rot naa ni eha kane ni yɔɔ bulb wuji lɛ amli lɛ ashɛ babaoo.

english: How does trimming excess branches from my fruit trees help prevent diseases in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai tsei aniji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ helai anaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Trimming dense foliage improves airflow through the tree, allowing leaves and fruit to dry faster after rainfall, which significantly lowers the risk of fungal diseases like black pod disease.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni afolɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ aduawai ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my garden egg branches break so easily when the plant starts producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Branches break under heavy fruit weight when plants grow too top-heavy. Removing weak lower branches early encourages the main stem to grow thicker and stronger to support the harvest.
ga: Niji lɛ fãa yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi kɛji tso lɛ da ni etsii tsɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe awa koni eye ebua ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ.

english: Is it harmful to remove too many branches from my crop at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ majie tsei niji babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome?

english: Yes, cutting off too many branches at once shocks the plant because leaves are its primary source of food production through sunlight. Always prune gradually, leaving enough healthy branches for the plant to recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji babaoo ni afoɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ haa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ejaakɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ titri ni enáa niyenii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ. Esa akɛ afo tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli fiofio. Enɛ haa tso lɛ niji ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why does my maize keep getting sick every time I plant it in the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni abaadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, hela mɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Diseases can live inside the soil even after you harvest your crops. If you plant the same crop like maize in the same spot every year, the disease stays in the ground and attacks the new plants as soon as they start growing.
ga: Helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni okpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ he kome daa afi. Hela lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutuaa tsei heei kɛji amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ pɛ.

english: How can I clean my farm land if the soil is infected with a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsumɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hela?

english: You can practice crop rotation by planting a completely different crop, like groundnuts or cassava, that the maize disease cannot feed on. Without maize to attack, the disease in the soil slowly dies off.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsakemɔ atsu nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi kwraa, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa hela nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ Kɛji ŋmãa bɛ ni baatutua Helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaho aya fiofio.

english: Why does my soil seem to stay sick even after I leave the farm empty for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ mi beni mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi po lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases and fungi can survive deep in the soil or on wild weeds for a very long time. Simply leaving the land untouched for a few months is usually not long enough to kill the disease.
ga: Tsei ahe helai kɛ ŋmeii babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo yɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ashi he ko ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ, etsɛɛɛ tsɔ ni ekɛgbeɔ helatsɛmɛi.

english: Why are my maize plants dying so quickly when sickness attacks them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛji hela ba amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not have natural resistance to a disease or are growing in weak soil, their immune systems cannot fight off attack. The disease spreads rapidly through the plant tissues and destroys it.
ga: Beni tsei bɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ helai loo amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛgbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nii ni gbeɔ helai lɛ nyɛɛɛ awuu ashi tutuamɔ lɛ. Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ tsei amli fãji amli ni efiteɔ.

english: How do I stop maize diseases from destroying my crop every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa ŋmãa hela ni fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii daa be lɛ?

english: You can buy certified disease-resistant seed varieties from registered seed dealers. These seeds are naturally bred to survive and produce good yield even when disease is present in your area.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohe dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Atsɔ adebɔɔ nɔ akwɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji helai ba he ni oyɔɔ lɛ po.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing maize leaves are caused by disease or lack of soil nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ ni mi-ŋmãa baa ni ji yellow lɛ ba lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nutrients, the lower leaves usually turn yellow smoothly starting from the tips. When it is a disease, you will see spots, patches, or strange streaks scattered randomly across the leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛjɛ naagbee lɛ Kɛ́ hela lɛ mɔ lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baaje kpo ni egbɛ eshwã baai lɛ fɛɛ amli.

english: Will applying fertilizer to my farm cure my crops if they are already sick?
ga: Ani miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji hela mɔ amɛ momo?

english: Fertilizer acts like food, not medicine. It helps healthy plants grow strong and resist sickness better, but if a plant is already heavily infected by a disease, fertilizer alone cannot heal it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii, shi jeee tsofa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ emɔ lɛ waa momo lɛ, Fertilizer pɛ nyɛŋ atsa lɛ.

english: What can I do to feed my maize if I cannot afford chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha kooloi ŋmãa kɛji mibɛ shika ni mikɛbaahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: You can use farmyard manure, compost made from dried plants, or animal droppings. These natural materials feed the soil well at very low cost and improve soil health over time.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii. Kompost ni akɛ tsei ni egbi loo kooloi aŋmei fee Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shika ni baa shi waa mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it a waste of money to put fertilizer on maize that is already suffering from disease?
ga: Ani eji shika fitemɔ akɛ aaawo ŋmãa ni hela emɔ lɛ momo lɛ mli ŋmãa?

english: Yes, putting fertilizer on heavily diseased plants wastes money because the sick roots cannot absorb the nutrients properly. It is better to treat the disease or clear the field before investing in fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ heɔ shika ejaakɛ shishifãi ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsa helai loo ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ dani okɛ shika awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Can planting groundnuts or beans help my maize crop grow better next season?
ga: Ani ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them before maize enriches the ground naturally and helps break disease cycles.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii. Ebuaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dani adu ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ akumɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a natural protective cover that shields young trees from heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant food crops like cassava or maize on the same farm with my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Mixing short-term food crops with long-term trees allows you to harvest food and earn money while waiting for your tree crops to mature, while also making good use of farm land and suppressing weeds.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni otsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough for growing strong crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃mɔ?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, soft to dig through, holds moisture without staying flooded, and contains decaying leaves. When crops grow thick stems and dark green leaves, it shows the soil has good nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ efo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ mli Ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ. ni baai ni fiteɔ yɛ Be mli ni tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is clogged with too much water. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer gives plants the strength to make green leaves and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu babaoo efo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds regularly around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ ji daa.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Keeping the farm clean gives your crops full access to everything they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: This is typically caused by fungal diseases like Black Pod, which spread in overly damp and shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight flow through the farm, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal helai, tamɔ black pods, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the hottest time of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to the hot sun to conserve water inside its stems and roots.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ koni nu ahi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I trim branches off my grown cocoa trees when they seem fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛ kookoo tso ko ni ama shi shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cutting off dead, diseased, or overcrowded branches helps the tree direct its energy into producing bigger pods and healthy flowers, while also reducing dark hideouts for pests.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛ fɔfɔii wuji kɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the flowers on my fruit trees?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While moderate rain helps plants grow, heavy rainstorms can knock fresh flowers off the tree before they can form fruits or pods, which reduces the total amount you harvest later.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa moŋ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ atswa fɔfɔi heei kɛjɛ tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shika fɛɛ ni okpaa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa take years to bear fruit while vegetable crops take only months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tsei tamɔ kookoo woɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni aduawai heɔ nyɔŋ kome pɛ lɛ?

english: Tree crops spend their early years building deep root systems and strong trunks so they can live and produce for decades, whereas short-season crops put all their energy into quick flowering and fruiting within a single season.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni wa Koni enyɛ ehi shi ni ewo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Shi tsei ni yeɔ be kuku lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from hot, direct sunlight during their early years. Shade crops like plantains act like umbrellas, keeping the air cool and moist so the tender young cocoa roots do not dry out.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa Koni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi.

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, tomato plants experience heat stress and cannot pollinate properly. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy until weather conditions become cooler.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Leaf curling is usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies are sucking nutrients from under the leaves, or transmitting a virus. The plant curls its leaves as a reaction to this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies miimu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo amɛmiigbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. Tso lɛ baafolɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ hetoohamɔ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen food in the soil. The plant naturally pulls stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen ni ato kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and skinny with small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of building thick stems and large cobs, they waste energy stretching upward to catch light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ feɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji moŋ. Amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛmɔ la.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival trick to prevent water from evaporating. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts fresh leaves and continues growing its roots.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ koni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya ni shishifãi lɛ baaya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to capture sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves dry and healthy, which helps the plant produce bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa egbiɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I throw dry fertilizer directly touching the stem of my plants on a dry day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ anɔ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated minerals that need soil moisture to dissolve safely. Placing dry fertilizer directly against a plant stem strips moisture away, causing severe burns to the plant tissue.
ga: Minerals ni mli wa ni biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ mli. Ekɛ shãa ni naa wa baa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does growing maize on the exact same piece of land year after year give me smaller yields each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating with crops like groundnuts recharges the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive roots that steal fertilizer, water, and space away from your crops. If weeds are not removed early, they eat the plant food before your crops get a chance to use it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ wɔjieee jwɛi kɛjɛɛɛ jɛmɛ dani be shɛɔ lɛ, Amɛbaaye tsei aniyenii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are often caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this from ruining your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Niji ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves are turning light green because they need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia amɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn pale green or yellow starting from the leaf tips down the center, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen. Adding a top-dressing fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps restore healthy green leaves and strong cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting seeds too closely forces the young crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each stalk room to grow strong roots and yield larger, fuller ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná shishifãi ni wa ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji ni yɔɔ nii babaoo.

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by mulching around the plants helps protect the flowers so they can turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and how can I protect them?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu he?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Spraying recommended biopesticides or safe insecticides directly into the plant whorls early in the season protects the growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans alongside my main grain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko kɛɛ mi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and improves the growth of neighboring grain crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yams need loose, deep, and well-mounded soil to grow properly. Hard or stony soil blocks the tubers from expanding downward, forcing them to become stunted or twisted.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to powder and get tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powder ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: This damage comes from grain weevils that lay eggs inside dry maize. Drying your grain thoroughly on clean tarpaulins and storing it in airtight hermetic bags prevents these insects from surviving.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɔne ni mli tse nɔ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akahi shi.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Pruning shady tree branches to let sunlight reach the farm and clearing infected pods regularly stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni hulu la lɛ ayashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce my harvest even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your plants absorb all the nutrients they need to produce a full yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the surrounding trees from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei fɛɛ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow roots that burn under full, direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do older farmers tell me to plant cassava together with maize on the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛɛ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ akɛ amɛdu ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and takes nutrients from near the soil surface, while cassava grows slower and roots deeper into the ground. Planting them together uses the land efficiently without the two crops fighting for the same soil depth or space.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni enine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ daa blɛoo ni eshishifãi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Tsei ni fata he lɛ kɛ he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsei enyɔ lɛ ewuuuu amɛhe kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ loo he kome.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer restores this key nutrient so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii titri nɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.
